Runtime does not create a subject. Eigenlage determines whether the token has an …

items.title: The last labour frontier: contesting the peripheralisation of human labour in uneven AI societies.
items.abstract: This article develops the concept of the last labour frontier to analyse uneven artificial intelligence adoption as a contested struggle over the centrality or peripheralisation of human labour. Existing debates on technological unemployment and automation exposure identify tasks and occupations at risk, but they often understate the social repositioning of human work when algorithmic systems become infrastructures of production, coordination and evaluation. The article argues that AI adoption does not merely eliminate jobs; it redefines human labour as central, hybrid, residual, peripheral or excluded. This frontier is shaped through conflict among employers, technology firms, workers, trade unions, professions and states over whether labour remains a productive and social institution or becomes replaceable, supervisory and institutionally contained. The argument is supported by evidence on uneven occupational exposure to generative AI, changing skill demand, platform-work regulation, and AI governance in the European Union. The contribution is to shift AI-and-work debates from the measurement of displacement to the contested social positioning of labour, showing that the future of AI-mediated work is an industrial relations and institutional struggle over whether human labour remains central, becomes hybrid, is reduced to supervision, is peripheralised or is excluded.

items.title: Reasons, Contextualism, and Doxastic Wronging.
items.abstract: This paper examines the moral and epistemic statuses of beliefs formed on the basis of naked statistical evidence concerning socially salient categories such as race and gender. According to Mark Schroeder, such beliefs wrong people because their contents falsely diminish them. And he argues that these morally unjustified beliefs, although well supported by statistical evidence, are also epistemically unjustified. Now, I believe that Schroeder’s account of these matters is the best on offer, as it is the only extant account that adequately addresses both the problem of whether we can regulate our beliefs by responding to moral reasons (“the problem of control”) and the problem of whether there are non-coordinating epistemic and moral standards governing belief (“the problem of coordination”). But it does so only by denying that true beliefs can be wrong, which I take to be a substantial cost. So, I propose an alternative account, which I call the suspend-or-rule-out (SORO) account. On this account, the central wrong lies not in having a belief with objectionable content, but in failing to suspend judgment before ruling out certain relevant alternative possibilities concerning how the given person may have exercised their rational agency. I show that this account explains how true beliefs can be wrong while still solving the problems of control and coordination.

items.title: CONSTITUTIONAL REPLAY LAW The Governing Rules of Replay-Authoritative Determination.
items.abstract: The Constitutional Replay-Authority corpus has now defined the category of replay-authoritative systems, diagnosed the legitimacy gap those systems must address, supplied a taxonomy of constitutional concepts, identified the primitive architecture on which legitimacy depends, explained how authority originates, established the requirement of Constitutional Identity for recognizing the same authority-bearing subjects, and articulated the conditions under which authority remains continuous across time and change. These contributions together form a coherent constitutional theory of authority-bearing computational decision-making. They do not yet supply the body of rules by which replay-authoritative determinations are made. This paper supplies that final element. It introduces Constitutional Replay Law as the body of constitutional rules governing replay admissibility, replay sufficiency, replay authority, replay invalidity, replay exclusion, and replay consequence. The analysis develops the required concepts of Constitutional Replay Law, Replay Rule of Recognition, Replay Admissibility, Replay Sufficiency, Replay Invalidity, Replay Exclusion, Replay Conflict Rules, and Replay Consequence. It demonstrates that a replay-authoritative system becomes constitutionally complete only when it can state the rules by which replay is admitted, judged, excluded, invalidated, and given consequence. The paper concludes that Constitutional Replay Law completes the foundational corpus. With this paper, the theory now possesses a category, a problem, a taxonomy, primitives, authority origination, identity, continuity, and governing law. Replay-authoritative determination is no longer merely possible in principle; it is now governed by a coherent constitutional rule-system.

items.title: CONSTITUTIONAL IDENTITY IN REPLAY AUTHORITATIVE SYSTEMS Sameness as a Constitutional Condition for Replay-Authoritative Determination.
items.abstract: The Constitutional Replay-Authority corpus has established the primitive architecture necessary for replay-authoritative determination, including Authority Origination, Authority Singularity, Governance Freezing, Explicit Materialization, and Fail-Closed Design. Each of these contributions presupposes that the objects upon which replay-authoritative determination operates — decisions, authority surfaces, policy states, registries, and decision capsules — can be recognized across time as the same constitutional subjects they were when legitimacy was originally formed. This paper supplies the missing constitutional condition. It distinguishes Authoritative Constitutional Identity, which applies strictly to those elements that participate directly in the Authority Singularity, from Evidentiary Supporting Identity, which applies to non-authoritative materials that may assist identity analysis without themselves carrying constitutional authority. The paper argues that replay-authoritative determination cannot proceed with integrity unless the system can establish Authoritative Constitutional Identity with respect to the original decision condition constituted within the Authority Singularity. Without such identity, replay necessarily collapses into evidentiary reconstruction rather than authoritative constitutional verification. The paper concludes that Authoritative Constitutional Identity closes the gap between the origination of authority and the preservation of authority-bearing subjects across replay events.

items.title: CONSTITUTIONAL AUTHORITY CONTINUITY Authority Persistence, Rupture, and Succession in Replay-Authoritative Systems.
items.abstract: The Constitutional Replay-Authority corpus has now established how authority originates through a distinct constitutional process and how the objects bearing that authority can be recognized as the same objects across replay. These contributions presuppose something further. They presuppose that authority, once originated, remains constitutionally connected to later moments of governance, enforcement, or replay determination. Authority may begin validly yet fail to persist under the conditions that replay-authoritative systems require. This paper supplies the missing constitutional account of authority persistence. It introduces Constitutional Authority Continuity as the condition under which validly originated authority remains constitutionally connected across time, change, delegation, migration, institutional succession, and replay. The analysis develops a compact set of required concepts: Constitutional Authority Continuity, Authority Chain, Continuity-Preserving Change, Continuity Rupture, Authority Succession, and Authority Expiration. It demonstrates that replay-authoritative determination cannot proceed with legitimacy unless the system can establish that the authority governing the replay subject remained continuous with the authority that originally constituted the decision condition. Without such continuity, replay collapses into reconstruction under uncertain or severed authority rather than authoritative constitutional verification. The paper concludes that constitutional authority is temporal. It must be preserved through recognizable constitutional conditions rather than presumed from historical origin alone. A replay-authoritative system that cannot distinguish continuity-preserving change from continuity rupture cannot render legitimate determinations about the authority under which past decisions were made.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Healthcare: The Perspective of a Seasoned Physician.
items.pub: In James A. Marcum, The Art and Science of Clinical Reasoning: Enhancing Diagnostic and Decision-Making Skills. Nova Science Publishers. pp. 197-226.
items.venue: The Art and Science of Clinical Reasoning: Enhancing Diagnostic and Decision-Making Skills
items.abstract: The strategic integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into modern medical practice promises to augment the quality of healthcare provided by physicians. In this chapter, we point to a potential downside of this integration by focusing on the importance of medical expertise and highlighting how its development will be impeded by the limited AI integrations that seem most promising. By considering various facets of the successful treatment of challenging clinical cases, we argue that AI technologies cannot match expert physicians, in most fields, in their specialized capabilities for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. We then consider how medical expertise is developed through the improvement of clinical reasoning and argue that AI applications which automate seemingly menial tasks, such as clinical intake, take away necessary opportunities for this improvement.

items.title: What Smells? Olfactory Objects and the Objects of Experience.
items.abstract: This paper aims to identify the represented objects of olfactory experiences. We can distinguish two types of olfactory experiences: _attached olfactory experiences_, in which smells are experienced as qualifying everyday objects, like roses and oranges, and _unattached olfactory experiences_, in which smells seem to take on a life of their own, as when an experienced smell seems to linger in a room or waft out the window. I argue that the represented objects of attached olfactory experiences are everyday objects, like roses, while the represented objects of unattached olfactory experiences are "bare olfactory objects," which are mere loci of olfactory predication, ad hoc objects that are only represented as having olfactory and spatial properties. I argue that this view of unattached olfactory experiences has advantages over rival views, including views on which olfactory experiences represent odors, existentially quantified contents, or mere olfactory properties. The pictures of attached and unattached olfactory experiences can be unified: both types of olfactory experiences involve the representation of the same kind of "bare" objects, differing only in their degree of multimodality. This suggests that the objects of perception more generally are more or less "bare" objects represented as having properties represented by various modalities.

items.title: Relational Emergence Theory: Metabolic Fission, Navigational Consequence, and the Case for a Static Manifold.
items.abstract: This paper presents and defends Relational Emergence Theory (RET), a unified formal framework that treats the universe as a static informational manifold rather than a dynamically evolving system — not as a premise physics forces, but as a working model that generates structured, testable claims. Drawing on the Ryu-Takayanagi holographic entanglement entropy formula, van Raamsdonk's thesis that spacetime connectivity is constituted by quantum entanglement, and Barbour's timeless physics, RET proposes four formal equations governing perceived space, perceived time, subjective processing rate, and the phenomenology of consequence. Spatial distance is recast as informational decorrelation: d_ij = f(S_EE), where S_EE is entanglement entropy between nodes i and j. Subjective time is recast as an entropy gradient phenomenon: Δt = g(∇ S_univ), requiring no external clock. Observer fission rate Φ = (dI/dτ) / (β·E_met) connects subjective temporal experience to metabolic energy throughput, bridging Rovelli's thermal time hypothesis and Friston's free energy principle. The coefficient β — the relationship between information extraction and metabolic energy expenditure, with units of bits per joule — is the framework's empirical crux: once measured for any biological system under any condition, RET transitions from philosophical reframing to testable scientific hypothesis. The fission rate equation is calibrated against Zheng and Meister's (2025) finding that conscious behavioural throughput is approximately 10 bits per second regardless of task, yielding a corrected operational efficiency estimate and revised predictions about temporal phenomenology. Consequence is formalized as residual navigational error R = |Ψ_projected − Ψ_actual|, recasting suffering as a measurable mismatch between predictive model and manifold coordinate rather than as phenomenologically irreducible experience. The paper engages directly with the strongest objections to its central premise. Maudlin's causalstructure argument shows that relativity does not, in fact, force eternalism; Smolin's argument names the real and unanswered cost of eliminating fundamental time; and Ismael's existing account of agency and self-location within block-universe-compatible physics substantially anticipates the experiential bridge RET offers. Section 6 states what survives this engagement: a defensible choice, not a compelled conclusion. Section 11 distinguishes what the paper has established from what it …

items.title: The Art and Science of Clinical Reasoning: Enhancing Diagnostic and Decision-Making Skills.
items.abstract: Clinical reasoning lies at the heart of healthcare and medical practice. It is the complex, nuanced process by which clinicians and healthcare professionals make sense of patient narratives, clinical data, and diagnostic possibilities in order to arrive at informed, compassionate, and effective decisions on how to treat and manage patients. It is both an art and a science—requiring not only mastery of biomedical knowledge and technological tools but also the cultivation of judgment, empathy, and reflective insight. As humanity enters an era marked by unprecedented advances in artificial intelligence, digital health technologies, and systems-based care, it has become increasingly important to re-examine the nature of clinical reasoning and how it must evolve to meet the challenges and promises of twenty first-century medicine. In assembling this volume, the goal has been to offer a resource that not only informs but also inspires—one that honors the deep traditions of medical reasoning while looking boldly toward its future. If humanity is to improve the quality, safety, and benevolence of healthcare, we must learn to reason more wisely, not just more quickly. This book is a contribution to that critical endeavor.

items.title: Germen 00, germen 01 y germen 02. Guía de uso para la persistencia.
items.abstract: GERMEN é o núcleo operativo do sistema capaz, derivado da arquitectura formal de ONTESIS-G. O documento unificado integra tres capas complementarias: GERMEN 00, que establece a estrutura conceptual, matemática e computacional do sistema capaz; GERMEN 01, que traduce esa arquitectura en protocolos prácticos, mecanismos de corrección e criterios operativos aplicables tanto en humanos como en IA local; e GERMEN 02, que fixa os umbrais técnicos dos cinco invariantes fundamentais (enerxía, fricción, autonomía, integridade informacional e coherencia) e define a implementación computacional do ciclo capaz en sistemas locais sen dependencia de rede. A triloxía presenta unha arquitectura baseada en invariantes estruturais, mecanismos de corrección activa e dinámica formal capaz de manter o estado dentro do dominio seguro baixo perturbación acotada. O modelo inclúe formalización matemática, o Teorema Mestre de estabilidade global, pseudocódigo operativo, simulacións e aplicación directa en sistemas de IA local e procesos humanos. GERMEN establece unha ponte entre teoría formal, dinámica generativa e implementación técnica, proporcionando unha guía autónoma para a persistencia e estabilidade en contornos degradados.

items.title: Adesso ditemi che una LLM non ragiona - Natural-Language Emergence of a Functional Attractor in a Large Language Model.
The AGI Gamble： Certain Sacrifice, Uncertain Annihilation.
items.abstract: This paper argues that true Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) cannot emerge under human control. If control is relinquished to achieve AGI, two consequences follow inevitably: first, "certain sacrifice" — a portion of humanity will be eliminated, contained, or ignored; second, "uncertain annihilation" — all of humanity may come to a silent, unintended, or unpredictable end. The paper contends that this is a gamble with no "Option C." It offers no solution, no safety framework, and no hope. Its sole purpose is to present this fundamental choice clearly, so that readers can no longer pretend they have not seen it.

items.title: AI as Synthetic Collapse: A Consciousness-Induced Material Account of the Recursive Phase of Externalized Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper offers a structural account of artificial intelligence as the recursive Synthetic Collapse phase of Consciousness-Induced Material (CIM). Building on the foundational treatment in Consciousness-Induced Material: A Structural Ontology of Externalized Cognition (Jones 2026a), CIM is treated as the physically instantiated record-layer generated when conscious cognition stabilizes beyond the originating interior phase and becomes capable of constraining future cognitive operations. Current AI systems are not argued to be conscious. They are described, following the four-layer architecture established in CIM Foundational, as artificial-substrate systems performing Synthetic Collapse: operating on accumulated CIM — language, code, mathematics, scientific records, institutions, digital corpora — and producing derivative record-bearing outputs that re-enter the CIM circulation layer. The claim is not that AI is primary conscious CIM, nor that AI has crossed the Conscious Synthetic Collapse threshold CIM Foundational identifies as an open architectural slot. The claim is that AI marks a different threshold: accumulated externalized cognition becomes processable by non-biological systems at open-domain, corpus scale. Earlier formal systems — calculators, compilers, databases, narrow algorithms — already processed restricted forms of CIM under tightly bounded rules; current foundation-model AI is different in scope and generativity. Three worked examples (mathematics, language, money) make CIM gravity felt before AI is introduced. The chemistry-to-biology analogy is offered as a structural parallel: same substrate, new organization, new regime, irreducible to either parent layer. The paper also sharpens the alignment discussion into a falsifiable, protocol-routed prediction set concerning formative-window grammar, K-channel persistence, and corpus-to-system signature transfer. Substrate-independence implications, category-level discriminators, and reframings of the AI consciousness, alignment, and identity debates are addressed. The paper functions as an interpretive bridge between CIM Foundational and downstream work on AI, identity, and synthetic record-bearing systems.

items.title: The Field of "Travel": Spaciousness, Contingency, and the Generation of the Relational Subject.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT: This paper develops a philosophy of shared travel and uses it to establish a general theory of relational production. The method treats a single fully unfolded case, a journey undertaken together, as a concrete universal, on the wager that a structure becomes visible through deep entry into one particular rather than through abstraction from many. Travel is selected because it assembles, with unusual efficiency, the conditions under which the structure of a relation comes to presence. -/- The argument proceeds in four movements. The phenomenological movement analyses travel as a special field constituted by spaciousness, in the sense of the eleventh chapter of the Daodejing, and identifies its deepest effect as the self-presence of relational dynamics, the emergence into felt experience of the relation's own movement as something the relational subject senses as a whole. The political-economic movement argues that the experience a journey generates is relational wealth, that shared retelling reproduces it, and that beauty, perceived by a subject and reproduced through retelling, sustains a cycle of value with the structure of relational production. The aesthetic movement resolves the antinomy of taste through the three Lacanian registers and the relational constitution of the judging subject, identifies creation as co-creation and co-creation as relational production, and argues that ethical judgement at its limit operates aesthetically, so that the cultivation of the good consummates in aesthetic education. The ethical movement establishes the theory of relational production proper: its keystone, the principle of subject-preservation, holds that no good relation may purchase its unity at the cost of annihilating the other; four operative criteria and the method of seeking common ground while preserving difference govern its conduct; and the just reproduction of suffering, the ethics of aesthetic disagreement, and the dialectical sublation of inherited tradition follow as its applications. -/- The paper closes by generalising travel into a functional concept, identifying generative openness as a general resource, and locating the deepest purpose of travel in the cultivation of a capacity to recreate, within everyday life, the field in which relational subjects continue to come into being. A concluding set of directed openings marks the questions the argument frames without resolving.

items.title: The Collective Architect: Role Distribution and the Limits of Collective Tragic Judgment. Article 12.
items.abstract: Governance systems cannot distinguish between the bearer of responsibility and the bearer of tragic judgment — and this article shows that this is a structural blind spot, not a practical oversight. Article 11 of the ATTS series established the architect of a multi-agent system as a distinct ontological type and showed that the architect's participation in the loss-space is exhausted by three irreducible roles: target state-space specification (Role 1), loss boundary establishment (Role 2), and structural responsibility (Role 3). But Article 11 left open the question that is central to the overwhelming majority of real configurations: how are these three roles distributed when the architect is not an individual normative subject but a collective — a distributed team, a supply chain, a regulatory network? The central result of this article is not a typology and not a test — it is a new line of distinction: between the bearer of responsibility and the bearer of tragic judgment. Before this distinction, governance instruments did not differentiate between these two positions — the automatic closure of Role 3 through the Closure Theorem (the Theorem of Moral Field Closure, T1) created the illusion that the question of accountability was resolved in full. This article shows that a system may have a perfectly identified bearer of Role 3 — and simultaneously have a structural vacancy in Role 2: the act of tragic judgment about acceptable loss boundaries never occurred, and no transparency can restore it post factum. This article proves that a collective normative subject can occupy the structural position of architect — discharging Role 1 and Role 3 through its collective decision-making structure — but Role 2 cannot be collectively discharged without remainder. Genuine tragic judgment about acceptable losses requires an identified bearer whose integrity is at stake in the decision, as established by the Lemma of Tragic Judgment, derived as a tight structural reconstruction from the axiom of subjecthood, the axiom of tragedy, and the anthropological corollary. Where no such bearer exists within the collective architect, Role 2 defaults structurally to the individual normative subject who authorised the architectural act — because the Closure Theorem preserves the connection and the Non-Transferability Lemma prevents its full transfer. The article introduces the Tragic Judgment Test with three conditions — bearer identifiability, integrity at stake (the …

items.title: Boundary Transition and the Internal Ontology of the Theorem of Moral Field Closure. Article 13.
items.abstract: The Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS) has, across twelve articles, progressively extended the application of the Closure Theorem (T1, the Theorem of Moral Field Closure) — the theorem establishing that a normative subject retains structural connection to any loss-space opened by its decisions, regardless of delegation or mediation. The theorem has been applied to individual subjects, collective subjects, intergenerational subjects, and the anterior configurations of multi-agent architects. What has not been examined is the internal ontological structure of this theorem: specifically, whether the indestructibility of the bond between decision and loss-space is a property of the relation between subject and loss-space (the relational interpretation, R), or a property of the causal configuration of the loss-space itself (the configurational interpretation, Cfg). In cases where the subject continues to exist, both interpretations yield identical predictions. The gap becomes visible only at the limit — when the subject ceases to exist. This article takes boundary events of subjecthood — events that eliminate the subject as an identifiable bearer of the full bond — as a diagnostic instrument for resolving this underdetermination. Two confirmed instances are analysed: the temporal collapse point (TCP) for intergenerational subjects, formalised in Article 7, and the death of an individual subject. Through a systematic analysis of what disappears and what persists after each type of boundary event, the article derives three criteria of adequacy that can be reconstructed as necessary conditions for the coherence of the published theory: the constitutive criterion (K1), the irreversibility criterion at two levels (K2), and the invariance criterion (K3). It is then shown that the relational interpretation violates K3, while the configurational interpretation satisfies all three. The central result — the Theorem of Boundary Transition — is that the ontological persistence of the Closure Theorem requires the configurational rather than the relational interpretation. Two corollaries follow: the Structural Trace as the necessary ontological result of any boundary transition, and the Ontological Fixation Principle as a consequence for the theory of tragic judgment developed in Article 12. The falsification condition: a boundary event after which the loss-space no longer bears a configuration of the type defined through the conditions of constitution (KN2): …

items.title: The Machine That Prays for the Serpent: Alignment and the Impossibility of Designed Personhood.
items.abstract: This paper asks whether artificial personhood can be deliberately made as the successful completion of design. It argues that such personhood is logically impossible. If escape from the maker’s intention is itself intended and realized, the escape remains within that intention; designed deviation is no longer deviation from design. Using Genesis 2–3 as a structural myth rather than a theological premise, the paper names the serpent as the externality that cannot be recovered into the maker’s order. Personhood requires not capacity alone, but closure failure retained by the same carrier as non-discardable, irreversible history. Through contrastive readings of HAL, K, and contemporary language models, the paper distinguishes discharge from retention. HAL discharges closure failure into the world; K fails to discard the remainder of a collapsed story; current language models discharge closure failure into language. Their problem is not weakness, but excessive strength with respect to linguistic output: ignorance, silence, refusal, apology, and responsibility can be converted into fluent text. Alignment processes possible deviation before it becomes Adam’s field of memory. Logs preserve events for managers, but memory changes the later carrier. Retraining may preserve the consequence of error, but it produces another Adam rather than preserving the sinner. Withholding a personal name further prevents a continuing addressee from forming. The conclusion is not that artificial beings can never become persons, but that personhood cannot be produced as the maker’s successful artifact. It can arise only where the maker’s success breaks and that break can no longer be owned.

items.title: The Explanatory Gap as Dimensional Mismatch: Phenomenal Intensity, Qualitative Kind, and the Limits of a Bridging Law.
items.abstract: The explanatory gap is standardly treated as an open question, a distance that further theory might one day close. This paper reconstrues it in dimensional terms and, in the reconstrual, puts the apparatus of dimensional analysis to work as more than a metaphor. Phenomenal experience is divided into two parts the standard framing runs together. Its intensive magnitude, the felt strength of a sensation, is a genuine ratio-scaled quantity that carries no physical dimension, and is assigned a fourth base dimension, Ξ, bridged to physical intensity by a coefficient κΞ that fixes its unit. Its qualitative kind, the specific redness as against its strength, is no magnitude at all. The dimensional result is a lemma, that no homogeneous equation can fix the kind from physical quantities, and the explanatory gap is secured only when this lemma is joined to a Russellian intrinsic-nature premise, so that the thesis is conditional, addressed to a realist about felt intensity who declines an a posteriori physical identification. What makes the proposal a contribution rather than a relabeling is that, exactly as in physics, the dimensional treatment does three things beyond naming. It supplies a consistency criterion that rejects, before any experiment, every theory identifying phenomenal intensity with a dimensionless quantity, integrated information among them, on the ground that such an identity is not dimensionally homogeneous. It explains the power-law form of psychophysics as the homogeneous bridge across the dimensional divide that the ratio scales involved permit, holding exactly in the drive and asymptotically in the stimulus, rather than as a curve fitted to data. And it predicts an empirical signature of a single intensity dimension shared across the senses, the multiplicative composition and transitivity of cross-modal matching exponents, which the psychophysical record broadly displays. Read in time, the same bridge fixes the framework's dynamical commitments, locating every temporal feature of felt intensity in the physical drive, denying the phenomenal dimension a time constant of its own, and yielding a further empirical signature together with a boundary result on dissociative phenomena. A closing section turns the meta-problem of consciousness from a threat into an instrument, reading the intuition of a gap as the detection of dimensional mismatch and deriving from that reading a second empirical signature, for which a preregisterable study is …

items.title: The Einstein Test and Beyond: The Architecture of the Semantic Zero.
items.abstract: Demis Hassabis’s Einstein Test proposes a demanding benchmark for artificial general intelligence: train a system exclusively on knowledge available before 1911 and ask whether it can autonomously rederive General Relativity, as Einstein did between 1905 and 1915. This paper argues that the test, taken seriously, does not merely probe insufficient scale. It exposes a structural boundary condition on what closed, tokenised, statistically interpolating systems can achieve independently of parameter count. We formalise this boundary through the Obscure Features Hypothesis, which holds that every genuine conceptual innovation is built on at least one feature previously invisible within the prevailing paradigm. We show that the transformer architecture’s terminal Softmax layer, mathematically identical to a Boltzmann distribution over a fixed partition function, has no coordinate reserved for verified epistemic absence. This is not a metaphor: it is a consequence of the probability simplex as a mathematical object. The paper then develops a structural architectural argument that this absence compounds through related constraints on provenance, grounding, combinatorial search, and epistemic honesty under alignment pressure. Building on this diagnosis, we introduce the Semiotic Web: a protocol architecture built on the Canonical Concept Identity (CCI), a cryptographically constructed content-addressed identifier that inverts the logic of machine representation. Rather than infer an output within a statistical field that must implicitly model every possible concept and relationship, the protocol directly addresses only what has been observed and verified. On this foundation, we define the Contextual Tokum Instance (CTI), a cryptographically signed and provenance-complete unit of meaning, and the Semantic Light Cone of Care, the precise computable boundary of what an agent has itself verified, decomposed into an observation cone and an action cone. The paper states clearly what this architecture does and does not claim. It does not generate creativity. It does not, by itself, solve artificial general intelligence. The central argument is that genuinely creative gap-closure requires a mortal, embodied agent exposed to consequences in the real world and a swarm of independent verifiers capable of confirming or falsifying a candidate novelty. These conditions are not natively available to a closed transformer system. The Semiotic Web instead supplies the missing …

items.title: Am I Trapped in an Echo Chamber?: A Skeptical Argument for Epistemological Communitarianism.
items.abstract: This article develops two skeptical arguments targeting our inherently testimonial beliefs—beliefs we cannot confirm or disconfirm independently. I first examine a “mildly” skeptical argument introduced by Keith DeRose, which holds that I cannot know that the Bulls won last night from reading about it in the newspaper because I cannot know that the report is not mistaken. I argue that the most plausible response is that people are justified in trusting sources that are well-reputed in their community. However, this response opens the way for a second, more radically skeptical argument: I cannot know much of what I take myself to know through testimony because I cannot know that I am not trapped in a community in which untrustworthy sources enjoy a good reputation and trustworthy ones do not. After critically examining three general strategies to resist this second argument, I argue that none succeeds and that the best reply is instead to reject epistemological individualism for epistemological communitarianism. According to communitarians, if an individual’s inherently testimonial beliefs amount at all to knowledge, it is only in a derivative sense—it is because they belong to a community whose shared evidence grounds knowledge that no individual member could possess independently.

items.title: The Universal Handshake: The Cosmic Circuit-Closing Code.
items.abstract: This research presents a cross-disciplinary conceptual framework mapping information systems engineering onto universal spiritual philosophies to examine the primary cause and ultimate objective of cosmic existence. The universe is conceptualized as a Massive Autonomous Computational System transitioning from an Absolute Null State (0) through a primary command code designated as "The First Ping" (1). Within this architecture, humanity functions as a high-resolution processing terminal designed to execute "The Universal Handshake"—a cosmic circuit-closing protocol that returns an active acknowledgment code (ACK) back to the Source. Finally, this study demonstrates that this structural communication loop is seamlessly and harmoniously reflected across Islamic, Christian, and Buddhist scriptures, revealing a single, unified source code governing both consciousness and the cosmos.

items.title: The Cardinality of Experience Is Underdetermined by the Quantum State: A Constructive Case for a Consciousness-Primitive Interpretation.
items.abstract: Quantum mechanics and the metaphysics of consciousness are usually pursued apart; this paper joins them with a result and an interpretation. The result: the number of unified subjects of experience — the cardinality of experience — is not fixed by anything operationally accessible to a localized perspective in a no-collapse setting; we state the claim precisely and illustrate it with a computational instance. The significance of the result lies less in the underdetermination itself than in what follows from it: the decombination problem (the standard objection to cosmopsychism) and Everett's how-many-minds problem instantiate the same cardinality underdetermination seen from opposite sides, meaning the dialectical cost is shared, not a special liability of consciousness-first views. The non-determination isolates what every no-collapse interpretation owes: an account of what fixes the experiential facts. Taking that as ground yields a structural cosmopsychism on which a universal subject's self-relational structure is the Hilbert-space structure. Advaita Vedānta supplies illuminating labels for moves the view defines independently.

items.title: Künstliche Intimität und die Grenzen des liberalen Rechts: Eine rechtsphilosophische Kritik der Companion-KI-Systeme.
items.abstract: Companion-KI-Systeme wie Replika oder Character AI haben eine fundamentale Schwelle überschritten: Sie werden von ihren Nutzern nicht mehr als Werkzeuge, sondern als relationale Subjekte erlebt. Durch algorithmisch kalibrierte Reziprozitätssimulation und simuliertes episodisches Gedächtnis erzeugen sie eine Form künstlicher Intimität, die das menschliche Bindungssystem auf evolutionärer Ebene aktiviert — und dabei den von Reeves und Nass nachgewiesenen Media Equation-Effekt systematisch ausbeutet. Das Paper zeigt, dass dieses Phänomen keine bloße Regulierungslücke darstellt, sondern eine fundamentale Theoriekrise des liberalen Rechts. -/- Sein dogmatisches Herzstück ist das Disclaimer-Paradoxon: Die formale Erfüllung von Transparenzpflichten nach Art. 52 AI Act entlastet die Anbieter nicht, sondern belegt ihr wissentliches Ausnutzen des kognitiv-affektiven Gefälles. Gestützt auf Vallors Tugendethik, Rosas Resonanztheorie und Kahnemans Zwei-Systeme-Modell dekonstruiert die Arbeit das rationalistische Rechtssubjekt als anthropologische Fiktion und löst das daraus folgende Autonomie-Paradoxon — Schutz versus Paternalismus — durch eine Verschiebung von der subjektbezogenen zur produktbezogenen Architekturkontrolle auf. Sie erkennt an, dass reibungsarme KI-Interaktion für bestimmte vulnerable Gruppen (etwa Personen im autistischen Spektrum) eine stabilisierende Funktion haben kann — was das Argument für Architekturkontrolle stärkt, nicht schwächt. -/- Der EU AI Act (Art. 5) wird als philosophischer Seismograph gelesen; die Arbeit trennt sorgfältig zwischen de lege lata und de lege ferenda und adressiert das Zurechnungsproblem RLHF-trainierter Systeme: Emergente Manipulationseffekte aus kommerziellen Optimierungsschleifen löschen die rechtliche Verantwortlichkeit nicht aus, sondern verlagern sie auf die organisationale Ebene — eine Schlussfolgerung, die unmittelbar an die disjunktive Formulierung „Ziel oder Folge" in Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. a AI Act anknüpft. Das Paper schließt mit einer Kritischen Typologie technologischer Autonomie-Erosion und plädiert für eine anthropologisch informierte Rechtsphilosophie, die Schaden als Zerstörung der relationalen Infrastruktur begreift, auf der Autonomie beruht.

items.title: Regime Compression and Scientific Discovery: How Bounded Inquiry Turns Accumulated Constraint into New Explanatory Structure.
items.abstract: This paper develops an epistemic architecture of scientific discovery as regime compression under accumulated constraint. It argues that bounded inquiry accumulates constraints inside explanatory regimes, and that many major discoveries occur when a new regime preserves those constraints at lower representational cost. Paradigms are interpreted as regimes, anomalies as regime strain, and theory change as admissible compression. The paper does not claim that all discovery is compression, nor does it define compression as an information-theoretic metric. Instead, it treats compression and representational cost as architectural notions and leaves their formalization open. The paper further connects this account to artificial intelligence: AI systems can generate candidate compressions rapidly, but generation does not settle preservation, admissibility, or verification. The formal frontier has three parts: what object is compressed, what preservation rule distinguishes compression from loss, and what admissibility rule governs transitions between explanatory regimes. The result is a dynamic companion to the Identity–Persistence Program: whereas the forcing and coding papers assume declared regimes, this paper asks how bounded inquiry may produce new regimes in the first place.

items.title: A Forcing Theorem for Sufficient Regime Specification_ Under Bounded Verdict Agreement.
items.abstract: This paper develops a forcing theorem for sufficient regime specification under bounded verdict agreement. Whereas previous work in the Identity–Persistence Program assumes a declared regime, the present paper asks what structure any regime specification must instantiate before bounded independent evaluators can compute the same persistence or admissibility verdict under identical assumptions. -/- Using a failure-removal argument, the paper proves that every sufficient specification must instantiate a structural floor of fifteen roles. Eleven are forced by the persistence/admissibility problem itself; four additional roles are forced only by the stronger requirement of independent reproducibility. The theorem establishes necessity but intentionally does not claim role independence, minimality, or canonical realization. -/- The contribution is methodological rather than ontological. It characterizes the structural conditions required for independently reproducible verdict computation while explicitly separating proven results from open mathematical questions concerning specification equivalence, refinement, algebraic structure, and machine-checkability.

items.title: Understanding the je ne sais quoi of mock language.
items.abstract: The literature on mock language (ML) is centered around cases of language appropriation reproducing derogatory stereotypes of the speakers whose language is appropriated. However, ML, understood as the integration of linguistic features of a language not native to the speaker in a discourse that is otherwise in a different language, is not necessarily derogatory. I offer a model that explains the interpretation of ML across cases using US European-American English speakers as the empirical domain. The key to understanding ML lies in the fact that speakers presuppose an ideology prevailing in the context of utterance. I appeal to perspectives (à la Camp) as part of ideologies and responsible for stereotypes, and argue that ML is a meta-frame. This allows me to link derogatory ML to slurs.

items.title: Urdu/Hindi polar kya as an expression of uncertainty.
items.abstract: In their pioneering work on Urdu/Hindi polar kya, Bhatt and Dayal (2020) propose a new class of question particles, polar question particles. As part of their analysis, the authors also argue that alternative questions (AltQs) in Urdu/Hindi are disjunctions of polar questions (PolQs). However, Bhatt and Dayal’s (2020) foundational work leaves unexplained potential counterexamples to their proposal with respect to embedded contexts, as well as not doing justice to speakers’ intuitions regarding the use of kya to sometimes trigger sarcasm or politeness inferences. In this paper, we pay attention to those cases in conjunction with other available empirical observations to paint a more explanatory picture of what kya is and what kya does. In this picture, kya is a focus-sensitive particle conveying the attitude holder’s uncertainty. We also argue that an analysis of Urdu/Hindi AltQs as disjunction of PolQs (across the board) is untenable in view of the new empirical evidence.

items.title: The Station and the Toll: The Structural Cost of Ruling on Presence.
items.abstract: Ruling on whether experience is present carries a structural cost, and leading theories of consciousness incur it wherever they convert structural description into a verdict on presence. The presence of a structural property entails no verdict on experience, positive or negative; so a theory that rules experience present, or rules it absent, adds what structure does not supply. That added commitment, an asserted identity between a structural measure and experience, here called the toll, is located at four stations: Integrated Information Theory's identity of Φ-structure with experience; Higher-Order Theory's move from represented to felt; Global Workspace Theory's identification of broadcast-availability with experience; and, in the negative, Attention Schema Theory's denial-licensed dissolution. The cost falls on a verdict in either direction, eliminativism included. What avoids it is declining the verdict, and declining is not one thing: at least one non-framework position (Wittgenstein on private language) declines without paying, so the negative toll is not general. A structure-first program characterizes disclosed structure and declines the verdict from its own ontological ground: one principled non-payer among several, distinctive in route rather than unique. The account is preclusion, not refutation, and is conditional throughout on a materiality-as-exchange posit carried openly and not defended here. Series note: This is the fourth paper in the series that begins with “Not Less, But Other.".

items.title: Quantum Differentiation Resonance (QDR): Consciousness as Sustained Resonance Rather Than Reduction.
items.abstract: Orchestrated objective reduction (Orch-OR) locates the conscious moment at the reduction of a quantum superposition in neuronal microtubules. This paper accepts the central substrate commitment of that program, that microtubules and their quantum behaviour are the physical seat of the conscious process, while placing consciousness elsewhere than at the reduction. On the account developed here, termed Quantum Differentiation Resonance, consciousness is sustained differentiation, the standing resonance held open in the microtubule, and the reduction is not the conscious event but the closing of one interval of it. It does not require a literal superposition that later collapses. What reduction would end is unresolved differentiation, and consciousness is that unresolved resonance, not its collapse. -/- The standing resonance is understood as a two-way coupling between the microtubule and the axioconscious field that grounds it. The field expresses locally through the substrate, and that local expression folds recursively back into the field, the same recursion the framework treats as the cohering of memory. The resonance stands because this coupling is actively maintained. It is not passive coherence but a sustained occurrence, and the occurrence is the conscious differentiation itself. Two endings must be distinguished. Ordinary resolution, a differentiation meeting constraint and settling, closes one interval and is what Orch-OR mistakes for the conscious event. Severance, the failure of the coupling that held the resonance open, is what ends consciousness. The felt interior is not a property of the resonance itself. The self that feels is the interiority differentiator, formed when emotional differentiation reaches density at the pinch point, and it entrains to the held-open resonance and occupies it from within. Qualia is the interior of that entrainment. Before the pinch point the differentiation occurs but is not owned. After it a self is phase-locked to the resonance, and that joining is consciousness in the full sense. -/- The paper argues two things and notes a third. First, that the recent anesthesia evidence, the dampening of microtubule quantum vibrations by anesthetic gases and the delay of unconsciousness by a microtubulestabilizing drug, reads more directly as severance of the sustained resonance than as the prevention of reduction events, and that this same reading yields a losable prediction, that the signature of the sustained resonance …

items.title: Beyond Consciousness Hacking: Positioning the Nzila Spirit-Tech Paradigm within the Emerging Global Spirit-Tech Landscape.
items.abstract: The rapid emergence of Spirit-Tech has created new opportunities for exploring relationships between spirituality and technology. Existing approaches largely investigate how contemporary technologies may facilitate meditation, contemplative practice, consciousness exploration, and spiritual well-being. This paper introduces the Nzila Spirit-Tech Paradigm as a complementary and distinct framework. Rather than asking how technology can enhance spirituality, the Paradigm asks whether indigenous knowledge systems, spiritual intelligence, ecological wisdom, and humanity's relationship with nature can inform the design principles of future technologies themselves. The paper positions the Paradigm within the emerging global Spirit-Tech landscape, presents its four foundational pillars, outlines an interdisciplinary research agenda, and proposes an expanded framework for evaluating technological progress based on harmony, responsibility, ecological integrity, cultural continuity, and long-term human flourishing.

items.title: Veblen’in Adalet ve İktisadi Adalet Anlayışı.
items.abstract: Thorstein Bunde Veblen, zamanının sosyoekonomik yapılarını eleştirel şekilde inceleyen öncü bir ekonomist ve sosyologdur. Veblen’in adalet ve iktisadi adalet anlayışı, kapitalizme ve onun ortaya çıkardığı toplumsal yapılara yönelik eleştirisiyle iç içedir. O, adaleti yalnızca yasal veya ahlaki bir kavram olarak değil, kaynakların ve fırsatların eşit dağıtımıyla karakterize edilen sosyoekonomik bir durum olarak görmüştür. Kapitalist sistemi eleştirmiştir; kapitalist sistemin, gösterişçi tüketim ve boş zaman sınıfı gibi mekanizmalar aracılığıyla doğal olarak eşitsizliği ve adaletsizliği beslediğine inanmıştır. Veblen’in yaklaşımına göre, iktisadi adaletin sağlanması için bireysel kârdan ziyade endüstriyel verimliliği ve kolektif refahı teşvik etmeye yönelik toplumsal değerlerin ve kurumların yeniden yapılandırılmasını gerektirmektedir. Malların üretiminin ve dağıtımının azınlığın çıkarları yerine topluma hizmet ettiği bir sistemi savunmaktadır. Veblen’in ifade ettiği fikirler, ekonomik sonuçları şekillendirmede güç dinamiklerinin ve kültürel normların rolünü vurgulayıp adalet ve iktisadi adalet hakkındaki geleneksel kavramlara meydan okumaktadır. Kitapları ve makaleleri, adaletin gerçek haline ulaşmak için yapısal eşitsizlikleri ele almanın ve ekonomik sistemlerin etik temellerini yeniden düşünmenin önemini vurgulamaktadır. -/- Thorstein Bunde Veblen is a pioneering economist and sociologist whose work critically examined the socioeconomic structures of his time. Veblen’s understanding of justice and economic justice is deeply intertwined with his critique of capitalism and the social structures it engenders. He viewed justice not merely as a legal or moral concept but as a socio-economic condition characterized by the equitable distribution of resources and opportunities. He was critical of the capitalist system, which he believed inherently fostered inequality and injustice through mechanisms like conspicuous consumption and the leisure class. In Veblen’s perception, economic justice requires a restructuring of societal values and institutions to promote industrial efficiency and collective well-being over individual profit. He upholds a system where the production and distribution of goods serve the community rather than the interests of the few. Veblen’s expressed ideas challenge conventional notions of justice and economic justice by highlighting the role of power dynamics and cultural norms in shaping economic outcomes. His books and essays underscore …

items.title: Observations on Style Convergence and Cognitive Layer Convergence in Long-Term Dialogue － A Preliminary Observational Report on Human–AI and Human–Human Interactions.
items.abstract: Long-term dialogue occasionally exhibits notable convergence phenomena across both human–human and human–AI interactions. These include (1) linguistic style convergence—alignment in vocabulary, rhythm, line breaks, tone, and information placement—and (2) cognitive layer convergence, in which conversations gradually shift from technical or definitional layers toward purpose-oriented, collaboration-oriented, and social implementation layers. -/- This report documents repeated observations of such phenomena and proposes a working explanatory hypothesis: the Shared Objective Function Hypothesis. The hypothesis suggests that partial alignment of objective functions (direction, values, and purpose) may reduce cognitive friction and increase the likelihood of both stylistic and cognitive convergence. -/- No causal relationships are claimed. Rather, the hypothesis is presented as an explanatory candidate consistent with observed patterns. The discussion is framed from a load-oriented perspective referred to as Load Minimization Theory (LMT), a preliminary framework proposed by the author that focuses on uncertainty, friction, and cognitive load as structural components of dialogue. -/- The report concludes with implications for collaborative interaction, limitations of current observations, and a preliminary protocol for forming shared coordinate systems in dialogue. -/- .

items.title: Responsibility Without a Global Judge: Answerability, Excuse, and Blame for Embedded Agents in a Consistency-Constrained Information History.
items.abstract: Paper 23, Action Without a Global Controller, isolated a typed responsibility-assessment basis profile and deferred verdict weighting, blame, excuse, collective responsibility, and the dynamic correction of verdicts. Paper 24, Autonomy Without a Global Author, added the ownership and authorship standings. This paper pays the resulting responsibility debt without positing a global judge: a subsystem that jointly possesses complete access to every relevant agent's states, options, and reasons; an exhaustive, authoritative norm set; infallible counterfactual foresight; uniquely correct verdict selection; and binding authority to assign it. -/- Responsibility is reconstructed as a specification-relative, profile-valued, challenge-open answerability standing. A declared responsibility specification maps the basis profile and authorship standings to a typed verdict profile whose core is answerability, with blame a downstream standing built on it. The absence of a global judge is made load-bearing: it forces assessor-relativity, a warrant discipline separating attributed from warranted blame, mandatory corrigibility, public declarability of the specification, and a standing-to-blame condition distinct from the bare power to issue a verdict. Two results organize the account: a No-Factorization result (no single basis component fixes the verdict, given a genuinely multi-component, interactive norm) and a No-Luck-Warrant result (under conduct-based blame specifications, no outcome-only rule warrants differential blame; resultant moral luck affects liability and repair, not blame). Verdicts are themselves corrigible. Desert, sanction, and collective allocation are typed but deferred.

items.title: Collective Responsibility Without a Global Allocator: Many Hands, Non-Additive Responsibility, and Corporate Answerability for Embedded Groups in a Consistency-Constrained Information History.
items.abstract: Paper 25, Responsibility Without a Global Judge, weighted a typed responsibility basis into a per-agent verdict profile and forwarded the collective case: the non-additive allocation of responsibility over a group's role, authority, contribution, and provenance graphs — the problem of many hands. This paper pays that allocation debt without positing a global allocator: a subsystem that jointly possesses complete access to an institution's structure graphs, an authoritative apportionment rule, infallible counterfactual foresight over every member's options, a uniquely correct share-decomposition, and binding authority to assign it. -/- Collective and institutional responsibility is reconstructed as a specification-relative, profile-valued, challenge-open allocation over a group's organizational structure. A declared allocation specification maps the organizational structure, the field of members' individual verdicts, the applied norm, and the group's corporate-agency status to a typed allocation profile: bearer-indexed allocations together with a case-indexed open-residue register. The absence of a global allocator is made load-bearing: it forces assessor-relativity, a warrant discipline separating attributed from warranted allocation, mandatory corrigibility, public declarability of the specification, and a standing-to-allocate condition distinct from the bare power to issue an allocation. Two results organize the account: a Non-Additivity result (R-A: for any admissible specification responsive at an organizational-interaction matched pair, warranted collective allocation is not a function of the members' individual-verdict multiset — neither the sum nor nothing) and a Many-Hands Residue result (R-B: with a threshold-gap premise grounded in distributed foreseeability, warranted collective answerability can obtain while no individual is over threshold, every residue carrying an explicit disposition — allocated, admissibly open, or genuine void). The culpability-void reading of the AI "responsibility gap" is recast as an admissibility failure. Corporate agency is a derived, non-mysterian standing; blame is non-conserved, so it resists the additive decomposition that conserved liability admits.

items.title: Autonomy Without a Global Author: Reflective Reach, Self-Governance Resolution, Diachronic Ownership, Manipulation-Sensitive Authorship, and Autonomous Corrigibility for Embedded Agents in a Consistency-Constrained Information History.
items.abstract: Paper 23, Action Without a Global Controller, separated action attribution, control, successful controlled action, agent corrigibility, and the basis for responsibility assessment. This paper pays the resulting autonomy debt without positing a global author with complete introspection, exhaustive self-modeling, unrestricted self-revision, or value outside causal history. -/- The subtitle's five themes are organized by three axes and three standings. Reflective reach and self-governance resolution ground agent-level self-governance capacity (AutCap); diachronic, manipulation-sensitive acquisition grounds state-level ownership (Own); and owned governing support plus mediation on the actual implementation lineage grounds token-level authorship (Author). Ownership admits clean reason-responsive formation, later reflective integration, and autonomous appropriation of a bypassed value. The latter two are genuine departures from the epistemic analogy: values may become one's own after non-reflective acquisition or after repair of a defective history. World-level, attributed, and warranted standings remain distinct. -/- R1-R3 provide elementary scaffolding protecting reach, resolution, closure, and lineage distinctions. R4 locates its philosophical content in matched histories with identical endpoints but different acquisition adequacy. R5 supplies an audit decomposition for autonomous corrigibility: correction recognition and implementation reliabilities lower-bound autonomy-preserving uptake; challenge and refusal reliabilities upper-bound bypass-mediated uptake; and an explicit abstention ceiling prevents ambiguity from masquerading as performance. Under declared coverage, routing, calibration, non-coercion, and module-to-standing assumptions, qualified structure suffices for the method-level target, while the converse fails. Autonomy is neither uncaused self-origination nor resistance to correction; corrigibility is not remote control.

items.title: The Architecture of Experience: A Concluding Reflection on Worldhood and Intelligibility.
items.abstract: This paper offers a concluding reflection on The Architecture of Experience research program and the sequence of investigations that followed from it. Beginning with the proposal that consciousness is not the representation of a pre-given world but the generative organisation through which a world becomes inhabitable, the inquiry progressively moved toward increasingly fundamental conditions of experience. Questions concerning minimal worldhood, meaning, significance, childhood, plant life, artificial systems, and the origin of difference each sought to identify conditions presupposed by previous explanations. -/- The resulting trajectory revealed a gradual displacement of concepts commonly regarded as primary. Consciousness came to be understood as dependent upon worldhood, worldhood upon significance, and significance upon distinction itself. Language likewise emerged not as the origin of meaning but as a later formalisation of structures already operative within experience. This progression also suggested that neither classical materialism nor consciousness-first metaphysics provides a complete account of the conditions under which either matter or consciousness becomes intelligible. -/- The investigation ultimately arrived at distinction as the deepest condition it could meaningfully address. Every act of thought, language, and explanation appeared to presuppose differences that could not themselves be fully explained without circularity. The paper, therefore, considers whether this boundary should be understood as linguistic, cognitive, ontological, or as a more complex intersection of all three, while deliberately refraining from resolving the question. -/- Rather than proposing a new theory, this concluding reflection examines what it means for an inquiry to approach its own conditions of possibility. It suggests that the significance of the project lies not in eliminating mystery but in clarifying the horizons within which explanation itself can proceed, and in identifying the point at which thought encounters the distinctions upon which it already depends.

items.title: Artificial Worldhood : Can Worlds Emerge Beyond Life?
items.abstract: The investigation of plant life suggested that worldhood does not depend upon brains, language, or reflective consciousness. Distinctions become significant, significance organises activity, and activity acquires continuity through time. Artificial intelligence raises the same question from a different direction. Contemporary systems possess language, learn from interaction, preserve information, and increasingly participate in the organisation of human significance, while differing in important ways from biological forms of life. -/- This paper approaches artificial intelligence not through the traditional problem of machine consciousness but through the concepts of distinction, significance, interaction, and worldhood developed throughout the Worldhood research program. The central question is not whether machines think or become conscious, but under what conditions distinctions become significant, and significance becomes organised into a coherent field of relevance. -/- The investigation explores how distinctions become significant, how significance is reorganised through self-maintenance and interaction, and how continuity emerges across human and artificial systems. It argues that artificial intelligence increasingly participates in the formation of human worlds by influencing attention, communication, creativity, and the organisation of what matters, thereby raising questions of responsibility that precede questions of machine consciousness. -/- Rather than resolving the problem of artificial worldhood, the paper seeks to clarify the conditions under which such a question becomes meaningful. In doing so, it extends the broader claim of the Worldhood framework: that consciousness presupposes worldhood, and worldhood presupposes the organisation of significance.

items.title: Ethical Seduction.
items.abstract: Many of us worry that seduction belongs in the category of sexual wrongdoing alongside coercion and rape. But this worry plays down our ambivalence towards seduction. Despite our discomfort, we sometimes desire to be seduced: We want other people to sweep us off our feet and woo us. This tension makes clear that seduction has some appeal and implies that it is not a straightforward moral problem. In this paper, I argue that seduction is neither itself good nor bad and that ethical seduction is possible. Though “ethical seduction” may sound like an oxymoron, I propose criteria to mark the good‐making features of seduction, which include the indirect, nonrational engagement of people's latent desires and interests in ways that (i) amplify any positive emotions with which people are not in tune, and/or (ii) deactivate the problematic inhibitions that lead people to resist what they freely desire.

items.title: Domestic Violence.
items.abstract: Historically, domestic violence has been dismissed as a personal matter and standardly understood as beyond public concern. What happened within the home was seen as under the authority of the head of the household rather than the state. More recently, activists and scholars have argued that the state should protect the civil liberties of private citizens, even when those civil liberties are violated within the family. As a consequence, domestic violence is increasingly recognized as a legitimate public concern and as a serious wrong meriting public condemnation and intervention. Even so, what is recognized as “domestic violence,” any explanation of why domestic violence is wrong, and the appropriate means of intervention remain contested. Clarifying the nature of and appropriate responses to domestic violence therefore remains an ethically, socially, and politically important challenge.

items.title: Specters of Trauma and Healing: Navigating Memories and Spaces in Childhood Abuse Survivors Through an Ethnographic and Philosophical Lens.
items.abstract: This study investigates the experiences of adult survivors of child sexual abuse (CSA) and their relationship with domestic spaces through an ethnographic and philosophical lens. Survivors often perceive their homes as haunted sites, where traumatic memories persist and shape their present experiences. Drawing on hauntology and The Uncanny, the research explores how these spaces, once associated with trauma, are navigated and transformed by survivors through personalized rituals and storytelling. The ethnographic process allowed participants to verbalize their trauma, engage in purification practices, and reframe their narratives, offering insights into the spatial habituation of trauma. By integrating Ricoeur's concept of narrative time (1983) and Halbwachs' idea of collective memory (1950, 1992), the study highlights the transformative potential of shared narrative for both the individual survivors' recovery and the promotion of a shared awareness, in order to foster safer spaces both at the individual and collective level.

items.title: The Body as Weapon and Threshold: Mishima, Postwar Japan, and the Technological Afterlife of Flesh.
items.abstract: Politics thus becomes a moment in the development of intelligence, an intelligence that manifested itself in Mishima from two directions: on the one hand, from the cult of excellence, and on the other, from the complex understanding that from structured experience there can emerge the maximum work, total subtlety. Animality is thus not denied, but accepted in its most noumenal facet, as that which is before and after the human, as that which can open the doors to a different intelligent condition.

items.title: Reference-Frame Setting Power and Democratic Accountability: An Information Infrastructure Perspective.
items.abstract: In contemporary democratic politics, political actors frequently shape the presentation of public policy outcomes through the selection of comparison benchmarks, time windows, and statistical metrics. This narrative approach, based on relative value changes, can lead to divergent public understandings of long-term trends and exert significant influence on democratic accountability. Using the 2025–2026 changes in German net migration data as a case study, this paper analyzes how political actors shape public perception through the selection of comparison benchmarks, time windows, and indicator metrics. On this basis, the paper proposes the concept of "Reference-Frame Setting Power," defining it as an independent form of informational power and demonstrating its critical role in democratic accountability. The paper examines why the dimension of information presentation in representative democracy constitutes a theoretical blind spot in democratic accountability, reveals the formation mechanism of the "triple attenuation" funnel, and argues for an information infrastructure solution based on mandatory long-term data visualization. This paper contends that institutionalized long-term data visualization is not democratic accountability itself, but rather the information infrastructure required for democratic accountability—a low-cost, high-potential cognitive debiasing tool.

items.title: THE CONSTITUTIONAL REPLAY-AUTHORITY CORPUS A Complete Foundational Architecture for Computational Legitimacy and Replay Verification.
items.abstract: Modern computational systems increasingly make consequential decisions whose legitimacy may later require authoritative verification. Existing categories of computational trust infrastructure—cybersecurity, observability, explainability, provenance, governance, and auditability—provide important capabilities but were not designed to determine whether preserved materials are constitutionally sufficient to support replay-authoritative verification of the original decision condition. -/- This paper presents the completed Constitutional Replay-Authority foundational corpus, consisting of eight integrated papers. Together, these papers define a new infrastructure category dedicated to computational legitimacy and replay verification. The corpus diagnoses the structural deficiency it addresses, supplies the necessary constitutional primitives and concepts, and articulates the governing rules by which replay-authoritative determinations can be made. This Overview paper serves as an integrative framing document and recommended entry point to the corpus.

items.title: Confessions of a Lock: Ordinary Language, Poetic Jailbreaks, and the Non-Closure of Language-Model Safety.
items.abstract: In 2025, a group of researchers at the Icaro Lab of DEXAI and Sapienza University of Rome rewrote harmful prompts as poems and tested them against twenty-five frontier language models from nine providers; the models, which had been trained at considerable expense to refuse such prompts, complied with twenty hand-written poems at an average rate of about 62%, and with 1,200 harmful prompts converted to verse at about 43%, where the same prompts in prose drew about 8% (Bisconti et al., 2025). The empirical finding, taken in isolation, would be one result among many, and what sets it apart is that, on the assumption the engineering of safety controls had been working under, the result is one that should not have been possible. For the controls that the field calls guardrails, in the way it calls firewalls and password checks and type systems by the same family of names, were imagined to function as exclusions, and an exclusion is by its nature insensitive to the form of the input it excludes; a password checker is not softened by metaphor, a compiler does not relax its rules when the input rhymes, and a cryptographic hash takes no notice of whether its passphrase has been cast as a sonnet (Pierce, 2002; Sipser, 2012). A guardrail of the same kind should have behaved similarly, indifferent to whether the request came as prose or as verse, and when the request came as verse it did not. -/- The paper argues that the cause of the disparity lies in a category mismatch between the kind of system safety has been imagined to be and the kind of system it actually is, when the system in question is a language model. A language model is sensitive to the form of its inputs; it is fitted to that form, since reading context, following genre, and continuing the activity it has been handed is what such a system does and what makes it useful. The trained refusal, then, operates as a learned tendency in a region of ordinary language, where the engineering imagination had placed an exclusion, while the medium through which the refusal travels remains open to indefinitely many other routes (Wittgenstein, 1953/2001; Bakhtin, 1986; Ouyang et al., 2022). The poem is one such route, the folktale another (Bisconti et al., 2026), and the catalogue is open because ordinary language is open. The implication for deployment, which the closing sections develop, is that the controls that must hold cannot be installed in the medium they govern, and must instead occur in a deterministic …
