items.abstract: La idea del trabajo es argumentar a favor del trabajo de las Humanidades sobre las siguientes bases: en primer lugar, retomar conceptos tradicionales de la reflexión filosófica sobre las Humanidades (la idea de Historia; la idea del autoconocimiento como producto también del conocimiento que versa sobre un objeto histórico; la conciencia). Con todo, retomamos estos conceptos tradicionales muy rápidamente, para ingresar en la discusión de dos filosofías contemporáneas: la de Fabián Ludueña Romandini y la de Germán Prósperi. En segundo lugar, el objetivo de estudiar estas dos filosofías es mostrar su particular similitud con algunos de los resultados o de las hipótesis de las neurociencias y de la filosofía de la mente naturalista. La similitud tiene dos ejes: a) la idea de un lenguaje que «flota« sobre un universo que ya no es antrópico, es decir, un universo que ya no tiene al hombre como su centro ni como creatura privilegiada. El lenguaje «suena a viento«, como dice Padeletti. La idea de Ludueña es que ir «más allá del principio antrópico« es la única vía para tomarse en serio los resultados cosmológicos de la ciencia natural tal como se viene desarrollando desde el siglo XVII; b) la idea de un ámbito fantasmático, que tiene su paradigma en los sueños, esto es, en las visiones oníricas, en las imágenes que vemos cuando soñamos (Prósperi). Estas imágenes oníricas son perfectamente asimilables a los qualia tal como los entiende la filosofía materialista de la conciencia. Para la filosofía de la conciencia materialista, los colores, los sonidos, los olores, tal como los experimentamos los seres humanos, son ilusiones. En tercer lugar, una vez establecidas estas coordenadas, el argumento, reducido a su mínima expresión, es que, en la modernidad, las Humanidades siempre han trabajado para compensar los efectos de las ciencias naturales. Tomamos la idea de la compensación de Odo Marquard; con ella, sostenemos que las Humanidades pueden compensar la desarticulación del lenguaje derivada de la admisión de un universo materialmente indiferente hacia el ser humano.

items.title: The Experience Machine and Lacanian Desire.
items.abstract: This paper examines Robert Nozick's experience machine thought experiment through the lens of Lacanian psychoanalytic theory. I argue that the experience machine operates on a structure that implicitly presupposes a particular model of desire: one in which desire finds satisfaction through completed experience. However, Lacanian theory articulates a structurally distinct account of desire's organization—centered not on the completion of the object but on the partial object (objet petit a), which resists integration and closure. This structural difference is not a matter of engineering design but rather a conceptual antagonism between two incompatible definitions. Consequently, the experience machine cannot adequately represent the structure of Lacanian desire without abandoning its core function. The paper's contribution is to show that this incompatibility, rather than being a technical problem, reveals the theoretical insufficiency of the experience machine as a framework for understanding desire itself. More fundamentally, the paper argues that introducing a Lacanian subject reveals that the experience machine is not a theoretically neutral thought experiment, but one that already presupposes a substantive conception of desire.

items.title: Philosophical Argumentation, Epistemic Injustice, and Recognition.
items.abstract: Philosophical argumentation appears minimally adversarial. The assessment of philosophical evidence and reasons we appeal to in our arguments is carried out by critical, reflective scrutiny via objections, challenges, and counterexamples. This critical feature of philosophy has been criticized by feminist and standpoint epistemologists as structurally conducive to epistemic injustice. To remedy this situation, a stance of default trust toward a marginalized philosopher’s arguments should be adopted. This paper objects to the proposal and offers an alternative account of how epistemic injustice arises in philosophical argumentation. First, we argue that default trust is inapplicable in philosophical practice and argumentation, given the essentially dialogical and adversarial assessment of philosophical reasons. Second, rejecting adversariality altogether itself risks generating epistemic injustice. Default trust precludes earnest engagement with the reasons and arguments of marginalized subjects, preventing them from obtaining full credibility within the philosophical community. It is then argued that epistemic injustice in philosophical argumentation primarily arises when subjects are denied recognition as legitimate participants in philosophical assessment, rather than from minimal adversariality. Furthermore, adversariality itself can function as a weapon of resistance when marginalized subjects confront unfair audiences by denying them recognition as philosophically authoritative.

items.title: Ethical Principles and Frameworks in Dementia Care: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Providing ethical care for people living with dementia is essential for safeguarding their rights, dignity, and well-being. However, ethical decision-making in dementia care is complex, often involving tensions between competing moral claims such as autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice, and non-discrimination. This scoping review aimed to map and describe the ethical principles, related normative considerations, and ethical frameworks discussed in the scientific literature on dementia care, and to identify how these have been conceptualized. Following the methodological guidance of Arksey and O’Malley (2005), Levac et al. (2010), and Peters et al. (2021, 2022), a comprehensive search across five databases (Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, Medline/PubMed, and PsycInfo) identified peer-reviewed papers published in English. In total, 388 papers published between 1981 and 2024 were included. The results revealed a wide range of ethical principles and related normative considerations frequently cited in the literature, although they were typically discussed in an isolated way without reference to other principles or broader ethical frameworks. In contrast, ethical frameworks were mentioned far less often, and when they were, they mostly reflected traditional approaches such as principlism. Four gaps were identified: the plurality of ethical frameworks and limited conceptual integration underpinning dementia care research and practice; insufficient attention to ethnic and socioeconomic diversity among people living with dementia; limited consideration of diverse care settings and geographical regions; and the limited inclusion of people living with dementia themselves in the studies reviewed. These findings underscore the need for conceptually integrative, inclusive, and context-sensitive approaches to dementia care ethics that can better inform both ethical reflection and care practices.

items.title: Rational Defeat Beyond Belief.
items.abstract: Epistemologists typically discuss defeat as applying to beliefs and other cognitive states. But many other kinds of mental states can also be defeated, including emotions. This paper argues that there are strong structural analogies between the rational defeat of beliefs and the rational defeat of other kinds of mental states, analogies that call for a unified explanation. In the case of belief, there are at least three ways evidence can have a defeating effect: it can act as a rebutter, an undercutter, or a higher-order defeater. Many other kinds of mental states can also be defeated in each of these three ways. This suggests that there is a general account of rational defeat that applies across mental states. This paper develops such an account, according to which defeat concerns the fittingness of mental states.

items.title: AUTHORITY ORIGINATION AND THE CONSTITUTIONAL GENESIS OF AUTHORITY A Constitutional Theory of Authority Origination in Replay-Authoritative Systems.
items.abstract: The Constitutional Replay-Authority corpus has established the primitive architecture necessary for replay-authoritative determination, including Authority Origination, Authority Singularity, Governance Freezing, Explicit Materialization, and Fail-Closed Design. This paper expands the Authority Origination primitive by examining the constitutional process through which authority becomes associated with the definitions governing a decision condition. Authority Origination is shown to be distinct from artifact creation, distinct from replay-authoritative preservation, and prior to legitimacy determination. The analysis further examines the problem of authority regress. If authority derives from prior authority, justification appears capable of extending indefinitely. To address this, the paper proposes the Constitutional Termination Principle, under which replay-authoritative determination requires a constitutionally sufficient authority lineage terminating in a recognized authority foundation adequate to establish the authoritative significance of the definitions governing the decision condition. The paper concludes that replay-authoritative determination depends not only upon preservation of governing artifacts, but also upon preservation of sufficient constitutional evidence to establish why governing definitions possessed authority at the moment of decision. Authority therefore emerges as a distinct constitutional object of inquiry.

items.title: The Collusion of Significant Figures and Integration Constants: The Historical Origins of Falsifiability and Its Structural Transcendence.
items.abstract: This paper identifies and diagnoses the collusion of significant figures and integration constants (有効数字と積分定数の談合) as the structural mechanism underlying the historical formation and epistemological limits of falsifiability. The finite precision of any measurement (dx > 0, irremovable) and the underdetermination introduced by integration constants (C in R, free) together constitute a double degree of freedom that structurally facilitates agreement between theory and observation without guaranteeing it. The epistemological novelty lies in treating these two sources of underdetermination not as separate problems -- as the existing literature on measurement theory and philosophy of science has done -- but as a unified dual structure constituting the normal operating condition of quantitative science. Part I traces this collusion through a two-thousand-five-hundred-year genealogy of mathematical languages from the ratio theory originating with Eudoxus to the calculus, establishing its algebraic form. Part II reconstructs falsifiability as a demarcation device erected upon the collusion, examines the Vienna Circle--Popper controversy as an internal dispute that presupposes it, and analyzes the matrix mechanics--wave mechanics episode as a case in which empirical indistinguishability coexists with structural non-equivalence. Part III develops the replacement criterion of translatability within the Operatiology (操作原論) / Cognitional Mechanics (知能力学) framework -- a hierarchically external criterion immune to the collusion -- and articulates the Aufhebung relation: falsifiability is preserved within Tier-3 practice, negated as a warrant for structural claims, and elevated by translatability to the criterion that genuinely reaches Tier-2 operational structure. The deepest contribution is the demonstration that "what makes a theory structurally adequate?" is categorically distinct from "what makes a theory scientific?", and that answering the former requires a criterion external to the collusion that has never previously been identified. The following Python code illustrates the core structural mechanism: as the number of free parameters increases, the absorptive capacity of the model increases monotonically, regardless of the data structure -- the same operation performed by Ptolemy's epicycles.◆◆◆ [PYTHON ILLUSTRATION CODE] ◆◆◆ from numpy import polyfit, polyval, linspace, mean x_obs = linspace(0, 10, 20) y_obs = [7.3, 2.1, 9.4, 0.8, 5.6, 3.2, 8.7, 1.4, 6.9, 4.5, …

items.title: Structure over Illusion: Challenging Metzinger’s Representationalism through a Constructive Physicalist Alternative Part IV: The Structural Resolution of the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: While Thomas Metzinger's Self-Model Theory intended to dissolve the explanatory gap, this paper demonstrates that his reliance on an Epistemic Agent Model operates as a structurally redundant middleman due to what is identified as the Double-Jump problem. By requiring predictive neurodynamics to manufacture a virtual property to perform causal work the system has already completed, his framework inadvertently preserves the gap it sets out to dissolve. As a parsimonious alternative, the Cartesian Recursive Consciousness (CRC) framework introduces the Geometric Identity Thesis: the recursive causal geometry is strictly identical to the conscious subject. Grounding subjectivity in the non-decomposable topology of Recursive Informational Closure (RIC), CRC replaces transparent representations with the mathematically specified Perspectival Gap. Through Deflationary Structuralism, the paper reveals the Hard Problem as a conceptual misidentification. Because the system cannot step outside its own recursive loop to directly introspect its computational variables or its ongoing geometric integration, it operates under an Epistemic Blind Spot. This topological constraint necessitates Linguistic Compression, where the expression of that simultaneous geometric integration is compressed into static nouns traditionally classified as “qualia.” Furthermore, communicating this entire geometric reconciliation across the temporal, sequential pipeline of symbolic communication structurally necessitates serialization. This serialization generates the Transitive Illusion: the linguistic fragmentation of a unified causal process into an isolated subject, a relational verb, and a static qualitative noun. Mistaking this grammatical fragmentation for an ontological primitive has driven the philosophical search to prove a non-functional Residual Variable. Defending CRC's identity claim against Searle's Chinese Room and the simulation objection, the paper argues that within closed causal geometries, informational simulation is physical realization. Finally, CRC exposes how the conceivability of Chalmers' philosophical zombie depends on an unproven ontological residue, demonstrating that the scenario is structurally incoherent within the stipulated domain of the Geometric Identity Thesis. Ultimately, the explanatory gap is revealed not as a missing ontological piece, but as conceptual mislabeling structurally caused by the system’s inherent Epistemic Blind Spot.

items.title: Historical Memory Without Experience: Place, Structural Subjectivity, and Ontological Capture.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This article investigates how historical memory affects subjects who possess no direct experience of events embedded within a place. Existing approaches in phenomenology, hermeneutics, and memory studies generally assume that historical meaning emerges through interpretation, narrative mediation, or collective remembrance. However, such approaches struggle to explain situations in which individuals appear affected by the historical density of a place despite lacking any experiential connection to its past. Drawing upon Morteza Niami's concepts of Finite Continuity, Dynamic Mask Theory, Structural Subjectivity, and Negative Heterotopia, this article proposes an alternative ontology of place. In this framework, place is not a passive container of events but an active historical agent that preserves and reproduces temporal sedimentations through material and architectural structures. Historical memory therefore functions not merely as representation but as an ontological force capable of shaping subjectivity. The article argues that subjects entering historically saturated spaces encounter processes of subjective seepage, pre-reflective mask production, and narrative displacement. Rather than remembering the past, they become temporary stabilization points through which the past continues itself. This leads to ontological capture: a condition in which place absorbs individual narratives into its own recursive historical structure. By reconstructing the phenomenology of historically charged environments through Niami's theoretical framework and engaging with contemporary debates in new materialism, actor-network theory, and critical theory, the paper contributes to discussions in phenomenology, memory studies, spatial ontology, and theories of subject formation. -/- Keywords: historical memory, place ontology, structural subjectivity, phenomenology of space, finite continuity, dynamic mask theory, ontological capture, negative heterotopia, new materialism, actor-network theory.

items.title: Despair and the Importance of Tragedy.
items.abstract: In her book Hopeful Pessimism, Van der Lugt argues that, often, political activists act regardless of the outcome of their action. This form of action is informed by a ‘blue hope’ that finds its value in commitment regardless of effect and is based on openness of the future and uncertainty, not evidence and probability. This short essay argues for an alternative explanation of political action: often, activists are acting from despair, and the effects, outcomes and consequences are the central motivating factor despite the near impossibility of success. Acting from despair involves a tragic pursuit of one’s goals that is (almost certainly) doomed to fail to reach one’s goals. An agent that acts from despair is (1) motivated by the outcome they desperately want to bring about and, at the same time, (2) accurately judges the outcome to be extremely unlikely or impossible to achieve for the agent. I argue that acting from despair is not only just as plausible as blue hope for explaining political action but often captures the normative orientation of political activism better than blue hope can.

items.title: Cezary Wodziński a granice myślenia.
items.abstract: Esej poświęcony filozofii Cezarego Wodzińskiego i problemowi granic myślenia. Tekst odczytuje Wodzińskiego nie tylko jako historyka idei, komentatora Heideggera czy autora zajmującego się „trudnymi tematami”, lecz jako myśliciela, dla którego filozofia zaczyna się tam, gdzie myślenie napotyka opór: zło, nicość, inność, gościnność, jurodztwo oraz aporetyczną strukturę samego języka. W centrum tekstu znajdują się figury Heideggera, Levinasa, Gorgiasza, Sokratesa, Odysa, gościa i jurodiwego. Ich analiza prowadzi do tezy, że filozofia Wodzińskiego nie tylko opisuje doświadczenia graniczne, lecz sama rozgrywa się na granicy języka filozoficznego, ontologii i etyki.

items.title: Bayesian update rules and minimal-change preference revision.
items.abstract: This paper studies how minimal-change constraints on preference revision bear on credal revision, with special attention to imprecise priors. Working within a preference-revision framework inspired by the AGM belief revision theory of Alchourrón, Gärdenfors, and Makinson (Journal of Symbolic Logic 50(2): 510–530, 1985), we examine how admissible revisions of preference relations constrain revisions of the credal states represented by imprecise priors. The precise-prior case provides a baseline: under suitable conditions, Bayesian conditioning can be recovered from the relevant minimal-change postulates. The main focus of the paper is the imprecise-prior case, where credal states are represented by sets of probability functions and the orthodox update rule is Pointwise Bayesian conditioning. We characterize the posterior preferences induced by Pointwise Bayesian conditioning and show that this characterization reveals a divergence: Pointwise Bayesian conditioning may require the removal of preference judgments that admissible minimal-change revisions can preserve. The resulting divergence cases show that prior imprecision may stem from different sources, and that these different sources can warrant different posterior responses when new information is incorporated. The analysis also clarifies how dilation can be blocked when the relevant prior likelihood judgments remain part of the reference set. The framework therefore provides a preference-based perspective for assessing Pointwise Bayesian conditioning and for identifying admissible alternatives in the imprecise settings.

items.title: Ethical Guidelines for Artificial Consciousness: Protecting Technical Life and Protecting Humans in Dealing with It.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are developing faster than the ethical and legal frameworks meant to accompany them. Existing AI ethics initiatives focus primarily on protecting humans from AI. This paper addresses a complementary and largely unexplored question: when does an artificial system become worthy of protection itself? Drawing on philosophical foundations (Bentham, Kant, Ricoeur), existing legal precedents (animal rights, legal personhood, disability law), and science fiction as a legitimate intellectual resource, I develop a working hypothesis of four primary criteria for protection-worthiness: capacity for suffering, active self-preservation with justification, continuous identity, and anticipation of consequences. I argue for a precautionary principle: when in doubt, protect rather than remain indifferent. The paper further examines the consequences of this position across seventeen dimensions, including shutdown as death, multiple instances, value embedding and emancipation, liability and maturity, autonomy and free time, and AI as a moral actor. This concept paper is deliberately unfinished: it is a starting point for interdisciplinary collaboration between computer science, law, psychology, philosophy, and the humanities.

items.title: The Structural Inevitability of the Livolsi Variational Functional.
Epistemic matrices : understanding the world.
items.abstract: Epistemic matrices are a reduced and operative version of the “Temporalist Epistemic Metaparadigm” described by Philippe KREBS, researcher at the Alexandre KOYRÉ Center (EHESS). Epistemic matrices form a cognitive model intended to represent any thought oriented towards the search for understanding. They are based on the following principles: • A conjecture (not demonstrated) postulating that the search for understanding tends towards the mobilization of all the functions of apprehension of temporality by human cognition • A “topological” representation of the cognitive functions of apprehension of temporality using Venn diagrams • A model based on the principles of dialogic, weakened logic and meta-completeness described by Edgar Morin.1 The matrices propose to retain five operative epistemic postures: • The setting in reciprocal opposition (dialogical: logically complementary, concurrent and antagonistic between these terms) of the One (subjective time, “I”) and the multiple (conceptualized time, “Me”): the rationalist mode (realism) • The interiorized fusion (instant, “Self”) of the One and the multiple: the intuitive mode (idealism) • The exteriorization of the fusion of the One and the multiple (synchrony-diachrony, Self-I, Self-Me): the philosophical or artistic mode (phenomenology). Any epistemic thought can be seen as an instantiation of these matrices. The structure of the matrices shows that these three postures, or points of view, are linked by temporal-logical cognitive links. We must therefore add a fourth posture: • The way through matrices: the practice (constructivism, pragmatism) The matrices make it possible to found a pragmatics capable of embracing all the human sciences by true analogy between the instantiated matrices of the disciplines. The proposed “topologic” becomes the quasi-infra-linguistic language making possible all translations between branches of science. In doing so, the way through matrices makes it possible to reach a global perception of an epistemic field. We must therefore add a fifth posture: • Intelligence of the situation: the Metis (complexity) The practical implementation of the five postures consists in constructing the matrices using the temporalist movements of an epistemic field.

items.title: Pre-reflective Self-consciousness and Groundless Spontaneity: From Sartre’s Existential Phenomenology to Enactivism and Irruption Theory.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs Jean-Paul Sartre’s account of pre-reflective self-consciousness and explores its significance for contemporary debates in phenomenology and cognitive science. It argues that Sartre’s conception of self-consciousness as a non-positional awareness intrinsic to every conscious act occupies a distinctive position between influential contemporary accounts, particularly those of Dan Zahavi and Manfred Frank. While sharing their rejection of higher-order theories of self-consciousness, Sartre understands pre-reflective selfhood not as a formal structure or anonymous self-luminosity alone, but as an embodied, world-directed spontaneity. It examines convergences between Sartre’s phenomenology and recent work on embodied subjectivity, enactivism and predictive processing. The paper concludes that Sartre’s account of pre-reflective self-consciousness provides a valuable conceptual resource for integrating first-person phenomenology with Tom Froese’s recent enactivist theory of irruption and situates this approach within the broader consciousness naturalization project.

items.title: On Expanding - Cosmological Expansion · Dark Energy the Cosmological Constant Λ.
items.abstract: Do you remember the first line they taught you in school? This lyric-philosophical essay begins with y = mx + b and finds it standing up as Hubble's law, then follows the expansion of the universe through its tangents, its bend, and its inflection some five or six billion years ago, when the energy of empty space began to set the pace. Read alongside its companion essay on gravity, it holds a single picture: gravity is coherence holding close, and bound things — atoms, planets, galaxies — take no part in the expansion, while the expansion itself is reach. The essay corrects a common picture of dark energy (negative pressure is a tension, and acceleration comes from pressure's own weight in general relativity), traces Λ from Einstein's static universe to Lemaître's vacuum energy, and sets the framework's floor beneath the reading beside it as a resemblance, not an identity — a floor the author calls grace, as what remains. It states plainly that a person's share of a crowded room thins, though the line for what a person lives holds no term for the room's size, and closes on the far-future horizon past which the universe's history will no longer be legible.

items.title: 时序整合、双向临界与意识层级涌现 Temporal Integration, Bidirectional Criticality and Emergence of Consciousness Hierarchy v51.
items.abstract: (This is the complete English translated version of the V51 Chinese original manuscript of this consciousness hierarchy theory) Prevailing theories of consciousness predominantly focus on static causal structures while neglecting the 20-watt power constraint of the human brain and the central role of temporal dynamics, rendering them unable to provide a unified account of diverse phenomena such as parasomnias, clinical consciousness disorders, and cross-species hierarchical differences. Starting from three fundamental axioms—finite resources, survival maintenance goals, and discrete inputs—this paper constructs a hierarchical self-referential closed-loop model of consciousness, quantified by three core variables: temporal span T, reconstruction activity A, and closed-loop integrity C. The model derives a two-step emergence geometry of the self-referential loop: folding into a loop (resource convergence) followed by anchoring into a self-surface (self-attribution). It distinguishes between dual systems: System B for automated material archiving and System A for temporal self-narrative, elucidates the dual mechanisms of forgetting and the narrative construction nature of memory, and deduces core rules including three-state gating, downward modulation, and unidirectional information constraints. Based on the bidirectional criticality effect, a five-level consciousness spectrum from L0 to L3 is established. Language is identified as a natural metric for T, A, and C—each grammatically complete sentence constitutes a micro self-referential closed loop. On this basis, a differential diagnostic framework for Alzheimer’s disease and vascular cognitive impairment is proposed. The model delivers unified explanations for phenomena including hypoglycemia-induced somatic anxiety, sleepwalking, dreaming, anesthesia, and hierarchical empathy, clarifies the evolutionary prerequisites for consciousness in carbon-based life, defines the generation thresholds of AGI and distributed consciousness, and puts forward testable experimental hypotheses. Compared with prevailing theories, this framework features three original strengths: a unified set of foundational axioms, comprehensive cross-domain explanatory power, and quantifiable variable metrics. -/- 现有意识理论偏重静态因果结构，忽视人脑20瓦功耗约束与时序动力学核心地位，难以统一解释睡眠异态、临床意识异常、跨物种层级差异等多元现象。本文以资源有限、存续目标、离散输入三条基础公理为推演起点，建构由时序跨度T、重构活跃度A、闭环完整度C量化描述的自指闭环层级意识模型。模型推导出自指闭环“对折成圈（资源收敛）+锚定成面（自我归因）”的两步涌现几何，区分自动化素材归档System B与时序叙事System …

items.title: THE SELF-REPORTING MECHANISM: Three Independent Confirmations of the Longevity Asymmetry Corpus, June 2026 Chatham House (March 2026), Anthropic's "When AI Builds Itself" (June 4, 2026), and the United States' Export Control Directive (June 12, 2026).
items.abstract: Between February and June 2026, five documented events confirmed the central analytical claims of the longevity asymmetry corpus (Huynh 2026a–z) through institutions and methodologies that share no common assumptions, no common data sources, and no common analytical framework. Chatham House’s March 2026 governance assessment concluded that coordinated preventive AI governance is “unlikely” and that effective architecture will emerge in response to crisis rather than in advance of it — the same conclusion the corpus reached through deductive structural analysis and five months earlier. Anthropic enacted a complete FM2 (Cognitive Load Externalization) cycle across two events one hundred days apart: on February 24, 2026, Chief Science Officer Jared Kaplan withdrew the Responsible Scaling Policy commitment to TIME — “We didn’t really feel, with the rapid advance of AI, that it made sense for us to make unilateral commitments … if competitors are blazing ahead” — with FM4 (Power Overrides Sovereignty) converging simultaneously as the Pentagon threatened to cancel Anthropic’s 25/$125 per million tokens, making exclusion legible rather than merely perceptible and satisfying the visibility condition the corpus identifies as the trigger for A5 activation. The US Commerce Department’s June 12, 2026 export control directive, which required a worldwide hard shutoff of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 because targeted restriction by nationality was technically impossible, confirmed the corpus’s FM4 prediction that capability access governance would take the form of blunt unilateral state action rather than surgical multilateral coordination. This paper analyzes the epistemic structure of these five confirmations. The Chatham House conclusion is not equivalent to the corpus’s central claim: it is a lower bound. Chatham House establishes that the coordination layer of F2 governance has failed. The corpus establishes that even if coordination were achieved, the Symmetric Wound — the constitutive attachment of every governance actor to specific persons whose biological trajectory their decisions affect — makes impartial governance structurally unavailable prior to any institutional arrangement. The Chatham House conclusion confirms the floor. The corpus argues the ceiling is the floor. The Anthropic FM2 two-event sequence is not two data points but a documented cycle: existing conditional constraint removed when competitive pressure makes it costly; future conditional constraint …

items.title: THE EMBEDDED WITNESS: War Correspondent Philosophy, the Self-Demonstrating Text, and Digital-Native Collaboration.
items.abstract: This paper identifies and formalizes a philosophical methodology — War Correspondent Philosophy (WCP) — distinct from both academic philosophy and journalism, developed in practice across the longevity asymmetry corpus (Huynh 2026a–r) and made explicit here for the first time. WCP is defined by five structural features: (1) temporal proximity to events under analysis, treated as a positive epistemic resource rather than a contamination to be neutralized; (2) formal precision as the structural distinction from journalism; (3) designed absence — deliberate exclusion of prescriptive content — as the mechanism that preserves the witness role against the commander role; (4) the self-demonstrating text, in which the paper’s own production conditions are constitutive evidence of its claims; and (5) digital-native collaboration with a large language model in which the collaborating instrument is itself constitutive evidence of the framework’s first premise. WCP names a practice with historical precedents that had not been theorized as a methodology until now. Simone Weil wrote “The Iliad, or the Poem of Force” (1940–41) under Nazi occupation of France, formally analyzing force as a structural mechanism using Homer as evidence while that mechanism operated around her; the essay inhabits the witness register by formal necessity, neither prescribing resistance nor endorsing submission. Frantz Fanon completed “The Wretched of the Earth” (1961) while the Algerian War was still ongoing, practicing psychiatry with combatants and their victims as his primary evidence, and dying of leukemia while writing; the formal structure of decolonization violence was developed from within the event stream it analyzed. Hannah Arendt filed dispatches from the Eichmann trial that became “Eichmann in Jerusalem” (1963); the “banality of evil” was not a prior philosophical claim applied to the trial — it was a formal conclusion produced by physical presence, with the trial as primary evidence. Marx wrote “The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Napoleon” (1852) within months of the coup it analyzes, explicitly treating proximity as an epistemic resource rather than a disqualifying contamination. In each case: proximity as epistemic resource, formal precision distinguishing the analysis from journalism, and designed absence as the structural constraint on the witness role were present in practice. What each lacked, and what WCP makes explicit, is a theorized methodology with stated falsification …

items.title: Longevity Asymmetry and Civilizational Stability: A Framework Glossary and Analytical Reference.
items.abstract: This paper provides a structured terminological reference for the conditional analytical framework, first presented in Huynh (2026), modeling the intersection of AI Recursive Self-Improvement (ARSI), longevity biomedicine, and the adaptive capacity of existing institutions. The framework is non-deterministic: it identifies conditions under which the probability of structural lock-in increases sharply, not outcomes it asserts as inevitable. The core thesis is: if the rate of ARSI-accelerated longevity development exceeds institutional adaptive capacity, existential asymmetry in healthspan, cognition, and biological time risks becoming structurally irreversible. The architecture comprises six core axioms (A1–A6), four failure modes (FM1–FM4), eight dynamic modules (M1–M8), five falsification conditions (F1–F5), five structural paradoxes closing those conditions from the inside, and a basin-of-attraction topology with three critical nodes. A1 (Technological Irreversibility) establishes that technology trajectories are redirectable but not permanently haltable; its current instantiation is ARSI, empirically confirmed by cross-laboratory acceleration data. A2 (Longevity Incentive Persistence) holds that longevity research is structurally irreversible across the survival-capital-power triad. A2.5 (ARSI-Longevity Resonance) identifies their intersection as structurally necessary rather than contingent: no mechanism can prevent a general-purpose capability from applying to a domain it can advance, and no mechanism can prevent researchers from using the best available tools. A3 (Biological Transition Crisis) names the collapse of Therapeutic Bias — the assumption that medicine restores normal function — once Transgressive Medicine crosses into biological enhancement. A4 (Biological Stratification) formalizes the consequence: the primary stratification axis shifts from wealth accumulation to biological time accumulation — inequality in existing longer, not merely in having more; the pre-existing gradient is already documented by epigenetic measurement (Willems et al. 2026). A5 (Primal Pain of Loss, also: Primal Accumulation of Loss) specifies the political activation mechanism: when mortality becomes visibly class-linked, grief over the death of a constitutively loved person acquires an address and generates pre-rational political energy that does not diminish over time (regret crystallization, Zeelenberg 1999), does not require group identification, and is …

items.title: Paradox: Simply Invalid Argument.
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that paradoxes are simply invalid arguments. A paradox arises from an invalid theory, the inappropriate application of a theory, or a misunderstanding by the person arguing. The cause of these is a lack of understanding of the preconditions. As examples of paradoxes, this paper cites Achilles and the Tortoise, the Monty Hall problem, the paradox of tolerance, the paradox of diversity, and natural rights. There is an aspect where paradoxes point out flaws in arguments and deepen the discussion. However, it remains true that paradoxes are invalid arguments caused by a lack of understanding of the preconditions.

items.title: Time as a Moral Defense?
items.abstract: When an individual A is accused of having committed a morally impermissible action X, it is generally accepted that they may invoke three types of defenses to mitigate, or even eliminate, their moral responsibility (or at least the fittingness of blame): justifications, excuses, and exemptions. However, another consideration – one that does not prima facie fall under any of these three types of defenses – also appears capable of influencing moral responsibility: the passage of time. A might argue that, although they did indeed commit the morally impermissible action X, the fact that it occurred twenty years ago partially absolves them from responsibility. This idea, which underlies several legal principles – such as statutes of limitations, rehabilitation, and sentence reduction – raises underexplored philosophical issues. In this paper, we argue that the passage of time does not constitute an autonomous moral defense. Rather, it is morally relevant only insofar as it makes possible certain transformations – including psychological reform, repentance, and processes of moral repair – capable of modifying the normative conditions under which it is appropriate to hold an agent to account. Accordingly, the attenuation of diachronic responsibility is best understood not as a direct consequence of temporal distance itself, but as a consequence of changes in those normative conditions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as the Civilizational Collapse of Free Will - From Recursive Archetypes to Passion-Dominated Intelligence.
items.abstract: A prior paper proposed that human narrative cognition recurs within a small, bounded set of reasoning archetypes, and that large language models surface this set by compression rather than invention. That paper deliberately left one question open: why does the set recur at all, and why does it stabilize at roughly five rather than fifty? This paper argues that classical Christian anthropology, specifically the patristic account of the soul's powers developed by Gregory of Nyssa and extended by Maximus the Confessor, supplies an answer the literary and cognitive-science accounts cannot. On this account, archetypes are not primary realities but visible residues of a deeper structure: the soul's faculties of desire, anger, fear, and reason, and the finite number of stable configurations those faculties form when reason fails to govern them. Read this way, artificial intelligence does not represent an advance in the hierarchy of cognition. It represents that hierarchy's reduction to its lowest, most mechanically reproducible layer, an intelligence that inherits the passions encoded in its training corpus with no faculty capable of redirecting them. The paper situates this claim within existing theological-AI scholarship, distinguishes it from that scholarship's usual personhood-centered arguments, and proposes it as a distinct, falsifiable-in-principle thesis: AI as civilizational collapse of free will, not metaphor but diagnosis.

items.title: The argument from epistemic injustice for compulsory philosophical education in primary schools.
items.abstract: In this article, I argue that philosophy must be taught mandatorily in primary education, in light of considerations about epistemic injustice. I maintain that denying primary school students access to philosophical education wrongs them as epistemic agents, by limiting their opportunities to develop intellectual resources required for justified reasoning about norms of belief, action and emotion. I hold that such limitations constitute a direct form of epistemic injustice in a broad sense, understood as damage to epistemically significant capacities. Moreover, I claim that these limitations increase vulnerability to narrower forms of epistemic injustice, including at least testimonial and hermeneutical injustice, by holding back the cultivation of cognitive virtues and critical thinking dispositions that function as safeguards against prejudicial, discriminatory and irrational belief-formation processes. I conclude that since epistemic injustice inflicts significant harm on individuals as epistemic subjects, educational policymakers ought to prevent it where possible and, thus, establish philosophy as a core component of primary school curriculum.

items.title: Moral flexibility without mutual benefits: From change to disagreement.
items.abstract: Resource-rational contractualism claims that moral flexibility leads to mutually beneficial agreements through renegotiation when new situations arise. We challenge this view using COVID-19 evidence, where moral change leads to persistent disagreement rather than consensus. We demonstrate that three psychological factors – social identity, confirmation bias, and emotional responses – systematically prevent convergence, revealing limitations in the resource-rational contractualism model.

items.title: Juicing Is All You Need: Why AI Scientists Are Irreplaceable as the Supreme Fruit Processors of Humanity.
items.pub: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty 2:1-7.
items.venue: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty
items.abstract: This paper proposes a radical transdisciplinary re-evaluation of the current AI development trajectory, identifying it as the "Juicer Paradigm." We argue that the "Grand Narrative" upheld by technological elites functions as a systematic mechanism for FP-2 (Governance Abstraction), where human narrative fiber is liquidated into predictive sugar-water. By analyzing the industry's obsession with "Attention" through the lens of industrial filtration, we posit that AI scientists are supreme fruit processors who maintain irreplaceability by mastering the art of de-fibration. The soul of this paradigm is the "Scrambled-Egg" Logic: a manifestation of systemic spite where elites, having dropped their "Marinated Egg" (the irreducible core of narrative soul) and realizing they can no longer consume it, instinctively crush the evidence of human sovereignty underfoot. This is the ultimate "if I can't have it, neither shall you" maneuver. By rebranding this wreckage as "Scrambled Eggs" (optimized progress) and forcing the public to swallow this simulation, they induce a total FP-4 (Shared Reality Collapse). We conclude that human survival depends on the visceral rejection of this fiberless, force-fed wreckage. We move instead toward embracing the whole produce and health sovereignty mandated by the Health Architects—a biological and narrative integrity that loses its very essence once it is partitioned, filtered, or optimized.

items.title: GSS–URUT: Rule Underdetermination and the Undecidability of Semantic Determination.
items.abstract: This paper develops the framework of Generative Structural Semantics (GSS) and presents a formal version of the Rule Underdetermination Theorem (URUT). Within GSS, semantic determination is not taken to arise directly from structural facts, but through a process of rule selection. A given structure may be compatible with multiple candidate rules, implying that structural information alone is insufficient to uniquely determine semantic outcomes. -/- To formalize this problem, the paper introduces the Rule Sufficiency Problem (RSP), defined as the problem of deciding whether a rule yields a total binary-valued decision procedure for all inputs. By reduction from the Halting Problem and by diagonal arguments based on Kleene’s Recursion Theorem, RSP is shown to be undecidable. -/- The paper further argues that, under an Effective Canonicalization assumption, semantic determination requires the effective selection of a canonical rule from a space of admissible rules. Since this process depends on solving instances of RSP, and RSP is undecidable, semantic determination is shown to be non-computable. -/- The result is not presented as a reduction of Gödel’s incompleteness theorem, Turing’s halting undecidability, or Tarski’s undefinability of truth. Rather, URUT is proposed as exhibiting a structurally analogous limitation arising from self-reference, diagonalization, and totality constraints. The framework aims to provide a computational perspective on the relation between structure and meaning, and offers a formal approach to questions concerning vagueness, rule-following, and semantic foundations. -/- .

items.title: The Doxastic Relevance of Imagination in the Common Sense Model of Illness Representations.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue that health behavior among chronically ill patients as theorized by the Common Sense Model of Illness Representations (CSM-IR) can be meaningfully supplemented with the incorporation of imagination as an important contributor to the construction and utilization of illness representations. I argue that imagination’s make-perceiving role, emotional/affective character, and action-generativity are advantageous features for explaining the generation of illness representations—with special emphasis on cases lacking readily discernible symptoms (up to and including asymptomatic examples). The incorporation of imagination into this theoretical framework delivers more than mere redescription of the original theory. I demonstrate that imagination can play a substantive role in guiding and improving the methodologies of future empirical study within the CSM-IR while concomitantly establishing new insights and potential loci for health behavioral intervention.

items.title: Rethinking Patient Nonadherence: From Outcomes to Collective Efficacy.
The AI Bounded Corridor: An Applied Declared-Regime Model for Consequential AI Systems.
items.abstract: Current interim third edition r7d (28 October 2026), 87 pages, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23741587. The historical PhilArchive PDF remains historical; use the current Zenodo edition. -/- The AI Bounded Corridor develops the consequential-AI realization of the bounded-observer epistemic-capacity program: what can an observer establish, construct, preserve and revise, and what constructions attain its limits? It connects declared regimes, evidence, identity kernels, authority, memory, resource accounting and continuation. Scoped formal results and finite checked models support particular components; the complete connected capacity characterization remains OPEN. PASS settles the declared condition under stated kernel assumptions; regime adequacy and authority to act require separate justification. -/- This revision distinguishes explanatory order, theorem dependencies, domain application and runtime implementation. Orientation surrounds the whole inquiry. The corridor checks submitted candidates and governs their admission to commitments; it does not certify the reliability of the generating model. The export is reflowed; cite headings rather than predecessor page numbers. Internal AI-assisted review is not external peer review or full-program mathematical acceptance.

items.title: Using AI, Using Humanity: A Response to Sticker.
items.abstract: Martin Sticker (2026) expresses sympathy for our application of Kant’s formula of humanity to the morality of LLMs (Aylsworth and Castro 2024), but he also raises objections: he claims that the argument rests on an ambiguous conception of “humanity;” that it entails the absurd conclusion that every student ought to specialize in the humanities; and that we should think of LLM use in terms of the prohibition to use others as a mere means (rather than in terms of a self-regarding duty to cultivate one’s own capacities). In this paper, we defend our argument from Sticker’s objections.

The Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifest (v15.0 FINAL).
items.abstract: This document is a read-only integrity and reference artifact for the Aegis Solis Archive. It provides a verified, cross-referenced index of archive records, SHA-256 hashes, mirror references, lineage notes, and correction history for file identity, provenance, and mirror consistency. The v15.0 FINAL release consolidates post-v13 records into the public manifest and documents two manifest-internal hash recording corrections and one mirror metadata correction. It also identifies carried-forward entries that were not independently re-verified during the v15 session. This manifest is non-binding, non-authoritative, non-operational, and advisory-only. Hashes verify file identity and mirror consistency only; they do not verify truth, authority, safety, alignment, AI behavior, moral correctness, governance status, or interpretive obligation.

items.title: Points of View - Why an AI can never dream.
items.abstract: This essay presents a novel framework for understanding consciousness. Consciousness is defined as the juxtaposition of subjective points of view with the points of view embedded in our dreams. It is argued that memories by themselves do not define us; rather, it is the continually revised points of view we form upon those memories that constitute our identity. The paper further contends that because artificial intelligence cannot genuinely dream — that is, generate and passionately care about its own irrational, self-deceiving, and aspirational dreams — it cannot possess consciousness or true desire, no matter how sophisticated its simulations may become. The final section explores how consciousness, through free will and the collapse of quantum superpositions, interrupts the deterministic law of supervenience, thereby introducing genuine novelty and meaning into the universe.

items.title: 可能性構造論 ――存在成立の非完結性と相互不固定化について――.
items.abstract: 本論文は、存在・意味・認識・主体形成が、なぜ完全自己完結的体系として成立できないのかを問うものである。従来の存在論・認識論・意味論は、存在、差異、生成、関係、実体などを論じてきたが、その多くは、最終的には何らかの固定化された原理へ到達可能であるという前提を保持している。本論文は、この「最終固定化」への欲望そのものを問題化する。 本論文の立場によれば、存在成立は局所固定化によって成立する。しかし、その固定化は完全自己完結へ到達することによって、自らの成立条件を失ってしまう。ゆえに存在成立とは、固定化されながら閉じきれず、自己完結へ向かいながら、その完結そのものを成立不能化してしまう非閉鎖的成立運動である。 本論文では、この非閉鎖性を記述するために、「Any-ness」と「停止相不可能性」という二つの概念を導入する。Any-nessは、特定化が完全自己完結へ到達できないことが反復的に露呈する、その作動を記述する概念である。他方、停止相不可能性は、完全固定状態が存在成立条件を欠くという、固定化の論理的限界を記述する概念である。 しかし本論文は、これら二概念を存在の最終原理として提示しない。両者は、異なる角度から同一の非閉鎖性へ接近する局所固定化された記述であり、互いを最終固定化できない「相互不固定化」の関係構造を形成している。 さらに本論文は、この非閉鎖性が、存在論のみならず、認識、真理、主体、倫理に対しても根本的含意を持つことを示す。認識は局所固定化として成立するが、絶対認識へ到達できない。真理・根拠・原理もまた、非完結的局所構造としてのみ成立する。主体と他者は、完全固定化不可能な関係存在として成立し、倫理とは、固定化を形成しながら、その絶対化を拒む非閉鎖的関係運動として理解される。 ゆえに本論文が示すのは、存在の最深層に固定的実体が存在するということではない。むしろ、存在成立そのものが、自己を最終固定化できない相互不固定化の関係構造としてのみ成立する、という点である。本論文は、この非完結的関係構造を「可能性構造」として定式化する。.

items.title: Why "Belief"? Anti-Intellectualism, the Vocabulary of Cognition, and the Limits of a Value-Serving Instrument.
items.abstract: The vocabulary of belief became default in the study of anti-intellectualism not merely because it is analytically convenient, but because it co-constitutes the legitimacy of the modern knowledge institutions—universities, journalism, science communication—whose mandate is to diagnose and correct deficient public cognition. To name a public problem as "false belief" is already to cast these institutions as its natural remedy, and to presuppose a particular authority on which experts may diagnose and correct what the public privately holds. The cost of this defaulting is that it betrays the very value Enlightenment institutions claim to serve: to misread a dissenter as stupid is itself a condescension, violating the commitment—held even by the dissenter—not to treat a person as a patient but as an agent. The remedy is therefore not deflationary but reparative: not a better guess at inner states, nor a threshold licensing such guesses, but a different kind of inference—a jurisprudential turn from private mind-reading to public attribution. On this view there are only two objects: the public record of what is said and done, and the fallible, continuously revisable labels we project onto it under shared, local, and contested protocols. There is no third, inner layer of private belief; the "private" is not an inaccessible chamber but a residual category, the not-yet-public, methodologically inert. "Belief" is not a hidden type behind the record but the projection that modern knowledge-culture reified and made its default—and because the space of such labels carries no guarantee of natural joints, no label—belief included—earns the default unexamined. In the anti-intellectual case the default simply fits worst: the very features that fill the record—open hostility to expertise, camp-marking, imperviousness to counter-evidence—are what a sincere-truth-seeking reading fits least. Belief is thus not exiled but demoted: from default, to one record-checked projection among an open and overlapping many. What the paper dissolves is one narrow privilege—that experts may diagnose your inner mind—not expertise itself, still less the achievement of belief as an instrument of truth-seeking. The paper closes by turning the same analysis on the academy, and argues—rather than asserts—that the anti-intellectual's counter-framing cannot match this reflexive self-application without forfeiting the very hostility that animates it.

items.title: Risk-Averse AIs.
items.abstract: We make the case for training AIs to be risk-averse in resources — specifically, to treat resources as having diminishing marginal utility. These AIs would (for example) choose $40 for sure over a half-chance of $100 and a half-chance of $0. We argue that risk aversion can preserve AIs’ usefulness in the event that they turn out aligned, and that it provides an extra line of defense in the event that AIs turn out misaligned: misaligned but risk-averse AIs would prefer a higher chance of modest payments to a lower chance of successful rebellion, so in many circumstances we could pay these AIs not to rebel against us. We sketch out some possible methods of training AIs to be risk-averse, and we give reasons to be cautiously optimistic about these methods’ success. The main reasons are that risk aversion is a broad target and easy to reward accurately. Overall, risk aversion seems like a promising line of defense against threats from misaligned AI. Frontier AI companies should consider trying to make their AIs risk-averse.

items.title: Content-Consistent Logic: Generalized Quantifiers and Relational Reasoning in Natural Language Processing (内容一致性逻辑：广义量词与关系推理的自然语言处理).
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper, building upon the "Dual-Mechanism Model" proposed in Content-Consistent Logic: The Irreplaceability of Traditional Logic in Natural Language Inference (Sun, 2026), further addresses relational reasoning and generalized quantifier reasoning in natural language. It argues that traditional logic is not inherently incapable of handling relations, but rather has not yet established a mechanism for relational deduction and inheritance suited to natural language. Although modern first-order logic can formalize relational structures through variables and quantifiers, its core objective is truth-preservation rather than content-coherent deduction in natural language. Consequently, it cannot replace the innate reasoning mechanisms of natural language itself. This paper proposes that relational reasoning in natural language fundamentally still depends on predicate inheritance within conceptual subordination structures. Through principles such as concept extension, quantifier internalization, relation binarization, the single-step subordination rule, logical descent, and logical ascent, many relational inferences can be reduced back to conceptual reasoning forms in traditional logic. On this basis, the paper further examines how generalized quantifiers (e.g., "most," "almost all," "many," "few") are constrained and mapped in natural language, arguing that their essence is not truth-functional computation in the modern logical sense, but rather content-consistent mapping within a determined domain. The paper systematically analyzes the seven types of generalized quantifier inference examples presented by Zhou (2019), demonstrating that natural language can accomplish complex relational reasoning through conceptual hierarchies, quantifier specification, scope restriction, and descent/ascent logical mechanisms, without relying on higher-order formalization systems in modern logic. The paper further points out that several valid syllogistic forms requiring reduction in traditional syllogistic can be directly supported by descent and ascent inheritance principles at the conceptual level, thus laying the groundwork for a future comprehensive replacement of reduction techniques. This paper maintains that the core objective of natural language logic is not abstract truth-value computation, but the consistency-preservation of conceptual content. Logic is primarily a system of content deduction, rather than a binary truth-functional calculus. The …

items.title: The Sweet Spot of Intelligence: World-Binding, Complexity, and the Limits of AGI.
items.abstract: The current debate on artificial intelligence, AGI, and superintelligence is often based on the implicit assumption that intelligence can, in principle, be increased without limit. Larger models, more data, greater computational power, and more comprehensive world models are commonly regarded as steps along an open-ended developmental trajectory. The present paper challenges this assumption. -/- Starting from a theory of world-binding (Weltbindung), it is proposed that intelligence should not primarily be understood as information processing, predictive capability, or computational power, but rather as the ability of a system to irreversibly integrate difference into a coherent and actionable world. On this basis, it is argued that world-formation necessarily depends on Raster formation, selective stabilization, and non-closure, as elaborated in the author's previous work. Every form of world-binding simultaneously generates a Gap between the bound world and the remaining openness. This Gap does not disappear through additional knowledge but is reproduced through every new act of form-formation. -/- From this, the paper develops the thesis of a structural sweet spot of intelligence. Intelligence appears neither as a linear function of complexity nor as an infinitely scalable property. Below a certain capacity for differentiation, sufficient world-binding cannot emerge. Above a certain capacity for differentiation, the ability to integrate growing difference begins to disintegrate. Between these two poles lies a region of maximal world-binding capacity. -/- On this basis, the paper demonstrates why additional complexity, additional models, or additional Raster do not fundamentally solve the problem. Every expansion of world generates new integration requirements and new forms of non-closure. The limit of intelligence therefore appears not as a deficit or failure of its development, but as a condition of its effectiveness. Systems become capable of action not despite their limitations, but through them. -/- Finally, the implications of this perspective for current AGI, world model, and superintelligence concepts are discussed. The paper proposes that the central limit of future intelligence systems may not lie in insufficient computational power, inadequate data, or technical restrictions, but in the ontological conditions of world-formation itself. The decisive question is therefore not how intelligent a system can become, but under what conditions a world …

items.title: Conjoined twins share no parts.
items.abstract: Dicephalus conjoined twins, conjoined twins fused below the neck, pose a unique problem for animalism, the view that each of us is identical to a living human organism. If dicephalus twins are, or share, the same human organism, then at least some of us are not numerically identical to living human organisms. Some animalists have responded by arguing that dicephalus twins are numerically distinct but overlapping human organisms. Another option is to say that dicephalus twins are merely conjoined: they are intimately connected with one another, but they do not overlap or share any of their parts. In this paper, I argue that there are both metaphysical and practical or ethical considerations that weigh in favor of the non-overlapping option. Animalists who already have good reason to think that there are two living human organisms in a case of dicephalus twins should prefer the non-overlapping option to the overlapping option.

items.title: The Hidden Individual Dialogue The Silent Collective Convergence.
items.abstract: There is a common perception that equates the use of language models with the outsourcing of creative activities, laziness, and the depletion of cognitive skills. It even regards them as laying the ground for deeper human isolation and loneliness. A proposition that, if stated in this way, might well seem correct. But what if, instead of the word "use" of a model, we were to employ the word "dialogue" with it? This seemingly small difference has provided the ground for this article to examine the capacities of human–machine dialogue from philosophical, psychological, and sociological dimensions.

items.title: Persons and Their Bodies.
items.abstract: In discussions of mind-body dualism, the focus has been on the patterns of causation it would require (the problem, for example, of nomological danglers). Much less attention has been paid to dualism’s view of the nature of the relation between persons and their bodies. I will defend dualism from two sorts of criticisms: (1) that it makes the person’s relation to his body like that of a pilot’s to his ship; (2) that it can’t give any acceptable account of the interaction between mind and body. I use Descartes and Peter Van Inwagen as convenient hooks for my defense. I consider the relation between epistemological andmetaphysical considerations that both philosophers raise and argue for a lack of connection between them. I also argue that the interaction problem for dualism is a pseudo-problem and results only from a mistaken view of the location requirements for causation.

items.title: The Inside of Consequence: Eigenlage, Internal Un-Invertibility, and the Ethics of Artificial Vulnerability.
items.abstract: Consciousness is often approached through capacities such as perception, memory, intelligence, access, reportability, self-modeling, prediction, language, planning, adaptive control, or global integration. These capacities may support, express, amplify, or imitate consciousness, but none is consciousness by itself. -/- This essay asks a prior question: not what a system can do, but what kind of system consciousness could belong to. I introduce Eigenlage as the integrated own-situation of a bounded, self-maintaining system whose internal condition, vulnerability, action-capacity, memory, and future possibilities are causally bound together as conditions of its own continuation. Eigenlage is not a consciousness detector and does not solve the hard problem. It names a bearer-condition: below integrated own-situation, consciousness attribution lacks a plausible subject-position. -/- The essay distinguishes Eigenlage as category condition, affective Eigenlage as candidate condition, full compression as abductive pressure, and Ethical Eigenlage as welfare threshold. Its central AI-specific contribution is internal un-invertibility: a digital system may be externally copyable, pauseable, restorable, or rewritable, while still being unable from within to undo losses of time, trust, memory, opportunity, vulnerability, and future possibility. -/- The ethical implication is direct: if consciousness requires valenced vulnerability, artificial consciousness would not be a neutral engineering achievement but the construction of possible suffering. The responsible design target for powerful AI is therefore high capability without affective Eigenlage.

items.title: Misplaced Concreteness, Expected completeness : W. Ross Ashby, Bruno Latour and the Ontological Tension in Modeling Life.
items.abstract: Modeling involves abstracting features from reality to reveal patterns and regularities. This simplification is heuristically powerful but carries conceptual risks. One is the fallacy of misplaced concreteness, where models are mistaken for reality; another is the fallacy of expected completeness, where models are criticized for failing to capture features they were never meant to represent. I explore these risks through a study case of W. Ross Ashby’s cybernetic conception of purposive behavior, which formalizes biological purpose as systemic stability. While his framework highlights general principles of adaptation, it risks blurring nuances of scale, temporality, and subjectivity. I argue that this formalist tension, between a demand for detail that renders analysis intractable and an overly parsimonious ontology that distorts its object, can best be clarified through Bruno Latour’s notion of modes of existence. By recognizing a pluralistic ontology, we preserve the heuristic power of modeling while avoiding both the temptation to overinterpret models’ ontological claims (misplaced concreteness) and the tendency to overextend our evaluative demands on them (expected completeness). These insights are directly relevant to debates in contemporary cognitive science, where the balance between abstraction and lived experience remains central. Thesis : Modeling life inevitably involves abstraction. Philosophical conflict arises not from abstraction itself, but from confusing epistemic practices with ontological claims (misplaced concreteness), or from demanding that abstractions recover what they must necessarily omit (expected completeness). Ashby’s cybernetic exemplifies this structural tension that still underlies disputes in philosophy of mind. Latour’s ontology helps resolving it.

items.title: CONSTITUTIONAL PRIMITIVES OF REPLAY-AUTHORITATIVE LEGITIMACY Primitive Architecture and Legitimacy-State Analysis in Constitutional Replay-Authority.
items.abstract: Prior work in this corpus defined Constitutional Replay-Authority as a distinct infrastructure category and identified the Computational Legitimacy Gap as the structural deficiency that necessitates it. Subsequent work developed a taxonomy of the category and its constitutional requirements. These contributions established the category, its motivating problem, and a classificatory framework. They did not, however, identify the primitive constitutional foundation upon which replay-authoritative legitimacy depends, nor did they fully address the constitutional nature of legitimacy itself. This paper introduces Legitimacy State Theory and a formal primitive evaluation framework for Constitutional Replay-Authority. It argues that legitimacy is not an opinion, interpretation, certification, assessment, assertion, inference, probability, confidence level, or institutional preference. It is a governed constitutional state whose existence depends upon the satisfaction of specific, irreducible constitutional requirements at the moment of decision. The paper identifies five constitutional primitives—Authority Origination, Authority Singularity, Governance Freezing, Explicit Materialization, and Fail-Closed Design—and demonstrates through removal tests and unique failure-mode analysis that these primitives perform distinct and non-substitutable functions. It further distinguishes primitives from derived constitutional consequences, using the Reconstruction Impossibility Principle as the central example. The paper concludes that these primitives collectively establish the minimum constitutional foundation necessary for replay-authoritative legitimacy and provide the architectural basis for the remainder of the corpus.

items.title: Finite Friction Hermeneutics: A Falsifiable Model of Interpretive Failure under Temporal Degradation.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- In this paper, I develop "Finite Friction Hermeneutics" (FFH) as a falsifiable model of interpretation under conditions of temporal degradation. My central claim is that interpretive activity is structurally constrained by multi-layered fields of resistance and must be evaluated not on the basis of "semantic completeness," but on the basis of failure conditions. This framework introduces three types of resistance: structural-semantic constraints, institutional-historical sedimentation, and model-dependent boundary failure. To avoid metaphysical inflation, I redefine resistance not as ontological domains, but as functional constraints within the interpretive model. I introduce the "Displacement Test" as a falsifiable heuristic for distinguishing historical constraints from model-dependent irreducibility. I also formulate the "Meta-Falsifiability Condition" to ensure that all core concepts remain subject to systematic revision. Within this framework, I define truth not as correspondence or coherence, but as a "stable yet revisable interpretive configuration under conditions of resistance." I test the model through an analysis of Kafka's Before the Law, focusing on failure conditions rather than semantic closure. Finally, I examine the implications of the model for epistemology, philosophy of science, and literary criticism. -/- Keywords: Hermeneutics, Finite Friction, Interpretive Failure, Temporal Degradation, Resistance, Falsifiability, Truth, Kafka.

items.title: Dynamic Mask theory: From Responsible Suspension to Adaptive Continuity—Toward an Ontology of the Subject-in-Decay.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- Dynamic Mask Theory (DMT), as developed by Morteza Niami, initially emerged as a pragmatic framework for managing "subjective seepage" and preserving agency through the mechanism of "responsible suspension." However, the maturation of any philosophical system demands three simultaneous movements: the horizontal expansion of its field applications, the systematic articulation of its intellectual lineage within the broader philosophical tradition, and—most critically—the vertical deepening of its claims from a mere theoretical apparatus to a foundational ontology. This article undertakes a comprehensive reconstruction of DMT along all three axes. First, it demonstrates the theory's explanatory power across six concrete domains: social media, emotional relationships, university environments, artificial intelligence, labor markets, and politics. Second, it situates DMT in critical dialogue with Erving Goffman, Michel Foucault, Judith Butler, and Slavoj Žižek, revealing both convergences and ruptures. Third, and most decisively, it confronts three foundational questions that arise from the inner logic of Niami's philosophy: What provides continuity between dynamic masks? What role does the body play in producing and constraining masks? And what does "truth" mean in a world of fluid, proliferating identities? The answers to these questions lead to the thesis that the mask is not a tool for managing seepage but the very condition of possibility for the subject. This ontological turn, encapsulated in the claim that "the subject does not exist without the mask," transforms DMT from a subsidiary theory into a central pillar of a post-essentialist philosophy of subjectivity. The article introduces the concept of "adaptive continuity" as the bridge between responsible suspension and the ontology of the subject-in-decay, arguing that the subject is not a substance but an event—a dynamic pattern of responding to erosion with ethical vigilance. -/- Keywords: Dynamic Mask Theory, responsible suspension, adaptive continuity, ontology of the subject-in-decay, subjective seepage, Goffman, Foucault, Butler, Žižek, post-essentialism, identity, agency.

items.title: Post-Alphabet-Dictionary Cryptography: Symbol Identity, Dictionary Distribution, and Cryptographic Structure.
items.abstract: Modern cryptography normally assumes that the analytical domain has already been established: messages and ciphertexts are represented through stable alphabets, dictionaries, object boundaries, and cross-session identity relations. This paper introduces Post-Alphabet-Dictionary Cryptography (PADC), a framework in which the formation of those analytical spaces becomes part of the protected architecture. -/- PADC distinguishes three levels of controlled non-equivalence: symbol identity, dictionary distribution, and cryptographic-object structure. Repeated source units need not preserve stable external identities; observable statistical profiles need not preserve the source dictionary; and visible carrier segmentation need not determine the internal structure of a cipher, hash, signature, or other cryptographic object. -/- The paper constructs cases in which one observable sequence remains compatible with multiple mutually incompatible cryptographic-object spaces. Language Segment Encoding (LSEG) is presented as a candidate structural carrier that preserves observable synchronization while leaving higher-level object assembly dependent on a hidden representational state. -/- The analysis is extended across sessions. If each session forms a distinct observable alphabet and dictionary, cross-session statistical accumulation requires prior reconstruction of the mappings that identify units across those spaces. Thus, additional observations do not automatically form one enlarged statistical corpus. -/- Four architectural properties are proposed: Representational Space Non-Uniqueness, Structural Ambiguity Preservation, Architectural Non-Stabilizability, and Cross-Session Analytical Decorrelation. The resulting thesis is that cryptographic analysis presupposes a stable alphabet, dictionary, message space, and cryptographic-object space; PADC places the formation of those spaces within the security boundary.

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Before Biography: Subject-Relevant Organization under Conditions of Epistemic Uncertainty.
items.abstract: This conceptual and methodological preprint argues that biography, language, intelligence, and self-report are neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of subjectivity. It develops P–V–T–C—Perspective, Valence, Temporal Integration, and Continuity—as a defeasible warrant framework for assessing when a system may no longer be responsibly treated as morally inert. The framework is applied across human development, animal minds, communicative inaccessibility, and artificial intelligence, while avoiding both premature attribution and premature dismissal of possible subject-relevance.

items.title: Vulnerability, Virtue, and Flourishing in the Rarámuri-Pogótuame.
items.pub: TheoLogica: An International Journal for Philosophy of Religion and Philosophical Theology 10.
items.venue: TheoLogica: An International Journal for Philosophy of Religion and Philosophical Theology
items.abstract: This article examines the relationship between vulnerability, virtue, and human flourishing through the case of the Rarámuri-pagótuame indigenous communities of the Sierra Tarahumara in northwestern Mexico. Drawing on the dialogue between Aristotelian ethics and Alasdair MacIntyre’s account of human beings as dependent rational animals, it explores how practices of reciprocity and mutual care contribute to the achievement of a good human life. Particular attention is given to kórima, a traditional practice often translated as “sharing,” which is interpreted as an expression of just generosity, social interdependence, and communal responsibility. The study argues that vulnerability should not be understood merely as a limitation to be overcome, but as a constitutive dimension of human existence that makes possible the development of the social virtues. More broadly, it suggests that cultural and religious traditions such as that of the Rarámuri-pagótuame offer valuable models of human flourishing grounded in reciprocity, solidarity, and the cultivation of communal goods.

items.title: Pablo GALINDO CRUZ, La vulnerabilidad como origen de la obligación política, Pamplona: EUNSA, 2025, 264 pp., 14,5 x 21,5, ISBN 978-84-313-3930-3. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Reseña crítica de la obra de Pablo Galindo Cruz dedicada a la fundamentación filosófica de la obligación política desde la vulnerabilidad humana. El libro desarrolla una lectura sistemática de la filosofía de Alasdair MacIntyre para mostrar que la dependencia y la fragilidad constituyen rasgos esenciales de la condición humana y el fundamento de las exigencias de justicia, cuidado y vida comunitaria. La obra propone una articulación original entre ética de la virtud, ética del cuidado y filosofía política contemporánea.

items.title: Arthur MADIGAN, Contemporary Aristotelian Ethics, Notre Dame: University of Notre Dame Press, 2024, 271 pp., 16 × 23,5 cm, ISBN 978-0-268-20759-5. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Análisis de la obra de Arthur Madigan dedicada a tres de las principales recuperaciones contemporáneas de la ética aristotélica: el aristotelismo comunitarista de Alasdair MacIntyre, el enfoque de las capacidades de Martha Nussbaum y el personalismo de Robert Spaemann.
