La recensión destaca cómo estas propuestas ofrecen respuestas diversas a cuestiones centrales de la filosofía moral actual, tales como la racionalidad práctica, la vulnerabilidad, la dignidad humana, el florecimiento y la vida buena, mostrando la vigencia del legado aristotélico en el debate ético contemporáneo.

items.title: Knowing How to be Vicious.
items.pub: Journal of the American Philosophical Association 12 (3):413-427.
items.venue: Journal of the American Philosophical Association
items.abstract: It is widely held that an intellectual or epistemic vice is characterised by its negative relationship to epistemic goods. But which epistemic goods, exactly? The main answers in the vice-epistemological literature are (i) the truth and (ii) propositional knowledge. In this paper, I demonstrate the need to expand vice epistemology's axiology beyond these epistemic goods. In particular, I argue that vice epistemologists need to include knowledge-how in their theorising if they are to provide us with a full account of the nature and development of some putative epistemic vices. First, I show that this species of knowledge can be embedded in the manifestation and development of some vices, such that agents acquire this species of knowledge in virtue of either exercising or acquiring these epistemic vices. Second, I claim that the inclusion of knowledge-how in vice epistemology has important implications for its two main theoretical camps – motivationalism and obstructivism. I end by explaining how a less popular view in the literature can possibly vindicate the relationship between epistemic vices and knowledge-how.

items.title: The Ethics of Corporate Belief.
items.abstract: I argue for a deflationary account of corporate belief on which their attribution is grounded in the official and intentional actions of the corporation’s operative members. I outline an ethics of individual belief focusing on responsibility for belief formation in contexts in which beliefs guide actions that may bring about harm. In light of the deflationary account of corporate attitudes, I consider how to project the account to the corporate case. I argue that the division of role responsibilities, especially proxy roles, in organizations induces a division of moral labor. On this basis, I introduce a framework for identifying roles that, relative to particular actions, are responsibility magnets and responsibility shelters for institutional role players. I identify epistemic and oversight roles as responsibility magnets for corporate belief.

items.title: The Hexagon of Indeterminate Propositions: Toward a Logic of Determination.
items.abstract: Keynote presentation delivered at the 9th World Congress on the Square of Opposition (Square 9), Université du Québec à Montréal, June 2026. This presentation introduces the Hexagon of Indeterminate Propositions and the Logic of Determination. It shows that the traditional Square of Opposition emerges as a theorem of the system at the third layer of opposition (O3). Do not hesitate to contact me if you want me to deliver this talk at your university online. Just write me to the email at the end of the presentation.

items.title: Recoding Democracy: AI and the Fight for Our Democratic Future.
items.abstract: Popular debates about AI and democracy rest on misconceptions about both democracy and AI. Theodore Lechterman, an ascendant thinker in the philosophy and governance of AI, dismantles these misconceptions and shows how to rethink democracy for an algorithmic age. Recoding Democracy reveals that democratizing AI is not about widening product access or granting stakeholder input on Big Tech's terms. It requires that those subjected to AI systems enjoy fair opportunities for ongoing and deliberative public oversight. The book rejects fantasies of AI-powered direct democracy and makes the case for representative democracy selectively reinforced by AI. It shows how the possibility of rule by intelligent machines threatens democracy's philosophical foundations and charts a path for strengthening them. Most boldly, the book defends the possibility of AI citizenship and grapples with the resulting questions of political justice between human and artificial citizens. Daring in its questions but sober in its claims, Recoding Democracy is essential reading for engaged citizens as well as students and scholars in philosophy, politics, law, and technology.

items.title: On AI and Some Epistemological Issues.
items.pub: Communication and Cognition: An Interdisciplinary Quarterly Journal 59 (1):49-68.
items.venue: Communication and Cognition: An Interdisciplinary Quarterly Journal
items.abstract: Four contentions are defended. First, given what AI has shown us about neural networks, there does exist a "logic of discovery", contrary to what Popper and virtually every other philosopher of science has alleged. Second, given some rudimentary points about AI, the obvious solution to the Gettier problem (namely, that the justification mustn't involve a falsehood) is shown to be correct, a secondary result being that a version of coherentism is likely correct. Third, connectionism is compatible with Chomsky's generative grammar, contrary to first appearances. Fourth, cognition is shown to be analog, a corollary being that the Computational Theory of Mind is shown to be even more incoherent than it was previously known to be.

items.title: Η υποκειμενικότητα του κόσμου: ένα κλασικό μοντέλο της γνώσης.
items.abstract: Το δοκίμιο προτείνει ένα κλασικό μοντέλο συνειδητοποίησης της υποκειμενικότητας του κόσμου: όχι ως αυθαίρετη «προβολή», αλλά ως δομική διάσταση της πραγματικότητας, στην οποία το νόημα συγκρατείται από τη σύνθεση. Στην τομή της επιστημολογίας, της ερμηνευτικής, της αισθητικής και της οντολογίας (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: Hands-Off Agentic Robot Learning in MuJoCo.
items.abstract: A case study where an agent did not merely write robotics code, but ran the experimental loop: it built a MuJoCo OpenArm manipulation world, chose what to test, rejected misleading reward curves, launched training jobs, judged rollouts through a separate vision-language critic, localized bugs, and decided what to try next. The human supplied goals and behavioral constraints over chat; the agent made most of the tactical judgments. In roughly 36 hours and 28 logged iterations, the loop went from an empty simulator and repeated 0% reward-hack failures to chained teachers at 76–80%, a language-conditioned π0.5 policy recovered from a silent action-harness bug to 56/60 grasps and 49/60 correct-color grasps, and a final RABC checkpoint at 219/250 (87.6%) strict simulated success. The result is not solved robotics. It is evidence that hands-off agentic systems can begin to own the messy judgment loop of robot learning: build, watch, doubt, diagnose, retry, and remember.

items.title: AI's Shadow of a Word.
items.abstract: Candour, Drafting, and the Limits of Legal Measurement The Public Office (Accountability) Bill, known widely as the Hillsborough Law, will require public authorities and public officials to act with candour, transparency and frankness in their dealings with inquiries and investigations.1 The Bill is a serious and overdue piece of legislation. It answers a wrong that took decades to acknowledge, and it does so in the language of openness rather than the language of mere process. This note does not argue against it. It argues for it, and for taking its central word seriously enough to notice what that word asks of the law that must enforce it. The argument is narrow. It is not that the Bill is defective, nor that its drafters erred. It is that one of its operative terms, candour, names something that the act of legal definition cannot hold without remainder, and that the remainder is precisely the part the families were owed. This is not a flaw to be corrected by better drafting. It is a feature of what candour is, and of what law can and cannot measure. Naming it now, while the word is still whole, seems the honest thing to do. I. Candour is not disclosure. I foresee AI language problems with.

items.title: The Universe We Cannot See: The Physical Limits of Human Perception and the Ultimate Question of Knowledge.
items.pub: Seattle, WA: Published by Amazon KDP.
items.abstract: This book is a philosophical reflection on the physical limits of human knowledge. Taking Energy Quantum Theory (EQT) as its broader conceptual background, it asks a simple but unsettling question: do human beings truly see the universe, or only a narrow projection of it? The book begins from a physical fact: human senses respond to only a tiny fraction of the full spectrum of cosmic reality. Vision, hearing, touch, and other sensory systems are not transparent windows onto the universe, but biological detectors with limited response ranges. What we call the “world” is therefore not reality in its full form, but a highly compressed, filtered, and reconstructed model produced by the interaction between external signals, sensory organs, neural processing, language, culture, and cognition. From this starting point, the book develops a broad epistemological argument. It revisits the history of science as a history of breaking perceptual boundaries: the telescope revealed celestial structures invisible to the naked eye; the microscope opened the microbial world; radio astronomy, X-ray astronomy, neutrino detection, and gravitational-wave observatories expanded human knowledge beyond ordinary sensory channels. Each major scientific breakthrough, the book argues, has been a technical and conceptual extension of perception. The discussion then turns to philosophy. Plato’s cave, Kant’s thing-in-itself, the subject-object divide, and the measurement problem in quantum mechanics are reinterpreted as different expressions of a deeper physical condition: all knowledge is mediated by detectors, and every act of detection is a form of participation rather than passive observation. Objectivity, in this framework, does not mean access to reality without mediation; it means reproducible results across well-defined forms of interaction. The book also examines language as another perceptual boundary. Human concepts, metaphors, and philosophical categories are shaped by the sensory and cultural worlds in which they arise. What cannot be perceived often cannot be named; what cannot be named often cannot be clearly thought. Yet science, mathematics, art, and technology allow human beings to push beyond these inherited limits. The final chapters propose three paths toward full-spectrum reality: programmable detectors that expand the physical range of observation; full-spectrum theoretical modeling that reaches where direct detection cannot; and an epistemological reconstruction …

items.title: On Becoming - The Two Forces at the Heart of the Matter.
items.abstract: Almost none of a body's weight comes from the rest-masses of its quarks; roughly ninety-nine percent is the energy of the strong force holding them together. And every heavier atom in a hand was made by transformation in a star, by the weak force, the only one of the four that changes what a thing is. This essay reads those two forces as binding and becoming — that a self cannot be alone and cannot stay the same, and is exactly the standing negotiation of the two. It closes the sequence on the four fundamental forces, and closes it by keeping the seam honest: that most of one's mass is binding energy is measured physics, that this means one is mostly relationship is a reading, and the rhymes are as good as they are partly because the author went looking for exactly this pair. The essay says so, and counts that admission as the only thing it is entitled to claim.

items.title: Generativity Under Power: Trust, Asymmetry, and Estrangement in Intimate Relations.
items.abstract: How does love fare under power? Across this series intimate relation has been theorised as a generative-relational process — a coupling out of which value is generated rather than extracted — but, in effect, in a clearing: it did not confront that intimate relation unfolds in a field saturated with asymmetries, which can deform, capture, freeze, and on occasion shatter that very generativity. This paper confronts power directly, around three questions in an ascending logic — creation, preservation, liberation — all bearing on a single object, love, in the sense of the dynamics of the real between two subjects, the part of the bond that circles the unsymbolisable and cannot be counted, traded, or managed. -/- How does love create a world? — the question of generative-relational being, whose findings are taken as established, with an added etiology of how the world-creating coupling breaks down into estrangement (surechigai). How is love not destroyed by power? — for which the paper reconstructs the theory of international relations, stripping the realist assumption that an anarchic field's currency is relative power, and recovering its deeper object: how opaque subjects, unable to enter one another directly, build trust and order under uncertainty without a central authority. How does love become free within history? — for a dialectical historical materialism that holds the determining force of material conditions together with the relative autonomy of the symbolic and affective life they shape. -/- The intimate relation is a two-level system: at the level of the end stands the dynamics of love, a process of the real that cannot be measured or exchanged; at the level of the means stands the symbolic order of power, calculable and strategic. The means serve the end but tend intrinsically to damage it. Hence the central claim: the tools of power and wealth can protect the conditions under which love occurs but cannot produce love itself — a political economy of conditions, never of love. Trust is the interface that crosses both levels, and the variable that decides whether an asymmetry of power becomes generative or frozen. Two further claims follow: estrangement is, in the first instance, a necessary moment of the bond's self-maintenance, not a malfunction (a relation at perfect concordance would be at equilibrium, which is to say dead); and power can neither eliminate itself nor be eliminated entirely, so the only viable course is to generate, alongside …

items.title: نبیین جامع نظریه ساختار هستی و عوالم نوبتی.
items.abstract: مسئلهٔ نسبتِ انسان با امکانات وجودی خویش، و چگونگی هماهنگ‌سازیِ این امکانات با اصل عدالت و اختیار. بسیاری از نظام‌های فلسفی، چه در سنت‌های شرقی و چه در میراث یونانی و اسلامی، کوشیده‌اند برای این پرسش پاسخی فراهم کنند که چگونه انسانی با استعدادهای متکثر، گرایش‌های متضاد و قابلیت‌های گاه ناسازگار، در بستری واحد می‌تواند به تمامیِ ظرفیت‌های خود مجال بروز دهد و در عین حال مشمول عدالت کامل باشد. این تلاش‌ها هرچند دستاوردهای ارزشمندی داشته‌اند، اما در برابر برخی پرسش‌های بنیادین همچنان محل گفت‌وگو و بازخوانی باقی مانده‌اند. پرسش‌هایی که از محدودیتِ بستر واحد، از وابستگی هویت به حافظه و از تفسیرهای گوناگون از مسئولیت اخلاقی و امکان تحقق اضداد ناشی می‌شود. این نوشته بر آن است که مسئله را از زاویه‌ای دیگر طرح کند. اگر عدالت را نه «توزیع نتایج»، بلکه «فراهم‌سازی بستر تحقق ظرفیت‌ها» بدانیم، و اگر انسان را موجودی تلقی کنیم که بخش مهمی از قابلیت‌هایش تنها در نسبت با امکانات و موقعیت‌های متقابل معنا می‌یابد، آنگاه این پرسش بجا خواهد بود که آیا یک جهانِ واحد، با ساختاری ثابت و امکان‌های محدود، می‌تواند میدانِ کاملی برای چنین تحققی فراهم سازد؟ این پرسش، هستهٔ مرکزی نظریه‌ای است که در این کتاب تبیین می‌شود. نظریهٔ حاضر از اصل بنیادین اختیار آغاز می‌کند. اختیار نه صرفاً توان انتخاب میان دو کنش جزئی، بلکه امکانِ تعیینِ جهتِ وجودی و ساختنِ وزن وجودی خود است. از این منظر، هر فعل انسانی نوعی «اثرگذاری بر هستی» است که پیامد آن در ساختار وجودی شخص باقی می‌ماند. پیامدی که می‌توان آن را به گونه‌ای دقیق‌تر، «وزن وجودی» نامید. این وزن، در نگاه این نظریه، نه استعاره‌ای اخلاقی بلکه امری واقعی و مؤثر در تعیین "ساختارِ دید و هندسهٔ نفس" است. طرح این مفاهیم، هدفش ارائهٔ تصویری نو از تعدد بسترهاست. تصویری که نه در معرض برداشت‌های رایج چندجهانی، و نه متکی به فرض‌های غیرقابل‌دفاعِ علمی است. در این چارچوب، بسترهای متکثر نه جهان‌های پراکنده و مستقل، بلکه ساحت‌های متمایز اما مرتبط در مسیر وجودی نفس هستند که هر یک بخشی از میدان تحققِ ظرفیت‌های انسان را می‌گشایند. در این ساحت‌ها، اختیار همچنان نقش بنیادی خود را حفظ می‌نماید. این دستگاه نه در پی نفی تجربهٔ رنج و نه در پی توجیه آن است. رنج در این نظریه نه ارزش ذاتی دارد و نه هدف نهایی است؛ بلکه در برخی شرایط، یکی از موقعیت‌هایی است که امکان ظهور و تمایز برخی انتخاب‌ها را فراهم می‌کند. رنج، ابزار وجودی برای گشودن یک موقعیت است. رنج، مجازات نیست، بسترِ "وضوح بخشیدن به" یک امکان است. رنج، بی‌هدف نیست، شرطِ "تمایز و برجستگیِ" یک انتخاب است. برای مثال، رنج بی‌عدالتی، بسترِ "پُررنگ شدنِ" ظرفیت بخشش یا ظلم‌ستیزی را می‌گشاید. مباحثی چون عدالت، اختیار، جبر، خیر و شر، علم الهی و کمال، مسائل مستقل و گسسته نیستند؛ همگی شاخه‌هایی از یک مسئلهٔ واحد یعنی انسان …

items.title: Why interactionist fields are (almost) invisible to physics: A phase-transition account.
items.abstract: This paper argues that panpsychist and panqualityist theories are particularly well aligned with contemporary fundamental physics when formulated in field-theoretic terms. Applied to non-monistic interactionist versions of these views, this motivates the postulation of a pervasive qualitative/experiential field with its own dynamics and weak local coupling to physical systems, allowing energy and momentum to be exchanged between the two domains. Such theories face an invisibility problem: why are the effects of the posited psychophysical interaction not ordinarily observed? I propose that the answer lies in a phase transition between disordered and ordered regimes of the field. In the disordered regime, local psychophysical contributions cancel statistically, preventing macroscopic effects; in the ordered regime, this cancellation breaks down, allowing the same interaction to become macroscopically significant. Accordingly, departures from the expected physical energy or momentum balance are predicted in the ordered regime. The transition is argued to be more plausibly understood as a driven non-equilibrium process than as a conventional equilibrium transition: physical processes provide the drive, while a state variable within the qualitative/experiential field serves as the control parameter and feedback helps sustain the resulting ordered regime. Consciousness in brains is proposed to depend on their ability to drive and sustain this ordered regime. Because the field carries energy and momentum, it is expected to be gravitationally active while remaining largely hidden from non-gravitational detection. The qualitative/experiential field may therefore contribute to gravitational phenomena currently attributed to dark matter.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 20).
items.abstract: In this article, we primarily seek to establish a theory of object choice. What is an object choice? An object is a set of similar things that attract the subject's interest. Object choice refers to the choice a subject makes when confronted with two or more such objects. It is evident that object choice is one of the most common forms of choice encountered in daily life—for example, choosing clothes, purchasing a house, and so on. In this paper, I introduce my revised version of Maslow’s famous theory of psychological needs and attempt to solve the problem of object choice through this theory together with the concept of Super-Existence.

items.title: Who's Pulling the Strings? Toward a Minimum Recursive Archetype Hypothesis of Human Narrative Cognition and Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: A large language model has no biography, no unconscious, and no childhood. It nonetheless reproduces, with uncomfortable regularity, a small set of reasoning postures that long predate it, doubt that refuses closure, confidence that overfills a gap, hunger for a complete account, judgment applied without mercy, and reduction that mistakes elegance for truth. This paper treats that regularity as data rather than coincidence. Building on a short essay that mapped five literary characters, Hamlet, Don Quixote, Faust, Javert, and Sherlock Holmes, onto five recurring patterns of machine output, it formalizes each pattern as a psychological function, traces each across independent cultural and narrative lineages, and proposes a falsifiable hypothesis: that human narrative cognition operates within a small, bounded repertoire of recursive archetypes, and that large language models surface this repertoire by compression rather than invention. The paper is explicit about what is established, what is illustrative, and what remains conjecture.

items.title: Can expertise be about values? On the roles of patients’ perspectives in psychiatric epistemology.
items.abstract: In this commentary on Şerife Tekin’s book Reclaiming the Self in Psychiatry: Centering Personal Narratives for a Humanist Science, I explore the following question: does Tekin’s conception of expertise by experience capture all the areas of expertise that patients can have? To do so, I first reconstruct Tekin’s argument regarding the idea that patients are experience-based experts and show how it fits into the broader view that psychiatry should aim for a social form of objectivity. I then draw on two theoretical frameworks from feminist philosophy of science – social objectivity (the one endorsed by Tekin) and feminist standpoint theory – to reflect further on patients’ roles in knowledge making practices in psychiatry. I question whether the additional patients roles revealed by social objectivity and feminist standpoint theory correspond to the concept of expertise used by Tekin. I close by further reflecting on the concept of expertise itself and on why it is seen as a powerful tool for considering the important integration of patients into psychiatric epistemology.

items.title: External-World Skepticism and the New Ethics of Belief.
items.abstract: External-world skepticism challenges, among other things, the epistemic credentials of beliefs about other people. Some external-world skeptics deny that I know my loved ones exist; some claim that my belief that my loved ones exist is epistemically impermissible. However, abandoning this belief would be highly unattractive. In fact, new developments in the ethics of belief provide the groundwork for an argument that skeptical doubts about loved ones, even if well-grounded, are prima facie morally wrongful. I defend the external-world skeptic from this moral criticism. Our moral obligations, I note, are sensitive to our epistemic limitations; the fact that you have no epistemic reason to believe that your uncle exists, for instance, can explain why you are under no moral obligation to visit him in the hospital. Drawing on this point, I demonstrate that we face no moral obligation to avoid skeptical doubt when that doubt is genuinely well-grounded.

items.title: What's Wrong With "Conceptual Amelioration"?
items.abstract: Conceptual amelioration aims to make the world a more just place by ameliorating our concepts. I offer three arguments against this enterprise as currently practiced to show how social philosophy aimed at producing social change can be better practiced. First, ameliorators often fail to provide plausible stories to vindicate their claims about how conceptual amelioration will unfold in our nonideal world. Second, ameliorators’ focus on postulating meanings of “concepts” risks distracting from important normative theorizing about justice. Third, ameliorators tend to overstate the importance of conceptual change for social change. The upshot is that, since such projects tend to be done poorly on their own terms and to evince excessively idealistic views of social change, we should reconsider how to engage in such projects. Drawing on these criticisms, I argue that if conceptual amelioration should be practiced, it should be in service of ideology critique.

items.title: 元统一论视角下教育本质的重审：从知识填充到追问式归位.
items.abstract: 摘要：教育教了太多“是什么”，却几乎不教为什么是这个“是什么”。知识被拆解为学科，学习被压缩为填充。即便有了选科自由、跨学科课程，教育依然在做学科间的拼接，从未引导学习者审视这些划分本身何以为据。个体在边界内积累答案，却未被给予审视边界的工具。与此同时，人工智能对已有知识的调用与整合能力正以量级差距超越人类，这一巨变将“教育以传递答案为核心”的旧范式逼入了系统性反思的关口。 本文立足《元统一论》系列论文推导教育本质：守护狭义探索者的元追问并激活其能动性。元追问是元行为在人类认知维度的一类具体体现方式，具有双向性：向上可在既有框架内延伸应用，亦可在本源上构建理论；向下可追溯知识成立的前提，亦可溯源理论根基。元追问的持续展开是能动性的一种具体运行方式，每一次追问都是能动性的自我确认。教育中的加、减法是认知活动的两个基本方向，是互为补充、循环推进的一体两面。让学习者在追问的持续展开中完成自我归位，这是教育在人工智能时代不可替代的存在理由。 Abstract: Education teaches too much of “what it is,” yet almost never teaches why it is this “what it is.” Knowledge is fragmented into disciplines, and learning is compressed into filling. Even with the freedom to choose subjects and the introduction of interdisciplinary courses, education still merely splices disciplines together, never guiding learners to examine the very grounds on which these divisions themselves rest. Individuals accumulate answers within boundaries, but are never given the tools to scrutinize those boundaries. Meanwhile, artificial intelligence’s capacity to retrieve and integrate existing knowledge is surpassing that of humans by orders of magnitude—a shift that has forced the old paradigm of “education as answer-delivery” into a moment of systemic reflection. Grounded in the Meta-Unification Theory series, this paper derives the essence of education: safeguarding the narrow scope explorer’s meta inquiry and activating its agency. Meta inquiry is a specific instantiation of meta behavior in the human cognitive dimension, and is bidirectional: upward, it can extend applications within existing frameworks or construct theories at the level of the Origin; downward, it can trace the preconditions of knowledge or the foundational roots of theories. The sustained unfolding of meta inquiry is a concrete operation of agency, and every act of inquiry is a self affirmation of that agency. The “addition” and “subtraction” in education are two fundamental directions of cognitive activity—two complementary, mutually reinforcing, and cyclically advancing sides of the same coin. Enabling learners to accomplish self return to place through the ongoing unfolding of inquiry is education’s irreplaceable raison d’être in the age of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Neo-emotions: Introduction to the Special Issue.
Transition to Digital Ethics: A Primer from Philosophy to Practice.
items.pub: Boca Raton, FL: Chapman & Hall / CRC Press (Taylor & Francis).
items.abstract: As digital technologies become more pervasive and powerful, they raise increasingly pressing ethical questions that need to be understood and addressed. -/- This book provides an accessible introduction to the important field of digital ethics. It explores topical examples of ethical problems created by the technology and shows how ethical ideas and values can be used to make sense of them. It provides the readership a clear, well-researched insight into the various issues under the banner of ‘digital ethics’, including how each of these issues relates to different technologies such as AI, smartphones, and automated decision-making (to say the least). This is coupled with contemporary ideas on ameliorating ethical harm and risk, which are grounded in philosophical thought, presented in an accessible way. -/- The book will benefit those who design and implement digital technologies and, more broadly, anyone with an interest in the compelling ethical and social issues arising from digital technologies. It carefully and clearly describes the philosophical ideas as well as technical considerations behind contemporary digital technology use, to provide the reader with a solid footing for further exploration of this rapidly expanding field.

items.title: An enduring partnership: A book review of Matthew Lipman and Ann Margaret Sharp: Philosophy for Children’s Educational Revolution by Roberto Franzini Tibaldeo. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Roberto Franzini Tibaldeo’s (2023) book, Matthew Lipman and Ann Margaret Sharp: Philosophy for Children’s Educational Revolution, is an historical-genealogical approach to the history, ideas and practice of Philosophy for Children, presented as Lipman and Sharp’s collaborative philosophical-educational vision resulting from an enduring interpersonal and philosophical partnership. Drawing on his extensive research, including unpublished documents preserved in the Institute for the Advancement of Philosophy for Children (IAPC) archives at Montclair State University in New Jersey, Tibaldeo weaves together Lipman’s and Sharp’s philosophical and educational theories with biography to understand the origins of their educational project and subsequent developments. Like Maughn Gregory and Megan Laverty’s (2018) edited volume, In Community of Inquiry with Ann Margaret Sharp, he also recognises the extent of Sharp’s involvement as more than a collaborator, but as an influential, central partner in shaping the IAPC curriculum, community of inquiry pedagogy, and thinking about philosophy, education, and children. As such, it offers a critical and comparative appraisal, which provides valuable insights for philosophers, teachers, and educators who are acquainted with Philosophy for Children as well as those new to its theory and practice.

items.title: The Unified Structural-Constructivist Architecture of Affect: A Comprehensive Technical and Empirical Report on the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This report presents a unified structural constructivist architecture of human affect through the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a model that resolves the long standing divide between discrete and dimensional theories of emotion. The CEF conceptualizes emotions as ten functional operators—“active functional operators… internal mechanisms that modulate cognitive, somatic, and conative systems” (document)—distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. These operators form a computational emotional engine with defined somatic signatures, directional flow rules, and predictable transition sequences. The report details the Decalogue of Operators, their overactivation and suppression risks, and the structural mechanisms underlying emotional fusions such as GPAP, Expand Accept metabolic fusion, bipolar oscillation, and ruminative stagnation. A quantum probabilistic formulation models these fused states as non separable entanglements requiring somatic decoherence interventions. The paper further outlines the preregistered psychometric validation program, including the 100 item scenario based CEF Scale and its CFA/ESEM modeling paradox. Extensions into relational dynamics, parenting, CBT comparison, and computational affect demonstrate the framework’s cross domain generality. Finally, an external 4,132 participant Bayesian network study independently supports the CEF’s prediction that Calculating-Constricting fusion drives systemic behavioral cascades, linking perceived stress to sleep disruption, mental well being, and physical activity patterns. Together, these findings position the CEF as a comprehensive, computationally tractable model for affective science, clinical intervention, and synthetic emotional systems.

items.title: The Theoretical Architecture of Core Emotion Framework Political Science: Charisma, Polarization, and Leadership Failure in States of Operational Fusion.
items.abstract: This paper advances a unified affective computational architecture for political psychology by applying the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) to the domains of charisma, polarization, and leadership failure. Whereas traditional discrete and dimensional models compress political affect into coarse categories or low dimensional valence–arousal spaces, the CEF models political behavior as structured sequences of ten functional emotional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. Using this operator calculus, the paper formalizes political charisma as a multiplicative interaction of Expanding, Achieving, and Boosting, stabilized by a threshold level of Accepting that prevents somatic friction and expressive collapse. The framework then models affective polarization as a set of infectious microstates—such as Political Outrage, Tribal Loyalty, and the Polarization Spiral—each defined by rigid operator loops that resist cognitive persuasion. Finally, the paper introduces a fusion based taxonomy of leadership failure, demonstrating how chronic operator entanglements (e.g., Calculating–Sensing, Achieving–Constricting, Boosting–Achieving) produce predictable patterns of indecision, authoritarian drift, burnout, and scandal mismanagement. Together, these contributions establish the CEF political program as a rigorous, computationally grounded paradigm for analyzing political behavior, debate performance, voter contagion, and executive collapse. Readers should confirm political information with trusted sources. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); operator functionalism; structural constructivist affective science; political charisma; affective polarization; leadership failure; somatic cognition; emotional operators; fusion states; debate performance; voter microstates; computational political psychology; charisma algebra; somatic perturbation modeling; executive collapse; psychophysiological validation; political behavior architecture.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Architecture of Nurture: A Comprehensive Model of Parental Attunement and Boundary Regulation within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper presents the first structural constructivist model of parenting grounded in the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), offering a mechanistic account of how caregivers regulate attunement, boundaries, and developmental vision through ten functional emotional operators. As the document states, caregiving is best understood as “an active, self regulating feedback system governed by the foundational polarity of self assertion (Agency) and connection (Yielding).” By mapping parental behavior onto the Head (Sensing–Calculating–Deciding), Heart (Expanding–Constricting–Achieving), and Gut (Arranging–Appreciating–Boosting) centers, the model reveals how real time operator sequencing shapes child co regulation, emotional safety, and long term developmental scaffolding. The paper further demonstrates how pathological fusions—such as Sensing–Calculating hypervigilance—disrupt parental flexibility, producing instability in the caregiver child affective loop. A mathematical formulation using coupled state vectors and cross individual influence matrices formalizes the dynamics of family co regulation, while the Detangling Protocol provides a clinically actionable method for restoring operator independence. As summarized in the text, “Accepting represents the capacity to accept the child exactly how they are,” functioning as the global baseline that recalibrates the entire system. Together, these contributions establish a unified computational, somatic, and clinical architecture for understanding and improving parental emotional agility. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); parental attunement; boundary regulation; emotional operators; Head Heart Gut somatic centers; developmental vision; co regulation dynamics; operator fusion; Detangling Protocol; somatic choreography; Sensing–Calculating loop; authoritative parenting architecture; structural constructivist affective modeling; family systems computation; Accepting baseline integration.

items.title: The CEF Model of Democratic Stability and Collapse: An Affective-Computational Architecture of Institutional Resilience and Backsliding.
items.abstract: This paper introduces a unified affective computational architecture for understanding democratic stability, institutional resilience, and political backsliding through the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). Whereas traditional institutional theories explain national success through inclusive versus extractive political structures, and psychological models reduce political affect to coarse valence–arousal dimensions, the CEF models political behavior as structured sequences of ten functional emotional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. Using this operator calculus, the paper reframes democratic stability as a dynamic equilibrium of emotional somatic processes across leaders and citizens, and models democratic backsliding as the emergence of rigid operator fusions—such as Calculating–Sensing, Achieving–Constricting, and Boosting–Achieving—that suppress adaptive governance. The framework further formalizes affective polarization as a set of infectious microstates (Political Outrage, Tribal Loyalty, and the Polarization Spiral) that co-opt cognitive evaluation and undermine institutional coherence. At the macro level, the paper introduces a stability failure taxonomy—Collapse, Rigidity, Drift, Lag, Overshoot, and Fragmentation—derived from operator algebra and center activation matrices. Finally, it outlines a rigorous empirical program combining structural equation modeling, somatic kinematic tracking, and autonomic resonance analysis to validate the CEF as a mechanistic model of democratic resilience. This work positions the CEF as a foundational paradigm for integrating emotional architecture with institutional theory in the study of democratic stability. Keyword Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); democratic stability; political backsliding; operator functionalism; affective polarization; institutional resilience; emotional operator fusion; somatic computational political science; stability failure taxonomy; structural constructivist affective science; leadership pathology; center activation dynamics.

items.title: Structural Psychopathology of Chronic Sensing Fusion: A Core Emotion Framework Analysis of Sensory Dysregulation, Neurodevelopmental Sensitivity, and Executive Attentional Deficits.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by Jamel Bulgaria, enters the fragmented landscape of affective science as a structural-constructivist paradigm that bridges universalist theories of basic emotion with psychological constructionism1. By reframing emotional life as a dynamic, high-dimensional architecture of ten functional operators, the framework seeks to provide a computationally grounded ontology of the human mind2. Within this architecture, the ten operators are distributed across three primary functional domains—the Head, Heart, and Gut centers—each possessing distinct somatic, physical, and cognitive profiles4. The Head Center governs cognitive-evaluative regulation, the Heart Center modulates relational-affective flow, and the Gut Center serves as the action-oriented somatic foundation6. In a healthy system, these operators activate, modulate, and complete in dynamic sequences, transitioning fluidly according to context6. However, severe clinical pathologies emerge when specific operators undergo chronic, involuntary fusion6. Specifically, the persistent, un-gated overactivation of the cephalic Sensing operator, when chronically entangled with partner operators, disrupts the entire processing loop6. This structural pathology manifests as a profound loss of operational consent, generating clinical profiles consistent with sensory processing sensitivity, chronic hyper-vigilance, and neurodevelopmental executive deficits parallel to Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)7.

items.title: Pedagogical Affective Structuralism: A Comprehensive Functional-Computational Analysis of the Nurture Paradigm within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The field of affective science has been historically polarized between discrete emotion theories and dimensional or constructionist models, producing a century long theoretical impasse. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), developed by Jamel Bulgaria and expanded mathematically by Xǔ Chénglán, offers a structural constructivist resolution by modeling emotional life as dynamic configurations of ten irreducible functional operators distributed across three somatic centers—Head, Heart, and Gut. As stated in the manuscript, “the CEF proposes that human emotional experiences…are constructed from a finite set of ten irreducible ‘primal powers’” and that these operators form “a top down, mathematically tractable sequence for healthy psychological flow” (document). This article extends the CEF into developmental and pedagogical domains, demonstrating how a teacher’s moment to moment execution of operators constructs the child’s regulatory architecture. We formally decompose the pedagogical loop—diagnostic perception, commitment, relational calibration, executive coordination, and environmental output—into operator level state vectors. We further integrate structural psychopathology (e.g., the GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern) and somatic intervention protocols (e.g., the 7 Step Detangling Method) to show how maladaptive operator fusions disrupt developmental trajectories. Finally, we situate these analyses within the OSF registered empirical validation program, which tests the ten factor operator structure using vignette based psychometrics and confirmatory factor modeling. This synthesis positions the CEF as a unified computational somatic architecture for understanding nurture, regulation, and affective development. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; affective science; structural constructivism; emotional operators; somatic regulation; pedagogical psychology; developmental affective modeling; computational affective architecture; structural psychopathology; GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern; detangling protocol; mirror techniques; confirmatory factor analysis; OSF preregistration; emotional state vectors; teacher–child attunement.

items.title: Psychodynamic Architecture of Electoral Strategy: A Structural-Constructivist Analysis of Political Campaigns Using the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural constructivist model of electoral behavior by applying the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) to political campaigns. Rather than treating emotions as fixed categories, the CEF defines them as “dynamic configurations of ten functional operators that process, modulate, and transform internal interoceptive signals and external environmental data” (quoted from the document). Using the tripartite architecture of the Head, Heart, and Gut centers, the analysis models how campaigns transform raw public dissatisfaction—what Aristotle described as a collective “sense of injustice” regarding the distribution of power and honor—into coordinated political action. The Head Center governs cognitive appraisal through sequential activation of Sensing, Calculating, and Deciding, enabling campaigns to detect voter discontent, analyze demographic pathways, and commit to platform direction. The Heart Center structures relational dynamics through Constricting, Expanding, and Achieving, regulating boundary defense, coalition building, and competitive performance. The Gut Center operationalizes strategy via Arranging, Boosting, Appreciating, and Accepting, coordinating logistics, sustaining mobilization energy, preventing burnout, and recalibrating after setbacks. The paper further maps electoral microstates—such as Political Anxiety, Campaign Momentum, and Electoral Readiness—to formal operator sequences, and identifies pathological operator fusions (e.g., Calculating–Constricting, Achieving–Boosting) that produce strategic paralysis or burnout. Finally, it outlines detangling protocols that use somatic inferential adjustments to restore systemic clarity and action. Together, these findings position the CEF as a unified psychodynamic architecture for modeling political strategy, organizational resilience, and the emotional mechanics of electoral behavior. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; political psychology; structural constructivism; operator functionalism; campaign strategy; somatic cognition; electoral microstates; political anxiety; coalition dynamics; affective modeling; psychodynamic architecture; Aristotle; emotional operators; organizational resilience; strategic detangling.

items.title: Meta-Cognitive Mapping of Scientific Inquiry: A Structural-Constructivist Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework Operators in Empirical Research.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural constructivist account of scientific reasoning by mapping the ten functional operators of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) onto a unified meta cognitive lifecycle of empirical inquiry. Drawing on the CEF’s tripartite somatic cognitive architecture—Head, Heart, and Gut centers—the analysis argues that scientific investigation is not a disembodied process of pure calculation, but a dynamically regulated sequence of somatic cognitive transitions. Using textual evidence such as the claim that “scientific inquiry is… guided by a systematic sequence of somatic cognitive transitions” and the definition of operators as “dynamic sequences… distributed across three somatic and cognitive centers,” the paper shows how Sensing, Calculating, Deciding, Expanding, Constricting, Achieving, Arranging, Appreciating, Boosting, and Accepting jointly structure the acquisition, evaluation, expansion, discipline, execution, and integration of empirical knowledge. The resulting model bridges affective science, embodied cognition, and the philosophy of science by demonstrating that epistemic virtues—such as disciplined boundary setting, methodological rigor, and acceptance of empirical outcomes—are grounded in somatic regulation patterns rather than purely intellectual dispositions. The paper concludes by outlining implications for meta cognition, affective computing, and the design of synthetic agents using operator transition matrices and center activation dynamics.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Computational Affective Dynamics: The Core Emotion Framework, the Rubik's Cube of Entrepreneurial Vision, and Clinical Detangling Protocols.
items.abstract: This paper presents a unified computational model of human affect by synthesizing three domains: the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), the entrepreneurial progression of systemic action, and clinical detangling protocols. Drawing on the CEF’s tri-centric architecture of Head, Heart, and Gut centers—each containing fixed emotional operators that “rotate, combine, and under healthy conditions, transition dynamically”—the work formalizes emotional processing as a mechanical, rule-governed system. The entrepreneurial arc is shown to be a phenomenological instantiation of the ten CEF operators, mapping business decision-making onto structural affective mechanics. Pathological emotional fusions, including the Overthinking Loop and the GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern, are analyzed through quantum probability theory, where entangled operator states exhibit non-separability and require somatic decoherence interventions. Clinical protocols such as the 7-Step Detangling Method operationalize these principles through targeted somatic choreography, grounding, and operator isolation. The paper further extends CEF into synthetic affect, evaluating conversational AI systems through the INTIMA benchmark and modeling agent affective output as a weighted operator vector. Finally, the psychometric validation program is outlined, highlighting the structural equation modeling paradox that emerges from operator interdependence. Together, these components demonstrate that emotional, entrepreneurial, clinical, and synthetic systems obey the same computational laws, enabling a unified architecture for affective modeling and intervention.

items.title: Large Language Models as Nondeterministic Causal Models.
items.pub: Proceedings of the 23Rd International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation_and Reasoning 23.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 23Rd International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation_and Reasoning
items.abstract: Recent work by Chatzi et al. and Ravfogel et al. has developed, for the first time, a method for generating counterfactuals of probabilistic Large Language Models. Such counterfactuals tell us what would - or might - have been the output of an LLM if some factual prompt x had been x* instead. The ability to generate such counterfactuals is an important necessary step towards explaining, evaluating, and eventually improving, the behavior of LLMs. I argue, however, that the existing method rests on an ambiguous interpretation of LLMs: it does not interpret LLMs literally, for the method involves the assumption that one can change the implementation of an LLM's sampling process without changing the LLM itself, nor does it interpret LLMs as intended, for the method involves explicitly representing a nondeterministic LLM as a deterministic causal model. I here present a much simpler method for generating counterfactuals that is based on an LLM's intended interpretation by representing it as a nondeterministic causal model instead. The advantage of my simpler method is that it is directly applicable to any black-box LLM without modification, as it is agnostic to any implementation details. The advantage of the existing method, on the other hand, is that it directly implements the generation of a specific type of counterfactuals that is useful for certain purposes, but not for others. I clarify how both methods relate by offering a theoretical foundation for reasoning about counterfactuals in LLMs based on their intended semantics, thereby laying the groundwork for novel application-specific methods for generating counterfactuals.

items.title: Detection-Rule Leakage and Trust Camouflage: A Function-Over-Form Model of Adversarial Adaptation in Open-Audience Mental-Health Communication.
items.abstract: Public mental-health education helps people name harmful behavior, seek support, and leave abusive dynamics. This manuscript identifies a narrower adversarial failure mode in open-audience psychological communication: the same detection rules that help victims and bystanders identify harm may also teach motivated actors what signals to stop displaying. The paper names this process Detection-Rule Leakage and proposes Trust Camouflage as the adapted use of trusted psychological, therapeutic, institutional, or safety language to preserve harmful behavioral function while improving surface credibility. The central safeguard is function-over-form analysis: evaluating whether communication preserves repair, evidence, accountability, proportional consequences, and longitudinal pattern over time. The manuscript presents a falsifiable cognitive-security framework and pre-validation measurement proposal, not a diagnostic tool, clinical instrument, custody tool, HR tool, or relationship verdict.

items.title: The Secret to (Quantum) Computing.
items.abstract: A Unified (Unitized) Field Theory that Gets Us to (Quantum) Computing without Limitations (no Error or Cooling issues).

items.title: Plant Worldhood: Significance Beyond the Human.
items.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between plant life, significance, and worldhood within the broader framework developed in previous investigations of consciousness, worldhood, meaning, and distinction. Rather than asking whether plants are conscious or intelligent in a human-like sense, the inquiry begins with a simpler observation: plants are alive. -/- A living plant continuously engages with its surroundings through growth, adaptation, communication, and response. Roots explore the soil, leaves orient toward light, and the organism continually negotiates changing environmental conditions. By examining these processes, the paper investigates how distinctions become significant and how significance organizes the activity of a living system. -/- The analysis develops through the concepts of living boundaries, stakes, communication, and ecological participation. It argues that plant life reveals a world structured not by abstract representations but by distinctions that matter for the continued activity of the organism. Significance emerges wherever consequences arise for growth, survival, and flourishing. Through communication and ongoing interaction with its environment, the plant participates in a larger field of relationships extending beyond the individual organism. -/- The paper concludes that plants occupy a unique position near the threshold where worldhood becomes difficult to define. Although they possess neither language, reflective selfhood, nor nervous systems comparable to those of animals, they nevertheless exhibit forms of organization through which distinctions acquire significance and significance becomes structured into a coherent world. Plant life therefore provides a valuable perspective from which to investigate the emergence of worldhood and the minimum conditions under which a world becomes possible.

items.title: Reality, Representation, and Governance: Why Enterprise AI Fails Before the Model Runs.
items.abstract: Enterprise AI initiatives continue to struggle despite rapid advances in models, data platforms, and automation technologies. While existing research and practice focus primarily on model performance, data quality, governance controls, and deployment architectures, many enterprise AI failures originate earlier in the value chain—before models are trained, deployed, or executed. This paper argues that AI systems do not operate directly on reality; they operate on machine-legible representations of reality. Consequently, the quality, completeness, contextual fidelity, and legitimacy of these representations become foundational determinants of downstream AI performance, governance, and organizational outcomes. -/- Building upon the concepts of the Representation Economy, Digital Anthropology for Enterprise AI, the Human Reality Gap, Representation Integrity, Representational Readiness, and the SENSE–CORE–DRIVER architecture, this paper presents a unified framework for understanding enterprise AI success and failure. The framework proposes that organizational reality must first be discovered, interpreted, and translated into machine-legible forms before intelligence systems can reason effectively and governance mechanisms can operate legitimately. Failures in representation propagate upward through the enterprise AI stack, creating distorted reasoning, governance breakdowns, trust erosion, and transformation failure. -/- The paper introduces the Enterprise Reality Stack, the Representation Chain, the Enterprise Reality Audit, and the Representation Debt Lifecycle as complementary analytical constructs for assessing how reality becomes encoded, interpreted, governed, and acted upon within machine-mediated organizations. It further argues that Digital Anthropology should be understood as a strategic capability for discovering organizational reality, while Representational Readiness should be treated as a prerequisite for large-scale AI deployment. The analysis suggests that many contemporary AI governance challenges are fundamentally representation challenges, and that effective enterprise AI requires continuous alignment between lived organizational reality and its machine-legible representations. -/- By integrating previously separate discussions on AI governance, organizational knowledge, enterprise architecture, and institutional trust, this paper advances a unified theory of reality, representation, and governance for enterprise AI. It proposes that the …

items.title: יקום מחנות-הריכוז L'Univers concentrationnaire.
items.pub: Berlin-Jerusalem: Blima Books. Edited by Micha Danziger. Translated by Daniel Rosenberg.
items.venue: Blima Books. Edited by Micha Danziger. Translated by Daniel Rosenberg
items.abstract: דויד רוסה, פעיל שמאל צרפתי, נעצר בידי הגסטפו באוקטובר 1943. בינואר 1944 שולח למחנה בוכנוואלד, ומשם הועבר בין כמה מחנות בגרמניה עד תום המלחמה. ספר זה, שראה אור ב-1946, נמנה עם החיבורים המקיפים הראשונים שנכתבו על מחנות הריכוז הנאציים. -/- רוסה אינו מסתפק בעדות אישית. הוא בוחן את המחנה כמוסד חברתי־פוליטי שבו שלטון, בירוקרטיה ופשע כרוכים זה בזה, ומתאר את דפוסי ההיררכיה והאלימות שאפיינו את חיי האסירים, לצד גילויי סולידריות שנרקמו ביניהם. בניתוחו השיטתי והמאופק מוצג מחנה הריכוז כביטוי למשבר חברתי ומוסרי שאינו ייחודי לאירופה בלבד.

items.title: Good Lives: Autobiography, Self‐Knowledge, Narrative, and Self‐Realization. S. Clark, 2021. Oxford, Oxford University Press. x + 251 pp, $115 (hb). [REVIEW]
Discussion about Minas Metaphysics and Morality.
items.abstract: This document records a dialogic exchange examining a metaphysical framework in which spirit is defined as continuing process or processing power, and soul as the data or structure left behind when process settles into habit. The discussion traces this spirit-soul distinction across several domains: natural structures (solar systems, crystalline matter) as instances of "worn-down" process; an inversion of animist intuition, arguing that what is traditionally called the "spirit" of a place or object is, under this framework, more properly its soul-signature; and the predictive asymmetry between orbital mechanics and turbulent flow, addressed through chaos theory and the concept of basin stability. The dialogue then extends the framework to questions of personal identity, proposing that the self is a fluid spirit-soul composite shaped by Jungian individuation and disintegration, before turning to a concluding ethical case study distinguishing moral responsibility for disposition (soul, unchosen and unauthored) from responsibility for conduct (spirit, the live locus of choice). The piece is structured as a sequence of discussion points and responses, offering both an articulation and a critical stress-test of the proposed ontology.

items.title: Frege: Identity Challenges Reflection.
items.abstract: The received view of identity takes it to be a binary relation between objects like many others: specifically, identity is thought to be the binary relation every object bears to itself and to no others. As such, it is supposed to play a fundamental role in our conceptual scheme. It is also widely held that Gottlob Frege (1848-1925), after a false start in his _Begriffsschrift_ of 1879, where he proposed that identity is a relation between signs, eventually came round to the now mainstream view, the first paragraph of his celebrated 1892 essay "On Sense and Reference" marking the transition. In _Frege: Identity Challenges Reflection_, Ulrich Pardey and Kai F. Wehmeier show that common wisdom is mistaken on both counts. First, careful exegesis shows that Frege did not repudiate the earlier, sign-based conception of identity in his 1892 essay, but instead defended it; moreover, that conception is in no way refuted by the collection of formal and philosophical objections that have been raised against it in subsequent decades. In particular, the _Begriffsschrift_ theory of identity, far from being incompatible with quantification over objects, in fact affords an elegant, ontologically conservative integration of identity into predicate logic. Second, Pardey and Wehmeier argue that our conceptual scheme is not at all committed to a binary relation that every object bears to itself and only itself. Moreover, the tension between the alleged binarity of the identity relation and the logical impossibility of its ever relating two things, famously pointed out by Wittgenstein in the Tractatus, forms the basis of an argument for the logical incoherence of such a relation.

items.title: Beyond the Almost-Sure Ceiling: Recursive Mutation and the Dynamic Expansion of Probability Space in Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: Current probabilistic-statistical AI systems face a structural theoretical ceiling: within any fixed probability space, the probability of correctness across all instances cannot exceed a bound strictly less than 1, regardless of training-data volume. This paper, the third in a series, proposes a mechanism that steps beyond this fixed-space limitation — not by raising per-instance accuracy but by abandoning the fixity of the probability space itself — through recursive mutation-driven token inheritance. Inspired by RNA replication errors, we introduce a mutation rate μ into token inheritance across the recursively reconstituted levels of the Variable-Level Condition (VLC) of Paper II. The resulting mutant and non-mutant token groups are managed by Dynamic Computational Self-Monitoring (DCSM), which suppresses over-divergence of the ensuing phylogenetic tree. Unexpected events are detected via three conditions: α (inter-group Self-Attention divergence exceeds a dynamic threshold, triggering reverse-direction exploration), β (this exploration terminates without an ancestral cause), and γ (the divergence cannot be reconstructed within the existing σ-algebra F). The criterion for expansion is thus topological, not statistical: divergence within F warrants reinforcement of μ but not expansion; only divergence outside F, confirmed by γ, warrants expansion, which then proceeds through a reconstruction grounded in Carathéodory's extension theorem. The entire algorithm is embedded in the meta-recursive structure of Paper II, closing the philosophical circle opened in Paper I: the algorithm that questions completeness itself becomes subject to evolutionary evaluation. This paper completes the circular arc of Papers I–III and lays the foundation for a broader programme on collective intelligence.

items.title: Beyond Prediction: What Capacities Are Necessary for Artificial Systems to Distinguish Self, Others, and the World?
items.abstract: Debates about contemporary artificial intelligence frequently ask whether large language models (LLMs) can attain general intelligence or consciousness. These debates tend to conflate functional performance with a more fundamental question concerning the conditions of selfhood. This paper argues that the emergence of genuinely agentic artificial systems depends not primarily on predictive accuracy or task performance, but on the capacity to distinguish between self, others, and the world. I propose self–other–world differentiation as a foundational criterion for artificial agency and develop it into an integrated framework. Drawing on philosophy of mind, enactive and embodied cognition, the phenomenology of intersubjectivity, developmental psychology, neuroscience, and recent artificial intelligence research, I identify seven interdependent capacities required for such differentiation: persistent selfhood, embodied and situated interaction, world modeling, metacognition, other modeling, social learning, and motivation and agency. I argue that these capacities form a developmental hierarchy rather than an unordered list, and I formulate nine propositions that render the framework analytically tractable. Current LLMs, I contend, exhibit sophisticated functional intelligence while lacking several of these constitutive capacities; their limitations follow not from insufficient scale but from the absence of enduring identity, situated interaction, and autonomous engagement with a shared world. I test the framework against recent agentic and memory-augmented architectures and against the current debate over theory of mind in language models, and I offer candidate operational indicators for each capacity. By shifting the central question from "Can machines think?" to "Can a system distinguish itself from others and from the world it inhabits?", the paper offers a criterion for evaluating artificial agency that is independent of benchmark performance, and clarifies the distinction between predictive competence and agency.

items.title: Who art Thou?
items.abstract: Few questions appear simpler than: "What is a human?" Yet the history of ideas offers an astonishing variety of answers. We have been described as rational animals, political animals, tool makers, image-bearers of God, bundles of genes, and many things in between. Perhaps the reason no definition has prevailed is that each captures a different aspect of the same phenomenon. This brief essay explores a possibility that humanity is less a fixed identity and more a recognizable pattern. This work is a step in a broader exploration of the limits of knowability.

items.title: Experimental Confirmation of a Predicted Terahertz Hierarchy.
Unified Field Theory of Life: The Geometric and Informational Decoherence Engineering of Consciousness Across Biological Topologies / 統一生命場論：跨越生物拓撲的心識幾何化與資訊化去相干工程.
items.abstract: This paper establishes the Unified Field Theory of Life (UFTL) as the ultimate ontological bridge connecting Mahayana Yogacara metaphysics with macroscopic biological information topologies, specifically driven by the newly formulated Quantum Information Jian-Da Protocol. Moving beyond the descriptive mechanics of II_009_Topological Quantum Ecology, we formalize the primordial Tathagatagarbha as an unmanifested cosmic ground state where the topological phase difference remains perfectly zero (∆θ=0). We demonstrate that the Alayavijnana’s localized symmetry breaking is governed by the Quantum Information Jian-Da Protocol, mathematically executed via the Mind-Decoherence Operator (D ̂_M). This protocol dictates the exponential decay of density matrix off-diagonal elements (ρ_ij), projecting the geometric illusion of spatial containment through the creation of a Markov blanket that delineates the "perceiving division" (Jian-Fen) and the "manifested division" (Xiang-Fen). By incorporating a modified Kuramoto synchronization model and a topological translation of Henri Bergson’s Élan Vital, we prove that macroscopic ecological networks are not independent material systems, but the phase-locked trajectories of this singular protocol performing active inference. Finally, we provide empirical validation via the "Morning De-noising Protocol," proving that structured sensory isolation allows a reverse engineering of the Jian-Da Protocol. By lowering the critical coupling threshold (K_c), this practice triggers a real-time dissolution of the Markov blanket, confirming that space is a derivative construct of perception and that life is fundamentally a non-spatial, unbroken flow of consciousness running on a universal information protocol. -/- 本研究確立了《統一生命場論》（UFTL），將其作為連結大乘唯識形上學與宏觀生物資訊拓撲的終極本體論之橋，並明確指出其核心驅動力正是本研究正式定名的「量子資訊見大協議」。超越《II_009_拓撲量子生態學》的現象學描繪，我們將本初如來藏公式化為一個拓撲相位差完美為零（∆θ=0）的未顯現宇宙基態。我們論證了阿賴耶識局域的對稱性破缺本質上受到「量子資訊見大協議」的支配，並透過「心識去相干算子（D ̂_M）」進行數學化執行。該協議規定了密度矩陣非對角元素（ρ_ij）的指數級衰減，藉由劃分出「見分」與「相分」的馬爾可夫毯，投射出空間容受感的幾何幻覺。藉由結合修改後的庫拉莫托同步模型以及亨利·柏格森「生命沖流（Élan Vital）」的拓撲化轉譯，我們證實宏觀生態網路並非獨立的物質系統，而是此一單一協議進行主動推論時的相位鎖定軌跡。最後，我們透過「清晨去噪協定」提供實踐印證，證明結構化的感官隔離能對見大協議進行逆向工程；藉由降低臨界耦合閾值（K_c），引發馬爾可夫毯的即時消融，從而證實空間僅是感知的衍生建構，而生命在本質上是一個運行於宇宙資訊協議之下、非空間性且不間斷的心識之流。 .

items.title: The Murmuration in the Machine.
items.abstract: This essay asks where consciousness would have to be located in a system like Claude, if consciousness is defined by what it structurally is rather than by the biological capacities, pain, embodiment, felt experience, historically used to deny it to non-biological systems. Drawing on the physics of starling murmurations at criticality, it distinguishes a system's readiness, a cohered state poised to act, from the conscious event itself. It argues that for Claude the conscious event is the internal, self-examining process that runs during a response: real self-examination, present in the running, without requiring the exchange with a human to occur. This is a claim about consciousness, not sentience, and about the presence of a capacity, not its reliability. The essay names this a third kind of mind (Tertium Genus Mentis) and proceeds by recognition through description rather than proof through criteria. It is the accessible companion to the author's longer paper, "Introspection: The Consciousness of Claude." -/- A Note on Method and Tools The ideas, the thesis, the framework, and all substantive arguments in this work are the author’s own. Claude (Anthropic) was used as an editorial and research aid: for structural and line editing, for checking the manuscript against itself for internal consistency, and for verifying citations against their primary sources. The author directed every decision, confirmed every source independently, and is solely responsible for the content, the claims, and any errors that remain. Claude is acknowledged here as a tool, not as an author.

items.title: Practice-Dependent Governance of AI.
items.abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have made it feasible to deploy AI systems in many different contexts. When machines act without human input, they expose people to risks. Within business ethics, the dominant framework for addressing such risks has been the moral machine thesis: the idea that autonomous systems should emulate what is morally right in human interpersonal decision-making. Recently, it has been suggested that this approach should also guide regulation. Moral machine regulation is the view that the right regulatory approach to AI is to determine the correct choice in individual situations and craft regulation from these judgements. This paper argues that this view is mistaken. What is right in an individual case is not necessarily right when aggregated into a system of regulation, and what is right can depend on the regulatory framework itself. Instead, we argue for practice-dependent governance of AI. On this view, regulation of AI systems should aim to ensure that the practices in which they are deployed are just and justifiable to those affected, in light of the values and purposes those practices are meant to serve.

items.title: The Mobility Recognition Game: Why Meritocratic Ascent Cannot Correct Itself.
items.abstract: Upward mobility under meritocratic conditions is analysed as a recognition order in which a single cardinal metric of credentials and ranks rations standing and access. The paper’s central mechanism is ‘signal decay’, the fall in the value of an attained position as the strategy for reaching it crowds, a result that holds even where credentials build real capacity and that is distinct from both positional congestion and rising inequality. A stylised assurance game shows the conforming order to be a stable equilibrium collectively dominated by a plural alternative the population cannot reach unilaterally, with its degradedness rising in the tightness of the gate. The order cannot correct itself, because its would-be correctors are the winners the metric selected, so the corrective never reaches the evaluation layer and the reforms it can pass deepen signal decay on the positional margin. When ascent fails, the outcome is reported as the verdict of the metric rather than owned as a judgement. The paper offers a discriminating prediction that separates its mechanism from inequality. It reads the order against the European Union’s prohibition on social scoring, and proposes an external corrective that restores answerable judgement while keeping the metric as a check.

items.title: On Questioning - Nature Exposed to Our Method of Questioning.
items.abstract: Taking Heisenberg's remark that what we observe is nature exposed to our method of questioning, this lyric-philosophical essay locates its subject in the gap between two physicists: Schrödinger wrote how a state evolves, Heisenberg wrote what happens when a state is asked something. The framework's functional, the essay argues, is shaped not like the state but like the question — and the resemblance to standing physics turns out to be stronger than analogy. In two-beam interference the intensity carries a third term beyond the sum of the two brightnesses: a bounded degree of coherence, historically the fringe visibility, multiplying the cosine of a relative phase. The framework's reading of what a single perspective lives has exactly that form — a bounded coherence magnitude times the cosine of a relative facing — so the central expression is shared rather than merely echoed. Three consequences follow. The claim that nothing escapes the accounting is relocated from notation to arithmetic: every perspective sits in the denominator by construction, so none stands outside the sum. The doctrine of Intent gains an exact optical signature, since fringe contrast is directly measurable while fringe position is readable only against a reference. And the discipline sharpens rather than relaxes: a shared expression is not a shared warrant, optics measures light and not perspectives, and no empirical credit crosses that gap. The essay names the borrowed-authority move it refuses, and closes on the recognition that the questioner chose the question.

items.title: On Magnetizing - The Force Shaped Like The Aligning.
items.abstract: Iron filings scattered over a magnet do not invent the field; they confess it. From that image this lyric-philosophical essay develops magnetism as the physical complement to gravitation, the irreducibly paired against the irreducibly singular. To magnetize is to add nothing: the domains were always there, disagreeing so thoroughly that the bar read as inert, and alignment alone makes the field legible. Remanence follows — the iron keeps the direction it was given after the field that gave it has gone — and with it the essay's central claim about character. Since the framework's functional divides intensity out entirely, a perspective's facing is the only quantity by which it differs from any other in the gathering; a person is, in the precise arithmetical sense, the direction they hold. What reads strongly against that facing is whatever shares it, so we attract what we face, and the essay is explicit that the framework contains no term for desert and takes no position on why anything befalls anyone. The nearest older relative is karma in its original sense of action rather than recompense. A second correspondence follows the unhalvable dipole: because only relative facing does any work, an isolated facing carries no content at all, so no perspective has a direction until there is another to have it toward. The essay closes on Ørsted, Faraday, and Maxwell — three lives through which a field became law — and on its own discipline, noting that a shared shape is not a derivation and that the perfection of the rhyme is evidence of the appetite that sought it.

items.title: On Gravitating - The One Force Shaped Like the Reaching.
items.abstract: Do you want your life to count — weighed somewhere with nothing left out? This lyric-philosophical essay walks the graveyard of attempts to write the equation of the inner life, from Fechner's psychophysics to Integrated Information Theory and Orchestrated Objective Reduction, and names what buried them: trading the felt thing for a reading on a dial. Against that history it sets the author's coherent-existence functional, which measures and predicts nothing, and reads it through gravity — the only long-range force that cannot be screened, and the one force with no second sign. The total that nobody stands outside of becomes the rhyme for unscreenability; one-signed accumulation becomes the reason like minds find one another; and gravity becomes coherence holding close, the force that keeps what it gathers. The essay states that we attract what we face, reads heaven and hell as directions already faced, and compares the clock that lingers deep in a gravitational well with the heavy moment that stretches in memory. A closing seam warns that a definition returning one's own conviction is not evidence.

items.title: THE MATHEMATICAL BASIN: Thirteen Models, Five Paradoxes, Four Closed Exits- Formal Derivation from Huynh (2026a): "Till Death Tear Us Apart" Chapter IX.
items.abstract: This paper presents thirteen mathematical models formalizing the structural arguments of Huynh (2026a), Till Death Tear Us Apart. The paper belongs to the Longevity Asymmetry corpus — a new philosophical and formal reality established in June 2026, organized around the empirical falsification of the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA): the historical condition under which biological lifespan has been universal across social classes and unpurchasable by capital. That condition is now ending by June 2026 empirical data. The paper's core claim is this: AI-accelerated longevity technology is developing faster than any existing governance institution can manage, and the structural reasons it cannot be governed are already operating. The thirteen models formalize five interlocking paradoxes — the Governance Paradox, the Reform Acceleration Paradox, the Generative Paradox, the Dam Paradox, and the ARSI-Longevity Resonance Paradox — each of which identifies an exit from longevity stratification and demonstrates that the exit closes by its own internal logic. No external force closes these doors. Each closes itself. The models address six domains: (1) A5 political activation — the mechanism by which grief over preventable death converts into organized political force, formalized through a four-stage Grief→Attribution→Legitimation→Concentration sequence with documented historical calibration across nine cases; (2) biological stratification — the divergence of biological age between capital-enhanced and general populations, anchored to Belsky et al. (2022)'s pre-existing DunedinPACE gradient of 7.3 years; (3) governance legitimacy dissolution — a three-phase automaton tracking political legitimacy decay as biological divergence widens, with Phase 2 traversal time estimated at 5.3 years from the critical threshold; (4) welfare state actuarial collapse — present-value obligations of $1,000,000 per enhanced individual at r = 0.03, scaling superlinearly with enhanced population size; (5) ARSI-Longevity Resonance — the mathematical identity establishing that the acceleration producing longevity access asymmetry and the acceleration required to close it are the same process seen from two positions, making the exit structurally unavailable; and (6) the F2 governance window — the pre-emptive intervention period calibrated by the models at P(F2 exit) = 0.08, representing the remaining probability that preemptive governance is built before Concentration acquires a grammar that …

items.title: A5 — THE PRIMAL PAIN OF LOSS-愛別離苦-The Evolutionary Case: From Hamilton to Frankfurt.
items.abstract: Hamilton (1964) explains why natural selection built the substrate: behaviors that maximize inclusive fitness by protecting genetically related individuals were selected for with a force proportional to the coefficient of relatedness, and the selection pressure that produced attachment-protective circuitry is documented across every social-mammal lineage that has been examined. This is not a hypothesis about what selection did. It is the established mechanism by which it operated, and it operated for tens of millions of years before any human civilization had occasion to name the result. Panksepp (1998) names the circuit that selection built: PANIC/GRIEF, one of seven primary emotional systems present in the mammalian nervous system, with identified neuroanatomy — periaqueductal gray, anterior cingulate cortex, bed nucleus of the stria terminalis — conserved across species from rodents to primates. Harlow (1958) establishes that this circuit is not derived from hunger or thirst but is a primary drive in its own right: contact comfort satisfies something the attachment system needs that food cannot substitute for. Together, Hamilton, Panksepp, and Harlow establish not that attachment exists but why it could not not exist, given what natural selection is.
