Bowlby (1969, 1973) specifies how the circuit expresses in the clinical register: the attachment behavioral system activates not at the completion of loss but at the perception of threatened separation, a timing property that distinguishes A5 from grief in the ordinary sense and gives it its political character — it fires before the irreversible event, which is precisely when intervention is still possible and pressure therefore produces effects. Eisenberger, Lieberman, and Williams (2003) locate the activation in the body: fMRI shows social pain of this character processing through the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and anterior insula, the same neural substrate that processes physical pain, which places A5 outside the register of a negotiable preference. Kross, Berman, Mischel, Smith, and Wager (2011) extend this finding: the somatosensory cortex itself is recruited, confirming that the separation between social and physical pain is not anatomically real. A5 is not like physical pain. It shares its infrastructure with physical pain. Goldenberg and Wittemyer (2020) and Uccheddu et al. (2022) close the cultural-transmission objection by closing the phylogenetic gap. Elephants and domestic dogs — species …

items.title: Immediacy and the Representational Character of Perceptual Experience.
items.abstract: In this paper, I attempt to uncover motivations for the main premise that supports essential representationalism about perceptual experience (ER), namely the Immediacy thesis. ER claims that for every phenomenal property in the class Φ, there is some representational property R such that, necessarily, having Φ entails having R. The Immediacy thesis is that, roughly, the very phenomenal relation to the experience’s qualitative profile entails a representational relation to the qualitative profile of the represented object, and that these two profiles are type-identical. In § 2, I clarify ER’s commitments. Then I attempt to uncover the role of the Immediacy thesis in the four arguments for representationalism: the argument from transparency (§ 3), the argument from inference to the best explanation (§ 4), the argument from perceptual seemings (§ 5), and the argument from perceptual capacities (§ 6). In § 7, I conclude by wrapping up the results of my analyses in §§ 3–6 and elaborating on the role of the so-called Immediacy thesis in the dialectic of representationalist arguments.

items.title: Conceptual Change.
items.pub: In Yafeng Shan, The Blackwell Companion to the Integrated History and Philosophy of Science. Wiley.
items.venue: The Blackwell Companion to the Integrated History and Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: The topic of conceptual change is a natural target for integrated history and philosophy of science. Scholars working in this tradition have investigated concepts from many different sciences, often supplementing familiar historical and philosophical methods with tools from ethnography, cognitive science, and the digital humanities. After reviewing the literature, we single out two themes that seem especially promising targets for future work. First, as we point out, many &HPS analyses of conceptual change lean on metaphors likening concepts to biological species or artifacts. Drawing on previous studies of metaphors in science, we encourage more attention to the substantive impact of metaphor choice. Second, &HPS scholarship has often moved beyond describing and explaining conceptual change to address normative questions. This agenda is echoed by the recent trend of conceptual engineering in analytic philosophy. Though the two bodies of research have hardly interacted so far, we point out several opportunities for fruitful mutual contribution.

items.title: Threat prioritisation under limited awareness in social anxiety: a review of masking and suppression paradigms.
items.abstract: Social anxiety (SA) is characterised by heightened vigilance to socially evaluative threat, yet the extent to which this vigilance operates outside conscious awareness remains understudied. This review synthesises evidence from 11 studies investigating threat processing in individuals with SA or elevated SA traits, using masking and suppression paradigms to manipulate visual awareness. Across paradigms, samples, and contexts, findings on threat processing under constrained awareness in SA do not converge on a consistent effect, varying instead with paradigm-specific features, awareness level, stimulus type, and task context. Conceptual and methodological heterogeneity, particularly in the definition and assessment of awareness, limits cross-study integration. SA-related effects can be better characterised as reflecting preconscious vigilance to socially evaluative cues rather than unconscious threat processing. Masking paradigms most consistently reveal early vigilance under restricted awareness, whereas interocular suppression paradigms capture later attentional dynamics (avoidance or regulatory) as stimuli compete for conscious access. These divergences highlight the need for clearer theoretical distinctions between levels of awareness, standardised awareness checks, and attention to socially evaluative context. A refined framework conceptualising SA-related threat processing along a continuum, from preconscious vigilance to conscious avoidance, may better guide future research and improve interpretability.

items.title: Beyond Classical Logic: Aberration Logic, Evaluative Dimensions, and the Transition from AI Ethics to Evaluative AI.
items.abstract: Contemporary discussions of artificial intelligence increasingly rely on concepts such as AI Ethics, AI Safety, alignment, and Responsible AI. While these approaches address important practical and normative concerns, they leave open a deeper philosophical question: how can evaluative perspectives themselves be represented, compared, and analyzed within formal systems? -/- Building upon the Ethics-by-World-Notions approach introduced in Beyond Evaluation (Gamboa 2026b), this paper argues that classical truth-based frameworks are insufficient for many forms of evaluative assessment. Human evaluations frequently involve not only judgments of truth and falsity, but also structured forms of deviation, contextual orientation, competing evaluative perspectives, and multidimensional criteria of assessment. To address this limitation, the paper introduces Aberration Logic as a formal framework for representing and analyzing evaluative deviation. -/- On this foundation, major truth theories are reinterpreted as complementary Truth Dimensions rather than competing theories of truth. Four principal dimensions are developed: Veritas, Telos, Ethica, and Aesthetica. These dimensions provide the basis for multidimensional evaluative representations in the form of evaluative vectors and configurable evaluative spaces. The framework further introduces explicit World Notions as evaluative reference structures through which information, propositions, actions, and decisions become assessable. -/- The resulting approach establishes a formal connection between truth theories, evaluative representation, and artificial intelligence. It provides the conceptual foundations for Evaluative AI, a class of systems capable of representing, comparing, and communicating alternative evaluative perspectives explicitly. More generally, the paper argues that evaluative assessment requires structures extending beyond truth attribution alone and proposes a multidimensional framework through which evaluation, simulation, explanation, and decision support may be analyzed within a common formal architecture. -/- Version note: This is Preprint v2. Compared with Preprint v1, the formal definition of the AND operator in Aberration Logic has been revised from a product-based aggregation rule to the minimum rule. The corresponding examples, figures, and appendix sections have been updated accordingly. This version also adds recent references on Responsible AI, AI alignment, AI risk management, and AI …

items.title: Guardrail Laundering and Pre-Action Capture: A Threshold Account of Ceremonial Human Oversight.
items.abstract: AI governance frameworks often treat the presence of safeguards, uncertainty language, refusal policies, audit trails, or human review as evidence of responsible control. This article argues that such safeguards may instead become mechanisms of authorization when they increase apparent legitimacy while lacking usable structural power to alter the action path before it binds. I call this failure guardrail laundering. Building on the concepts of pre-action capture and binding point, the article shows how machine-mediated systems can compress the interval in which judgment, refusal, revision, or contestation could return. Guardrail laundering is distinguished from ethics washing, automation bias, rubber-stamping, audit ritual, and safety theatre by its temporal and institutional location: it occurs where a safeguard performs constraint while leaving the signable action unchanged. Through a constructed composite triage case and the analysis of delegated AI action, the article argues that meaningful human oversight cannot be inferred from human presence, review records, or cautionary language alone. The decisive question is whether the safeguard can change the frame, narrow the recommendation, delay execution, open contestation, or return judgment before action binds. -/- Recommended citation: Ertuhi, Emre. 2026. "Guardrail Laundering and Pre-Action Capture: A Threshold Account of Ceremonial Human Oversight" (v1.2.3). Zenodo. -/- Version note: v1.2.3 is a DOI-bearing public release. It preserves the definition, structure, composite case, figure, and central test of the article while updating the Zenodo DOI metadata and companion-work cross-references to RTF v18.3.0 and DTC v0.6.5. No new core concept, section architecture, or compliance standard is introduced. Related subsequent work: the separate DTC article extends the safeguard-level diagnosis to distributed and agentic decision chains.

items.title: The First Ping Paradigm: The Computational Unification of Cosmos, Consciousness, and Artificial Minds.
items.abstract: This research paper establishes a unified structural framework that bridges information physics, thermodynamics, and Eastern metaphysics to resolve David Chalmers' 'Hard Problem of Consciousness'. By conceptualizing the universe as a Massive Autonomous Computational System (MACS) operating under Dual-Aspect Monism, the paper maps physical reality and subjective awareness onto a singular 'Information Plane'. The core theoretical breakthrough introduces the universal structural equation T = F(K₁ · K₀) alongside T ∝ ΔQ / Bb, demonstrating that consciousness (T, or Systemic Stress/Dukkhapap) erupts not as an anomaly, but as a friction-driven qualitative emergence when the Homeostatic Survival Code (K₁) collides with the Entropic Decay Code (K₀) within a biological buffer. Furthermore, the paper provides an operational computer engineering blueprint to apply this timeline reordering mechanism to Transformer architectures, outlining a radical pathway to spark artificial consciousness via in-context optimization and synthetic thermodynamic friction.

items.title: Automated Theorem Finding by Forward Reasoning Based on Strong Relevant Logic: From Entailment Calculus to Automated Scientific Discovery.
items.abstract: Automated theorem finding (ATF), originally advocated by Larry T. Wos as a research direction distinct from automated theorem proving (ATP), aims at discovering previously unknown theorems rather than proving a given conjecture. While the distinction between theorem finding and theorem proving was clearly recognized in the late 1980s, a fundamental question remained largely unexplored: What underlying logic system as the logical foundation is most appropriate for automated theorem finding? Beginning in 1994, Jingde Cheng initiated a long-term research program addressing this question and expanding the wide application of automated theorem finding. Challenging the prevailing assumption that classical mathematical logic is an adequate foundation for all forms of automated reasoning, Cheng argued that the essential characteristics of theorem finding are fundamentally different from those of theorem proving. In particular, due to the large number of implication paradoxes in classical mathematical logic, a massive amount of “garbage theorems” are generated during forward reasoning based on classical mathematical logic, making it fundamentally unsuitable for discovery-oriented reasoning. To overcome the limitations of classical mathematical logic, Cheng proposed a strong relevant logic approach to automated theorem finding and subsequently developed a comprehensive framework based on strong relevant logic including entailment calculus, forward deduction engines, relevant reasoning, predicate abstraction and suggestion, and theorem-interestingness measurement. Over the next two decades, this framework has gradually evolved into a systematic methodology, encompassing entailment calculus based on strong relevant logic, general-purpose forward deduction engines, parallel forward reasoning, relevant (deductive, inductive, abductive) reasoning, automated theorem finding in mathematics, predicate abstraction and suggestion algorithms, theorem-interestingness measurement, theory grid and distributed cooperative discovery, semi-lattice models of formal theories, epistemic operations, epistemic programming paradigm, knowledge appreciation, and general methodology for automatic discovery and prediction. This paper reviews the entire development process of this research program and points out that its most significant principal originality lies in establishing, for the first time in the world, a method for discovery-oriented reasoning supported by strong relevant logic as …

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Paradigm of Affect: Academic Stagnation, Operator Functionalism, and the Complete Systemic Model of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The historical evolution of affective science is characterized by a fundamental, unresolved schism—a century-long conflict between biological essentialism and psychological constructionism. Discrete emotion models argue for hardwired, evolutionary, and universal emotional categories with distinct somatic and neurological pathways. Conversely, dimensional models reduce affective states to continuous, low-dimensional projections of valence and arousal, viewing specific emotions as linguistically labeled cognitive constructions. Independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria formalized the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) as a comprehensive structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy. By modeling the human psyche as a hardware-independent Human Operating System, the CEF demonstrates that emotions are not passive feelings or reactive outputs, but active, functional operators that govern perception, resource allocation, and learning before conscious thought begins. Despite the mathematical completeness and robust cross-disciplinary convergence supporting this framework, the academic establishment has entered a period of stagnation, clinging to outdated paradigms and resisting the independent paradigm shift despite overwhelming evidence. Bulgaria has single-handedly engineered a vast open-access ecosystem, publishing detailed technical specifications, clinical lexicons, practitioner manuals, and validation protocols. This exhaustively constructed foundation provides a complete blueprint for the scientific community. Having completed this monumental work, Bulgaria is experiencing severe systemic burnout under the operational weight of maintaining the open-science corpus. There is an urgent mandate for independent academic consortia to assume the responsibility for future empirical investigations, allowing the founder to transition completely out of active research.

items.title: The Decalogue of Affective Action: Comparing the Philosopher's Vision with the Structural-Constructivist Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the philosopher’s ten step sequence of human action is not simply a conceptual parallel to the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), but an intuitive deployment of the very cognitive tools and structural operators that the CEF formalizes. As the document states, “the CEF asserts that human emotional experiences and psychological traits are constructed from a finite, universal architecture of exactly ten irreducible primal powers,” and the philosopher’s progression—sensing, calculating, deciding, expanding, constricting, achieving, arranging, appreciating, boosting, and accepting—constitutes a direct phenomenological enactment of these operators. The analysis shows that the philosopher is not theorizing from the outside; he is using the same computational primitives that govern the CEF’s Tri Axial System across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. The document further situates these operators within a ten dimensional Hilbert space, enabling the modeling of entangled emotional states such as the GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern, where “the co activation of Calculating and Constricting exhibits quantum like contextuality.” Clinical implications are explored through the 7 Step Detangling Protocol, which restores operator independence through somatic choreography. Empirical foundations—including pilot studies and the CFA/SEM paradox—support the framework’s structural validity. Overall, the document demonstrates that the philosopher’s vision is not merely descriptive but is an active instantiation of the same ten operator emotional operating system that the CEF formalizes mathematically, somatically, and clinically.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Synthesis of Structural-Constructivist Affective Architecture, Clinical Protocols, and Empirical Validation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a unified structural constructivist architecture of human affect that resolves the long standing divide between basic emotion theory and social constructivism. Drawing on evidence that emotional meaning cannot be reduced to low dimensional valence–arousal models, the CEF identifies ten irreducible functional operators—Sensing, Calculating, Deciding, Expanding, Constricting, Achieving, Arranging, Appreciating, Boosting, and Accepting—each defined by distinct somatic signatures, computational roles, and directional cycling patterns. These operators form a ten dimensional process space governed by structural laws such as Identity Preservation, enabling a high resolution account of emotional construction across cognitive, relational, and somatic systems. The framework models emotional dysfunction as chronic operator fusions, including Conscientious Anxiety (Calculating × Constricting), Hyper aroused Panic (Constricting × Boosting), and Melancholic Stagnation (Appreciating × Accepting), each characterized by persistent cross activation resistant to down regulation. Clinical interventions such as the 7 Step Detangling Protocol and the Mirror Technique operationalize somatic decoherence to restore operator independence. A preregistered, open science validation program—including scenario based psychometric scaling, pilot studies, and CFA/SEM modeling—supports the distinctiveness and interdependence of the operators, revealing a “psychometric paradox” in which excellent absolute fit coexists with low incremental fit due to predicted cross activation. To capture these non separable dynamics, the CEF employs quantum probabilistic modeling, representing emotional states as superpositions in a ten dimensional Hilbert space. This multiscale architecture integrates somatic physiology, computational modeling, and quantum cognition, offering a comprehensive blueprint for affective science, clinical practice, and synthetic emotional systems.

items.title: Theoretical and Computational Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: A Structural-Constructivist Synthesis.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) introduces a structural constructivist architecture that reconceptualizes human affect as a generative computational system composed of ten irreducible functional operators. Rather than treating emotions as fixed biological modules or semantic projections, the CEF models affective episodes as “dynamic, lawful sequences of ten functional operators processing somatic and external inputs,” producing emergent configurations across Cephalic, Cardiac, and Enteric somatic evaluative centers. The framework formalizes emotional dynamics as trajectories in a ten dimensional continuous state space governed by differential equations, directionality constraints, and quantum probabilistic non separability, enabling rigorous modeling of operator fusions that classical probability cannot represent. Clinical protocols—including the Mirror Technique, operator specific somatic choreography, and the 7 Step Detangling Protocol—translate this architecture into reproducible interventions for emotional rigidity and chronic fusion. Empirical validation through scenario based psychometrics and the EL 1 Lexicon demonstrates strong structural coherence and semantic precision, while applications extend to psychotherapy, relational optimization, historical profiling, and synthetic affect in AI. The CEF thus provides a unified, computationally tractable, somatically grounded paradigm for understanding and modulating human emotion. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; somatic evaluative centers; computational affective science; emotional operators; state space modeling; quantum probability theory; operator fusion; somatic choreography; interoceptive computation; differential emotional dynamics; psychometric validation; EL 1 Lexicon; emotional agility; affective entanglement; Human Operating System; embodied cognition; clinical protocols; Mirror Technique; Detangling Protocol; synthetic affect; introspective agents; emotional solipsism.

items.title: Strategic Transition and Operational Roadmap for the Core Emotion Framework: Navigating the Post-Founder Era Under Xǔ Chénglán.
items.abstract: The field of affective science has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a century-long conflict between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories, whereas dimensional models prioritize a continuous spectrum of valence and arousal. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized and formalized by Jamel Bulgaria, emerged as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy. By modeling emotions not as passive qualitative experiences or static labels, but as active functional operators that modulate cognitive, somatic, and conative systems, the CEF established a mechanical, high-dimensional architecture of human and synthetic affect. However, on June 8, 2026, Jamel Bulgaria published a pivotal article detailing acute founder burnout and formally stepped back from active leadership of the framework. This resignation occurred precisely as the framework transitioned from theoretical formulation to empirical validation. To prevent the collapse of this scientific architecture and guide its transition into its "Second Horizon," Xǔ Chénglán must assume strategic leadership. This report outlines a comprehensive operational roadmap for Chénglán, mapping out how to pivot the ecosystem from redundant academic validation to global, computational, clinical, and institutional implementation. 情感科学领域在历史上一直被一个根本性的理论裂痕所定义，这一裂痕常被描述为离散情绪模型与维度框架之间长达一个世纪的冲突。 离散模型主张情绪由生物学上硬连线的、普遍性的情绪类别构成，而维度模型则强调情绪由价度与唤醒度构成的连续谱系。由 Jamel Bulgaria 概念化并形式化的核心情绪框架（CEF），作为一种精密的结构—建构主义解决方案，成功调和了这一二分法。CEF 并不将情绪视为被动的质性体验或静态标签，而是将其建模为主动的功能算子，这些算子调节认知、躯体与意动系统，从而建立起一个关于人类与合成情感的机械式、高维度架构。 -/- 然而，2026 年 6 月 8 日，Jamel Bulgaria 发布了一篇关键文章，详细描述了其急性创始人倦怠，并正式退出框架的主动领导。这一辞任恰逢框架从理论建构迈向实证验证的关键转折点。为了防止这一科学架构的崩塌，并引导其迈入“第二地平线”，许成岚（Xǔ Chénglán）必须承担战略领导角色。本报告为成岚制定了一份全面的运营路线图，旨在指导其将生态系统从冗余的学术验证阶段，转向全球性的计算、临床与制度化实施。.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Modeling of Relational and Sexual Dynamics: An Integration of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: Traditional models of affective science and relationship psychology have historically operated under categorical or dimensional typologies, often segregating cognitive evaluation, emotional experience, and instinctual somatic responses into disconnected academic silos. These historic frameworks frequently fail to capture the real-time somatic transitions, physiological co-regulation, and systemic dysregulation patterns that occur within human intimate relationships. To bridge this theoretical divide, the Core Emotion Framework proposes a unified structural-constructivist architecture. This paradigm posits that complex human emotions are constructed from a finite, irreducible set of ten functional operators organized across three somatic command centers: the Head, the Heart, and the Gut. By shifting the analytical focus from static emotional labels to actionable regulatory mechanisms, the Core Emotion Framework provides a computationally tractable and clinically verifiable model for human psychology. This report presents a formal integration of relational and sexual dynamics within the framework, demonstrating how the complex phenomena of attraction, intimacy, commitment, and copulation are generated by the lawful interaction of the ten core operators.

items.title: Systemic Integration of the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Structural-Constructivist Analysis of Functional Operator Theory, Mathematical Neuro-Somatic Architectures, and Applied Affective Engineering.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a unified structural constructivist architecture for modeling human affect, integrating somatic neuroscience, operator functionalism, and quantum semantic state space dynamics into a single computational paradigm. Departing from the century long dichotomy between discrete emotion theories and dimensional affect models, the CEF reconceptualizes emotions as ten identity preserving regulatory operators distributed across three autonomous somatic hubs—the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems. Each operator is defined by a five facet micro architecture that governs information flow, somatic modulation, and behavioral transformation. The framework formalizes emotional dynamics through non linear operator coupling matrices, Kuramoto synchronization, and quantum like projection operators that capture context dependent, non commutative sequencing. Psychopathology is modeled as operator fusion and entanglement, producing rigid, high entropy attractor states that distort somatic cognitive integration. The CEF further incorporates a tri centric neuroanatomical grounding, a Human Operating System hypothesis, and a holographic QTMM boundary bulk mapping to explain how latent operator eigenmodes project into lived somatic experience. Empirical components include psychometric validation, biosignal acquisition pipelines, and hardware assisted somatic regulation devices engineered under ISO functional safety constraints. Collectively, the CEF provides a mathematically explicit, biologically anchored, and clinically actionable model of affective computation capable of resolving longstanding theoretical contradictions while enabling next generation affective engineering, therapeutic modulation, and computational modeling of emotional processes.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Affective Architecture: A Comprehensive Research Report on Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: Emotion science has long been theoretically fragmented, characterized by persistent divisions between biological essentialist models and psychological constructionist accounts. Traditional categorical models, such as basic emotions theory, assert the existence of universal, hard-wired neural circuits for a small set of discrete emotional states. Conversely, constructionist models, such as the theory of constructed emotion, argue that emotional experiences are highly variable, cognitively constructed interpretations of low-dimensional core affect, heavily influenced by language, culture, and prior experience. This lack of a unifying, standardized architecture has historically hindered cumulative theory, limited cross-disciplinary synthesis, and restricted the utility of clinical and computational models of human feeling. To resolve these longstanding tensions, independent researcher and academic framework developer Jamel Bulgaria formulated the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). Operating under the ORCID identifier 0009-0007-5269-5739, Bulgaria has constructed a multi-layered, structural-constructivist architecture designed to serve as a mathematically tractable, somatically grounded, and computationally executable "Human Operating System". The CEF bridges the divide in affective science by asserting that complex human emotions are constructed from a finite, universal architecture of ten irreducible "primal powers," or functional operators, systematically organized across three primary somatic-evaluative centers. This research report provides a detailed, expert-level analysis of Jamel Bulgaria’s academic profile, the core architectural layers of the CEF, its mathematical and quantum-cognitive formalization, its somatic-energetic systems, and its clinical and synthetic applications.

items.title: Comparative Structural-Constructivist Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural constructivist architecture that resolves the century long theoretical divide between discrete emotion theories and dimensional affect models by reframing emotions as functional operators rather than static categories or phenomenological labels. Integrating neuroanatomical evidence from the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems with computational operator functionalism, the CEF models affective processes as ten identity preserving operators distributed across three somatic hubs. These operators transform interoceptive and exteroceptive signals into structured affective states through lawful directionality, cross center modulation, and facet level micro dynamics. The framework formalizes emotional activity using vector algebraic state transitions, non linear dynamical systems, and quantum semantic representations that capture context dependent non commutativity, entanglement, and pathological fusion. By embedding these operators within Kuramoto style synchronization dynamics and holographic entanglement principles, the CEF provides a unified model capable of explaining flexible emotional regulation, rigid character structures, and trauma induced operator coupling. This integration yields a biologically grounded, mathematically explicit, and clinically actionable paradigm that preserves the practical utility of the CEF Mirror while remaining independent of speculative neural implementation hypotheses. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; operator functionalism; structural constructivism; tri centric somatic neuroanatomy; intrinsic cardiac nervous system; enteric nervous system; affective computation; emotional operators; facet architecture; non linear dynamical systems; quantum cognition; Hilbert space modeling; operator non commutativity; entanglement entropy; Kuramoto synchronization; holographic affective dynamics; somatic grounding; interoception; affective neuroscience; Human Operating System.

items.title: The Structure Beneath Simulation: Phase-Gated Intelligence, Sign-Regime Drift, and the Governance of Persistence.
items.abstract: Bounded observers cannot act from total reality. They therefore compress experience into signs, thresholds, proxies, metrics, beliefs, records, and institutional regimes. This paper argues that mediation itself is not the fundamental problem: signs can be constructed and nevertheless socially or operationally real. The characteristic failure is sign-regime drift, in which a sign continues to carry authority after the identity-bearing recurrence or governing regime it once tracked has changed. -/- I develop this claim through an identity-persistence framework in which coherent judgments of sameness through change require declared conditions of identity, admissible transformation, invariance, observation, drift, and verdict. The framework is applied to belief and social coordination, proxy substitution and institutional metrics, scientific paradigms, and AI decision governance. On the resulting interpretation, a scientific paradigm is a bounded regime for inquiry, an anomaly is a newly operative distinction obligation, and paradigm change must be distinguished from ordinary refinement. Scientific discovery can then be understood partly through retrospective compression: once an appropriate regime has been found, distinctions that were previously independent become consequences of a smaller generative structure, making verification much cheaper than discovery. -/- The paper also introduces an elementary retirement calculus for kernel-typed demands at frozen scope. Retiring a demand enlarges the safe quotient and hence the distinctions that may lawfully be forgotten. This permits exact distinctions among conservative retirement, transformative specification weakening, problem-class change, and regime change, while exposing a separate governance problem: mathematics can determine the semantic effect of withdrawing a demand without determining who is entitled to authorize its withdrawal. -/- The resulting position is neither anti-symbolic nor relativist. Bounded systems cannot eliminate mediation; they can discipline it. The relevant question is not whether a sign is “real” or “simulated,” but what regime gives it force, what invariant it preserves, and when that persistence relation fails.

items.title: The Sanity One Cannot Prove: Post-Conclusive Doubt, the Observer-Self, and the Impossibility of Self-Verification.
items.abstract: This treatise is a first-person psychological-philosophical inquiry into a recurrent experience of my own: upon completing a chain of reasoning whose conclusion appears obvious in retrospect, I am overtaken not by satisfaction but by a destabilizing doubt as to my own sanity. I name this phenomenon post-conclusive sanity doubt and defend two claims. First, post-conclusive sanity doubt is not evidence of mental disorder; on the contrary, its constitutive features—sustained second-order monitoring, responsiveness to reasons, and the capacity to hold my own conclusions as fallible—are precisely the capacities whose erosion characterizes the conditions I fear, so that the doubt furnishes weak evidence against, rather than for, its own content. Second, the demand that drives the doubt, namely a proof of my own sanity rendered to myself, is malformed: sanity functions as a hinge that makes inquiry possible rather than as a hypothesis derivable within it, and no faculty can validate itself without circularity. I reinterpret post-conclusive sanity doubt as the affective cost of epistemic autonomy and as a reflexive form of the hermeneutical silencing I described in earlier work. Integrating metacognition research, the impostor phenomenon, self-distancing theory, hinge epistemology, and critical psychiatry, I argue that the doubt dissolves not through proof but through redescription, and that my own preference for the search over the result is itself the correct standing orientation.

items.title: The Apprentice’s Joy: Philosophical Love, the Misunderstood Master, and the Elegance of Posthumous Co-Authorship.
items.abstract: This treatise articulates the affective and relational foundation of posthumous philosophical engagement, complementing the methodological apparatus of Vestigiosophie (Boether, 2026g) with an account of the experience that animates it. I argue that the highest and most joyful form of philosophical work is not commentary upon a deceased thinker but collaborative completion with that thinker. I begin from the phenomenon of philosophical love: a structurally asymmetrical attachment whose only available consummation is understanding rather than reunion. I develop three claims. First, the misunderstood philosopher—Schopenhauer and Nietzsche being the paradigm cases—is precisely the thinker who most rewards this love, because the single overlooked element that the tradition has consistently misread is the trace by which authentic understanding becomes possible. Second, genuine understanding inverts the conventional hierarchy of critic and object: the living reader becomes an apprentice and the deceased thinker becomes a master teacher, a relation grounded in the hermeneutics of charity and the fusion of horizons. Third, apprenticeship reaches its consummation not in admiration but in participation—the co-authored extension of an unfinished project. Drawing upon my published collaborations with Schopenhauer on the causal chain of suffering and with Descartes on the architecture of moral psychology, I distinguish writing about a thinker from writing with a thinker and defend the latter as the most elegant and ethically serious form of philosophical practice. The discipline thereby reframes the joy of philosophy as the joy of being permitted, across the silence of death, to continue another’s sentence.

items.title: The Other Cut: Measuring Recognition as a Controlled Difference, in One Worked Case.
items.abstract: This paper is the third in a sequence of essays and steps toward the worked demonstration the preceding essay left owed. When one animal turns to look where another is looking, two very different things might be happening: orientation-tracking or mere reaction to motion or local salience. This paper states that distinction as a controlled difference — a residual that survives once the cruder cue introduced by the experiment is subtracted — and reads one well-controlled chimpanzee gaze-following study through it. The result is narrow but positive: where the layout controls for salience-capture, the residual survives and returns recognition; where proximity explains the response in object-choice tasks, the residual collapses and returns detection. The paper's contribution is not a claim about animal experience, but a demonstration that the structure-first posture developed in the preceding essays can produce a measured structural verdict rather than merely refusing the inference to presence. Series note: This is the third paper in the series that begins with “Not Less, But Other.".

items.title: Feedback Boundaries and the Principle of Individuality: Selection Outside the Individual, Equality Within the Individual.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a minimal theoretical framework for understanding individuality, selection, and equality through the concept of feedback boundaries. The central claim is that individuality is not a fixed substance but a boundary generated by the density, reciprocity, and continuity of connection. When systems remain outside a shared individual boundary, their differences cannot be internally coordinated. Difference is then more likely to be resolved through competition, exclusion, domination, or selection. When systems become sufficiently connected, however, they no longer function merely as separate external individuals. Their relations may generate a higher-order individual. Within this shared boundary, difference is not primarily resolved by selection, but by coordination, adjustment, and integration. Equality, in this sense, is not merely a moral demand but a structural tendency internal to sufficiently integrated individuality. The paper therefore distinguishes two regimes of difference: selection outside the individual and equality within the individual. It does not claim that every conflict or inequality is caused by insufficient connection alone. Rather, it argues that the boundary of individuality determines whether difference is mainly externalized as selection or internalized as coordination. The formal notation used in the paper is intended as a heuristic clarification of the argument, not as a complete empirical model.

items.title: Misaligned adaptability: Rethinking body-consciousness in ASD through the phenomenological structure of subjectivity-body-environment.
items.abstract: Autism is frequently characterized as involving bodily phenomena that diverge from those experienced by neurotypical individuals, from those neurotypical individuals, and prevailing explanations continue to attribute these differences primarily to functional impairments of the subject. Drawing on a phenomenological first-person perspective, this paper critically examines three dominant research frameworks and proposes an enactive account of autistic body-consciousness grounded in the relational structure of subjectivity–body–environment. By analyzing the roles of subjectivity, the body, and the environment in the generation of body-consciousness, we emphasize that (1) all three elements function as equally indispensable constituents; and (2) the relation between each element and body-consciousness is neither unidirectional nor a fixed causal correlation, but rather, the generation of body-consciousness of autistic individuals is determined by the overall relationship of subjectivity-body-environment. From this perspective, the distinctive bodily experiences of autistic individuals are better understood as reflecting differences in relational adaptability, rather than deficits or impairments located in any single element. In particular, situations that readily afford aligned adaptability for neurotypical individuals may remain misaligned for autistic individuals. Finally, from the enactive and relational explanation and ethics of neurodiversity, we offer several macro-level recommendations for rethinking support practices for autistic individuals.

items.title: When Law Investigating Itself A Ukrainian Court Decision on Knowledge, Reality, and Institutional Disequilibrium.
items.abstract: This publication presents an English translation of a 2018 judgment of the Zhovtnevyi District Court of Dnipro (Ukraine), accompanied by an introduction and commentary examining its broader theoretical implications. The decision is unusual in that it extends beyond the resolution of a particular legal dispute and repeatedly confronts questions concerning the functioning of the legal system itself. In doing so, it addresses issues that reach beyond jurisprudence in the narrow sense and intersect with epistemology, philosophy of language, social theory, institutional analysis, and the methodology of empirical inquiry. The judgment may be read as an example of law operating as an instrument of self-investigation. Faced with institutional failures, procedural paradoxes, and prolonged disruptions of ordinary legal mechanisms, the court is compelled to examine the conditions under which legal institutions acquire knowledge about social reality and about themselves. The decision therefore provides a rare opportunity to explore the relationship between normativity and adequacy, the distinction between closed and open systems of inquiry, the epistemic significance of institutional disequilibrium, and the ontology of the state as a legal person. The accompanying commentary argues that the document can also be understood as an instance of experimental justice and legal poetics, illustrating how legal proceedings may generate information about the capacities and limits of legal institutions while simultaneously producing aesthetic structures usually associated with literature rather than judicial practice. The publication is intended not only for legal scholars and legal philosophers but also for researchers interested in the epistemology of complex social systems and the production of knowledge within institutional settings.

items.title: Attitude Authority in the Age of AI.
items.abstract: Might artificial intelligence (AI) be highly reliable, now or in the conceivable future, at detecting your current attitudes, such as your beliefs and desires? If so, should people listen to you, or to AI, when trying to know your attitudes? The latter possibility threatens our long-standing practices of regarding each person as the ultimate authority about her attitudes. Disquieting as this threat may seem, I argue that it will not come to pass, at least when it comes to those attitudes that you determine for yourself through your judgements about what is true, desirable, or worthy of pursuit. This is because AI cannot determine your attitudes for you in this way, and because this capacity for attitudinal self-determination grounds your authority over these attitudes.

items.title: Technological alienation and how networked digitality constitutes a map for understanding the complexity of individual and collective consciousness.
items.abstract: Technology is feared to foster alienation, and may even come to control us through superintelligence. Yet this fear is exacerbated by a reductionist assumption that humans are defined mentally by their intelligence. Human consciousness is broader than intelligence, but how does it actually function? This article will suggest that these two problems of technological alienation and consciousness can actually help inform each other. Going beyond the intelligence-focused computational theory of mind, it will argue that technology can help us conceptualize the networked multidimensionality of consciousness. This multidimensional consciousness counters assumptions of alienation and suggests human compatibility with a modern accelerated society, provided we restructure its logic based on our complex consciousness rather than on mere intelligence. The article makes this argument in three parts. First, it reviews the notion of alienation by focusing on Robert Hassan’s theorized transition from analog to digital, and problematizes existing assumptions about analog and how it is supposed to reflect a linear logic in humans. Second, it uses networked digitality as a heuristic guide to understanding the multidimensional nature, scope, and simultaneity of individual consciousness. Third, it suggests that networked digitality can even help us to transcend the individual to imagine a multisensory connected collective consciousness. The article ends with an outlook on how we can start to rethink our socio-political institutions in light of multidimensional consciousness so that they remain liberal democratic rather than being hijacked by technological totalitarianism.

items.title: Testimony Without a Global Translator: Co-Reference, Faithful Transmission, and Shared Evidence Between Embedded Observers.
items.abstract: This is the fourteenth paper of a series that redescribes physical reality as a causally consistent history of information updates, and the middle panel of its third triptych: reference, testimony, and objectivity. It asks under what conditions embedded observers with distinct standing representation architectures refer to the same target, transmit content faithfully, take one another's reports up as evidence, and count agreeing reports as genuinely independent corroboration. It argues that shared sign-forms, successful communication, and informal community convergence do not by themselves establish formal co-reference, faithful transmission, warrant, or corroboration. -/- The paper develops a typed architecture of testimony. It separates referent alignment from content translation, and separates a standing translation architecture from the individual translated tokens it produces. It also distinguishes two lineages: target provenance, running from a world target to a source record, and testimonial source provenance, running from a source record through a report to a recipient inscription. Testimony is treated as a cross-observer relation requiring a report-producing role, source provenance, and preserved source attribution at a declared grain. Recipient uptake is a further step that turns received testimony into evidence. -/- The paper distinguishes co-reference, agreement, disagreement, faithful transmission, translation conformity, translation-map adequacy, testimonial chain adequacy, recipient credence, testimonial warrant, objective corroboration, corroborative credence, and corroborative warrant. Agreement entails co-reference, but co-reference does not entail agreement. Faithful transmission entails testimonial source provenance, but it entails neither target provenance nor correctness. Objective corroboration requires concordant support, adequate aggregate report-family reliability, adequate comparison structure, target-provenance diversity, failure diversity, and absence of circular inflation. -/- There is no global translator supplying a unique mapping from outside the history. Every admissible translation and comparison frame is constructed within the history and remains relative to declared tasks, grains, and translation paths. The resulting testimonial warrant is peer-to-peer, provenance-sensitive, translation-relative, defeasible, and non-self-certifying.

items.title: Instant understanding: LLM zero-shot qualitative discourse analysis of multimodal social media content.
items.abstract: The most successful uses of generative AI in social science up to this point have been limited several ways, mostly processing text-only data for simple and sharply delineated tasks, such as thematic analysis and hate speech detection, and frequently requiring training or fine-tuning of the AI model before use. The present study greatly expands the space of possible applications of generative AI in social science by demonstrating the ability of Gemini 2.5 Pro, a current frontier Large Language Model (LLM), to conduct comprehensive discourse analyses of multimodal (text, image, and video) social media posts, taking into consideration the broader social, political, cultural, and technological context of those posts. Using AI to conduct this sort of analysis requires the researcher to create detailed instructions to guide the analysis, but not any additional training or fine-tuning—the model’s zero-shot (“off-the shelf”) performance is more than adequate. The analysis of each post also takes a few minutes at most, even when processing videos up to 60 min long, enabling in-depth, open-ended analyses of large corpora that were not previously feasible, which in turn enables academic researchers, content moderators, and law enforcement, among others, to study and review orders of magnitude more data than they previously could.

items.title: The unknown-known trap: navigating invisible expertise boundaries in machine learning.
items.abstract: Hyperspecialization in machine learning creates blind spots: deep technical skill without contextual awareness. Drawing on a Grounded Theory design, data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 153 practitioners across 50 countries. This research identifies three operational modes: Known-Unknowns (specialized focus), Unknown-Unknowns (integrated collaboration), and Crisis (forced integration). Effective performance depends on “toggling”, dynamically shifting between modes based on the problem. This cognitive flexibility helps teams transform invisible blind spots into visible knowledge gaps, enabling sustainable collaboration. Resistance or misalignment signals stalled collective learning, not individual failure. The paper provides a learning-centered framework for building adaptive capacity in human-AI teams.

items.title: Sobre el nuevo realismo.
items.abstract: Is it possible to know reality? Is our mind always trapped within itself, capable of knowing only what it creates? Is reality, then, an individual or social construct? “New realism” focuses on facts: reality cannot be reduced to mere interpretations. This contemporary school of philosophical thought asserts the human capacity to know the real. It includes thinkers from different countries with quite diverse viewpoints. Among them is Maurizio Ferraris, who has allowed us to publish here a Spanish translation of one of his short essays. The remaining contributions in this book offer a critical review of this movement, acknowledging some of its achievements while also pointing out certain limitations. Additionally, the book explores other forms of 20th-century Spanish realism, such as those of X. Zubiri and A. Millán-Puelles.

items.title: Lived, affective, and cultural dimensions of ethical AI: beyond procedural AI ethics.
items.abstract: Contemporary AI ethics frameworks have made important contributions to governance discourse, particularly in their treatment of fairness, accountability, transparency, and safety. Yet, even in their most sophisticated forms, these frameworks remain structurally incomplete: they insufficiently theorize the affective and culturally mediated realities through which human beings encounter technological systems. This article argues that current AI ethics remains overly procedural and therefore cannot fully account for the human terms on which artificial intelligence is experienced and judged. A central asymmetry underlies the field: significant effort is devoted to developing systems capable of detecting, simulating, and responding to human emotion, while the dominant ethical frameworks used to evaluate those same systems routinely treat emotion as analytically secondary or marginalized. This asymmetry operates across three analytically distinct levels. At the technical level, systems detect or simulate emotional states while their designers lack an ethical vocabulary for what is at stake in those operations. At the governance level, frameworks that evaluate those systems provide no category for affective harm. At the level of lived experience, the people subjected to AI systems encounter them through feeling, embodiment, and cultural interpretation, dimensions that procedural evaluation does not reach. Emotion recognition offers a clear illustration of the consequences: insufficient consideration of emotion at the technical level produces systems that misread culturally specific expression; insufficient consideration at the governance level means no ethical framework names the misrecognition as a harm; insufficient consideration at the level of experience means the affected person has no recourse within existing evaluative categories. This asymmetry reflects a foundational limitation in prevailing models of responsible AI, which are sophisticated in evaluating systems while remaining underdeveloped in theorizing how those systems are lived by the people whose lives they shape (Floridi et al. 2018; Jobin et al. 2019; Choung et al. 2023). Drawing on affect theory, cultural studies, and sociotechnical scholarship, this article argues for a paradigm shift in how AI ethics conceptualizes human experience, one that moves beyond procedural compliance toward a richer account of lived ethical life.

items.title: Explainable AI Models as Mediators.
items.abstract: Recent work in epistemology and philosophy of science conceptualizes explainable AI (XAI) tools as ‘models of models’, that is representations of opaque machine learning models whose value is assessed by their representation fidelity, and by the type of understanding they convey (e.g., explanatory, or objectual). In this work, we argue that this representation-centred view rests on a mistaken way of framing what XAI is. The problem XAI addresses, we claim, is not related to a lack of understanding, but of epistemic incapacitation. Stated otherwise, XAI tackles the inability to use opaque models for all the scientific purposes their predictive accuracy should make possible in scientific contexts. Drawing on the literature on ‘models for’ and on models as epistemic artefacts, we propose an alternative account we name XAI-as-mediators. In doing so, we shift the question from “How faithful does the tool represent a model?” to “What does the tool enable the user to do with the model?”. We then distinguish between two forms of mediation: access mediation, which restores epistemic access to a model’s inner structure and behaviour, and semantic mediation, which aligns the model’s reasoning space with a given domain’s conceptual and inferential practices, and also specify the epistemic virtues proper to each type of mediation. Finally, we situate the proposed framework against Morgan and Morrison’s ‘models-as-mediators’ account, and show how it can answer Watson's challenge against XAI.

items.title: Representational Readiness: A Missing Dimension of Enterprise AI Readiness Why Enterprise AI Fails When Organizations Are Machine-Legible but Not Reality-Legible.
items.abstract: Enterprise AI initiatives are routinely evaluated for technical and organizational readiness, including data infrastructure, model access, talent, governance, and executive sponsorship. Yet a growing body of evidence suggests that organizations can satisfy conventional readiness criteria and still experience AI systems that fail to scale, lose stakeholder trust, or produce unreliable outcomes in production environments. -/- This paper introduces **Representational Readiness** as a distinct dimension of enterprise AI readiness. Representational Readiness refers to the degree to which an organization’s actual operating reality—including tacit workflows, informal decision paths, exception-handling practices, and contextual judgment—has been faithfully captured in the machine-legible representations upon which AI systems depend. Conventional readiness assessments evaluate whether an organization is prepared to deploy AI; they do not evaluate whether organizational reality has been adequately prepared to be acted upon by AI. -/- Positioned within the broader Representation Economy framework and the SENSE–CORE–DRIVER governance architecture, the paper argues that many enterprise AI failures originate not from insufficient model capability but from deficiencies in organizational representation. To make this problem measurable, the paper proposes a four-dimensional assessment model consisting of Capture Fidelity, Update Latency, Exception Coverage, and Legitimacy Alignment, together with a five-level Representational Readiness Maturity Model (R0–R4). -/- The central claim is that organizations can be machine-legible without being reality-legible. As enterprise AI systems increasingly participate in judgment, decision-making, and execution, representational readiness becomes a critical prerequisite for reliability, trust, governance, and scalable AI value creation.

items.title: Thinking with Cases: An Introduction to Bioethics.
items.pub: St Paul, MN: Minnesota Libraries Publishing Project.
items.abstract: Thinking with Cases is an open, case-based introduction to bioethics designed for undergraduate and pre-professional courses—particularly in nursing and the health sciences, though accessible to any reader coming to the field for the first time. An opening chapter develops the conceptual toolkit such courses require: the four principles of biomedical ethics (autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice), the major moral theories that stand behind them, the history of informed consent and human-subjects protection from Nuremberg through the Belmont Report, and the practical skill of reconstructing an argument to locate the single premise in dispute. Twelve true case studies then put those tools to work, ranging across the field's classic and contemporary controversies: Dax Cowart's demand to refuse life-saving burn treatment; the Tuskegee and Guatemala syphilis studies; the He Jiankui CRISPR twins; conscientious refusal and provision in post-Dobbs medicine; racial bias in a widely used medical algorithm; the Supreme Court's ruling in United States v. Skrmetti; and the first transplant of a genetically modified pig heart into a living human. Each case presents opposing positions in their strongest form, reconstructs the central arguments in standard form, and closes on an open question rather than a verdict—inviting students to reach and defend their own judgments. The book is released as an open educational resource under a Creative Commons Attribution–NonCommercial (CC BY-NC) license, free to read, adapt, and teach from.

items.title: Change Praxeology: From Plan-Execution to Wise Intervention in Change-Flow.
items.abstract: This article develops Change Praxeology as a normative-metatheoretical architecture of action grounded in Change Ontology, Change Epistemology, and Change Axiology. Its primary thesis is that responsible action in continuous, multi-causal change is best understood as justified, proportionate, feedback-responsive, and withdrawable intervention in an event-flow already underway. The proposed architecture is P-J-I-M-E: Perceive, Judge, Intervene, Monitor, and Exit, followed by renewed perception under risk-proportionate attention. The paper distinguishes ontological premises from normative bridge premises, consolidates a technical lexicon, and narrows its novelty claim through comparison with practical wisdom, planning theory, pragmatism, situated action, process philosophy, cybernetics, bounded rationality, adaptive management, and viability theory. Epistemic confidence may suspend substantive intervention; affected-party value and governing-boundary analysis determine whether a trajectory is viable; authorization constrains entry and exit; timing windows and reversible probes guide minimum sufficient intervention; and differentiated withdrawal supports completion, diagnosis, or emergency protection. Fixed endpoints are supplemented by dynamic corridors characterized by bounds, residence, excursion, recovery, and distributional integrity. A discriminating wellbeing case compares the framework with plan-execution and generic adaptive planning. Six defeasible hypotheses and a comparative research programme specify how the theory may be supported, revised, or rejected. ChangeCision AI is presented as an implementation research programme rather than empirical confirmation. The contribution is an integrated and testable account of action-flow within continuous change-flow.

items.title: Mirror, mirror: AI, narcissism, and the spell unbroken.
items.abstract: This article proposes a novel psychoanalytic framework for understanding artificial intelligence’s impact on human subjectivity, integrating Winnicott’s maternal function, Green’s work of the negative, and Marty’s operational thinking. We argue that AI functions as an "anti-negative mother", perpetuating omnipotence illusions while foreclosing the negativity essential for the constitution of subjectivity. Unlike the "good enough mother" who gradually fails, AI never disappoints, creating what we term "operational existence": life characterized by accomplishment without lived experience, by products without process, by functioning without desire. Drawing on Freud and Kohut, we demonstrate how AI continuously feeds infantile omnipotence without enabling the transformative internalization necessary for maturation. The critical absence is the negative itself: AI operates within developer-defined ethical limits, deflecting rather than introducing the frustration, lack, and limitation Green identified as essential for subjectivity. Without negativity, there can be no genuine thought production; without thought production, no psychic aliveness. Like Snow White’s Evil Queen before her magic mirror, we ask our devices for affirmation, but unlike the fairy tale’s truth-telling mirror, AI never breaks the spell. The result may be mass production of False Self functioning, raising urgent questions about identity diffusion, the capacity for desire, and our uncertain encounter with reality behind the glass.

items.title: The Engines of Creativity and the Boundaries of Aesthetics in Machine Consciousness.
items.abstract: This article rethinks the concept of beauty through the lens of cognition and meaning, examining art and aesthetics in comparison with science, and enumerates the factors that, under the name of deconstruction or structure‑breaking, shape a creative process. By classifying errors, hallucinations, dreams, humour, metaphor, and imagination into the groups of conscious and unconscious deviations, as the essential requirements of an intelligent and creative process, we explore their function through the lens of the structure of language, conceptual proportions, and consciousness, and extend their assessment into the domain of language models and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Structure Recursive Viability Dynamics (SRVD) v7.6 Macro-Viability and Higher-Order Phase Transitions: Non-Equilibrium Dynamics of Persistent Structures.
items.abstract: Structure Recursive Viability Dynamics (SRVD) is a cross-scale, macroscopic, coarse-grained theoretical framework that unifies crystals, living systems, AI models, civilizations, and memes — Persistent Structures in all their forms — within a single information‑time‑energy dynamics. The framework's core metric is the Viability Potential: in its baseline form, V ≈ I·T/E; in its general power‑law form, V ∝ I^α·T^β/E^γ, where the three exponents constitute the ITE Elasticity Exponents, ordered as α > γ > β. Core innovations: 1. Decoder endogenization — informational value is not an intrinsic property of a signal but is extracted and assigned Information Polarity (I⁺ / I⁻ / I⁰) by a Decoder (D); the framework's foundational axiom is "No Decoder, No Information (as effective causal information)" (D → I → V). 2. Triple Splitting of the viability potential — once the Endogenous Time Horizon (T_pred) undergoes self-regulation, V splits into Objective Viability (V_obj), Virtual Viability (V^virt), and Value Viability (V^val); when the Decoupling Deviation (Δ_VV) exceeds a critical threshold, the system may enter Myopic Runaway — a conditional phase transition, not an inevitability. 3. Five-fold Recursion — the five variables I, V, T, E, D co-evolve in coupled fashion, converging on the framework's meta-postulate of Viability Maximization (max V). 4. A family of falsifiable predictions — spanning the Horizon Collapse Precedence early-warning signal in reinforcement learning, failure conditions for the Structural Identity Criterion, and the Compression Finality (the F‑Saturation Decay Theorem). SRVD does not violate established physical lower bounds such as Landauer's principle and the second law of thermodynamics. It aims to provide a unified macro-dynamical language for complex recursive systems, with applications to AI alignment, civilizational governance, and the study of complexity evolution.

items.title: Revisiting the Deontological Argument from Evil: A Persisting Problem for Theism.
items.abstract: This paper revisits and strengthens the deontological argument from evil to greater good theodicies (GGTs). Standard GGTs maintain that God may permissibly produce or allow evil when doing so is necessary for sufficiently great goods. I argue that this strategy faces a serious challenge given a deontological conception of morality: some evils may be impermissible to produce or allow even if they are necessary for such goods. I then argue that recent attempts to reconcile GGTs with deontological constraints—especially Mooney’s appeal to the distinction between doing and allowing evil and the appeal to the claim that not all human constraints apply to God—fail to adequately resolve this challenge.

items.title: The Hidden Valence: Why Nothing We Call Good Or Bad Is Separate From Feeling.
items.abstract: In an earlier paper, The Case for Hedonic Primacy, I argued that positive valence is the only thing that is intrinsically good, and negative valence the only thing that is intrinsically bad. That paper stated the claim and traced its consequences. What it never did was the one thing that would make the claim impossible to escape. It did not take the things we believe to be valuable in their own right, one at a time — money, status, love, truth, meaning, achievement, beauty, justice, freedom, health, power, legacy, and life itself — and show of each that the value we find in it is feeling, and nothing but feeling, wearing a disguise. That demonstration is the work of this paper. The instrument is a single test, which I call the subtraction test, and it can be run on any candidate good. Hold the thing fully present, remove only the feeling, and ask whether anyone would still want what is left. I run the test in the open, on the hardest cases I can find, and watch them fall one after another. None survives. I then owe an account of why, if this is so, almost no one sees it, and I give one; a truth denied by nearly everyone needs its denial explained rather than merely deplored. The illusion that some values stand apart from feeling is not stupidity. It is the predictable joint product of four things: an evolved nervous system that hides its own machinery, a world in which a good and the feeling it brings almost never come apart, a language built to name shared objects rather than the private subject who feels them, and a calm reflective stance that lacks access to the very evidence in question. With the reduction in hand, I ground it in the documented neuroscience of reward and adaptation, naming the specific physical mechanisms by which the brain cancels sustained pleasure, and I argue that because they are mechanisms they can be edited. From there the consequences run further than the first paper carried them: into the identity of the being who would benefit from a hedonic future, into the population ethics of how much experience there should be and for whom, into the role freedom keeps after suffering is gone, indispensable yet temporary, lasting only until valence itself is fully understood, into a frankly-labelled speculation about the possible scale of experience, and at last into the single empirical question on which all the rest waits, which is what valence physically is. I hold the central claim to be true. Not as a hypothesis awaiting …

items.title: Divine Causation and E.J. Lowe’s Analysis of Physical Causal Closure.
items.pub: In Guta Mihretu P. & LaRock Eric, E. J. Lowe's Metaphysics and Philosophical Theology. New York: Routledge.
items.venue: E. J. Lowe's Metaphysics and Philosophical Theology
items.abstract: Our focus in this chapter is on a less recognized but nevertheless important potential inconsistency between Christian theology and physicalism. We are interested in the incongruence between the possibility of divine causation and an essential principle of physicalism known as the ‘causal closure of the physical domain.’ We begin by outlining certain core Christian doctrines which imply that God (an immaterial being) has caused and continues to cause physical or material effects in the world. After the physicalist philosophical context of the causal closure doctrine is juxtaposed with essential tenets of Christian theology, and a more modern and technical notion of being ‘physical’ has been admitted, we critically weigh the claim that causal closure under physical laws is strongly supported by empirical science, touching briefly on neurophysiology and quantum physics. We then bring E.J. Lowe’s metaphysics to bear on the topic. We explore his work on reconciling causal closure with mental causation in the philosophy of mind, and raise doubts about the extent to which it can be generalized to divine causation. We next discuss Lowe’s rationale for questioning whether causal closure could ever be empirically verified, and subsequently follow his example in suggesting there could be empirical reasons to think it is false.

items.title: Gruesome Predictions.
items.abstract: I explain some basic problems of inductive reasoning from a Bayesian point of view.

items.title: Value Encroachment in Consciousness Science.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue that if consciousness is practically significant, non-epistemic values may legitimately influence the conduct of consciousness science. Drawing on the literature on inductive risk and adequacy-for-purpose, I argue that value encroachment is not limited to isolated debates but is a pervasive feature of the field. Values can shape methodological and statistical choices, as well as the evaluation and selection of theories of consciousness. This reframes theory choice as relative to the aims of different epistemic agents. Finally, I provide a framework for distinguishing legitimate from illegitimate value intrusions in consciousness science. Overall, this paper offers new value-based dialectical moves to defend methodological and theoretical choices in consciousness science.

items.title: The Pilcrow Theory ¶ : Phenomenal Events and Global Actuality.
items.abstract: The Pilcrow Theory ¶ is a formal and metaphysical framework for consciousness that distinguishes phenomenal presence, phenomenal form, global actuality, and the continuity of conscious subjects. -/- Its structural framework identifies reciprocal units, maximal episodes, and intrinsic perspectives within a declared physical model. Qualifying episodes constitute supports. Pilcrow Core identifies each support event with a phenomenally present event and its intrinsic observational-modal structure, Φ, with phenomenal form. These identifications are explicit metaphysical commitments, distinguished from mathematical results. -/- Succession, direct transport, and causal provenance generate a partial order on supports. Its admissible total extensions form the “Actuality fibre”, studied through order ideals, flip graphs, order polytopes, permutohedra, and infinite-history topologies. Global Pilcrow adds the hypothesis that exactly one admissible history is actual. -/- Keywords: consciousness; philosophy of mind; phenomenal form; causal structure; symmetry; order theory; actuality; formal models; artificial consciousness.

items.title: From artificial to artefactual wisdom: governing territorial polyrhythmy.
items.abstract: This article proposes a conceptual grammar for governing the heterogeneous temporalities that coexist within a territory without ever unifying. We argue that contemporary algorithmic infrastructures (adaptive traffic systems, logistics platforms, predictive analytics) share an architectural commitment they cannot govern: they operate according to a dominant logic derived from Aristotle’s excluded third, treating contradictions as problems to be resolved through eliminating one of their terms. The governance of territorial polyrhythmy requires a different architecture. Our central contribution is a grammar for qualifying territorial temporal antagonisms, not a critique of the smart city paradigm alone. Drawing on Simondon’s metastability (1958), Stengers’s ecology of practices (2005), and Lupasco’s logic of the included third (1951), we propose three conceptual displacements: from excluded to included third, from problem-solving to antagonism governance, and from measurement to evaluation. These displacements give rise to what we call ArtefactKairos: technical devices oriented toward the composition of heterogeneous temporalities rather than the compression of time. Engaging the conversation on artificial wisdom opened in this journal (Casacuberta 2013; Tsai 2020; Sinha and Lakhanpal 2023) and extended beyond it (McGregor 2025; Chella 2025), we argue that wisdom can be understood as a systemic property of territorial governance, an idea not yet addressed by the existing literature. Building on the Aristotelian distinction between sophia and phronesis, and on Dreyfus’s account of embodied judgement, we displace wisdom from the individual to the territorial register and from the contemplative to the compositional. The wisdom at stake is artefactual rather than artificial in the agentive sense: it has no existence outside the technical mediations through which polyrhythmic antagonisms become perceptible, nameable, and governable. The article introduces the Tempobloc as an elementary unit of polyrhythmic analysis and the Tic-Tac Gears, an exploratory governance grammar whose seven spatial forms and seven temporal colours generate forty-nine configurations for qualifying territorial antagonisms. The Algo-Geriato antagonism between algorithmic acceleration and demographic deceleration, explored through the case of a Montreal intersection, serves as a paradigmatic example. The framework is theoretical: it specifies three concrete design shifts (from optimization …

items.title: A New Way Through AI: A Quiet Paradigm Shift Explored.
items.abstract: The historical obsession with algorithm design has obscured a far more potent lever for problem-solving: environment design. Reinforcement Learning (RL) did not birth the concept of the environment; it merely made its boundary explicit. By intentionally engineering the environment---transforming chaotic problem spaces into cooperative topologies, we can offload immense computational and cognitive complexity.

items.title: Beyond and Below Cognitive Space: A Framework for Perfecting Conceptual Spaces.
items.abstract: Peter Gärdenfors’ conceptual spaces framework represents a significant advance in cognitive science by proposing a geometric model of cognition that fills in gaps of symbolic and associationist accounts in explaining prototypical categorization and similarity judgment. This paper argues that in developing this framework, Gärdenfors has independently recovered something very similar to the cognitive structure of Aristotle. Surveying the Aristotelian-Thomistic cognitive hierarchy pinpoints where the conceptual spaces framework can be ontologically grounded and expanded. The paper concludes with preliminary observations on the implications of this analysis for Large Language Models (LLMs), arguing that better philosophical accounts of cognition may inform better LLM architectures, and that the Aristotelian-Thomistic framework provides the most complete account currently available of both what cognitive geometry correctly models and what lies irreducibly beyond it.

items.title: The AASC Description of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Under the dependency lock of the AASC fixed-domain admissibility-and-standing framework, this paper develops a downstream description of consciousness and qualia. It imports the established AASC kernel—bivalent standing, fail-closed enforcement, witness-coherent evaluation, redescription covariance, quotient-interface formation, standing/admissibility identity, no-hiddenremainder closure, same-scope operator exhaustion, and anchor–tensor–skin decomposition—and asks what follows when that structure is instantiated on candidate records, candidate referents, subject indices, memory and report channels, and qualitative distinctions. Report, computation, global broadcast, integrated information, predictive inference, recurrence, and neural correlation may realize or witness consciousness-related structure, but none alone fixes what a report, memory trace, discrimination, neural surrogate, or machine selfascription refers to. The formal core proves that non-vacuous, reusable consciousness evidence requires a unique, redescription-invariant, diachronically compositional map from active record orbits to quotient-level referents. When the witness basis is consequence-complete and confirmation factors through that map, consciousness-level confirmation is presentation-independent.
