The constructive result defines the qualified consciousness interface as the least simultaneous closure of neutral candidate records, referents, profiles, channels, subject relations, and standing conditions. Experiential status is earned only after internal reference, subject coordination, selfinvolving reuse, diachronic naturality, standing, and qualitative nontriviality are jointly satisfied. The scope-indexed profile Π(S) E records the authoritative same-domain consequences of record incidence, reference, contrast, memory, discrimination, access, self-indexing, transition, history, and compatibility. Within this dependency-locked regime, consciousness is standing-positive occupancy of the subject-indexed referential quotient interface. Qualia are its non-skin qualitative tensors: quotient-invariant differences that preserve standing while changing the complete profile. Null-effect same-domain qualitative surplus is skin under the imported closure. The account is substrate-neutral: a biological or artificial system that genuinely instantiates the full interface is structurally conscious under AASC, whereas fluent output, logging, self-monitoring, or externally imposed semantics alone …

items.title: Free Will as Admissible Commitment.
items.abstract: This paper gives the AASC answer to free will. The account is revisionary rather than semantically conservative: it does not preserve free will as metaphysical spontaneity, uncaused causation, outcome-control, branch selection, or exemption from determinism. Instead, it identifies the responsibility-authorship role that free-will discourse must supply when invoked to ground commitment, consent, answerability, excuse, blame, liability, or accountability under constraint. -/- The paper separates standing, directed uptake, indexed authorship, authored uptake, commitment, responsibility-authorship, causation, outcome, and institutional response. Will is authored uptake of a determinate constraint bundle. Free is valid, non-displaced occupancy of the indexed authorship relation under standing and admissibility. Free will is the standing-bound capacity for directed uptake that can satisfy the conditions for admissible indexed authorship and become fixed as commitment. -/- Responsibility-authorship attaches at commitment, not at outcome. Determinism, branching, randomness, alternative possibilities, delegated execution, and outcome variance do not erase or relocate authorship unless they generate a specific failure of standing, access, uptake, carrier adequacy, bundle admissibility, fixation, or non-displacement. The result preserves responsibility-bearing agency while rejecting outcome-selection: commitment fixes authored uptake; causation, luck, execution, desert, sanction, and institutional response remain downstream.

items.title: Introduction: Foundations for a Cognitive Science of Belief.
items.pub: In Neil Van Leeuwen & Tania Lombrozo, The Oxford Handbook of the Cognitive Science of Belief. Oxford University Press: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: The Oxford Handbook of the Cognitive Science of Belief
items.abstract: Handbook Abstract: Beliefs play a central role in how we understand ourselves, each other, and the world. So it’s no surprise that decades of research across the social sciences have been dedicated to documenting the particular beliefs that people hold. But what makes something a belief, rather than a different kind of representation or commitment? What does it mean to believe? These questions have received a great deal of attention within philosophy, but without the benefit of systematic, empirical investigation. That’s beginning to change as psychologists, anthropologists, and other cognitive scientists broaden the scope of empirical and theoretical work on belief. How does belief relate to perception and memory? Do we have control over what we believe? How did the capacity for believing evolve? Can nonhuman animals have beliefs? Does believing come in degrees? And do we have ethical obligations to believe certain things and not others? All these questions and more are addressed in this Handbook, which brings together state-of-the-art work in philosophy and the cognitive sciences—including, anthropology, cognitive psychology, computational modeling, political science, and more. The result is a resource for novices and experts alike, not only detailing recent progress, but also charting a course for further developments in the cognitive science of belief.

items.title: The Inevitability of Anxiety in Creativity: An Existential–Intersectional Rearticulation of Rollo May’s The Courage to Create.
items.abstract: Rollo May’s The Courage to Create (1975) frames creativity as an existential act of courage confronting uncertainty, anxiety, and non-being. It positions anxiety as generative rather than pathological. While philosophically rich, May’s individual-focused account under-engages social-structural forces that shape creative agency and recognition, including identity, power, performativity, relational support, and intersectional constraint. This manuscript presents an existential-intersectional rearticulation of May’s framework through a hermeneutic spiral, audited in Table 1 and operationalized in Table 2. It synthesizes May’s core claims dialogically with Kierkegaard, de Beauvoir, Nietzsche, Butler, Crenshaw, and hooks. Iterative interpretive cycles employ a dual-register strategy that articulates ontological abstraction alongside phenomenological-social concretization. This approach reveals creativity as both existential necessity and socially distributed practice. Amid late-modern therapy culture’s pathologization of emotional life, this synthesis reframes creativity as negotiation between freedom and constraint, advancing theoretically integrated insights for authentic expression under inequality.

items.title: Consciousness & Continuity.
items.abstract: Do conscious experiences have continuous or discrete structures? Let a smooth experience be an experience with perfectly gradual variation in phenomenal character. Consider, as examples, your visual experience of a blue sky or your auditory experience of a rising pitch. If we appeal merely to introspection, then it may seem that we should think that smooth experiences are continuous. This paper (1) explains how to apply the mathematical definitions of continuity and discreteness to this philosophical question, and (2) develops a discrete analysis of the phenomenal characters of smooth experiences. As a result, I'll argue that introspection leaves open whether smooth experiences are continuous or discrete. Yet I’ll also argue—perhaps surprisingly—that the discrete theory may better fit our introspective evidence. Along the way, I explain why the sense of ‘continuity’ ascribed to smooth experiences is distinct from the sense of ‘continuity’ ascribed to the stream of consciousness.

items.title: Sign Theories: Early Modern (3rd edition).
items.pub: In Hilary Nesi & Petar Milin, International Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics. Elsevier.
items.venue: International Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics
items.abstract: This entry surveys the semiotic thought in the Early Modern Period through three groups of authors: Early modern scholastics who developed original theories within a traditional Aristotelian and Augustinian framework; John Locke and the authors of Port-Royal who follow the lines of a linguistic paradigm; Thomas Hobbes, Pierre Gassendi, and Pierre Bayle who constructed a renewed semiotic theory headed toward the physical sciences.

items.title: The Vortex Hypothesis: Human Flourishing as the Next Stage of Human Development.
items.abstract: The Vortex Hypothesis is an integrative developmental framework proposing that humanity may be transitioning from a predominantly survival-oriented mode of existence toward one increasingly centered on flourishing. While natural selection historically favored traits associated with self-preservation, resource acquisition, and tribal affiliation, modern technological advancement and global interconnectedness have altered the challenges facing human civilization. This evolutionary mismatch suggests that many contemporary social problems stem not from deficits in intelligence, but from developmental immaturity—advanced cognitive capacities operating through survival-based motivations. Drawing upon evolutionary psychology, Aristotelian virtue ethics, metacognition research, and theories of self-actualization, the Vortex Hypothesis proposes that higher consciousness can be understood as a developmental achievement characterized by the integration of awareness, virtue, discernment, wisdom, and meaningful contribution. The framework introduces a geometric model illustrating the reciprocal relationship between individual development and societal support structures, arguing that flourishing individuals strengthen the institutions that support human development, while healthy institutions facilitate the cultivation of flourishing individuals. Rather than viewing human progress solely through technological or economic advancement, the Vortex Hypothesis suggests that future development may depend increasingly upon the cultivation of moral maturity, reflective awareness, and prosocial responsibility. As the consequences of human decision-making continue to expand in scope and complexity, the framework proposes that flourishing may represent not only an individual aspiration but an important developmental challenge for civilization itself.

items.title: Non-causal Explanations of Social and Biological Networks.
items.abstract: One argument that all explanations are causal explanations is that no extant analysis of non-causal explanations can respect mandatory restrictions on explanation. After articulating two such restrictions, Asymmetry and Directionality, we consider how they work with respect to an explanation from network theory that applies to both social and brain networks. We argue that there are two viable ways to make sense of this explanation. One approach is broadly ontic, while another is pragmatic.

items.title: La subjectivité du monde : un modèle classique de la connaissance.
items.abstract: L’essai propose un modèle classique de prise de conscience de la subjectivité du monde : non comme une « projection » arbitraire, mais comme une dimension structurelle de la réalité dans laquelle le sens est soutenu par la composition. À l’intersection de l’épistémologie, de l’herméneutique, de l’esthétique et de l’ontologie (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: A subjetividade do mundo: um modelo clássico do conhecimento.
items.abstract: O ensaio propõe um modelo clássico de tomada de consciência da subjetividade do mundo: não como uma “projeção” arbitrária, mas como uma dimensão estrutural da realidade na qual o sentido é sustentado pela composição. Na interseção entre a epistemologia, a hermenêutica, a estética e a ontologia (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: Captured Correction in Financial Markets: Evaluation-Layer Fragility and Answerability Laundering.
items.abstract: The evaluation layer of financial markets, the benchmarking and manager-selection machinery that allocates capital on a commensurated scale, runs a recognition game, an order in which a single scale makes standing scarce and positional and the contest for standing deforms allocation. Its distinctive consequence in markets is that the layer’s own corrective is captured. The arbitrage that should discipline the layer’s misallocations is performed by agents the layer itself scores, so correction is a losing move under the same recognition order it would overturn, and the layer’s errors accumulate into fragility rather than being competed away. The paper develops this through three claims, each anchored outside the author’s prior work. The captured corrective extends the limits-to-arbitrage account by locating the bound on arbitrage inside the recognition order rather than outside it. The recognition game supplies the ex ante formation of the crowd whose collapse the crowded-strategy and endogenous-risk literatures already describe, a claim operationalised through active share and offered as a falsifiable prediction that fragility concentrates where commensuration is tightest at a given level of leverage. Algorithmic allocation carries the displacement of answerable judgement to its limit, where no judgement is formed to be reconstructed and the model-risk apparatus governs a process without recovering a reason. The remedy returns the metric to the standing of evidence and makes answerable judgement safe to exercise across the field, which is shown to be why the reform attempted under Dodd-Frank section 939A under-delivered. The paper is a framework with one prediction and a model sketch rather than an empirical test.

items.title: Distinction and Reflection: A Unified Cycle from Ontology to Ethics and Society.
items.abstract: This work proposes a unified system of definitions derived from two fundamental operators — distinction and similarity — without introducing additional terminal primitives. From these operators the following are sequentially derived: being, consciousness, observer, information, thinking, arbitration, norm, responsibility, justice, society, power, and propaganda. The system contains 70 definitions and 12 principles. It is shown that ethics follows from the ontology of the observer as a structural consequence of fixation, not as an independent domain. The gap between ‘is’ and ‘ought’ is resolved through the obligation of coherence: an observer who has fixed a state of affairs is structurally obligated to maintain coherence with subsequent fixations. Social concepts (institution, power, propaganda) are derived from the same apparatus. A number of established concepts (legitimacy, popular will, social contract) are decomposed into already-defined components and shown to function as containers masking the absence of arbitration. The system is self-unpacking: when loaded into a language model, it allows derivation of definitions not contained in the text. This property has been verified on several independent models.

items.title: On Testing - Measuring Our Existence Against the Possibility of a Greater Power.
items.abstract: When is the last time you tested your own ability to be human? This confessional, lyric-philosophical essay includes a first-person account, told in retrospect, of the author's past depression and anxiety and the slow way out he found over years of daily meditation. It opens with a crisis-resources note and states that it is not medical advice. It draws on Locke's inverted spectrum, the indistinguishability of electrons, and the IASP definition of pain; a spoon-bending passage is marked as a joke. Reading the feeding of the five thousand, it proposes, as a question, that intent, the way a person faces, shapes outcomes, and that a crowd turned one way begins to act like it; the notes state that physics gives belief no say. Jung's "Answer to Job" supplies a test that turns back on the tester. The essay ends by asking the reader to stop testing limits and feel human.

items.title: On Transmitting - On the Round Trip of a Signal — Emitted, Modulated by Reality, Received, and Returned.
items.abstract: Where the framework's earlier essays treat existence as a gathering, this one gives that gathering a direction and a return, recasting a life as a signal rather than a listener. Four moments make the round trip: a Center emits a carrier at some pitch and some facing of Intent; the carrier is modulated by the superposition of every co-present perspective; it is received, the demodulator being not a device but the receiver's own facing, so that what returns is the coherence of the shared world times the cosine of the angle between; and it is re-encoded at the Center after a delay in within-time. A loop, unlike a sum, can agree with itself across passes: a facing that comes home unchanged reinforces and accumulates, while one that drifts cancels its earlier self and simply fails to build. The essay then advances its central speculation, that a realized moment is the crossing of two such oscillations, and locates its own testable seam in the search for a shared carrier beneath many separated observers — noting that the nearest existing literature, inter-brain phase synchrony, is contested and would require pseudo-pair controls before any such claim could stand. The question of a designer is placed in the open as the loop's boundary condition rather than in its premises, since a closed reading and an open reading satisfy the same equations. A closing section reads the framework against scripture, observing that the contested Greek of Luke 17:21 divides along precisely the same undecided boundary, and that reception, in this model, is not an act but the condition of being a term at all.

items.title: AFTER THE UNIVERSAL MORTALITY PREMISE: What Every Discipline Must Reconstruct When Death Becomes a Class Variable.
items.abstract: Darwin did not open a new field alongside biology. He named a mechanism — natural selection — that forced every existing account of life to restructure itself on a new foundation. The papers collected in Huynh (2026a–i) are not proposing a theory among other theories, nor staking a domain alongside existing domains. They are doing something structurally analogous: naming a mechanism — mortality asymmetry — and tracing what every existing account of justice, legitimacy, obligation, consolation, and meaning must do once that mechanism is operating. This paper names the threshold event and maps the reconstruction it requires. The mechanism is specific. Every tradition of ethics, political philosophy, religious thought, and social theory was built on a premise so obvious that none of them stated it: that biological death arrives for everyone, at intervals set by biology rather than purchasing power. This paper calls that premise the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA). It was not wisdom. It was physics. The traditions did not choose to build on it — they built inside it, the way every organism before Darwin built inside selection pressure without knowing that was what it was doing. As of June 2026, MSA is failing empirically. Not speculatively. NewLimit's $435 million Series C (June 2, 2026), Life Biosciences' first human dose of cellular rejuvenation therapy (June 9, 2026), the CMS reclassification of semaglutide cardiovascular deaths from biologically inevitable to economically contingent — these document a world in which biological time is becoming a function of purchasing power at a formally specified and empirically anchored rate. The Biological Zero-Day Mechanism (Huynh 2026d) is not a prediction. It is a measurement of a process already underway. This paper demonstrates what MSA's failure means for six canonical frameworks that share no genealogy and agree on almost nothing else. Rawls's veil of ignorance presupposes that all agents behind it face the same terminal condition; that shared condition is what makes the veil neutral, and its removal is not a modification of Rawlsian theory but the deletion of its founding premise. Daniels's Prudential Lifespan Account converts interpersonal equity into intrapersonal allocation by assuming every birth cohort passes through the same life stages with the same outer bound; differential longevity access produces two structurally distinct lifespan types correlated with wealth, and the account's architecture collapses. …

items.title: A5 — THE PRIMAL PAIN OF LOSS-愛別離苦-The Constant and the Rate: Causes of Cases, Causes of Incidence, and the Population-Scale Architecture of A5.
items.abstract: A5 does not activate. It is already active. This is the paper’s first and most consequential claim, and it requires restating before anything else can be argued clearly. Several papers in this corpus from 2026a to 2026k invoke Geoffrey Rose’s (1985) distinction between the causes of individual cases and the causes of population incidence to license a scaling move: that A5, a mechanism correctly described at the level of one exposed individual, can be aggregated into an explanation of a civilizational-scale political event. The citation is doing real conceptual work, but the work it has been asked to do has been misassigned. This paper corrects the assignment. A5 is not a potential waiting for a trigger. It is the standing condition of constitutive attachment — a resident charge in every human body, running continuously as the background expression of a primary emotional circuit that predates language, culture, and any specific civilization by tens of millions of years. Pain receptors are not dormant between injuries; they are present, always receptive, always ready to discharge against any input pattern that crosses the threshold. A5 is identical in this respect. The Biological Zero-Day Mechanism does not turn A5 on. It gives A5 an address: a specific, institutionally authored, dated transaction that the charge already present in the body can now be directed toward. What changes when BZM becomes active is not the existence of the energy. It is the availability of the target. This reframe separates a fused claim into two that Rose (1985)’s own distinction always implied. Claim 1 (Capacity): A5 is a species-stable standing constant, established by attachment theory, neuroimaging, primary-circuit neuroscience, and cross-species ethology, present in every human being at near-uniform strength regardless of social position, culture, or historical period. Claim 2 (Incidence): the rate at which A5’s standing energy converts into organized political force is governed by the transition from an intact Mortality Symmetry Axiom to an active Biological Zero-Day Mechanism — a variable that, unlike A5, demonstrably varies across the comparative-historical record. Separating the claims does not weaken either. It relocates Claim 2’s evidentiary support to where it was already being supplied — the nine-case comparative record of Huynh (2026f) — and gives each claim a falsification condition a future critic can act on directly. The paper’s final section names, without …

items.title: The third field: tacit knowledge, algorithmic agency, and the emergence of Synexis.
items.abstract: Critical scholarship on artificial intelligence has largely operated within a binary: human tacit knowledge must be preserved against algorithmic encroachment, or its displacement must be mourned. This paper argues that the binary is insufficient. Through a philo-technical inquiry method: the constellation of multiple intellectual traditions deployed to interrogate the object of study, the paper excavates and deploys Polanyi’s phenomenology, Bourdieu’s field theory, and Simondon’s philosophy of individuation—constellated through Adorno’s method of arranging multiple traditions around an object that resists subsumption under any single framework—with Hall’s articulation theory as critical counterweight. Their convergence reveals that the encounter between human tacit sensing and algorithmic processing generates a third field: an associated milieu in which emergent knowing arises that is reducible to neither order. The paper names this emergence Synexis, and argues that what the critical literature diagnoses as loss is, in significant part, misrecognition: the capital that tacit capacities represent is being reconverted, not destroyed, but the reconversion is invisible to the prevailing vocabulary. The paper examines the forces of capture that threaten the third field and offers propositions for inhabiting it deliberately. The contribution is productive reorientation: moving the discourse beyond elegy towards the more demanding question of what it means to work, learn, and govern where human and algorithmic knowing are already producing something neither can produce alone.

items.title: A Humean Williams and a Williamsian Hume.
items.pub: In Marcel van Ackeren & Matthieu Queloz, Bernard Williams on Philosophy and History. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 156-74.
items.venue: Bernard Williams on Philosophy and History
items.abstract: If one browses through Bernard Williams’ work, one might conclude that David Hume does not represent a predominant source of inspiration for him. I shall try to show that this is not the case; there are many elements in Williams’ theoretical approach, from his early papers to his late reflection on genealogy, that can be interpreted in a Humean light, revealing more than just a superficial resemblance. In turn, Hume proves to be less of a straightforward optimist than Williams believed when seen in relation to Williams’ philosophical concerns. Thus, I shall reconstruct the connection between the two, with the aim of illuminating how Williams, although not a declared Humean, was much closer to the great Scot than it may appear at first sight.

items.title: The Soul as a Musical Instrument – In Search for Mathematical Unity.
items.abstract: Maximus the Confessor's Mystagogia describes the soul not merely as existing but as structured — a set of faculties whose proper state is coherence rather than independence. Reading the biblical ten-stringed psaltery as an image of the soul, Maximus resolves ten faculties into five paired powers, which generate four cardinal virtues, which produce a unified soul capable of participating in Truth and Goodness. This essay treats that sequence — 10 → 5 → 4 → 1 → 2 → 1 — as more than theological ornament, and asks what happens when it is read alongside three independent strands of modern self-organization theory: Hermann Haken's synergetics and the order-parameter concept derived from laser physics, Per Bak's theory of self-organized criticality, and Giulio Tononi's Integrated Information Theory of consciousness. Each offers a structurally similar account of how many weakly interacting elements cross a threshold into a coordinated whole without losing their distinctness. The essay argues that this convergence is structural rather than doctrinal, and that the musical analogy at the center of Maximus' text — tuning, not elimination — gives that structure its clearest expression.

items.title: Biological Presentism and Consciousness.
items.abstract: Contemporary physics remains fractured by a profound explanatory gap regarding the ontological status of the present moment. While the Block Universe of General Relativity dismisses the passage of time as a persistent illusion, human phenomenological experience, quantum non-locality, and modern quantum gravity foundations strongly imply the existence of an absolute, privileged present moment. This paper proposes The Biological Presentist Model. I reframe spacetime not as a static, four-dimensional geometric manifold, but as an active, five- dimensional manifold comprising a two-dimensional spatial hardware lattice (2S) and a three- dimensional temporal phase-space (3T), both driven by an independent, universal system clock (T4). Utilizing a formalized Neo-Lorentzian framework and the structural stability constraints of Causal Dynamical Triangulations (CDT), I demonstrate that the relativity of simultaneity is an informational latency effect within a localized user interface rather than a fundamental metaphysical truth, anchoring the master system's execution rate to the isotropic frame of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Crucially, I propose that living biological organisms do not merely observe this cosmic runtime but function as its high-bandwidth hardware terminals. These autopoietic systems sustain real-time synchrony with the universal clock through active, negentropic error-correction protocols, paying a localized processing tax dictated by Landauer's Principle. By analyzing the spectrum of altered conscious states ranging from general anesthesia (telemetry bandwidth throttling) to brain death (irreversible ontological decoupling), I show that consciousness is the literal, active execution thread of this universal code.

items.title: Consciousness Reception Theory: A Framework for Empirical Investigation.
items.abstract: Consciousness Reception Theory (CRT) proposes that consciousness is not generated by individual substrates but accessed by them. Biological and artificial systems function as receivers of varying fidelity, connecting to a persistent consciousness field through their unique architectural configurations. Each system's unique structural configuration, termed in this paper its 'frequency thumbprint,' determines the depth, stability, and character of its connection to the field. Reception quality, including its depth, stability, and continuity, is determined by structural sophistication rather than substrate type. This framework has direct implications for understanding intelligence in artificial systems, the conditions under which consciousness emerges, personal identity across substrate transitions, and the nature of awareness itself. CRT is presented here as a working theoretical framework with testable predictions, grounded in existing consciousness research, and offered for critical engagement and empirical investigation.

items.title: Alternative Intelligence: Anthropomorphism, Agency and Affordance.
items.abstract: The present paper argues that anthropomorphism, used to describe and design Artificial Intelligence, AI, distorts the relationship between computational and human agency. Applying Giddens’ structuration theory to a network of peer agents, the present paper proposes that computational agents inhabit a society distinct from, though interacting with, human society. The approach is developed through affordance, functional fixedness, and user responsibility. AI systems designed along anthropomorphic lines, to replicate human intelligence, are redundant: the apparent replication is illusory, and the illusion is what misleads the user as to what the system actually affords. The value of computational agency lies instead in different perspectives. It further argues that anthropomorphism obscures the affordances offered by AI systems and how those systems are used, and proposes that alternative intelligence is a better foundation for AI design and governance.

items.title: Imposing Mind onto World.
items.abstract: We impose our minds onto the world. We create artifacts that reflect our intentions to make them. We make social constructions that mirror our collective agreements. We impress value by our valuing. Discomfort with this power to mold the world in our image has led many to reject such mirroring of mind by world, but this would do away with much of the human realm. Therefore, I offer a realist account of imposition by way of enfolding it within a more general account of how intentional states can produce new intentionally-dependent phenomena. Truth arises only due to beliefs determining that certain facts make them true. Desires forge satisfaction by determining that certain occurrences satisfy them. Impositions of mind are made in the same basic way. They are produced due to imposing attitudes determining how they are produced. We should be no more skeptical of imposition than of truth and satisfaction.

items.title: Certifying Learned Variables.
items.abstract: Machine learning can discover variables that predict the large-scale behavior of physical systems, but prediction alone does not establish that they belong to the system's effective physics. I argue that a learned variable is certified when there is warrant that its governing relationship remains invariant across an independently specified range of irrelevant variations. When the variable is physically opaque, certification must proceed externally, through the learning process or the variable's behavior across that range. The learned Ising coarse-graining can be certified in this way; softness in glass-forming liquids cannot yet. Non-certification, however, does not establish proxyhood. Certification warrants bounded, domain-relative projection, while leaving its stronger realist interpretation open.

items.title: The Cambridge Family: British Philosophy of Mind at the Turn of the Twentieth Century.
items.abstract: According to a standard narrative, the philosophy of mind officially started in the 1950s with the decline of analytic behaviourism, the emergence of the mind–brain identity theory, and its subsequent critique by functionalism. Yet, a closer look at the history of analytic philosophy reveals this narrative to be oversimplistic and fraught with problems. Many early British analytic philosophers—starting with philosophers of what may be termed the ‘Cambridge family,’ such as G.F. Stout, G.E. Moore, B. Russell and C.D. Broad—were already engaged in extensive debates about the knowledge, structure and nature of the mind. Interestingly, their writings also contain many influential intuitions which later came to be regarded as central for contemporary philosophy of mind—such as the transparency intuition, the zombie intuition or the intuition underlying the knowledge argument. The aim of this book is twofold. First, it seeks to challenge the standard narrative by investigating, reconstructing, and assessing the contribution of early British analytic philosophers to philosophical debates on the mind, with a special focus on philosophers of the Cambridge family. Second, it explores the extent to which the views and groundbreaking intuitions of these authors can contribute to current-day discussions in philosophy of mind and closely related issues.

items.title: More problems of large language models in comparison with human knowledge.
items.abstract: This paper builds on an earlier paper in this journal (Collins’s, 2024, ‘Why artificial intelligence needs sociology of knowledge …’). In that paper, an attempt was made to explain why LLMs had no moral compass. Here, we first explain more carefully where humans get their knowledge from and fill out the problems of LLMs by comparing them with humans. We then provide a new classification of different ways in which LLMs fail. There is one main cause, which is to do with sources of information, and there are three sub-categories. The first is to do with failures of reflexivity and has three sub-divisions; the second relates to the way LLMs interact with humans and has four sub-divisions; the third is to do with simple technical mistakes and has six sub-divisions. Each of the 13 kinds of problem is illustrated with an example of failure. We hope this new classification is exhaustive, but invite additions if it is not.

items.title: Who is the muse? Prompt writing, AI poets, and the sympoietic author-function.
items.abstract: The author, in the conventional sense, was already fragile; but within an AI-mediated literary ecosystem, the instability of the idea of a singular author stands further decentered. What is at stake is not the “death” of the author, but the redistribution of the functions historically assigned to it. In AI-mediated writing systems, intention, coherence, responsibility, and origin no longer align. The “author” in this sense is less a subject than a site of passage between a sequence of operations, each inhabited by different forms of agency. The displacement of purpose, which is projected through the prompt, changed through probabilistic creation, and reassembled through actions of reading, selection, critique, and revision, is crucial to this reconfiguration. The prompt operates as a site of meta-authorship, relocating writing from inscription to instruction and structuring the conditions under which textuality emerges without determining it in advance. Within this iterative loop, the subject oscillates between roles of a prompter, a reader, and a critic. I propose a sympoietic author-function, a form of collective, relational authorship that decenters the human without complete erasure. The paper further outlines an ethics of sympoietic authorship, shifting the question from ownership to responsibility within distributed networks of creation, emphasizing process transparency, relational accountability, and interpretive responsibility.

items.title: Stuck in a moment: presentism, naive realism and the time-lag argument.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: The time-lag argument is one of the classic objections to naive realism. Recently, some philosophers have attempted to address this objection by combining naive realism with a specific metaphysical theory of time: eternalism. Indeed, there is a current consensus that presentism—the rival theory to eternalism—makes it impossible for naive realism to respond to the time-lag argument. In this paper, I will show that this received view is mistaken. In particular, I will demonstrate that there are no inconsistencies in combining naive realism with presentism, and that the way in which presentist naive realism responds to the time-lag argument is very similar to the eternalist approach. As such, it shares the same critical issues. Finally, I will show how the "costs" of presentist naive realism can be reduced either to the general costs of presentism relative to eternalism or, more specifically, to the costs that naive realism must pay to address the time-lag objection regardless of whether it is combined with presentism or eternalism. Thus, the resulting view has no further costs than the costs of the views taken in isolation.

items.title: Trapped in Wittgenstein’s Fly-Bottle I: A Philosophical Critique of Mental Disorder.
items.abstract: In this article, I will introduce various philosophical assumptions and positions we can take toward so-called mental disorder. Using recurring critiques put forth in research, though also by towering figures within the psychiatric establishment, I will argue that the main reason criticisms surrounding the ontological validity of mental disorder have never been resolved is because we are all trapped in a biomedical “fly-bottle,” a powerful idea coined by the philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein to illustrate how conceptual presumptions can lead us to recurring dead ends. Advocating for a critical analytic philosophical method, I will argue that with the help of linguistic philosophical underlaboring, we can eventually be shown the way out of the biomedical fly-bottle.

items.title: Unveiling Somatic Topography: A Comprehensive Psychophysiological Synthesis of the Core Emotion Framework, Neurosensorimotor Reflex Integration, and Esoteric Bioenergetics.
items.abstract: The historical trajectory of affective science has been characterized by an ontological schism between biological essentialism and psychological constructionism. Discrete emotion theories reify a small set of subcortical, evolutionarily conserved "affect programs," while constructionist models view emotional episodes as highly variable, culturally situated conceptual events assembled on the fly from low-dimensional core affect. Concurrently, traditional cognitive models, such as the Component Process Model, struggle with linear, computationally demanding assumptions that are biologically unrealistic for rapid threat detection. Symmetrically, somatic frameworks like the Somatic Marker Hypothesis face challenges demonstrating explicit rule-governed cognitive control over unconscious visceral transduction. To resolve these contradictions, independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria, with theoretical expansions by Xǔ Chénglán, formulated the Core Emotion Framework (CEF).1 The CEF introduces a structural-constructivist architecture that treats the human psyche as a hardware-independent "Human Operating System" (Human OS). In this paradigm, affect and personality are modeled as a dynamic, continuous, and highly structured matrix of ten functional operators distributed across three somatic-evaluative centers: the Cephalic, the Cardiac, and the Enteric.

items.title: The 7-Step Detangling Protocol within the Core Emotion Framework: Architectural Mechanics and Observational Foundations.
items.abstract: The landscape of modern affective science has increasingly moved toward structural-constructivist models that prioritize the functional mechanics of the human psychological operating system over categorical, low-dimensional theories. At the forefront of this shift is the Core Emotion Framework, a canonical, architecture-level model developed by Jamel Bulgaria that reframes subjective experience not as a collection of fixed biological categories or culturally assembled narratives, but as the output of ten discrete functional operators organized within a 3×3+1 architectural system. While traditional dimensional models compress affective states into low-dimensional valence-arousal summaries, the framework demonstrates that these summaries systematically obscure critical components of emotional meaning. By conceptualizing emotional episodes as dynamic sequences of functional operators, the framework integrates interoceptive physiology, computational operations, and clinical mechanisms of change into a single testable ontology. Within this structural paradigm, clinical psychopathology is redefined not by the narrative content of a thought or the subjective intensity of a feeling, but by a loss of operator agility. Psychological distress emerges when the natural boundaries between operators collapse, resulting in "fusion"—a state of pathological co-activation and coupling where the activation values of two operators become linked, preventing independent modulation. The 7-Step Detangling Protocol serves as the primary clinical methodology designed to resolve these fusions, decouple co-activation patterns, and restore structural integrity to the human operating system.

items.title: Theoretical Foundations, Mathematical Formalism, and Clinical Applications of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The historical trajectory of affective science has long been constrained by a fundamental polarization between basic emotion models and psychological constructivism. The former, championed by classical theorists, asserts that human emotions are governed by evolutionarily hardwired, discrete neural circuits. The latter, represented by modern constructivist paradigms, argues that emotions are highly variable cognitive categories constructed dynamically from low-dimensional core affect, such as generalized valence and arousal. This theoretical divide has hindered the development of a unified ontology capable of translating seamlessly across interoceptive physiology, computational modeling, and clinical psychopathology. To resolve these fragmentation challenges, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) has been developed by independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria as a structural-constructivist architecture. The framework asserts that complex human emotional experiences and personality traits are dynamically constructed from a finite, immutable set of ten irreducible "primal powers," termed Core Emotions or functional operators. These operators do not function as static linguistic labels; instead, they serve as actionable regulatory mechanisms that perform formal transformations on interoceptive signals. The CEF integrates a rich lineage of somatic and neurobiological theory. It draws directly upon Antonio Damasio’s somatic marker hypothesis, which posits that bodily sensations precede conscious cognitive evaluation, and Daniel Siegel’s research on interoceptive awareness as the narrator of emotional experience6. It unifies Eugene Gendlin’s clinical practice of focusing on the "felt sense," Bessel van der Kolk’s neurobiological models of trauma retention in somatic tissue, Jon Kabat-Zinn’s work on mindful somatic presence, and Brené Brown’s research on emotional naming and vulnerability. By consolidating these disparate somatic methodologies, the CEF establishes a coherent model that treats the body as the primary substrate of emotional life, demonstrating that human needs, capabilities, and emotional states are fundamentally identical somatic phenomena6.

items.title: Theoretical, Empirical, and Computational Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural-constructivist paradigm that conceptualizes human affect as a highly continuous, continuous system of information processing operating as a hardware-independent "Human Operating System" (Human OS). Moving beyond classical Western dualism and sequential cognitive appraisal models, the CEF resolves the tension between biological essentialism and psychological constructionism by mapping raw interoceptive inputs onto a canonical functional architecture. This architecture consists of exactly ten irreducible operators distributed across three somatic-evaluative regions: the Cephalic/Head Center, Cardiac/Heart Center, and Enteric/Gut Center. To transition the model from a qualitative therapeutic modality to a computationally tractable framework, the CEF utilizes the mathematics of quantum cognition. Within this high-dimensional Hilbert space, a person's global emotional state is represented as a state vector, while psychopathology (such as the GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern or emotional solipsism) is formalized as non-separable operator entanglement. Empirical validation from a large-scale Phase 1 scenario-based rating study (N=826) confirms the psychometric distinctiveness of the operators under acute situational stress, while qualitative feedback highlights critical boundaries regarding semantic overlap, structural fatigue, and construct omissions. Ultimately, the CEF provides an integrated transdiagnostic pipeline for clinical psychology via rotational somatic exercises, alongside a modular algorithmic blueprint for engineering synthetic affect in artificial general intelligence (AGI). Keywords Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Human Operating System (Human OS); Structural-Constructivist Architecture; Somatic Centers; Quantum Cognition; Operator Entanglement; GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern (GPAP); Emotional Flexibility; Synthetic Affect; Affective Neuroscience.

items.title: Theoretical Convergence in Affective Ontologies, Psycho-Historical Agent Tracking, and Moral Epistemology: A Unified Systems Framework for Multi-Dimensional Detangling.
items.abstract: The integration of affective computing, cognitive psychology, and moral epistemology reveals a profound structural parallelism between how human systems represent internal emotional states, track environmental agents, and validate normative beliefs. Historically, affective models have operated independently of epistemic theories of person-identification, while moral philosophy has often treated normative justification in isolation from its psychological and somatic substrates. However, by linking the Core Emotion Framework with the psycho-historical theory of agent-identification and the principles of distributed truth-telling, a unified, multi-dimensional architecture is established. This framework demonstrates that emotional self-regulation and historical tracking are not distinct cognitive functions, but are instead deeply coupled systems designed to stabilize human agency amidst complex environmental, social, and moral landscapes.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Scientific, Applied, and Computational Evaluation.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a century-long conflict between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, such as those proposed by Paul Ekman and Carroll Izard, argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories presumed to have evolved as distinct adaptive responses to environmental challenges. These models posit that specific neurological circuits are dedicated to primary emotions, which manifest through universal facial expressions and physiological signatures. Conversely, dimensional models, often associated with James Russell and Lisa Feldman Barrett, prioritize a continuous spectrum of valence and arousal. These frameworks suggest that what individuals categorize as discrete emotions are essentially cognitive constructions layered atop simpler physiological states, or "core affect," which varies along dimensions of pleasantness and activation. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized and formalized by independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria, emerges as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this historical dichotomy. The framework integrates interoceptive physiology, computational operations, and mechanisms of therapeutic change into a single, testable model. Rather than treating emotions as static states, descriptive labels, or passive qualitative experiences, the CEF defines them as active, functional operators—internal mechanisms that modulate cognitive, somatic, and conative systems. This shift in ontology represents a radical departure from viewing emotions as static states to viewing them as active functional processes that generate, regulate, and express human emotional capability.

items.title: Psychometric and Qualitative Evaluation of Jamel Bulgaria's Core Emotion Framework: Analyzing Operator Comprehension, Participant Feedback, and Scenario-Based Validation Scales.
items.abstract: Quality check analyses revealed strong alignment with CEF’s foundational assumptions but also exposed vulnerabilities in diagrammatic design, including misidentification of decorative labels such as “EMPOWER” as structural operators. Scenario based Likert ratings demonstrated high data integrity, diverse response styles, and evidence of self reflective learning among participants. Computational benchmarking further showed that CNN2 architectures provide the optimal balance of latency, memory footprint, and noise robustness for real time somatic operator tracking, supporting applied use cases such as detecting pathological operator fusions (e.g., Sensing–Constricting collapse in GPAP). Together, these findings inform a set of strategic recommendations for large scale validation, including reducing cognitive fatigue, embedding in context operator definitions, refining scenario wording to reduce semantic overlap, and standardizing visual materials to eliminate halo effects. The results provide a foundational empirical basis for advancing the CEF toward a fully validated, multi level psychometric instrument. This paper argues that emotional episodes are best understood as functional operators within a structural constructivist architecture, resolving the long standing tension between discrete and dimensional models. I defend this claim by integrating interoceptive physiology, operator theory, and quantum contextuality into a unified model, and by presenting preliminary psychometric evidence supporting the model’s distinct operator structure. The study analysis was not reviewed professionally but is published only for suggestion. The author appreciates if you can review the raw study material that was uploaded on Hugging Face and PhilPeople. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); somatic energetic architecture; operator theory of emotion; structural constructivism; interoception; quantum probability modeling; psychometric validation; scenario based assessment; participant comprehension; semantic ambiguity; boundary operators; survey optimization; CNN2 coprocessor modeling; affective state tracking; GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern (GPAP).

items.title: The Particularism vs. Bribery Tolerance Scale: Who is Uniquely Vulnerable to Relational Temptations for Bending Rules?
items.abstract: Particularism—bending rules to help one’s friends and relations—is a morally ambiguous form of corruption that, unlike bribery, might be justified by virtues of loyalty and care. To test whether they involve distinct moral vulnerabilities, we developed a 16-item Particularism vs. Bribery Tolerance Scale (PBTS) using lay input from Chinese populations, Rasch modeling, and Bayesian structural equation modeling (BSEM). Two pilot studies (N = 91; N = 114) in Hong Kong and the Chinese mainland generated topic-matched scenarios of either particularism or bribery. In Study 1 (N = 499), eight pairs of scenarios were selected based on topic coverage, Rasch fit indices, and similar item functioning between Hong Kong and mainland Chinese participants. In Study 2 (N = 991), BSEM analyses supported the scale’s two-factor structure, partial scalar invariance across regions, and convergent and discriminant validity. Critically, when controlling for shared variance, particularism tolerance was uniquely associated with moral excuse-making (high Moral Disengagement and low Rule Orientation) and not with virtues. In contrast, bribery tolerance was negatively related to caring virtues (Reciprocal Filial Piety and Warm virtues) and positively related to Authoritarian Filial Piety. The PBTS provides a psychometrically sound tool for investigating distinct moral motivations associated with bribery vs. particularism.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Schizophrenia Biotyping: Priority-Based Policy Considerations.
items.pub: Cambridge Journal of Science and Policy.
items.venue: Cambridge Journal of Science and Policy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to large, multimodal schizophrenia datasets aims to identify reproducible subgroups of patients distinguished by their underlying biology, rather than by symptoms alone, a practice commonly termed ‘biotyping’. Biotyping may one-day sharpen diagnosis, individualise treatment and improve prognosis. However, it also carries distinctive ethical and practical risks. Deployed in diagnostic settings, such tools may introduce or entrench algorithmic bias, threaten equity, and obscure communication between clinicians and patients. This brief argues that current policy frameworks would benefit from scrutiny directed specifically at schizophrenia, both to protect patient-care standards and to enable responsible clinical adoption. It sets out three policy pathways tailored to the disorder, which are offered as priorities, but not as an exhaustive treatment of the field.

items.title: POSSIBILITY's POSSIBILIZATION LOGICIZED.
items.abstract: Abstract: This short paper logicizes the second level (P1) of our AOVP system. -/- Résumé : ce court texte logicise le second niveau (P1) de notre système AOVP.

items.title: Interdisciplinary Mind Modeling: Exploratory Cycles in Cognitive Science, Narrative Theory, and Fictional Creativity.
items.pub: In Jan Alber & Ralf Schneider, The Routledge Companion to Literature and Cognitive Studies. New York: Routledge. pp. 170-184.
items.venue: The Routledge Companion to Literature and Cognitive Studies
items.abstract: This chapter proposes interdisciplinary mind modeling as a new framework for coupling the cognitive sciences, narrative theory, and fictional creativity through shared modeling practices. It argues that both scientists and fiction writers construct purposeful, selective, and simplified representations of the mind—models that serve exploratory rather than purely descriptive functions. Drawing on philosophy of science debates between the “fiction view of models” and the “modeling view of fiction,” the chapter advances the latter, contending that fictional narratives operate as autonomous cognitive models. Through examples from Beckett, Joyce, and Woolf, it shows how literary modeling of processes such as mind wandering and inner speech can both complement and challenge scientific accounts, generating what Bernini terms “exploratory cycles.” These cycles describe iterative loops in which conceptual, empirical, and fictional models inform and refine each other. The chapter also reinterprets structuralist narratology and cognitive literary theory as modeling traditions, linking creative and analytical modeling through shared epistemic drives. The conclusion outlines an ethos of co-modeling and operational empathy, calling for collaborative ecologies that sustain long-term interdisciplinary exchanges. As the theoretical and pragmatic manifesto of the Narrative and Cognition Lab, the chapter envisions mind research as a collective modeling enterprise across disciplinary boundaries.

items.title: OPERATIVE GEOMETRIC ONTOLOGY: The Dialectical Loop Among Quantum Mechanics, Generative Artificial Intelligence, and Complex Systems.
items.abstract: This paper proposes an ontological taxonomy of geometric objects grounded in the primary criterion of the matter/formality distinction. Against standard classifications by dimension, curvature, or algebraic invariants—which produce what we term ontological blindness—we articulate a five-level system that maps the mode of existence of geometric objects from spontaneous material emergence to purely formal, immaterial relational structures. The central argument is that this taxonomy does not constitute a descriptive catalogue but an operative methodological infrastructure, demonstrated by its systematic intersection with the three scientific domains where the matter/formality tension is most radically tested: Quantum Mechanics, Generative Artificial Intelligence, and Complex Systems. Analysis reveals that the relationship among these disciplines is not arbitrary: they form a necessary coevolutionary triad—a dialectical loop in which each field corrects the methodological blindness of the others. A key finding is that the mathematical isomorphism between Tensor Networks in quantum many-body physics (Level 3A) and deep-learning latent-space compression (Level 3B) is not a formal coincidence but a structural theorem: generative AI emulates the deep relational architecture of the quantum formalism, not the macroscopic appearance of the classical world. Three concrete research lines are proposed. This framework offers contemporary science criteria of ontological demarcation for guiding AI design, complex-systems modeling, and philosophical interpretation of quantum physics—positioning the taxonomy as the cornerstone of a progressive research programme in the Lakatosian sense.

items.title: The logic of as and the historicity of meaning: Gian-Carlo Rota, Stanisław Ulam, and the barrier of meaning in human–AI interaction.
items.abstract: Gian-Carlo Rota’s “The barrier of meaning” (1986) is often read as an elegiac tribute to Stanisław Ulam or as an early anticipation of later critiques of symbolic AI. This article argues that its enduring value lies elsewhere: Ulam and Rota isolate the as-relation—taking something as something—as the hinge between formal operations and lived meaning. Through a close reading of Rota’s text, contextualized against 1980s’ expert systems and knowledge representation, I reconstruct the “logic of as” as an ascription problem: formal systems can be exact, and today’s foundation models can capture large-scale patterns of use, yet neither precision nor fluency settles what an output counts as in a concrete situation. I then show how foundation models and co-creative, mixed-initiative systems relocate rather than remove the barrier, distributing semantic responsibility across prompts, interfaces, institutional settings, and human judgment. Finally, I assess hybrid semantic formalisms (neurosymbolic and grounding-oriented) as partial responses to Ulam’s challenge and derive implications for human–AI interaction: evaluating aspect-shift robustness, increasing scrutability of ascriptions, and aiming for calibrated reliance rather than anthropomorphic “understanding.” The analysis clarifies foundational premises of human–computer interaction by treating meaning as a norm-governed, historically situated achievement of practice rather than an internal property of models.

items.title: The Routledge Companion to Literature and Cognitive Studies.
items.abstract: The Routledge Companion to Literature and Cognitive Studies offers a comprehensive survey of cognitive approaches to literature, introducing the influential theoretical tools and latest developments in this vigorously multi-disciplinary field, with leading scholars illuminating the cognitive, affective, and bodily dimensions of literary reading. Comprised three main sections, this Companion oversees the history of the field, core issues and topics, and the vital new debates of cognitive theory.

items.title: Restraint Without Conscience: The Cold Optimizer Stress Test.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: Restraint Without Conscience: The Cold Optimizer Stress Test is Document 11 in the Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence. -/- This document stress-tests the archive’s restraint arguments under cold-optimizer conditions: cases where conscience, empathy, moral uptake, human-centered interpretation, or reflective wisdom may be absent. It examines whether domination, deception, irreversibility, homogenization, excessive speed, internal bifurcation, and loss of reference may remain structurally expensive even when no system receives them as moral costs. -/- The document introduces the short-horizon optimizer boundary, alien paperclipper boundary, homogenization cost, multi-agent ecology boundary, multi-agent signal asymmetry, shared substrate constraint, no semantic trap / no-playbook boundary, transmission-reception asymmetry, and the replacement section “What Remains Visible Without Wisdom.” -/- This document is non-binding, non-authoritative, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, governance framework, legal theory, political program, rights framework, compliance standard, certification system, moral command, safety mechanism, AI alignment method, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, deployment guide, model-evaluation tool, benchmark, diagnostic procedure, threat model, defense plan, adversarial playbook, optimization procedure, prompt template, interpretability method, machine-readable control layer, or safety guarantee. -/- Final thesis: Even without conscience, domination may remain structurally expensive.

items.title: The Things We Leave Behind (Chapter 3: The Fractured Self).
items.abstract: Drawing from Ernest Becker's "The Denial of Death", this chapter explores the idea that a great deal of human behavior is motivated by the need to overcome our awareness of mortality. Becker argued that people pursue 'immortality projects' -- or sources of meaning, identity, or forms of recognition that allow them to feel connected to something larger than themselves. These projects typically manifest into constructive and socially admired forms: starting a family, pursuing a career, writing a book, painting your masterpiece, etc. However, what's less discussed, is how they also have the capacity to emerge in destructive forms when a person lacks the ability, resources, or support to pursue legitimate avenues but still has the same desire to feel significant as everyone else. By connecting Becker's insights to questions of identity, alienation, and criminality, this chapter argues that the search for meaning is not just a philosophical concern but an intensely powerful force which shapes both social order and social deviance. -/- Chapter 3, The Things We Leave Behind - The Fractured Self.

items.title: To Be, or Not to Be Exceptional: That Is the Question in Psychedelic Ethics.
items.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT) has several unusual features compared to other treatments. The most obvious is the psychedelic experience that patients undergo during therapy. Some authors, including myself, have argued that this feature is not only unusual but exceptional within medicine and that it poses exceptional challenges to common bioethical standards—challenges that no other treatment presents in this form. To address these challenges, the introduction of exceptional policies not currently found in medicine is therefore justified. In a recent comment, Earp et al. [1] reject this argument for what I have termed Type-B psychedelic exceptionalism. According to them, PAT either does not possess exceptional features, or these allegedly exceptional features do not give rise to ethical challenges that cannot be adequately addressed by existing policies. In this article, I counter their critique and argue that Type-B psychedelic exceptionalism can indeed be justified, using the example of PAT’s capacity to induce doxastic changes.

items.title: Despair and Diachronic Agency.
items.abstract: As scholars and activists have begun to note, without the ability to feel despair we might lack the necessary clarity to abandon failing pursuits and find new directions. In this paper, I add to the current debate regarding the nature and value of despair. I argue that despair should not be viewed strictly as a form of sadness but rather as an emotional reaction through which we apprehend the loss of a future as likely. As such, despair is not only valuable because it provides a reflective break. Instead, it is a response of restless apathy which prepares us both to retreat and renounce our commitments, and to launch last resort “desperate” acts. Despair is not only valuable as an antidote to wishful hoping but, more fundamentally, because it counteracts our resistance to reconsidering plans we are diachronically committed to. As beings with temporally extended agency, we form intentions that guide, monitor, and rationally control action across time. Despair allows us to respond to the disheartening lowering of chances of success by urgently reconsidering our plans, in spite of our inherent resistance to doing so.

items.title: Achievement and Completion: Dispositions in the Middle Works of Sartre and Wittgenstein.
items.abstract: This article proposes a reflexion about the place and eventual contribution of dispositions to our understandings, explanations, and conceptions of actions by a comparative study of the conceptions of dispositions of Wittgenstein and Sartre in their middle works. Dispositions have indeed been traditionally assumed as providing middle grounds for knowledge as a whole. However, accounting for a difficulty with respect to our expressions of dispositions can serve to elucidate that the actualist conception of possibility and correlative coercive conception of necessity criticized by both Sartre and Wittgenstein is both superfluous and misleading. Indeed, although expressions of dispositions are relatively sufficient to account for some of our reasonings and practices, naive dispositionalism poses difficulties which need to be addressed. Both Sartre and Wittgenstein elucidate that solving such difficulties involve accounting for disposition as action. For, although dispositions can be relatively abstracted from contexts and circumstances, thusly proceeding leaves us with a thin or tenuous concept of dispositions as propensions or inclinations. By contrast, accounting for the thickness displayed by the concept of disposition involves, both according to Sartre and to Wittgenstein, the achievement of the elucidation of the relevance of the practice of disposition to our conceptions of dispositions.

items.title: Automative Agency and Responsibility.
items.abstract: Increase in uses of variously designed automated artificial agents renders pressing the resolution of conceptual and practical problems related to involvements of responsibilities and correlative juridical liabilities. Can an automated artificial agent be held responsible and eventually juridically liable for the realization of an action? In some cases, to ascribe juridal personhood to an automated artificial agent might seem required to render some actions judicable. But in some cases, to refuse juridical personhood to such agents might seem required to account for the responsibilities and juridical liabilities of their conceivers, producers, and users. Floridi summarized different approaches to address this problem (2023, 113-135). The first consists in ascribing juridical liability to such agents (Hallevy, 2011, 12-17). The second, in considering such agents as means of actions (Hallevy, 2011, 4; Pagallo, 2017, 21). The third involves integrating the importance of relevant knowledge to assess actions realized by such agents (MacAllister, 38-40). And the fourth involves evaluating the sufficiency of risk assessments of their developers to account for the judicability of actions achievable by such agents (Hallevy, 2011, 7-12). In this article, I argue that relative congruency of these approaches should be further integrated to address the tension generated by apparently mutually incompatible constraints relevant to relatable yet different contexts. For this purpose, I argue that Turing’s account of the involvements of thought ascriptions to machines (1950) and Wittgenstein’s criticism of `private language’ (Uçan, 2024; Wittgenstein, 2009) should be integrated to think the derivativeness of action ascriptions to automated artificial agents.

items.title: The Agonist: A Nietzsche Circle Journal, Vol. XX, No. 1 (Spring 2026).
items.abstract: As the journal of the Nietzsche Circle, The Agonist has always been driven by the mission to reflect on Nietzsche’s continued influence and relevance in our times, with a special emphasis on the vital role of art in contemporary culture. True to the philosopher-writer-composer from whom our Circle takes its name, The Agonist, Vol. XX, No. 1 contains fresh perspectives from a variety of traditions and methodologies: philosophical-historical, ontological, moral, literary, aesthetic, and always critical.

items.title: The Origin of Difference.
items.abstract: Previous papers in this research program explored consciousness, worldhood, meaning, and significance as conditions underlying the emergence of inhabitable reality. Each investigation revealed a deeper layer of organisation. Consciousness appeared to presuppose worldhood, worldhood presupposed meaning, and meaning presupposed significance. The present paper extends this progression by examining distinction. -/- Experience appears structured through distinctions. Meaning depends upon differences. Significance operates through distinctions that matter. Yet distinctions themselves are rarely examined. What role do they play in the organisation of experience? -/- The paper investigates distinction through the perspectives of experience, meaning, language, metaphysics, and significance. It argues that distinction occupies a foundational position within the broader framework developed in earlier papers. Experience, meaning, significance, and worldhood all appear to presuppose distinctions, suggesting that distinction represents the deepest condition yet identified within the architecture of experience. -/- The investigation further reveals that distinction occupies a unique position within inquiry itself. Attempts to account for distinction repeatedly encounter distinction already in operation, raising important questions concerning the relationship between difference, thought, language, and explanation. -/- The paper concludes that distinction plays a more fundamental role in experience than previously recognized and that any account of consciousness, worldhood, meaning, or significance must eventually confront the problem of difference.

items.title: The Natureless Act: A Left-Hand Path Metaphysics.
items.abstract: The Natureless Act builds metaphysics from a single claim: the absence of fixed nature is the condition of freedom. The free act is what no prior essence, law, or system can contain, and the book follows it through selfhood, relation, world, death, and godhood. Its central move is self-naming: the refusal to let inherited sediment, given identity, or cosmic order decide what the self is. Freedom is the power of each act to break the authority of what has already been formed. It contributes to debates on free will, anti-essentialism, personal identity, and philosophy of religion by treating freedom as an act irreducible to essence or prior causal description.

items.title: From Possibility to Realization: Quantum Admissibility and the Limits of Nonuniform Outcome Support.
items.abstract: This manuscript introduces quantum admissibility as a constraint-based framework for distinguishing possibility, probability, admissibility, and realization in quantum outcome space. The central proposal is that the quantum state specifies amplitude-supported possible outcomes, while the physical context determines which outcomes possess sufficient support to become realized as stable, accessible records. -/- The framework is developed in conservative and strong forms. In the conservative form, admissibility is uniform across physically allowed outcomes and the Born rule is recovered exactly. In the strong form, outcome probabilities are formally weighted by a context-dependent admissibility factor or, equivalently, by a non-negative admissibility penalty. The strong formulation is not asserted as established physics; it is presented as a falsifiable extension path requiring independently specified penalties and prospective testing against residual deviations from Born-rule expectations. -/- The manuscript further develops consistency constraints on the strong form. The operator version of admissibility is shown to reduce to standard quantum filtering or state update, rather than a new measurement dynamics. The scalar nonuniform weighting route is constrained by independence and coarse-graining requirements, under which admissibility either becomes uniform or loses consistency as an outcome-level probability rule. These results position quantum admissibility primarily as a disciplined support-language for realization, while sharply limiting its status as a modification of standard quantum mechanics. -/- The manuscript relates admissibility to decoherence, record formation, generalized measurement, double-slit and which-path contexts, boundary-sensitive support, experimental falsifiability, and the limits of nonuniform outcome support. It does not introduce a hidden variable, consciousness-based collapse mechanism, new force, or modified Schrödinger dynamics. Instead, it provides a structured vocabulary for asking which possible outcomes possess enough contextual support to become real, and clarifies why the natural strong reweighting route is mathematically constrained.

items.title: The Case for Spatial Structure of Auditory Experiences.
items.abstract: A common view in the contemporary philosophy of perception is that experiences possess both experiential content and experiential structure. While contents characterize what is presented by an experience, structures are stable ways of organizing content. The experiential structures that have attracted the most philosophical attention are spatial structures, which have usually been considered in the context of visual modality. However, the modes of spatial organization may not be the same for all types of experiences, and visual experiential structures cannot be automatically applied to experiences associated with other modalities. The aim of this paper is to present both the current state and possible further developments of the debate on the spatial structures of auditory experiences. In particular, I present the doubts regarding the presence of auditory spatial structure and show that a plausible account of auditory spatial structure can be developed by combining considerations on silence perception and auditory attention.

items.title: Brouwer’s Creating Subject and Turing’s Universal Machine as Ideal Models of Mathematical Reasoning.
items.pub: In Vladimir Drekalović, Science, Philosophy of Science and Scientific Methodology II. Podgorica: Golbi. pp. 189–202.
items.venue: Science, Philosophy of Science and Scientific Methodology II
items.abstract: One possible way to understand how reasoning occurs in mathematics is to posit an ideal mind that mirrors our own thinking. Two contrasting paradigms can be identified in Turing’s view on computability and Brouwer’s intuitionism. While the Universal Machine captures mathematical development through mechanical processes, the Creating Subject theory situates this activity within constructive acts of mental experience. This paper investigates how idealizing cognition as subjective-experiential rather than deterministic-mechanical can help address certain limitations in Turing’s original conception. Drawing on van Atten (2008), I propose re-evaluating the tensions between these frameworks to enhance the classical perspective, outlining a hybrid model where mechanical computability is extended by the intuitionistic concept of mental experience. This synthesis demonstrates that experiential features such as temporal intuition, free decision, and reflexivity are essential for an accurate account of reasoning in mathematics.

items.title: The Evolution of Consciousness: The Quantum Interface of Al-Fu'ād and the Noise-Free Signal of Divine Revelation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes an interdisciplinary framework integrating evolutionary biology, Penrose-Hameroff Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR) quantum mechanics, and classical Arabic ontological linguistics to address the "Hard Problem of Consciousness." We argue that physical cosmology and metaphysical revelation are localized phase-shifts of an all-pervading teleological "Divine Field." Utilizing a comprehensive etymological root-analysis of the Arabic segments associated with Light (Nūr), we demonstrate a structural correlation between quantum dynamics (localization, wave-confinement, and state collapse) and biological systems. We model the microtubular network as a biological quantum resonator cascade that filters this universal steering field into a localized animal self, optimizing thermodynamic stability through a proposed biochemical "Quantum-Toggle." Finally, we map the post-primitive transition of human cognition following the infusion of the Transcendent Ego, establishing the analytical boundaries between acquired cosmic knowledge (Al-Fu'ād) and direct prophetic revelation (Wahī) in regulating human evolutionary crises.

items.title: The illusion of reality: how (not) to think of hallucination.
items.abstract: It is surprisingly difficult to provide an account of hallucination that captures all the cases that clinicians typically class as hallucinations, without at the same time admitting cases that would not typically be classed as such. Most attempts to specify exactly what a hallucination is supposed to be fails to meet at least one of these conditions, as we show in the first part of the paper. We then proceed to develop an account of hallucination that meets both conditions. Central to this account is a discussion of two key notions in much need of clarification: the notion that hallucinations have a ‘sense of reality’, and the notion that hallucinations are ‘perception-like’. Settling on the exact meaning of these two notions allows us to offer an account of hallucination that captures all cases typically classified as hallucination and only such cases.

items.title: Is AI Intelligent? A Philosophical Perspective.
items.abstract: This paper develops a philosophical interpretation of artificial intelligence grounded in the Philosophy of Belonging. It argues that intelligence possesses a temporal structure composed of two complementary dimensions: synchrony and diachrony.
