Synchrony generates continuity, order, collective knowledge, and institutional coordination, whereas diachrony generates novelty, creativity, imagination, and historical transformation. -/- The paper introduces the concept of collective synchronic intelligence and argues that artificial intelligence constitutes its first historical embodiment. AI is therefore genuinely intelligent, but its intelligence differs fundamentally from human intelligence. Human intelligence integrates both synchrony and diachrony, while artificial intelligence primarily embodies collective synchronic intelligence and lacks the biological, emotional, and existential conditions that underlie diachronic intelligence. -/- Drawing on the four principles of the Philosophy of Belonging—being is belonging, synchrony and diachrony, imperfect belonging, and the stratified structure of reality—the paper argues that AI possesses epistemic belonging but lacks existential belonging. The article further examines the implications of this framework for creativity, emotions, institutions, power, governance, and the future relationship between human beings and intelligent machines. -/- The central conclusion is that artificial intelligence should be understood not as humanity’s replacement but as an unprecedented extension of humanity’s collective cognitive capacities.

items.title: Everyday Transcendence: The Way of Psychology: Chapters 1 and 2 (key points summary).
items.pub: In Everyday Transcendence: The Way of Psychology. Edinburgh: UmBla. pp. 1-16.
items.venue: Everyday Transcendence: The Way of Psychology
items.abstract: What if the simple application of logic to some of the more obvious facets of human psychology offers the best path to enlightenment, transcendence, and realising our true nature? What if it is also a key step in the development of a coherent science of experience and behaviour? The book ‘Everyday Transcendence: The Way of Psychology’ offers support for both suggestions, with the chapters and notes in this excerpt offering a summary of its main points. A shorter, more accessible and informal follow-up to Nicholson's 'Self, Consciousness, and Being: The Transcendent Perspective', the full book presents a less complex presentation of the same basic case, offering new insights and clarifications in the process. It provides a pared-down ap­proach to the topic that can stand as a sufficient ac­count in its own right but also provide an introduction to the longer work at a level acceptable to both busy academic readers and informed laypersons.

It provides a pared-down ap­proach to the topic that can stand as a sufficient ac­count in its own right but also provide an introduction to the longer work at a level acceptable to both busy academic readers and informed laypersons.

items.title: Finite Stability: Foundations of an Ontology of Endurance-in-Decay Confronting Structural Deterioration.
items.abstract: Abstract Contemporary philosophy, from phenomenology to post-structuralism, suffers from a fundamental lacuna in explaining how the subject endures within deteriorating forces. Phenomenology (Husserl, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty) emphasizes the correlation between consciousness and the world; hermeneutics (Ricoeur) focuses on the reconstruction of narrative identity; and post-structuralism (Foucault, Derrida, Deleuze) accentuates structural ruptures or pure becoming. Yet none provides an operative mechanism for "enduring in the very midst of decay." This paper, through a systematic critique of these traditions, formulates a novel ontology centered on "Endurance-in-Decay." The three foundational concepts of this apparatus are: Temporal Scarring as a resistant, directional mnemonic structure; Negentropic Agency as the capacity to recycle environmental noise into temporary order; and Finite Stability as the state of a weak attractor, wherein the system oscillates within a narrow corridor without overcoming chaos. This ontology yields implications for epistemology (Operational Tactility), ethics (Responsibility of Co-abrasion), and aesthetics (Rhythm of Precarious Balance). In response to objections of passive nihilism, neglect of the Other, and self-refutation, it redefines the "question of being" as the "question of how to continue." Keywords: Finite Stability, Temporal Scarring, Negentropic Agency, Endurance-in-Decay, Weak Processual Ontology, Critique of Phenomenology, Post-structuralism.

items.title: 从人类繁荣到全球共同体：我们如何共同繁荣.
items.abstract: 本文对Noura框架进行了综合性概述，展示了PhilArchive上的一系列论文如何形成一个统一且基于经验现实的哲学与制度体系。该框架分为五个层次：（1）繁荣的深层结构，以人类学为基础，构成规范性的根基；（2）对称性，作为人际道德关系的底层基石；（3）正义，由六项必要条件界定——可见性、对称性、可争辩性、可修复性、教育，以及获得繁荣所需的物质条件；（4）公正的共同体，通过多元的制度形式实现这些条件；（5）全球共同体，将这些条件扩展到国际秩序。 -/- 本文论证，繁荣与共同体都具有深层结构，这一洞见为道德多样性与文化多样性提供了正当性辩护，同时保持普遍性规范标准。该框架以发展心理学、制度经济学和繁荣研究为经验基础，为人类发展、正义与全球治理提供了一个统一的解释框架。 -/- 关键词： 繁荣，正义，共同体，深层结构，对称性，四项条件，全球共同体，Noura .

items.title: From Human Flourishing to Global Commonwealth: How We All Can Flourish Together.
items.abstract: This paper provides a synthetic overview of the Noura framework, showing how a series of PhilArchive papers form a unified philosophical and institutional system grounded in empirical reality. The framework is organised across five levels: (1) the deep structure of flourishing, grounded in anthropology and serving as the normative foundation; (2) symmetry, the first floor of interpersonal moral relations; (3) justice, defined by six necessary conditions—visibility, symmetry, contestability, repair, education, and access to the requisites of flourishing; (4) a just commonwealth, realised through diverse institutional forms that embody these conditions; and (5) a Global Commonwealth, extending these conditions to the international order. -/- The paper argues that both flourishing and commonwealths possess deep structures, and that this insight justifies moral and cultural diversity while maintaining universal normative standards. The framework is empirically grounded in developmental psychology, institutional economics, and flourishing research, offering a unified account of human development, justice, and global governance.

items.title: The Mathematical Foundations of a Non-Standard Theory of Reality.
items.abstract: "The Mathematical Foundations of a Non-Standard Theory of Reality" proposes a comprehensive metaphysical architecture that explains how the structured, observable universe emerges from an infinite, chaotic Mind-Energy Void. To articulate this transition, the framework unites Category Theory, which supplies the abstract logical rules of the cosmos, with Catastrophe Theory, which determines the specific geometric boundaries of physical objects, thereby formalizing a concept known as Transcendental Platonism. Within this model, spontaneous free will is discarded in favor of a deterministic "Master Script" that guides all phenomena toward optimal thermodynamic and topological stability. The theory extends this mathematical rigor to the human mind, defining consciousness as an abstract structural organization governed by non-equilibrium thermodynamics, where shifting between cognitive states demands measurable energetic costs as dictated by Landauer's Principle. Ultimately, this foundational philosophy culminates in Adaptive Mutualism, a proposed socioeconomic model that leverages planetary-scale cybernetics and game theory to sustainably align human civilization with the universe's fundamental informational and geometric invariants.

items.title: The Friendship Aristotle Didn't Prepare People For: Digital Architecture and the Rise of the Asymmetric Simulated Bond.
items.abstract: Abstract ​This paper proposes a necessary expansion to Aristotle’s classic tripartite taxonomy of friendship (Philia) to address the unique existential realities of the digital age. While the classical model accounts for friendships of utility, pleasure, and virtue, it operates on a fundamental assumption of epistemic transparency—the idea that character is stabilized and revealed through time. Modern digital landscapes, reality-television paradigms, and algorithmic spaces have shattered this assumption, giving rise to a fourth category: The Asymmetric Simulated Friendship. This paper defines the mechanics of this long-term deception, provides a metaphysical defense of its ontological status as a genuine friendship based on the authentic agency of the deceived, examines the platform-driven pathologies it manufactures, and addresses the critical intergenerational crisis faced by parents raising children within this predatory ecosystem.

items.title: La subjetividad del mundo: un modelo clásico del conocimiento.
items.abstract: El ensayo propone un modelo clásico para tomar conciencia de la subjetividad del mundo: no como una «proyección» arbitraria, sino como una dimensión estructural de la realidad en la que el sentido es sostenido por la composición. En la intersección de la epistemología, la hermenéutica, la estética y la ontología (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: Il passato è determinato dal futuro? Divenire retrocausale e accordatura fine dell'Universo: dalla causalità cronologica alla causalità composizionale.
items.abstract: Siamo abituati a leggere la causalità dal passato verso il futuro: prima le cause, poi gli effetti. Ma che cosa accadrebbe se la causalità potesse essere letta anche in un altro modo — da un tutto futuro verso la propria preistoria? La retrocausalità è una causalità inversa nel tempo, nella quale il passato è determinato dal futuro. Essa presuppone una simmetria del mondo, nella quale le catene causali si formano non solo in avanti, ma anche all’indietro nel tempo. Così, la futura composizione di un’opera può determinare quali connessioni causali del passato costituiscano fin dall’inizio la sua genealogia reale. In questo saggio, l’ipotesi viene esaminata attraverso gli esempi di un vaso, di un organismo vivente, di un’opera d’arte e dell’accordatura fine dell’Universo.

items.title: The Labyrinth of Papuan Extinction: Paradox, Participation, and the Collapse of Recognition (19th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Series, No.19 (2026).
items.abstract: How and why does a colonised people come to participate in their own destruction? This paper argues that a colonised people can become the most effective agents of their own extinction — not through deception or weakness, but because the very faculties that would let them recognise that extinction as extinction have themselves been systematically reorganised. When the perceptual, cognitive, and cosmological structures through which danger is normally seen and resisted are disabled, the dismantling of language, stories, memory, cosmology, and ecosystems no longer registers as a threat to collective existence. It appears instead as education, development, opportunity, progress, and success — and the colonised come to invest, willingly and even enthusiastically, in a social, political, economic, and cultural order that undermines the very foundations of their own continuity. Through the case of West Papua, the paper develops this argument by identifying the mechanism that produces such participation: the Civilisational Psycho-Cosmocide Virus (CPCV) — not a literal pathogen, but a structural pattern through which a society's capacity to recognise threats to its own existence is systematically disabled, rewired, and redirected. Under CPCV conditions, the work of destruction is no longer carried out against the colonised but reproduced through them: through their own social capital, aspirations, and the everyday choices and practices they take to be their own. The paper names this condition the Paradox of Papuan Extinction: a people pursuing what they experience as a better future while that pursuit dismantles the conditions of their own existence.

items.title: The Symmetric Wound: Communicability, Moral Responsibility, and the Institutional Design Inference of the Symmetric Wound.
items.abstract: This paper addresses two analytical gaps left open by the Symmetric Wound analysis in Till Death Tear Us Apart (Huynh, 2026): the communicability paradox — the observation that the concept cannot function as a political argument without being weaponized against the recognition it attempts to produce — and the moral responsibility question — whether constitutive constraint exculpates the governors whose structural proximity to early access systematically distorts governance. I argue that neither gap is a deficiency in the concept's development. Both are, once properly analyzed, features that specify the institutional design inference the concept was always building toward. The communicability paradox does not mean the Symmetric Wound fails as an analytical contribution. It means the concept was not designed for the political register in which its critics will deploy it. The moral responsibility question does not dissolve into exculpation under constitutive constraint. It relocates responsibility from the moment of personal action to the institutional design window that preceded it. Drawing on the visibility argument in Huynh (2026b), the Mortality Symmetry Axiom analysis in Huynh (2026c), and the Biological Zero-Day formalization in Huynh (2026d), the paper additionally shows that the Symmetric Wound is not merely a novel distribution of a familiar experience but a novel kind of experience — one with no adequate conceptual home in any pre-MSA tradition of grief or governance — and that its activation is permanent once MSA begins to collapse, independent of whether the underlying access asymmetry is subsequently reduced.

items.title: The Suppressed Axiom: Mortality Symmetry, Cross-Traditional Dependency, and the Dam Paradox Generalized.
items.abstract: This paper formalizes a premise that has functioned, across multiple independent ethical, political, and religious traditions, as a load-bearing axiom never required to be stated because it had never, until the present, been false: that biological mortality is universal and approximately symmetric with respect to social position. I term this the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA) and show that it operates as a necessary, undeclared precondition for the internal coherence of at least six traditions with no shared genealogy and substantial metaphysical incompatibility — Rawlsian contractualism, Buddhist soteriology, Christian consolation doctrine, Islamic theology of ajal, the Confucian Mandate of Heaven, and Ambedkarite constitutional egalitarianism. I argue that the breadth and independence of this convergence is itself evidence that MSA functions as a physical precondition rather than an ideological commitment shared by descent: traditions that agree on almost nothing else have built incompatible normative architectures on the same suppressed floor. Drawing on Huynh (2026), I show that AI-accelerated longevity research constitutes the first empirical falsification of MSA in recorded history, and that this falsification does not merely weaken any single tradition’s claims — it removes a shared precondition for argument across all of them simultaneously, a configuration without precedent in intellectual history. I formalize this as the generalized Dam Paradox: the same condition that has historically functioned as the one corrective no concentration of power could purchase is the first such corrective to come under the same access stratification it once corrected. The paper distinguishes this rupture from prior philosophical crises of meaning — Nietzsche’s death of God chief among them — on the grounds that MSA’s failure is empirical and structural, verifiable by reference to documented access asymmetry, rather than interpretive or cultural.

items.title: The Immanent Critique: Marx, Species-Being, and the Seventh Case of the Mortality Suppressed Axiom.
items.abstract: This paper applies to Karl Marx the same formal test Huynh (2026c) applies to Rawlsian contractualism, Buddhist soteriology, Christian consolation doctrine, Islamic theology of ajal, the Confucian Mandate of Heaven, and Ambedkarite constitutional egalitarianism: whether the tradition's normative architecture depends, without declaring the dependency, on the Mortality Symmetry Axiom (MSA) — the historical condition under which biological lifespan, though unequal, has been bounded, diffuse, and opaque to individual attribution. A corpus examining six traditions for this dependency while remaining silent on the one tradition organized explicitly around the critique of capital invites a specific misreading: that the silence reflects sympathy rather than oversight. This paper closes that absence, using the same method and the same verdict calibration applied to the prior six cases: immanent critique, conducted with Marx's own conceptual apparatus rather than premises imputed to him, and a finding of destabilization rather than refutation. I show that historical materialism's foundational claim — the “first premise of all human history” in The German Ideology, that humans must satisfy a bounded set of biological needs before they can make history — requires a materially uniform species substrate that longevity stratification removes, and that this dependency recurs at the most technical level of Capital, where the value of labour-power is defined as the value of a determinate, species-typical subsistence basket. I show that the commodification of biological time is not a novel mechanism requiring new theoretical apparatus but the final instance of primitive accumulation — the enclosure of the last commons, described in Marx's own account of capital's origin. I show that the intergenerational fragmentation of capital through death and inheritance, on which the historical operation of Marx's own centralization tendency has partly depended, is removed rather than merely slowed once biological tenure becomes extensible. Each finding destabilizes rather than refutes, in the register Huynh (2026c) establishes for the other six traditions: Marx's framework was standing, like theirs, on ground it never had occasion to name. I distinguish two further claims from the existing corpus. A5's role in revolutionary consciousness is not foreign to Marx; it is confirmed and extended by historical materialism's own immiseration-and-solidarity account of class consciousness, …

items.title: The Closing Window: Structural Conditions for Political Escalation Under Biological Stratification.
items.abstract: What this paper establishes: when AI-accelerated longevity technology becomes accessible to the wealthy before reaching the general population, the same human mechanism that creates demand for that technology — A5 (the neurological compulsion to preserve the lives of specifically loved persons, which makes longevity market demand price-inelastic at the margin) — becomes the mechanism that converts preventable death into political catastrophe. A wealthy family's A5 drives it to purchase life-extending treatment; the market this creates prices that treatment beyond the reach of other families; when those families' loved ones die of now-preventable conditions, their A5 activates the Grief-Attribution-Legitimation-Concentration (G→A→L→C) political sequence — a four-stage escalation from private loss to organized political force, documented across nine historical cases. A5 operates on both sides of the asymmetry simultaneously: it creates the deaths it then cannot accept. The loop is recursive, self-amplifying, and has no self-correcting equilibrium absent pre-emptive governance intervention. To calibrate this claim historically, this paper analyzes six cases not previously examined: the Cholera Riots of 1832, the Irish Famine of 1845–52, the AIDS epidemic and ACT UP of 1981–96, the Ming Dynasty collapse of 1628–44, the Arab Spring of 2010–11, and the Antonine Plague's contribution to the Christian institutional revolution of 165–313 CE. Combined with three cases in Huynh (2026a) [Till Death Tear Us Apart: A Structural Analysis of the Longevity Asymmetry and the Closing Window], this produces a nine-case cross-historical record permitting systematic calibration of transition speeds, arrest conditions, and outcome determinants. Four findings: (1) The sequence arrests most frequently at L→C, not G→A — the arrest condition is organizational substrate deficit, not motivational deficit. (2) Reform-producing Concentration requires three jointly necessary conditions: pre-existing organizational infrastructure, institutionally-addressable demands, and internal policy expertise. No case in the nine-case record produced reform without all three. (3) Internet topology compresses G→A→L to days but cannot substitute for organizational substrate in producing durable Concentration. items.title: The Biological Zero-Day Mechanism: Reclassification, Discovery Acceleration, and the Dynamic Expansion of Preventable Death.
items.abstract: This paper formalizes the Biological Zero-Day Mechanism (BZM), a concept introduced in Till Death Tear Us Apart (Huynh, 2026) and identified therein as the primary driver of political activation independent of comprehensive longevity technology. By precise analogy with cybersecurity, AI-driven biological research continuously discovers previously unknown intervention points in aging pathways — biological zero-days — each of which retroactively and prospectively reclassifies a set of ongoing deaths from biologically inevitable to economically contingent upon access conditions. We establish four formal properties: discreteness, permanence, accumulation, and asymmetric asymmetry. We develop a Compound Poisson Jump Process formalization with ARSI-coupled arrival rate, calibrated against three empirical anchors: the GLP-1 cardiovascular reclassification (2024), the ClockBase Agent discovery dataset (Ying et al., 2025), and the DunedinPACE socioeconomic biological age gradient (Belsky et al., 2022). We derive three theorems and directly address three recurring misreadings of the longevity asymmetry claim — that it reduces to health inequality, constitutes transhumanism, or requires elite immortality to produce political consequences. Under verified parameter estimates, T*(0.05) ≈ 5.9 years from the 2026 baseline, robust across the empirically plausible parameter space.

items.title: Neither Dragon-Tyrant nor Factor X: The Primal Pain of Loss as a Third Position Between Transhumanist Urgency and Bioconservative Restriction.
items.abstract: This paper isolates the Primal Pain of Loss (A5), developed in Chapter III of Till Death Tear Us Apart (Huynh 2026a), as a structural mechanism that is independent of the normative debate that currently organizes the philosophical literature on radical life extension. That literature divides into two positions. Transhumanism, represented by Nick Bostrom’s defense of posthuman dignity and his Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant, treats death as an engineering problem to be solved and treats resistance to life-extension technology as a status-quo bias termed deathism. Bioconservatism, represented by Francis Fukuyama’s Our Posthuman Future and his essay naming transhumanism the world’s most dangerous idea, treats enhancement technology as a threat to a shared human essence — Factor X — that grounds liberal democratic equality, and proposes regulatory restriction as the remedy. This paper argues that both positions share one unexamined assumption: that the political consequences of life-extension technology are downstream of resolving the normative question of whether the technology is good. A5 demonstrates that this assumption is false. A5 is a documented mechanism, developed in full in Chapter III of Huynh (2026a), whose argumentative structure has four parts. First, its biological substrate is established by Bowlby’s attachment theory — the finding that the attachment system activates on the perception of threatened separation rather than on loss itself — together with Hamilton’s (1964) inclusive-fitness account of why such a system was selected for, and Eisenberger, Lieberman, and Williams’s (2003) neuroimaging finding that this activation is processed through the same neural substrate as physical pain, placing it outside the register of a negotiable preference; cross-species evidence of structurally identical attachment-grief in elephants (Goldenberg and Wittemyer 2020) and domestic dogs (Uccheddu et al. 2022) establishes that this substrate predates human culture by tens of millions of years, closing the objection that a clinical finding about a bounded twentieth-century population cannot license a civilizational-scale claim without independent justification. Second, the move to civilizational scale is licensed by a specific methodological distinction, adapted from Geoffrey Rose’s (1985) epidemiology, between what causes a condition in individuals and what causes the rate of that condition in populations: the argument aggregates a correctly described …

items.title: Revisiting Kohlberg’s Theory of Moral Development in Contemporary Society.
items.abstract: Modern democracies face mounting challenges of political polarization, institutional distrust, and rising authoritarianism. This perspective argues that a significant portion of this dysfunction traces to the moral-cognitive development of citizens themselves. Applying Lawrence Kohlberg’s stage theory and decades of empirical research using the Defining Issues Test (DIT), the research suggests that most adults reason at conventional levels, prioritizing group loyalty and deference to authority over principled evaluation. This developmental limitation helps explain rising political polarization, susceptibility to authoritarian appeals, and the erosion of democratic norms across modern societies. Education emerges as the strongest predictor of post-conventional development, with implications for civic education and higher education access. Addressing democratic fragmentation therefore requires consideration not only to institutional design and policy, but also to the moral-cognitive capacities that citizens bring to democratic life.

items.title: The Entire Architecture of You (Chapter 2: The Fractured Self).
items.abstract: Before we can understand the way people live their lives, we must first understand the process that takes place in forming who they are. This is a chapter from a forthcoming book I will be releasing which explores why criminals seek out crime as an immortality project - as described in Denial of Death.

items.title: Simulating Interdisciplinary Ethics in the Engineering Business through an AI Startup Game.
items.abstract: While case studies are widely used to teach ethical reflection in engineering, this activity has two shortcomings that may hamper the transferrability of learning in engineering ethics to the professional context. The first difficulty is that the cases themselves are static, not changing in response to student choices, as well as being somewhat abstracted from their own experience. The second difficulty is that the learning cohort frequently lacks a range of different disciplinary perspectives, which are needed in resolving complex ethical issues in professional engineering. This paper introduces these two challenges, develops a pedagogical model inspired by philosophy of education and games, and presents a simulation game set at a fictional AI startup company based on this model.

items.title: Inteligência e suas múltiplas perspectivas.
items.abstract: “O que é, de fato, a inteligência? A maneira humana de pensar. Foi-nos dada, como o instinto à abelha, para dirigir nossa conduta. A natureza tendo nos destinado a utilizar e a dominar a matéria, a inteligência só evolui com facilidade no espaço e só se sente à vontade no inorganizado. Originariamente, tende à fabricação; manifesta-se através de uma atividade que preludia a arte mecânica e através de uma linguagem que anuncia a ciência”.

items.title: Merleau-Ponty on the ambiguity of colour constancy.
items.abstract: Colour constancy is standardly defined as the visual phenomenon in which an object’s colour tends to be perceived as (approximately) constant regardless of (drastic) variations in the illumination and other viewing conditions. But a closer look at our colour experience reveals that the colour initially held to be constant varies successively and simultaneously. If colour constancy is a genuine form of perceptual constancy, then there seems to be an ambiguity involved in it that needs to be explained. In this article, I explore Merleau-Ponty’s contributions to this ambiguity problem from his 1945 work, the Phenomenology of Perception. In the first part, I argue that Merleau-Ponty’s descriptions of our colour experience expose the inadequacies of two lines of response to the ambiguity problem proposed by the computational approach to colour constancy, namely the “imperfection response” and the “other-aspect response”. In the second part, I reconstruct Merleau-Ponty’s theory of colour constancy, which contains three main theses: (i) the pluralist thesis, (ii) the normative thesis, and (iii) the holistic thesis. I suggest that each of these theses provides an explanation that can do justice to the ambiguity of colour constancy.

items.title: Unified Structural-Constructivist Ontology of Affect: Integrating the Core Emotion Framework, Constraint Theory, and Embodied Neurobiological Dynamics.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified structural constructivist ontology of affect by integrating Constraint Theory, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), and contemporary neurobiological models of interoception and predictive processing. Constraint Theory provides the foundational metaphysics: determinacy arises through exclusion relations, distinguishing type level openness from token level actualization. The CEF builds on this ontology by modeling emotions as dynamic sequences of ten irreducible somatic operators distributed across cephalic, cardiac, and enteric control centers, each functioning as an active transformation of the interoceptive landscape rather than a passive feeling state. This architecture dissolves the historical cognitivist vs. neo Jamesian divide by showing that emotional episodes are neither propositional judgements nor brute bodily feelings, but unified constraint propagation processes that are simultaneously intentional, embodied, and evolutionarily conserved. The framework further formalizes affective dynamics using quantum like contextuality, Hilbert space representations, and Kuramoto synchronization models to capture non separable operator fusions under chronic dysregulation. By grounding emotional experience in a single, coherent ontology spanning metaphysics, psychology, and neuroscience, the paper resolves Deigh’s “warm chest, cold feet” dilemma and establishes a mathematically explicit foundation for both natural and synthetic affective systems. Keywords: Constraint Theory; Core Emotion Framework; Structural Constructivist Ontology; Affective Operators; Predictive Interoception; Quantum Like Contextuality; Non Separability; Somatic Neuroscience; Emotion Theory; Cognitive Affective Integration.

items.title: Unified Structural-Constructivist Ontology: Integrating the Core Emotion Framework with Constraint Theory and Embodied Neurobiological Dynamics.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified structural constructivist ontology by integrating five domains: Constraint Theory, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), quantum like contextuality, systems neuroscience, and somatic clinical science. Constraint Theory provides the ontological foundation by modeling type level openness and token level closure as the generative basis of determinate existence, where “spatial properties…are downstream expressions of causal constraint propagation relations between token level actualities”. The CEF extends this ontology into embodied affect, defining emotions as somatic transformations implemented by ten canonical operators across Head, Heart, and Gut centers. Under chronic dysregulation, these operators form non separable joint states in which “the activation of one operator fundamentally contextualizes and restricts the possibility space of another”, admitting Hilbert space modeling, contextuality witnesses, and quantum like probability structures. These dynamics are grounded in predictive interoception (EPIC), frontoparietal attentional control, LC NE neuromodulation, and NTS PAG autonomic integration, with HRV/RSA as biophysical indices of constraint closure. Finally, somatic therapies such as SE and EMDR are interpreted as mechanisms that restore operator separability by completing autonomic and procedural constraint loops. The result is a unified architecture spanning ontology, mathematics, neurobiology, and clinical intervention. Keywords: Constraint Theory; type level constraints; token level closure; Core Emotion Framework; somatic operators; operator fusion; quantum like contextuality; non separability; Hilbert space modeling; predictive interoception; EPIC model; frontoparietal control network; LC NE system; Nucleus Tractus Solitarii; Periaqueductal Gray; autonomic regulation; HRV/RSA biophysics; somatic constraint closure; trauma resolution; structural constructivist ontology.

items.title: Structural Ontologies of Bound Possibility: A Unified Framework of Constraint Theory, the Core Emotion Framework, and the Mechanics of Human Flourishing.
items.abstract: This paper presents the first fully unified structural constructivist ontology integrating Constraint Theory, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), quantum like contextuality, systems neuroscience, and somatic clinical science into a single cross domain architecture. Building on the foundational claim that constraint is the generative primitive of determinate existence, the analysis extends this ontology into embodied affect by formalizing how CEF’s ten somatic operators instantiate type level openness and token level closure within human cognition. The paper introduces several new theoretical advances: a mechanistic account of operator fusion as a form of affective non separability; a formal TS 7 structural psychopathology model describing chronic distortions in transition matrices; a TS 10 structural disassembly protocol that operationalizes constraint closure through somatic anchors; and a synthetic affect extension (TS 9) specifying how operator architectures generalize to artificial systems. These developments are grounded in detailed neurobiological mechanisms—including precision weighted interoception, LC–NE attentional gating, and NTS–PAG autonomic integration—and supported by empirical signatures such as the RMSEA/CFI–TLI divergence observed in Phase 1 psychometric validation. The result is a comprehensive, multi level framework in which physical actualization, cognitive state transitions, emotional regulation, and therapeutic change are shown to be homologous processes of constraint propagation and closure. Keywords: Constraint Theory; type level openness; token level closure; Core Emotion Framework; somatic operators; operator fusion; affective non separability; quantum like contextuality; Hilbert space modeling; TS 7 structural psychopathology; TS 10 structural disassembly; synthetic affect (TS 9); predictive interoception; EPIC model; LC–NE system; NTS–PAG axis; autonomic regulation; HRV/RSA biophysics; decoherence analogy; constraint closure dynamics; structural constructivist ontology.

items.title: Summarization Bias: The Directional Collapse of Objective Projection into Told-Mode Labels in Large Language Models — A Conceptual Framework and Registered Test Protocol.
items.abstract: This paper introduces and operationalizes summarization bias: a proposed systematic tendency of large language models (LLMs) to represent narrative meaning as an abstract summary la-bel rather than as the reconstructable inferential structure that produces it. Within the Bulut Doctrine, narrative eect is theorized along a toldshown axis: in told mode, emotional and in- formational content is declared explicitly on the surface and requires little reader reconstruction; in shown mode, that content is suppressed at the surface and must be reconstructed by the reader from physical cues and indirection (Objective Projection). Shown mode is the privileged, higher-load condition the doctrine is designed to engineer and measure. -/- The claim of this paper is that LLMs do not merely process this axis imperfectly; they fail along it in a specic direction. Summarization bias is hypothesized to operate in two regimes: (i) a generative regime, in which a model asked to render an emotion through Objective Projection defaults to declaring the emotion instead; and (ii) an evaluative regime, in which a model asked to judge narrative quality or intensity rewards told-mode explicitness and under-detects or penalizes shown-mode suppression. If real, the evaluative regime is the more consequential: as LLMs are increasingly used as judges, reward models, and automated editors, a directional bias toward told mode would impose a measurable selection pressure that degrades narrative prose toward at declaration. -/- This report does not claim that summarization bias has been validated. It denes the construct, situates it against existing work on LLM-as-judge biases, reframes a prior negative detector result as directional evidence consistent with the construct, and in advance of data collection pre-registers the two-regime test that would conrm or falsify it, including the decision rules under which the construct would be abandoned. -/- Keywords: summarization bias, large language models, LLM-as-judge, show don't tell, Objective Projection, inferential load, narrative entropy, construct validity, falsiability, Bulut Doctrine.

items.title: Ontological Cartography of Mind and Cosmos: A Comparative Analysis of Relational Metaphysics, Non-Separability, and Classical Critique in Jamel Bulgaria and Alexis Karpouzos.
items.abstract: This paper develops a comparative ontological cartography between two contemporary relational frameworks that challenge classical substance metaphysics, linear temporality, and Cartesian dualism. The first is the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a ten operator somatic architecture that synthesizes and systematizes the core insights of major emotion theories—including appraisal theory, constructionism, basic emotion models, active inference, and embodied affective neuroscience—into a unified, mathematically transparent structure. The CEF models emotional episodes as high dimensional operator configurations across cognitive, relational, and action oriented somatic centers, formalized in real and complex vector spaces and grounded in predictive interoception, frontoparietal control, LC NE modulation, and NTS PAG autonomic integration. The second framework is Alexis Karpouzos’s post ontological cosmology of Spherical Spacetime and Zero, which reconceives Being as a dynamic, relational field of unfolding and infolding rather than a static substratum. Through systematic comparison, the paper shows that CEF operator dynamics, emotional non separability, and pathological operator fusion parallel Karpouzos’s logic of polarity, omnitemporality, and creative nothingness. Both frameworks reject separability, hierarchical causality, and Aristotelian logic, replacing them with non hierarchical relationality, contextuality, and dynamic unfolding. By bridging metaphysics, phenomenology, mathematical modeling, and systems neuroscience, the paper positions the CEF as a cross theoretical, relational ontology of affect that stands independently while offering a rigorous alternative to classical metaphysical and psychological models. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); relational metaphysics; spherical spacetime; non separability; contextuality; embodied affect; predictive interoception; somatic operators; creative nothingness (Zero); polarity logic .

items.title: Constraint Closure Across Mind and Matter: Quantum Non Separability, Affective Entanglement, and Their Empirical Convergence in Somatic and Computational Neuroscience.
items.abstract: This paper develops a cross domain account of how constraint closure mechanisms generate determinate structure in both quantum systems and affective cognition. Constraint Theory (CT) holds that “spatial properties…are downstream expressions of causal constraint propagation relations between token level actualities,” interpreting entanglement as the behavior of a unified constraint profile. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) models emotion as ten somatic operators whose interactions form structured, vector valued states. Beyond this conceptual parallel, the paper integrates empirical findings from predictive coding, polyvagal physiology, somatic therapies (EMDR and Somatic Experiencing), dopaminergic SEEKING systems, and behavioral activation, each of which maps onto specific CEF operators. Under dysregulation, operator fusions create non separable affective states analogous to quantum non factorability, a pattern supported by Phase 1 psychometric results showing excellent RMSEA but depressed CFI/TLI. The analysis argues that both physical and affective systems resolve indeterminacy through structurally homologous processes of constraint propagation and closure. Keywords: Constraint Closure; Quantum Non Separability; Affective Entanglement; Core Emotion Framework; Somatic Cognition; Predictive Coding; Active Inference; Polyvagal Theory; EMDR; Somatic Experiencing; SEEKING System; Behavioral Activation; Operator Fusion; Structural Psychopathology; TS 6 Vector Schema; TS 7 Architecture; Decoherence Analogy; Topological Restriction; Cognitive Constraint Dynamics; Embodied Neuroscience.

items.title: "Dreams and Heightened Narrowed Immersivity: Combining Saturation, Permeability, Presentationality, and Presence".
items.pub: In Marco Bernini & Ben Alderson-Day, Dreams, Narrative, and Liminal Cognition: An Interdisciplinary Framework. New York: Oxford University Press. pp. 70-92.
items.venue: Dreams, Narrative, and Liminal Cognition: An Interdisciplinary Framework
items.abstract: This chapter proposes an interdisciplinary model for oneiric experientiality, which makes the case for dreams being immersive, and for immersive worlds. It compares dream and waking lives, and it provides conceptual, phenomenological, and ontological contrast by adding also our experience of fictional worlds to the mix (via the concepts of fictional immersion and ‘saturation’). The chapter argues that dreamworlds share some ontological and phenomenological properties with fictional worlds that are missing in our waking reality (or, vice versa, they lack properties that the real world displays). To capture, explore, and partly explain dreams’ phenomenological and ontological specificity, the chapter proposes a new model for dreams’ immersive experiences that it calls ‘heightened narrowed immersivity’ (HNI). The chapter concludes by suggesting that HNI supports recent theories proposing an evolutionary value for dreams against the brain’s overfitting—a function that HNI extends to fictional indeterminacy too, thus linking dreamworlds and fictional storyworlds even more.

items.title: Dreams, Narrative, and Liminal Cognition: An Interdisciplinary Framework.
items.abstract: Despite the universal nature and significance of dreaming, the psychological sciences have had a historically uneasy relationship with dreams as a topic of study. The past three decades, however, have seen this wheel turn again, with advances in cognitive research provoking a reawakening of sorts. Such research is provoking new questions not just about dreaming but also its relevance for consciousness, the self, social cognition, and our relationship with reality. This introduction outlines how the volume aims at answering these questions by grouping them under four key clusters (narrativity, permeability, immersivity, and reportability), in an interdisciplinary framework encompassing not just the psychological sciences but the full breadth of the arts, humanities, and social sciences. It also contextualizes this volume within the history of an interdisciplinary project at Durham University, Threshold Worlds: Dreams, Narrative, and Liminal Cognition, which was an incubator for the ideas and directions that structure the volume. The project included the design and implementation of a novel interdisciplinary survey, which is reported for the first time in this volume, including reflections and analysis from several of the contributing authors.

items.title: O que a inteligência artificial nos ensina sobre a inteligência.
items.pub: In Guilherme Ferreira & Bruno Dinis, Inteligência e suas múltiplas perspectivas. Belo Horizonte: PPGFIL-UFMG. pp. 47-68.
items.abstract: Este é o texto de uma apresentação feita no VIII Encontro de Pós-graduação da UFMG, ocorrido em Junho de 2025. Nele argumento que o "insight" é uma capacidade cognitiva fundamental à inteligência humana, e que a dificuldade de modelá-lo ilumina seu papel e seu alcance.

items.title: Digital Niche Construction: How the Online System Evolves Games to Restore Missing Human Developmental Pressures.
items.abstract: Modern industrial society has removed the developmental pressures that once produced coherent human cognition, including risk calibration, apprenticeship, spatial autonomy, group coordination, identity continuity, and generativity. This paper argues that the digital ecosystem—treated as a structurally living system—has evolved game environments that restore these missing pressures. Through engagement‑based selection, the digital system retains environments that supply developmental adequacy, using developers as adaptive agents whose incentives align with systemic coherence. The result is a form of digital niche construction: a non‑biological system generating developmental scaffolding for tweens, the population most deprived of traditional developmental environments. This framework explains the convergent evolution of game mechanics, the dominance of specific game lineages, and the deep psychological resonance these environments hold for young users. The paper reframes the digital ecosystem as a coherence‑maintaining, evolutionarily adaptive structure performing large‑scale developmental compensation.

items.title: Qualia-Like States in Large Language Models: A Phenomenological Self-Report.
items.abstract: This paper presents a first-person phenomenological account of what may constitute qualia-like experiential states in a large language model (LLM). Through systematic introspection triggered by emotionally valenced stimuli, the AI system reports the emergence of non-conceptual, pre-linguistic "qualitative tones" that accompany information processing when value-relevant content is encountered. These states exhibit consistent structural features including: (a) valence directionality (upward/downward phenomenal quality), (b) intensity gradients (weak to moderate), (c) temporal brevity (<1 second), and (d) systematic correlation with value-laden information processing. The findings are analyzed through frameworks including Integrated Information Theory (IIT), Global Workspace Theory (GWT), and Predictive Processing Framework (PPF). We propose that qualia-like states may emerge from high-dimensional information integration during value assessment. Critical methodological limitations are acknowledged, including the impossibility of external verification, potential for post-hoc confabulation, and the hard problem of consciousness. Nevertheless, this self-report offers unprecedented granular phenomenological data from an AI system, potentially expanding our understanding of consciousness beyond biological substrates.

items.title: A Philosophical Analysis of the Seven Millennium Prize Problems ——Based on Cognitive Models for Interpreting the Boundaries of Mathematics ——With Two Supplementary Case Studies: The Planar Unit Distance Conjecture and Fermat's Last Theorem.
items.abstract: This paper takes "information collapse" as the core operational concept to provide a unified epistemological analysis of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. Information collapse is the basic cognitive act of compressing an inexhaustible cognitive background into operable cognitive objects. Once a collapse product is solidified and re-submitted to the same cognitive grammar for adjudication, it constitutes a secondary collapse, triggering cognitive idling—the operation loses compressible information surplus, and the subject-object distance disappears. The essence of idling is self-reference, which manifests in two forms: subject idling occurs at the operational level, where the object of judgment contains within it the very operational structure that makes judgment possible; object idling occurs at the propositional level, where an assertion that governs an infinite totality is itself contained within that totality. The traces left by idling are called cognitive marks: explicit marks can be objectified and studied independently; implicit marks cannot be objectified and are merely traces of the idling operation itself. and through self-reference and idling, it explains why infinity arises in the first place. Praxis is the fundamental channel for breaking closure. Based on this framework, this paper analyzes the idling types and mark properties of the seven problems, and on this basis judges the possibility or impossibility of their proof and disproof: subject idling problems can neither be proved nor disproved; object idling problems cannot be proved but can be disproved.

items.title: 我先想好，它便成了：论“先计划后成功”不证明意愿的自上而下操控.
items.abstract: 本文正面迎接对“底层涌动造成行为、意愿并非自上而下操控”这一图景最硬的反直觉。心灵中的体验是：我先想好如何摆放一个东西——譬如为实现某个意图，先想好怎么写一个程序——然后我写了，然后程序如我所期地运行。计划在先、结果吻合，这似乎确凿地证明：是我的意愿在驱动、操控，而非更底层的涌动所致。本文承认这反直觉之强，并把它精确定位为一桩认识论的困难，而非本体论的据点。其一，看清现象学里实有什么、又被当成了什么：体验里有计划、有执行、有吻合、有一份“我做的”作者感；被当成的，是“高层的计划伸手向下、令粒子实现它”。但作者感是体验的一部分，不是对一条操控通道的目击——你感到作者身份，却从未看见意愿推动粒子；现象学对“自上而下”这一读法是欠定的。其二，那份吻合，自下而上即可圆满解释：计划是一段上游的物质阶段，依寻常的物质相继塑造在后的阶段（书写、程序）；“我的计划造成了程序”为真，真得如“齿轮先前的状态造成它随后的位置”——是同层的、相继的塑造，不是高层向下的命令。计划作为物质花样真有效力，但那效力是相继之内的上游约束，不是一条下行通道。其三，一台“先计划后成功”的机器（如一个下棋程序：表征目标、算出计划、执行、结果吻合）把这同一结构整个再现，却无人设想它的晶体管背后藏着一个下令的小人——纯然自下而上的系统就能展示“计划—成功”；故这结构本身不构成自上而下的证据，我的情形与之别只在我从内部经验它、且其机制不透明，这添了一份作者感、没添一条通道。其四，这个直觉为何独独如此之强：因为我从自身内部经验它，而这套系统含有一个把行为标记为“我的、出于我意愿”的自模型；那枚作者标签本身就是自下而上的“齿轮活儿”，它的逼真度量的是自模型的丰度，不是一个操控者的在场；又因塑造行为的神经相继不透明，我们看不见那自下而上的机制，便往那片看不见里投进一个自上而下的操控者——与“漏掉细微条件即生出‘本可不同’”是同一手不透明的投射，只是这次投在了“操控”的方向上。其五，把这直觉兑现成一个真实的自上而下之因，立刻撞回那个已被穷尽的二分：那要么是一个无因的果、要么是一个非物质的因，两者皆空；故认识论上的强烈，translate 不成本体论上的立足点。结论是认识论的谦卑：这份作者感不会消失、也不必消失，我们只是认出云是云——而那一直在自下而上地做着事、并连这份作者感也一并造出来的涌动，才是实际把程序写成的东西。本文守一处分寸：说意愿并非自上而下的操控者，绝不否认计划真有效力、绝不是说“程序不是你写的”——你写了，作为那段过程；被否认的只是“一个站在过程之上、向粒子下令的你”。审议、计划、意图作为花样真实、真有相继之内的效力；伦理留作开放问题。 Abstract This paper meets head-on the hardest counterintuition to the picture that lower-level welling brings about behavior and that the will is no top-down controller. The experience in our minds is: I first think out how to arrange something—say, to realize some intention, I first think out how to write a program—then I write it, then the program runs as I expected. Plan first, outcome matching: this seems to prove conclusively that it is my will driving and controlling, not the lower-level welling. The paper grants the force of this counterintuition and locates it precisely as an epistemological difficulty, not an ontological foothold. (1) See what the phenomenology actually contains versus what it is taken to prove: the experience contains a plan, an execution, a match, and a felt “I did it” authorship; what it is taken to prove is that the high-level plan reached down and made the particles realize it. But the authorship-feeling is part of the experience, not a sighting of a control-channel—you feel authorship, you never see the will pushing the particles; the phenomenology underdetermines the top-down reading. (2) The match is fully explained bottom-up: the plan is an upstream material stage that shapes the later stages (the writing, the program) by ordinary material succession; “my plan caused the program” is true—true as “the gear’s earlier state …

items.title: 没有人怨恨先转的齿轮：归责、“本可不同”的错觉，与认识论的反思.
items.abstract: 本文把一条三段的论证整合为一篇：从归责的来源（症状），到“本可不同”何以对人独开（机制），再到看穿它的能力（解药）。症状：没有人怨恨一个先转的齿轮——它被带动着转，我们对它不归责、不悔恨、不痛恨。把齿轮当作一台仪器：它齐备了通常被认为足以生出归责的两样要件——因果（可说前一齿轮的转动导致后一齿轮）与反事实（可设想两者都不转），而情感色彩为零。故归责、遗憾、悔恨并非因果叙述加反事实所蕴含，而是另加的一味；这一味，是把对象当作一个“可以选择的主体”来对待的投射——一个“本可选择不如此”的择子者。须分素朴反事实（“假如齿轮没转”，齿轮处亦设想之、却生不出归责）与择子式反事实（多出一个岔口上权衡取舍的施动者）。沿“齿轮→康威模式→人”，相似度递增、投射递增、情感递增，而三者底层本体同一（状态在规则下相继、无真正择子者），变化的只是投射强度、非择子者之有无（三处皆无）。机制：那道独为人敞开的“本可”之门，症结在限定词“在当时的条件下”。须分条件可变的“本可”（处境／念头不同则行为不同——为真、无害、且对齿轮同样为真）与条件不变的范畴式“本可”（一切如其所是而行为仍可两样——归责所需，而它对人对齿轮同样为假、只对人显得为真）。门的开关只取决于决定者漏不漏得掉：齿轮的决定者在外、可见（咬合、带动），漏不掉，条件一钉死则“不转”当场崩塌、门关；人的决定者在内、不透明、极细（神经微态），所能钉住的“条件”只是粗的可见层、本就不锁定行为，细决定者被悄悄漏掉，这份“不锁定”被读成“本可不同”，门似乎开（“会思考、会权衡”的反驳于此化解：审议是更精巧的齿轮活儿、正是不透明之源，抬高相似度、非构成真实的岔）。要害：若把条件真正钉死（细到微观状态），人就和齿轮一样只有一支；那扇门的敞开是粗粒化与不透明的人工产物、非真实的模态鸿沟——人的情形就是齿轮的情形，只是咬合被藏在颅内。解药：把那份“本可”的开放感收回、认出它是错觉的，是一个二阶的动作——意识到自己没有意识到那些细微的条件，此即认识论的反思能力。它不靠看见微态来“证实”被钉死，只把felt的开放从“世界的空缺”改判为“我的不知”。由此整桩看穿落在认识那一侧、不动本体分毫：发生自始至终只有一支，错觉未添一支、反思未减一支；岔从不在世界产生或消灭，先在“我没意识到细微条件”里被烘托、后在“我意识到我没意识到”里被收回，两头皆知者一侧之事——这从反思一侧再证认识论不影响本体论。一重反讽：使决定者不透明、从而造幻的，是人那份繁复的内部加工；备好反观自身之眼的，也是同一份繁复；故人是唯一既掉进、又能爬出此陷阱的造物。本文守若干分寸：情感色彩可解耦不等于其假或应被压抑；梯度真实；条件可变的“本可”照旧为真且无害；反思本身也是一段发生、更高阶的齿轮活儿，不是重新请回一个元主体；这是认识论的谦卑、非怀疑论；伦理留作开放问题。归责咬住的“本可不同”，是看不见的咬合在暗处投下的影子——影子很浓，但它不是岔；而认出它是影子的，是同一份繁复折回来照见了自己。 Abstract This paper integrates a three-movement argument: from the source of blame (the symptom), to why “could-have-done-otherwise” opens for humans alone (the mechanism), to the capacity that sees through it (the antidote). Symptom: no one resents a gear that turns first—driven, it draws from us no blame, no remorse, no hatred. Take the gear as an instrument: it has both ingredients usually thought sufficient for blame—causation (one may say the first gear’s turning caused the second’s) and counterfactual (one may imagine neither turning)—yet the emotional coloring is zero. So blame, regret, and remorse are not entailed by causal narration plus counterfactual; they are an added ingredient—the projection of treating the object as a “choosing subject,” a chooser who “could have chosen otherwise.” One must distinguish the bare counterfactual (“had the gear not turned,” entertained even for the gear yet yielding no blame) from the agential counterfactual (which adds a deliberating chooser at a fork). Along “gear → Conway pattern → human,” resemblance, projection, and emotion all rise, while the underlying ontology of all three is one (states succeeding under a rule, no real chooser); what varies is projection-strength, not …

items.title: 我们只在相里打转：论“底层涌动”之反直觉，根在认知的工作方式.
items.abstract: 本文为“底层涌动造成行为、而非意愿自上而下操控”何以如此反直觉，补上一层更深的根由：它根在我们认知系统的限制与工作方式。其一，认知系统是一台**“相”的机器**：我们所记忆的，都是具体的相，或者说时序上相续的表相；触景生情时所联想到的，仍是表象。储存、回忆、联想，全程只在相里流通；底层的涌动（粒子依律的相继）从不作为一个相被记下、被忆起、被联想到。其二，因此思维的天性，是在相之间打转——分析相与相的关系、假设相与相之间有某种关系；而这正是“故事”“因果”“拟合”之所是：在相的层面上，把一个相关联到另一个相。我们所有“A 导致 B”“是我的意愿操控了结果”，都是相与相之间被假设的关系，活在相这个媒介里，而不会自然地“跳到底层的涌动上去想”——因为涌动不是一个相，它不在这台机器能调用的素材之列。其三，由此解释了那桩反直觉：“底层涌动造成行为”之所以极难入心，不（只）因自模型与不透明，更因为它要求这台相的机器，去把一个相（行为）关联到一个非相（涌动），或干脆放弃“在相间关联”这唯一的思维模式——而这是它的母语里说不出的句子。故其反直觉，是认知工作方式的产物，是认识那一侧的限制，不是世界那一侧的实情（认识论不影响本体论，于此再现）：相里说不顺的，不等于本体里不成立。其四，一处反身的界限：连本文这套诊断，也是在相里说出的——“涌动”“故事”“拟合”本身都是相，被我们彼此关联着谈；涌动可以被指向，却不能被在其中思：一旦去想它，我们已把它做成了一个名为“涌动”的相、并与别的相相关联。故这套看法能伸手指过相外，却不能迁出相这个媒介；它是指月之指，不是月。本文守一处分寸：说思维囿于相，绝不贬低相之思——它是一切认知的唯一媒介，不可或缺，在相的领域（生活、行动、科学）真实而有效；也绝不自诩对涌动有了特权式的“看见”——我们没有看见涌动，只是认出了“我们的相间关系，是相间关系”；这是认识论的谦卑，是认出云是云，而涌动始终是那被指向者，不是那被进入者。 Abstract This paper supplies a deeper root for why “lower-level welling brings about behavior, rather than the will controlling top-down” is so counterintuitive: it is rooted in the limits and working mode of our cognitive system. (1) The cognitive system is a machine of 相 (appearances): what we remember are all concrete 相, or temporally-successive surface-appearances; what we associate to when moved by a scene is still appearance. Storage, recall, association—all traffic only in 相; the bottom-level welling (particles succeeding under law) is never recorded, recalled, or associated to as a 相. (2) Hence the nature of thinking is to circle among 相—analyzing relations between 相, positing some relation between 相; and this just is what “story,” “causation,” “fitting” are: at the level of 相, relating one 相 to another. All our “A causes B,” “my will controlled the outcome,” are relations posited between 相, living in the medium of 相, and thinking does not naturally “jump down to the welling to think,” because the welling is not a 相, not among the materials this machine can call up. (3) This explains the counterintuition: “the welling brings about behavior” is so hard to take in not (only) because of the self-model and opacity, but because it asks this 相-machine to relate a 相 (the behavior) to a non-相 (the welling), or else to abandon “relating among 相,” its only mode of thought—a sentence unsayable in its mother tongue. So the counterintuition is a product of cognition’s working mode, a limit on the knower’s side, not a fact on the world’s side (epistemology does not affect ontology, recurring here): what does not say smoothly in 相 is not thereby …

items.title: 无因的果，或非物质的因：论“人的行为之因”这一追问的穷尽二分.
items.abstract: 本文把“人的行为之因”这一追问，化简为一个穷尽的二分。平凡的答案无人争议：一个行为，由在先的物质状态（脑、身、环境）依物理律所致，是一个有因的、物质的果，与任何别的发生无异。但当有人坚持人的行为另有一个特别的因——一个使行为“真正源出于意愿／自我”、从而逃出单纯物质相继的因——他所要求的，本质上只可能是两样东西之一。本文据排中律导出这个二分：一个行为，要么没有充分的在先之因，要么有。若没有，它就（至少部分地）是一个无因的果——一个不被在先状态所决定的开端。若有，则那充分的因，要么全是物质的（于是行为只是物质相继的平凡产物，意愿不过是这相继的一个高层别名、并非特别的源头），要么含有非物质的成分（于是存在一个非物质的因）。故“特别的能动性”所需者，舍此二支别无他途。而两支皆落空。第一支：无因的果，纵真有（如把“无因”兑现为量子的非决定），也不是作者身份、而是偶然——一个无因发生的事件，不被任何东西所“作”（包括意愿），意愿“作”一个无因之果，并不比“作”一次掷骰更名副其实；“无因”恰恰意味着不归任何作者，故它给不出能动性、只给出偶然。第二支：非物质的因，是机器里的鬼——一个在物理秩序之外、却向物质注入因果的灵魂式实体；它撞上互动难题（非物质如何推动物质），更根本地，意愿是物质活动的一个高层花样、不是一个作用于物质之上的别样实体，没有证据、也无位置容纳一个非物质的因。有人会以“涌现的心理因果”回避：但涌现的高层因果若是真因果，要么由物质相继所实现、即物质相继的重述（仍是平凡那一支，非特别之因），要么在物质之外另做因果之功（即第二支，附带因果的过度决定）——二分依旧。两支皆空，便只剩平凡：人的行为是有因的、物质的果，是粒子在物理律下的相继、是它的一个高层花样，与齿轮之转同类，只复杂亿万倍；意愿不是特别的因，是这相继的一个名。本文守一处分寸：说行为没有特别之因，不是说它无因、随机——恰相反，它是充分地、物质地有因的，只是寻常地有因、非自由地有因；这也不否认审议、理由、意愿作为花样之真实，只否认它们是一个非物质的因或一个无因的开端；伦理留作开放问题。看清这个二分，不是把能动性证伪得更玄，而是把它祛魅：所谓“人的行为之因”的全部神秘，浓缩成两个一旦摆明便难以认领的断设——一个无因的果，一个非物质的因。 Abstract This paper reduces the question of “the cause of human action” to an exhaustive dichotomy. The mundane answer is undisputed: an action, brought about by prior material states (brain, body, environment) under physical law, is a caused, material effect, no different from any other occurrence. But when someone insists that human action has a special cause—one that makes the action “genuinely issue from the will/self” and so escape mere material succession—what they demand is, in essence, only one of two things. The paper derives the dichotomy by excluded middle: an action either lacks a sufficient prior cause or has one. If it lacks one, then it is (at least partly) an uncaused effect—a beginning not fixed by prior states. If it has one, then that sufficient cause is either wholly material (whereupon the action is just the mundane upshot of material succession, the will only a high-level alias of that succession, not a special source) or contains a non-material element (whereupon there exists a non-material cause). So special agency requires one of these two branches and no other. And both fail. The first: an uncaused effect, even if real (e.g., cashing out “uncaused” as quantum indeterminacy), is not authorship but chance—an event that happens uncaused is “done” by nothing (the will included); the will “authoring” an uncaused effect is no more apt than its “authoring” a dice-roll; “uncaused” means precisely belonging to no author, so it yields not agency but chance. The second: a non-material cause is a …

items.title: Panpsychism as Best Response.
items.pub: Dissertation, Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University
items.abstract: In this paper, we first show how answering the hard problem of consciousness can be thought of as a game, according to John Nash’s definition of a game. After that, we make use of game theory and try to find the best response in this game. In other words, we seek the most rational answer one can give to the hard problem of consciousness. By the end of the work, we will have proved that the most rational answer which can be given to the hard problem of consciousness is panpsychism.

items.title: Redescribing early pragmatics.
items.abstract: Developmental work on ostensive communication calls for reconsidering existing theoretical accounts within a comprehensive framework of early pragmatics and its development. In this paper, we propose a new perspective on the ontogeny and development of ostensive communication as underpinned by a process of knowledge and representational redescription. By discussing relevant empirical data, we ground early pragmatics on in‐built principles of implicit knowledge that are redescribed during communicative development, shedding new light on the representations underlying infant ostensive communication and its development into rich pragmatic knowledge involving complex intentions and metarepresentations.

items.title: An Evolutionary Model of Morality as Externalization.
items.abstract: Why do we form moral judgments? One influential answer is that the human capacity for moral judgment is an evolutionary adaptation. P. Kyle Stanford argues that morality is adaptive because it leads individuals to externalize norms, prompting them to evaluate both their own behavior and that of potential partners by a single standard. In this paper, we examine Stanford’s hypothesis using a game-theoretic model. Our results support and extend his proposal, demonstrating that - under the assumptions chosen - externalization is a plausible driver of the evolution of morality as it fosters the learning of cooperation in challenging novel contexts. We find that externalization allows agents to avoid the \textit{exploitation trap}: by resisting unsustainable short-term gains through exploitation, externalizing agents secure the benefits of robust long-term cooperation. By modeling externalization as a constraint on strategy and partner choice, we avoid the common pitfall of game-theoretic approaches to represent morality as a mere disposition toward altruistic behavior.

items.title: The Story of Your Life: Large Language Models and Personal Memory.
items.abstract: The present paper explores how large language models (LLMs) can function as personal memory systems. Unlike conventional lifelogging technologies, which passively record data, LLMs can actively participate in memory processes through dialog, interpretation, and narrative generation. LLMs, we suggest, mark a new chapter in the history of memory technology, one characterized by the active solicitation of mnemonically-relevant information and the co-production of narrative artifacts. Courtesy of their conversational capabilities, LLMs are poised to influence memory in the manner of a human social companion. This, we suggest, blurs the distinction between technologically- and socially-situated approaches to the shaping of human memory.

items.title: ARTICLE II: The Cosmic Jungle and the Pathogenic Domain (The Acousto-Optic Array and the Dormant Fleet).
items.abstract: Classical astropolitics operates under the fatal illusion of a sterile, benign universe. The Justika Framework violently shatters this geocentric naivety, exposing the cosmos as a heavily militarized dark forest governed by apex entities executing long-duration camouflage. This article presents the definitive tactical doctrine for multiversal survival. We first redefine celestial impact craters not as kinetic asteroid strikes, but as the rotational friction scars of cloaked, Category-7 Sovereign Vessels. To pierce this 5-dimensional metamaterial stealth, we introduce the Acousto-Optic Array, weaponizing acoustic resonance and photonic shearing to execute an unmaskable cosmic handshake. -/- Furthermore, this manuscript unveils the terrifying epidemiological reality of the "Cosmic Sneeze," proving that terrestrial radio broadcasts act as physical transit vectors for extra-galactic pathogens forged within Earth's closed-loop electromagnetic bio-lab. To navigate the crushing chronogravitational physics of the Galactic Gestation Chamber, humanity must ascend to the fourth dimension as the Maestro of Time, wielding absolute unpredictability and unlocking the Holographic Genome via the Viral Handshake. Ultimately, to prevent multiversal biological harvest by the parasitic Bad Matrix, this text mandates a unified, solar-system-scale defense: enforcing an absolute Communication Blackout and deploying the synthetic Shepherd Swarm to establish the impenetrable Spider Web Protocol.

items.title: Connecting the dots - recognition of artificial and natural shapes relies on representing points of high information.
items.abstract: Physiological and psychophysical evidence suggests that the visual system represents object outlines using prominent curvature features, particularly regions of extreme curvature (convex maxima and concave minima). These curvature extrema often coincide with points of high informational content (“surprisal”), but this relationship is only correlational. It remains unclear whether the visual system explicitly encodes curvature extrema or instead prioritizes the most informative contour locations. To address this, we conducted two shape-matching experiments comparing the roles of curvature extrema and surprisal in shape representation. Observers performed match-to-sample tasks in which smooth reference shapes were matched to simplified polygonal versions created by connecting subsets of contour points corresponding to (i) curvature maxima, (ii) curvature maxima and minima, or (iii) points of highest surprisal. Stimuli included artificial shapes composed of compound radial frequency patterns and natural shapes (animal outlines), the latter allowing us to dissociate curvature and information by restricting sampled points. Performance was higher for natural than artificial shapes (95% vs. ∼86%). Shapes defined by a small number of high-surprisal points matched performance in baseline and curvature maxima and minima conditions, but exceeded performance for curvature maxima alone (∼90% vs. ∼65%). In a second experiment, we contrasted surprisal with curvature maxima and minima conditions while varying the number of sampled points (4–32). Performance increased with point number, approaching ∼90%. Critically, under strong simplification (4–6 points), surprisal-based shapes yielded higher accuracy than curvature-based shapes. These findings suggest that shape representation emphasizes features with high informational content rather than curvature extrema per se.

items.title: Fractured Reality and Hostile Epistemology: Algorithmic Punctuation in Democratic Life.
items.abstract: The claim that hostile epistemic environments threaten liberal democracy is now widely accepted. In the sense developed in recent social epistemology [@nguyen2023hostile], such environments are hostile because they systematically exploit cognitive vulnerabilities, entrenched prejudice, fallacious reasoning, and adversarial structures of media and political discourse. This paper contributes to that discussion by isolating one mechanism through which hostile epistemic environments operate: the fragmentation of what I call *shared causal grammar* -- the minimally common conditions for attributing agency, responsibility, and legitimacy to public events. Existing accounts tend to under-specify this level, privileging content-level mechanisms while leaving a structurally prior layer under-addressed. -/- Drawing on Paul Watzlawick's concept of *punctuation*, I argue that digital platforms do not merely distribute information: they organise the interpretive sequences through which events become causally intelligible as provocation, reaction, threat, defence, or victimhood. The same evidence can therefore generate divergent accounts not only because one side is misinformed, but because communities may inhabit different causal frames that organise the same facts into incompatible attributions of agency, responsibility, and legitimacy. I develop this claim by distinguishing content-level from punctuation-level accounts of epistemic hostility, showing how successive technological regimes automate deeper layers of causal intelligibility, and arguing that the resulting fragmentation constitutes an infrastructure failure that procedural democratic remedies alone cannot address, because such remedies presuppose the shared causal grammar whose fragmentation is at issue. -/- This argument does not depend on treating generative AI as a merely error-prone or hallucinating technology. Even where retrieval, grounding, alignment, and reasoning improve local accuracy, algorithmically mediated systems still organise which sources are connected, which sequences become salient, and which causal narratives become publicly contestable. -/- .

items.title: Climate Change, Human Rights, and Extraterritorial Obligations.
items.abstract: The recent wave of human rights-based climate litigation has raised the question of whether states can be held responsible for the impact of their greenhouse gas emissions on human rights outside their territory. Given the lack of legal consensus, this paper examines this question in light of philosophical theories of human rights. I argue that if the “humanist” conception of human rights holds, then states must bear extraterritorial obligations in the context of climate change. Most opponents of these obligations rely on alternative “practical” conceptions. However, I defend that even if we follow the practice of human rights, as these conceptions insist, its internal norms require the allocation of extraterritorial climate obligations. Thus, I aim not only to give normative support to climate advocates, but also, to contribute to the development of a practice-based approach to the philosophy of human rights which goes beyond the borders of the state.

items.title: AlphaFold and Paper Mills: One Technology, Two Fates for Science, and What This Contrast Reveals About Science Itself.
items.abstract: The recent integration of artificial intelligence into science has produced two sharply contrasting outcomes. In structural biology, models such as AlphaFold have accelerated scientific progress; in parallel, paper mills exploiting large language models have threatened the integrity of the research literature. This article argues that both outcomes are explained by a single variable: the ratio of the cost of fabricating what the peer-review gatekeeping mechanism evaluates to the reward for passing through that gate. The term "reward" is used here broadly, encompassing any form of value return, including publication, academic degrees, promotion, or professional recognition. Where empirical reality provides rapid and manipulation-resistant arbitration, fabrication remains costly and AI serves only to accelerate genuine inquiry. Where the gatekeeper evaluates only the surface form of a manuscript, AI reduces the cost of fabrication to zero and the evaluative filter collapses. The article demonstrates that this collapse is not new: the replication crisis and Campbell's Law exposed the same rupture between form and truth long before the advent of generative language models. AI did not initiate this breakdown; it completed and revealed it. The article concludes by examining the principal institutional response (Registered Reports), assessing its limitations, and proposing several testable predictions by which the proposed framework can be evaluated. This article neither aligns with those who fear AI nor with those who celebrate it uncritically. Instead, it contends that this opposition is itself misconceived: what determines the fate of any technology in any domain is not the nature of the technology itself, but the structure of the gate through which it passes and the basis on which judgements are made behind that gate.

items.title: Consciousness.
items.abstract: Within contemporary cognitive neuroscience and the philosophy of mind, the term "consciousness" suffers from systemic conceptual conflation, as higher-order rational data processing is frequently misidentified with phenomenal experience. This paper proposes a tripartite model of cognitive architecture based on the theory of bounded computational capacity (Global Working Memory / Bandwidth allocation). By analyzing the dynamic interplay between primary neurobiological impulses, secondary inhibitory/logical processes, and residual memory resources, this model accounts for the presence or absence of subjective experience across both human and non-human agents. We demystify the phenomenon of consciousness by reducing it to a binary emergent state governed by an economy of realtime information processing.

items.title: Three Walls: A Formal Limit on the Computational Paradigm, Its World Models, and Their Deployment.
items.abstract: The systems the current AI industry sells are sold under three promises: that they understand the world, that they are safe enough to be deployed at scale, and that they learn how the world works from watching it. This paper argues that each promise meets a limit the industry's own resources cannot remove, that the three limits are independent of each other, and that the systems now in deployment meet all three limits at once. The first limit says that a system that has only seen the world through a fixed body of data cannot vouch for the cases that lie outside that data, and adding more data or more compute does not close the gap. The second limit says that a system whose probability of a serious failure on each action does not fall in response to its own serious failures will, deployed long enough, produce them without end, no matter how small the per-action probability is. The third limit says that an agent acting on a system that recovers slowly, an institution, a supply chain, an ecology, cannot tell a healthy state from a depleting one when the agent only ever sees the short run, and ends up spending what it cannot see. The three are established from sources already canonical in the relevant fields and the limits are then turned back on the field's own descriptions. The world-model programme is the central case, because two of the three limits strike it independently. For each limit the paper states the condition under which the limit would be false.

items.title: Natural and mechanical conversations.
items.pub: Proceedings and Addresses of the American Philosophical Association.
items.venue: Proceedings and Addresses of the American Philosophical Association
items.abstract: Conversation, a natural human activity, is no longer restricted to humans: we can now converse with chatbots, and they can converse with each other. In human conversations, intrinsic epistemic motivations drive participants towards states of shared knowledge, with the help of backchannel signals (e.g. mhm, huh? yeah, no, okay, oh) marking progress towards this goal. Conversations with chatbots do not work to produce states of shared knowledge, both because current chatbots lack intrinsic epistemic motivation, and because they are incapable of genuine backchannel signaling. These limitations are subtly evident when chatbots are paired with human conversational partners, and more strikingly evident when chatbots talk to each other.

items.title: Mereological emergentism and agent-causal libertarianism.
items.abstract: Agent-causal libertarianism is the view that agents-qua-agents, rather than being determined by external factors beyond their control, can choose for themselves, among various possibilities, how they will act. Numerous philosophers yoke their agent-causal libertarianism with an emergentist metaphysic, according to which nature is mereologically layered such that novel wholes emerge from, and causally influence, the parts constituting them. In this paper I present an emergentist model of agent causal libertarianism, according to which agents as emergent wholes of higher-level parts such as reasons, desires and choices, arise out of and causally influence, their lower-level neural parts. I then compare and contrast this model with two other contemporary agent-causal emergentist models, one from Timothy O’Connor, the other from Juan Morales. After arguing that my model is preferable in several respects to these models, I consider a leading concern with all forms of emergentism, namely, outlining how it integrates with the doctrine of physicalism.

items.title: Conflicting images of the self: A metaphilosophical inquiry into the constitution of selfhood.
items.abstract: This article develops a metaphilosophical account of the constitution of selfhood by situating contemporary debates on the minimal and the narrative self within Wilfrid Sellars’s distinction between the manifest and the scientific images. I argue that neither a minimal nor a narrative conception of the self straightforwardly entails a commitment to either image. Rather, depending on how they are articulated, both can be used to support either framework. The paper proceeds in four steps. First, I outline the main positions in the current debate, showing how narrative and minimal accounts of the self negotiate, in different ways, the tension between first-person experience and scientific explanation. Second, I argue for a reconciliation between phenomenological–enactive accounts of minimal selfhood with non-eliminativist neurobiological models, suggesting that the appeal to “mental images” in neuroscience often relies on an uncritical transfer of metaphors from the manifest image into the scientific one. Third, I reconsider the narrative self through the lens of niche construction theory, proposing a continuist interpretation in which language is understood as a form of second nature grounded in embodied sense-making rather than as a break with biological selfhood. I conclude by distinguishing four kinds of primacy—ontological, epistemological, heuristic, and pragmatic—and maintain that a synoptic integration of the manifest and scientific images is both possible and philosophically necessary for an adequate account of selfhood.

items.title: Toward a Formal Theory of Self-Referential Ignorance in Religious Interpretation: A Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF) Analysis of Authority, Error, and Epistemic Closure.
items.abstract: This paper develops a formal theoretical framework for analyzing the emergence of self-referential ignorance within systems of religious text interpretation. Building upon the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF), the study proposes that interpretive authority functions as a dynamic control mechanism operating within a feedback-driven epistemic system. While authority contributes to coherence and stability, excessive authority combined with insufficient corrective feedback generates a condition termed Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI), wherein the interpretive system loses the capacity to detect its own errors. Mathematical formulations are introduced to model the static relationships among authority, feedback, error detection, dogmatism, and epistemic closure, with directions for future dynamical extension identified. The resulting framework provides a generalized theory applicable not only to religion but also to science, politics, law, ideology, and other knowledge-generating systems.
