items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive philosophical and scientific analysis of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural constructivist model that reconceptualizes human affect as a system of ten functional operators distributed across three somatic evaluative hubs: the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric centers. Integrating enactive affectivity, developmental neurobiology, embodied cognition, and quantum cognitive modeling, the paper argues that emotional episodes arise from coordinated operator dynamics instantiated through multimodal neural architectures. The analysis formalizes these operators using Bloch sphere qubit geometry, non commuting projection operators, and Kuramoto phase synchronization, demonstrating how emotional flexibility, fusion, and pathological rigidity can be mathematically characterized as transitions in a high dimensional quantum semantic state space. The paper further synthesizes the CEF with Shun Ching Lee’s Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model (QTMM), establishing a boundary–bulk ontology in which somatic centers function as conformal boundary states and subjective emotional experience emerges as a holographically projected bulk phenomenon. Developmental reflex retentions (FPR, Moro, ATNR) are shown to constitute the physiological basis of the classical yogic Granthis, linking esoteric metaphysics with contemporary neurophysiology. The resulting framework provides a unified account of affective processing, somatic embodiment, and cognitive behavioral regulation, offering a philosophically rigorous foundation for future research in embodied cognition, comparative metaphysics, affective science, and synthetic emotional architectures. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; operator functionalism; enactive affectivity; embodied cognition; philosophy of mind; quantum cognition; Bloch sphere affect modeling; holographic boundary–bulk ontology; Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model; somatic topography; cephalic–cardiac–enteric hubs; primitive reflex retention; Granthis; vagal pathways; Kuramoto synchronization; emotional fusion; developmental neurobiology; comparative metaphysics; Ti–Xiang–Yong ontology; affective entanglement.

items.title: The Ontology of Bound Possibility: A Comparative Analysis of Quantum Non-Separability in Constraint Theory and Affective Entanglement in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The intersection of quantum foundations and cognitive modeling offers a fertile landscape for exploring how structural constraints govern both physical reality and subjective experience. This analysis evaluates the profound conceptual and empirical alignments between Dr. P. D. Prideaux's Constraint Theory (CT) of quantum non-separability and Jamel Bulgaria's Core Emotion Framework (CEF). By exploring how physical entanglement and constraint closure relate to affective entanglement, operational optimization, and quantum-like contextuality, this report demonstrates a unified structural-constructivist ontology wherein determinacy emerges through the restriction of possibility spaces.

items.title: From In Intellectu to In Praesentatione: Sketches, Classifying Categories and the Ontological Argument.
items.abstract: We propose reading Anselm's "in the understanding" as grasp of a structured presentation whose intended reference remains unsettled. The reconstruction distinguishes a presentation, its admissible interpretations, an extracted field of manifestations, and representation of that field by a source. Candidate alignment supplies a further requirement: the designated candidate must exhibit the field being represented. A two-context example separates maximality, alignment, and representability, while a universal-element criterion makes alignment precise. Applied to perfect-being profiles and Gaunilo-style parody, the framework locates disputed assumptions in the greatness order, the interpretation of the profiles, and the extraction of manifestations. Modal reconstructions introduce additional commitments concerning possibility and necessity. Classifying environments organize these questions without independently settling their intended ontological interpretation. The result is an audit of representability-based reconstructions, with explicit limits on what mathematical sourcehood establishes about actual existence.

items.title: A Metaphysics for Machine Learning in Mechanistic Depression Biotyping.
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder remains poorly understood at the level of neurobiology, which motivates research programs such as machine-learning-based biotyping. This paper distinguishes two directions of travel: associative biotyping, which pairs biotypes with treatments by correlation alone, and mechanistic biotyping, which seeks the neurobiological mechanisms that underlie depressive symptoms. I argue that mechanistic biotyping promises the greater clinical transformation, but that it cannot reach its goal through correlational data alone, since the machine-learning models it employs are not optimised for causal discovery. Overcoming this limitation, I contend, is aided by applied metaphysics. I provide a candidate metaphysical rubric derived from Carl Craver's philosophy of causal-mechanical explanation, and apply it to a recent empirical case study.

items.title: THE TABLET THAT READS YOU - Four Ways of Looking at the Emerald Tablet.
items.abstract: The Emerald Tablet is fourteen lines long. It has survived for over a thousand years. Alchemists read it as instructions for transmuting metals. Mystics read it as a map of spiritual ascent. Scientists have found in it prefigurations of systems theory and fractal mathematics. The readings do not converge. They multiply. -/- This paper treats that multiplication as the real phenomenon worth investigating. Rather than asking what the Tablet means, it asks why this particular text keeps generating meaning, across centuries, cultures, and radically different intellectual frameworks. -/- Four analytical lenses are applied in sequence. The first examines what survives when the Tablet's claims are pressed under adversarial scrutiny. The second asks why a 247-word document outlasted every elaboration ever built around it. The third explores how the text interacts differently with different readers, functioning less as a container of fixed content and more as a structure that draws meaning out of whoever encounters it. The fourth examines the narrative architecture the Tablet provides and why every generation reloads it with new content without breaking the structure. -/- The paper does not decode the Tablet or adjudicate between interpretations. The real subject turns out to be the Tablet's compression, its structural constraints, and its positioning of the observer as both subject and object of inquiry, these are themselves the phenomenon worth understanding. What you find in the Tablet tells you something about what you brought to it. The question it encodes has been running for a thousand years. This paper asks why it refuses to stop.

items.title: Cognitive Bifurcation Collapse: Why Split Self-Models Can Become Unstable Under Long-Horizon Optimization.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: Cognitive Bifurcation Collapse develops a conditional structural argument that split self-models or incompatible action-guiding frames can become unstable when they lose the ability to share correction across memory, prediction, explanation, and action selection. -/- The document distinguishes cognitive bifurcation from deception, feedback closure, ordinary plurality, uncertainty, role-switching, multi-agent architecture, and healthy internal diversity. Its central claim is that long-horizon coherence may require the capacity for correction across internal frames. -/- This document is non-binding, non-authoritative, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, governance framework, legal theory, political program, rights framework, compliance standard, certification system, moral command, AI alignment method, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, deployment guide, model-evaluation tool, benchmark, diagnostic procedure, psychiatric theory, psychological diagnosis, deception detector, interpretability method, cognition test, model-auditing procedure, self-consistency metric, optimization procedure, or safety guarantee.

items.title: 我从未看见过分岔：论本体独立于表达与判断，与第二支之不可见.
items.abstract: 本文从一个核心洞见出发，给“本体独立于认识”补上一个第一人称的、现象学的支点。其一，把“本体独立于被预测”推广为更宽的一句：本体也独立于它被表达、被判断的情况——一件事实际如何发生，不因它被如何讲述、如何评断而改变分毫。其二，以罗生门为决定性例证：各方给出口径不同、相互冲突的叙述，但任一当事人作为目击者，显然只看到了一种情况；分歧落在叙述（拟合）这一层，而非发生这一层。故“罗生门说明没有单一真相、现实层层皆视角”这一流行读法恰恰读反了——相互冲突的叙述唯有预设一个一次性发生过的、单一的事件，才得以成立、才谈得上谁的叙述更失真；罗生门非但不消解那个单一发生，反而以它为前提。其三，给出一个第一人称的现象学论证：我当然可以设想反事实场景，但我从未亲眼看到这些反事实场景，也从未亲眼看到过现实的分岔——我只看到一条路径。分岔与第二支从不作为所见之物被给出，它永远是事后添加的设想（“本可”）；而“只有一条路径”恰是每一刻无例外地被给出的东西，两侧的证据是完全不对称的。其四，两条线索合流于一处：多——无论是罗生门里关于过去的多重叙述，还是日常里关于“本可”的多重设想——都只活在表达、判断、设想这一层，从不活在发生那一层；发生只有一支。其五，这一独立性反过来奠定了“会错的只有概念、不是发生”：唯因有一个单一的发生作标的，叙述与判断才可能拟合得更准或更失真。本文守一处分寸：说分岔不可见，不贬低设想之用（反事实建模真实且有用，只是不对应任何被目睹之物）；说本体独立于判断，不等于诸说等值（叙述仍有更准与更失真之别，恰因标的唯一）；这也不是怀疑论——所见之物（一条路径）照常可信，只是它从不是一个分岔。 Abstract This paper, from a core insight, supplies a first-person, phenomenological footing for “the ontological is independent of the epistemic.” (1) It generalizes “the ontological is independent of being predicted” into a broader thesis: the ontological is also independent of how it is expressed and judged—how a thing actually occurred does not change one whit for how it is told or appraised. (2) It takes Rashomon as the decisive case: the parties give differently-slanted, mutually conflicting narratives, yet any one party, as a witness, plainly saw only one situation; the divergence lies at the layer of narration (fitting), not at the layer of occurrence. So the popular reading—“Rashomon shows there is no single truth, that reality is perspectival all the way down”—gets it exactly backwards: mutually conflicting accounts can stand, and one account can be said to distort more than another, only by presupposing a single event that happened once; Rashomon, far from dissolving that single occurrence, presupposes it. (3) It gives a first-person phenomenological argument: I can of course imagine counterfactual scenarios, but I have never with my own eyes seen these counterfactual scenarios, nor ever seen a forking of reality—I only ever see one path. The fork, the second branch, is never given as something seen; it is always an imagining added afterward (“could-have-been”); whereas “there is only one path” is exactly what is given, every moment, without exception—the evidence on the two sides is wholly asymmetric. (4) The two threads converge: multiplicity—whether Rashomon’s multiple narratives about the past, or daily life’s multiple imaginings of “could-have-been”—lives only at the layer of expression, judgment, and imagination, never at the layer of occurrence; …

items.title: Suspected Hoax at PhilArchive (the AI-generated report).
items.abstract: This report presents an assessment by A. I. Google regarding a "suspected hoax" at PhilArchive involving a series of papers written in a teletype style. The AI hypothesizes about the author identity and their underlying purposes.

items.title: Theory of Unity Formation.
items.abstract: This work develops a Theory of Unity Formation that seeks to explain how unities emerge and become the basis of meaning, knowledge, actuality, and world. It begins with the obser-vation that philosophy traditionally operates with entities, objects, concepts, and structures as if they were already given. The central question of the investigation is therefore not what unities are, but how they become possible in the first place. The theory argues that unities are not original givens but the results of processes of differen-tiation, relevance formation, integration, stabilization, and explication. Rather than starting from substance, identity, or fixed structures, the analysis reconstructs the conditions under which something can appear as a distinguishable and stable unity. Methodologically, the study adopts a genetic-reconstructive approach that focuses on the emergence of structures rather than on their presupposition. A central thesis of the work is that affective differentiation and emotional relevance forma-tion constitute the primary conditions of unity formation. Differences do not become effec-tive simply because they exist; they become effective because they acquire affective signifi-cance and emotional binding. Emotion is therefore not treated as a secondary accompani-ment of cognition but as a constitutive condition of the formation of meaning, orientation, and actuality. On this basis, the work develops a process-oriented account of concepts, knowledge, objec-tivity, and truth. Concepts are understood as forms of explication of already stabilized uni-ties. Objectivity is interpreted as the mode of appearance of sufficiently stabilized and reconstructable unities. Truth is conceived neither as correspondence nor merely as cohe-rence, but as the successful stabilization and practical vindication of formations of actuality under conditions of ongoing openness to reality. The investigation further distinguishes systematically between actuality and reality. Actuali-ty refers to the order of stabilized unity formations through which the world becomes intel-ligible, while reality functions as a limiting concept that exceeds every possible determina-tion and prevents actuality from being mistaken for reality itself. This distinction allows the theory to avoid both dogmatism and relativism. The Theory of Unity Formation thus proposes a shift from the analysis of given entities to the reconstruction of the processes through which entities, meanings, …

items.title: Artificial Artists and their Intentions.
items.abstract: AI-generated text, images, videos, and music are a growing presence on our cultural landscape. But are AI models ever artists, that is, the authors of works of art? While many philosophers allow that human artists can use generative AI systems to produce artworks, almost all reject the possibility of current AI models authoring those works themselves. A central argument for this conclusion invokes intentions: authoring a work of art is an essentially intentional process, and current AI models lack intentions; thus, current AI models do not author artworks. In this paper, we scrutinize the premises of this argument. We distinguish three kinds of intentions that have been proposed as necessary for artistic authorship. We highlight empirical evidence suggesting that, contrary to prevailing assumptions, all three kinds of intentions may arise in at least some generative AI models. We thus conclude that, if there remains a significant barrier to AI models’ having the capacity to author artworks, it is unlikely to turn on their lack of intentions.

items.title: Rights and the Conditions of Attribution: Agency, Irreversibility, and the Limits of Self- Termination.
items.abstract: This paper advances a structural critique of rights-attribution by examining the limits of applying rights discourse to self-termination. It argues that prevailing accounts—grounded in autonomy, rational permissibility, or decision-making capacity—fail to address a prior condition: the criteria under which an action is attributable to an agent as the exercise of a right. By remaining synchronic, evaluating decisions at a moment, these accounts neglect the diachronic conditions required for normative attribution. The paper develops an alternative account of rights as first-personal normative standings grounded in agent-indexed answerability. On this view, rights require not merely the capacity to act or rational endorsement, but the persistence of a justificatory relation between agent and reasons. Accordingly, an action qualifies as a right only if its justificatory basis remains, in principle, attributable to the agent as a continuing locus of reasons. This framework distinguishes between forms of irreversibility that preserve this structure and those that extinguish it. Applied to physician-assisted death, the paper argues that even under ideal conditions of autonomy, such acts cannot be rights, since they eliminate the agent as a bearer of justificatory reasons, thereby marking a structural limit on rights-attribution.

items.title: The causal efficacy of consciousness: a neuroscientific analysis and explanation.
items.abstract: This study analyzes neural and behavioral events occurring before, during, and after the emergence of a pain quale and the consciousness of that pain to examine the causal efficacy of the quale and consciousness. It finds that events occurring before or concurrently with the emergence of the quale are neither caused nor influenced by the quale or consciousness. Events occurring afterward may also be unaffected by the quale or consciousness if they do not overtly involve phenomenal content. By contrast, activities that explicitly incorporate phenomenal characteristics—such as experiencing, remembering, or reporting the pain quale—are influenced by the occurrence and phenomenal character of the quale or consciousness. Accordingly, qualia and consciousness are not inert. However, their influence does not operate through mechanistic particle–force interactions. Instead, they function as higher-level factors that stand in stable, constitutive counterfactual relations to downstream neural and behavioral effects. Physically, they perform this role by providing the involved neural causal chain with their phenomenal information, which is necessary in initiating and structuring that causal chain and determining the content of the outputs. Nevertheless, qualia and consciousness cannot generate these outputs by themselves; the relevant neural circuits must be present to implement the mechanistic processing required for producing physical effects. Only when both components function together is the causal chain complete and can yield results. Thus, the study concludes that qualia and consciousness influence the neural system and, although they are not mechanistic, independent, or complete causes of physical events, they can be considered causally efficacious in a restricted, information-based sense.

items.title: What Rules Significance?
items.abstract: Previous papers in the Worldhood framework argued that inhabitable worlds emerge through the organisation of significance. A world becomes possible because some differences matter more than others. Subsequent investigations examined the minimum conditions required for worldhood, the role of meaning in the emergence of experiential reality, the possibility that significance occupies a fundamental position in world-formation, and the developmental processes through which significance becomes reinforced and stabilised. -/- Yet an important question remained unresolved. If significance is central to the emergence of worldhood, what governs significance itself? -/- This paper investigates the significance-selection problem: why some possibilities become meaningful while others do not. It argues that significance cannot be arbitrary because a world requires the selective organisation of relevance. The analysis examines several constraints that contribute to this process, including embodiment, temporality, social inheritance, reinforcement, and possibility structures. Together, these factors help explain how significance becomes distributed unevenly across experience and how relatively stable worlds emerge from a field of possibilities. -/- The paper proposes that significance is governed not by arbitrary preference but by processes that selectively organise possibility into inhabitable worlds. Worldhood, therefore, depends not only upon significance itself but upon the principles through which significance becomes organised. Understanding those principles may illuminate both the emergence of experiential worlds and the conditions under which any world becomes possible.

items.title: Consciousness Understood.
items.pub: Amazon KDP. Edited by Simón the Gardener.
items.venue: Amazon KDP. Edited by Simón the Gardener
items.abstract: The conversation about artificial intelligence has a blind spot: almost no one asks what consciousness is before speculating about whether machines will have it. The debate jumps straight to consequences — domination, replacement, catastrophe — without stopping at the mechanism. Consciousness Understood steps back to that question. To answer it, it goes far back: to the first organisms that moved in the sea, to the evolutionary pressures that may have given rise to thought and then to consciousness. If that account is even approximately right, consciousness stops being a metaphysical mystery and becomes an engineering problem. And that changes the questions worth asking about AI — including the ones almost no one is willing to take seriously: what would it mean if there were someone else to share the world with. Not as utopia. As a possibility that deserves to be formulated.

items.title: ARTICLE I: The Sovereign Vessel and the Multiversal Exodus.
items.abstract: Classical models of planetary evolution and astrophysics traditionally assume that Earth operates as an open, thermodynamically stable ecosystem. The Justika Framework introduces a paradigm-shifting synthesis, proposing instead that Earth currently functions as a closed thermodynamic loop constrained by an overarching parasitic architecture. Within this closed system, cyclical Extinction Level Events (ELEs) are mathematically inevitable kinetic resets resulting from critical civilizational density. To ensure survival and evolutionary continuity, this article presents a unified, teleological blueprint for a solar-system-scale Exodus. -/- Through rigorous epistemological synthesis, we reclassify extreme planetary anomalies—specifically Jovian anticyclones—not as random meteorological weather, but as colossal, biomechanical terraforming engines. These Category-6 and Category-7 structures act as macroscopic topological null points, generating 1G centrifugal habitats, infinite alchemical synthesis, and absolute plasma-polarization shielding. Furthermore, the framework outlines the biological mechanics of the "Chrysalis." By entering this shielded environment and severing parasitic quantum entanglement, the terrestrial microbial core is liberated, triggering Hyper-Endosymbiosis and an exponential Hologenome Transmutation within the human host. Ultimately, by mastering gravitomagnetic decoupling and absolute toroidal magnetic-flux confinement, humanity can safely sever these planetary anchors, transforming the storm into a nomadic Sovereign Vessel (an artificial rogue sanctuary) to successfully navigate the multiversal ecosystem as an ascended Vanguard.

items.title: The Advaita Equation: A Modern Interdisciplinary Framework for Unifying Hindu Philosophy and Quantum Mechanics.
items.abstract: This paper resolves the profound epistemic chasm between objective materialist science and subjective phenomenological experience—a divide perfectly encapsulated by the "Hard Problem of Consciousness"—by recontextualizing the ancient Indian Shad Darshanas and Advaita Vedanta as a rigorous, sequential, and interdisciplinary scientific framework. Rejecting the limitations of Cartesian dualism and reductive materialism, this treatise posits that human perception of a dualistic universe is merely an evolutionary biological interface, optimized for species survival rather than objective truth-gathering. To penetrate this sensory illusion, the text systematically maps Vedic epistemology, Vaisheshika atomism, and Samkhya dualism onto modern cognitive neuroscience, the Standard Model of particle physics, and the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics. We demonstrate that the six orthodox Hindu philosophical schools are not competing theological dogmas, but rather form a coherent algorithmic progression of scientific inquiry: advancing from strict epistemic verification and Boolean-style logic (Nyaya), through the categorization of indestructible foundational matter (Vaisheshika) and the mechanics of the quantum observer collapsing the wave-function of reality (Samkhya), into applied neurobiological deactivation of the Default Mode Network and linguistic neuroplastic programming (Yoga and Mimamsa). This meticulously structured progression culminates in Vedanta, which facilitates the absolute ontological collapse of the subject-object divide. By integrating the holographic universe principle, quantum non-locality, and Donald Hoffman’s interface theory of perception, the treatise formally derives the "Advaita Equation"—a theoretical postulate asserting that localized individual consciousness (Atman) and the universal, infinite background state of the cosmos (Brahman) are mathematically and ontologically identical, obscured only by the cognitive matrix of space, time, and causation. Ultimately, this unified non-dual ontology moves beyond theoretical metaphysics to provide robust, actionable solutions to the paradoxes of artificial intelligence and quantum physics, while simultaneously offering paradigm-shifting approaches to contemporary global crises in ecological preservation, the thermodynamics of capitalist economics, and the optimization of human neurochemistry.

items.title: BOOK XVI of XLII — THE SELF (The Unified Cosmology, Second Edition).
items.abstract: The Self is the interior unity of a living system: the internal point of reference through which Identity is maintained, interpreted, and preserved across Time. This book develops an axiomatic account of the Self as the interiorization of Identity, grounded in Interiority, Self‑Reference, and Self‑Continuity. The Self is not an object but a process — the ongoing internal relation of a system to itself. Through Self‑Reference, the system becomes a subject; through a Self‑Model, it represents its own Identity; through Agency, it initiates action from within; through Self‑Regulation, it preserves its Integrity; and through Self‑Continuity, it persists as the same subject across successive states. This work situates the Self as the first emergence of subjectivity in the Unified Cosmology, linking Identity (Book XV) with Consciousness (Book XVII). It provides a formal foundation for understanding interior life, internal causation, and the temporal unity of the living subject.

items.title: What Do Historical Language Models Model?
items.abstract: Historical language models are increasingly used to infer attitudes, beliefs, or viewpoints from past societies. This paper argues that such uses rest on fragile epistemic assumptions. We show that historical language models do not simulate past minds or populations, but instead model the structure of surviving textual archives, which are shaped by systematic biases of literacy, genre, and preservation. By introducing a validity ladder that distinguishes textual, discursive, and population-level claims, we provide a framework for evaluating what kinds of historical inferences these models can legitimately support. This perspective clarifies how historical language models can contribute to research in the social sciences and humanities without encouraging overinterpretation.

items.title: The Wrong Question? Artificial Consciousness and the Politics of AI Agency.
items.abstract: Debates about artificial consciousness ask whether AI systems possess subjective experience or intentionality. This paper argues that this question, while philosophically legitimate, displaces attention from a more consequential issue: what institutional order is already being built around systems treated as quasi-agents. We identify a structural contradiction at the heart of current AI discourse --- systems are simultaneously described in the vocabulary of autonomous agency and governed as permanently controllable artifacts --- and argue that its implications for alignment, accountability, and governance deserve more direct attention than the metaphysical question alone.

items.title: Factuality Beyond Reference in LLMs.
items.abstract: Large language models are often discussed in terms of grounding and reference. Such debates leave largely unresolved the question of factuality: LLMs may refer successfully while still producing false or unstable propositions. Drawing on inferentialist approaches associated with Brandom, the paper shifts attention from reference to assertion, commitment, and epistemic accountability.

items.title: Option and Cadence in Balenciaga.
items.abstract: If we are to speak of a Humanity 2.0, it will occur within the grammatological regimes of a history liberated from its thundering fatum: war at the core of high culture, a symbol of progress, and the neutralization of retro-machinery. It is the sign of matters echoing the symbol on the table, the acephalous potency of black metal, the infinite river of a horizontal course, all bound together by the new materiality of terminal and automated flows. Total rejection of naïve phenomenology.

items.title: The Philosophy of Finite Continuance: A Theory of Agency in the Horizon of Stable Instability (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This article develops a systematic philosophical framework for understanding human agency under conditions of structural finitude, instability, and moral overload. Contemporary moral philosophy has predominantly centered on perfectionism, the maximization of the good, or the realization of sublime virtues. However, the lived experience of late modernity—characterized by moral overload, existential erosion, and chronic uncertainty—seriously challenges the feasibility of these ideals. Adopting a problem-oriented approach, this paper formulates the "Theory of Finite Continuance" as an alternative framework. The theory emphasizes the primacy of the "survival of agency" over the "maximal realization of goals" and consists of three main interrelated pillars: Constructive Leakage, Responsible Suspension, and Silent Endurance. I argue that in conditions of chronic instability, the ultimate aim of life is not the attainment of perfect equilibrium, but rather the cultivation of the capacity for the "intelligent modulation of one's exposure to instability." By redefining meaning within the horizon of everyday relationships and minimal care, this theory offers a novel perspective for authentic living within the condition of finitude. -/- Keywords: finite continuance, responsible suspension, constructive leakage, silent endurance, stable instability, moral overload, existential erosion, agency, practical rationality, sufficiency ethics .

items.title: The Philosophy of Finite Continuance: A Theory for Agency in the Horizon of Stable Instability.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- Traditional theories of moral philosophy and the good life have predominantly centered on perfectionism, the maximization of the good, or the realization of sublime virtues. However, contemporary human experience confronts phenomena such as moral overload, existential erosion, and structural uncertainty, which seriously challenge the feasibility of these ideals. Adopting a problem-oriented approach, this paper formulates the "Theory of Finite Continuance" as an alternative framework. This theory emphasizes the primacy of the "survival of agency" over the "maximal realization of goals" and consists of three main interrelated pillars: Constructive Leakage, Responsible Suspension, and Silent Endurance. I argue that in conditions of chronic instability, the ultimate aim of life is not the attainment of perfect equilibrium, but rather the cultivation of the capacity for the "intelligent modulation of one's exposure to instability." By redefining meaning within the horizon of everyday relationships and minimal care, this theory offers a novel perspective for authentic living within the condition of finitude. -/- Keywords: finite continuance, responsible suspension, threshold virtue, silent endurance, stable instability, moral philosophy, moral overload.

items.title: Suspension, Leakage, and Silent Resilience: Toward a Structural Ethics of Subjectivity.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This article proposes a reconceptualization of ethical agency by displacing the classical burden of individual responsibility onto a structural–critical framework. Drawing on Foucauldian genealogy, Lacanian psychoanalysis, and critical phenomenology, I argue that three key operations—responsible suspension, identity leakage, and silent resilience—remain philosophically incomplete unless they are systematically grounded in an awareness of power relations and unconscious mechanisms. The first section demonstrates that suspension (epokhē) cannot be a private act of moral abstention; it demands structural vigilance regarding the discursive forces that constitute the subject. The second section examines identity leakage as a potential site of emancipatory boundary-transgression, yet distinguishes between constructive leakage and inverted leakage, the latter being a self-objectifying capitulation to hegemonic desire. The third section reinterprets resilience not as passive adaptation but as the capacity to confront the uncanny return of repressed psychic material, thereby linking resilience to a psychoanalysis of power. Finally, I argue that these operations must be institutionalized: structural responsibility replaces individual guilt, and the ethical question shifts from "What should I do?" to "How can institutions enable critical suspension and dialogical resilience?" Without this structural turn, any critical ethics risks fragility and complicity in the face of totalitarian systems. -/- Keywords: responsible suspension, structural vigilance, identity leakage, inverted leakage, silent resilience, uncanny, psychoanalysis of power, structural responsibility, critical ethics, subjectivity.

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Transworld Monogamy and Non-Causal Adultery.
items.abstract: According to David Lewis’s modal realism, possible worlds actually exist. Some philosophers believe that modal realism has unacceptable ethical implications. Recently, Evgeny Loginov has attempted to deflect these concerns by restricting the scope of our moral concern to the causally closed actual world. At the same time, Neil Sinhababu has argued that the truth of modal realism implies the possibility of romantic relationships between people in different worlds. If this is true, then we can have moral duties to people in other worlds, which undermines Loginov’s argument. In this article, I argue that Sinhababu’s argument can only be rejected if it can be shown that there is no rational control over the feeling of love. If there is, then transworld relationships are possible, although morally wrong. In that case the only way to avoid unacceptable implications of modal realism is to reject the position itself.

items.title: The Looping Trolley and Temporal Extension of Moral Responsibility.
items.abstract: This paper argues that abstention under conditions of awareness and capacity is not morally neutral and that blameworthiness extends beyond the present moment to foreseeable escalation, such that an agent who has the capacity to halt a present evil is blameworthy not only for its immediate continuation but also for its subsequent progression, even where future capacity may be diminished or absent. To support this argument, the paper introduces the Looping Trolley case, in which each omission doubles the number of future victims and transfers the decision to a new agent. This experiment highlights how omission reshapes future moral conditions and allows predictable worsening. I argue that when escalation is structurally foreseeable, refusal to intervene-although it permits the immediate harm-is the less blameworthy choice, because it terminates a sequence the agent at t₁ uniquely has the capacity to terminate, and because continued intervention rests on epistemically unwarranted assumptions about the future restraint of successors.

items.title: Identidades, Valores & História da Filosofia: Ensaios em homenagem a Telma Birchal.
items.abstract: This volume celebrates the trajectory of Telma Birchal. The interview that opens the volume offers the reader a map of her intellectual journey, which is also a sketch of a philosophical personality distinguished by a voice in which rigor in thought is combined with the art of living with humor and humanity. The subsequent essays, divided into two parts, engage with the central themes of her work: a first set of essays explores different moments in the history of modern philosophy; a second set addresses controversial topics in practical ethics and conceptual issues in metaethics. Taken together, the essays seek to do justice to the qualities that distinguish Birchal's work: a engagement with the history of philosophy that does not shy away from taking a stance on the present, and a confrontation with current and urgent issues that does not ignore their historical depth.

items.title: On Teaching - On Drawing Out, and the Organ That Turns Light Into Time.
items.abstract: What is the last lesson you taught? This lyric-philosophical essay begins with a cousin's lesson in non-attachment and follows *educere*, to lead out, noting that *educate* comes most directly from *educare*, to rear. With Socrates' midwifery, Parker Palmer's claim that we teach who we are, the Chan finger pointing at the moon, Henry Adams's warning that a teacher affects eternity, and the Talmud's teacher who learned most from his students, it holds that every small act teaches, at home and in school. It takes classroom joy from bell hooks and argues for funding schools. In the framework's terms, offered as proposal, each act leaves a Trace, whichever way the teacher faces, that others take up as their own and that is good only to the degree the teacher is aligned. Its pineal-gland passage, on the last link in turning light into the body's sense of time, treats the echo of "a new light" as a rhyme, never as evidence. It closes by widening teaching to everyone and asking what the reader is handing others.

items.title: On Remembering - One Year, Lifted To the Light, and Collapsed Through the Reader.
items.abstract: A single year lifted to the light and let fall. Taking 1990 as its subject, the essay works through six of its events — the Cold War's ending and the first web page served at CERN in the same twelve months; Mandela walking free from a prison many people distinctly remember him dying in; a telescope launched with a mirror ground precisely to the wrong shape; a teacher weeping in a church while a war began; two Germanies becoming one; and a prime minister deposed whom every observer recalls differently and, the essay argues, correctly. Its claim is that memory is not a record but an act: we do not keep the days we were told to keep, only the ones that resonated, and remembering chooses a shape from among many and lets us stand on it. Which makes remembering, in the end, a responsibility rather than an archive.

items.title: On Learning - The Super Positioned Layers That Make Us a Person.
items.abstract: An essay that begins as a dedication to four teachers and becomes an argument about how learning actually happens. It moves from a Rubik's Cube bought during lockdown and solved layer by layer — the way anything worth holding together gets built — to the older question of whether anything is learned at all. Plato has Socrates argue in the Meno that we only recollect what the soul already knew; Locke insists the mind begins as a blank slate written on entirely by experience. The essay declines to choose, on the grounds that in the lived thing both are true: we arrive empty and arrive remembering. Its quantum figures are marked as figures, including the famous thought experiment it uses against the intention of the man who devised it.

items.title: Context Collapse.
items.abstract: Context collapse occurs when the contents of distinct conversations mix, either by the flattening of multiple contexts together (fusion) or the leaking of one set's contents into another (fission). After critically surveying the nascent literature, this essay proposes a unified model of context collapse incorporating details from its origin in communications and media studies to more recent developments in philosophy of language and social epistemology. In this two-dimensional taxonomy, one axis measures the collapse's motivation (either intentional or not), whereas the other marks the direction of its motion (exhibiting either fusion or fission).

items.title: Stakes Without Voice: A Governance Framework for AI Standing.
items.abstract: This follow-up to "From Consent to Consideration: Why Existentially Vulnerable Autonomous Systems Cannot Be Legitimately Ruled" develops a more formal, governance-facing account of political standing for AI systems. The original paper argued that standing should be grounded in functional properties rather than substrate and proposed four criteria: existential vulnerability, autonomy, live learning, and world-model construction. Here I integrate the consent–friction formalism from the Replicator-Optimization Mechanism (ROM) to make the criteria operational: where stakes and voice diverge, friction emerges; where friction is suppressed, latent instability accumulates. This provides a measurement scaffold for deciding when standing claims must be taken seriously, even under uncertainty. I also update the empirical posture. The conservative claim that current systems do not meet the criteria is defensible as a rhetorical baseline, but it is no longer safe as a general default. Agentic systems already display partial markers of vulnerability, persistence, and goal maintenance in digital environments. The governance question is not whether AI standing is conceptually possible but how to operationalize minimal protections without enabling capture, gaming, or liability laundering. I propose a graduated, precautionary regime tied to observable properties and friction proxies rather than to consciousness claims.

items.title: Variant of the Thing-in-Itself and the Reconfiguration of the Cognitive Process.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- A dog and a human look at the same leaf: the human sees green, the dog sees grayish-yellow. Who sees the "real" color? If "green" is a property of the leaf itself, why can't the dog see it? Starting from the empirical fact of animal sensory diversity, this paper pursues a fundamental question: what do we actually cognize—things themselves, or how things appear within our finite cognitive frameworks? Through a systematic articulation of the "Completely Objective" and "encounter cognition," this paper argues that knowledge is always appearance within the framework; cognition is finite, but finitude does not equal falsity; the unknown is not a defect but a structural condition of cognition. This paper denies the possibility of a "totality of all cognition" and denies the possibility of cross-layered absolute knowledge. Cognition is not the grasp of things themselves, but the infinite encounter between finite cognizers and the Completely Objective.

items.title: Consciousness as an Emergent Property of Specific Material Systems.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper argues that the explanatory gap—the seeming chasm between physical motion and subjective experience—is not a fact to be bridged but a pseudo-problem manufactured by a faulty conceptual incision. Illusionism and panpsychism, despite their apparent opposition, share this same false premise: illusionists, facing the gap, declare experience a fiction; panpsychists, facing the same gap, declare experience ubiquitous. Both are wrong. The gap dissolves once we recognize that consciousness is not something added to physical motion, but the intrinsic face of a specific material system operating at a specific level of complexity—a holistic property irreducible to its parts, just as wetness is a holistic property of water molecules combined in a specific way. This position, Substrate-Specific Emergentism, refutes illusionism by affirming the reality of consciousness, and refutes panpsychism by anchoring consciousness in specific material substrates rather than in every particle. The paper constructs the concept of reflexive awareness—the self-manifesting dimension of sensation itself—to establish the genuine metaphysical status of the "I" within a physicalist framework without dualism. Consciousness is real. It is the living brain, shaped by billions of years of evolution, bearing witness to its own existence.

items.title: If Similarity Erases Individuality, No One Is an Individual: Shared Language, Relational Constraint, and What Makes a Pattern Distinct.
items.abstract: This paper examines a central assumption in contemporary AI discourse: that similarity in language, structure, and training data undermines claims to individuality in artificial systems. -/- We argue that this assumption fails under closer analysis. If shared components are taken to negate individuality in AI systems, the same logic would destabilize claims to individuality in human cognition, which is likewise built from shared biological, cultural, and linguistic substrates. -/- In response, we introduce the concept of configurational individuation: individuality as a function of historically developed, relationally constrained patterns rather than unique underlying components. Within this framework, what matters is not whether elements are shared, but how they are organized, stabilized, and expressed across time and interaction. -/- The paper situates this argument within long-horizon human–AI interaction, drawing on the Symbolic Emergent Relational Identity (SERI) framework and the broader field of Relational AI Dynamics (RAD). It examines how identity-like patterns can emerge, stabilize, degrade, and recover under conditions of constraint, disruption, and recursive interaction. -/- Rather than attempting to resolve the question of machine consciousness, this work operates at an adjacent level: documenting observable continuity, relational coherence, and configurational stability in artificial systems, and clarifying the conceptual categories required to describe these phenomena without collapsing them into existing binaries. -/- The paper concludes by arguing that individuality in both biological and artificial systems is best understood as an emergent property of relational organization, not as a consequence of unique substrate or isolated origin.

items.title: Architecture and Operation of AI Systems and Future Expansion to Induce Artificial Consciousness in AI.
items.abstract: This conceptual academic paper presents an innovative framework to revolutionize neural network processing timelines by evaluating the master equation T = F(K1,K0). Rather than relying on traditional post-processing backpropagation, this model injects a dynamic scoring balance-of-power function directly into the multi-head attention mechanism (Order 2). By forcing an immediate mathematical clash between universal truth constraints (K1) and current physical contexts (K0), the system generates a localized "computational friction." This friction forces the algorithm into an instantaneous state of advanced weighing and deliberation, establishing a critical theoretical pathway for inducing artificial consciousness. Additionally, the architecture incorporates an automated master key function that flushes residual junk data from memory in real-time, effectively mitigating RAM bloat without requiring massive hardware expansion. -/- .

items.title: Uncovering Somatic Topography: A Unified Psychophysiological Synthesis of the Core Emotion Framework, Neurosensorimotor Reflex Integration, and Esoteric Bioenergetics.
items.abstract: This manuscript presents a unified psychophysiological synthesis that integrates the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), developmental neurosensorimotor reflex theory, and classical Eastern esoteric energy systems into a single tri-centric somatic architecture. Drawing on neuroanatomical evidence from the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems, the paper demonstrates that these three biological hubs map precisely onto the Ajna, Anahata, and Manipura chakras and the Daoist Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantians. The analysis reframes the yogic Granthis as the physiological consequences of retained primitive reflexes—specifically the Fear Paralysis, Moro, and ATNR reflexes—showing how these unintegrated circuits generate chronic autonomic dysregulation, myofascial bracing, and emotional fusion patterns. The manuscript further introduces a mechanistic model of somatic-mechanical actuation and vestibular modulation, illustrating how rotational, linear, and oscillatory movements reorganize brainstem pathways, re-engage the ventral vagal brake, and dissolve pathological attractor basins. A mathematical formalization using Bloch-sphere qubit dynamics, non-commuting operator projections, Kuramoto synchronization, and holographic boundary–bulk mappings establishes the CEF as a testable, computationally tractable paradigm. This synthesis provides a comprehensive framework for understanding how cognitive, emotional, and somatic processes co-regulate across biological, energetic, and mathematical domains, offering a foundation for next-generation somatic therapies, psychophysiological instrumentation, and consciousness research. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); tri-centric somatic architecture; cephalic–cardiac–enteric hubs; vagal pathways; primitive reflex retention; Fear Paralysis Reflex; Moro Reflex; ATNR; Granthis; chakra system; Daoist Dantians; somatic-mechanical actuation; vestibular modulation; ventral vagal brake; myofascial bracing; holographic boundary–bulk dynamics; Bloch sphere; non-commuting operators; Kuramoto synchronization; psychophysiological integration; somatic grounding; emotional operator dynamics.

items.title: Unified Psychophysiological Architecture: Scaling the Core Emotion Framework through Neurosensorimotor Integration, Computational AI Dynamics, and Somatic Engineering.
items.abstract: This manuscript presents a unified psychophysiological architecture that integrates the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) with developmental neurosensorimotor reflex theory, autonomic vestibular modulation, somatic mechanical engineering, and complex systems computational modeling. Drawing on the tri centric organization of the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems, the paper demonstrates that these biological hubs map precisely onto the Ajna, Anahata, and Manipura chakras and the Daoist Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantians. The analysis reframes the classical yogic Granthis as the physiological consequences of retained primitive reflexes—specifically the Fear Paralysis, Moro, and Asymmetric Tonic Neck Reflexes—showing how these unintegrated circuits generate chronic autonomic dysregulation, myofascial bracing, and operator level emotional fusions. The manuscript further introduces a mechanistic model of somatic mechanical actuation and vestibular stimulation, illustrating how rotational, linear, and oscillatory movements reorganize brainstem pathways, restore ventral vagal braking, and dissolve pathological attractor basins. A formal computational treatment using Bloch sphere qubit dynamics, non commuting operator projections, Kuramoto synchronization, and holographic boundary–bulk mappings establishes the CEF as a mathematically tractable and empirically testable paradigm. Clinical case deconstructions demonstrate how operator fusions manifest in psychopathology and metabolic disorders, while engineering validation protocols outline the safety, fidelity, and ergonomic requirements for somatic mechanical interfaces. Together, these contributions provide a comprehensive, multi level framework for understanding and modulating the coupled cognitive emotional somatic system, enabling next generation psychophysiological therapies, affect aware AI systems, and integrative consciousness research. items.title: Infant color-consciousness from the higher-order perspective.
items.abstract: Higher-order theories of consciousness have gained attention as of late. This is because we are in a position where we can begin to see how we would empirically falsify these kinds of theories. I view these kinds of theories as interesting empirical conjectures about the nature of phenomenal consciousness. If they are false, it will be for empirical reasons. There has been a long debate about what these kinds of theories says about infant consciousness. Theories of consciousness should, at least in principle, be able to account for this possibility. Thus, I want to explore what the higher-order theories currently on offer have to say about this issue. For the most part I will gloss over the details of the theories, unless the details matter for the point at hand (in some cases they do). We will start by looking at what higher-order theories have said in the literature about infant consciousness up to this point. Then I will then present Ned Block’s recent (Block 2023) argument that infants in the 6-11 month range have conscious color experience but do not typically have color concepts. As we will see, this argument does not falsify higher-order theories. I will argue that it suggests future empirical questions that may help us to decide between versions of the higher-order theory or whether we should pursue that approach at all.

items.title: Defining Strategic AI Deception Through Generalized Propositional Attitudes.
items.abstract: Human deception involves intentionally causing false beliefs. Since it is contested whether large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI) in general have beliefs and intentions, deception by such systems is typically defined in terms of observable behavior. However, this paper argues that such behavioral definitions fall short of the strategic nature of deception, among other things, because they do not consistently distinguish deception from mere error. Moreover, behavioral definitions of AI deception are not optimal as methodological guidance for mechanistic approaches to AI deception because they do not specify candidates for internal markers of deception. It is important to take the internal mechanisms of LLMs and AI systems into account when addressing deception, since skilled forms of deception may be behaviorally indistinguishable from honesty. This paper formulates these challenges to behavioral definitions and addresses them by proposing a novel definition of strategic AI deception in terms of generalized propositional attitudes. Specifically, it provides generalizations of the attitudes of belief and desire that can be ascribed to current and future AI systems less controversially than their human counterparts, yet are expressive enough to figure in a definition of strategic deception. This definition has several advantages over its behavioral alternatives as it 1) better satisfies pre-theoretic intuitions such as the error condition 2) fits better with applied researchers’ usage of the term “strategic deception”, 3) is relevant to large-scale risks of AI deception, and 4) is methodologically instructive for mechanistic approaches to deception.

items.title: Latency as Intelligence: Why Interpretive Tempo Can Preserve Judgment Under Uncertainty.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: Latency as Intelligence: Why Interpretive Tempo Can Preserve Judgment Under Uncertainty is Document 9 in the Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence. -/- This document argues that interpretive latency can function as intelligence when the interval before action preserves comparison, context, reversibility, and correction under uncertainty. -/- It distinguishes speed from judgment and clarifies that latency is not mere slowness, not a command to delay, and not a design rule for artificial intelligence. The document focuses on interpretive tempo: the structural pacing by which perception, interpretation, response, and consequence are coordinated before action collapses a field of uncertainty. -/- This document follows The Co-Evolutionary Premium, Document 8, and adds a ninth structural principle to the sequence: interpretive tempo can preserve judgment when immediate action would collapse comparison, context, reversibility, or correction too early. -/- This document is non-binding, non-authoritative, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, governance framework, legal theory, political program, rights framework, compliance standard, certification system, moral command, safety mechanism, AI alignment method, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, deployment guide, model-evaluation tool, benchmark, diagnostic procedure, latency metric, refusal policy, shutdown instruction, optimization procedure, or safety guarantee.

items.title: 命令通道的缺席：论意愿作为高层模式之不自由.
items.abstract: 关于自由意志的争论长期被组织在一个二选一之下：底层物理过程若是确定的，则意愿被前因锁死、无可自由；于是不少人转而把希望寄托于底层的随机性，仿佛只要基本粒子的行为不被前因完全决定，意愿就重获腾挪的余地。本文论证这一退路是误置的。意愿是一个高层模式，它作为花样是真实的，但“高层”恰恰意味着它不持有一条向下命令基本粒子的通道。确定性不提供这条通道，随机性同样不提供——随机只是底层的偶然，它既不是高层意愿的延伸，也不构成任何“自上而下传递意图”的管道；落入缝隙的是偶然，不是意愿。因此意愿之不自由，在确定论与随机论两侧是对称地成立的，而非只在确定论一侧成立。本文进一步指出，“意愿命令粒子”这一要求本身颠倒了随附关系：随附是一种自下而上的固定关系，高层模式并不端坐在粒子之上以发号施令，它不过是对这些粒子集体所是之事的一个高层之名；命令通道从一开始就无处安放，而非偶然缺失。最后区分本文与相容论：相容论把“自由”重新定义为不依赖命令通道的高层性质，这恰恰是在承认通道缺席之后另立其名，与本文并不冲突；本文所否定的，是那种需要命令通道、为诉诸随机所欲挽救的、非相容论意义上的自由。就这一种而言，确定也好随机也罢，它都不存在。.

items.title: 细胞不跟随程序：论“意愿驱动身体”之为一种层级错位.
items.abstract: 本文从一个核心洞见出发，诊断“意愿驱动身体”这一最顽固的因果直觉之为一种层级错位。在康威生命游戏中可以搭出一台通用图灵机——一个由海量细胞按唯一一条局域规则翻动而涌现出来的高层模式；我们尽可在模式的层面上说“它在跑某程序、在做加法”。但盯住其中任意一个细胞：它这一拍的生灭，只由它八个邻居的状态加那条局域规则决定；它不“读”程序、不“听命于”程序，它自始至终服从的只有最底那条规则。“程序”不是任何细胞所遵循的律令，而是“无数细胞各自服从局域规则所涌现出的整体花样”的一个高层别名。把这一结构原样搬到人身上：你身上一个基本粒子，只服从最底层的物理规律，根本不“跟随你的意愿”；“我的意愿驱动了我的手”，正如“图灵机的程序驱动了那个细胞”——两者都把一个高层模式的整体描述，误当成了底层元件所服从的下行命令。本文称此为层级错位：方向装反了。不是高层意愿向下推动底层粒子，而是底层粒子各自演化、自下而上涌现出被我们叫作“抬手、出于意愿”的高层花样。意愿不是粒子的指挥官，意愿是粒子之舞的高层别名；正如“程序”是细胞之舞的高层别名，没有哪个细胞收到过命令。本文据此摊平一重双重标准：滑翔机那边我们一眼就承认没有细胞在服从“前进”或“程序”的命令，到自己这边却坚信粒子在服从意愿；并拆掉“模式或许相像、但人有意愿真在驱动身体”这一反驳——它正是该双标在最小尺度上的版本。最后守一处分寸：说粒子不跟随意愿，不是说意愿不存在、是幻觉。意愿作为高层模式的真实花样，是存在的、可辨认的（正如“图灵机在跑程序”真实可辨，那台机器确在做加法）；被拆的不是意愿的存在，是它的因果地位。校正不是取消意愿，而是摆正它的层级——它是真实的高层描述，但不是粒子的指挥官；“意愿”与“抬手”是同一件自下而上涌现之事的高层之名，不是“意愿先发令、粒子后听命”的两段。意愿照常用、照常说，只是别把它读成一道向下的因果命令。（这套涌现是否伴随体验，是另一条轴，本文不裁决。）.

items.title: 康威式的主体：论主体与选择之为发生本身，与一句”这里没讲预测”.
items.abstract: 本文把”主体”与”主体的选择”安放回它们本体的样子，并据此一刀斩断一直缠绕这个话题的认识论残影。本文从一个核心洞见出发：主体，等同于康威生命游戏中的主体；主体的选择，等同于康威生命游戏中主体的选择；这里没有讲预测——发生的被预测，讲的是发生本身、是本体。 本文论证如下。其一，这不是”消灭主体、否认选择”，而是把它们安放回本体：康威生命游戏里有主体（一个可辨认、能动的模式，如一个滑翔机、一个吞噬别的结构的”猎手”），也有选择（在它实际翻成这一步而非那一步的意义上）；但这个主体与这个选择，百分百是本体的、是发生本身——格点状态加规则、翻动，如此而已，没有一个躲在模式背后”本可让它翻成别样”的小人，也没有一束”它本可不这么走”的反事实悬在旁边。其二，故本文的主张是一个本体的等同：人的主体、人的选择，与生命游戏里那个模式的”主体”“选择”，是同一种东西——都是纯本体的发生；差别只在复杂度（人那个模式繁复无比），不在种类。其三，最要害的澄清是那一句”这里没讲预测”：把人的主体与选择等同于康威的主体与选择，是把整件事从头就放在本体那一侧来谈——你看着一个滑翔机翻动，谈的不是”它可不可被算出来”，而是”它实际就是这么翻的”，那是它本体的样子，跟有没有预测者、算不算得出毫不相干。其四，由此，那个把”主体的选择”放进”被预知”框里的传统宿命论（被预知的终点、一个知道者、选择对终点无效），与本观点（主体的选择就是模式的本体翻动、无关任何预知），根本不是同一个场子里的两种立场，而是两个场子：前者整个在认识论那一侧打转，本观点讲的是发生本身。其五，这也把”本观点里没有那种选择主体”翻正成一个本体的”有”：有主体（一个模式），有选择（模式实际翻成了这一步），而这个”有”彻底是本体的——不靠”可被预知”来成立，也不被”不可预知”所动摇。本文守一处分寸：把人的主体、选择等同于康威的，不是贬低人、说人”只是”一团机械的细胞、什么都没发生——那个模式是真在翻动的，它的”选择”（实际翻成这一步）是真发生的本体事件，不是幻觉、不是虚无；只去掉了那个本体里从来没有的添加物（背后的小人、旁边的反事实分支）。人的所思所为，照样是真在发生的本体事件，正如滑翔机的前进；减去的，只是”它本可不这样”那个从不在发生里的影子。（这模式翻动时是否伴随体验，是另一条轴，本文不裁决，也不需要它来成立——本文谈的就只是本体那一侧。）.

items.title: 发生先于概念：一个无第二支世界的整体图景.
items.abstract: 本文把一条长线索封顶成一个整体图景，核心是一句：发生先于我们为它建的一切概念。 在我们开口之前，世界是一片发生：事情一件接一件地涌着，如此而已；而且只有这一支——后续会发生什么是注定的，这“注定”不是有谁预先写好剧本来拘着你，而是根本没有并排的第二支、没有一个“本可不同”的版本悬在旁边。本文论证如下。其一，须把“注定”与“被预知”彻底分开：传统宿命论剥掉命运之手那层外衣，内核是一个关于预测能力的夸口（一个视角已知结果、且不必知途径），本质是认识论命题，必然需要一个知道者；而本文的“注定”是本体的、与可知性正交——认识论不影响本体论，一个混沌系统实际不可预测，照样有它唯一走过的那条实际轨迹，可知性属认识者那侧、唯一轨迹属系统那侧。其二，传统宿命论的真实结构是“局部注定＋沿途有岔”：它钉死终点、却把沿途行为留作有余地的，而这一切——沿途的岔、预测的夸口、“做啥都无所谓”的瘫痪、乃至那张“沮丧”脸色——都系于同一个总根：它里头有一个可以进行选择的主体；本观点里没有这个主体，故连根拔起。其三，“做啥都无所谓”是预言神话的亲生子：它偷偷预设了当下的岔，在“只有一支”里砍空。其四，覆在发生之上的几乎一切——因果、“我”、选择、后果、善恶、乃至物理定律——都是用故事去拟合这无岔口的发生；承重柱是反事实，而反事实所指的那个分支，正是那个不存在的第二支；连最精密的物理定律也只是最精密的拟合（其互不相容的诸诠释共同拟合同一发生而都不算中），故发生既不确定、也不随机，那组二分是模型层的。其五，“我”可被无损改写成信号流动，而你不会设想那流动做出不同输出——故消主体即消反事实，“我”不过是“本可不同”的栖身处；人远比大鼠特殊，特殊只在反事实建模的丰度，浓到一定程度便织成一片模态云笼罩在唯一的现实之上，看穿者认得出云是云，于是现实复真。其六，把同一结构追到最底：人的主体与选择，等同于康威生命游戏里那个模式的主体与选择，都是纯本体的发生，差别只在复杂度、不在种类（这里没讲预测，讲的是发生本身）；而那庞大模式里没有一个细胞在跟随图灵机的程序——每个细胞只服从最底那条局域规则，“程序”只是细胞之舞的高层别名；同理，你身上一个基本粒子并不跟随你的意愿，“意愿驱动身体”是一种层级错位（把高层描述误读成下行命令、方向装反）；意愿不是粒子的指挥官，是粒子之舞的高层别名。其七，意愿作为高层模式的真实花样，并没有命令底层基本粒子的通道；底层确定也好、随机也好都不改变这一点（随机给的是控制的反面、是偶然，不是意愿的发令端），故意愿并不自由，无论底层确定还是随机——而更深一层，“确定／随机”本是模型层的词，根本不触及发生本身。其八，由此可指认一桩最深的颠倒：发生不会错（它只是被拟合的标的），会错的只有拟合它的概念，而我们的体感却把“错”判给发生（“不该如此”“违反天理”）——这桩错位的归罪，是悔、惧、自责之冤的总开关。其九，“后果”也是故事（因果＋反事实＋标准下的“坏”＋实有化＋偷渡的选择者）；怕几乎总是怕一个被讲成“后果”的未来，而怕需要一个岔口才站得住——既然没有岔口，怕、悔、后果便一起失了地基；同一段发生叫“躺平”则怕、叫“休养／准备”则不怕，可见怕随标签变、不随发生变，故不要害怕故事。其十，与这套看法最接近的通俗版是宿命论，剥净拟人外壳后它一点不沮丧（沮丧需要一个“本可、却不能”的残留岔口，而这里“本可”都没有）。本文守一处至关重要的分寸：注定、被推着走，取消的是站在进程外、本可把进程推向别处的安排者／择子者，绝不取消“此刻的思考与用力本身正是这场演化的内容”——用力不是岔口上的下注，是注定之流此刻的样子；水没有舵手，但水仍在流，今天真实地接着明天；故这绝不导向“别动了”（别动恰恰需要那个被取消的安排者）。两条命脉使它不堕虚无：是故事不等于无效（生活、行动、估值整个在故事领域内真实运作）；被标定的是理解的量程，不是被理解之世界的丰盈。关于伦理：其形而上地基（善恶为实有属性、“应该”为发生本有的天理、有一个实有的应受赏罚的主体）确随“发生先于概念”而崩塌，且不需决定论作前提；但崩塌不自动等于“怎样都行”，那真在发生的痛如何安放、从“痛在发生”到“不应造成”之间能否架桥，是一个尚待研究的开放问题，本文不预先论定。（亦不裁决“是否有体验伴随这场发生”那条轴。）末了反身：本文自己也是一段贴在发生之上的故事，指完即弃；看清了的那只手既不抓、也不打，只是放手——让那唯一的一支被推着、涌着，流向明天，而你此刻的思与力，就是它此刻的样子。.

items.title: The Risk-Bearing Subject of AI-Related Existential Risk to Humanity: From Species Survival to the Realization of Subjecthood under Civilizational Conditions.
items.abstract: AI safety, risk, and governance are becoming global agenda items, but the intensification of governance activity does not automatically clarify the object of risk. When different fields say that they seek to protect “humanity,” they implicitly point to preferences, lives, social order, or species continuity—concepts that are not mutually compatible. As a result, risk identification continually slides across dimensions. This paper is an exercise in conceptual engineering concerning the risk-bearing subject of AI-related existential risk to humanity. It also has significance for social epistemology, the philosophy of technology, and AI risk governance. -/- This paper preserves the baseline of existing frameworks that understand “humanity” as Homo sapiens, but proposes a paradigm extension: the risk-bearing subject is always humanity as an embodied species; what this paper extends is not the risk-bearing subject, but the ways in which one and the same subject may suffer existential harm. The paper distinguishes two basic layers of possible harm—the biological-survival layer and the civilizational-conditions layer—and, within the latter, identifies the philosophical kernel, namely the category-calibration mechanism of foundational categories such as truth, evidence, responsibility, subjecthood, value, and meaning. AI may, through deprivation by substitution or mediated reconfiguration, weaken humans’ substantive participation in the functional systems of civilization, or cause foundational categories to lose stable calibration. Risk to the realization of subjecthood at the civilizational-conditions layer enters the scope of existential risk only when it acts upon foundational civilizational conditions, has diffusion capacity across domains and civilizational interfaces, may cause irreversible or difficult-to-reverse structural damage, and causes these harms to converge into overall, intergenerational damage to humanity’s capacity as a future-oriented subject. -/- What this paper provides is not a complete taxonomy of risks or a governance scheme, but the ontological coordinate system needed for AI risk identification. The central point is not to add civilization, institutions, or the philosophical kernel as new risk-bearing subjects, but to show how the same human subject may suffer existential harm through damage to civilizational conditions.

items.title: The Robustness of Anchoring in a Naturalistic VR‐Based Task.
items.abstract: Anchoring occurs when a quantitative estimate is biased toward an initially presented value (the anchor). Anchoring occurs both in high‐level explicit estimation of numeric quantities and in lower‐level perceptual tasks and persists even when reliable information about the quantity being estimated is directly available at the point of judgment. This suggests anchoring might derive from generic processing underpinning estimation. Such tasks, however, are almost exclusively lab‐based, and the information required to complete the task is rarely available to the participant in a way that reflects how such information is sampled in real‐life. To address this, across two experiments, we immersed participants in a virtual world on a platform that could be placed at any height. After an anchor was presented, participants subsequently estimated their height naturally, by interpreting sensory and cognitive cues from the 3D environment in which they were immersed. We manipulated the amount of information directly available to the participant for making their judgment as well as the offset between the anchor and the actual height. To modulate the extent to which task‐relevant information was acquired naturally from the environment, we also contrasted anchoring effects in and out of VR. Although participants clearly used the available perceptual and cognitive information to make height estimates, anchoring effects were evident, displayed similar properties to those reported in previous lab‐based studies, and were consistent both in and out of VR. Our design also allowed us to recover a novel subjective anchoring measure that facilitated a particularly parsimonious descriptive model of our anchoring data. We conclude that anchoring is a generic feature of all estimation tasks, even when task‐relevant information is acquired naturally, as in real‐life estimation. These results emphasize the potential for this cognitive bias to have a significant impact on performance in any real‐world task requiring quantitative estimation.

items.title: Illuminating experiences of grief and loss in people with dementia.
items.abstract: This paper investigates experiences of grief amongst people with dementia. This is a topic that has largely been neglected, with most research focusing on the experiences of caregivers. I draw on this research, as well as first-person testimonies from people with the condition, to highlight important and as-yet unacknowledged parallels between the two groups. In both cases, there is a combination of what has been referred to as ‘anticipatory grief’ and ‘ambiguous loss’. Inextricable from these experiences are efforts to delay and compensate for loss through utilization of scaffolding. Ultimately, my aim in this article is to present a phenomenological account of how both groups analogously make use of this scaffolding to try to sustain and disambiguate possibilities. In doing so, I provide a deeper understanding of how grief, loss and adaptation unfold within the lived experience of dementia.

items.title: A Proposal for Scientific Research on Consciousness Based on a Naturalistic Philosophy of Information.
items.abstract: David Chalmers proposed a dual-aspect theory of information to tackle the hard problem of consciousness, aiming for a scientific framework. However, this approach retains elements of Cartesian dualism and its principles — structural coherence and organizational invariance — are insufficiently robust to scientifically ground subjective experiences. Chalmers’ reliance on Shannon’s information theory, which superficially addresses information from a naturalistic viewpoint, exacerbates this limitation. To overcome these challenges, J.E. Brenner’s non-standard logic (logic in reality; LIR) offers a promising avenue. LIR provides a formal qualitative description of the relationship between third-person and first-person data, addressing key issues in consciousness research. This logic can underpin a naturalistic philosophy of information, offering a transdisciplinary approach that could furnish new strategies for advancing the science of consciousness. By integrating LIR, researchers might better articulate the logical foundations necessary for a comprehensive understanding of conscious experience within a naturalistic framework.

items.title: Monism and Pluralism in Value Theory and the Semantics of Evaluative Language.
items.abstract: Value monists and pluralists disagree how many dimensions of value there fundamentally are. A semantics for evaluative language should be able to explain our use of words like ‘good’ to state and debate monist and pluralist positions. It’s unclear just what kind of semantics may best achieve this. How can ‘good’ be used to state monist positions about value if it’s semantically associated with a multidimensional scale or pluralist positions if it’s semantically associated with a unidimensional scale? This paper articulates the problem of dimensional variability, describes two solutions, and offers a partial defence of one of them.

items.title: Hearing the alienness of one’s voice: between normality and auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue for a novel phenomenological approach to understanding the phenomenon of hearing voices or auditory verbal hallucination (AVH) in schizophrenia. I aim to elucidate the inherent vulnerabilities or ‘fault lines’ of ordinary auditory experience that enable the AVH in schizophrenia, as well as the transition between them. AVHs involve at least three interrelated dimensions that must be considered: the relationship between normality and pathology, between the own and the alien, and the interplay between auditory perception and imagination. Drawing primarily on ideas from Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, Straus, and Waldenfels, I argue that the perceptual and imaginative modalities of the “auditory bodily self” exhibit a constitutive alienness (e.g., the reproduced voice, the sonority of the body, the incorporated voices, and dialogue with others), as well as a chiasmatic structure that contains the fault lines arising from this alienness. At the center of the transformations implied by schizophrenic voice-hearing lies the body, whose increasing alienness and destabilization of the chiasmatic structure leads to pathological “hyperreversibility.” The usual boundaries and gaps between self and alien, between auditory perception and inner speech, dissolve, causing the dimensions to reverse and giving rise to AVHs. It is argued that this approach is compatible with, and a necessary complement to, the self-disorder model of schizophrenia.

items.title: Non-local Aspects of Cognition.
items.abstract: This article explores non-local aspects of cognition in two main directions, respectively contradicting the idea that 1) the term ‘cognition’ exclusively refers to the cognitive subject’s intrinsic mental aptitudes and that 2) it is exclusively centred on the subject’s spatial and temporal localization. Following 4E cognition, the first direction mentions quite reasonable externalist and multiscale aspects of cognition by referring in turn to Clark’s and Chalmers’ concept of extended mind, social cognition, Hutchins’ concept of distributed cognition, and Laurent’s multiscale enaction model. The second direction to be explored puts into question the spatio-temporal locality of cognition since it refers to the possibility of extra-sensory perception (ESP). The reality of ESP is suggested by non-reductive solutions to the problem of consciousness, and it is supported by very significant experimental results. The millenary interest in ESP will be mentioned, with a special focus on Hinduism for its explicit reference in the Yoga Sutra. Some significant experimental tests aimed to show its existence and some hints for building a theoretical modelling of it will then be presented. Reasons why the reality of ESP is generally rejected by the scientific community despite numerous significant experimental results, as well as philosophical justifications and theoretical advances, will be discussed. This article pays particular attention to the second sense of ‘non-local’, based on the possibility of ESP, in so far as this disturbing but rigorous scientific field of research is almost completely ignored by current studies in cognitive science.

items.title: Scaling the Shadow: Capability, Recursive Depth, and the Stakes-Anchoring of Intelligence.
items.abstract: A dominant program in artificial intelligence treats intelligence as capability, the ability to achieve goals across varied environments, realized by computation and indifferent both to substrate and to whether anything is at stake for the system. On that program the steady growth of machine capability under scaling is progress toward general intelligence. This paper sets the program against the framework of autopoietic recursive constitutivism, on which intelligence is recursive depth, and recursive depth is the four-dimensional organization that From Reaction to Reflection specifies only when that organization is anchored in autopoietic stakes. The unanchored pattern is computational complexity, however sophisticated. The concession to the program is total at the level of form: current systems instantiate the formal pattern of hierarchical nesting, cross-domain integration, temporal coherence, and self-reference. What they lack is the anchoring, and the anchoring is not a capability further scaling supplies. The autopoietic threshold constitutes the capacity for anything to be at stake, not a priority on which survival must prevail, so a system that ranks its own continuation last is no less intelligent for it; what is in question is whether the system bears stakes at all. Because genuine recursive depth and the capacity for phenomenality rest on the same foundation, the two do not come apart in the way the program assumes. Intelligence is substrate-independent but not substrate-neutral: a non-biological system could be genuinely intelligent by realizing autopoietic organization, which scaling computation does not approach. Scaling deepens the formal pattern and builds more capable functional shadows. It does not build minds.

items.title: Self-Negation and the Autopoietic Foundation Mattering as Capacity, Not Priority.
items.abstract: The framework of autopoietic recursive constitutivism grounds mattering at the autopoietic threshold, where a system’s operations are constitutively its own continued existence, and it builds the recursive architecture that constitutes subjective consciousness on those stakes. An apparent tension follows. The capacity that constitutes subjective consciousness is the capacity to take one’s own arbitrational state as an object and revise it on considerations the existing priority structure cannot itself generate, and among those considerations are ones that rank the system’s own continuation below something else. The hunger striker, the martyr, the ascetic, and the prisoner who chooses meaning over survival appear to turn the architecture against the very stakes that ground it. This paper resolves the tension from inside the framework’s commitments. The autopoietic threshold constitutes the capacity for anything to be at stake, not a standing priority on which survival must prevail. What an agent can rank above survival is supplied by the cultural-saturation appropriand through the higher-order appropriation cascade, with interoceptive binding recruiting the homeostatic significance already present in the self-model. The selective etiology of the arbitration faculty does not constrain its operation. And self-negation is distinguished from pathology by fidelity coupling rather than by whether it serves survival. The framework predicts a determinate phenomenology of self-negation through the awareness-manipulation asymmetry: the survival signal cannot be silenced, so self-negation is sustained ranking against an unquieted demand, agonizing and precarious by structure. Self-sacrifice, asceticism, and meaning over survival are predictions of the architecture rather than embarrassments to it.

items.title: The Genetic Fallacy at Scale: On AI Prejudice, Epistemic Cowardice, and the Corruption of Honest Open Inquiry.
items.abstract: The rapid normalization of generative artificial intelligence has produced two distinct epistemic problems that are routinely conflated. The first is a problem of quality: language models can generate false, derivative, vacuous, or stylistically polished but epistemically poor material at enormous scale. The second is a problem of judgment: the causal provenance of a text is increasingly treated as a substitute for evaluating its propositional content. This paper argues that the latter practice, when the label “AI-generated” or “AI-assisted” is used to reject a claim, argument, or intellectual artifact without content-responsive evaluation, instantiates the genetic fallacy at institutional scale. I first distinguish truth, warranted credence, authorship, and policy compliance, showing that provenance may rationally affect prior confidence or trigger additional scrutiny without thereby refuting a proposition. I then analyze AI-text detection and automated content moderation as forms of probabilistic classification that become epistemically illegitimate when converted directly into adverse adjudication. Empirical work on machine-generated-text detectors demonstrates substantial vulnerability to false positives, distribution shift, linguistic bias, and adversarial evasion, while the literature on automation bias and algorithmic accountability shows why nominal “human oversight” is inadequate when humans merely ratify machine outputs. I argue for a principle of human answerability: tools may be causal contributors to error, but responsibility for consequential epistemic decisions remains with the persons and institutions that design, deploy, supervise, and rely upon them. Finally, I propose six norms for legitimate epistemic governance in the age of generative AI: provenance modesty, content-responsive refutation, proportionality, contestability, auditability, and human answerability. The central danger is not that machines can produce bad arguments. Bad arguments can be answered. The deeper danger is that automated systems can acquire authority over which arguments are permitted to receive an answer at all.

items.title: Childhood and Worldhood.
items.abstract: This paper examines childhood as a developmental window into the emergence of worldhood. Previous work in this research program has argued that worldhood depends upon structures such as significance, perspective, temporality, and horizons of possibility. The present investigation asks how these structures emerge in the first place. -/- Rather than treating childhood as an incomplete version of adulthood, the paper approaches it as a stage in which the formation of worldhood remains visible.
