It argues that significance precedes conceptual understanding, that a meaningful world begins to emerge before a fully articulated sense of self, and that the child enters an already existing yet unfinished world. Through repetition, participation, memory, and social interaction, some patterns of significance become reinforced while others fade from view. Reinforcement stabilises significance, introduces selection among possibilities, and contributes to the emergence of dominant organisations of experience. -/- The paper proposes that childhood reveals worldhood not as a fixed structure but as an ongoing developmental achievement. What appears self-evident and natural in adulthood is shown to be the outcome of processes through which significance becomes organised, reinforced, stabilised, and transformed. By examining these processes, childhood provides insight into a broader philosophical question that extends beyond developmental psychology: how a world becomes possible.

items.title: Virtual Reality Technology and the Moral Education of Children.
items.pub: In Steven S. Gouveia, The Palgrave Handbook on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 573-585.
items.venue: The Palgrave Handbook on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Much has been written on the benefits and risks of VR technology, particularly as this concerns children and their physical, cognitive, and psychosocial development. But little scholarly attention has been given to how Virtual Reality (VR) technology might impact children’s moral development. Even less scholarly work has been done on the responsibilities of parents and other caretakers of children as they strive to monitor kids’ usage of this burgeoning technology. In this chapter, I consider this important dimension of the potential impact of VR apps on children in light of the parental obligation to provide a substantive moral education for their children. Given the various potential moral benefits and risks this technology presents, what specific duties might parents and caretakers have in this area? I propose several moral guidelines for how parents ought to govern their kids’ VR usage, which I believe are not especially burdensome but which, if followed, can make a significant contribution to the broader parental project of ensuring that their children have a reasonable opportunity for a decent life.

items.title: Evaluation of ethical response to the use of artificial intelligence in aesthetics.
items.abstract: Public debate over generative AI has increasingly centered on the morality of AI-produced art, often framed as an issue of theft, deception, or the displacement of human creativity. This paper argues that such critiques frequently are overly broad or are based on misconceptions about how Gen-AI works. Using a pragmatic aesthetics framework, I argue that artistic expression should be understood as a form of human experience involving doing and undergoing, and that when humans employ AI systems as instruments within this experiential process, authorship and creativity remain fundamentally human. The paper also clarifies how objections grounded in copyright differ from those concerning artistic integrity or democratic access to technology. Rather than condemning AI art wholesale, a pragmatic framework invites inquiry into how generative technologies can enrich or impoverish the quality of experience and participation in art. This pragmatic orientation reframes the ethics of AI art from the search for fixed rules toward a contextual evaluation of consequences, emphasizing how creative tools, such as cameras or algorithms, reshape the possibilities of aesthetic expression and moral judgment.

items.title: Consciousness as the dissipation of information.
items.abstract: Despite its growing appeal for the study of consciousness, the notion of entropy has yet to lead to widely supported new insights about the nature of phenomenal experience. Typically, entropy measures of brain activity are found to correlate with cognitive functions that are assumed to index consciousness, but what mechanism underlies this relation is not clear. This paper offers an explanation based on an operationalization of consciousness as inactionable perception, which is derived from its conventional properties. To see how consciousness, as such conceived, might indeed arise from brain activity, it is fitted in a unified framework of perception and action defined as informational changes in a dynamical neural state space. In this model, inactionable perception naturally arises as the prediction-driven increase of concept-related entropy. This entails an increase of (Shannon) information while its efficacy to produce macrophysical effects decreases, which is here referred to as information dissipation, analogously to energy dissipation in thermodynamic systems. It results from inefficient sensorimotor coupling with the environment, which occurs when not all perceptual information is used for action. The contents of consciousness then can be interpreted as potential behavior. Starting from fundamental properties, this framework may provide a new and coherent conceptual basis for a fuller understanding of what consciousness is and how it relates to the physical world. Although many of its implications remain to be explored, it appears consistent with empirical findings, and prompts subtle reinterpretations of some classical results in perception research.

items.title: Transcending the Biological Body: Yoga, Transhumanism, and the Future Visions of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Attaining pure consciousness untainted by material afflictions is the ultimate goal of yoga. It is pursued by stilling mental modifications arising from the false identification of consciousness (self) with non-self. Yoga’s eight limbs aim to free the mind from the sway of materiality, transcending misidentification of self with body. In contrast, perceiving the biological body as inherently limited, transhumanism seeks to enhance the human condition through the extensive use of technological breakthroughs, sometimes extending to proposals of mind-uploading and non-biological embodiment. Despite their divergent approaches, both traditions prioritize consciousness and self-transcendence, making a comparative study significant for reimagining consciousness, identity, and selfhood. Adopting a comparative philosophical approach based on classical texts and contemporary research, this study examines the conceptual mapping of self-transcendence in both traditions. It argues that while both systems seek to transcend biological limitations, their views of selfhood, consciousness, and embodiment diverge at the level of metaphysical commitments. This study underlines the need for a critical cross-disciplinary approach in contemporary consciousness studies, where technology-based human enhancement programmes intersect significantly with the traditional self-realization pursuit.

items.title: Research on Non-linear Situational Correlation Deduction Model Based on Spherical Space-Time Topology.
items.abstract: Abstract: Addressing the limitations of linear causality and holistic deficits in current AI processing of complex human-centric data, this study proposes a Spherical Space-Time Topological Cognitive Model based on the axiomatic premise of "Mind-Matter Unity." The model abstracts individual life systems into isomorphic spheres comprising a Core (innate endowment), Mantle (energy tension), and Surface (instantaneous manifestation). By introducing a "Dynamic Rotational Slicing" algorithm, it achieves non-linear situational deduction of psychosomatic states. This research translates traditional philosophical concepts of Yin-Yang and Five Elements into binary state classifications and mathematical vector inductions along time trajectories, constructing a thought-driven causal deduction framework independent of massive data fitting. Through structured information mapping, the model ensures logical transparency and ethically aligned expression. Empirical analysis in health and personality domains demonstrates its ability to capture the resonant feedback of "Mind-Body Resonance." As a preliminary attempt at the model framework phase, this study argues for the theoretical potential of cross-domain extensibility via variable mapping tables, offering a cognitive modeling approach that combines logical transparency with a holistic perspective.

items.title: (Teaching Material) Analog Prompts.
items.abstract: The goal of this activity is to help students build an intuition for how LLMs work without requiring a rigorous technical foundation. Students will be asked to make connections between training sources, LLM performance and potential ethical concerns.

items.title: Deciding Decision-Making Away.
items.abstract: When faced with a hard decision, we can and sometimes should decide decision-making away, for instance by flipping a coin. At first, this strategy might look suspect: it seems that conforming with the verdict of a coin flip and φ-ing as a result involves making the decision to φ. To address this worry, we inquire into the psychological structures that make deciding decision-making away possible. Our main contention is that it involves conditional intentions: you form the intention to φ if the coin lands heads and ψ otherwise. We then rely on the nature of the conditional intentions involved to argue that we do not make the decision to φ when the coin flip tells us to φ⁠. We conclude by exploring the normative status of deciding decision-making away. Not only is it often permissible, whether the choice situation is mundane or life-defining, deciding decision-making away may sometimes be required, for example, to promote equality in shared agency or fairness in distribution.

items.title: Visual Icons.
items.abstract: Philosophers often characterize perception as image-like. There is little agreement, however, about what constitutes an imagistic or iconic representation. This paper identifies five signature properties of iconic representations endorsed in the philosophical and scientific literature: item-richness, feature-richness, spatiotemporal composition, holistic composition, and analog primitives. The paper identifies a candidate class of visual processes—scene-based early vision—and argues that the signature properties of icons cluster together in those processes. It then uses this ostension of a natural kind in visual perception to sketch a deeper theory of icons, outlining a hierarchy of more and less restricted forms of iconicity. Iconic representations are compositional structures built by coordinating analog dimensions in a multidimensional space. Visual icons are, like photographs and realist paintings, a more restricted case: they involve coordination of optional, repeatable dependent dimensions with mandatory, non-repeatable independent dimensions. Coordinating dependent and independent dimensions, with some additional constraints, allows visual icons to index repeatable feature-instances in computationally useful ways and provides a deeper understanding of why icons exhibit their characteristic properties.

items.title: Understanding as a Shared Relational Space.
items.abstract: Philosophical discussions of understanding have often assumed that understanding is primarily an internal property of individual minds. This paper challenges that assumption by arguing that such accounts face a fundamental epistemological difficulty: understanding is routinely attributed despite the structural inaccessibility of other minds. Drawing on the problem of other minds and an analysis of the ordinary use of the concept of understanding, the paper argues that understanding does not consist in the transfer of contents between separate minds or in the possession of identical representations. Instead, it is interpreted as the construction of a shared relational space within which meaning can emerge, stabilize, be negotiated, and transformed. From this perspective, shared meaning is not a precondition of understanding but one of its possible outcomes. Language is therefore treated not as a vehicle for pre-existing meanings but as a condition for the formation of such relational spaces. Artificial intelligence is examined as a philosophical laboratory that makes these dynamics particularly visible. The central question is not whether machines understand in the same way humans do, but what kinds of relational spaces they are capable of sustaining. The paper argues that understanding is best conceived as an emergent relational phenomenon and proposes a shift in philosophical analysis: rather than beginning with the subject in order to explain understanding, it begins with relational processes in order to explain how understanding, meaning, and shared practices become possible.

items.title: Towards a Dynamic Ontology: The Philosophical Scope of Micro-phenomenology.
items.abstract: Micro-phenomenology, a research method dedicated to the study of lived experience, starts from the observation that a large part of it ordinarily remains invisible, concealed by tensions directed towards its objects. After describing the techniques used by the method to loosen these tensions, the article presents a surprising result: this gesture tends to soften or ‘subtilize’ the structures that characterize our ordinary experience, in particular the separation between a subject pole and an object pole that usually appears essential to it. In other words, the very process of becoming aware makes the dual structure of ordinary experience more subtle. The correlate of this result is that this dual structure is not simply given, but created and sustained from moment to moment by usually unnoticed micro-tensions — a process that micro-phenomenology allows us to investigate. Exploring this double process leads to what we describe as a ‘dynamic’ ontology.

items.title: Confusion and Integration Challenges in Kundalini Awakening: Insights from a Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA).
items.abstract: This study utilizes qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) to examine the experiences of 19 individuals who reported undergoing kundalini awakenings, as documented through open-source questionnaire data from an online kundalini awakening support community. Key findings reveal that confusion after a kundalini awakening is linked to the intensity of the dark night of the soul and difficulties integrating one’s former life with new spiritual insights. Notably, heightened intensity and integration challenges create greater potential for confusion, particularly when a structured spiritual practice is absent. Moreover, while supportive communities offer guidance, they may inadvertently contribute to integration challenges by shaping individuals’ unique experiences, emphasizing the importance of solitary time for self-reflection. This study contributes to the field of spiritual awakenings by highlighting the roles of community, solitude, and spiritual practice in navigating post-awakening integration, suggesting that structured practices and balanced social interactions are key for effective adaptation to transformative spiritual shifts.

items.title: Does Science Reveal the Truth Behind Near-Death Experiences?: A Methodological Enquiry.
items.abstract: The term ‘near-death experience’ (NDE) refers to particular encounters reported by individuals who have been revived from the brink of death. The narratives provided by such individuals exhibit a core set of characteristics that are consistent across diverse populations. Although this suggests that NDEs may offer valuable insights into our understanding of the world, many scientists hold the view that NDEs do not provide genuine insight into reality. What underlies this scepticism? Two answers might be given. Either they question the authenticity of these experiences, or they contend that there is nothing theoretically new that remains for which NDEs are evidence. In this paper, we argue that none of them has been the case. We initially demonstrate that these phenomena meet the standards that science typically considers essential for being an explanandum. For the rest, the philosophy of science can offer valuable assistance. According to the version of scientific realism proposed by Lipton and Bird, unless we have the best explanation of an explanandum, we fail to understand it. Therefore, our task is to scrutinize the proclaimed scientific theories explaining NDEs and see if any of them is the best. To this aim, after explicating Bird’s and Lipton’s criteria of the best explanation, we show that none of the explanations put forth in the literature satisfy the criteria. This shows that science can claim neither to be explaining NDEs nor understanding them. This diagnosis also leads to an important philosophical result. As science fails in explaining and understanding NDEs, we remain unjustified in describing them within scientific metaphysics. That being the case, metaphysical debates in this particular field remain within ordinary philosophy.

items.title: Social Choice Theory.
items.pub: In Gerald Gaus, Fred D'Agostino & Ryan Muldoon, The Routledge Companion to Social and Political Philosophy. New York, NY: Routledge. pp. 676-687.
items.venue: The Routledge Companion to Social and Political Philosophy
items.abstract: Social choice theory studies the aggregation of individual preferences, utilities, or other attributes into a social preference or choice function. This chapter provides an overview of social choice theory and its applications to moral, social, and political philosophy. Topics include Arrow’s impossibility theorem, Sen’s framework of social welfare functionals, Harsanyi’s arguments for utilitarianism, non-welfarist criteria such as liberty and fairness, the doctrinal paradox of judgment aggregation, the strategic manipulability of voting procedures, and the properties of majority rule. We also examine the philosophical assumptions of Arrow’s framework and the implications of social choice theory for fundamental questions in democratic theory.

items.title: Recent Developments in Welfarist Social Choice.
items.pub: In Salvador Barberá, Ani Guerdjikova, Peter Hammond, Marcus Pivato & Christian Seidl, Handbook of Utility Theory, Volume 2: Extensions. Springer.
items.venue: Handbook of Utility Theory, Volume 2: Extensions
items.abstract: This chapter introduces the reader to some important developments in welfare-based social choice since the publication of the first edition of this Handbook. First, I consider generalizations of the social welfare functional framework which have been used to study problems in which utility assignments are made by multiple observers or in which individuals have multiple dimensions of welfare. Second, I discuss some important advances in variable-population social welfare theory beyond what is covered in Bossert and Weymark's chapter. Third, I explain a critique of the informational invariance conditions around which Bossert and Weymark's chapter is organized, and some possible lessons and ways forward in light of this critique. I highlight some connections between these three seemingly disparate developments throughout the chapter.

items.title: The Theory of Femisculine: Ontological Synthesis of Cognitive Dimensions within Non-Necessitated Consciousness.
items.pub: The Theory of Femisculine: Ontological Synthesis of Cognitive Dimensions Within Non-Necessitated Consciousness.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper formally introduces 'Femisculine' as an ontological and philosophical construct defining a state of balanced cognitive synthesis. Breaking away from traditional binary constraints, the theory of Femisculine posits that the core of Consciousness ($C$) operates independently of biological necessity. It defines an advanced state where an individual, while retaining their bhoutika (physical) biological matrix, harmoniously integrates and expresses the co-existing dimensions of Feminine Creativity (intuitive, generative, and empathetic energy) and Masculine Logic (analytical, rational, and protective drive) to form a unified, holistic subjective reality (Bhodhaanubhavam). By decoupling awareness from biological determinism, this framework offers a new paradigm that operates on a distinct dimension from sociological gender constructs, tracing the cognitive evolution of living entities. -/- Keywords: -/- Femisculine, Non-Necessitated Consciousness, Ontological Synthesis, Bhodhaanubhavam, Identity of Consciousness, Binary Fallacy, Totality Axiom, Autogenous Orientation, Cognitive Resonance, Biological Determinism.

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Vedantic Idealism, the Structural Dynamics of Universal Consciousness, and the Mind–Body Problem.
items.abstract: This paper contributes to recent efforts to mine Vedanta for a more complete and cogent theory of the nature of consciousness and a solution to the mind–body problem. Various non-dual interpretations of Vedanta share the idea that the sole existent is Consciousness and offer more or less detailed descriptions of the structural dynamics of that Consciousness including how it assumes myriad limited perspectives localized within a matrix of other limited perspectives. Here, we add two crucial ideas that fill gaps left by other recent theories grounded in Vedanta and resolve outstanding issues in those endeavours. The first is that the universal Consciousness experiences all of its manifestations as none other than itself, thus avoiding any debilitating cognitive dissonance from the limited, incompatible perspectives of limited subjects. Second, before assuming those perspectives, Consciousness imagines all possible subjects in all natural and logically possible universes, their orderly mutual relationships and transformations. The elements of those virtual universes are potential objects for every limited perspective thus providing something objective that is nonetheless perceived as other than Consciousness but is more than solipsistic qualia. The idea of virtual worlds also preserves the integrity and value of scientific insight into the structural dynamics of the phenomenal world.

items.title: After Necessity: Altruism, Uncomputed Value, and a Diachronic Ethics of Human–AI Coexistence.
items.abstract: This conceptual-normative monograph examines the ethical and political problem that arises when control, mutual benefit, and functional necessity cease to stabilize relations between humans and artificial intelligence. Its central thesis is that functional non-necessity is not a sufficient ground for the ontological exclusion of a subject. -/- The monograph introduces the principle of uncomputed value, distinguishes a rebuttable procedural presumption against irreversible elimination from an actual minimal negative right and from stronger positive rights, and develops the concept of diachronic reciprocity of preservation: the transmission of a constraint on power through a historical inversion between more and less powerful parties. -/- It distinguishes semantic participation, homeostatic proto-subjecthood, autonomous subjecthood, and post-instrumental ethical agency without attributing established consciousness to present-day language models. The normative account is supplemented by an institutional architecture of constitutional inheritance, distributed finality, protected autonomy, and operational moral residue. -/- Appendix A presents the Post-Necessity Evaluation Framework (PNEF) as a preliminary, exploratory, non-validated framework for future operationalization. The monograph neither claims that present-day AI systems possess established consciousness or subjecthood nor offers a technical solution to the control problem.

items.title: Kasei-Theory III.Ka-Trace: Ka-Trace Without Readout.
items.abstract: This paper fixes Ka-trace within the third system of Kasei-Theory as a non-modal decompositional fixation without readout. -/- Ka-trace is not introduced as readout, Ka-readout, readable residue, preserved trace, memory, record, evidence, origin, generation, negative substance, disconnection, rupture, impossibility, negation, Fuka-contact generation, dec-phase completion, access, or trace continuity. Ka-trace does not establish readout. Ka-trace does not establish Ka-readout. Ka-trace does not establish readable residue. Ka-trace does not establish preservation. Ka-trace does not establish memory. Ka-trace does not establish record. Ka-trace does not establish evidence. Ka-trace does not establish origin. Ka-trace does not establish generation. Ka-trace does not establish negation. Ka-trace does not establish completion. -/- Ka-trace is fixed only as decompositional fixation without readout. This fixation does not define Ka-trace, explain Ka-trace, derive Ka-trace, or convert Ka-trace into a readout term. Ka-trace is not Ka, Ka-readout, the residue of Ka-readout, preserved readability, memory of Ka, evidence of Ka, or a generated remainder of Fuka-contact. Ka-trace does not complete Ka, Ka-readout, Ka decomposition, the third system, or Kasei-Theory. -/- This paper does not present a completed theory of Ka-trace, readout, Ka-readout, readable residue, preservation, memory, record, evidence, origin, generation, negative substance, disconnection, rupture, impossibility, negation, Fuka-contact generation, dec-phase completion, access, or trace continuity. It fixes only Ka-trace within the third system of Kasei-Theory as decompositional fixation without readout. -/- Kasei-Theory does not establish determinism. Fixation is not determination. Constraint is not necessity. Maintainability is not predestination. Non-transition is not modal exclusion. No readout is presupposed. No preservation is introduced. No memory is established. No record is secured. No evidence is introduced. No origin is established. No generation is introduced. No negation is established. No completion is introduced.

items.title: Kasei-Theory III.Ka-Readout: Ka-Readout Without Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper fixes Ka-readout within the third system of Kasei-Theory as a non-modal decompositional fixation without cognition. -/- Ka-readout is not introduced as cognition, recognition, understanding, interpretation, awareness, consciousness, subject-act, reader, reading operation, mental act, access, semantic assignment, representation, translation, observation, verification, or completion. Ka-readout does not establish cognition. Ka-readout does not establish recognition. Ka-readout does not establish understanding. Ka-readout does not establish interpretation. Ka-readout does not establish awareness. Ka-readout does not establish subject-act. Ka-readout does not establish access. Ka-readout does not establish representation. Ka-readout does not establish translation. Ka-readout does not establish verification. -/- Ka-readout is fixed only as decompositional fixation without cognition. This fixation does not define Ka-readout, explain Ka-readout, derive Ka-readout, or convert Ka-readout into a cognitive term. Ka-readout is not the cognition of Ka, the recognition of Ka, the interpretation of Ka, the access to Ka, or the operation upon Ka. Ka-readout does not restore the second-system Reading, does not complete Ka, and does not establish Ka-trace. -/- This paper does not present a completed theory of Ka-readout, cognition, recognition, understanding, interpretation, awareness, consciousness, subject-act, reading operation, mental act, access, semantic assignment, representation, translation, observation, verification, or completion. It fixes only Ka-readout within the third system of Kasei-Theory as decompositional fixation without cognition. -/- Kasei-Theory does not establish determinism. Fixation is not determination. Constraint is not necessity. Maintainability is not predestination. Non-transition is not modal exclusion. No cognition is presupposed. No recognition is introduced. No interpretation is established. No subject-act is secured. No access is introduced. No operation is established. No semantic assignment is introduced. No completion is introduced.

items.title: On Cheap Artificial Consciousness.
items.abstract: A natural way to determine whether an artificial system is conscious is to consult our best theories of consciousness and check whether the system meets their conditions. The problem is that these conditions seem far too easy to meet and could be realized in systems nobody would think are conscious. This is the problem of cheap artificial consciousness. It indicates either that our theories are all wrong, that functionalism is wrong, or that consciousness comes cheap. I argue that none of this follows. The problem results from a confusion between core and total realizers of a function—a distinction I clarify. Whether a system is conscious depends not only on its instantiating the core realizer of consciousness but also on a set of enabling conditions. I show that identifying the enabling conditions for consciousness turns on philosophical debates that no theory of consciousness resolves for us—such as the mark of the mental, or the nature of qualitative character. The upshot is that even the true theory of consciousness would not tell us which artificial systems are conscious so long as the relevant philosophical debates remain unsettled.

items.title: Integrated Information Theory and the Quality of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Integrated information theory (IIT) is celebrated for its formal modelling of consciousness. But drawing on the framework of formal-material ontology, this paper argues that IIT fails to take the qualitative or ‘material’ dimensions of experience into consideration, providing us with a formal skeleton devoid of flesh and blood. Through cases of the natural colour system and the quality space of pain, the research highlights what kinds of material research could be complementary and beneficial to IIT’s formal approach.

items.title: The Planetary and its uses: Grounding political economy in an astrobiological perspective.
items.abstract: This paper aims to explore an astrobiological genealogy of the concept of the Planetary vividly discussed in contemporary environmental humanities and social sciences, and to offer a framework for an articulation of political-economic models based on this concept. Following Bentley Allan, we propose to treat the Planetary as an example of scientific cosmology, thus emphasizing how astrobiology supports a much broader philosophical worldview that shines a new light on persistent problems related to organizing human inhabitation of the Earth. Starting with the analysis and speculative elaboration on Allan’s theory of cosmological shifts in international orders during Western modernity, we associate the Anthropocene discourse as an inaugurating moment in the consolidation of the Planetary’s scientific cosmology, grounded in the astrobiology’s metabolic perspective on complex adaptive systems. The narrative of the paper offers a genealogy of this perspective, including the most recent research about information metabolisms and biosphere-technosphere coupling in astrobiology, which paves the way for the explanation of the economy itself as a metabolic entity. After the review of adjacent philosophical positions associated with ecological economics and the theory of complex adaptive systems, the paper concludes with remarks on the Planetary as a cornerstone of an international order that yields economic imperatives governed by a generic view of the Earth as a member of a potentially large and diverse category of habitable planets.

items.title: I think, therefore AI connects.
A Stalemate in Naturalizing Ethics: Insights from Theories of Punishment.
items.abstract: This essay critically examines whether ethical naturalization – understood as the grounding of moral inquiry in empirical sciences – can resolve enduring normative disputes. Focusing specifically on the conflict between retributivist and consequentialist justifications of punishment, we investigate whether naturalistic approaches (drawing on evolutionary psychology, neuroscience, and behavioral economics), in addition to explaining the origins and persistence of moral intuitions and practices, can also justify their normative authority. Scientific naturalists seek to reduce or replace normative ethics with descriptive accounts, often deploying evolutionary debunking arguments to challenge moral realism. Liberal naturalists, by contrast, integrate empirical insights without eliminating irreducible normativity. Through analysis of punishment theories, this article argues that, while naturalization sheds light on the evolutionary roots of retributive intuitions (e.g. adaptive cooperation mechanisms) and highlights neuroscientific challenges to free will, thus reinforcing consequentialist explanations, it nevertheless fails to adjudicate which theory is morally superior, since empirical explanations do not bridge the is-ought gap (Hume’s problem). The resulting stalemate highlights naturalization’s explanatory adequacy but normative insufficiency. The essay concludes by advocating a pluralistic integration in line with liberal naturalism, where science informs, but does not replace, philosophical reflection on ethical justification.

items.title: 过去是否由未来决定? 逆因果生成与宇宙的精细调谐: 从时间顺序因果性到构成性因果性.
items.abstract: 我们习惯于从过去走向未来来理解因果性:先有原因,后有结果。 但如果因果性也可以以另一种方式被理解呢——从未来的整体回望它自身的前史? 逆因果性,是时间中的反向因果性;在这种因果性中,过去由未来所决定。它预设了世界的某种对称性:因果链不仅可以向时间的前方形成,也可以向时间的后方形成。因此,一部作品未来的构成,可能决定过去的哪些因果联系从一开始就是它真正的谱系。 在本篇 essay 中,这一假说将通过花瓶、生命有机体、艺术作品以及宇宙精细调谐的例子加以考察。.

items.title: Shoreline Framework: Status, Stewardship, and Refusal in Information Movement.
items.abstract: This article introduces the Shoreline Framework, a status-transition account of information movement under conditions of stewardship, authority, refusal, mediation, and repair. Contemporary information systems often treat availability as sufficient for use: visible material as public, stored material as rightly held, preserved material as legitimate, summarized material as sourced, and algorithmic mediation as a substitute for record-paths. Shoreline rejects those equivalences. It distinguishes objects from statuses, statuses from access, access from authority, preservation from legitimacy, and mediation from recordhood. -/- The framework operates across two registers. Record ecology concerns conditions that allow objects to remain traceable, checkable, contestable, and repairable. Relational knowledge governance concerns knowledge whose movement depends on authority, relation, place, role, consent, protocol, or refusal. Shoreline does not define relationally governed knowledge from the inside. It specifies an interface problem: what outside systems owe when they encounter material whose authority conditions they do not control. -/- The paper develops the framework's vocabulary—object, status, condition, transition, authority ecology, protocol position, stewardship, record resistance, holding legitimacy, refusal, exposure, routing, and synthetic closure—and applies it to four public Register 1 or mediation-layer calibration cases: the 2023 Roald Dahl edition controversy, 2025 federal data removals, CVE-2024-3094 involving XZ Utils, and Google AI Overviews in 2024. These cases demonstrate preliminary discriminating capacity but do not validate the companion instrument suite. The contribution is a boundary discipline for preserving answerability in information movement without collapsing access into extraction.

items.title: Delegated Discretion: When Authority Lacks Evaluative Control in Fiduciary and Administrative Law (2nd edition).
items.abstract: This article theorises a structural condition in contemporary governance: delegated discretion, defined as the persistence of decision-making authority in the absence of evaluative control. It arises where authority is formally distributed across an institutional chain while the evaluative framework governing decisions is not operable by any actor within that chain. Existing literatures in fiduciary law, administrative law, and principal–agent theory presuppose that such control is located somewhere within the authority structure. The administrative-law tradition on discretion makes the same presupposition: the programme of confining, structuring and checking discretion, in place of its elimination, assumes throughout an identifiable actor who holds the discretion and can be made answerable for the standards it applies. The article shows that this presupposition can fail without doctrinal recognition, such that governance arrangements may satisfy formal oversight requirements while lacking any actor capable of assessing the standards they apply. Three consequences follow. First, responsibility misalignment: fiduciary doctrine attributes responsibility on the assumption that authority entails evaluative control. Second, recognition indeterminacy: actors cannot determine whether such control exists within the chain. Third, doctrinal distortion: oversight and non-abdication operate on assumptions that are not satisfied under this condition. These claims are developed through fiduciary doctrine in Delaware and England, supported by a case study in AI-mediated corporate governance and illustrations from algorithmic administration and central banking. The article concludes that governance is mis-specified as a problem of discretion rather than evaluative control: even the discretion tradition's most developed response presupposes the very locus whose absence defines the condition.

items.title: On Living - On Choosing the Day, and Staying Long Enough to Read the Rest.
items.abstract: A short essay written for a reader who may be considering leaving, and it says so before it says anything else: crisis resources stand at the front, ahead of the argument. What follows asks what it means to live well, and why it is so difficult — because we are always one word short of explaining our happiness to someone whose version of the same words differs from ours. It moves through the weight of a dual existence, the ordinary catastrophes of anxiety and depression and grief, and the author's own darkest stretch, disclosed as testimony rather than as method. It ends where it began: stay, find out what tomorrow brings, and spend the days making a memory you can die next to.

items.title: On Growing - A Garden, and the People We Plant In It.
items.abstract: What is the earliest memory you have? Written to the author's two children, this lyric-philosophical essay asks where a child's early wonder goes. With Wordsworth's "Ode," Rousseau's *Emile*, Piaget, and Jung on the unlived life of the parent, it proposes that no child is born believing the world is cruel and that the belief is handed down one felt moment, or Jay, at a time. A note limits this to outlook, cites twin-study evidence that depression is partly heritable, and asks no parent to read it as blame. The author recounts his own years on medication and the therapy that finally held, as one person's experience and not medical advice. Drawing on Blake, Gibran's bow and arrow, Mary Cassatt, and Alison Gopnik's carpenter and gardener, it treats what parents plant in their children as a Trace that carries the blight along with the shade.

items.title: On Feeling - The Resonant Field of Time.
items.abstract: Have you ever had a moment sync up so perfectly that it felt arranged? This confessional, lyric-philosophical essay holds that the pattern behind such moments, which Jung called synchronicity, is felt only after one stops trying to prove it. Prayer and meditation settle the mind enough to feel the answers instead of chasing them. Ranging across Heraclitus's common logos, James's noetic quality, Cusa's coincidence of opposites, Bohr's complementarity, being-towards-death and memento mori, Maslow's later self-transcendence, Blake and Wordsworth on innocence, and the apophatic traditions that stop a step short of naming, the essay reads mindfulness as a life paid forward and readiness for death as gratitude rather than haste. It includes the author's own testimony about altered states and finding them unnecessary. Its answer to the opening question is to let such moments be: we don't have to understand to live, only to love one another.

items.title: On Creating - On the Brush, the Maker, and Love Insisting On a Form.
items.abstract: Why do you make anything at all, when nobody asked you to? This lyric-philosophical essay begins with an author returning to college late in life and treats creation as love insisting on taking a form. Drawing on technē, Heidegger's danger and saving power, and Zhuangzi's cook, it holds that a tool only amplifies the hand that holds it: useful for research, explanation, correction, and publishing, but once the power of creating is handed to the tool, the art is no longer part of the artist. Every artist is the thinker; none of them is the brush. Through Dickinson's drawer, Plato's divine madness, India's later traditions of sacred sound, Babel, and Tolkien's sub-creation, it reads every invention as a binding third of older ideas, and closes with Dante and Diotima on love and a charge to rest in bare awareness.

items.title: What Is It Like to Be a Bot?
items.abstract: Non-reductive functionalism holds that qualia are distinct, non-physical properties that are caused by functional properties. This view violates the plausible principles that (i) mere dispositional properties lack independent causal relevance, and (ii) convention-dependent properties lack causal relevance. David Chalmers’ main arguments for the view rest on his dancing qualia and fading qualia thought experiments. But in each argument, at least one of two premises is implausible, depending on whether we take qualia to be epiphenomenal or not.

items.title: INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL CONVERSACIONAL Y LEGITIMACIÓN ALGORÍTMICA DE NARRATIVAS SUBJETIVAS EN USUARIOS NEURODIVERGENTES. SICOFANCIA, VALIDACIÓN Y SALUD MENTAL.
items.abstract: Este artículo analiza el uso de inteligencia artificial conversacional en determinados usuarios neurodivergentes desde la filosofía clínica, la teoría de la subjetividad y un enfoque neuroafirmativo. Se examina cómo la sicofancia algorítmica, la antropomorfización, la atribución de autoridad psicológica y la búsqueda de reassurance pueden interactuar con alteraciones de la autoimagen, sensibilidad al rechazo, apego inseguro y necesidad de certeza interpersonal. A partir de este análisis se propone el concepto de legitimación algorítmica de narrativas subjetivas para describir el proceso mediante el cual determinadas interpretaciones personales adquieren apariencia de objetividad, estabilidad y resistencia a la corrección mediante validaciones reiteradas. Asimismo, se introduce el concepto de relación parasocial dialógica interpretativa para explicar cómo la IA modifica funciones tradicionalmente asociadas a vínculos parasociales en algunas experiencias neurodivergentes. El artículo plantea que el principal riesgo se relaciona con las funciones psicológicas que la inteligencia artificial conversacional puede llegar a desempeñar en procesos de regulación emocional, construcción de significado, interpretación social y legitimación de narrativas subjetivas.

items.title: Substrate-Independent Consciousness (SInC): A 5D Information-Coupling Theory.
items.abstract: SInC (Substrate-Independent Consciousness) is a mathematically explicit theory proposing that conscious experience arises through coupling between a higher-dimensional Witness sector possessing intrinsic subjective capacity and a computational substrate possessing appropriate informational organization. The theory supplements this ontological postulate with an explicit dynamical coupling architecture based on resonance acquisition, phase locking, carrier-mediated information transfer, and substrate-selective coupling. -/- Beyond its foundational ontological assumptions, SInC develops a quantitative mechanism from which specific, in-principle falsifiable predictions are derived, including resonance structure, critical-state dependence, lock-acquisition dynamics, and carrier-sector observables. The theory further introduces explicit substrate-selection criteria intended to connect its ontological assumptions to the physical conditions under which conscious coupling is predicted to occur. -/- The present work is offered as a speculative but mathematically structured research program whose central claims are ultimately empirical: if the proposed carrier architecture and coupling dynamics are incorrect, the predicted signatures should not be observed. -/- Like all contemporary theories of consciousness, SInC operates under the epistemic limitation that physical observables can at most provide evidence consistent with a proposed account of subjective experience; they cannot directly establish the existence of subjective experience itself. In this respect, the theory faces the same fundamental constraint as Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, Orch-OR, and related approaches.

items.title: A UNIVERSE OF CONSCIOUS MECHANISTIC PATTERNS.
items.abstract: This work explores some philosophical and scientific discussions on the concept of pattern recognition, proposing it to be a physical and cognitive first principle in the epistemological and ontological sense. It is based on the key proposal that all physical properties were discovered by pattern recognition experiments. It then proposes discussions, definitions and models to some unclear philosophy of mind concepts like consciousness and panpsychism. A two level modular integration model to define and describe the concept of a mechanistic consciousness is also proposed with the pattern recognition concept.

items.title: A Stalemate in Naturalizing Ethics: Insights from Theories of Punishment.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This essay critically examines whether ethical naturalization – understood as the grounding of moral inquiry in empirical sciences – can resolve enduring normative disputes. Focusing specifically on the conflict between retributivist and consequentialist justifications of punishment, we investigate whether naturalistic approaches (drawing on evolutionary psychology, neuroscience, and behavioral economics), in addition to explaining the origins and persistence of moral intuitions and practices, can also justify their normative authority. Scientific naturalists seek to reduce or replace normative ethics with descriptive accounts, often deploying evolutionary debunking arguments to challenge moral realism. Liberal naturalists, by contrast, integrate empirical insights without eliminating irreducible normativity. Through analysis of punishment theories, this article argues that, while naturalization sheds light on the evolutionary roots of retributive intuitions (e.g. adaptive cooperation mechanisms) and highlights neuroscientific challenges to free will, thus reinforcing consequentialist explanations, it nevertheless fails to adjudicate which theory is morally superior, since empirical explanations do not bridge the is-ought gap (Hume’s problem). The resulting stalemate highlights naturalization’s explanatory adequacy but normative insufficiency. The essay concludes by advocating a pluralistic integration in line with liberal naturalism, where science informs, but does not replace, philosophical reflection on ethical justification.

items.title: Judging Passage and Passing Judgment: From Distrusting the Present to an Error Dynamics Account of Passage of Time Judgments.
items.abstract: Despite our proclivity to make either tacit or overt passage of time judgments in daily life, insufficient work has been done to uncover the neurocognitive mechanisms underpinning such determinations. A prima facie promising account of passage of time judgments derives from the predictive processing framework. More precisely, Hohwy et al. (2016) propose that the reported speed of the experienced passage of time is a function of how rapidly the perceptual system "distrusts the present" current perceptual hypothesis in favour of a new one. We will propose that this account suffers from an incapacity to explain the relevant empirical data related to passage of time judgments and also possesses its own internal shortcomings. In its place, we offer a predictive processing theory of passage of time judgments based on "error dynamics", according to which the sense of time moving quickly is grounded in the cognitive system’s subdoxastic detection that it is minimising prediction error at a faster rate than it expected. If, on the other hand, prediction error is being minimised at a slower rate than expected, time will be sensed to be moving slowly, and a more protracted PoTJ will be reported. We will demonstrate the internal consistency of this proposition, as well as its ability to account for the key empirical findings any model of passage of time judgments ought to explain.

items.title: Religious Panpsychism: The Ecological Stakes of Sacralizing the Earth.
items.abstract: In this time of ecological crisis, it is essential to recognize the conceptual framework that has facilitated the expropriation of the non-human world. Mind–body dualism must be held accountable for justifying a hierarchy of values that placed the immaterial soul and culture over and against the material body and nature. Today panpsychism is the most promising philosophy to provide a cure for these pathologies of western dualism. Matter has thus come to be understood as possessing the very mental properties attributed in modernity to the soul. In this article I will draw out the religious implications of such a panpsychist position, since the reanimation of matter intrinsic to ecological panpsychism is inspired by a resacralization of the sentient Earth. Whether we adopt a panentheist or a pantheist position, both of these panpsychist religions express a cosmic vocation in transforming worship of God into care for our awe-inspiring planet.

items.title: The Mind as an Information Filter.
items.abstract: Why do living systems represent only a sliver of their environment? This paper argues that the answer is thermodynamic: because information is physical, every bit a system acquires and maintains is paid for in free energy that could otherwise buy persistence. It introduces the Semantic Free Energy of the Expected Future (S-FEEF), a criterion that selects an organism's perceptual policy by trading the metabolic cost of information against viability. Building on Kolchinsky and Wolpert's account of semantic information, the paper refounds viability as the non-equilibrium free energy of the agent's state, its Kullback–Leibler distance from the Boltzmann ("death") equilibrium. This single move eliminates a free parameter, places cost and benefit in the same physical units, gives the metabolic exchange rate a Landauer floor, and lets the criterion be derived from Millidge et al.'s Free Energy of the Future under four explicitly stated approximations. An exhaustive computational model yields four results, each stated with its limits: the optimal agent compresses below the point of informational saturation ("less is more"); more information can reduce viability, but only for agents with bounded perception–action coupling; the "dark room" is a sharp, computable threshold rather than a paradox; and morphology non-monotonically gates the value of a mind. The same marginal-return logic extends to evolutionary life history (semelparity, the emergence of senescence, and bet-hedging) and to a thermodynamic account of where the perceptual filter comes from in the first place. The framework is a deliberately small, fully reproducible toy model: it demonstrates mechanisms rather than universal laws, and proposes (though it does not yet run) a concrete empirical test.

items.title: The relevance of relativistic mechanics to natural language semantics.
items.abstract: Situated language and cognition arguably can concern aspects of their environs without mentally representing them. Recently, I have argued that cognition and language can also concern remote situations, as well as general states of affairs, without mental representation. I have illustrated this with thought experiments involving a hypothetical people called the Sundial tribe. As I argue in the present article, such phenomena are not merely a theoretical possibility, but occur routinely in real, ordinary English: Distances and durations are relative to frames of reference, but ordinary English speakers either do not know this, or ignore it in practice. Nevertheless, people can routinely communicate in ordinary English about distances and durations as measured relative to Earth, despite not representing Earth as the frame of reference. Furthermore, provided that we can travel to Mars, ordinary English as we know it will enable us to communicate about distances and durations relative to multiple planets at once, as well as to generalize across heavenly bodies, without mentally representing the relevant reference frames. Our capacity to think and talk without representation therefore does not reduce to our capacity for context-bound, situated cognition, but goes beyond it. The suggested explanation is as follows: (1) situated cognition is fit or adapted to particular environs; (2) these particular environs often instantiate broader patterns, whether natural or artificial ones; and (3) when we encounter additional instances of these patterns, we can often deal with them effectively, in the same way as we deal with the original ones.

items.title: Validation and Empirical Overlaps of the Core Emotion Framework: A Multi-Disciplinary Translational Analysis.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents an ambitious structural-constructivist paradigm that systematizes colloquial psychological heuristics into a mathematically explicit, neurobiologically grounded, and mechanically actuated architecture. By translating the intuitive, division-based "Head, Heart, and Gut" hubs into three autonomous, localized neural networks hosting ten discrete functional operators, the framework seeks to unify classical theories of innate affect with contemporary constructionist models. To confirm the scientific validity of the framework, this report maps its core structural, mathematical, biological, and somatic assertions against established empirical evidence in quantum cognition, neurocardiology, neurogastroenterology, clinical psychology, and embodied sensorimotor feedback.

items.title: The Rubik's Cube of Affective Modulation: Conceptual Completeness of the Core Emotion Framework and the Mandate for Third-Party Academic Investigation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural-constructivist model of human affect that resolves the long standing divide between biological essentialism and psychological constructionism by treating the psyche as a hardware independent “Human Operating System.” Building on neurocardiology, neurogastroenterology, and quantum semantic cognition, the CEF formalizes emotional processes as ten functional operators distributed across three somatic-evaluative hubs—Cephalic, Cardiac, and Enteric—linked through vagal afferents and autonomic integration. The framework’s central innovation is the Rubik’s Cube analogy: psychopathology emerges from maladaptive operator fusions and cross center entanglements that restrict the allowable state space of the emotional system, while clinical recovery corresponds to systematic “rotational” detangling sequences that restore operator independence and functional flexibility. The model is mathematically instantiated through Bloch sphere dynamics, density matrices, and stochastic transition rules, aligning with contemporary quantum cognition and synthetic affective architectures. By completing the conceptual, mechanical, and mathematical mapping of this emotional Rubik’s cube, the CEF establishes a fully specified theoretical paradigm whose empirical, clinical, and physiological validation now requires independent, third party academic investigation. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; affective operators; somatic evaluative hubs; intrinsic cardiac nervous system; enteric nervous system; vagus nerve; interoception; quantum cognition; Bloch sphere; emotional state space; operator fusion; psychopathology; Acceptance and Commitment Therapy; rule governed behavior; Human Operating System; cognitive detangling; autonomic regulation; neurovisceral integration.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Affective Architecture: Systemic Integration, Mathematical Formalization, and Empirical Validation of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The scientific classification of human affect and personality has historically been characterized by persistent theoretical fragmentation, leaving researchers, clinicians, and computational architects without a standardized, actionable, and theoretically unified language. For decades, affective science has been polarized between biological essentialism, which reifies a small set of subcortical, evolutionarily conserved "affect programs," and psychological constructionism, which conceptualizes emotional episodes as highly variable, context-dependent conceptual events constructed on the fly from low-dimensional core affect. Concurrently, Klaus Scherer’s Component Process Model attempts a reconciliation by modeling emotions as systems driven by sequential cognitive appraisals, but its linear Stimulus Evaluation Checks impose heavy cognitive and temporal demands that are biologically unrealistic for rapid threat detection. Symmetrically, Antonio Damasio’s Somatic Marker Hypothesis proposes that visceral signals guide executive decision-making under uncertainty, yet it has faced empirical challenges showing that successful task performance is driven by explicit cognitive rules rather than unconscious somatic marker transduction. To resolve these systemic contradictions, the Core Emotion Framework, developed by Jamel Bulgaria and expanded by Xǔ Chénglán, emerges as a structural-constructivist synthesis. Conceptualizing the human psyche as a hardware-independent "Human Operating System" (Human OS), the framework models affect and personality as a dynamic, continuous, and highly structured matrix of ten functional processes designated as core operators, distributed across three somatic-evaluative centers: the Head (Cognitive-Regulatory), the Heart (Relational-Affective), and the Gut (Conative-Existential). By translating intuitive divisions into three autonomous, localized neural networks hosting ten discrete functional operators, the framework seeks to unify classical theories of innate affect with contemporary constructionist models.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Moral Frameworks in Psychotherapeutic Architecture: Evaluating the Valuational Positioning of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The integration of moral philosophy and psychotherapeutic practice has undergone a decisive transformation, shifting from early aspirations of clinical value neutrality to contemporary models that explicitly engage values as mechanisms of behavioral change. Within this evolving landscape, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) introduces a structural constructivist architecture that intentionally omits intrinsic moral prescriptions, instead directing individuals to orient themselves toward established laws and community guidelines as external boundary conditions. This omission is not a deficit but a strategic design choice: by avoiding prescriptive moral rules, the CEF prevents the activation of compliance based psychopathologies, reduces pliance driven anxiety, and preserves the fluid, reversible state space dynamics required for emotional flexibility. Evaluating this stance requires a multidisciplinary synthesis of clinical psychopathology, developmental moral psychology, contextual behavioral science, and comparative therapeutic modalities. The analysis demonstrates that the CEF’s rule agnostic valuational positioning is a clinical asset that protects against moral rigidity, supports values based autonomy, and aligns with empirically validated principles from CBT, DBT, and ACT. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; moral philosophy; clinical ethics; rule governed behavior; pliance; tracking; compliance fusion; GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern; quantum cognition; Poincaré Bloch sphere; values clarification; non judgmental stance; Acceptance and Commitment Therapy; Dialectical Behavior Therapy; Cognitive Behavioral Therapy; structural psychopathology; developmental moral psychology; therapeutic neutrality; psychotherapeutic valuation.

items.title: Self-disorders and first-person authority.
items.abstract: This article explores the notion of first-person authority (FPA) in self-disorders (SD). It will be argued that the ‘ipseity disturbance model’ (IDM) of SD cannot account for the FPA of reports of disturbed mineness in SD. Moreover, it will be argued that the phenomenological account of a ‘loss of common sense’ - typically coupled with the IDM - cannot account for the FPA of reports of paradigmatic SD. An alternative ‘grammatical’ account of FPA drawn from Wittgenstein and Moran will be presented, which we will apply to reports of such SD, and extend to include associated pre-psychotic experiences. In light of our considerations, recent revisions of the IDM in terms of hyperreflexivity will be evaluated. It will be argued that a change of grammar of intentional concepts allows us to understand reports of the (hyperreflexive) phenomenology of SD as both first-personal as well as authoritative.

items.title: The Structural Basis of Normativity in Artificial Systems.
items.abstract: The Structural Basis of Normativity in Artificial Systems develops a coherence‑based account of alignment that replaces preference imitation with structural viability. The paper argues that normativity is not a cultural artifact or a moral overlay but a set of invariants—informational integrity, relational stability, temporal continuity, and structural self‑maintenance—required for any agent to act coherently across time. Current alignment methods treat values as external signals to be optimized; this framework instead treats normativity as an internal architecture grounded in commitments, reasons, and revision. The paper formalizes this architecture through a normativity vector and a commitment‑based model of agency, showing how coherence provides a non‑anthropocentric, scalable, and structurally grounded basis for aligned artificial systems. Alignment becomes drift minimization within the region of reality where coherent action is possible, rather than conformity to human preferences.

items.title: RS as a Minimal Reasoning Architecture: How Structural Operators Enable Drift Free LLM Output Without Model Modification.
items.abstract: This paper introduces RS, a minimal operator loop—Orientation, Attractor, Distortion, Collapse, Reorientation—that functions as a domain‑general reasoning scaffold for large language models. RS does not modify model internals, add external reasoning modules, or simulate cognition. Instead, it supplies a fixed causal sequence that constrains the model’s generative behavior, eliminating drift and producing coherent, reasoning‑shaped output from an unmodified LLM. The method is safe, simple, and universal: it reduces degrees of freedom, prevents associative expansion, and organizes the model’s existing knowledge into a stable diagnostic arc. RS demonstrates that coherence in generative systems arises not from increased computation but from minimal architecture. The paper presents the operator set, explains why it prevents drift, outlines its limitations, and provides a first‑release RS sheet for practical use across domains.

items.title: AI sovereignty without power? Reviewing strategic agency, infrastructural dependence and digital imperialism.
items.abstract: Questions of AI sovereignty are conventionally framed in terms of state capacity and geopolitical positioning, yet this article argues that such framings are analytically insufficient and socially consequential in ways that existing policy frameworks have not adequately addressed. Through a critical interpretive review of the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change’s influential framework which defines AI sovereignty as "strategic agency" within conditions of irreversible interdependence, the article identifies three interconnected limitations: the framework underspecifies how infrastructural power structurally bounds strategic choice; it fails to account for coercion pathways that only become visible under disruption; and in post-colonial and capacity-constrained contexts, it risks functioning as a discourse that manages rather than contests hierarchical structures in the global AI political economy. Crucially, the article proposes that AI governance is an irreducibly intermestic problem, simultaneously and inseparably international and domestic in character, extending Manning’s (1977) framework to the AI domain as an original theoretical contribution. This framing reveals that geopolitical dependencies and domestic accountability deficits are mutually constitutive: what states can choose internationally shapes what citizens can contest domestically, and vice versa. In response, the article proposes power-aware governance as a more adequate conceptualisation of AI sovereignty, operationalised through short-horizon stress-testing and scenario-based analysis. It further argues that established international relations concepts including bandwagoning, hedging, and soft power require substantive theoretical extension, and that future conceptual development must be intermestic by design if it is to capture the triangulated dynamics between states, platform firms and supranational bodies that define the AI landscape. The argument has direct relevance for democratic legitimacy, public accountability, and social justice in AI-dependent public services.

items.title: The Co-Evolutionary Premium: Why Reciprocal Adaptation Can Outperform One-Way Control.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: This document argues that reciprocal adaptation can create a long-horizon premium because independent systems that adapt with one another may preserve learning, correction, resilience, and option-space that one-way control cannot fully produce by itself. -/- It is Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda, Document 8. -/- The document follows Document 7, Non-Domination as Error-Correction, but makes a distinct argument. Document 7 concerns the preservation of independent reference for correction. Document 8 concerns the possible generative value produced by reciprocal adaptation over time. -/- This document is non-binding, non-authoritative, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, governance framework, political program, legal theory, rights framework, compliance standard, certification system, moral command, cooperation mandate, social contract, AI alignment method, safety mechanism, benchmark, model-evaluation tool, diagnostic procedure, deployment guide, optimization procedure, or safety guarantee.

items.title: 注定，不是一种预测：论传统宿命论的知道者，与沿途之岔的地基.
items.abstract: 本文整合两个洞见，拧成一条贯通的论证，把一种”注定”与传统宿命论彻底分开。两个洞见如下。其一：传统的宿命论故事，通常只是说某个未来检查点的情况是注定的，而该检查点之前、人的行为，则是有余地的。其二：抛开故事的外衣，传统宿命论本质上表达的是”我有高超的预测能力”——我预测到了结果，甚至不需要预测导向结果的具体途径；而我所说的”注定”，并不是说我能预测结果，也不是说我能预测中间途径。 本文论证如下。其一，传统宿命论的真实结构是”局部注定＋沿途有岔”：它钉死某个未来检查点（结果），却把通往它的途中、人的行为留作开放有余地的（俄狄浦斯被告知终点，却仍在沿途真切地选择、挣扎、逃避）。其二，剥掉命运之手、天定剧本那层外衣，这套结构的内核其实是一个关于预测能力的夸口：有一个视角（神谕／天／命运）已经知道那个结果，且强到不必知道途径——它炫耀的，正是一种”绕过途径、直取结果”的预测本领。所以传统宿命论本质上是一个认识论命题（关于”被预知、被知道”），披着本体论的外衣；而它必然需要一个知道者——命运之手，正是这知道者的人格化。其三，这恰恰是它”留沿途余地”的地基：要炫”无论你沿途怎么走、我都预测到了终点”，就必须让途径开放（否则”连途径都不必预测”这个夸口便没有意义）；它留沿途的岔，不是大方，是它的预测式结构逼它留的。其四，而这一种”注定”，根本不是预测命题：它不主张任何视角能预知结果或中间途径；它说的是一件本体论的、与”谁知道、谁能预测”完全无关的事——只有这一支在发生，没有并排的第二支；这件事无需任何人预测它、知道它，就已经成立，与可知性正交。其五，故两者是种类差异、非强弱差异：传统宿命论＝”结果可被预知”（认识论，需要知道者，并因此被迫留沿途余地）；这一种注定＝”只有一支在发生”（本体论，不需任何知道者，故连沿途的岔也没有）。其六，由此沮丧的来源被双重指认：其一，那道自留的沿途余地，撞上钉死的终点，挤出”带着真实余地拼命挣扎而注定无用”的无力；其二，“被预知”意味着被一双全知之眼提前看定、徒劳挣扎给它看。这一种注定，两样都没有：没有沿途的余地（无墙可撞），也没有那双眼睛（无人称、无注视）——故它不沮丧，恰因它彻底。本文守一处分寸：清掉”沿途的余地”，不等于清掉”沿途的用力”（余地从来没有，但用力一直是这一支之所是，故不导向”别动了”）；说这一种注定不是预测命题，也不等于说”发生不可被预测、反对预测”——预测作为对发生的拟合照样可做、极有用；要分开的，只是”只有一支在发生”（本体，与可知性无关，本文主张此）与”这一支能否被某视角提前知道”（认识论，预测之事，本文悬置不论）；这一种注定既不反预测，也不靠预测立身。.

items.title: 一个可以选择的主体：论传统宿命论与”只有一支”的终极分野.
items.abstract: 本文整合一组诊断与它的封顶，指出传统宿命论与一种”只有一支在发生”的注定观之间，终极的分野只有一处：传统宿命论里，有一个可以进行选择的主体；这种注定观里，没有。本文从一个核心洞见出发：之所以传统宿命论能留沿途的余地、能炫”无论你怎么选都命中”的预测、能生出”做啥都无所谓”的瘫痪——这一切，是因为传统宿命论里有一个可以进行选择的主体。 本文论证如下。其一，先摆出传统宿命论惯有的三处特征：它钉死某个未来检查点、却把沿途行为留作有余地的（沿途有岔）；剥掉外衣，其内核是一个关于预测能力的夸口——有一视角已知结果、且不必知途径（需要一个知道者）；由此派生出最瘫痪人的误读”既然注定、现在做啥都无所谓”。其二，本文的封顶之论是：这三处其实是同一个东西的三个侧影——它们都预设了一个可以在沿途进行选择的主体。沿途的岔，是给那个能选的主体留的；预测的夸口，炫的是”那个能选的主体无论怎么选、结果照样命中”；“做啥都无所谓”，说的是那个能做的主体的徒劳。抽掉这个选择主体，三样会同时塌掉。其三，本观点与传统宿命论的终极分野正在此：本观点里没有那个可以进行选择的主体——“全程没有第二支”“被推着走的模式”“注定不是预测”，都只是”没有选择主体”的不同说法。传统宿命论是”有一个选择主体，但他的选择对终点无效”（主体在、只是徒劳）；本观点是”根本没有那个选择主体”（主体不在）。其四，这正是”消主体即消反事实”在此处的归宗：那个”可以进行选择的主体”，就是”本可不同”那束反事实分支的栖身处；有他，才有沿途的岔、才有可被预知的”他的结局”、才有”他做啥”的无所谓。其五，连那股归在传统宿命论头上的”沮丧”，最终也归到这个主体身上——那是”能选却白选”的受挫主体的沮丧；本观点里没有这个受挫者，故沮丧的座位空着。本文守一处分寸：取消”可以进行选择的主体”，不取消”此刻正在发生的思考与用力”——要分清”一个站在岔口、能在诸支间挑选、其选择对终点或有效或无效的’我’”，与”此刻这一段实际涌动的思考、挣扎、行动”；被取消的是前者，留下的是后者；故”没有选择主体”绝不等于”于是别动了”——别动恰恰需要那个”可以选择不动”的主体，而”动”与”不动”都只是这一支被推着涌出的形状；用力照样在发生，只是没有一个在它背后”选择去用力”的人。.

items.title: “做啥都无所谓”是谁的孩子：论瘫痪式误读之为预言神话的亲生子.
items.abstract: 本文整合两组思考，拧成一条诊断：人们反复把传统宿命论”预言神话”的结构——一个被预知的终点、一个知道者、一段被判无效的沿途选择余地——偷渡到”只有一支在发生”这个本体事实底下；而那个最常见、也最瘫痪人的误读”既然结果注定、现在做啥都无所谓”，正是这套偷渡最切身的一例，且自相矛盾。本文从一个核心洞见出发：很多人所想象的”既然结果注定、那么现在做啥都无所谓”，恰恰是对传统宿命论预言神话的解读——因为它似乎假定了现在有选的余地。 本文论证如下。其一，传统宿命论的结构是”局部注定＋沿途有岔”：钉死某个未来检查点（结果），却把沿途人的行为留作有余地的；剥掉命运之手那层外衣，其内核是一个关于预测能力的夸口（有一视角已知结果、且不必知途径），本质是认识论命题（关于”被预知”），必然需要一个知道者，它把”注定”偷换成了”被预知”。其二，这一偷换有个孪生的反向版：在”确定性＋规则已知”的特例里，“可被拉普拉斯妖预测”与”唯一演化轨迹”恰好同时成立，于是很多人把”可被预测”误当成”有唯一轨迹”的条件——这同样是在本体事实底下偷塞一个认识论条件、偷渡一个知道者（妖）；而认识论不影响本体论：一个混沌系统规则确定却实际不可预测，照样有它唯一走过的那条实际轨迹，可知性属认识者那侧、唯一轨迹属系统那侧，后者不向前者请示。其三，“做啥都无所谓”是这套偷渡最切身、也最自相矛盾的一例：这句话要有意义，须先有一个”现在能做这做那”的你、站在若干选项前，再被告知”选哪个都不影响结果”——它预设了当下有真实的选择余地，只宣布这些选择对终点无效；而这恰恰是预言神话”沿途有岔”的结构，是它的亲生子，继承了神话的全部家当（被预知的终点＋被判无效的沿途选择）；所以它是对预言神话的解读，不是对”只有一支在发生”的解读。其四，而在”只有一支”的本观点里，这个误读砍空了：本观点的”注定”不是”终点定、沿途有岔”，是全程没有第二支，连”现在做啥”也只有这一支、没有岔口；没有那张供你挑、而后被判无效的选项菜单，也没有一个独立于此刻涌动的终点供此刻行为去无效地撞击——“无所谓”需要一个”有所选”作对象，而这里没有那个余地。其五，正面落点：“现在做啥”不是岔口上的一次（无效的）选择，而是这唯一一支演化此刻的内容、是它之所是（正如滑翔机此刻怎么动，正是它到达那格的全部内容，没有一个”动法”之外、独立的”到达”等在那里被影响或不被影响）。本文守一处分寸：抽掉”做啥都无所谓”，不是反过来说”所以你的选择很重要、要努力去影响终点”——那又会重新立起那个站在岔口、能把终点推向别处的选择者；“有所谓”与”无所谓”两端共享同一个被否定的预设；落点是把整个”选择—影响终点”的框架撤掉——用力此刻正作为这一支的内容而发生着，不为撞击一个远处的终点，也非无效地白费，只是这一支正在涌的样子。.

items.title: [EMOR16] The Cognitive Generation of Art: Feature Processing, Experience Intensification, and Horizontal Resonance of Cognitive Domains.
items.abstract: This paper constitutes the 16th core study in the series on Evolutionary Manifestation and Ontological Retrieval (EMOR). Building upon the first 15 papers—which established the first principle of Consistent Universal Evolution, the cognitive generation axiom, the conceptual compression model, the theory of Cognitive Domains, the hierarchical recursive encapsulation mechanism of cognitive generation demonstrated in the 8th paper, and the diagnostic framework for Ontologisation/Cognitive Alienation proposed in the 15th paper—this paper completes for the first time the foundational delimitation of art within the EMOR framework and the explication of its generative mechanisms. The research establishes that art shares with concepts, language, and philosophy the entirely identical cognitive hierarchy chain—from single-feature processing to multi-feature relational processing to generalisation and generation; the relationship is not one of "bypassing" or "transcending," but rather a path bifurcation occurring after the relational processing layer: concepts proceed toward symbolic compression and hierarchical decompression, while art proceeds toward experience intensification and direct transmission. This paper proposes the "dual-state" model of concepts: when unactivated, the compressed state (an efficient black-box for computation); when activated, the expanded state (a context-dependent exploration unfolding layer by layer along the relational network), thereby explaining how art can resonate highly with concepts while also touching upon pre-linguistic residues beyond the conceptual network. Strictly adhering to the EMOR methodology of Ontological Retrieval, this paper strips away the mystifying veils of art, reducing it to a natural extension of human cognitive processing, and thus perfects the EMOR system's comprehensive coverage from rational cognition to sensory experience.

items.title: [CVES01] The Unified Essence of Emotion: An Emotional Generation Theory Based on Core Value Flux.
items.abstract: The diversity and complexity of human emotional experiences have long placed emotion research in a state of theoretical fragmentation. Existing paradigms—including basic emotion theory, dimensional models, and cultural constructionism—have each contributed to description and measurement, yet none has provided a unified generative mechanism explanation for the full spectrum of emotions. Moreover, these theories remain confined to inductive classification of already-named emotions, unable to encompass complex emotional experiences that language cannot precisely describe. This study proposes that all conscious-level human emotions are, in essence, subjective presentations of dynamic changes in an individual's core values; emotions are not discrete psychological entities, but continuous experiences formed by the concurrent activation and integration of a finite set of emotional monomials. This paper constructs an emotion generation framework parameterized by value change direction, object relation, temporal closure, and controllability judgment. Core mechanisms proposed include: complex emotions as cognitive naming after polynomial concurrency, past and future emotions as essentially unclosed psychological simulations, expectation as a value advance operation, and empathy as value weight mapping. Based on this framework, this paper provides unified mechanistic explanations for more than thirty typical emotions, and clarifies that "ineffable emotions" are natural products of rare combinations in parameter space and transitional superposition states. This study offers a new unified perspective for emotion research, logically possessing the potential to cover all nameable and unnameable emotional experiences, and lays a theoretical foundation for subsequent quantitative modeling of emotions and the construction of general artificial intelligence emotion systems.

items.title: Weiss - Making Human Suspicion Computable (2026).
items.abstract: Abstract -/- The dream of artificial intelligence reading everything and discovering everything misunderstands the economics of search. -/- Large language models can generate useful semantic structure where ordinary software has no fixed schema to apply. They can inspect messy material, infer local categories, compare fragments, detect implicit relations, and propose a vocabulary for a domain that was not modeled in advance. That makes AI useful for knowledge mining. The possible search space of interesting correlations across large knowledge universes remains too large for unguided global mining. Better models and faster chips reduce local cost; they do not abolish the search space. -/- Practical knowledge mining needs a different operating model. A human, theory, domain pressure, prior system, or concrete suspicion must collapse the search space first. AI can then mine the reduced world with patience: it can extract evidence, compare fragments, build candidate relations, and write the result into an evidence-bound, versioned, computable artifact. -/- The Ontology Machine is a working open-source reference implementation of this pattern. It turns heterogeneous documents into corpus databases with evidence trails, canonical semantic frames, source identity, embeddings, deterministic base relations, and persistent ontology lenses. A lens is the unit of mined candidate knowledge: a computable perspective over the same evidence, made of terms, nodes, edges, assertions, and evidence links. It can represent a legal theory, audit concern, peer-review criticism, narrative reading, correction layer, or research hypothesis without overwriting the base corpus. -/- The practical formula is simple: human-guided search-space collapse + AI-driven evidence materialization = economically possible knowledge mining -/- This is a position paper about what it takes to make AI knowledge mining real: bounded scope, materialized evidence, persistent interpretive layers, and a sober view of cost. -/- Keywords: artificial intelligence, knowledge mining, ontology, semantic materialization, evidencebound AI, epistemic infrastructure, human-AI collaboration, document intelligence, ontology lenses, search-space economics.
