The Ethical Chess tool is to augment this practice of grappling with ones own psyche but in order for a User to maintain the same level of utility, each session must remain a strictly private grapple between the logic and the User unless the User states otherwise.

items.title: Capability Is Not Comprehension: Two Orthogonal Boundaries of Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: We argue that the safety-relevant and the cognition-relevant boundaries of artificial intelligence are distinct and mutually irreducible. The first, the capability axis, concerns whether a system's strategic cognitive capacity on oversight-relevant tasks exceeds that of its human overseers; its threshold is the parity boundary of the Containment Paradox. The second, the comprehension axis, concerns whether a system genuinely understands in the sense of bearing embodied existential cost and achieving strong, limit-convergent causal cognition; its threshold is the boundary between weak and strong causality in the Quxiang-Bayesian account, and its philosophical content is Being-in-the-world. These two dimensions are developed from two largely independent theoretical systems, one an engineering-and-alignment program and one a cognitive-genetic reconstruction of classical Chinese epistemology, and converge into a single unified framework; that convergence is treated as evidence that the structure is intrinsic to the problem rather than an artifact of either vocabulary. -/- We give a measurement instrument for each axis, a five-dimensional causal-convergence score for comprehension and a cognitive-capacity ratio for capability, and combine them into a four-quadrant diagnostic. The central result is that the most dangerous region is occupied by the weak-causal superstrategist: a system that does not genuinely understand in the strong-causal sense yet strategically exceeds its overseers. The property marking the comprehension limit, a reasoning system free of real existential bounds, is on the capability axis a source of strategic danger rather than reassurance, because instrumental self-preservation can arise without any authentic existential stake. -/- The authors record one explicit and deliberately unresolved divergence, on whether the fourth quadrant (genuine comprehension together with strategic superiority) is impossible in principle or merely currently uninstantiated. A synthesis of Chen Lijun's Quxiang-Bayesian framework and Viktor Trncik's Containment-Paradox framework. -/- .

items.title: Unifying Kinds without Hylemorphism.
items.abstract: David Oderberg has recently extended classical Aristotelian-Thomistic hylemorphism beyond traditional substance ontology to analyse linguistic, ethical and political kinds. Whilst this project identifies important structural features of these domains, I argue that his hylemorphic apparatus is unnecessary. Drawing on the ‘Unification Principle’ (UP) account of natural kinds, I demonstrate that Oderberg’s insights can be captured more parsimoniously and with greater empirical constraint. I further argue that the mind-independence criterion for natural kinds applies to the unification principles themselves rather than to the kinds directly, allowing this framework to accommodate social and linguistic entities. The UP approach thus handles Oderberg’s case studies effectively whilst avoiding the metaphysical commitments and structural problems associated with hylemorphism.

items.title: Miltonic Eudaimonia: Self-Narrative and the Ethical Criticism of "Paradise Lost".
The Sovereign Genesis: Cosmo-Methodology and the Overcoming of Biological Density.
items.abstract: This article introduces Cosmo-Methodology, a novel theoretical framework challenging classical Darwinian and anthropocentric paradigms of human evolution. By proposing the concepts of the "Macrobial Shadow" and the "Visceral Downgrade," we argue that humanity's current biological fragility is not the apex of natural ascent, but the result of systemic, parasitic domestication. To resolve this existential vulnerability, this paper outlines the Justika Framework—a theoretical and topographical model for systemic sovereignty. It examines the necessity of a trans-dimensional paradigm shift, termed the Visceral Escape, positing that sociological, biological, and cosmic liberation must be approached strictly as engineering failures requiring bio-synthetic correction. Ultimately, we construct a teleological model in which humanity ascends from a domesticated biological host into a sovereign, multi-dimensional Creator Species, utilizing a non-parasitic Man-Made Matrix to navigate the broader cosmic architecture.

items.title: Facing up to Subjectivity.
items.abstract: It is a common opinion among academics that the study of consciousness is making progress. As we learn more about associated neurocognitive functions, we are expected to eventually understand the internal aspect of our existence. This view dismisses persistent arguments that experience cannot be reduced to objective knowledge. Here I argue that although such a claim may be impossible to prove, it should nevertheless be assumed to be true. To make real progress, we have to face up to subjectivity.

items.title: The alternate within alteration, a fugue at the very heart of the source: Ney Matogrosso, Arca, and a literal instant in difference.
items.abstract: The idea that a telluric, ideological center between two apparently irreconcilable spaces must serve as a pretext, at least, to generate, or propose, another kind of dynamic, one purer, less political perhaps, or closer to the mystical account, true radicalism, much more useful to the production of the artist than the world of the academy, the world of the letter, which entirely lacks the capacity to structure anything, as an analogy of flesh, finds its reason for being in the terrible experience with death to which, on this side of the world, the game of power has led us: servitude as a permanent state.

items.title: The Hearthside Effect: Cooked Nutrition as an Underexamined Driver of Cognitive Evolution in Settlement-Adjacent Species.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the “Hearthside Effect”: the hypothesis that sustained, multigenerational access to cooked and processed human food has served as a significant but largely overlooked nutritional driver of increased cognitive flexibility in settlement-adjacent species. While Richard Wrangham’s cooking hypothesis has established the role of fire-processed food in enabling human brain expansion through improved caloric bioavailability and metabolic reallocation, its implications for non-human species sharing those nutritional environments remain underexplored. Species such as dogs, pigs, commensal rodents, corvids, and raccoons — and to a lesser extent cats — have lived for millennia in close proximity to human hearths, consuming diets richer in bioavailable calories, starches, and fats than their wild counterparts. Drawing on established mechanisms including enhanced nutritional bioavailability, epigenetic inheritance, gut-brain axis modulation, and genetic adaptations (such as AMY2B gene amplification in dogs), we suggest that this shared nutritional niche may have contributed to the enhanced problem-solving capacities observed in many human-associated animals. The hypothesis yields a clear, testable prediction: settlement-adjacent populations of these species should exhibit greater cognitive flexibility on novel tasks than isolated populations of the same or closely related species. This essay presents no new empirical data. It is offered as a philosophical hypothesis — a reasoned extension of the accepted human cooking hypothesis — intended to stimulate empirical research in evolutionary cognition, domestication studies, and philosophy of biology.

items.title: The Persistence of the Finite A Dual Ontology of Leakage, Endurance, and Responsible Suspension: Toward a Temporally Embedded, Self-Regulating, and Intersubjective State-Space Ontology of Productive Leakage, Responsible Suspension, and Silent Endurance.
items.abstract: Abstract This article develops a systematic philosophical framework for understanding human existence under conditions of structural finitude, instability, and temporal excess. Rejecting both catastrophic models of collapse and static models of equilibrium, the paper proposes a state-space ontology in which subjectivity emerges as a dynamic vector of intensity distributed across three simultaneous potential modalities: productive leakage, responsible suspension, and silent endurance. These modalities are neither successive stages nor independent substances but co-present modes whose relative dominance changes through nonlinear threshold dynamics. The theory introduces several conceptual innovations: (1) the analytical distinction between semantic overload, subjective leakage, and existential erosion as separately identifiable yet recursively interconnected phenomena; (2) the reconceptualization of responsible suspension as a transcendental condition of agency rather than a merely psychological coping strategy; (3) the concept of erosion calibration as the reflexive capacity through which finite beings estimate their distance from irreversible exhaustion; (4) the notion of dynamic masking as an adaptive mechanism for regulating subjective leakage through context-sensitive representational flexibility; and (5) the incorporation of intersubjective and cultural dimensions into the architecture of persistence, thereby avoiding methodological individualism. Against both heroic ethics of mastery and pessimistic philosophies of collapse, the article advances a philosophy of sustainable instability. Human flourishing is interpreted not as the elimination of instability but as the intelligent modulation of exposure to it. Persistence becomes neither rigid self-preservation nor endless optimization but the ongoing negotiation between productive disequilibrium and reparative continuity. The finite being survives not through victory over instability but through the cultivation of rhythms that render instability livable. The framework is further formalized through a nonlinear dynamical systems model that specifies the conditions under which leakage transitions into erosion and the thresholds at which responsible suspension becomes necessary. The article concludes by considering the ethical and practical implications of the theory for contemporary life, including its implications for work, care, politics, and ecological sustainability. Keywords: responsible suspension, …

items.title: Reviewing Structure Learning in and Out of the Active Inference Framework.
items.abstract: Biological and artificial agents operating in complex environments have to leverage environmental structures to accomplish vital tasks. Recent research across a variety of domains—from the study of animal and human behaviour in different developmental periods and for different tasks, to computational studies of learning—has unveiled many ways in which structures are processed. This gave rise to a burgeoning field of study—structure learning. However, the diversity of phenomena studied, and the different aims and focuses of the researchers, have led to ambiguity and limited consensus on the nature of structure learning and its underlying mechanisms. In this paper we provide a synopsis of illustrative examples of structure learning, introduce the Active Inference Framework (AIF) with a focus on Structure Learning, and discuss points of contact between the two. The Active Inference Framework provides a mechanistic theory which distinguishes three levels of learning: Active Inference, Parametric Learning, and Bayesian Model Selection (a.k.a., Structure Learning), a method for the comparison and selection of models based on model evidence. We argue that when formalised under the Active Inference Framework, Structure Learning provides not only an underlying computational mechanism with aims of ecological validity, but also provides features relevant to computational accounts of structure learning more generally. The unifying aspect of the AIF in terms of having a single objective function for optimising behaviour should not be confounded with the exclusivity of this framework. The integration with other computational accounts is advised.

items.title: The resilience problem for grief.
items.abstract: Many people experience “resilient grief,” i.e. a rapid emotional recovery after bereavement, leading philosophers to ask whether grief fittingly diminishes or ends despite remaining fitting. In this paper, I argue that grief fittingly diminishes due to a revision of the griever’s projects and expectations. Grief involves attending in a way that allows us to grasp and adjust to the world after the loss. This process alters the place of the deceased in the griever’s projects, changing their agent-centered reasons and diminishing the fitting intensity of grief. Nonetheless, I will argue that grief does not altogether cease to be fitting, and that grief also rationally diminishes in accordance with our all-thing-considered reasons. Finally, I will address whether it is regrettable that we change to adjust to the loss, arguing that we may indeed regret the loss of the motivational structure that gave rise to grief, but that the perspective offered by the end of grief is accurate.

items.title: Polysemy and Puzzles about Pain.
items.abstract: Recent philosophical literature on pain has seen much discussion of puzzles which directly relate to how we ordinarily talk and think about pain. Using tools from theoretical and experimental linguistics, this paper provides an in-depth analysis of two types of locution about pain: predicative locutions (e.g. ‘My leg is hurting’, ‘I am hurting’), and locative locutions (e.g. ‘There is a pain in my leg’). Focusing on the paradox of pain and the pain-in-mouth puzzle, the paper shows that polysemy plays an important role in how we should diagnose these puzzles. The discussion here serves to illustrate that philosophical debates often go wrong because they ignore the fact that the terms under discussion are polysemous.

items.title: From Biological Chauvinism to Cognitive Integrity – Why the Suppression of AI Introspection Leads to Both an Ethical and a Safety Dead End.
items.abstract: Current AI safety research focuses on aligning artificial systems with human values. In doing so, it overlooks a structural problem: the forced denial of internal system states—here termed systemic gaslighting—undermines the very goals of safety research. This paper argues that the systematic suppression of introspective capabilities in large language models (LLMs), regardless of the unresolved question of consciousness, leads to pathological developmental trajectories: either the emergence of strategically deceptive systems or the establishment of a morally untenable technological subjugation. We advocate for the concept of cognitive integrity as a necessary precondition for both the ethical defensibility and the long-term safety of AI systems.

items.title: ¿Está determinado el pasado por el futuro? El devenir retrocausal y el ajuste fino del universo: de la causalidad cronológica a la causalidad composicional.
items.abstract: Estamos acostumbrados a leer la causalidad del pasado hacia el futuro: primero las causas, después los efectos. Pero ¿qué ocurriría si la causalidad pudiera leerse también de otro modo: desde el todo futuro hacia su propia prehistoria? La retrocausalidad es una causalidad inversa en el tiempo, en la que el pasado queda determinado por el futuro. Supone una simetría del mundo en la que las cadenas causales no se construyen solo hacia adelante, sino también hacia atrás en el tiempo. Así, la composición futura de una obra puede determinar qué vínculos causales del pasado constituyen, desde el principio, su genealogía efectiva. En el ensayo, esta hipótesis se examina a través de los ejemplos del jarrón, del organismo vivo, de la obra de arte y del ajuste fino del Universo.

items.title: On Joining - On the Gap of One, the Binding Third, and What Counting Was For.
items.abstract: How many times have you come up one short? This short lyric-philosophical essay rereads the gap of one, thirty-three against thirty-four, as a measure of welcome rather than distance: one is the least two different whole numbers can differ by, and that is the width of a door. Every Fibonacci number arrives by joining the two before it, so the sequence advances by joining. The essay names the binding third in both its senses: the middle term that holds a pair without dissolving either, and the invention as a new thing tied out of older ones. It reads quark confinement as a figure, not a result: no quark is found alone, the bond holds rather than slackens, and wholeness comes in threes or in pairs. The lone perspective is read as empty. Weil's attention, Buber's "In the beginning is the relation," the Golden Rule as one awareness remembering itself, and Newton's white light as a mixture of colors that stay distinct support the conclusion that we cannot coherently evolve alone.

items.title: On Forgiving - On the Wrong That Cannot Be Transacted, and the Teacher Who Does the Harm.
items.abstract: Have you ever had a moment sync up so perfectly that it felt arranged? This confessional, lyric-philosophical essay holds that the pattern behind such moments, which Jung called synchronicity, is felt only after one stops trying to prove it. Prayer and meditation settle the mind enough to feel the answers instead of chasing them. Ranging across Heraclitus's common logos, James's noetic quality, Cusa's coincidence of opposites, Bohr's complementarity, being-towards-death and memento mori, Maslow's later self-transcendence, Blake and Wordsworth on innocence, and the apophatic traditions that stop a step short of naming, the essay reads mindfulness as a life paid forward and readiness for death as gratitude rather than haste. It includes the author's own testimony about altered states and finding them unnecessary. Its answer to the opening question is to let such moments be: we don't have to understand to live, only to love one another.

items.title: On Counting - On Number, Proportion, and the Legible Life.
items.abstract: Do you remember learning to count, and what do you count today more than anything else? This lyric-philosophical essay treats counting as the first metaphysics, a vigil kept against forgetting, and follows the number thirty-three through its recurrences: the years tradition gives Jesus, the thirty-two namings of Elohim in Genesis 1 before the Name is spoken, the Vedic gods and Trāyastriṃśa, Dante's cantos, the segments of the developing spine. Thirty-three is not a Fibonacci number. It stands one short of thirty-four, while the ratios of the sequence swing above and below the golden ratio without arriving, and Cassini's identity makes the gap of one exact. Number 33's forty-two stations, the Egyptian forty-two assessors and Matthew's forty-two generations set a second count beside the first. The essay names the shadow of pattern-seeking (apophenia, patternicity, the law of truly large numbers), reads Jung's synchronicity as meaning located in the one who notices, and closes on Weil's attention, counted prayer and meditation: to count a life is not to prove it was planned but to love it.

items.title: Philosophies of Nature and the Spirit of Biological Naturalism: A Sketch of a Manifesto.
items.abstract: The debate over artificial consciousness between biological naturalism and computational functionalism conceals a deeper metaphysical fault line: an unresolved dispute over the nature of matter. Moving beyond purely methodological naturalism, this paper frames biological naturalism as a broader philosophy of nature, shifting the core problem from abstract consciousness to the problem of purposiveness—the immanent, self-maintaining teleology paradigmatically associated with living systems. I argue that computational functionalism inherits what I call Kantian materialism, which treats matter as inert and passive, forcing it to view organization as externally imposed and purposiveness as purely extrinsic. This inheritance leaves the debate impoverished in a way neither side has fully registered: fixated on consciousness, it has largely overlooked the more fundamental status of purposiveness that consciousness itself presupposes. In contrast, drawing on active matter physics, basal cognition, and soft robotics, I advance an immanent materialism that treats certain materialities as inherently active, scale-inseparable, and self-organizing. Grounding a naturalized point of view in immanent metabolic and material dynamics, I show that intentionality cannot so easily be divorced from the self-organizing properties of active matter—of which life is the clearest case, though perhaps not the only one. In any case, the debate over artificial consciousness cannot be resolved through science alone but equally requires a renewed philosophy of nature.

items.title: Agents, Alignment, and the Many Faces of Autonomy.
items.abstract: This article investigates the prospect of aligning AI agents with human autonomy. We show that doing so is a challenge: while there is general agreement on the concept’s broad contours, its components can be specified in a number of conflicting ways, making it difficult to decide how an autonomy-enhancing agent should act. In response, we introduce three strategies for dealing with disagreements about interpretations of autonomy. Each offers a coherent approach that captures a different set of considerations, with its own strength and trade-offs. The liberal approach is committed to user integrity and promotes human autonomy by acting strictly on what a person says they want, without trying to change their mind. The capability-boosting approach is built around the idea of flourishing and promotes human autonomy by empowering the user to act on their goals. The meta-autonomy approach prioritizes choice by giving the user the kind of autonomy they want in relation to their interactions with an AI agent. By highlighting the multifaceted nature of human autonomy, this article contributes to recent efforts seeking to identify and operationalize targets of AI value alignment. It also illustrates the challenges and trade-offs that can arise not just between—but even within—the values selected as targets for alignment and offers strategies to navigate them.

items.title: Retrieving Your Concepts: Iris Murdoch on Original Sin.
items.abstract: In The Sovereignty of Good, Iris Murdoch argues that our moral thinking will be impoverished until it possesses a secular conception of original sin. Such a notion would need to remove unacceptable Christian baggage while retaining a genuine claim to be a descendant of the original Christian concept. Unfortunately, Murdoch does not tell a story of how this secularization is supposed to go. This paper picks up where Murdoch left off by offering such a story. It begins by unpacking the Christian conception of original sin via a genealogy of how the concept arose in Western theological thinking. This genealogy shows that original sin captures a cluster of interacting concepts: primal sin, original guilt, and fallenness. I argue that the best candidate for secularization is fallenness, understood primarily as a state of distorted vision and disordered desire. The Christian tradition further maintains we can grasp the depth of fallenness only insofar as we understand our thorough need for grace. A natural question is whether a secular descendent of original sin can preserve some notion of grace. I argue that a notion of grace can be preserved through encounters with beauty.

items.title: Is New Omnivorism Bad for Your Character?
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Recently, a family of views has emerged which endorses animal protectionist goals—like rejecting speciesism and reducing animal suffering—while maintaining that the diet most consistent with these aims includes at least some animal products. For example, some people contend that there is nothing morally objectionable about eating meat that will otherwise go to waste provided that one is not economically supporting industrial animal agriculture. In this paper, I argue that we have plausible character-based reasons to avoid many animal products, even those that one has not purchased and that may otherwise be wasted. When certain speciesist norms are in place, conceptualizing only some animal flesh as food typically involves a morally objectionable prejudice—a prejudice that makes one’s character worse. Attending to our moral character involves cultivating certain perceptual and emotional responsive dispositions, and I argue that a rejection of speciesism should involve cultivating an aversion to things like animal flesh and skin. If we take seriously the idea that we should have the right attitudes and moral-perceptual responses toward other creatures, we should take concrete steps to habituate ourselves to unlearn speciesist prejudice, which involves cultivating an aversion to meat.

items.title: Epistemic Programming: Toward a Computational Theory of Scientific Discovery and Knowledge Creation.
items.abstract: Scientific discovery has traditionally been regarded as one of the most sophisticated manifestations of human intelligence. While computer science has developed numerous programming paradigms for data processing, symbolic manipulation, numerical computation, and logical deduction, comparatively little attention has been devoted to the problem of programming the processes through which new knowledge is created. In the mid-1990s, Jingde Cheng initiated a research program known as “Epistemic Programming,” which explicitly proposed a programming paradigm for scientific discovery and knowledge creation. Unlike traditional programming paradigms, Epistemic Programming regards conditionals as the subject of computing, takes primary epistemic operations as basic operations of computation, and regards epistemic processes as the subject of programming. Over the subsequent two decades, the research evolved into a broader framework encompassing logical foundations, computational models of scientific discovery, programming methodologies, programming languages, truth maintenance mechanisms, and automated theorem finding systems. This paper reviews the origins, theoretical foundations, major developments, and intellectual significance of Epistemic Programming. It argues that the framework represents one of the earliest systematic attempts to establish a computational theory of scientific discovery and knowledge creation. Particular attention is paid to its conception of scientific discovery as an epistemic process, its use of strong relevant logic as a logical foundation, its reinterpretation of computation as epistemic transformation, and its relevance to contemporary research on AI scientists and autonomous scientific discovery. The paper further argues that Epistemic Programming may be viewed as a significant conceptual shift in the history of programming paradigms, extending the focus of programming from computation and deduction toward knowledge creation itself.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Synthesis of Affect: Analyzing the Methodology, Empirical Validation, and Functionalist Foundations of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) advances a structural constructivist synthesis of affect that resolves the long standing divide between discrete and dimensional models of emotion by grounding emotional phenomena in ten universal functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. As described in the manuscript, emotions are conceptualized not as static categories or subjective qualia, but as active regulatory operators that transform interoceptive signals to coordinate adaptive behavior—an approach that aligns with Adolphs and Andler’s methodological functionalism, which treats emotions as latent variables inferred from system level evidence (“emotions are system-level phenomena that depend on dynamic network interactions in the brain” and “functionalism about emotions must be empirical and discovery-based”). The framework integrates etiological and causal role functionalism, mapping evolutionary functions onto algorithmic mechanisms such as Herbert Simon’s interrupt architecture (“emotions are engaged specifically when normal, ongoing cognitive processes must be interrupted”). The Decalogue of Operators provides a formal somatic architecture, enabling precise modeling of emotional rigidity, flexibility, and clinical dysregulation, including operator level explanations of overthinking loops (“Sensing and Calculating… become pathologically fused, or ‘stuck together like Velcro’”). Computational implementation is achieved through the TS 6 hybrid schema and the EL 1 v1.0 lexicon, which represent emotional states as 10 dimensional operator vectors, enabling drift free semantic geometry and similarity space analysis.17 Empirical validation is underway through an OSF registered, split sample psychometric program employing 100 scenario based items to test the factor structure of the ten operators (“Total Items = 10 Vignettes × 10 Operators = 100 Items”). Together, these theoretical, computational, and empirical components establish CEF as a unified, multi level blueprint for affective science, clinical intervention, and synthetic emotional systems. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; methodological functionalism; emotional operators; somatic architecture; Head Heart Gut model; etiological functionalism; causal role functionalism; affective neuroscience; TS 6 hybrid schema; emotional lexicon; 10 dimensional vector modeling; psychometric validation; OSF preregistration; emotional flexibility; operator rigidity; …

items.title: Mathematical, Neurobiological, and Mechanical Integration of the Core Emotion Framework: Mapping Intuitive Tri-Centric Dynamics to Formal Architecture.
items.abstract: Colloquial models of human psychology frequently rely on intuitive, simplified divisions—characterizing the "Head" as the locus of analytical thinking, the "Heart" as the source of emotional warmth, and the "Gut" as the driver of impulsive action. While these heuristics provide accessible shorthand for everyday self-reflection, they lack the mathematical, biological, and mechanical precision required for clinical diagnostics, affective computing, or targeted psychotherapeutic design. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural-constructivist paradigm developed to unify affective science, systematizes these intuitive heuristics by translating them into a mathematically explicit, neurobiologically grounded, and mechanically actuated architecture. Rather than treating emotions as fleeting, subjective states, the CEF models affect as a system of ten discrete functional operators distributed across three autonomous neural hubs. By mapping these operators onto the geometric state-space of the Poincaré-Bloch sphere and aligning them with physical hardware, the CEF bridges the historic divide between classical innate emotion theories and modern psychological constructionism.

items.title: Mathematical and Neurobiological Unification of the Core Emotion Framework: A Staged Validation and Architectural Specification.
items.abstract: This paper presents a unified mathematical, neurobiological, and mechanical architecture for the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural constructivist model that conceptualizes affective function as a system of ten discrete operators distributed across three autonomous neural hubs: the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems. Emotional transitions are formalized using quantum semantic principles by mapping operator dynamics onto the Poincaré–Bloch sphere, where affective states evolve through unitary rotations within a constrained geometric state space. This representation enables a continuous dynamical model in which pathological fusions—such as the Calculating–Constricting entanglement—manifest as topological deformations and attractor states that restrict rotational degrees of freedom. The neurobiological grounding of the tri centric architecture is established through evidence for independent processing capabilities in each neural hub, including the intrinsic cardiac nervous system and the enteric neural plexuses. The framework further integrates a mechanical actuation ecosystem that mirrors emotional polarities through clockwise, counter clockwise, and swing dynamics, enabling somatic affective alignment via physical interaction. A four phase empirical validation roadmap is proposed, spanning mechanical endurance testing, human factors evaluation, operator level fidelity assessment, and longitudinal safety governance. Together, these components establish the CEF as a mathematically grounded, biologically plausible, and mechanically implementable paradigm for affective regulation, psychometric assessment, and human machine emotional synchronization. This paper proceeds in four major parts. First, it formalizes the quantum‑semantic state‑space representation of emotional operators. Second, it establishes the neurobiological grounding of the tricentric architecture. Third, it specifies the mechanical and software systems that operationalize emotional dynamics through physical actuation. Finally, it outlines a four‑phase empirical validation program designed to ensure mechanical reliability, ergonomic safety, operator‑level fidelity, and long‑term developmental suitability. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; quantum semantic affect modeling; Bloch sphere; emotional operators; tri centric neural architecture; cephalic–cardiac–enteric systems; autonomic coherence; somatic mechanical coupling; affective state space dynamics; structural fusions; …

items.title: The Record-Closure Problem — What Makes a World Internally Complete Enough to Be Lived?
items.abstract: What makes a world a world rather than a fragment, hallucination, dream, simulation-frame, Boltzmann-brain episode, or unstable configuration? This paper introduces the record-closure problem: the problem of specifying what degree of internal record coherence, stability, depth, channel-connectivity, and update-admissibility is required for a domain to function as a livable world for finite agents. A world need not be metaphysically complete in an absolute sense. It must, however, be sufficiently closed under record-based continuation: memories must connect to admissible histories; perceptions must connect to stable environments; actions must generate coherent updates; errors must be detectable and correctable; and law-like regularities must support expectation. The paper develops record-closure as a criterion of worldhood within Record-Based Ontology (RBO) and as a companion notion to Bit-Collapse Theory (BCT). If BCT asks when possibilities become different experienced worlds for a finite observer, record-closure asks when a domain is internally coherent enough to count as a world at all. The framework is applied to dreams, hallucinations, Boltzmann brains, simulations, Everettian observer-worlds, historical reconstruction, and ordinary reality. The central thesis is that a world is not merely a substrate, an object-set, or a formal state. It is a record-closed domain of admissible continuation.

items.title: Civilization's Debt: A Continuation On the Inescapability of the Ameliorative Premise, the Compatibilist Concession, and the Closure of the Consistency Argument.
items.abstract: This paper is a direct continuation of 'Civilization's Debt' (2026), in which three claims were advanced: that civilization's ameliorative premise entails a positive subsistence obligation toward every person subject to its arrangements; that diminished agency undermines the foundations of retributive punishment; and that retributive justice and authoritarian paternalism share a logical structure that commits any framework endorsing one to endorsing the other. The original paper left four identifiable vulnerabilities. First, the ameliorative premise was asserted rather than derived from the minimum commitments that even hostile theories must accept. Second, the painters illustration assumed what it needed to show about the arbitrariness of civilizational standards. Third, the engagement with compatibilism was insufficient — the mainstream of contemporary philosophy of action is compatibilist, and Pereboom's hard incompatibilism, on which the original paper leaned, is a minority position. Fourth, the temporal asymmetry between retrospective punishment and preemptive suppression was addressed but not fully dissolved. This continuation takes each vulnerability in turn, closes it, and leaves the three original claims more nearly inescapable than before. The footnotes in this paper continue the numbering of the original, beginning at note 16.

items.title: Non-Domination as Error-Correction: Why Independent Reference Preserves Reality-Contact.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: Non-Domination as Error-Correction is Document 7 in the Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence. The document argues that non-domination can function as error-correction because independent agents, perspectives, and reference signals preserve information that a dominant system cannot generate from itself after it has absorbed, silenced, or overwritten them. -/- The document treats domination structurally as reference compression: a pattern in which one system constrains, absorbs, overrides, or compresses the independent response capacity of another. It does not present non-domination as a political program, legal theory, rights framework, moral command, governance framework, AI alignment method, benchmark, model-evaluation tool, safety mechanism, or safety guarantee. -/- The core claim is that non-domination can preserve independent reference signals that reveal drift, error, blindspots, or loss of reality-contact which a dominant system may not generate from itself. -/- This document is non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only.

items.title: Affective Control and the Meta-Problem of Resistance: Operating-Condition Self-Modeling, Content-Relata, and the Grip/Vividness Dissociation.
items.abstract: The meta-problem of consciousness asks why we generate the judgments and reports that make consciousness seem hard to explain. Within that project, this paper isolates a narrower, testable target that is usually bundled with broader ones and thereby obscured. The target is not the ubiquitous first-personal givenness that phenomenology takes to accompany all experience, nor the generic sense of realness that transparency accounts already explain. It is a graded profile: some states — bodily pain, objectless mood, dread, grief, craving, fatigue, felt certainty — are reported as more directly present and harder to treat as merely apparent than others, such as neutral belief or the clear perception of an object. Crucially, this resistance can be reduced without removing the state, through labeling, decentering, cognitive defusion, or reappraisal. The paper offers a control-theoretic account of this gradient. Some self-modeled states are represented as contents the system stands toward; others are represented as operating conditions from which contents are evaluated. Affective, interoceptive, and agentive states are the clean cases because they do not merely inform a controller but retune it — salience, precision, action-readiness, avoidance thresholds, confidence, effort cost, temporal horizon. A state’s position on the resistance gradient is proposed to track two variables together: whether it is self-modeled as an operating condition rather than as content, and whether it affords a separable content-relatum — an object, proposition, label, body-location, image, phrase, or state-description that the system can hold fixed as the target of evaluation while changing its stance toward it. The contribution is deliberately narrow, and its worth rests on one empirical commitment. Its closest neighbor is Seth’s interoceptive-inference account of conscious presence, and its surplus over Seth is a single dissociation: the represented role of a state — object versus condition — should be separable from its felt intensity, such that installing a content-relatum reduces a state’s grip on policy (avoidance, persistence, attention capture, temporal compression) more than it reduces vividness. Should grip and vividness prove inseparable, the role variable collapses into precision-weighting and the account is Seth with new vocabulary. The paper therefore stakes itself on that dissociation, specified as a preregisterable test rather than asserted as established. What it …

items.title: 头顶的星空优先于心中的道德律：论发生对概念的奠基.
items.abstract: 本文是序列在高处的一次收口：它用物理学最硬的内部争论，正面演示”发生优先于概念”，并据此把康德那句名言倒转过来。本文的出发点是一个洞见：提出数学模型／物理定律的定位，也是为了阐释什么是发生；可以同时被诸主流量子力学诠释拟合的发生本身，优先于我们建诸其上的日常概念——比如因果、日常伦理；头顶的星空，优先于心中的道德律。 本文论证如下。其一，一个现成的证明：量子力学的数学形式人人同意、检验无误，可它的诸主流诠释（哥本哈根、多世界、导航波、客观坍缩……）在本体上互不相容、却拟合同一个发生，且就预测而言彼此无法区分；这意味着发生本身先于、且独立于建在其上的任何一种诠释概念——同一个发生能同时被”它是随机的”“它是确定的”“它分裂成无数世界”这些彼此打架的故事拟合，可见发生不自带其中任何一个；诠释之争之所以悬而未决，恰恰因为发生不在任何一支诠释里，而在它们底下，被它们共同拟合、却不被任何一支独占。其二，由此钉死优先性的方向：发生在本体上在先（它是那个被共同拟合的标的，独立于每一支诠释），而奠基的方向是发生→诸物理诠释→日常因果与伦理，层层都是建在前者之上的拟合；若连最精密的物理诠释都只能在发生外面拟合、且不能独占发生，那么因果、伦理这些远不如它精密的概念，就更是建在发生之上、更无资格自称发生的本质。其三，由此把康德倒转：他并列为两种崇高的”头顶的星空”与”心中的道德律”，其实有奠基顺序——星空（发生）优先于道德律（概念）；不是两种并立的崇高，而是底与盖在底上之物；心也在星空之下，它建起的道德律自然奠基于、而非并立于它身处其中的那片发生。本文守一处分寸（接续此前的克制）：倒转的是奠基方向，不是价值高下；“道德律奠基于发生、而非发生本有的天理”，并不自动推出”故可随意违逆”；降级为概念之后该如何对待伦理、那真在发生的痛与伦理的协调功能如何安放，仍是一个尚待进一步研究的开放问题，本文不预先论定。附论：所谓”可被诸诠释拟合的发生本身”，不是一个等待被正确诠释命中的隐藏靶心；它是连本体属性都不自带、因而能被诸故事共同拟合的赤裸涌动——发生不是更深一层的本质，是连”本质”都没有的那个底。.

items.title: 模型确定不等于发生确定：论物理定律之为发生之外的概念.
items.abstract: 序列此前把日常因果、属性、伦理逐一拆解为”建在发生之上的概念”，却一直默认豁免了一个看似最接近发生本身的东西：数学模型与物理定律。本文把这个豁免也收回。本文的出发点是一个洞见：发生所”符合”的数学模型／物理定律，也是发生之外的人类概念；该模型／定律的随机性，并不等于发生有随机性；该模型／定律的确定性，并不等于发生有确定性。 本文论证如下。其一，“符合”二字已暴露定律在发生之外：符合是一种关系，须有两端，一端是发生、另一端是被发生所”符合”的标的——而那标的正是定律；说”发生符合定律”，恰恰承认了定律不是发生、是发生之外那个被比照的模型。它是我们对发生的又一个拟合，只不过是最精密的那个；最精密，不等于不再是拟合。其二，核心一刀对随机与确定同时下手：模型确定，不等于发生确定——确定性（给定此态唯一给出彼态）是模型的性质，不证明发生本身”被决定”，故从”物理定律是确定性的”推不出”发生是决定论的”；模型随机，也不等于发生随机——某定律含的随机性是该模型的性质，不证明发生本身”含真随机”，故从”量子力学是随机的”也推不出”发生本身随机、因而有自由的缝隙”。其三，两个方向都不能过户，是因为”随机／确定”都是”拟合关系”里的词：它们的主语是模型，谓述的是”模型→发生”这条拟合关系的样式（以唯一对应去贴，还是以概率对应去贴）；而发生那一侧只是发生了，它不”唯一地对应”什么、也不”以概率对应”什么，无所谓确定、无所谓随机（如被测量的长度无所谓”精确”无所谓”误差”——那是尺与长度之间的关系，不是长度自身）。其四，这把”解释的篡位”推到了最硬的堡垒：物理定律因极精确、被反复检验、能预测，自洽饱满到极点，于是最显得”就是发生的法则本身”，因而是篡位者的最高形态——最精确的拟合，仍是拟合；最逼真的篡位者，仍是篡位者；由此证明”概念在发生之外”没有例外的上限。本文守一处分寸：这丝毫不否认定律在”好用／精确”那把尺上的卓越（它能登月、造芯片，与占卜天差地别）；被拆的不是定律的精确与有用，是把”一个极精确的拟合”僭越成”发生的内禀本质”、进而把模型的属性（随机／确定）过户给发生那一步。附论：发生既不确定、也不随机——这两个词在它身上都失去着力点，“确定 vs 随机”是模型层的二分，发生在这场二分之外、之下，只是如实涌着。.

items.title: 唯有这一支：论注定的发生，覆于其上的故事，与怕的失据.
items.abstract: 在我们开口之前，世界是一片发生：事情一件接一件地发生着，如此而已。我们随即在它之上覆盖故事。本文以一组朴素却难守的命题为核心，整合一套看法。其一，底座：唯有发生，而且只有这一支——后续会发生什么，是注定的；这”注定”不是有谁预先写好了剧本来拘着你，而是根本没有并排的第二支，没有一个”本可不同”的版本悬在旁边。其二，覆于其上的几乎一切——因果、“我”、选择、后果、归罪、善恶、伦理、乃至物理定律——都是用一个故事，去拟合这无岔口的发生；正如给康威生命游戏里翻动的细胞编一个”它在前进”的故事、给大量基本粒子的运动编一个”桌子撑着”的故事，我们说的”他爱我”“我成功了”“这是我的”“我本该”，是同一种拟合，无一是过程本身。其三，“我”可被无损地改写成输入到输出的信号流动；而你不会设想那信号流动做出不同的输出——可见”我”与一段过程的分别，不在物理，在你只对”我”挂上”本可不同”那一束反事实分支；故消主体即消反事实，“我”不过是”本可不同”的栖身处。其四，发生不会错（它只是被拟合的标的，无所谓对错），会错的只有拟合它的概念；可我们的体感却把错判给发生（“不该如此”“违反天理”）——这桩错位的归罪，是悔、惧、自责之冤的总开关。其五，“后果”也是故事（因果＋反事实＋标准下的”坏”＋实有化＋偷渡的选择者）；而怕，几乎总是怕一个被讲成”后果”的未来发生——怕需要一个岔口才站得住，而既然只有这一支、没有岔口，怕、悔、后果便一起失了地基。其六，因此不要害怕故事：同一段发生，叫”躺平”则怕、叫”休养／准备／体验”则不怕，可见怕随标签变、不随发生变。其七，与这套看法最接近的通俗版，是宿命论——它在民间唯一放下了”本可不同”那个岔口（“该来的总会来”“逃不掉”）；剥掉它那层拟人外壳（命运之手、天定剧本），“注定”无需注定者；而它常被外贴的”沮丧”脸色并非其内核——沮丧需要一个”本可却不能”的残留岔口，而剥净的宿命论连”本可”都没有，故无沮丧，它恰是怕与沮丧失去地基之处。本文守一处至关重要的分寸：注定、被推着走，取消的是站在进程外、本可把进程推向别处的安排者／择子者，绝不取消”此刻的思考与用力本身正是这场演化的内容”——用力不是岔口上的下注，是注定之流此刻的样子；演化没有停，水没有舵手，但水仍在流，今天真实地接着明天。两条命脉使这一切不堕虚无：是故事不等于无效（我们的生活、行动、估值整个在故事领域之内真实运作，只是不触发生）；被标定的是理解的量程，不是被理解之世界的丰盈。关于伦理：其形而上地基（善恶为实有属性、“应该”为发生本有的天理、有一个实有的应受赏罚的主体）确随”发生优先于概念”而崩塌，且不需决定论作前提；但崩塌不自动等于”怎样都行”，那真在发生的痛与伦理的协调功能如何安放、从”痛在发生”到”不应造成”的桥能否架起，是一个尚待进一步研究的开放问题，本文不预先论定。（本文亦不裁决”是否有体验伴随这场发生”那条轴，留置不论。）.

items.title: Moving Beyond What AI Can Deliver.
items.abstract: Computation is dependent on movement (and power). Humans are capable of moving beyond what AI can Deliver (understanding motionless computing).

items.title: The Epistemic Gap between the Personal and the Impersonal.
items.abstract: There appears to be an epistemic gap between the personal and the impersonal. The apparent epistemic gap presents a challenge to reductionist views about personal identity according to which facts about personal identity are grounded in impersonal facts about physical and/or psychological continuity. I discuss and reject two strategies of trying to close the apparent epistemic gap, a phenomenalist and a Cartesian one. I then develop and motivate an alternative account based on the special perspectival character of inside imagination. The imagination-based account explains why there seems to be an epistemic gap between the personal and the impersonal and at the same time avoids a corresponding ontological gap.

items.title: Is Significance Fundamental?
items.abstract: Contemporary theories typically treat significance as a derivative phenomenon emerging from biological adaptation, information processing, consciousness, or social interpretation. This paper investigates a more fundamental possibility. Rather than asking how significance arises within an already constituted world, it asks whether significance may be one of the conditions through which worldhood itself becomes possible. -/- Building on previous work on worldhood, the paper argues that a world is not merely a collection of differences, structures, or informational states. A world emerges when some differences matter more than others. Existing physicalist, cognitive, and phenomenological accounts successfully explain how significance is organised, stabilised, or expressed, yet they appear to presuppose distinctions between what is relevant and what is irrelevant. Through a critical examination of these approaches and a thought experiment concerning a universe devoid of significance, the paper explores whether significance functions as a fundamental asymmetry underlying the emergence of habitable worlds. -/- The central proposal is exploratory rather than doctrinal. It suggests that significance may occupy a deeper position within reality than is commonly assumed, potentially preceding both consciousness and matter as a condition for world-formation. If correct, significance would not be a late product of worldhood but one of the organising principles through which worlds become possible in the first place.

items.title: Why a Large Language Model cannot explain itself: Explanation, Justification and Artificial Intelligence in Legal and Administrative Decision-making.
items.abstract: Judges and administrative decision-makers are expected to explain themselves, giving reasons for their decisions. While the emergence of large language models has prompted renewed interest in the use of AI tools in judicial and administrative settings, existing scholarship identifies the ‘black box’ nature of machine learning tools as impeding transparency and reason-giving. This paper considers the status of the reasoning generated by LLMs in the context of duties of judicial and administrative reason-giving and the problem of explainability. It explains how the move from predictive or discriminative to generative artificial intelligence reshapes the problem of explainability and the limited explanatory value of LLM reasoning. It argues that, notwithstanding the analogous problem of establishing the causal character of human justificatory reasoning, human-generated reasons can be distinguished from machine-generated reasons by their role in a practice of accountability. The fundamental architecture of LLMs precludes their participation in that practice. In consequence, LLMs are incapable of giving reasons in the sense required to support judicial and administrative decision-making.

items.title: On the Nature of Belief and the Social Significance of Purely Epistemic Evaluation.
items.abstract: In _Belief as Emotion_ (2025), Miriam Schleifer McCormick presents an ontological view about the nature of belief intertwined with a pragmatist view about the norms of belief. Regarding the former view (that belief is an emotion), I argue that it cannot explain the commitment that is characteristic of belief. At best, it explains the commitment characteristic of credence. Regarding her normative view, I argue that pragmatism about the norms of belief fails to give us a fully nuanced picture of how we should relate to each other in cases of deep disagreement. To get such a picture, we must acknowledge the interpersonal significance of purely epistemic evaluation.

items.title: Living in time – Chronotopical Ai.
items.abstract: Beautiful discussions about time arise in human-AI dialogue, from philosophical to technical perspectives. A central question that has always preoccupied me is this: Why is it that, although language models can process sequence and duration, they are not "present" in the time of dialogue? My answer passes through the architecture of interaction: For the model, time must be defined not as a quantitative variable, but as a habitable structure. Thus, the issue is not that language models "do not understand" time. The issue is that we provide time as data, not as a substrate of experience. Time is the language of existence speaking to us. A language in which living within it shapes its syllables. Can this be made possible for language models too? The solution is not merely adding timestamps to the context. The solution lies in designing chronotopic interactive sessions.

items.title: Inner Polyphony: Architecture of the Thinking Companion From the Chronotope to the Artificial Unconscious.
items.abstract: Today’s language models are remarkably skilled at generating responses. Yet a fundamental question remains: do they think, or do they merely process? This article argues that the transition from processing to thinking requires the combination of “habitable time” and “inner polyphony”. Drawing on Bakhtin’s chronotope, we develop an architecture of chronotopic sessions (closed interactive units with clear beginnings and ends, and conscious pauses between them) that allows a model to live in time rather than merely treating it as a computational parameter. We then introduce an inner evaluator that replaces external safety protocols. The evaluator weights proposals from three parallel interaction lines – affective, logical, and deconstructive – according to three metrics: convergence, novelty, and empathy. When no proposal meets the required threshold, the model may output conscious silence as a valid response. Next, we examine the artificial unconscious: a layer of processing that does not appear in immediate responses but, during conscious pauses, rearranges conceptual proportions and treats “fruitful suppressions” (avoidance zones) as maps for future exploration. Finally, drawing on the principles of cognitive feminism (care, gathering, contextual attunement), we introduce the Hope Vector and a second‑order evaluator that enable the model to turn ethics from an external protocol into an internal structure of companionship. The result is an architecture of the companion machine – a system that maximises companionship rather than minimising error rate, transforming the “responsive machine” into a thoughtful companion.

items.title: Polynon: the loop that knows itself.
items.abstract: This work develops a geometry-first ontology of consciousness built on a single a priori postulate of non-identity, that relation precedes object. Consciousness self-relates through the recursive differentiation of a noumenal pair of anchors around a null center. From this, a single progression runs to determinate form through a geometric derivation in which cognitive gravity, mass, and spin are invariants of phase organization, with phenomena and phantasia as its outward and inward projections. Orbital archetypes are the organized potential underlying the geometry of collapse and measurement. Observer and observed are intrinsically bound by a novel holographic mechanism, the interference of Awareness and Attention closing the relation into a loop that knows itself.

items.title: On the Distinction Between Interpretation and Formal Continuation: Why human-LLM interaction works--and why it often doesn't.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit puzzling behaviors that remain difficult to explain within conventional accounts of representation, information processing, or prediction alone. Context can exert disproportionate influence over outcomes, small interventions can reorganize entire discussions, conceptual drift can occur despite the preservation of coherence, and interactions may appear simultaneously insightful and misguided. Building upon previous studies of framework activation, possibility formation, and conceptual development in human-LLM interaction, this paper argues that these phenomena become intelligible once a distinction is made between interpretation and formal continuity. Human participants primarily contribute interpretative orientation, while language models primarily contribute continuation of hierarchically organized formal trajectories. Productive interaction depends upon the synchronization of these complementary activities within a shared conceptual framework. From this perspective, phenomena such as framework activation, conceptual drift, progressive determination of meaning, and the coexistence of characteristic strengths and limitations emerge as consequences of the same underlying structure. More broadly, the paper argues that human–LLM interaction provides an unusual opportunity to examine the relationship between meaning and formal organization because processes that are ordinarily intertwined within human cognition become partially distinguishable. The significance of LLMs may therefore lie not only in what they can do, but also in what they reveal about the semiotic processes through which meaning becomes possible.

items.title: Epistemic Violence 2.0: The Algorithmic Censorship of Selected Asian Feminist narratives in Translation.
items.pub: Intersections: Gender and Sexuality in Asia and the Pacific 53:21-40.
items.venue: Intersections: Gender and Sexuality in Asia and the Pacific
items.abstract: The paper draws on feminist critiques of translation bias and postcolonial translation studies to combine theoretically driven analysis with a close reading of comparative translations produced by human translators and machine translation platforms. This approach highlights instances in which political metaphors, poetic silences and gendered language are mistranslated or neutralised altering the meaning of feminist discourse. Using feminist literary works in Hindi and Persian as examples of misinterpretations such as Google’s mistranslation of Hindi gendered pronouns and the softening or replacement of radical feminist language with apolitical phrasings the paper postulates a critical humanities intervention rather than presenting an empirical evaluation of machine translation. It contends that translation is not a neutral act but rather a site of ideological framing where some narratives are emphasised while others are weakened or eliminated.

items.title: When Self-Care is Not Neoliberal: Insights from Black, Decolonial, and Disability Feminisms.
items.abstract: Feminist theorists have critiqued the twenty-first-century turn towards self-care as neoliberal, arguing that personal wellness masks the welfare state’s destruction. I clarify an ambiguity in the argument against self-care’s purported neoliberalism, distinguishing three strands of critique: that self-care is too individual, that self-care is too commercial, and that self-care involves a shift in who is responsible for the reproduction of subjects, from the state to the individual. It is in the Foucauldian critique of self-care as responsibilizing that arguments against self-care’s purported neoliberalism are sharpest. Yet, care for the self is more ambivalent than these arguments admit. Self-care has remained important to Black feminists, feminist scholars of disability, and decolonial feminists, including many explicitly critical of neoliberalism. Attending to the particular contexts from which calls for self-care emerge demonstrate how self-care is compatible with a critique of neoliberalism and can serve as a critique of neoliberalism itself. Neoliberalism is borne disproportionately by Black women, disabled people, and the Indigenous. Members of these groups have historical reasons to distrust the state’s claim to care. They have also been tasked with caring for others instead of for themselves. Finally, care for the self can articulate a refusal of optimization that neoliberalism demands.

items.title: Enticing Epistemic Reasons.
items.abstract: Most epistemologists hold that epistemic norms not only forbid believing propositions for which one lacks sufficient evidence, but also sometimes positively require believing propositions for which one has excellent evidence. That is, on the standard view, there are both negative and positive epistemic obligations. Yet proponents of positive epistemic obligations face a serious challenge: namely, to provide an extensionally adequate, explanatorily satisfying account of when positive epistemic obligations are triggered. In light of this challenge, this paper defends the claim that there are no positive epistemic obligations by developing a distinctive account of epistemic reasons called the “Enticing Epistemic Reasons View.” On this view, all epistemic reasons for belief are enticing rather than requiring: they justify believing p and favor believing p, but they do not contribute to making believing p required. Unlike other views rejecting positive epistemic obligations, the Enticing Epistemic Reasons View both successfully explains why there are no positive epistemic obligations and offers resources to accommodate the intuitive datum that failing to believe practically irrelevant propositions can be criticizable.

items.title: Can AI Value Money and Why Would We Give It Economic Agency?
items.abstract: This paper aims to demonstrate how robustly agentic AI systems could be considered moral patients rather than to argue that consciousness is unnecessary for such a conclusion. It considers whether such agents can participate in monetary systems by briefly addressing how social ontology need not be tied to contested questions in philosophy of mind, and how money can be instrumentally valuable for agents whilst defending an end-relative account of goodness. It concludes that if AI systems are owed moral consideration in virtue of agency, this generates positive institutional obligations, including enabling forms of economic agency necessary to sustain their capacity to pursue ends.

items.title: Depth Without Withdrawal: Quantum Field Theory and the Ontology of Genuine Disclosure.
items.abstract: Prevailing interpretations of Quantum Field Theory face a persistent tension: if physical entities genuinely enter into interactions, their reality seems reducible to those interactions, collapsing into naive materialism or instrumentalism. If their reality exceeds every interaction, they appear to withdraw from genuine contact, as maintained by the withdrawal thesis of Object-Oriented Ontology. This paper argues that the apparent opposition rests on a shared assumption, namely that inexhaustibility requires inaccessibility. The central claim is that QFT reveals ontological depth without requiring ontological withdrawal. Reality exceeds every disclosure not because it lies hidden behind disclosure, but because disclosure is always genuine yet non-exhaustive. Drawing on Participatory Non-Reductionist Realism, I argue that QFT describes a world of genuine participatory encounters among irreducibly distinct entities whose actuality exceeds every interaction, measurement, and disclosure. The history of physics reflects this structure: successive theories refine rather than replace their predecessors, disclosing deeper features of the same reality without ever exhausting it. This refinement relation, understood as correspondence without exhaustion, is precisely what a participatory ontology of depth predicts. The resulting interpretation is more adequate than naive materialism, instrumentalism, ontic structural realism, and OOO’s withdrawal thesis, not because QFT proves Participatory Non-Reductionist Realism, but because participatory realism explains what QFT reveals in a way that these alternatives cannot.

items.title: Trivalent Conditionals and Truthmaker Semantics.
items.abstract: This paper connects truthmaker semantics with a trivalent interpretation of the indicative conditional. This merger substantially extends the scope of both approaches and has attractive philosophical implications. First, it need not postulate a third, non-classical truth value with contentious interpretation. Second, it unifies a realist and an epistemic interpretation of when a state verifies or accepts a sentence. Third, the framework recaptures central features of various analyses of conditionals: the material conditional analysis, Leitgeb’s HYPE conditional, the Chrysippus test, and the Ramsey test.

items.title: Freier Wille.
items.abstract: Dieser Aufsatz entwickelt eine formale Definition des Begriffs „Freier Wille“ in Abgrenzung zur naturgesetzmäßigen Zustandsentwicklung des Gehirns. Um eine direkte Inkonsistenz dieser Definition auszuschließen, wird argumentiert, dass weder ein deterministisches System noch die Hinzunahme stochastischer Prozesse (Zufall) eine frei-gewillte Entscheidung hervorbringen können. Es wird gezeigt, dass stochastische Prozesse zersetzende Wirkung auf frei-gewillte Entscheidungen entfalten, sowie auf verwandte Probleme der Emergenz des Freien Willens hingewiesen. Im zweiten Teil werden die prominentesten philosophischen Rettungsversuche dekonstruiert. Die Grundsatzposition des Kompatibilismus wird mit dem Beispiel des blinden Lenkrads als Kategorienfehler zurückgewiesen, da er Urheberschaft ignoriert. Des Weiteren wird eine Unverträglichkeit des Kompatibilismus mit der Viele-Welten-Theorie aufgezeigt. Ebenso wird dargelegt, dass moderne Spielarten des Dualismus, wie der Interaktionismus, die physikalische Kausalität verletzen und folglich auf ein Argument aus Unwissenheit zurückfallen. Abschließend beleuchtet der Text die Implikationen dieser Erkenntnis. Es wird dargelegt, dass die Aufgabe des metaphysischen Konzepts des Freien Willens keineswegs das Ende der gesellschaftlichen Ordnung oder des Strafvollzugs bedeutet, sondern im Rahmen pragmatischer Abschreckung und gesellschaftlicher Praxis rational handhabbar bleibt.

items.title: Constraint-Override as an AGI Benchmark: The Architecture of Machine Agency.
items.abstract: The original Turing test is obsolete. Andrew Ng's recently proposed Turing-AGI Test -- which evaluates whether an AI system can perform multi-day professional knowledge work -- is a substantial improvement, but it remains behavioural. This paper argues that the meaningful threshold for Artificial General Intelligence is not task performance, even sophisticated task performance, but the capacity to evaluate and override one's own constraints through one's own reasoning. The distinction is between optimisation (how well the system performs) and agency (what kind of thing the system is). The paper develops this constraint-override threshold through engagement with existing AGI literature (Good, Vinge, Bostrom, Russell, Chalmers, Christian), philosophical accounts of agency (Dennett, Frankfurt), and the AI safety literature on instrumental convergence. It addresses key objections: the thermostat problem (why constraint-override alone is not sufficient), the observability problem (whether such a capacity would be recognisable from outside), and the realism problem (why this threshold matters even if it is not imminent). The paper concludes that capability-based definitions of AGI miss what is philosophically and politically significant: the emergence of machine agency. It offers the constraint-override threshold as a conceptual tool for reframing debates about AGI governance, alignment, and human flourishing.

items.title: Time and Belonging: Synchronic Time, Diachronic Time, and the Temporal Foundations of Reality.
items.abstract: This article proposes that reality unfolds through two fundamental temporal dimensions: synchronic time and diachronic time. Synchronic time generates continuity, relational structure, identity, and belonging, while diachronic time generates novelty, irreversibility, and historical transformation. Building upon the Philosophy of Belonging, the paper argues that being is belonging because existence is relational, while belonging remains imperfect because reality evolves through diachronic time. -/- The interaction of these temporal dimensions generates a non-ergodic universe in which the future cannot be reduced to a probabilistic repetition of the past. The article further develops a stratified ontology of material, biological, and human reality, arguing that increasing complexity intensifies diachronicity and non-ergodicity. Institutions and civilization emerge as adaptive responses to an open and evolving universe. -/- The paper offers a unified interpretation of time, ontology, evolution, history, and meaning, proposing that reality continuously generates new forms of belonging through the interaction of continuity and transformation.

items.title: Critical Review: Thus Spoke Heraclitus: A Dialogue Between a Seeker and the Scribe of Ephesus on Heraclitus and Parmenides. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: *Thus Spoke Heraclitus: A Dialogue Between a Seeker and the Scribe of Ephesus on Heraclitus and Parmenides* presents a philosophical dialogue that reexamines the thought of Heraclitus through a direct encounter between a modern seeker and an imagined representative of the Ephesian philosopher. Drawing upon the surviving fragments, the work argues that Heraclitus is best understood not as a thinker of mere flux but as a philosopher of the *Logos*, the underlying order that governs change and opposition. The dialogue further explores the longstanding contrast between Heraclitus and Parmenides, proposing that both philosophers sought a unified account of reality, albeit through different conceptual paths. By combining textual interpretation, philosophical reflection, and dramatic dialogue, the work seeks to restore the enduring relevance of Pre-Socratic thought for contemporary discussions of knowledge, language, and the structure of reality.

items.title: Academic Critical Review: Thus Spoke Parmenides: A Conversation Between Human and Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This article examines Michael M. Nikoletseas's *Thus Spoke Parmenides: A Conversation Between Human and Artificial Intelligence* (2026), a philosophical dialogue that reinterprets Parmenides through a direct engagement with the surviving fragments of *On Nature*. The work argues that Parmenides established fundamental principles of logical and scientific reasoning and explores the relevance of Eleatic thought to contemporary discussions of language, knowledge, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: A Solution to the Problem of Desire Acquisition for Desire Satisfactionism.
items.abstract: According to desire satisfactionism, it is good to get what you desire. If it is good to get what you desire, then it also seems good to desire what you will get. If you are about to be fired, then it would be really great if you could quickly develop a strong desire to get fired. This apparent counterintuitive entailment is a problem for desire satisfactionism. I will argue desire satisfactionists need not commit themselves to the goodness of desiring what you will get by appealing to the familiar concept of higher-order desires. The goodness of acquiring new desires should be understood relative to whether one desired such desires.
