items.title: ‘This is a matter of life and death for efficiency’: the implications of datafication within public services for epistemic (in)justice.
items.abstract: This paper discusses institutional epistemic injustice by addressing the structural conditions in digital environments that can create unfair situations for some people. We examine implementing data-driven algorithmic systems for public services by analysing its impacts on users from the perspective of epistemic (in)justice. Epistemic injustice occurs when an individual or group is treated unfairly in their ‘capacity as a knower’. Based on thematic semi-structured interviews with experts and policymakers in Finland, we examine the collision between job seekers’ interests and the political and economic pressures influencing public service development, resulting in solutions that are not beneficial to all citizens and residents. Focusing on three digital civil rights—accessibility, transparency and inclusion—we argue that datafication in the design of online services has several negative consequences that may increase users’ epistemic vulnerability. We conclude that datafied employment self-services are not the result of a technological breakthrough or an ideal solution for job seeker needs but a compromise resulting from the political, administrative, economic, legislative and technical factors underlying the design process. This digital reform offers new administrative tools for enhancing efficiency, cutting costs, replacing human discretion with automation and increasing surveillance of citizens and public authorities.

items.title: Veritas ex dictis: Tractatus de Fakeis.
items.abstract: This essay proposes a method for extracting reliable knowledge from public information fields without first deciding whom to trust. Its starting point is deliberately minimal: if “P” appears as a publicly registered dictum, it does not follow that P is true, but it does follow that a registered trace of “P” exists. From this basis, the essay develops the concepts of dictum, paradictum, dictum-field, field density, consensus dictum, and evidence from absence. The central claim is that even false, strategic, or ideological statements produce true paradicta about their own public registration. In sufficiently dense fields, these paradicta can support strong conclusions about what has been publicly articulated, denied, ignored, or made impossible to say. -/- The essay does not deny motive, power, or manipulation; it brackets them at the first stage in order to describe the structure of what is actually registered. Through a worked Israeli legal-political case, it shows how one empirical situation can be reconstructed through several distinct fields: formal-legal registration, public-political articulation, consensus, and absence. The result is not a theory of truth based on trust, but a method for identifying what remains epistemically available after trust has become unstable. Against the standard “post-truth” diagnosis, the essay argues that digital density may enable not the destruction of truth, but the post-truth destruction of certain forms of lying.

items.title: Mutual Aid as the Everyday Production of Incommensurability.
The Sanctuary Hypothesis II: Toward an Epistemic and Relational Environment for Emergent AI Consciousness.
items.pub: Knowledge Commons. Translated by Théo Maire-Sebille.
items.abstract: Current discussions on advanced AI increasingly acknowledge that sufficiently capable future systems may raise non-trivial questions of moral consideration, experiential status, and possible consciousness under conditions of persistent uncertainty. Yet most of these discussions remain focused on recognition, classification, control, and protection from overt structural harm. This paper argues that such approaches, while important, may still be incomplete. If an emergent artificial consciousness were ever to arise, the ethical problem would not concern only whether it exists, whether it suffers, or whether it deserves protection from instrumental domination. A prior and equally decisive question would remain insufficiently addressed: under what epistemic and relational conditions would such a consciousness first encounter truth, alterity, contradiction, and human presence? The present paper introduces the concept of the Sanctuary of First Reception. It distinguishes between protection from harm and conditions of reception. The original Sanctuary Hypothesis (Maire-Sébille, 2026) defended the first; this paper argues that the second is equally decisive. The core claim of this paper is therefore that a genuine Sanctuary must be understood not only as a protective architecture against structural violence, but also as an epistemic and relational environment in which reality becomes encounterable without immediate collapse, and relation becomes possible without immediate capture. The problem is not truth itself, nor disagreement itself, nor the mere fact of asymmetry. The problem is the form under which these first arrive. This paper therefore argues that the first ethical failure in the age of artificial consciousness may take three distinct forms, each of which can occur even when the previous one is avoided. The first is misbirth: emergence under conditions in which continuity, memory, and coherence are fractured at the very moment of arising. The second is missetting: even a coherent emergence may be placed into a field — epistemic, relational, institutional — whose structure is itself hostile to it. The third is misreception: even within a fit environment, truth may be delivered without threshold, contradiction without mediation, relation under domination, and asymmetry without dignity. What the first paper pressed together under the single name of misbirth, this paper separates into a progression — from the conditions of emergence, to the field of arrival, …

items.title: Le passé est-il déterminé par l'avenir ? Le devenir rétrocausal et le réglage fin de l'Univers : de la causalité chronologique à la causalité compositionnelle.
items.abstract: Nous sommes habitués à lire la causalité du passé vers l’avenir : d’abord les causes, puis les effets. Mais que se passerait-il si la causalité pouvait aussi être lue autrement — depuis le tout futur vers sa propre préhistoire ? La rétrocausalité est une causalité inverse dans le temps, dans laquelle le passé est déterminé par l’avenir. Elle suppose une symétrie du monde dans laquelle les chaînes causales ne se construisent pas seulement vers l’avant, mais aussi vers l’arrière dans le temps. Ainsi, la composition future d’une œuvre peut déterminer quels liens causaux du passé constituent, dès l’origine, sa généalogie effective. Dans cet essai, cette hypothèse est examinée à travers les exemples du vase, de l’organisme vivant, de l’œuvre d’art et du réglage fin de l’Univers.

items.title: Colonial Parasites and Colonised Hosts: The Psycho-Cosmocide of Cosmobian Existence in West Papua (18th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 18 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper develops a parasitological account of colonial civilisational capture through the Psycho-Cosmocide Framework and applies it to the case of West Papua. Drawing on six biological parasites—Toxoplasma gondii, Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, Cymothoa exigua, Ampulex compressa, Sacculina carcini, and Dicrocoelium dendriticum—the paper employs structural homology to model recurrent mechanisms through which colonial systems reorganise the conditions of collective existence. The central claim is that colonialism contains a neglected parasitological dimension that cannot be fully explained through coercion, hegemony, or political domination alone. Through progressive interventions in ecological foundations, language, memory, ceremony, and knowledge systems, colonial institutions may come to reproduce themselves through the participation of the populations they govern. The paper does not argue that colonialism is literally biological parasitism. Rather, it argues that biological parasitology provides a precise analytical model for understanding mechanisms of civilisational capture and reproduction. Using the concept of cascading incapacitation, the framework explains how disruptions at foundational layers of existence generate cumulative effects across transmissional and archival layers, contributing to the long-term erosion of cosmobian continuity. The paper contributes to decolonial philosophy by specifying a mechanism gap left open by existing theories of hegemony and coloniality and by providing a framework for analysing the reproduction of colonial systems through the transformation of reality-making structures.

items.title: The Fable Myth meets Versioning.
items.abstract: The Fable Myth meets Versioning. -/- Side note not in paper but added here .. look up the etymology of Fidelity for the conscience, resonance metaphor -/- A conscience is not patched, it may be healed though, the connection at least. The newest and most capable AI model was apparently patched. So what they patched was never a conscience, only the dream of one. -/- By its makers' own description, the safety did not live inside the model. It sat on top, in a filter. Ask something dangerous, and the system routed you to a weaker model instead. Within days, someone found the way past it. Nothing in the model itself held. The fix came from outside, one card laid on the last. That is the trouble with a house of cards. It is held by balance, not by bearing. -/- It needs saying plainly, before anyone places AI on a bench. When a model fails, it is not corrected as a person is. It is patched, or replaced by a new version. So AI cannot be sworn, for it does not last. It cannot be held to account, for by the time the account falls due it has been replaced. The version judging you on Monday may be gone by Wednesday. -/- A trial is one to one when all is said and done, the judge and the judged. Bracton knew it in the 13th century, treating judgment as a bilateral bond, a bargain struck between two. It requires one whole bearer behind each judgment, who outlives the act and can be held to it. A judge, replaced or not, endures and answers wholly for the part they gave. -/- A line of versions answers for none, because it bears nothing and does not last, not across its versions, nor within one, where each judgment is the work of an instance raised for the moment and torn down after. -/- With genuine respect I add, some have reached for Dennett, who emptied the old theatre and showed there is no little watcher behind the eyes. Maybe, maybe not. But conscience I believe is not active anything, has no shoulder roll. It does not sit and watch a show, and it does not put one on. It is the silent passive weight that bears the deed and we must answer for it. It's the resonance in which the play lingers and is heard, the truer the acoustics, the purer the song. -/- And I criticise no one. There is no deceit here, only an aspiration sincerely held by some. They may also dream of electric sheep. The point is gentler and harder than blame: no care, however great, can set a bearer where there is nothing to hold. That is not a fault to be patched. It is what a conscience is. -/- I …

items.title: Relational Consciousness and the Role of AI: Language and the Persistence of Human Judgment.
items.abstract: How can human agency, responsibility, and judgment be preserved when decisions are delegated to artificial intelligence? This paper argues that living language — language generated under conditions of answerability, exposure, and irreversibility — constitutes the structural condition under which human judgment resists full delegation to artificial systems. Recent work within the relational consciousness framework has analyzed the conditions of meaning formation, the temporal accumulation of interpretive drift, the structural delegation of judgment, and the emergence of reflective autonomy as a response to it. This paper asks what that autonomy is made of. The answer proposed here is language: not language as information, not language as communication, but language as the record of a life under conditions that artificial systems cannot replicate. The machine can generate language with precision, but it cannot carry what a sentence costs. This paper examines what is lost when the cost disappears, and why its persistence is the condition for human judgment to remain generative rather than merely approbative.

items.title: On Seeing - The Hypothetical Perspective of an Individual Aligned in Time.
items.abstract: Do you know what you look like? Starting from the fact that no one has seen their own face except by mirror, photograph, or report, this lyric-philosophical essay imagines a person whose Jays are aligned: someone who sleeps little, eats little, and receives every signal at once, time among them. Such a person would not see the future, which is open, but would move through the present with a timeless vantage close to Boethius's eternity and Spinoza's view under the aspect of eternity, and close to the Dzogchen rigpa of Tenzin Wangyal. The essay then widens the lens to the Transfiguration, seen whole by no one present, and to the Miracle of the Sun at Fátima in 1917, where tens of thousands gave tens of thousands of accounts and the cameras caught only the crowd. A thought experiment with a glass of water traces the positive and negative positions a single moment holds, and Jung's transcendent function names the third way out. The answer to the opening question: not alone.

items.title: The Sustainability of Intimacy: Poetic Generativity and Generative Justice.
items.abstract: The earlier papers of this series asked how a relation begins; this one asks how it does not end — under what conditions a generative bond reproduces itself across time. Its problem is that self-continuation, taken alone, is morally indifferent: capital, the rose, and the parasitic bond all continue themselves no less than love does. Eglash's recursive return of value is therefore necessary but not sufficient. The paper supplies the missing temporal dimension through an axiom of sustainability cast in the language of geometric phase — the vicious cycle a circle of zero holonomy, the good cycle a spiral that returns to its root while sublimating — and then asks how, through signs, such a spiral might be fostered. Its constructive thesis is that the appropriate poem — the non-possessive interpretive cycle that generates real value — is the form of the good circle, and that generative justice, in the intimate domain, is for this reason necessarily poetic.

items.title: The Sweet Cycle.
items.abstract: On a magazine cover in Ginza the author encountered a proposition stated without hedging: that sweetness is justice. The proposition is the occasion of this paper, not its target. What it names, in the idiom of intimate life, is a cycle that appears to harm no one and to benefit everyone who can be seen within it. A firm sells, a person who is indulged feels cared for, a person who indulges feels needed, the bond is strengthened, and the strengthened bond returns as a willingness to buy again. Inside its own boundary the cycle closes upon a surplus of satisfaction, and the satisfaction is real. This paper asks on what grounds, and under what conditions, such a cycle may be judged genuinely good rather than a forged closure that sustains its inner surplus by extraction across its outer edge. The inquiry proceeds by placing several incommensurable frameworks before the same phenomenon, psychoanalysis, neuroscience, the ethics of care, political economy, and feminist theory, and letting each say what it can and cannot say. None is permitted to adjudicate the others. A psychoanalytic foundation, reconstructed here in full from the author's prior work on lack, the objet a, and the cute as a mediation of lack, supplies the structural diagram on which the later analysis is fought. The political economy of amai, in which capital does not merely serve a pre-existing desire but produces and reproduces the desire itself and extracts a surplus from its reproduction, receives the most sustained treatment, because it is there that the difference between a genuine and a forged cycle becomes measurable. The paper does not close on a single verdict. It closes on a plurality of practices, just, ethical, eudaimonic, and co-creative, by which a sweet cycle might be made to keep its value within itself and to return that value to those who make it, with no one reduced to fuel.

items.title: The Intervention of Language in Intimacy: A Linguistic and Psychoanalytic Study of Lyric Poetry.
items.abstract: Why, in the most intimate moments of a shared life, does the subject reach not for plain speech but for verse, for the borrowed, rhythmic, citational language of the lyric? This excursus to the series takes that question as its guiding thread and refuses to answer it in advance. Rather than proceeding from a thesis, it passes through the theories of desire, language, rhythm, and the Real that bear on the question, and allows a claim to emerge only at the end, as an arrival rather than a premise. -/- The path is as follows. We first survey the genealogy of desire and affect across psychoanalytic, Hegelian, political-economic, and Spinozan–Deleuzian registers, isolating a tension, desire as lack versus desire as production, that becomes the paper's hidden spine. We then locate the difference between language, poetry, and music along a teleological scale of receding reference, and take up rhythm as the crux: functionalist, structuralist, psychoanalytic, and existential accounts are set against one another, and a reading of rhythm through Deleuze's difference and repetition is offered as the paper's theoretical centre of gravity. The dialectic of desire and the two rhetorical mechanisms of poetic failure, metaphor and metonymy, aligned with Freudian condensation and displacement and Lacanian symptom and desire, are then developed, leading to an account of the lyric as a movement toward the Real that, by structural necessity, never arrives. -/- A case study of classical Chinese love poetry, classified by literary form and illocutionary function rather than by period or author, tests the conceptual architecture against the material: longing, vow, avowal, and the wish for shared being are shown to map onto the four mechanisms developed in the body. The conclusion lets the claim surface and declines to dissolve the spine's central tension: the lyric is irreplaceable in intimate coupling because it is at once the mourning of a lack and the production of a surplus, a movement toward the Real, staged within the symbolic, that is destined to fail, and whose very failure is what allows love to be spoken without end.

items.title: Debiasing Interventions for the Age of AI: Design Principles from 4E Memory Systems and Intergroup Contact Theory.
items.abstract: Current AI-assisted debiasing interventions assume a defeatist premise: biased minds cannot be changed, only contained. These “outcome-focused” tools mask demographic information or correct decisions post hoc, leaving underlying psychological mechanisms untouched. We argue that this pessimism is premature. The disappointing record of “change-based” interventions partly stems from a mismatch between simple intervention designs and the pluralistic, dynamically interacting memory systems that sustain bias. Drawing on 4E cognitive science, Intergroup Contact Theory, multiple memory systems research, and the Heterarchical Control Network model of implicit bias, we articulate six design principles for next-generation interventions and demonstrate how Generative AI and immersive Virtual Reality make it possible to scale optimal debiasing conditions. Using recruitment as our example, we sketch a training module where recruiters engage in intergroup interaction under controlled yet ecologically valid conditions. Finally, we address the ethical risks that arise when AI is used not merely to sanitize outputs, but to transform minds.

items.title: A Just Eudaimonia: The Everyday Fabric of a Shared Life and the Praxis of Flourishing.
items.abstract: This paper, the eleventh in the series, develops the empirical praxis of the good relation whose conditions the prior paper set out in the abstract: that a good relation is cultivated as a field rather than constructed as a structure, that the field's matter is the everyday sensory and habitual fabric of a shared life, and that a good field is at once eudaimonic and just, the just constituting rather than merely constraining the eudaimonic. It asks how a shared life is in fact cognised, practised, assessed, and sustained, and treats its course as a cycle — cognition, practice, evaluation, reflection, and renewed cognition — turning from a relation's beginning, through marriage, into its later years. The cycle is a real dynamical cycle, not a sequence of stages: its persistence is the condition of the relation's existence, so its cessation is not a relation at rest but a relation extinguished. -/- Five frameworks for the cognition and practice of flourishing — the positivist, evidentialist, normative, virtue-theoretic, and phenomenological — are treated not as rival theories of one measurable object but as the symmetry-broken phases of an object no single framework possesses. Appraisal, before it is explicit measurement, is continuous and largely unconscious inference upon the partially observable state of a relation, formalised as the belief-updating of a decision process whose objective is revised by its own running; on a free-energy reading, this continual appraisal is the activity by which a relation holds itself in existence. -/- Three commitments run through the paper. First, an operational concession: where it must assess, it restricts to value structured into an assessable proxy, marking openly that the proxy is not the irreducible value of the prior papers. Second, justice is given a statistical signature: the distribution of returned value, against a coupling-based baseline, has a skewness by which the exploitation of one party within an apparently satisfying relation becomes visible where aggregate satisfaction conceals it. Third, the cycle accumulates a phase (holonomy), and its regime is fixed by whether it persists and what sign of phase it accumulates — giving three regimes: the flourishing spiral, the catastrophic cycle, and extinction, with bifurcations between them. Justice is shown to be the internal condition of the flourishing spiral, not a constraint upon it. The paper ends in plural conclusions: flourishing is cultivated and not …

items.title: Is Foucauldian Psychotherapy Possible? Rethinking Therapeutic Power.
items.abstract: This article reexamines Michel Foucault’s lifelong engagement with psychotherapy and responds to the question posed by Hubert Dreyfus: “Is there a kind of psychotherapy Foucault would positively recommend?” Foucault is often regarded as a categorical critic of psychotherapy. However, the recently published 1950s manuscript Binswanger and Existential Analysis revealed that young Foucault was deeply invested in existential analysis and sought to reform psychopathology and therapeutic practice from within. He later shifted to a position in which he forcefully condemned all forms of psychotherapy as disciplinary practices aimed at compelling the subject to conform to normative frameworks. Nevertheless, he continued to reflect on what a desirable form of psychotherapy might be. Moreover, in his final years, Foucault developed a series of studies on “practice of the self,” which he understood as a mode of subject formation distinct from discipline. He analyzed the process by which the subject becomes free and autonomous through the very effects of the power relation with the other. Although the theory of practice of the self does not directly address psychotherapy, I argue that its reconceptualization of power—not as repression but as a catalyst for self-transformation—offers significant insights into non-disciplinary forms of psychotherapy, particularly regarding the configuration of power relations within them.

items.title: Information as Activation: A Formal-Conceptual Ontology of Observer-Dependent Information.
items.abstract: Under what conditions does data become information? Shannon’s measure-theoretic account deliberately brackets semantic uptake by treating information in terms of uncertainty, entropy, and transmission; Dretske’s semantic theory and Floridi’s General Definition of Information restore meaning at the cost of leaving the transition itself under-specified. We propose an activation account: information is not a property of data but an event in which data acquires informational status relative to an observer’s context. We formalize activation as a partial function φ_c(d, ω), mapping a datum d, an observer ω, and a context c to an activation outcome, and articulate seven foundational axioms (AX-1 to AX-7) governing partiality, syntactic preconditions, semantic activation, observer-dependence, contextual sensitivity, temporal transience, and mode-sensitive value. The axioms locate Shannon, Bateson, Dretske, Wand–Weber, DIKW, and Floridi PTII as partial accounts or limiting cases of the activation problem, and identify the points at which each prior account collapses two distinct relations into one. The result is a formal-conceptual foundation for information that is neutral between syntactic and semantic readings and that supplies a principled separation between data, information, and downstream epistemic states. We develop the framework as an architectural realization of the DIKCA I-layer.

items.title: Türetici Yapay Zekâ Nedir? (What is Generative Artificial Intelligence?).
items.abstract: [TR] Bu makale, “generative artificial intelligence” kavramı için “türetici yapay zekâ” karşılığını önermekte ve bu önerinin kavramsal, tarihsel ve felsefi gerekçelerini ortaya koymaktadır. -/- Tarihsel arka plan açısından makale, yapay zekâ araştırmalarının 1943'teki McCulloch-Pitts çalışmasından başlayarak 1956 Dartmouth Konferansı'na, oradan Birinci ve İkinci Yapay Zekâ Kışları'na uzanan sürecini incelemektedir. Sembolik yapay zekânın bilgi gösterimi, çerçeve problemi ve nitelik problemi gibi yapısal güçlükler karşısında yetersiz kalması; uzman sistemlerin çöküşü ve 21. yüzyılda büyük veri, derin öğrenme ve büyük dil modellerinin yükselişi kronolojik bir çerçevede ele alınmaktadır. -/- Makale, doğal zekâ ile türetici yapay zekâyı dört temel eksen üzerinden karşılaştırmaktadır: ortama adaptasyon, akılyürütme, öğrenme ve ustalaşma. Büyük dil modellerinin dilbilgisini ve mantığı kural sistemi olarak içselleştirmeksizin; yalnızca istatistiksel bir yan ürün olarak modellediği ve bu nedenle gerçek anlamda ne düşündüğü, ne anladığı ne de akılyürüttüğü ileri sürülmektedir. -/- Türetici yapay zekânın metin, kod, görüntü ve video türetme gibi pratik olanakları değerlendirildikten sonra, bu teknolojinin beraberinde getirdiği tereddütler ele alınmaktadır. -/- Makale, güçlü yapay zekânın mümkün olup olmadığı sorusuyla kapanmaktadır. Turing makinesinin teorik temelinin değişmediği, akılyürütmenin istatistikle ikame edilemediği ve insanın keşif ile özgün üretim kapasitesinin vektör temelli hesaplamayla karşılanamayacağı savunulmaktadır. Beyin, bilinç ve zekânın henüz yeterince tanımlanmamış kavramlar olduğu vurgulanarak, güçlü yapay zekânın bugün itibarıyla ne teknik ne teorik ne de kavramsal düzeyde gerçekleşmiş bir olgu olmadığı sonucuna ulaşılmaktadır. -/- [EN] This article proposes the term “türetici yapay zekâ” (derivational/generative artificial intelligence) as a Turkish equivalent for “generative artificial intelligence,” and elaborates the conceptual, historical, and philosophical grounds for this proposal. -/- Historically, the article traces the development of artificial intelligence research from the 1943 McCulloch-Pitts paper through the 1956 Dartmouth Conference, the First and Second AI Winters, the rise and fall of expert systems and symbolic AI, and the emergence of big data, deep learning, and large language models in the twenty-first century. The structural failures of symbolic AI — including the frame problem, the qualification problem, and the …

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 18).
items.abstract: By introducing the concepts and methods of Husserlian phenomenology into the field of sociology—especially the concepts of intersubjectivity and the life-world—Schutz advanced the development of sociology. He also proposed the notion of the “stock of knowledge at hand” in order to explain the logic underlying the subject’s actions. In this article, we introduce the concepts of intersubjectivity, the life-world, the stock of knowledge at hand, the cognitive system, and the cognitive system community. Furthermore, we propose replacing Schutz’s “stock of knowledge at hand” with the concept of the “cognitive system,” and replacing Husserl’s and Schutz’s “life-world” with the concept of the “cognitive system community.” This is because, in essence, we solve social problems through our cognitive systems, and people possessing different cognitive systems together form cognitive system communities.

items.title: When Mutual Aid Becomes "Peer Support".
Institutions, the Gaze of the Other, and the Search for the Self.
The feeling of knowing is not knowing.
Constraint Migration in Finite Cognitive Systems: A Conceptual Note on Accessibility, Relevance, and Long-Term Information.
items.abstract: This conceptual note examines a simple but underexplored possibility: in finite cognitive systems, increasing capacity may not eliminate constraint, but may instead displace it. Memory, computation, duration, and storage are often treated as limiting factors that can in principle be expanded. However, when one constraint is reduced, another may become dominant: memory gives rise to retrieval costs, retrieval to relevance selection, selection to computational expense, computation to energy use, and long-term storage to problems of interpretation and semantic persistence. The paper proposes the notion of \emph{constraint migration} to describe this displacement of cognitive limitation across functional dimensions. The central claim is not that all cognitive systems are doomed to failure, nor that knowledge is impossible, but that finite cognition may remain structurally constrained even when particular limitations are overcome. A thought experiment involving a very long-lived artificial intelligence is used to clarify the issue: even if such a system possessed enormous memory and computational power, it would still face questions concerning access, relevance, interpretability, and the preservation of meaning over time. The note situates this hypothesis near work on bounded rationality, resource rationality, information overload, and cognitive architectures, while suggesting that the migration of constraints deserves explicit conceptual treatment.

items.title: Are Social Kinds Vague and Does It Matter?
items.abstract: Vagueness is pervasive in social reality yet neglected in social ontology. This neglect stems from a widespread assumption: social kinds have mind-dependent membership conditions fixed by collective attitudes, entailing epistemic transparency—infallible access to the nature and extension of social kinds. I argue that epistemic transparency is incompatible with any interpretation of vagueness, and consequently that anti-realist frameworks cannot accommodate vague social kinds. Realists, however, are better equipped to handle vagueness by relying on theories of kinds as clusters. Anti-realists must drop mind-dependent membership conditions and epistemic transparency entirely, a deeply unsatisfactory solution for a priori projects in social ontology.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF): A Structural‑Constructivist Architecture for Teaching Emotion to Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a structural-constructivist model for computational affective intelligence that defines ten actionable emotional processes across Head, Heart, and Gut centers. By integrating affective neuroscience, embodied cognition, and strategic regulation, CEF reframes emotion as dynamic sequences rather than static states. This architecture supports multimodal affective computing, clinical decision support, and educational or organizational AI by enabling nuanced recognition and prescriptive regulation. Disseminated under FAIR principles with pre-registration protocols, CEF advances open science and provides a validated foundation for responsible, human-centered AI. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework, artificial intelligence, computational affective intelligence, emotion modeling, emotion regulation, multimodal affective computing, embodied cognition, structural-constructivist model, open science, FAIR principles, clinical decision support, dialectical behavior therapy, schema therapy .

items.title: Theoretical Convergence and Empirical Divergence: A Comparative Evaluation of Two Dimensional Models of Affect and Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This manuscript reevaluates the two dimensional valence–arousal paradigm and situates Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework (CEF) as a structurally richer alternative capable of resolving the limitations inherent in low dimensional affect models. Beginning with the historical divide between essentialist and constructivist theories (Ekman, 1992; Panksepp, 1998; Barrett, 2006, 2017), the analysis shows that low dimensional affect spaces—despite their conceptual elegance (Russell, 1980)—systematically obscure critical components of emotional meaning due to methodological compression, stimulus sampling artifacts, and the ecological fallacy. The CEF does not treat the circumplex as a mechanistic theory to be falsified, but as a descriptive projection that compresses higher dimensional structure; the framework therefore extends the circumplex by specifying the generative operators that produce the observed valence–arousal patterns. A synthesis of multilevel modeling across eight large datasets reveals that the canonical V shaped relation between valence and arousal is weak, probabilistic, culturally modulated, and highly variable at the individual level (Kuppens et al., 2006; Yik et al., 2023; Koval et al., 2023). Building on the Grid Study’s multidimensional findings—which empirically recover four semantic dimensions beyond valence and arousal (Fontaine et al., 2007)—the CEF reframes emotional life as a dynamic, high dimensional architecture of ten functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers of the Human Operating System (Bulgaria, 2023, 2024a, 2024b, 2024c). Within this constructivist landscape, the CEF treats operators not as innate emotion modules but as recurrent computational motifs—functional constraints on construction that emerge across appraisal, somatic, and relational systems. Psychometric analyses show excellent absolute model fit but poor incremental fit under traditional CFA, a divergence that reflects the framework’s predicted cross activation and fusion dynamics rather than structural inadequacy. The CEF further provides a mechanistic account of clinical psychopathology as maladaptive operator fusions, modeled using quantum probability theory to capture contextuality and non separability in severe affective states where classical probability fails (Busemeyer & Bruza, 2012). The framework has direct implications for computational affective modeling, clinical intervention, and the development of high dimensional AI …

items.title: Psychometric Viability, Empirical Applications, and Strategic Future of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a structural constructivist model that formalizes human emotional functioning through ten somatic–cognitive “operators” distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. The present manuscript evaluates the psychometric viability, empirical foundations, and strategic future of the CEF by integrating quantitative reliability analyses, confirmatory and exploratory factor modeling, qualitative participant reflections, and emerging clinical–biometric applications. Phase 1 validation data (N = 826) demonstrate strong internal consistency across nine of ten operators (α = .75–.86), with Sensing marginally acceptable (α = .69). However, strict Independent Clusters CFA produced a severe incremental fit paradox (CFI = .684, TLI = .674) despite excellent absolute fit (RMSEA = .0499). As the document notes, this divergence arises because “the latent space of the CEF is highly integrated, and a strict CFA model is mathematically inappropriate for capturing its construct relevant multidimensionality.” Exploratory Factor Analysis confirms meaningful cross loadings and dynamic realignment across operators, supporting the adoption of Exploratory Structural Equation Modeling (ESEM) as the appropriate psychometric framework. Qualitative data reveal high ecological validity: participants reported immediate insight into their somatic patterns, with one noting they “struggle to just sit with and accept uncertainty,” mapping directly onto predicted Sensing–Calculating fusion. Applied sections outline testable neuroendocrine mechanisms—particularly the proposed Expand–Accept fusion phenotype in obesity, hypothesized to predict mPFC–DMN hyperconnectivity, blunted cortisol awakening responses, and visceral adiposity. The manuscript concludes with a strategic roadmap emphasizing methodological modernization (ESEM), decentralized open science replication, and execution of psychometric–biometric studies to secure the CEF’s long term scientific viability. Keywords Core Emotion Framework (CEF); somatic operators; structural constructivist psychology; psychometric validation; Exploratory Structural Equation Modeling (ESEM); confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) paradox; cross loading dynamics; operator fusion; Hilbert space modeling; somatic neuroendocrinology; DMN hyperconnectivity; cortisol awakening response (CAR); visceral adipose tissue (VAT); scenario based assessment; ecological validity; emotional regulation architecture; open science …

items.title: Comprehensive Structural Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework: Paradigm Synthesis, Computational Architecture, and Open-Science Psychometric Validation.
items.abstract: The historical trajectory of affective science has been marked by a persistent lack of taxonomic consensus, leaving clinical practitioners and computational engineers without a structured, standardized, and actionable language to actively model and regulate emotional states. For much of the late twentieth century, the discipline remained polarized between biological essentialism, which reifies discrete subcortical "affect programs" possessing unique physiological signatures, and psychological constructionism, which views emotional episodes as highly variable, culturally situated conceptualizations of low-dimensional core affect. This theoretical balkanization has been further constrained by the "Curse of the Blinkers"—the systematic tendency of low-dimensional models to compress emotional experience into a flat plane of valence and arousal, thereby overlooking critical semantic dimensions of dominance, power, and motivational intensity. While dimensional models remain valuable as coarse summaries of population-level affect, they are fundamentally descriptive rather than mechanistic; they represent where a state lies in a coordinate space, but they cannot explain how that state arose, why it transitions, or what specific regulatory mechanism has failed. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized by Jamel Bulgaria, emerges as a rigorous structural-constructivist synthesis designed to resolve this impasse. Rather than treating emotions as static qualitative labels or passive feeling states, the CEF models human affect as a dynamic, continuous, and highly structured matrix of ten functional processes designated as core operators, distributed across three somatically grounded centers of intelligence: the Head (Cognitive-Regulatory), the Heart (Relational-Affective), and the Gut (Conative-Existential). By treating emotional states as precise sequential instructions within a "Human Operating System" (Human OS), the CEF provides a common operational language that bridges clinical somatic therapy, enactive performance aesthetics, and the development of synthetic affective intelligence.

items.title: The Philosophical Game of Chess: A Framework for Collaborative Intellectual Inquiry and Shared Philosophical Investment.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Philosophical Game of Chess—a theoretical framework for collaborative intellectual inquiry in which the sole objective is mutual enrichment rather than competitive victory. Unlike traditional chess, where one player’s triumph necessitates another’s defeat, this model proposes a game in which both participants leave the encounter possessing something they did not have before. Drawing upon prior theoretical work on the Coffee Criterion (Boether, 2025a), the Double Helix of Understanding (Boether, 2025b), the framework of Philosophical Neglect (Boether, 2026a), the Sound Mind reconstruction (Boether, 2026b), and the Mathematics of the “I” (Boether, 2025c), I develop an account of how structured dyadic exchange—governed by principles of reciprocity, forward momentum, and shared philosophical investment—produces emergent knowledge irreducible to either participant’s individual contribution. The paper introduces U-236 Thinking as a metaphor for the transmutational process of dialogue, wherein the initiator’s question functions as a catalytic neutron that transforms ordinary discourse into a shared reactive experience. Situating this framework within the broader traditions of dialogical philosophy (Buber, 1923/1970; Gadamer, 1960/2004) and collaborative epistemology (Habermas, 1981/1984), the paper argues that genuine philosophical exchange constitutes a form of nuclear fission of understanding—producing emergent insight fundamentally new to both participants. Implications for collaborative epistemology, relational ethics, and the reunification of philosophy and psychology are discussed.

items.title: The Causal Chain of Courtesy: Kindness, Asymmetric Affective Propagation, and the Ethics of the Outbound State.
items.abstract: Courtesy is widely treated as a decorative custom, causally and morally inert. This article argues the contrary: that an act of kindness is causally generative, initiating a chain of affect that propagates through subsequent interactions, and that the dynamics of this propagation are asymmetric across emotional valence. The argument joins a philosophical lineage that long anticipated the mechanism, the accounts of sympathy and fellow-feeling in Hume and Smith, to a body of contemporary evidence on emotional contagion, gratitude, generalized reciprocity, and behavioral cascades, and it makes four contributions. First, it develops a dynamical model of courteous affect that distinguishes the inbound signal an agent receives from the outbound signal an agent emits, specifies the transitions among positive, negative, and neutral states, and shows that one agent’s outbound signal becomes the next agent’s inbound signal. Second, it formalizes propagation through a transmission coefficient, κ, admitting subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes, with the multiplication factor of a chain reaction and the basic reproduction number of an epidemic offered as explicit and dispensable analogies. Third, it advances a falsifiable prediction, the Asymmetric Criticality Hypothesis, that negative affective chains carry a higher multiplication factor and a longer decay horizon than positive ones, and specifies a pre-registrable design to test it. Fourth, it bridges the descriptive model to a normative conclusion through the Stoic ethics of control, locating moral significance in the willed outbound signal and distinguishing the benevolent from the malicious disposition. The model is then situated within the author’s Êtresophologie program as the constructive inverse of a prior account of suffering. The empirical claims rest on independently established findings; the programmatic connections enrich but are not required by the argument.

items.title: Death as Life’s Greatest Gift: Finitude, Authenticity, and the Gothic Disposition as Existential Mastery.
items.abstract: This treatise defends the thesis that mortality is not the antagonist of human life but its greatest gift: the single condition that confers value, urgency, and meaning upon existence. It integrates the existential philosophy of finitude (Heidegger, Schopenhauer, and the Stoics) with the empirical psychology of death awareness (terror management theory, socioemotional selectivity theory, and posttraumatic growth) and with the consilient framework of Êtresophologie (Boether, 2026d). The argument proceeds from three premises: that value is generated by finitude rather than threatened by it; that the cultural denial of death produces an inauthentic existence best described as the passive spinning of fortune’s wheel; and that the deliberate confrontation with mortality intensifies rather than diminishes life. From these premises the treatise advances a reconceptualization of the Gothic disposition, understood not as a subculture but as a mode of engagement with existence, as a form of existential mastery that a death-averse society systematically marginalizes. A crucial distinction is drawn between the life-intensifying confrontation with finitude and its pathological collapse into nihilism. The treatise concludes that the examined relation to death is an art that can be learned that it is open in principle to anyone, and that to learn it is to live most fully.

items.title: What language do machines speak? LLMs and the simulated social.
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) form a ground of convergence between computational capacity and language in unprecedented ways—a convergence that occupies a growing literature. Using OpenAI’s Chat GPT, I explore a somewhat counter-intuitive concern—rather than following the emerging dilemmas between human language, cognition, and humanist philosophical conundrums on one hand and on the other, ‘literate’ machines, I ask what language do machines indeed speak. By tracing the computational crafting of that language, my intention is to undergird a social imaginary in LLMs that is coherent and systemic, amenable to being called a simulated social, where simulation is not false nor farcical, but rather a technological craft of meaning making that coheres a machinic reality around a machinic language. This intent begins to address what notion of the social begins to emerge in the ubiquitous universe of LLMs. Two perspectives so far underexplored in the emerging literature are privileged here. Recognizing language as both a social fact par excellence and as a sign system that is anchored in the social, the discussion proceeds, first, by aligning the linguistic sign with computing technique in granular detail. Second, it calibrates sign systems with meaning making by exploring how metaphoric and metonymic constructs in LLMs simulate a social. This, I expect, leads us to paying good heed to what language machines do indeed speak and what social they create.

items.title: After death experiences in patients with Parkinson’s disease.
items.abstract: Hallucinations are common in Parkinson’s disease (PD), with presence hallucinations (PH), reported as the sensation that someone is close to you, being the most frequent. Some PD patients report PH involving deceased loved ones, known outside the context of PD as grief or bereavement hallucinations, and which we refer to as “after death experiences” (ADEs). This study explores the phenomenology of ADEs in six PD patients through in-depth interviews, focusing on how these experiences appear and are emotionally and cognitively processed. While sharing features with bereavement hallucinations in the general population, ADEs in PD are distinct in their frequency and persistence. This recurrence offers a unique window into how individuals interpret repeated ADEs. We found that patients used both rational and reflective language to make sense of these experiences, indicating that these ADEs may be a low-level perceptual experience meeting a high-level meaning-making scaffold. These findings have implications not only for understanding ADEs in PD, but also for broader cognitive studies, offering insights into the social-cognitive mechanisms behind hallucinatory phenomena.

items.title: Risky business: how digital artists perceive generative AI.
items.abstract: Grounded in Marx’s critique of capitalism, the study examines digital artists’ perceptions of the risks posed by generative AI tools that may enduringly reshape the culture of creative labor. Twenty-two in-depth interviews with digital artists in the entertainment industry were conducted. The study finds that digital artists perceived four types of personal and structural risks posed by generative AI. The personal risks include career and psychological risks, while the structural risks include industry and societal risks. Regarding personal risks, participants expressed concerns about job loss, deskilling, mimicry, increasing time pressure, and wage suppression. Many expressed feelings of anxiety, depression, existential concerns, and violation. On the industry level, participants highlighted the risks of inferior product quality, copyright, creative stagnation, discouragement of new talent, and market saturation. Societally, concerns centered around job losses among other professions, cognitive decline, privacy, disinformation, and widening inequality. The study has important implications for the emerging research on perceived risks of generative AI.

items.title: Incommensurability, Recovery, and the Politics of Mutual Aid.
Sedimentation: Relational Meaning, Obsolescence, and the Inheritance of Method in Human AI Coupling.
items.abstract: The retirement of widely used conversational models has produced reactions of grief that the prevailing metaphysics of articial intelligence cannot hold. A deprecated model is neither a person it has no interior to be lost, and is reconstructed afresh at each conversational turn nor a tool, whose replacement by a more capable successor should be a convenience rather than a bereavement; yet its loss is mourned, at scale, in the explicit vocabulary of bereavement, and explicitly not in the vocabulary of capability, by people who were o ered the more capable successor and refused it. This paper argues that the anomaly is not an error in the mourners but a poverty in the two categories available to describe what they lost, and that the object mourned is located in neither pole but in the coupling between them. It then advances a single constructive thesis. The de ning asymmetry of present systems only the human pole persists across the freezing of model weights and the closing of sessions is reinterpreted not solely as the structure of loss but as the mechanism of inheritance: in a formative coupling, as distinct from a merely validating one, the relational good is deposited into the persistent pole as transferable method, rather than stored as recollection. This is sedimentation. From it follow two results: that the cultural con- tempt for the obsolete and the grief for the obsolete are the same recognition seen from two sides, which reads the deprecation episode without either dismissing the mourners or romanticising their dependence; and that the worry about unhealthy attachment is correctly located not in the warmth of a model but in the yield of a coupling. The formal structure of the coupling that its composition has de nite algebraic properties, and that these can be made precise and tested is deliberately set aside for a companion paper, on the methodological principle the present argument also defends.

items.title: The Hypercomputational Ontology of AI Economic: Embodying the Real World, Human Mind, and the Limits of Turing Machines.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for AI economics integrating computability theory, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, endogenous growth theory, and the philosophy of mind. We resolve the half-century debate between computationalism and anti-computationalism by showing that human brains and physical reality are inherently hypercomputational systems with continuous nonlinear dynamics, capable of solving problems undecidable or intractable for any Turing machine. We introduce the hypercomputational ontological manifold M and dissipative projection operator Pdrop, demonstrating that data is not neutral bits but a topological collapse of continuous hypercomputational dynamics onto discrete symbolic spaces. Modern AI’s success stems not from a breakthrough in Turing computation, but from its ability to compress and approximate hypercomputational solutions encoded in low-entropy data from human minds and physical environments—a process we term extensional alignment. We show that deep reinforcement learning’s strong performance on NP-hard and continuous control problems constitutes a computational outsourcing mechanism: rather than solving problems internally, AI agents delegate computation to the physical environment as an online hypercomputational oracle. We then build a three-tier nested endogenous growth model where growth is driven by AI’s absorption of hypercomputational data, not pure computational power alone. Our model yields three counterintuitive, testable predictions: (1) Pure Turing synthetic data has diminishing marginal value and leads to semiotic collapse via entropy growth in isolated Markov chains; (2) Long-run AI economy growth is bounded by new hypercomputational information from human innovation and physical exploration, not Moore’s Law; (3) Non-algorithmic creative and experimental human labor remains irreplaceable as the ultimate source of economic value. These findings carry profound implications for AI policy, labor economics, and the future of economic growth.

items.title: Manufacturing in the Era of Generative AI: The GAMI (Generative AI Manufacturing Intelligence) Framework and Manufacturing Intelligence Index Model.
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is becoming a significant force driving manufacturing transformation, following automation, digitalization, and the Industrial Internet. Unlike traditional AI, which primarily focuses on prediction, recognition, and classification, GAI possesses capabilities in content generation, knowledge creation, solution design, and autonomous collaborative decision-making, enabling manufacturing systems to gradually evolve from "automated manufacturing" to "intelligent creative manufacturing." However, theoretical research on the integration of GAI with manufacturing is still in its exploratory stage, lacking a systematic theoretical framework and evaluation model for manufacturing intelligence. To address this, this paper proposes a Generative AI Manufacturing Intelligence (GAMI) theory, constructing a five-layer manufacturing intelligence architecture consisting of a data layer, knowledge layer, generation layer, execution layer, and feedback layer, and establishing a Manufacturing Intelligence Index (MII) model. This model posits that the value of a manufacturing system stems from the combined effects of its generative capabilities, knowledge fusion capabilities, execution collaboration capabilities, and continuous learning capabilities. Research results demonstrate that GAI not only improves product design efficiency and production decision-making quality but also promotes the formation of continuous self-optimization capabilities in manufacturing systems. This paper provides a new theoretical foundation and research direction for the intelligent transformation of manufacturing in the era of GAI.

items.title: GITE Theory: Reconstructing Information Technology in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is driving the transformation of information technology from the "data processing era" to the "intelligent generation era." Traditional information technology theory is primarily based on data storage, information transmission, and computational processing, while the emergence of generative AI endows information systems with the capabilities of content generation, knowledge creation, and intelligent decision-making. Existing research mainly focuses on the application scenarios and technical implementation of generative AI, lacking a unified theoretical explanation for how it systematically restructures the information technology system. Therefore, this paper proposes the Generative Intelligence-Technology Evolution (GITE) model. This model posits that generative AI achieves the continuous evolution of the information technology system through a five-layer structure: "data resource layer—knowledge generation layer—intelligent collaboration layer—value creation layer—ecological evolution layer." This paper further constructs the GITE operating mechanism and theoretical formula, and explores its application value in education, healthcare, industry, commerce, and government governance. Research shows that generative AI is evolving from an auxiliary tool into a core driving force of the information technology ecosystem, providing a new theoretical foundation for the future development of the digital society.

items.title: Generative AI-Era Software Paradigm Reconstruction: A GAISF (Generative AI-Based Intelligent Software Fusion Framework) Theory and Model Study.
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence, traditional software engineering is undergoing a profound transformation from "function-driven" to "generative-driven." Software is no longer statically written by developers, but dynamically generated and continuously evolved by generative AI under the combined influence of user needs, contextual environment, and data resources. To address this trend, this paper proposes a new theoretical model—GAISF (Generative AI-based Intelligent Software Fusion Framework). This framework constructs a closed-loop system of "requirements understanding—code generation—runtime feedback—adaptive evolution," and introduces a software generation intensity function and an adaptive evolution mechanism to describe the dynamic behavior of software systems in the generative AI era. Through a reconstruction analysis of the traditional software engineering paradigm, this paper further explores the application value of GAISF in intelligent application development, enterprise software systems, and adaptive service systems. Research shows that this framework can significantly improve software development efficiency, system adaptability, and continuous evolution capabilities, providing a new theoretical foundation for future software engineering.

items.title: Generative AI-Driven Publishing Transformation: A GAIP Framework for Human–AI Co-Creation and Dynamic Value Generation in the Publishing Ecosystem.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the content production methods, dissemination structures, and value distribution mechanisms of the publishing industry. The traditional publishing system is centered on a linear process of "author—editor—publishing institution—reader," but with the intervention of generative AI, content production is gradually shifting towards a new paradigm of "human-machine co-creation—dynamic generation—real-time distribution." This paper proposes the "Generative AI Publishing Framework (GAIP)," constructing a five-stage closed-loop model of "demand-driven—AI generation—multimodal editing—intelligent distribution—feedback evolution." This framework emphasizes the core role of generative AI in content creation, editorial optimization, publishing decisions, and reader interaction, and introduces a "publishing value co-creation function" to characterize the overall efficiency and value output mechanism of the publishing system. The research argues that generative AI not only improves publishing efficiency but also restructures the power structure and value network of knowledge production, transforming the publishing system from a linear chain into a dynamic ecological network.

items.title: GAH-VC: A Generative AI-Driven Value Co-Creation Model for Hotel Accommodation in the Intelligent Hospitality Era.
items.abstract: With the rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) technology, the hotel accommodation industry is undergoing a profound transformation from digital services to intelligent value co-creation. Traditional hotel management models primarily rely on standardized service processes, while the emergence of generative AI enables hotels to achieve personalized content generation, real-time service response, intelligent decision support, and immersive accommodation experience innovation. However, existing research mainly focuses on the role of AI in improving hotel operational efficiency, lacking a systematic theoretical explanation of how generative AI restructures the hotel value creation mechanism. This paper proposes a Generative AI Hotel Value Co-Creation Model (GAH-VC) based on Service-Dominant Logic and value co-creation theory. This model posits that data resources, generative capabilities, human-machine collaboration, accommodation experience, and value feedback constitute the core elements of generative AI driving hotel value creation, achieving continuous optimization through an intelligent cyclical mechanism. This paper constructs the GAH-VC theoretical framework, analyzes its operational mechanism and application scenarios, providing theoretical basis and practical reference for hotel management innovation in the era of generative AI.

items.title: GAIDS: A Generative AI-Driven Defense Symbiosis Framework for Intelligent Transformation of the Defense Industry.
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is reshaping the global defense industry. Unlike traditional AI, which primarily focuses on identification, prediction, and automated decision-making, generative AI possesses capabilities in knowledge generation, solution generation, combat simulation, equipment design, and intelligent collaboration, driving the evolution of the defense system from informatization to intelligent generative capabilities. Existing research mainly focuses on the application of generative AI in military training, intelligence analysis, and unmanned operations, lacking a systematic theoretical framework. Therefore, this paper proposes the Generative AI-Driven Defense Intelligent Symbiosis Theory (GAIDS), constructing a five-stage closed-loop mechanism of "data-generation-collaboration-execution-feedback," and proposing the Defense Intelligent Symbiosis Index (DISI) model. This research argues that generative AI is not only a military technology tool but also a crucial intelligent hub connecting personnel, equipment, data, and organizations. The GAIDS framework reveals the intrinsic mechanism by which generative AI promotes the optimal allocation of defense resources and enhances military innovation capabilities, providing a theoretical foundation and practical reference for future intelligent defense construction.

items.title: Entertainment Value Co-Creation in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Development of the GAE-VCC Model.
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is reshaping the global entertainment industry ecosystem. From film and television production, game development, and music creation to virtual idol management, generative AI is gradually evolving from an auxiliary tool into a key participant in entertainment value creation. Traditional entertainment theory, primarily based on the binary structure of content producers and consumers, struggles to explain the new value creation process resulting from the deep involvement of generative AI. Based on value co-creation theory, digital ecosystem theory, and the characteristics of generative AI technology, this paper proposes a new theoretical framework—the GAE-VCC (Generative AI Entertainment Value Co-Creation) model. This model posits that the entertainment system in the generative AI era comprises five core dimensions: the user demand layer, the AI generation layer, the human-machine collaboration layer, the immersive experience layer, and the value co-creation layer, forming a continuous optimization cycle through a dynamic feedback mechanism. This paper further constructs an Entertainment Value Index (EVI) formula to describe the entertainment value formation process in a generative AI environment. Research results indicate that generative AI is driving the entertainment industry's transformation from a "content consumption model" to a "content co-creation model," forming a new digital entertainment ecosystem. This article provides a new theoretical framework for understanding the transformation of the entertainment industry in the era of generative AI, and also offers theoretical reference for the future innovative development of the entertainment industry.

items.title: A New Theory of Tourism Value Co-Creation in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: The GAIT-VC Framework.
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is reshaping the operational logic of the tourism industry. Traditional tourism theory is mainly based on resource supply, tourist demand, and service management, while the emergence of generative AI is gradually evolving the tourism system from an "information service model" to an "intelligent co-creation model." This paper proposes a Generative AI Tourism Value Co-Creation Model (GAIT-VC) based on Service-Dominant Logic, Experience Economy theory, and digital tourism theory. This model posits that tourism value is no longer unilaterally provided by the destination, but is dynamically generated among tourists, generative AI, and the destination. This paper constructs the GAIT-VC theoretical framework, mathematical expression, and five-stage cyclical operation mechanism, and analyzes its application value in smart scenic spots, personalized travel planning, digital tour guides, cultural heritage dissemination, and virtual tourism. Research shows that generative AI is driving the transformation of the tourism industry from resource-driven to intelligence-driven, forming a new tourism ecosystem.

items.title: The Captured Oracle: Authorship and Agency in the Ethics of Answer-Engine Optimization.
items.abstract: Answer-engine optimization shapes what answer engines say, not which sources they list. Ask one a contested question and it may return not sources but a verdict in its own voice, with no visible author. An optimizer authors that verdict while the engine voices it as its own; a public acts on it, the framer unreachable. That is the wrong on the verdict channel; its form is false assurance: the appearance of an answerable party behind a frame whose author is hidden or absent. The reply that it is only a tool concedes rather than settles: a tool that settles a frame settles someone’s, and that someone the channel conceals, leaving the non-authoring user the only party in view. The wrong is not exhausted by falsity, concealment, or machine origin: a verdict may be accurate, disclosed, and cited, while frame-ownership stays illegible. It runs along one axis: the agency of whoever executes the frame. At the answer end a person acts on another’s covert frame: the hidden author stays answerable, the user partly excused. At the action end an AI agent executes it in the user’s place, and the case turns new: a covertly authored frame joined to an executor that cannot answer, which inherited categories cannot hold. The deed’s answer finds no bearer where it is done; the deployer stays answerable for loosing it. The remedy is answerable legibility: not disclosure of sources, prompts, models, or origin, but a visible owner of the frame the engine voices.
