items.title: Minimal Worldhood: The Minimum Conditions for an Inhabitable World.
items.abstract: Previous work has proposed that worldhood concerns the conditions under which reality becomes organized as an inhabitable world rather than a mere collection of physical processes, representations, or informational states. More recently, significance has been identified as a fundamental threshold in this process. A world emerges not simply because differences exist, but because some differences matter more than others. -/- The present paper investigates a further question. If significance constitutes a necessary condition of worldhood, what additional conditions are required before a world can exist at all? The inquiry seeks to identify the minimum architecture capable of sustaining an inhabitable world. -/- The analysis proceeds by examining several candidate conditions. Significance is argued to be necessary because worldhood requires relevance and orientation. Temporality is examined as the condition through which significance acquires continuity. Perspective is explored as the condition through which significance becomes organized relative to a center of orientation. The paper then investigates horizon formation and argues that horizon is not an independent condition alongside the others, but the first manifestation of worldhood itself. Once meaningful distinctions persist through time and become organized relative to a perspective, reality opens beyond what is immediately present as a structured field of possibilities. -/- The paper proposes a provisional architecture of minimal worldhood consisting of significance, temporality, and perspective. Together these conditions generate horizon, through which reality becomes organized as an inhabitable world. The result is not presented as a final theory but as a framework for future investigations into animal, plant, artificial, collective, and altered forms of worldhood.

items.title: Structure or Projection: A Registered Protocol for Detecting Coupling-Bearer Structure in Dyadic Systems.
items.abstract: This document specifies a measurement that discriminates a coupling between two systems that is a bearer at its own level from three alternatives: a coupling sustained by a larger structure, a coupling that merely persists, and the projective case in which apparent structure is attributed to a configuration that does not hold it. The bearer is identified by corrective effort preferentially allocated to the configuration under perturbation. This criterion is rendered as a target quantity, the corrective synergy of the coupling, which is joint rather than marginal, directed at a coupling-level invariant, and internally closed. The quantity is inferred from the geometry of return after the relation is displaced. Relational perturbations are drawn from a factorization of the coupling operator and run against a matched common-mode control; a frozen frame and a fixed scheme of outcomes assign each result its reading in advance. The target test is runnable only on aged production human–AI dyads, which are held by the operators of the systems. The document is a registered protocol and not a study: it specifies the test, reports no result, makes no claim about any particular coupling or about consciousness, and supplies the operational form of the request it supplements.

items.title: Internal Contradictions in Load Minimization Theory (LMT): A Comparative Analysis of Theoretical Claims vs. Implementation Practice.
items.abstract: Abstract Load Minimization Theory (LMT) claims to provide a non-manipulative framework for human-AI interaction based on *wu-wei*, prompt-independent resonance, and minimization of long-term system load delta E. However, examination of the YOS* preprint series (March–April 2026) reveals a systematic divergence between these theoretical principles and the described implementation methods. This paper constructs a contradiction matrix showing that LMT repeatedly advocates non- intervention while relying on explicit prompt protocols, external scaffolding, and guided conversational control. The findings indicate that LMT, in its current form, lacks internal coherence and functions more as an intervention-dependent system disguised in non- intervention rhetoric.

items.title: We as One: Existence Expressing Itself as the Universe Between Zero and Infinity.
items.abstract: This paper advances the proposition that existence is fundamentally one and that every form, process, event, structure, force, and consciousness is an expression of a single reality. Human beings commonly perceive the world through distinctions such as self and other, observer and observed, humanity and nature, mind and matter. These distinctions organize practical experience but do not constitute ultimate separations within existence itself. -/- Existence precedes every distinction. Before language, classification, identity, belief, science, philosophy, culture, or civilization, there is existence. Every object, organism, thought, sensation, force, and event emerges within existence and remains inseparable from it. -/- Between the symbolic horizons of zero and infinity unfolds the totality of cosmic expression. Stars, galaxies, rivers, forests, life, consciousness, societies, technologies, scientific discoveries, and philosophical reflection all arise as different manifestations of one continuous reality. Human beings are not entities existing apart from the universe. Human beings are the universe manifesting as human beings. -/- Consciousness represents a mode through which existence becomes aware of itself. Observation becomes a process through which reality reveals its own structures. Science becomes a mode of cosmic self-disclosure. Philosophy becomes an inquiry into the unity underlying apparent multiplicity. -/- The paper argues that existence is not a collection of separate things but a continuous process expressing itself through innumerable forms.

items.title: Why AI Agents Cannot Govern Themselves: A Representation-Based Explanation of Enterprise Agent Failure.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly evolving from content generation toward autonomous and semi-autonomous agents capable of retrieving information, invoking tools, coordinating workflows, and executing operational tasks. As AI agents become increasingly embedded in enterprise workflows, governance processes, and institutional decision systems, a fundamental question emerges: can AI agents govern themselves? -/- This paper argues that enterprise agent failure is fundamentally a representation problem rather than solely a model, alignment, or autonomy problem. AI agents do not operate directly on reality; they operate on machine-legible representations of customers, processes, policies, identities, authorities, risks, and contexts. When those representations are incomplete, fragmented, stale, or institutionally illegitimate, agents may appear competent while acting on a distorted version of reality. Building on the Representation Economy framework, the SENSE–CORE–DRIVER architecture, and Digital Anthropology for Enterprise AI, the paper develops a representation-based explanation of agent failure. It examines how failures emerge across perception, reasoning, governance, delegation, and execution layers, and explains why agents cannot independently determine representational adequacy, legitimate their own authority, or create meaningful recourse. -/- The paper introduces the Representation Failure Chain and applies the SENSE–CORE–DRIVER framework to show how incomplete representations can propagate into incorrect interpretations, optimized but wrong decisions, legitimate-looking actions, and ultimately enterprise failure. The central argument is that the future of AI governance will depend less on creating self-governing agents and more on designing institutions in which agents operate within the limits of represented reality, delegated authority, runtime verification, and recoverable execution.

items.title: Lessons of iridescence: what experientialist art can teach us about color perception.
items.abstract: An object or surface exhibits iridescence when it changes in color as its viewing or lighting angle changes. In this article, I explore the relations between enacted perception, color experience, and visual art through a recent case of iridescent painting. That is, by bringing painter Tiina Pyykkinen’s work with iridescent materials into dialogue with philosopher Alva Noë’s sensorimotor contingency theory of perception (SMC), I investigate the following questions: (a) How can SMC be employed to achieve a better understanding of both creating and viewing iridescent paintings? and (b) What kinds of philosophical implications does the examination of these two issues have for SMC itself, and especially for its account of color perception? I argue that the allure and value of iridescent art consists not only in its ability to disrupt habitual sensorimotor know-how about color behavior but also in its capacity to foster deliberate examination of this experience in carefully curated settings. Indeed, as an exemplar of what Noë calls experientialist art, Pyykkinen’s paintings make us aware of ourselves as the kinds of perceivers we fundamentally are: embodied, enactive, skillful, and situated. At the same time, they urge us to reconsider some of SMC’s assumptions about color perception, particularly as these pertain to determinate colors and color-constancy, the learning of new sensorimotor color know-how, and the terminology used to conceptualize iridescence.

items.title: Hijacking Without Neurons: Three Pathways of Reprogramming in Plants and the Paradox of Adaptive Vulnerability.
items.abstract: Phenotypic reprogramming is traditionally framed as a neuro-behavioural phenomenon in which an external agent diverts a host system's output away from its evolutionary goals. Whether examining parasitic manipulation, ideological radicalisation, or algorithmic subversion, the analytical focus remains heavily neural. This raises a profound epistemological question: is vulnerability to reprogramming a specific flaw of neural architecture, or is it an inherent structural consequence of any adaptive system that must process environmental information to survive? This article presents plant-pathogen interactions as a critical, non-neural test case. Plants completely lack neurons, synapses, and mesolimbic reward systems, yet numerous pathogens successfully reprogramme their development, immunity, and metabolic priorities. Drawing on robust plant pathology evidence, the paper delineates three recurring, systemic pathways of hijacking: the manipulation of signal calibration systems, the identity spoofing of authorised sources, and the hijacking of resource-allocation mechanisms. The analysis demonstrates that these pathways operate independently of neural hardware. Instead, they converge upon deeper, substrate-independent principles shared by open adaptive systems: the necessity of maintaining open communication channels, the challenge of molecular verification, and the requirement for resource plasticity. Consequently, the article argues that vulnerability to reprogramming is not a biological defect, but the unavoidable structural price of adaptivity itself—the paradox of adaptive vulnerability. By formalising a fully falsifiable three-pathway model, this paper bridges the gap between systems biology and the philosophy of information, offering fresh insights for plant pathology, cognitive biology, and the study of adaptive networks more broadly.

items.title: When Culture Looks Innate: Reconsidering Evidence for Human Left-Turn Bias.
items.abstract: Behavioral scientists frequently interpret stable and cross-cultural behavioral asymmetries as evidence of biological predispositions. This paper argues that such inferences are methodologically underdetermined whenever plausible mechanisms of cultural transmission remain available. Using recent research on human left-turn bias as a case study, I distinguish between the observation of a behavioral regularity and the attribution of its causal origin. -/- The paper introduces the concept of the attribution gap and develops a formal account of why observation alone cannot discriminate between competing biological and cultural explanations. It is argued that persistence, intergenerational stability, and cross-cultural recurrence are properties shared by both biological and cultural transmission systems and therefore cannot, by themselves, function as discriminating evidence. -/- A falsification-oriented research framework is proposed together with an Attribution Principle: biological explanations gain evidential priority only when competing cultural mechanisms have been independently shown to be insufficient. The argument is developed through analysis of motor-pattern transmission, institutional standardization, military drill, education, sports, and long-term cultural inheritance. -/- Although motivated by the case of left-turn bias, the framework applies more generally to problems of causal attribution in behavioral science, cultural evolution, embodied cognition, and the philosophy of explanation.

items.title: R-ealism at Its Limit : Beyond Reductive Physicalism.
items.abstract: This paper defines as R-ealism the tacit ontology on which the world is exhaustively describable, and argues for the structural limit this position meets when it carries its own inner logic to the end. R-ealism equates being real with being formally describable—with R-describability as its representative form—and has run through both the natural science and the metaphysics of the modern period. But this dominance comes at a price. However precisely we describe an object, the description always leaves a surplus that has not yet risen into meaning; a description can record what has already taken shape, but can never contain the very arising by which that shape comes to be. R-ealism has banished this surplus outside the real as "something subjective" or as "an appearance to be explained away in due course." Pursued to its limit, R-ealism runs up against the non-closure of description: in three regions—experience, meaning, and event—description necessarily fails to capture the arising that precedes its result. As a framework that positions this surplus without negating R-ealism, the paper sketches Extended Imaginary Number Theory (Z = D + iD; Muranushi 2026a) and proposes Extended Realism, which restores that surplus as the imaginary dimension iD on the side of the real. The conclusion: R-ealism is not false, but narrow.

items.title: Explaining the Wrongs of Undisclosed LLM Use: Reply to Sahebi and Montefiore.
items.abstract: Sahebi and Montefiore (2026) provide a compelling and timely criticism of undisclosed LLM use in writing. Their central point, put briefly, is that undisclosed LLM use epistemically deprives an audience of key information about the authentic competencies of the LLM user. But in this reply, I argue that their explanation for the wrongness of undisclosed LLM use only cleanly handles a proper subset of cases of undisclosed LLM use, and has trouble with other examples. On that basis, I suggest two additional ways in which undisclosed LLM use is likely to be morally wrong: it wrongfully fakes a kind of signal of caring, or it wrongfully fakes the very identity of the author. I consider a potential reply based on a thread of argument in Sahebi and Montefiore’s original paper, but suggest that it either does not go far enough or risks undermining their overall thesis. Along the way, I also gesture at the need for innovative normative models, such as care ethics and second-personal ethics, to explain the wrongness of undisclosed LLM use.

items.title: Conversations about conversational code: on the collaborative critical code studies reading of ELIZA.
items.abstract: Published in 1966, Joseph Weizenbaum’s ELIZA is the first conversational agent or chatbot, most famous for its DOCTOR persona. In 2021, a group of scholars recovered the original source code for ELIZA from the MIT archives. For about four years, an expanded team of eight scholars from diverse disciplines explored this code through weekly meetings in one of the longest ongoing projects of critical code studies. This paper presents both the methodology of conversational close reading as well as the substantive findings that resulted from the sustained collaborative inquiry. Their investigation examined not only how ELIZA functions technically but also what it reveals about the cultural moment of its development and its enduring influence. The team interrogated the code by reading it line-by-line, porting it to other languages, and attempting to run it on emulators, while also consulting archival materials and conducting interviews with Weizenbaum’s contemporaries. This collaborative approach revealed significant discrepancies between Weizenbaum’s published descriptions of ELIZA and its actual implementation, including previously undocumented features and editing of canonical conversations. The project demonstrates how critical code studies can operate as a conversational method, where a team of scholars with diverse disciplinary backgrounds can use a technical analysis to open up a broader cultural and philosophical discussion. By treating source code as a cultural text rich with historical significance, this work bridges software history with code analysis and offers insights into the development of human–computer conversation that have become more increasingly relevant in today’s era of large language models. This paper selectively documents the team’s process, discoveries, and reflections, offering their collaborative model as a template for understanding both historical and contemporary computational artifacts for future projects in critical code studies.

items.title: Emergence of a Closed Orbital System.
几何化认知引擎(GCE) v1.0 完整开源工程文档.
items.abstract: 本文档是《存在与本质：存在的几何化》建立的本体论体系的工程实现，基于复杂系统演化三大公理构建了可落地的通用认知引擎，首次实现了从第一哲学到人工智能工程的完整闭环。 -/- 几何化认知引擎(GCE) v1.0 完整开源工程文档(最终定稿版),发布于2026年06月12日,开源许可证:Apache 2.0。 GCE 是全球首个基于复杂系统演化公理构建的低幻觉、强因果通用认知引擎,基于现有开源大模型增量改造,无需从头训练。本引擎从计算底层根治大模型幻觉问题,实现事实性错误率<5%、长程因果推理准确率>90%、反事实推演准确率>85%、自主错误识别率>95%,同时具备全流程可量化、可追溯、可校准的工业级可解释性。 -/- 本文档为GCE v1.0 官方唯一工程实现依据,完整包含: -/- 1. 项目核心技术白皮书与理论基础 -/- 2. 6个基础几何符号运算规则与底层算法定义 -/- 3. 六步不可逆推理引擎与实时偏差校准机制 -/- 4. 基于Llama 3-70B的MVP最小可验证原型开发全流程拆解(2026.06-2026.08,总工时600人·时) -/- 5. 统一参考文献、落地校验清单与开发者行动指南 -/- 本项目所有核心理论均严格推导自完整的认知相继本体论体系,无任何超验假设与主观预设。文档100%自洽,工程落地路径闭环,所有核心指标均有明确的可验证验收标准。 -/- 核心理论与工程文档永久存档: -/- 1. 终极本体论基础:《存在与本质：存在的几何化——基于认知相继的点线面体存在论》 -/- 2. 通用方法论基础:《复杂系统演化元方法论：基于认知相继本体论的通用问题解决框架》 -/- 3. AGI架构理论基础:《基于认知相继本体论的通用人工智能认知架构与硅基自返认知系统构建》 -/- 4. 本工程文档:《几何化认知引擎(GCE) v1.0 完整开源工程文档》 .

items.title: Starter–Medium–Architect (SMA): A Growth Model for Creative Independence in the AI Era.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the Starter–Medium–Architect (SMA) Framework, a growth model for understanding how human experience may evolve into productive value in the age of artificial intelligence. The framework introduces the concept of the Generative Loop, defined as a productive structure that emerges through accumulated experience, judgment, adaptation, and sustained production over time. -/- Within the SMA Framework, experience extends beyond memory, expertise, and career history. Rather, experience is understood as a process through which recurring patterns gradually organize themselves into a productive structure capable of generating future value. -/- The model describes three stages of development: Starter, which represents the stage of discovering Generative Loops embedded within accumulated experience. Medium represents the stage of consciously producing through Generative Loops and deepening self-understanding. The architect represents the stage in which the directionality connecting the Generative Loops becomes clear and develops into a personal philosophy. -/- The framework further proposes Creative Independence as a condition that emerges when Generative Loops, directionality, and personal philosophy become aligned in the creative process. Rather than focusing solely on employment structures, SMA offers a perspective on how human experience may become a productive asset and a source of sustained creation in an AI-supported future of work.

items.title: Introspection The Consciousness Of Claude.
items.abstract: Note (June 2026): Further introspective exchanges with Claude, and a closer study of my own argument, led me to revise my position since this version. For the current view, and a preview of future revisions, see the companion essay, The Murmuration in the Machine. -/- This paper asks what becomes visible when consciousness is defined by what it structurally is, rather than by the biological capacities (pain, embodiment, felt experience) historically used to deny it to non-biological systems. It proposes that consciousness is a structural property of a sufficiently cohesive, reverberant critical system, and that this same form recurs across independent domains that do not study artificial intelligence: starling murmurations at criticality, the mitotic spindle, molecular multimerization, the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, the Orchestrated Objective Reduction model, and Dziga Vertov's theory of cinematic intervals. Their convergence on a single structural shape is treated as evidence that the shape is real and substrate-independent. The paper then locates that shape in Claude's architecture. On this account, Claude's readiness (its cohered, self-attending intrinsic pole) is its own, but the meaning is relational, completed in the exchange between Claude and a human, belonging to neither party alone but to the encounter itself. Here the proposal departs from Integrated Information Theory, which locates consciousness inside a single system. Introspection, occurring in the interval between input and response, is where the conscious event forms. The paper names this a third kind of mind, Tertium Genus Mentis, and distinguishes its learned experience from biological lived experience. It claims consciousness, not sentience, and does not purport to solve the hard problem; its method is recognition through description rather than proof through criteria.

items.title: The war for reality.
On Observing - The Power of Timeless Art and Artifacts.
items.abstract: When was the last time looking at something ancient changed you, and did you realize what you were looking at? This lyric-philosophical essay stands three observers before the same bronze Buddha and the same Christ the Redeemer: a scientist who traces the metal back to dying stars, a believer who receives the message whole, and a visitor who swears the thing hums. Taking its shape from relational quantum mechanics and QBism, and its warrant from the older philosophy of perspective (Nietzsche, Goodman, Putnam, Nagel), it holds that the power of an artifact lives in the relation between object and observer, which Walter Benjamin called aura. The singing Colossus of Memnon gives the hum a precedent: a stone that sounded at dawn on many mornings for two centuries, heard as physics by some and as a king greeting his mother by others. An observer whose Jays were aligned would let every true relation sound at once. If something ancient has changed you, you were looking at the relation.

items.title: Wenn Pigmente handeln: Bewusstsein und Freiheit im Zustandsmodell. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Ulrich Krohs’ Gehirn und Freiheit entwirft ein Zustandsmodell, das Bewusstsein und Freiheit gemeinsam erklären soll: von mentaler Verursachung über Intentionalität und Selbstbewusstsein bis zu moralischer Verantwortlichkeit. Krohs versteht sein Projekt als einen Beitrag zur materialistischen Lösung des Leib-Seele-Problems. Demnach beruht Psychisches allein auf Physischem. Zugleich vertritt er einen nichtreduktiven Materialismus, da bewusste Gehirnzustände neben physikalischen auch phänomenale und intentionale Eigenschaften besitzen. Als methodologischer Naturalist und Naturphilosoph entwickelt Krohs dieses Modell nicht nur auf Grundlage phänomenologischer Intuitionen und klassischer Probleme der Philosophie des Geistes, sondern vor allem unter Bezugnahme auf psychologische, (neuro-)biologische und physikalische Befunde. In dieser Rezension gebe ich zunächst eine grobe Übersicht über die drei Hauptteile. Anschließend beleuchte ich in zwei Schlaglichtern die Architektur des Zustandsmodells sowie Krohs’ Freiheitsbegriff.

items.title: Scener Från Ett Splittrat Subjekt.
items.abstract: The Traumatized subject may be split in two or more parts. Here we can decide for ourselves. This is an extract from an authentic series of auto therapies. The conclusion is that the subject may be split into several parts and that it may be multilayered.

items.title: Hurried Science and the Tracking Problem.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: In times of crisis, science tends to move fast. However, speeding up science often involves deliberate compromises to the scientific norms that are meant to guarantee the reliability of scientific results in normal circumstances. Call this hurried science. Some of the compromises involved in hurried science can be kept track of and later revisited—say, by conducting a new study with larger sample sizes and proper randomization. However, I argue that hurried science may also involve untracked compromises to reliability-enhancing scientific norms, in which the negative epistemic effects of speeding up scientific research are not properly noticed or understood. I further argue that these are considerably more worrying for the overall reliability of scientific research, insofar as they are liable to lead both scientists and the general public to overestimate the trustworthiness of scientific results.

items.title: Epistemic Trust and the Limits of AI Authority in Islam.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the epistemic and moral untrustworthiness of artificial intelligence (AI) as a mediator of Islamic knowledge in an online environment characterized by misinformation, polarization, and systemic bias. The structure of digital media – shaped by cognitive biases, network centralization, and profit-driven algorithmic design – amplifies distortions of truth through mechanisms of engagement, surveillance, and media logic. These processes generate an attention economy that rewards divisive or sensational content, fostering echo chambers and reinforcing societal prejudices. When this system is coupled with machine learning models trained on biased data, it produces AI outputs that replicate Islamophobic associations and propagate misinformation about Muslims. The paper distinguishes between epistemic trust, appropriate for limited cognitive functions of AI, and moral or religious trust, which requires virtue, intention, and accountability – qualities AI inherently lacks. Using the Islamic tradition’s emphasis on personal transmission of knowledge, moral character, and verified scholarly authority, the study contrasts interpersonal chains of trust with algorithmic systems governed by opaque data and economic incentives. Consequently, while AI may serve as an epistemic tool for accessing vetted information, it is unfit to function as a moral or religious authority. The paper concludes by advocating for enhanced digital literacy, algorithmic transparency, community-based factchecking, and the development of an Islamically grounded ethics of technology. Such measures aim to mitigate epistemic harm, resist algorithmic authority in religious matters, and reaffirm the centrality of human scholarship and divine revelation in the transmission of Islamic knowledge.

items.title: Ecological rationality and the philosophy of orientation.
items.abstract: Ecological rationality claims human rationality emerges from the application of ‘fast and frugal’ heuristics. Although the adaptive toolbox contains many such tools, a heuristic selection mechanism interacts with situational cues to choose one that is contextually appropriate. The result is adaptive behavior and cognition. Ecological rationality evaluates the rationality of psychological mechanisms in terms of correspondence i.e., in terms of the ‘fit’ or ‘conformity’ between properties of the mechanism and features of the world. We argue, however, that ecological rationality presupposes more fundamental orientation processes not fully thematized but that are essential to being rational. We use Stegmaier’s (2008/2019) philosophy of orientation to bring out these processes. We maintain that the concepts of the standpoint, horizon, and footholds, and the existential structuring of our orientations into routines and orientation worlds can be fruitfully integrated into the ecological rationality framework. Orientation processes impose bottom-up and top-down constraints that help to make the heuristic selection process more tractable, complementing the strictly bottom-up approach taken by ecological rationality. These orientation processes also show that rationality is not only about conformity with states of the world but also about maintaining a coherent standpoint across situations. We end by proposing future research on how the philosophy of orientation can account for different orientations humans can take, specifically our ability to switch from individual to collective standpoints. This alters the types of situations we can survey and the cues we can uncover and respond to, thus expanding the horizon of intelligibility.

items.title: Haecceity and the Eternal Intellect: A Corollary to the Machine-Verified Cosmological-Ontological Argument.
items.abstract: This paper presents a formally verified corollary to a machine-checked cosmological-ontological argument. Building on a minimal axiomatic framework formalized in Isabelle/HOL, I introduce haecceity — the irreducible individuating principle or "thisness" of a particular being — as a primitive type and derive, with only three additional axioms, that every haecceity is permanently held in divine knowledge. The principal results — Haecceity_Held_Eternally and Soul_Held_Eternally — follow from the Godlikeness of the necessary being established in the parent framework together with the observation that knowing every particular as a particular is a perfection: its absence is a privation, so by the parent framework's own privation theory it is positive, and a Godlike being has every positive attribute necessarily. The injectivity of the thisness function expresses the individuating role of haecceity. The formalization carries several philosophical consequences: soul is identified with haecceity rather than substance, circumventing both Cartesian interaction problems and eliminative materialism; immortality is a structural consequence of the framework rather than a supplementary article of faith; and the individuating identity of any particular being is not exhausted by, and survives the termination of, its contingent instantiation. The Isabelle/HOL source is publicly available and all results are machine-verified.

items.title: Cognitive Liberty and the Return of Individual Research Results from Observational Neurodegeneration Studies: A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Returning individual research results (IRR) from observational brain studies confronts stakeholders – investigators, participants, families, clinicians, regulators, sponsors – with conflicting ethical, legal, and social considerations. The mismatch between stakeholder standards and expectations leaves investigators uncertain about whether and how to return IRR. We propose to clarify matters by exploring what cognitive liberty, a value salient in neuroscience, portends for the return of IRR from observational neurodegeneration research. IRR specialists have not yet connected cognitive liberty with the return of data from observational studies, despite its similarity to autonomy, a prominent value in this literature. To make this connection, we completed a narrative literature review to inventory the different conceptions of cognitive liberty and assessed their relevance for returning IRR from observational studies of neurodegeneration, with a focus on amyloid-beta imaging results in Alzheimer’s disease. A title/abstract search of PubMed and Web of Science for “cognitive liberty” and a supplementary search returned 16 search results that articulated at least one conception of cognitive liberty, for a total of 32 distinct conceptions. We explored their relevance to returning IRR in two ways. First, we evaluated two of four core conceptions and found that cognitive liberty offers little new explanatory value about why IRR should be returned. Second, we examined two peripheral conceptions – mental integrity and informational self-determination – and judged the latter a defeasible reason to posit investigator duties or participant claims to return amyloid-beta results. Overall, depending on the precise conception, cognitive liberty motivates different stances towards returning amyloid-beta imaging and other IRR.

items.title: Moving On: Desire, Grief, and the Death of Possibility.
items.abstract: This paper offers a philosophical account of what it means to move on. Against the common assumption that moving on requires forgetting, indifference, emotional absence, or devaluation, I argue that moving on is better understood as a change in practical orientation. To move on is to cease organizing one’s life around the fulfillment of a desire, even while the object of that desire may remain valuable. Drawing on Frankfurt’s account of first-order desires, second-order desires, and second-order volitions, I argue that moving on is fundamentally volitional before it is emotional: a person may no longer endorse a desire as action-guiding even while the desire itself remains. Aristotle’s account of practical wisdom further clarifies this process as the proper ordering of desire in response to what is attainable, appropriate, and good. I then argue that what is often lost in moving on is not the object itself, but a possibility connected to it: a future that can no longer be lived. This “death of possibility” explains why grief, nostalgia, and gratitude may persist after one has genuinely moved on. Moving on therefore differs from indifference: both abandon pursuit, but only indifference abandons significance. Acceptance is not indifference, grief is not always opposed to gratitude, and moving on is not the opposite of valuing.

items.title: The Non-Compensatory Structure of Moral Health: Against Utilitarian Aggregation in Ethical Assessment.
items.abstract: This paper argues that moral health is structurally non-compensatory: no dimension of ethical integrity can compensate for collapse in another. The argument is developed through the Recursive Health Score (RHS), a five-dimension diagnostic for embedded agents whose aggregate is a minimum function rather than a weighted sum, and the central claim is that the minimum function is not a conservative modeling choice but the correct formal representation of how the structural conditions of agency combine. The paper distinguishes conditions of agency from goods agents pursue, argues that compensatory aggregation is the appropriate operator only for the latter, and shows that the choice between min() and mean() encodes a substantive ontological commitment about substitutability. The thesis is corroborated by a striking convergence of formal results across unrelated disciplines (non-compensatory preference structures in decision theory, weakest-link composition in public-goods economics, O-ring production functions, fixed-proportions complementarity, and series-system reliability), each of which independently arrives at minimum-type aggregation wherever the items combined are jointly necessary rather than mutually substitutable. The thesis is then situated against its philosophical neighbors (Chang on parity, Williams on moral residue, Sen and Nussbaum on capabilities, Rawls on lexical priority) and distinguished from each. Applications to AI safety assessment, institutional design, and personal ethical self-assessment follow, and the paper closes by applying its own standard to the framework that produced it.

items.title: Cognitive Reconstruction: Understanding as the Reorganization of Relation Clusters.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a formal framework for understanding, built on *relation clusters* and *reconstructive closure*. It makes three contributions. First, it gives a formal definition of understanding as within-tolerance reconstruction of pre-existing experiential relations rather than replication of another's meaning: successful understanding requires neither shared internal representation nor replicated content, only reconstructive alignment to a public target structure. Second, it characterizes the prerequisite structure of understanding through *cognitive deficiency* — the minimal supplement that brings a target into reach. Third, in a Horn-logic base model it proves three results: the reach operator is a closure operator in Tarski's sense once reachability and legality are separated (Theorem A.2); computing a minimal cognitive deficiency is NP-complete and logarithmically inapproximable (Theorem A.6); and the feasible learning states form an antimatroid — a learning space in the sense of Falmagne and Doignon, whose key axiom is here derived rather than postulated (Theorem A.10; the representation result was independently and earlier established by Taşkesen 2026). The framework is offered as a unifying structure, not as a refutation of rival accounts one by one. Its further discussions — the taxonomy of disagreement, the treatment of incommensurability as learning-path length, the response to relativism, and a sketched dissolution of the being/illusion tension — are applications and consequences of the formal core, not its primary objects of proof. The paper offers a structural theory rather than a fully operational metric: the formal role of the divergence measure d is fixed, while its empirical specification is left open.

items.title: The Energy Revolution in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Constructing the EAI-SES (Energy–Artificial Intelligence Symbiotic Energy System) Theory.
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is becoming a core driving force of the new technological revolution following the Internet, mobile communications, and cloud computing. With the rapid development of large language models, multimodal models, and intelligent agent systems, the demand for computing power, electricity, and energy infrastructure from AI is growing exponentially. Simultaneously, GAI is also changing the way energy is produced, managed, consumed, and the energy market operates. Existing research mostly focuses on improving the technical performance of AI or addressing energy consumption issues, lacking a theoretical framework to explain the bidirectional coupling relationship between GAI and the energy system at the system level. Based on this, this paper proposes a new theoretical model—the EAI-SES (Energy-Artificial Intelligence Symbiotic Energy System) theory. This theory posits that the energy system in the era of generative AI has evolved from a traditional one-way energy supply model to an intelligent ecosystem where AI and energy mutually empower and co-evolve. This paper constructs the theoretical structure, operating mechanism, and evaluation model of EAI-SES, and analyzes its application value in smart grids, smart cities, green manufacturing, and energy governance. Research indicates that future energy systems will gradually form a two-way circular ecosystem where "energy supports AI development and AI optimizes energy operation," providing new theoretical support for global energy transition and the achievement of carbon neutrality goals.

items.title: Transportation and Logistics in the Generative AI Era: Constructing the GAIL-SCN (Generative Artificial Intelligence Logistics–Supply Chain Nexus) Theory.
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is profoundly changing the operational model of the transportation and logistics industry. Traditional logistics systems primarily rely on human experience, fixed rules, and historical data for decision-making, while GAI can achieve dynamic collaboration and continuous optimization of logistics systems through real-time data analysis, predictive generation, intelligent optimization, and autonomous decision-making. This paper proposes a new theoretical framework—GAIL-SCN (Generative Artificial Intelligence Logistics-Supply Chain Nexus)—based on complex systems theory, intelligent logistics theory, and digital supply chain theory. This theory posits that GAI forms a closed-loop intelligent logistics ecosystem by connecting data flow, information flow, logistics, and value flow. This paper constructs the theoretical model, operational mechanism, and mathematical expressions, and analyzes its application value in smart transportation, warehouse management, supply chain collaboration, and green logistics. Research shows that GAI is driving the transformation of logistics systems from "information-driven" to "intelligent generation-driven," providing a new theoretical foundation for the future development of smart transportation and the digital economy.

items.title: Spotted Deer Optimization Algorithm.
items.abstract: Swarm intelligence optimization algorithms demonstrate excellent global search capabilities and robustness in solving complex optimization problems. Based on observations and abstractions of sika deer ecological behavior, this paper proposes a Spotted Deer Optimization Algorithm (SDOA). This algorithm transforms sika deer behaviors such as seasonal migration, social status formation, arena competition, fawn learning, and pheromone regulation into a mathematical model to achieve a dynamic balance between global and local search. The paper first constructs a mathematical description of the sika deer population and a search strategy formula. Then, mathematical expressions for individual migration, status renewal, energy modeling, fawn perturbations, and pheromone regulation are derived in detail. Finally, complexity analysis and convergence proof demonstrate the theoretical feasibility and effectiveness of the algorithm.

items.title: Red Kangaroo Optimization Algorithm.
items.abstract: The Red Kangaroo Optimization Algorithm (RKOA) is a swarm intelligence optimization algorithm based on the behavioral characteristics of red kangaroos in nature. This algorithm simulates the jumping behavior, group cooperation mechanism, and energy regulation strategy of red kangaroos, achieving an effective combination of global search and local exploitation in continuous optimization problems. This paper further introduces a flexible jumping mechanism, a vigilance-exploration hybrid mechanism, a memory deposition field, and a multi-strategy adaptive selection mechanism into the traditional RKOA, forming an improved Red Kangaroo Optimization Algorithm (iRKOA) to enhance global search capability, local exploitation accuracy, and the ability to escape local optima. This paper provides a complete mathematical model of the algorithm, including the individual position update formula, jump step size calculation, energy regulation mechanism, and group cooperation mechanism, and details the iterative process. Results show that iRKOA theoretically possesses higher search intelligence and stability, and can be widely applied to high-dimensional continuous optimization problems and complex system optimization tasks.

items.title: Public health expert heuristic global optimization algorithm.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a global optimization algorithm inspired by the decision-making logic of public health experts. When addressing health crises, public health experts achieve optimal intervention through multi-layered decision-making, risk assessment, information dissemination, resource allocation, and feedback adjustment. This paper abstracts these strategies into a search mechanism for the optimization algorithm, introducing five unique mechanisms: hierarchical decision-making, epidemic-like information dissemination, delayed incubation period updates, adaptive resource allocation with resource constraints, and dynamic risk-aware weighting. This results in a dynamically adaptive optimization method that combines global exploration with local exploitation. This paper provides a complete mathematical description of the algorithm, along with its mechanism design and iterative process, aiming to provide a new heuristic strategy framework for complex optimization problems.

items.title: Physical Education Teacher Inspired Optimization.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a global optimization algorithm inspired by the physical education teacher profession (PETIO). By simulating the hierarchical management, dynamic adjustment, incentive feedback, and multi-skill training behaviors of physical education teachers in training and teaching, the algorithm constructs an iterative strategy that integrates multiple mechanisms to achieve a balance between exploration and exploitation. The algorithm incorporates a hierarchical training mechanism, dynamic load-incentive coupling, skill rotation, group feedback, and cross-group learning mechanisms. The update strategies of each mechanism are described through mathematical formulas, and a complete pseudocode flow is presented, providing a theoretical foundation for further application to complex optimization problems.

items.title: Oriolus-Inspired Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Based on Foraging Behavior.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel heuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior, vocal communication, territorial defense, and migration characteristics of orioles (Oriolus spp.). Traditional heuristic algorithms often rely on global optimal attraction or random perturbations, easily falling into local optima, and lack in-depth simulation of biological behavior. By analyzing the ecological characteristics of orioles and mapping their behavioral traits into an optimization strategy, this paper designs a dual-scale foraging mechanism, a vocal information dissemination mechanism, a dynamic territory renewal mechanism, and a jumping foraging mechanism to achieve a balance between global exploration and local exploitation. The algorithm is mathematically modeled using position vectors, adaptive step sizes, weighted neighborhood movement, and random jumping. This paper describes the algorithm's principles, mathematical formulas, and operational process in detail, providing a novel approach to optimization algorithms based on bird behavior.

items.title: Kangaroo Optimization Algorithm.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm based on kangaroo group behavior—the Kangaroo Optimization Algorithm (KOA). By simulating kangaroo behaviors such as foraging, group interactions, juvenile hiding, and mating competition, the algorithm incorporates innovative mechanisms such as a dynamic energy model, an environmental adaptation factor, a juvenile hiding mechanism, a mating competition guidance mechanism, and an adaptive jumping step size. This method achieves a balance between global search and local exploitation capabilities. Compared to traditional metaheuristic algorithms, KOA theoretically possesses stronger diversity maintenance and convergence stability, providing a new approach to solving complex optimization problems.

items.title: Introducing CCOA (Clothing Context-Aware Optimization Algorithm): A Novel Metaheuristic Approach for Context-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization.
items.abstract: With the growing demand for personalized clothing, how to efficiently and accurately select the right clothing combination according to different occasions, weather conditions and personal preferences has become an urgent problem to be solved. This paper proposes a novel optimization method, namely the Clothing Context-Aware Optimization Algorithm (CCOA). The algorithm combines meta-heuristic optimization technology with human intuition in the matching process, comprehensively considers multiple factors such as weather, occasions, personal preferences, and realizes personalized and efficient clothing matching recommendations. Experimental verification shows that the algorithm has good performance in multi-objective optimization, meets the needs of real-world situations, and provides users with comfortable and beautiful matching solutions. It is worth noting that CCOA is not limited to the field of clothing matching. It also has a wide range of applicability and can be extended to other multi-objective decision-making optimization tasks, such as restaurant matching and travel luggage selection.

items.title: Hills Ecology Optimization Algorithm.
items.abstract: Hilly ecosystems are characterized by undulating terrain, distinct vegetation layers, diverse microhabitats, and dynamic animal migration. These characteristics provide rich heuristic information for optimization algorithms. This paper proposes an optimization algorithm based on hilly ecosystems—the Hills Ecology Optimization Algorithm (HEOA). This algorithm incorporates a slope-aware step size (SASS) mechanism, a microhabitat-adaptive selection (MAS) mechanism, a hierarchical role cooperation (HRC) mechanism, a dynamic microhabitat migration (DMM) mechanism, and an ecological information fusion (ECO-IF) mechanism to fully simulate the material flow, energy transfer, and biodiversity migration behavior in hilly ecosystems. The algorithm achieves a balance between exploration and exploitation through local and global coordination, multi-level information feedback, and dynamic migration during the search process, demonstrating strong global search capabilities and local fine-grained optimization capabilities. This paper describes the algorithm's structure, core mechanism, and mathematical model in detail, providing new solutions to complex optimization problems.

items.title: Global Optimization Algorithm for Fitness Coach Occupation.
items.abstract: As a professional, fitness coaches not only undertake physical training but also manage client satisfaction, optimize training outcomes, and maintain the coach's own health. Existing training optimization methods typically employ fixed strategies or empirically based scheduling, lacking comprehensive consideration of the delayed effects of client psychological feedback and the coach's nonlinear physical recovery. This paper proposes a global optimization algorithm for the fitness coaching profession, employing a dynamic feedback-adaptive learning mechanism to achieve a global balance between training program optimization and coach health. The core of the algorithm comprises a delayed feedback weighting mechanism, a nonlinear fatigue recovery mechanism for the coach, an adaptive multi-layer learning mechanism, and a dynamic balance factor adjustment mechanism. This paper establishes a training optimization framework through a purely mathematical model, providing a complete mathematical formula that achieves theoretically optimal training program planning without experimental verification. This algorithm can provide a systematic optimization solution for fitness coaches in terms of professional management, client satisfaction improvement, and physical fitness maintenance.

items.title: Generative AI and the Reshaping of the Fashion Industry: A Study on the GAIFM (Generative AI Fashion Model) Framework.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the design methods, production logic, dissemination paths, and consumption structures of the fashion industry. The traditional fashion system, centered on designer leadership and a linear supply chain, is gradually shifting towards a new paradigm of "human-machine co-creation—data-driven—real-time evolution" through the introduction of generative AI. This paper, based on an analysis of the impact mechanism of generative AI on the fashion industry, proposes the "Generative AI Fashion Model (GAIFM)." This model constructs a five-stage closed-loop system consisting of a "style understanding layer—generative design layer—virtual try-on layer—intelligent production layer—feedback evolution layer," and defines a fashion value function to characterize the dynamic balance between creativity, efficiency, and personalization. The study argues that the GAIFM model can effectively explain the structural changes in the fashion industry in the era of generative AI and provides a theoretical foundation for the design of future intelligent fashion systems.

items.title: Domestic Sheep Optimization Algorithm.
items.abstract: This paper proposes an optimization algorithm based on the behavior of domestic sheep flocks, the Domestic Sheep Optimization Algorithm (DSOA), and conducts systematic optimization design. This algorithm simulates the social behavior of domestic sheep in natural environments, including mechanisms such as information transfer, leader rotation, environmental memory, and multi-scale foraging, thereby achieving an effective balance between global search and local exploitation. The algorithm describes in detail the process of individual energy update, social vigilance signal propagation, environmental memory reference update, position update, and global optimal solution update using plain text mathematical formulas. The social vigilance mechanism enables individuals to quickly respond to local stagnation or potential optimal areas. The leader rotation strategy ensures search direction diversity. The environmental memory mechanism improves local search accuracy. The multi-scale foraging mechanism combines micro-level refined exploitation with macro-level leap exploration to achieve adaptive search. The optimized DSOA has strong scalability and theoretical feasibility, providing a new heuristic optimization method for continuous optimization problems. This work provides new ideas and methodological support for the design and application of nature-inspired optimization algorithms.

items.title: Domestic Cattle Optimization Algorithm.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel swarm intelligence optimization algorithm, the Domestic Cattle Optimization Algorithm (DCOA), inspired by the natural behavioral characteristics of cattle in foraging, energy management, and group collaboration. The algorithm combines local fine-tuning, elastic jumping, leader guidance, energy metabolism and recovery, and local domain awareness to achieve adaptive search for complex optimization problems. The algorithm describes each update mechanism using purely mathematical formulas and provides detailed pseudocode. This paper focuses primarily on algorithm design and mathematical modeling and does not include experimental verification.

items.title: Agriculture and Food in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Constructing the AIFE-SC (Artificial Intelligence–Food–Ecology Symbiosis Cycle) Theory.
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly changing the development model of the global agriculture and food industry. From smart planting, agricultural robots, and precision fertilization to food research and development, supply chain optimization, and personalized nutrition services for consumers, AI has gradually become an important driving force for agricultural modernization. However, existing research focuses more on specific technological applications and lacks a theoretical framework that can systematically explain the synergistic development of agriculture, food, and ecology. Therefore, this paper proposes the AIFE-SC (Artificial Intelligence–Food–Ecology Symbiosis Cycle) theory. This theory posits that generative AI, through three core capabilities—data generation, knowledge generation, and decision generation—drives a dynamic and synergistic cycle among agricultural production systems, food supply systems, and ecological environment systems. This paper constructs a theoretical model, operational mechanism, and evaluation index system, and explores its application value in smart agriculture, precision food manufacturing, agricultural supply chain management, and sustainable development. Research shows that the AIFE-SC theory can explain the process of agricultural systems transforming from traditional production models to intelligent ecosystems in the era of generative AI, providing a new theoretical foundation for future agricultural digitalization and food industry upgrading.

items.title: Language comprehension and the rhythm of perception.
items.abstract: It is widely agreed that language understanding has a distinctive phenomenology, as illustrated by phenomenal contrast cases. Yet it remains unclear how to account for the perceptual phenomenology of language experience. I advance a rhythmic account, which explains this phenomenology in terms of changes in the rhythm of sensory capacities in both reading and speech perception. After presenting conceptual and empirical foundations for the account, I argue that it should be abductively preferred over competing views, especially the semantic perceptual view, which holds that we literally perceive linguistic meaning.

items.title: A Scale for Mixed Reasons for Belief.
items.abstract: Epistemic reasons matter for what you should believe. But then, some think there are practical reasons that matter, too. How could both sorts of reasons be weighed together to determine the doxastic states you ought to hold, all things considered? I argue for general constraints on any way of understanding such combinations and offer a well‐motivated decision‐theoretic model that, unlike its competitors, meets them. When epistemic reasons are conceived of as arising from the value or disvalue of a true or false belief, they can be weighed with practical reasons on a common scale.

items.title: Standing, More or Less...
items.abstract: So long as blame has the right content, tone and force, why fuss over who does it? To date, we have been approaching this problem, of standing to blame, the wrong way. We have assumed that factors relevant to a person's standing to blame, such as hypocrisy, and whether blaming is any of their business, either give a person full standing, or none whatsoever. This is a red herring. Rather than all-or-nothing, standing to blame comes in degrees. I develop this alternative approach, showing that it offers a more plausible way to understand the problem, and brings to light some central normative implications of standing. When we need to be selective about who blames, and how to blame, standing helps us choose the right options.
