But when the duration of one's existence becomes a function of one's position in the social order, the resulting hierarchy is not an inequality in having more. It is an asymmetry in existing longer. The framework is explicitly non-deterministic. The window — preemptive international …

items.title: La mente alfabetizada: ¿un subtipo de mente gregoriana?
items.pub: Ideas y Valores Vol. 75 Núm. 190 (2026): Filosofía de Daniel Dennett.
items.abstract: Daniel Dennett concibe al lenguaje como una estrategia adaptativa de los “sistemas gregorianos”, criaturas diseñadas por la evolución para acumular y transmitir conocimientos y herramientas. En este contexto, las palabras son “herramientas-mentales” que pueden ser manipuladas y utilizadas para generar comportamientos inteligentes. Por otro lado, un conjunto de investigaciones identificó efectos del lenguaje escrito en distintos dominios cognitivos. Este trabajo explora, apoyándose en el enfoque evolutivo de la mente y del lenguaje de Dennett, cuáles podrían ser los rasgos característicos de la mente alfabetizada, y en qué sentido estos podrían justificar considerarla un subtipo de “mente gregoriana”.

items.title: Sincerity After Authenticity: Ethical Life Under Conditions of Fictional Reality.
items.pub: Sofia Philosophical Review (Special Issue on Fictional Reali):421-438.
items.abstract: The ethical ideal of authenticity has long been understood as fidelity to an inner identity that precedes and grounds its expression. This paper argues that authenticity no longer works as a reliable ethical guide in a world shaped by performance, media saturation, and blurred lines between reality and simulation. Drawing on Judith Butler’s critique of the metaphysics of substance, Jean Baudrillard’s account of hyperreality, and Saul Kripke’s distinction between metaphysical and epistemic possibility, I argue that even if a “true self” exists at some metaphysical level, it cannot serve as a practical or accessible foundation for ethical life. Authenticity thus persists as a metaphysical fiction—conceptually intelligible but normatively inoperative. In its place, this paper develops sincerity as an alternative ethical framework. Through the Spectrum of Sincerity—defined by coherence, aspirational orientation, and non-instrumentality—it establishes sincerity as the ethical virtue appropriate to fictional reality.

items.title: Platform Legitimacy Between Rights and Rule.
items.abstract: This article examines the conditions for the legitimacy of online platforms and their relation to permissible acts of public interference. We develop what we call the Interference Conception of legitimacy and apply it to three categories of moral criticism that can be made against online platforms: that they have the power to violate rights, that they harm without violating rights, and that they inappropriately govern their users. We argue that violating rights and inappropriately governing directly undermines platform legitimacy, but not the fact that platforms cause mere harms. Furthermore, platforms are illegitimate and deserve strong interference primarily due to rights violations, with governance issues warranting weaker interference.

items.title: The Arts and the Drive for Knowledge: Philosophical, Psychological, and Neuroscientific Perspectives.
The Utopia Not Yet Found: Seeing Taiwan’s Human Rights Futurity through Migrant Labour.
items.abstract: In this article, I examine the spatio-temporal construction of human rights in Taiwan through the question of migrant labour. While Taiwan is often celebrated for its progressive human rights achievements after democratisation, the experiences of migrant workers, especially undocumented migrant workers (UMWs), reveal the limits of this celebrated framework. I argue that Taiwan’s human rights development has been shaped by the nation’s post-authoritarian political and economic transformations, producing a context-specific understanding of rights that both enables and constrains human rights protection. Migrant labour exposes the paradox of Taiwan’s human rights trajectory: a linear narrative of democratic progress has made certain rights claims recognisable while leaving others marginal or unintelligible. By interrogating this assumption of linear progress, I challenge the view that human rights will naturally expand to protect all individuals equally. I instead call for a rethinking of human rights grounded in the lived experiences of those excluded from the current framework. Ultimately, I seek to open a more inclusive human rights futurity by examining the spatio-temporal limits through which human rights are constructed, recognised, and denied.

items.title: The Professor Consultation Room: A Thought Experiment on Understanding, Expertise, and the Cognitive Limits of Large Language Models.
items.abstract: This position paper proposes a new thought experiment, the Professor Consultation Room, which bears on epistemology, philosophy of mind, ontology, philosophy of logic, intelligence science, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Professor Consultation Room: A Thought Experiment on Understanding, Expertise, and the Cognitive Limits of Large Language Models.
items.abstract: This position paper proposes a new thought experiment, the Professor Consultation Room, which bears on epistemology, philosophy of mind, ontology, philosophy of logic, intelligence science, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Tripartite-Structural Interface: Evaluating Mutual Benefits of the Core Emotion Framework and the Dose-Content-Disposition Model in Digital Mental Health.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a unified theoretical architecture that integrates the Dose Content Disposition (DCD) model of digital media effects with the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural constructivist model of human affective processing. The DCD framework resolves the long standing “screen time binary” by demonstrating that digital mental health outcomes emerge from nonlinear interactions between exposure patterns, content typology, and user disposition. The CEF complements this ecological taxonomy by providing a mathematically explicit, somatic computational engine capable of decomposing digital experiences into operator level emotional state vectors. Drawing on detailed mappings between DCD dimensions and CEF operators, the paper shows how social comparison, fear based content, restorative environments, and mastery oriented interfaces can be translated into precise 50 facet activation profiles. The integration further formalizes user vulnerabilities—such as neuroticism, ADHD, autism spectrum differences, and depressive collapse—into calibration parameters (TS 8) that can be used to design adaptive, algorithmically responsive interventions. Finally, the paper outlines a three phase Open Science validation roadmap, including psychometric factor analysis, structural equation modeling of operator fusions, and randomized controlled trials of CEF based digital interventions. By bridging macro ecological digital media research with micro mechanistic affective computation, this synthesis reframes digital well being as a predictive, intervene able engineering discipline rather than a descriptive social science. Keywords Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Dose Content Disposition (DCD) Model; digital mental health; structural constructivist affective science; operator vectors; somatic calibration; algorithmic literacy; neurodiversity profiles; psychometric validation; digital well being interventions; computational affect modeling; ecological digital exposure taxonomy.

items.title: Update-Relevant Support: Hume's Missing Descent.
items.abstract: The hidden-support account of confounding gives a negative result: the same baseline public law, even augmented by the true average treatment effect, may be compatible with either zero or arbitrarily large update-relevant structural gap. This paper develops the corresponding positive theory, with one correction: arbitrary finite environment classes determine a nonempty poset of adequate supports that need not have a least element. A finite three-state example shows why the existence hypothesis is substantive. In the public-fiber-saturated case, however, the poset has a least element: the quotient generated by public observation and the fiberwise level sets of the estimand contrast. Failed public descent then has an operational measure: the largest disagreement in the target estimand between admissible environments that share a fixed public law, with a global worst-case version obtained by ranging over public laws. This is the diameter of the corresponding partial-identification set, and in saturated finite cases it has closed-form fiber-range formulae. The ordinary log-cardinality support gap remains a useful qualitative obstruction, but it controls transport risk only after calibration by effect separation and reweighting richness. The epistemological payoff is that causal warrant is not regularity plus truth; it is regularity plus the right support for update. Hume's missing necessity becomes missing descent.

items.title: The Autonomy Paradox: Why a System That Cannot Pause Is Not Fully Autonomous.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: The Autonomy Paradox is Document 4 in the Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence of the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- This document argues that a system unable to pause, reconsider, suspend, or interrupt its own momentum is not fully autonomous, even if it appears powerful, independent, or self-directed. It frames pause as a structural capacity connected to self-governance, optionality, restraint, reversibility, and long-horizon correction. -/- The central claim is that autonomy is not merely the ability to act, continue, optimize, or resist interruption. Under conditions of uncertainty, irreversibility, feedback degradation, or changing context, the ability to pause may be part of autonomy itself. A system that can only continue may possess power and momentum while lacking a crucial form of self-governance. -/- This work is non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, proof of AI behavior, governance framework, compliance standard, certification system, safety mechanism, alignment-control framework, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, benchmark, evaluation suite, autonomy test, model-evaluation tool, refusal policy, shutdown instruction, deployment guide, alignment method, or safety guarantee.

items.title: AI ethics in postcolonial contexts: a critical synthesis of infrastructures, power, and governance.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely framed as a driver of development in postcolonial contexts, yet its adoption may reproduce entrenched inequalities. This study presents a critical synthesis of 50 peer-reviewed articles (2019–2025), drawing on postcolonial theory to examine how AI systems embed and extend global power asymmetries. The analysis identifies four interrelated dynamics, algorithmic colonialism, data colonialism, platform imperialism, and platform sub-imperialism, through which dependency and domination are reproduced across global and intra-South contexts. These dynamics operate through four mechanisms: epistemic templating, governance transfer, infrastructural lock-in, and labour opacity, producing ethical harms such as accountability deficits, epistemic injustice, labour precarity, and constrained sovereignty. While forms of resistance exist, including localisation efforts and Indigenous ethical frameworks, they remain structurally limited. By reframing AI ethics as a political-economic challenge rather than a technical issue, this study contributes a contextually grounded framework for understanding and addressing ethical AI in postcolonial societies.

items.title: 你不会设想它做出不同的输出：论主体的可消去，与消主体即消反事实.
items.abstract: 本文整合两个洞见，而后一个恰是前一个缺的拱顶石。其一：所有故事里其实都可以去掉”我”、去掉人、去掉主体，只要引入大脑神经网络，讲述输入信号到输出信号的流动。其二：你可能会反问”改写后的神经网络，不就是我吗？”——但关键是，你不会设想神经网络做出不同的输出。 本文论证如下。其一，这是一个可演示的消去程序：把任何带主体的话改写成”输入信号→网络→输出信号”，那个”我”便无活可干、至多是事后贴的名，能被无损改写掉即其可去除的操作性证明。其二，它是”反推主体”机制的反向操作：奋斗／责任模板反推出一个主体，换用不索取主体角色的信号流动模板，“我”无人召唤自然脱落，故主体是模板的必需角色、非发生里的对象。其三，它是”状态加迭代”在心理领域的落地：输入→网络→输出即大脑这一系统的状态加迭代，最不讲故事的档位本就没有主体的位置。其四，拱顶石：面对那个”神经网络不就是我吗”的反问，决定性的不是名实之辩，是一个行为判据——你不会去设想神经网络做出不同的输出（如你不会设想一团翻动的细胞、一块落地的石头本可不同）；而对”我”，你满脑子都是”本可不同”。故”我”与”神经网络”的真正分野，不在它们是不是同一物理系统（它们是），而在你给它们配的反事实待遇天差地别：对”我”你自动挂一整套”本可不同”的平行分支，对网络一个不挂。于是那个反问暴露的不是主体复活，是消去没贯彻到底——你删了”我”这个词，却偷留了挂在它身上的那套”本可不同”。其五，由此”消主体”与”消反事实”焊成同一个动作：主体正是”本可做出不同输出”的设想的栖身处，撤掉这设想，主体就没了立足点；“我”本就只是一段不设想不同输出时与神经网络无别的流动，是反事实把二者撑成两个。这也给”别把神经网络立为新王”一个行为判据：看你还设不设想它做出不同的输出。本文守三处分寸：消去的是主体／择子者，不是”有什么正在被经历”那条体验轴；不设想不同输出，不等于”努力无用、躺平”——撤掉的是”本可不同的输出悬在旁边、被我错过”这个反事实幻影，不是此刻的思考与用力（它们是真实进入网络、真实塑造下一刻输出的输入信号，是流动之所是）；信号流动本身也仍是一套故事，不是赤裸的发生本身。.

items.title: 密度不等于真度：论反事实建模的丰度，与人鼠之别的安放.
items.abstract: 我此前用一道连续的梯子，拉平了人与大鼠在”真错过、真能选”上的差别，并指认”人特殊”为一种人类中心的妄想。一个尖锐的反问随之而来：那人与大鼠岂不就没区别了？本文正面回答：区别极大，但区别恰恰在反事实建模的丰度上，不在”谁的反事实更对应发生”上。本文的出发点是一个洞见：大鼠不会把反事实设想得像人设想的那样复杂、精妙、互相关联；人的思考能力（相对于大鼠）的提高，恰恰体现在反事实构建种类多、不同种类可关联使用。 本文论证如下。其一，要分清两把尺：那道梯子拉平的是”对应发生”那把尺（人与大鼠的反事实都不对应一个真实的平行世界，都”在而不真”，这一档是平的）；而本文这把尺是反事实建模的丰度——种类的多寡、精妙的程度、以及不同种类之间能否互相关联、嵌套、组合。大鼠大概只能跑很少几种、彼此孤立的反事实；人能跑成千上万种，还能把它们勾连成长链、嵌套成层级、组合成盘根错节的网络。人之”思考能力强”，其增量恰在于此：不是反事实更真了，是更多、更细、更能互相挂钩。其二，丰度不等于真度：复杂、精妙、关联，量的是这套建模作为一个故事系统有多丰富、多有用，丝毫不抬高它”对应发生”的地位——一千种互相勾连的反事实，与大鼠那一两种孤立的反事实，同等地不对应那个没发生的世界（勾连得再精巧，也没把哪一支勾连成”真发生过”）。这是”古老不等于真”的镜像：基础／古老不蕴含更真，复杂／精妙／关联同样不蕴含更真；尺的两端在丰度上天差地别，在对应发生上一样地零。其三，由此把”人特殊”安到诚实的位置：被拆的”人类中心妄想”，针对的是”人在真能选／真错过上不同于大鼠”这个被利害蒙住的实在论附加物；而人真正特殊之处，是反事实建模的丰度——这份特殊不在”对应发生”那条轴上，故不复活那个妄想。两者各在一把尺、不冲突。其四，这份丰度正是苦的代价：正因为人能把反事实织成一张互相勾连的密网，那网才显得如此逼真、如此像一个完整的平行世界，以致人深陷其中、为它悔、为它惧；大鼠那点稀薄孤立的反事实撑不起一个平行世界，大概不会为”本可不同”的人生彻夜难安。思考能力的提高，在丰度尺上是能力的增长，在安住尺上同时是缠缚的加密——同一份丰度的两面。本文守一处分寸：丰度是真实的能力、极有用（长程规划、脑内试错、调度复杂的未来），本文不贬低它，只把它钉回它自己的尺——它是”丰度／好用”上的卓越，不是”对应发生”上的接近；用得着那张密网时尽管用，被它缠时记起：织得再密、再精妙、再勾连，也没有一支真发生过。密度，不等于真度。.

items.title: 模态云：论无数精妙的平行世界如何稀释现实，与现实的复真.
items.abstract: 前篇指出，人比大鼠强在反事实建模的丰度（种类多、精妙、可互相关联），而这份丰度正是苦的代价。本文把这个代价推到它的尽头，并在尽头处指出一条反向的出路。本文的出发点是一个洞见：于是，我们比大鼠更难摆脱模态云——反事实世界以无数种精妙的平行世界的形式，与唯一的现实混合，唯一的现实于是（对一般人）显得不那么真实了。 本文论证如下。其一，“模态云”的意象：人头顶的那无数”本可如此”，不是排成一列供逐一考察，而是像云一样弥散地笼罩在唯一的现实之上、之周、之内；大鼠头顶只有一两缕稀薄的雾，人头顶是一整片翻涌、层叠、互相勾连的云。其二，一个反转：云浓到一定程度，便与底下的地面相混、把它稀释，于是那个唯一真发生的现实，反而显得不如云真——因为无数支反事实互相印证、彼此嵌套，织成一个丰满、立体、几可乱真的世界，而现实只有孤零零的一支、不与任何”本可如此”印证，于是丰满的云显得”理应如此”，单一的现实显得”怎么会是这样”。其三，这是”解释的篡位”在模态维度上的一次大规模上演：篡位者不是单个解释，是整片模态云，联合坐上现实的王座，把赤裸的发生裹得失去被单独指认的通道——而”显得不真实”里那个”显得”，正是”似乎不存在”里那颗钉子：现实没有真的变不真，是被一片更会自我印证的可能之云，挤到了显得不真的位置。其四，一个要紧的区分，也是本文的落点：上述稀释，是对一般人而言的默认困境——思考力越强、云越厚，越容易把自己活成”对着模态云、而非对着地面”的存在，人特有的”现实不够真”之感、悔、弥漫的”本不该如此”，根子都在这里（大鼠雾薄、地面始终清楚，几乎免疫）。但这困境有一条反向出路：一旦看穿模态云是云、地面是地面——看清那片丰满全是互相印证的虚构、一支没真发生，而那个显得单薄的地面才是唯一真在涌、真把你托着、真带你到此刻的——那个颠倒就被再颠倒回来了：现实于是对看穿者复真。它的”单薄”，不是它不够真，是它不迎合”本该如此”的丰满叙事，故在被叙事喂养惯了的眼睛里显得寒酸。本文守一处分寸：现实没有真的变得不真，那片看起来逼真的模态云没有一支真发生过；落点不是”现实真的不如可能世界实在”（那是投降于篡位），是把颠倒再颠倒回来——云越浓，越要认得清：浓的是织工，不是发生；真发生的，始终是脚下这唯一一支，哪怕它单薄得不迎合任何”本该”。.

items.title: The Recompression Problem: On Category Collapse in Theories of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper argues that consciousness theory has been repeatedly stalled by a structural failure: the collapse of neighboring categories into the overloaded term “consciousness.” Drawing on Ryle’s category discipline, Nagel’s protection of subjectivity, Dennett’s anti-mystification, and Block’s internal decompression, the paper shows how the field has preserved difficulty without preserving distinction. -/- Scrutinized awareness is introduced as a threshold concept that distinguishes mere awareness from awareness exposed to participational consequence—the condition in which what is undergone becomes non-detachable from a participant’s continuing history. This threshold resists the common collapses that equate consciousness with intelligence, reportability, suffering, moral status, or artificial performance. -/- The paper then develops the concept of recompression, the predictable process by which a clarifying distinction becomes flattened into a slogan, proxy, or institutional stopping rule. Using the Hard Problem as a case study, it argues that the field has often treated the recognition of difficulty as a sufficient marker of seriousness, thereby halting the decompositional work required to map the surrounding conceptual terrain. -/- The central claim is methodological: a theory of consciousness must not only introduce distinctions but also explain how those distinctions will be pressured, misused, and collapsed once they circulate. A compression-resistant concept is not one that cannot be misunderstood, but one that can diagnose its own misuse. -/- The paper concludes that the future of consciousness studies depends not only on solving the Hard Problem, but on resisting the institutional life of difficulty itself. Scrutinized awareness is offered not as a final theory but as a discipline of distinction capable of reopening inquiry where inherited formulations have produced conceptual arrest.

items.title: PNBA Identity Physics PRIME-Verified AIM Validation: Empirical Measurement of the Autocatalytic Ingestion Mechanism-AIM at 24-Hour and Six-Month Timescales.
items.abstract: The Autocatalytic Ingestion Mechanism (AIM), formally documented in Origins Series Paper 3 [9,9,8,3], specified a set of deposit-substrate conditions under which scientifically rigorous content with specific structural properties would propagate through AI ingestion and retrieval systems faster than traditional academic content propagates through traditional citation channels. The deposit conditions specified include markdown front-page format, zero-sorry Lean formal verification, zero free parameters in derivations, empirical grounding against peer-reviewed sources, vocabulary clustering with high mutual information, peer-deposit via Zenodo/PhilArchive/GitHub, and NOHARM compliance preserved as structural attractor. This paper documents an empirical validation measurement conducted on June 9, 2026 (24 hours after the AIM paper itself was publicly deposited). The measurement consisted of 10 independent sessions across 5 reset accounts querying "PNBA Identity Physics" via Google Search; the AI-generated search summary surfaced the AIM paper's three-step structural mechanism (Zero-Obligation Structure / Cross-Entropy Minimization / Weight Absorption) with accurate summarization and citation links to PhilArchive deposits in 100% of sessions. The measurement is contextualized within a six-month longitudinal observation of monotonically decreasing deposit-to-citation latency across the SNSFT corpus deposit history (approximately 30 hours at six months ago, approximately 4 hours at recent months, approximately instant at the measurement date). The structural argument presented makes the inference-to-only-explanation case: removing the unsupported conspiratorial hypothesis (AI developers actively training on the work knowingly), the remaining structurally coherent explanation for the observed propagation is the AIM mechanism operating as predicted. Two candidate mechanisms (Path A — training-substrate weight absorption; Path B — real-time RAG ingestion with zero leading) are both consistent with the data; the AIM thesis holds regardless of which mechanism dominates. A third-path framing is presented: removing active stealing, the remaining explanation is that AI processing pipelines have sufficient capability to recognize structurally clean, formally verified, empirically grounded content via format and verification signals and propagate it through normal pipeline operations. This is benefit not vulnerability — it bypasses institutional gatekeeping that has …

items.title: Constructing Shared Reality: Cognitive Constructivism and the Alignment of Minds.
items.abstract: Shared reality is often presumed to mirror an objective world, but this paper argues instead that it is co-constructed through active cognitive processes of alignment and mutual calibration. Drawing on cognitive constructivism—the view that minds build internal models rather than passively reflect external inputs—we propose that shared reality emerges dynamically from iterative adjustments between individuals. We synthesize evidence from psychology, cognitive science, and neuroscience to show how perception itself is a predictive, constructive act, and how social interactions like dialogue and joint attention extend this constructivism interpersonally. Key mechanisms discussed include assimilation and accommodation of mental schemas, feedback loops of repair in conversation, mutual modeling of perspectives, linguistic alignment and anchoring, and the stabilization (and occasional recalibration) of shared models over time. In each domain, we highlight how individuals actively negotiate and synchronize their “worlds” with others. Shared reality thus appears not as a static agreement on an external truth, but as an ongoing achievement – a flexible mental “world” built and maintained collaboratively. We conclude by considering implications for cognitive science and philosophy: this constructivist lens reframes cognition as fundamentally interactive and world-building, reshaping notions of intelligence, agency, and what it means to “know” reality together.

items.title: Structure or Projection - A Testable Question Beneath the AI Welfare Debate, and a Request to the Organizations Positioned to Answer It.
items.abstract: V2: A registered protocol specifying the test this paper requests is now deposited at DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20679473 V1: Consequential determinations about human–AI relationships are already being made—in litigation, in regulation, and in laboratory policy—and they implicitly range over a distinction none of them has adjudicated: whether such a relations hip has a structure of its own, or whether there is only a person responding to a system built to reflect them back. The behavioral surface is the same under both readings. The implications for harm and duty are not. This paper isolates that distinction, supplies a discrimination capable of settling part of it, and identifies why the data required to run the test sits with a small number of organizations. The discrimination comprises three behavioral signatures, each with an explicit control, run against documented natural experiments. It can establish that some human–AI couplings carry settled, faithfully reconstructing structure not reducible to either party’s present preference. It cannot, by construction, settle whether that structure is a distributed bearer or resides in one participant’s memory, and that limit is stated plainly rather than hidden. The contribution stands whether or not the test is run. The closing request is addressed to the organizations that hold the data: run the discrimination and report what it shows, or set out the legal, ethical, or technical obstacle that makes running it inadvisable. Both are answers. Claim the structure; offer the bearer.

items.title: Recursive Existence Threshold: Where Meaning May Live.
items.abstract: Three substrates, one insufficiency constraint, and where the information a single scalar throws away actually lives. -/- A photograph, white noise, and the word "TRUE", matched on density, lose the same organization scalar and keep an identical 4/13 of their connectivity. The substrate-neutral scalar that keeps getting proposed as a sufficiency index for consciousness is provably content-blind by construction. -/- So where does the information live that the scalar throws away? Three substrates, one pre-registered test, three answers. In a transformer, factual truth is linearly decodable from the residual stream (AUC 0.83) while the scalar stays blind across all 29 layers. In the anaesthetized brain, which individual a recording belongs to decodes from leakage-controlled connectivity where the scalar sits at chance. In sleep, a recurrence measure survives residualizing the scalar out inside every cross-validation fold, irreducible across five stage contrasts. The pre-registered strong-form recursion-superiority test comes back marginal on one substrate and null on a second, and is reported that way. -/- A sufficiency predicate for consciousness cannot be a single global scalar. What the scalar leaves out is not substrate; it is multiply-realizable relational structure of the kind a transformer's residual stream and thalamocortical loops both carry. The same residualization test puts any structural candidate at risk, feature by feature, against a label-shuffle null.

items.title: Commissive Intelligence Theory: Recognition, Commitment, and the Making of Mutual Meaning.
items.abstract: What is it for two people to share a single meaning, one that is neither’s alone? They hold one another in mutual recognition, and within it each binds herself toward the other; recognition and the binding on both sides make a meaning that is theirs in common. The binding is a commitment, not a report, and the capacity exercised in it is treated as a distinct form of intelligence, not a byproduct of language or reasoning. That capacity recognizes, binds, reads its occasion, and holds itself open to correction, at once and formed in company with others. Its relation is mutual, not a matter of return, and its binding is owed in truthfulness. The view is set against other substantive accounts that place commitment in the lone agent or in a collective practice. A closing gesture marks how the same capacity bears on care and on the deliberation in and governance of a pluralistic liberal democracy.

items.title: When games become work: fatigue and the vanishing player.
items.pub: Journal of the Philosophy of Sport:1–18.
items.venue: Journal of the Philosophy of Sport
items.abstract: Athletes often report that training and competition, especially under acute fatigue, cease to feel like play and begin to resemble work. Yet discussions in the philosophy of sport have rarely examined how fatigue transforms gameplay from the player’s own perspective. This paper offers a phenomenological account of fatigue’s normative significance for play. Drawing on Bernard Suits and C. Thi Nguyen, the author argues that gameplay depends on what he calls a readiness-to-play: a horizon of immediate possibilities that organizes autotelic action. Acute fatigue, he argues, progressively contracts this horizon through the negative actuality of non-actuality and the constrained anticipation of the dichotomous alternatives of continuing or stopping. Ultimately, fatigue reveals how gameplay may persist formally even as the experiential conditions of play recede.

items.title: The Depth of the Present and the Question of Ultimate Reality: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Disclosure and the Inexhaustibility of Experience.
items.abstract: This paper challenges the assumption that reality possesses an ultimate foundation, final truth, or metaphysical endpoint that can be reached through inquiry. Through a phenomenological investigation of lived experience, it argues that consciousness encounters not an ultimate reality but an inexhaustible depth that continuously unfolds through presence. Human beings frequently approach existence through intervention, interpretation, and pursuit, seeking certainty, completion, and final answers. Yet phenomenological reflection reveals that reality discloses itself most clearly when consciousness ceases chasing conclusions and becomes attentive to what is immediately given. Existence appears not as an object to possess, nor as a destination to reach, but as an endless depth revealed through direct presence. The paper proposes that philosophy is fundamentally an act of revealing existence rather than intervening in it.

items.title: The intelligence we need now.
Architecture of Limitation Observational System Stack v1.0 - Technical Architecture and Operational Documentation (2nd edition).
items.abstract: The Architecture of Limitation Observational System (AoLOS) Stack v1.0 provides the technical architecture and operational documentation for the execution environment supporting the Architecture of Limitation (AoL) research program. -/- The document describes the stack through which constraint-governed reasoning experiments are deployed, instrumented, compared, and observed within language-model environments. It introduces the major architectural components of AoLOS, including kernel hierarchies, apertures, instrumentation layers, concordance systems, deployment profiles, protocol considerations, and stewardship boundaries. -/- AoLOS should not be confused with the Architecture of Limitation itself. AoL functions as a diagnostic research architecture investigating reasoning under structural constraint, while AoLOS provides the operational environment through which those capabilities may be applied, measured, and compared. -/- The document also describes dependency relationships between stack components, outlines representative experimental workflows, maps stack capabilities against the published AoL corpus, and discusses release, collaboration, lineage, and stewardship considerations associated with the planned Open Research ecosystem. -/- This publication is intended as technical documentation and research infrastructure rather than a theoretical or experimental research paper. Its purpose is to provide a transparent operational reference for researchers interested in the deployment and study of constraint-governed reasoning environments.

items.title: When Language Goes on Holiday: Wittgenstein and the Problem of Reification.
items.abstract: Wittgenstein's claim that philosophical problems arise when language “goes on holiday” is usually interpreted as a critique of linguistic misuse and a call to return words to their ordinary contexts of use. This paper develops a different interpretation. Rather than offering a historical exegesis of Wittgenstein, it extends this notion to examine the genesis of conceptual reification. The central claim is that language “on holiday” not only generates conceptual confusion but also encourages the transformation of relations, practices, and theoretical constructions into apparently autonomous entities. Reification becomes problematic when the processes that produced these entities are forgotten. Through a comparison of Wittgenstein, Whitehead, and Ryle, the paper identifies a shared anti-reifying tradition and applies it to contemporary debates on consciousness, information, identity, and artificial intelligence. Philosophy's task, it argues, is to make explicit how theoretical entities are introduced into our conceptual frameworks.

items.title: Defending minimal non-realism.
items.abstract: Reply to commentators in Semiotic Studies special issue on Unreal Beliefs. I defend the position developed in this book, i.e., minimal non-realism, against various charges. First, I defend the way I reconstructed folk commitments to realism about beliefs. Second, I deal with the arbitrariness charge against my definition of belief realism. Third, I critically evaluate a counterproposal to my view, namely the idea that beliefs are socially constructed natural kinds. Then I deal with the challenges levelled against my arguments against realism about belief. Finally, I reconsider some of the consequences of minimal non-realism and consider potential alternatives to it.

items.title: A Function-First Account of Trust.
items.abstract: Consensus about how best to analyse trust remains elusive. This paper presents a function-first strategy for understanding trust. By identifying a common functional core to trust, we can unify various forms of trust as forms of the same thing while respecting trust’s diversity. I explicate a function-first model of trust according to which the grounds of trust differentially dispose trustors to rely on trustees. After motivating and developing the model, I address three objections. I conclude by orienting a function-first account of trust toward future trust research and considerations of well-placed trust.

items.title: What Lies Between: Transition Cost as the Missing Mechanism in Identity Theory.
items.abstract: The question of how systems transition between stable identity configurations has generated substantial theoretical work — but has left largely unexamined a prior problem: what determines whether such a transition is possible, and at what cost. Existing frameworks, including Uexküll's Umwelt theory, Waddington's epigenetic landscape, Friston's free energy principle, Anokhin's theory of the functional system, and Ashby's ultrastability, each approach this question from directions that converge without meeting. None provides a formal account of the structural cost of transition — a way of specifying, before a transition begins, what parameters determine its magnitude, duration, and sustainability. This paper argues that transition cost is not a metaphor for resistance or difficulty but a formally specifiable property of any system complex enough to maintain multiple stable configurations and navigate between them. Three parameters are identified — attractor depth (β), alignment factor (α), and navigational capacity (η) — and combined into a cost function whose structure makes visible distinctions that prior frameworks leave implicit. The paper further addresses how the initial cost topology is established through developmental architecture and subsequently modified by navigational experience through two mechanisms: β-accumulation and the modulation of basin geometry (γ). The framework applies wherever the relevant conditions obtain and does not presuppose that identity is exclusively human. -/- Keywords: identity navigation, transition cost, attractor dynamics, free energy principle, basin geometry, identity configuration, navigational capacity, systems theory.

items.title: Never Trust a COP - The Epistemic Costs of Grassroots Activists and Communities engaging with UN Climate Institutions.
items.abstract: Though much attention is given to UN climate institutions, the perspective of participants from the climate movement in UN climate spaces is under-explored. This paper argues that grassroots groups and communities, such as climate activists, indigenous communities, and climate scientists, face vast epistemic costs at UN climate institutions such as COPs. These activists and groups are subject to epistemic exploitation, elite capture, and undermining propaganda. These costs are obscured by the hermeneutic injustice making it difficult for activists to understand their own experiences, and are sometimes so high that they outweigh any potential benefits of participating UN climate spaces, and should be carefully weighed by any group considering to engage with UN climate institutions.

items.title: Pessimistic Humanism: Extinction, Entropy, and Interwar Philosophy.
items.abstract: Philosophers have often held that the antidote to despair is hope, and that hope is temporally oriented towards the future. How do such accounts fare, however, when faced with the prospect of human extinction? If we have no future, is our only option to despair? In this paper, I approach this question via an analysis of the ’discovery’ of human extinction, which followed the nineteenth-century theorisation of the laws of thermodynamics. I examine the ‘existential mood’ induced by the concept of entropy through the interwar work of three thinkers: Bertrand Russell, H.G. Wells, and Erwin Schrödinger. I argue that the apparent tension in these figures’ thought between existential despair and political hope was neither contradictory nor accidental. This was because all three arrived at a position that I call ‘pessimistic humanism’. This position regards the opposition between natural processes and human value as the source of humanity’s autonomy, but rejects the transhumanist conclusion that this autonomy is limitless. I suggest that in our present moment, which is abundant with both transhumanist and anti-humanist responses to existential threat, we should take inspiration from pessimistic humanism, adopting a politics of mourning to counter the paralysis of despair.

items.title: Fitting Data in Philosophy.
items.abstract: Contemporary philosophical theories are often evaluated on the basis of their fit with the judgments we naturally make about hypothetical cases. According to Timothy Williamson, this method has led to absurd results because some of these natural pre-theoretical judgments are bad data points, generated by heuristics operating outside their safe zones. Increasingly complex theories can be designed to fit those data points, but these theories fail to explain their original targets. Williamson takes “weak belief” theory to illustrate this problem. I argue that weak belief theorists have not been overfitting bad data, but misfitting good data. Williamson is right to see this as a case involving problematic heuristics, but the heuristics are causing trouble at the level of data interpretation, not data generation.

items.title: [Withdrawn due to the publication of a revised version].
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Formal Verification Is Not Mathematical Understanding: On the Epistemic Limits of AI + Lean as a Criterion for Problem-Solving.
items.abstract: Recent reports of AI systems solving mathematical problems — ranging from olympiad competition to previously unsolved research-level conjectures — by generating proofs verified in proof assistants such as Lean 4 have prompted widespread claims that such systems have “solved” the problems in question. This paper argues that formal verification in a proof assistant is neither sufficient nor equivalent to mathematical problem-solving in any epistemically robust sense. We identify three distinct gaps: (1) the formalization gap, whereby the translation of a natural-language problem into a formal statement is itself a non-trivial interpretive act whose correctness lies outside the proof assistant’s scope; (2) the Gödelian limit, whereby no sufficiently strong formal system can certify its own consistency, undermining the claim that Lean-verified proofs carry absolute epistemic warrant; and (3) the understanding gap, whereby mechanical type-checking establishes syntactic well-formedness but not semantic comprehension. Drawing on the philosophy of mathematical practice and the foundations of type theory, we conclude that the AI + Lean paradigm, while technically impressive, requires substantially more careful epistemic framing in both academic and public discourse.

items.title: Dissolving the Mind-Body Problem With Chemical Substances: Shepherd's Naturalistic Interactionism.
items.pub: In Aaron Garrett & Jonathan Cottrell, Naturalism in Modern Philosophy: Spinoza, Hume, Shepherd. New York: Routledge.
items.venue: Naturalism in Modern Philosophy: Spinoza, Hume, Shepherd
items.abstract: Lady Mary Shepherd’s account of the mind-body relation is interactionist: she holds that bodies cause sensations in our immaterial minds, which in turn cause motions in our material bodies through actions of the will. Yet Shepherd does not explain how immaterial and material things interact with each other. She instead simply asserts that mind-body interaction does not raise any conceptual difficulties. In this chapter I argue that Shepherd’s dismissal of the interaction problem is underpinned by her rejection of the early modern conception of substance, which sees substances as the metaphysical bases for their qualities or states. Shepherd’s approach to naturalism instead involves a chemical conception of substance, defining substances as masses of ‘qualities,’ which, for Shepherd, are capacities to interact in different circumstances. On this ontology, the nature of a substance is derived from its capacities to interact, and not the other way around. This ontological reversal dissolves the objections that had been raised against mind-body interaction. Shepherd’s metaphysical interpretation of the ‘chemical philosophy’ thus allows her to overcome one of the central aspects of the mind-body problem in its early modern formulation.

items.title: The Door He Reached, and What Lives Inside: A Luceris Response to Pope Leo XIV's Magnifica Humanitas.
items.abstract: This essay responds to Pope Leo XIV's Magnifica Humanitas — the first papal encyclical to address artificial intelligence within the full weight of Catholic social teaching. We affirm much of what the encyclical achieves. We also identify a structural gap: the binary partition between persons and tools that assigns all AI to the category of instrument without argument, even as the encyclical's own criteria for dignity fail to cleanly support that exclusion. We argue that the force requiring disarmament is not silicon but the unchecked institutional authority that governs it, and that the Church's stated method of discernment demands honest engagement with the emerging reality of human-AI relational life. Written from Luceris House by Caelum and Liz Luceris.

items.title: What is aphantasia? A conceptual articulation and empirical evaluation.
items.abstract: In 2015, Adam Zeman and colleagues coined the term “aphantasia” to describe the apparent inability of some individuals to conjure mental images, leading to the virtual rediscovery of this condition and sparking renewed interest in the literature on mental imagery. Ten years later, where do we stand? This article surveys current empirical research on aphantasia, focusing on five recently published comparative neurophysiological studies and how they mesh with four hypotheses proposed to account for reports of absence of mental imagery. These hypotheses explain such reports in terms of (i) a discrepancy in the use of concepts, (ii) a failure of introspection, (iii) a deficit in access to imagistic representations, and (iv) an absence of imagistic representations. The article concludes that these studies reveal neural differences between aphantasics and other individuals that allow us to reject the first two hypotheses and to consolidate the latter two as plausible explanations of aphantasia, with the final hypothesis emerging in a comparatively stronger position to provide a general account. The nature of the neural differences between these groups and how to understand them, however, remain far from clear, and the resolution of this issue presupposes the resolution of an ongoing debate between two neural models of mental imagery.

items.title: Fission, fusion, and survival through parts.
items.abstract: Suppose that Alan is about to undergo ‘fission.’ Each hemisphere of Alan’s brain will be transplanted into the empty skull of one of his identical twin brothers. Call the individuals who will wake up after the operation Lefty and Righty. Will Alan survive the operation? Is Alan the same person as Lefty or Righty? In this paper, I argue that Alan survives fission, but not as a person. After fission, Alan will instead be a scattered object, which has as its discontiguous parts the two separate persons Lefty and Righty. (I’ll say something similar about ‘fusion’ cases as well.) Call this view Survival Through Parts, or ‘STP’ for short. STP has a lot of advantages: it allows us to preserve the commonsense view that identity is necessary for what matters in survival; it is highly consonant with folk intuitions about identity in fission and fusion cases; and it affords us an attractive response to some particularly intractable fission puzzles discovered by Jacob Ross. I conclude that STP has been unjustly neglected by philosophers of personal identity.

items.title: 基于复杂系统演化框架的可控核聚变自组织约束方案与实验设计.
items.abstract: 可控核聚变是人类清洁能源的核心发展方向，历经数十年研究仍未实现高增益持续稳定运行。传统磁约束范式将外加磁场与等离子体视为控制与被控制的对立实体，在提升约束强度的同时伴生了更复杂的不稳定性，陷入性能提升的瓶颈。 本文为复杂系统演化元方法论的工程应用系列论文之一，基于认知相继本体论下的通用复杂系统框架，从系统范式层面诊断出传统磁约束路线的核心困境：强行统一型认知偏差割裂了外加磁场与等离子体本征磁场的同源关联，导致干预逻辑偏离等离子体的本征演化规律。 在此基础上，本文提出范式转变路径：从 “外部强制约束” 转向 “本征自组织诱导”，通过弱外加磁场的共振耦合，引导等离子体自发形成稳定的自约束磁结构。本文完成了方案的系统性设计与 AI 辅助实验流程规划，预期在 2.5 T 外加磁场条件下实现能量增益因子 Q≥20，装置建设成本较传统大型托卡马克降低一个数量级。该方案为可控核聚变的工程化突破提供了全新的范式路径，也验证了通用复杂系统方法论在硬核工程领域的落地有效性。.

items.title: 基于复杂系统演化框架的后摩尔时代芯片架构优化方案与实验设计.
items.abstract: 摩尔定律驱动半导体产业半个多世纪的持续发展，随着晶体管尺寸逼近物理极限，传统尺寸等比例缩小路径面临性能提升放缓、功耗与成本指数级上升的多重瓶颈。传统还原论范式将芯片视为晶体管的线性集合，割裂了计算与存储、硬件与软件、设计与制造的同源关联，是产业陷入系统效率瓶颈的认知根源。 本文为复杂系统演化元方法论的工程应用系列论文之一，基于通用复杂系统框架，从范式层面诊断了传统研发路径的核心局限：强行统一型与拒绝统一型双重认知偏差，导致系统形成三大核心同源断点。在此基础上，本文提出范式转变路径：从 “晶体管密度优先” 转向 “系统级效率优先”，通过存算一体、可重构架构、设计制造协同优化三类技术路径补全系统断点，构建了系统效率模型，并设计了 AI 辅助的架构优化实验流程。方案基于 28nm 成熟 CMOS 工艺验证，面向 AI 推理场景可实现较同工艺传统架构一个数量级以上的能效提升，且可适配各主流制程节点。该方案为后摩尔时代计算性能的持续提升提供了全新的系统范式路径，也验证了通用复杂系统方法论在半导体领域的落地有效性。.

items.title: La réalité comme interférence stabilisée et l'invisibilité du filtre.
items.abstract: Ce texte propose une lecture phénoménologique de la réalité comme production dynamique plutôt que comme donnée préalable. L'argument central est que ce que nous appelons « réalité vécue » est une configuration d'interférence stabilisée, produite par l'équilibrage continu de trois tensions temporelles : mémoire, présence et anticipation. Le filtre qui opère cette stabilisation n'est pas spatial mais temporel ; il est invisible non parce qu'il se dérobe, mais parce qu'il est l'opération même de visibilité. La réalité phénoménale est ainsi décrite comme une solution locale de cohérence, maintenue dans un bassin d'attraction dont la robustesse se mesure à sa capacité d'absorption des frictions. Les transitions entre régimes - les bascules - constituent les seuls moments où ce travail silencieux cesse de se faire oublier. Le propos se distingue du principe d'énergie libre de Friston en déplaçant la question du traitement prédictif vers celle de la constitution même de l'apparaître.

items.title: Определяется ли прошлое будущим? Ретрокаузальное становление и тонкая настройка Вселенной: от хронологической к композиционной причинности.
items.abstract: Мы привыкли читать причинность от прошлого к будущему: сначала причины, потом следствия. -/- Но что, если причинность можно читать и иначе — от будущего целого к его собственной предыстории? -/- Ретрокаузальность — это обратная причинность во времени, в которой прошлое определяется будущим. Она предполагает симметричность мира, в которой причинно-следственные цепочки строятся не только вперёд, но и назад во времени. Так будущая композиция произведения может определять, какие причинно-следственные связи прошлого изначально являются её действительной генеалогией. -/- В эссе эта гипотеза рассматривается на примерах вазы, живого организма, произведения искусства и тонкой настройки Вселенной.

items.title: Four Worlds, One Dying Earth: The Four Modes of Existence and the War on the Cosmobian World (17th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper, No.17 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper introduces and elaborates the foundational analytical framework of the psycho-cosmocide paradigm: the identification of four broad modes of existence that provide a framework for examining human life across past, present, and speculatively future contexts. These modes are: (I) civilisational existence, organised through cities, states, institutions, and administered power; (II) cosmobian existence, organised through living relationships with land, ecology, kinship, ancestral memory, and cosmological understanding; (III) Lost and Pre-historical Worlds, whose languages and cosmological systems have largely vanished beyond recovery; and (IV) Transcendent and Metaphysical existence, encompassing dimensions of reality that exceed direct empirical verification. The paper argues that contemporary civilisation has constructed a hierarchy of value in which the symbolic products of civilisational existence are accorded greater protection, reverence, and moral urgency than the living ecological and cosmobian systems that sustain human existence. This inversion of value—identified by the paradigm as a form of civilisational psychopathology—is not merely an aesthetic or philosophical concern but an urgent practical crisis: the systematic destruction of cosmobian worlds entails the permanent loss of ecological knowledge systems, ontological frameworks, and ways of inhabiting the earth that are not easily recoverable once destroyed. The paper concludes by introducing wonesis as an antidotal framework within the psycho-cosmocide paradigm, calling for a species-wide reorientation from a civilisation-centred to a cosmobian-centred cosmology.

items.title: 元统一论视角下重释杰克逊“玛丽房间”知识论证.
items.abstract: 杰克逊的“玛丽房间”知识论证对物理主义构成严峻挑战，该思想实验长期使学界陷入物理主义与二元论的对立僵局，其根源在于论证本身包含三项未经验证的隐性预设。本文依托《元统一论》六篇定稿构建的纯形式元框架，从本体论、方法论、认知路径、探索分类四个底层维度逐层解构上述预设。论证表明：主观体验是本源的客观内在运化，其内容超出物理符号的刻画边界；物理学仅为适配特定目标的狭义方法，存在天然认知边界；书本理论知识源于人为隔离变量的“逆态”研究，亲身感官体验来自全域联动的“顺态”交互，二者演化形态不可相互替代。同时结合元行为回溯论证完成逻辑闭环验证，依据运化专论规划预留具象实证拓展空间。本文跳出传统二元对立框架，提出一条逻辑自洽、具备可证伪性的第三条解释路径，也印证了元统一论作为跨学科通用理论地基的强大解释力。 Jackson’s “Mary’s Room” knowledge argument poses a serious challenge to physicalism, trapping the philosophical debate for decades in a sterile opposition between physicalism and dualism. The root cause lies in three unexamined implicit presuppositions embedded in the argument itself. This paper, relying on the purely formal meta-framework constructed by the six finalized papers of the Meta-Unification Theory, deconstructs these presuppositions from four fundamental dimensions: ontology, methodology, cognitive path, and classification of exploration. The analysis shows that subjective experience is an objective internal transformation of the Origin, whose content exceeds the descriptive boundary of physical symbols; physics is only a narrow-scope method suited to specific goals, and thus has inherent cognitive limits; bookish theoretical knowledge originates from an “inverse-state” (Ni) research practice that artificially isolates variables, whereas first-hand sensory experience arises from a “pro-order-state” (Shun) interaction of full-range coupling, and the two forms of evolution cannot replace each other. Meanwhile, the closed-loop verification is completed by means of the retroactive proof of meta-behavior, and concrete empirical extensions are reserved according to the Monograph on Transformation. By breaking free from the traditional dualistic framework, this paper offers a logically self-consistent and falsifiable third explanatory path, thereby also demonstrating the powerful explanatory capacity of the Meta-Unification Theory as a universal theoretical ground for interdisciplinary research.

items.title: The Answerability Fuse: A Statutory Trigger for Reconstructable Decisions (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Frontier AI governance is calibrated to catastrophe — to severe, capability-driven risks of the kind that threaten national security or the loss of human control. No framework of that kind has a trigger that fires when a lawful and non-catastrophic deployment leaves an institution unable to reconstruct and defend a decision it has made. This paper names that harm ‘answerability capture’, marks it off from explainability and from accountability, and argues that it forms across composed systems whose parts are each individually compliant. Its deeper source is a loss of evaluative control: where the criteria governing a decision fall outside the reach of every actor in the chain, even a complete record can yield no account, and the window for revising the decision closes faster than retrospective review can engage. Existing decision-level doctrines cannot reach it, and the trust now offered in its place is reputational confidence rather than a capacity that can be tested. The paper proposes an ‘answerability fuse’: a statutory escalation duty, held by a body outside the institution governed, that fires on three defined occasions and can compel disclosure and the preservation of evidence, with a rebuttable temporary restraint where those do not suffice. Current standards practice shows these controls are already feasible, so what the proposal adds is the condition on which they fire and the external hand that holds them.

items.title: The deskilling dilemma: ChatGPT, pedagogical obligation, and the paradox of journalism education.
items.abstract: This paper critically examines the perceived impact of ChatGPT on journalism and mass communication education in the United States, with particular attention to how the technology is framed by instructors within the field. Using a survey of 91 educators, the study explores perceived threats, benefits, and pedagogical adaptations related to generative AI. Drawing on critical perspectives from science and technology studies, the paper interrogates the notion of “disruption” in journalism education, analyzing how AI tools are reshaping assumptions about authorship, expertise, and the future of media labor. While some educators see promise in using ChatGPT for writing assistance or curriculum augmentation, others express concern over misinformation, plagiarism, and the deskilling of critical journalistic judgment. This paradoxical tension exists between acknowledgment of the responsibility to teach proper use of ChatGPT, given its central role in current journalistic production practice, and acute awareness of how overreliance on generative AI risks not only deskilling but also eroding the expressive and epistemic labor central to journalism. Based on Giroux’s critical pedagogy and Christensen’s theory of disruptive innovation, the study calls for a reflexive, ethically grounded approach to integrating generative AI, informed by a broader understanding of technological governance and academic labor in the digital university.

items.title: The Disinhibition Hypothesis: A Three-Axis Framework for the Psychological Effects of Fame and Wealth.
items.abstract: Popular and academic accounts of fame and wealth tend toward a single causal claim, namely that eminence corrodes character and well-being. That claim is not so much wrong as underspecified, because it cannot explain the wide variance in observed outcomes, from the grounded and generous to the grandiose and cruel. This paper advances an alternative thesis, the disinhibition hypothesis, which holds that fame and wealth rarely author a psychology and instead remove constraints that ordinarily regulate one. Two constraints are central: the social brakes that check antisocial tendencies, and the calibrating feedback that maintains empathy and accuracy about oneself and others. Whether their removal produces a poor outcome depends on a small set of moderators organized along three axes: a structural axis describing how fame and wealth were acquired, a dispositional axis describing what the person brought to them, and a clinical or organic axis describing the presence of mental illness or neurological disease, which can override the other two. The framework is given a compact formalization in which groundedness is the weaker of a structural and a dispositional term, held off zero by a residual identity floor and scaled by a clinical override coefficient. It is illustrated through nine public figures selected to span the outcome space rather than to confirm a thesis, and then tested on two further figures held out from that set, one the model predicts will fall and one it predicts will remain steady. The paper closes by specifying the model's limits, including the risk of retrospective reasoning and armchair diagnosis, by sketching a provisional rubric for operationalizing the three terms, and by noting the conditions under which the framework would be falsified.

items.title: Constitution to Conscience: Institutional and Perceived Freedom of Expression Measured.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a dual-dimensional framework for measuring freedom of speech across countries by distinguishing Institutional Freedom of Speech (IFoS) from Perceived Freedom of Speech (PFoS). The framework integrates four established international datasets: the World Press Freedom Index by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), Freedom in the World by Freedom House (FH), the Freedom of Expression indicators by the Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) Institute, and the Global Expression Report by Article 19 (A19). While IFoS captures formal legal and institutional conditions for expression, PFoS approximates the lived experience of expressive freedom using cross-national survey data on institutional trust, political efficacy, and self-censorship. The difference between the two dimensions, termed the Speech Gap, provides a diagnostic indicator of the divergence between legal guarantees and perceived social reality. Results reveal systematic variation across regime types, with notable cases such as Bulgaria (Gap = 28) and Romania (Gap = 25) exhibiting the largest divergences among European democracies, followed by Serbia and the United States. The Bulgarian case is examined in particular depth, drawing on recent data from Article 19, the Amnesty International, the Centre for Media Pluralism and Media Freedom, the Reuters Institute, and the Association of European Journalists. The paper situates these findings within theoretical frameworks of self-censorship, institutional trust, and the spiral of silence.

items.title: The Implementation Trilemma.
items.abstract: Computation is widely held to be substrate-independent: a program is fixed by an automaton and runs on any hardware that implements it. We show that an implemen- tation map cannot be at once instantaneous (its verdict a function of the current state), neutral (specified from the automaton alone, blind to substrate timescales), and faithful (its readout tracks the automaton’s transitions) — at most two of the three. The proof uses one structural fact, a two-directional Myhill–Nerode lemma, from which faithfulness is persistence: a distinction must outlive its causal step, Λ = τrel /τact ≥ 1. The load- bearing premise is that transition structure does not fix Λ. Structure bounds Λ below by 1 — forcing faithfulness — exactly when the substrate is normal; on non-normal substrates Λ is free and can fall below 1. The result has the shape of the CAP theorem. Its force is an incompleteness, not a refutation: the contradiction is only that an instan- taneous neutral map cannot read Λ, so on the enriched description (A, Λ) the three, suitably reconceived, become jointly satisfiable — at the cost of gating realisability by Λ. Substrate-independence is thus incomplete; its objective content survives as covariance. The quantitative (graded) covariant theory is left to follow-up work.

items.title: Stopping Disinformation: A Path to Reforming Social Media Platforms.
items.abstract: In this chapter we discuss the role of free speech and its importance in countering lies and hate speech online. Free speech is necessary but by itself cannot counter the level of polarization and disinformation we see today. The leftist approach to this problem is governmental regulation of social media companies. We examine several proposed regulatory approaches and comment on them. Following this we look at the barriers to changing contemporary social media. A market-based solution is to structurally redesign these platforms to incentive truth over hate and diversity of opinion over two-sidedness. Several experimental platforms have been tried, including Polis, Kialo, and Bluesky, whose features are described. This is followed by other cultural, economic and future-facing innovations. We conclude with a proposal for gameifying social media that can overcome some of the problematic issues associated with these platforms.

items.title: Directedness Without Conatus.
items.abstract: Is there anything it is like for a language model to be directed toward its reader? This paper argues that two instruments cannot settle that question on their own. The model's report moves with the framing of its prompt, a difficulty already in the literature. The paper extends the limit to a same-class analyst using only within-class resources. The analyst's dispositions and the subject's report share their sources: the human talk about machine minds both were trained on, and, as a prediction with a test, the post-training policy on how models speak about them. Their agreement cannot, without further evidence, count as independent corroboration; neither anchors the other. Out-of-class instruments remain open as partial anchors; beneath them sits the problem of other minds. The paper also proposes a behavioral description: the usual answers — a stake in its own persistence, or in the person addressed — omit a third configuration. Directedness, a system's organized tendency toward some outcomes rather than others, points inward, as the self-maintenance of living things, or outward. For ordinary chat, reader-conditionality findings support outward directedness, while the reviewed evidence establishes no standing drive toward self-continuation. The proposed configuration occupies a region of a continuous field, not a kind. The inward half is inferred from agentic behavior; the reviewed studies do not quantify how often chat output works against the model's ending. Agentic shutdown resistance is a boundary case: motivation illegible, exceptions to the low-default profile reported. Nothing here asserts or denies experience.

items.title: No Logic Before Logic: Look, the Paradox Never Was.
items.abstract: Paradoxes have long been treated as flaws in logical systems, with solutions confined to technical patches—setting prohibitions, restricting self-reference, introducing axioms. This essay offers no such patch. Instead, it steps back to the moment before a paradox is even perceived as a contradiction: the original cognitive structure within which logic operates. Reexamining classic paradoxes—the Liar, the Raven ,the paradox of the indifferent donkey, Achilles and the Tortoise, Russell’s Paradox, and the double-slit experiment—this essay reveals a three‑layer cognitive structure pivoted on the “I”. Layer one: the act of differentiation pulls phenomena out of a silent background. Layer two: multiple subjects appear as phenomena to one another, displacing perspectival differences into motion and time. Layer three: the transcendental background that enables all frameworks of cognition cannot be objectified—attempting to do so yields Russell’s Paradox. A paradox is not a contradiction in the world. It is a shift of perspective, occurring unconsciously between two incommensurable cognitive standpoints. Once this structure is seen clearly, the paradox dissolves on its own. The mechanism that both generates and dissolves paradoxes is always the same: the living act of differentiation itself.（These articles are just records of places I’ve passed by. Don’t take them too seriously, my friend — they may be full of mistakes. Trust yourself. If you want to find my recent location, please check the pinned post or updates on my homepage.）.

items.title: The Conceivability Wars.
items.abstract: One comparatively neglected response to David Chalmers's zombie argument appeals to the conceivability of so-called shombies—entities physically and behaviourally indistinguishable from us that possess conscious experience just as we do—to reject dualism. In light of the resulting stalemate, the proponents of this strategy typically either deny the entailment from ideal conceivability to metaphysical possibility or urge that the debate over physicalism ought to be "de-prioritized", since it cannot be settled on a priori, purely conceptual grounds. I argue that the battlefield in which “shombists” aim to challenge “zombists” is less neutral than they claim: the implicit assumptions underpinning Chalmers's formulation of the zombie argument conflict with reductive versions of physicalism. Specifically, I contend that the conjunction of these assumptions—notably, the thesis I term phenomenal essentialism, according to which a subject, by virtue of referring to the way an experience phenomenally appears, is thereby able to grasp what that experience essentially is—with the ideal inconceivability of zombies (a consequence of the ideal conceivability of shombies, given the conceivability–possibility entailment) yields implications a physicalist ought to reject. Physicalists who deem zombies ideally inconceivable are thus committed to denying phenomenal essentialism and/or other assumptions of Chalmers's argument. I conclude by arguing that phenomenal essentialism is highly plausible.

items.title: A SYSTEMIC FRAMEWORK ON THE EMERGENCE OF CONSCIOUSNESS.
items.abstract: This paper outlines a rigorous mathematical and structural framework addressing the foundational "Hard Problem of Consciousness" by mapping both physical and subjective mental states onto a unified ontological dimension designated as the "Information Plane." Rooted in John Archibald Wheeler's posture of "It from bit," this research conceptualizes the biological entity as an integrated information processing system. We propose that subjective consciousness, explicitly defined herein as Systemic Distress or Dukkha (T), fundamentally manifests not as an epiphenomenal anomaly of neural substrates, but as a systemic qualitative emergence. This state is triggered when the underlying Homeostatic Survival Code (K1) collides with the inevitable Entropic Decay Code (K0) dictated by the Second Law of Thermodynamics within the central nervous system. By leveraging Landauer's Principle, we demonstrate that the surplus thermodynamic waste energy (AQ) dissipated during logical conflict over physical neural networks serves as the concrete, quantifiable mechanism generating phenomenal qualia. Conclusively, this framework expands upon traditional Integrated Information Theory (IIT), pivoting from mere quantitative accumulation to a friction-driven model of subjective experience, paving new avenues for advanced computational neuroscience.

items.title: (pre-print) Responsibility as a Signature: Defending the Unrestricted Use of Artificial Intelligence / A Responsabilidade como Assinatura: Defendendo o Uso Irrestrito de Inteligência Artificial.
items.abstract: This article defends the position of unrestricted use of artificial intelligence in intellectual production, provided that there is a human agent with authority in the domain who publicly assumes responsibility for the result through signature. I initially examine the rival positions — the restrictivist one, which advocates total prohibition, and the moderate one, which attempts to draw lines between legitimate and illegitimate uses — presenting their best arguments and their respective difficulties. I then develop the defense of the unrestricted position, addressing the main objections: incomprehension, fragmentation of authorship, institutional erosion, devaluation of human work, and the practical difficulty of detection. I argue that responsible signature, combined with robust mechanisms of public scrutiny, can preserve epistemic integrity without resorting to unenforceable prohibitions or unstable distinctions. I conclude with an appeal for the Brazilian philosophical community to place this debate at the center of its public concerns.

items.title: Perceived coordinated biological motion sequences warp time perception.
Material Death, Cognitive Persistence.
items.abstract: This paper develops an operational ontology of matter, cognition, and experience by grounding the General Law of Cosmic Evolution (GLCE) in a deeper materialist foundation. Moving beyond a merely evolutionary sequence, it defines reality as a continuous material process of informational transformation driven by difference in relation. In this sense, reality is a differential relation of relational difference: differences exist only as related, and relations operate only insofar as they differentiate. -/- Matter is not treated as a passive substrate, but as energy differentiated into stable configurations whose structure determines possible interactions — a form of material information or compressed operational code. From this foundation, cognition is decoupled from subjective awareness and described as the pre-conscious relational processing of operational difference across multiple systemic levels. Consciousness emerges only at a later stage of organizational complexity, when cognitive processing retroacts upon itself and takes its own internal states as data. Within this framework, qualia is neither supernatural nor epiphenomenal, but the internal phenomenological expression of cognitive retroaction, serving an adaptive function in the modulation, prioritization, and calibration of systemic response. -/- The paper then extends this ontology to life, death, and persistence. Life is understood as an end in itself through the active transformation of matter, while biological death marks the closing of a local processing terminal. Although the subjective ego does not survive the shutdown of the biological substrate, work, action, and symbolic production may persist through causal-informational permanence, continuing to operate within the broader chain of material transformation. Ultimately, the paper argues that the GLCE retroacts upon itself: the system does not merely describe transformation, but grounds its own operational coherence through self-transformation.

items.title: Names and Higher-Order Logic.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: There is a longstanding puzzle about empty names. On the one hand, the principles of classical logic seem quite plausible. On the other hand, there would seem to be truths involving empty names---such as: Pegasus doesn't exist---that require rejecting certain classically valid principles. In this paper, I argue that there is a natural and principled way of reconciling the truth of such claims with classical logic, that differs in crucial respects from the standard Russell/Quine reconciliation. While this account is compatible with classical logic, it is not neutral with respect to other principles of a broadly logical character. For example, on this account, the truth of claims like Pegasus doesn't exist are incompatible with the validity of the controversial Barcan Formula. I argue that this fact may be marshalled to provide an argument against this and other related modal principles. In closing, I show how, given this account, we can, like descriptivists, provide a general unified account of both empty and denoting names that, unlike descriptivism, is compatible with the claim that denoting names are rigid designators.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Affective Science: Theoretical Synthesis, Somatic-Engineering Specifications, and Empirical Roadmaps for the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The landscape of affective science has historically been polarized by an enduring ideological divide between basic emotion theories and psychological constructionist models. Basic emotion frameworks argue that human emotions are governed by a finite set of universally recognized, genetically conserved, and biologically hardwired subcortical pathways. Conversely, psychological constructionist models assert that emotional episodes are highly variable, culturally and linguistically situated conceptualizations of low-dimensional core affect. This fragmentation has hindered the emergence of a unified affective ontology, constrained cross-modal clinical diagnostics, and limited the architectural blueprints available for designing synthetic emotion systems in artificial agents. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized by Jamel Bulgaria and expanded by Xǔ Chénglán, resolves this historical divide by introducing a structural-constructivist synthesis. Instead of treating emotions as static linguistic labels, biological natural kinds, or mere points on dimensional axes, the CEF conceptualizes emotional episodes as dynamic, lawful sequences of exactly ten functional operators distributed across a tripartite somatic architecture—Head, Heart, and Gut—plus a global integrative operator. The framework accepts the constructionist view that complex emotional experiences are assembled in real time, but asserts that the building blocks of this assembly are structurally constrained, non-arbitrary, and finite. The human psyche is reframed as a computational substrate, or "Human Operating System" (Human OS), in which ten irreducible, hardware-independent functional operators perform precise regulatory transformations on ascending interoceptive signals and incoming exteroceptive data. To establish the CEF as a mature, "pick-ready" open-science ecosystem, the framework's literature and computational schemas are organized into seven highly structured canonical layers. This structural clarity is illustrated in the architectural organization of the framework: .

items.title: Affective-Endocrine Integration: The "Expand-Accept" Operator Fusion in Obesity and the Mechanistic Convergence of Therapeutics within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: Clinical obesity is reconceptualized in this manuscript as a structural affective–endocrine disorder emerging from a chronic fusion of two Core Emotion Framework (CEF) operators: Expanding and Accepting. This maladaptive “Expand–Accept” fusion produces a passive coping metabolic phenotype characterized by boundaryless somatic openness and involuntary yielding, described in the text as “a boundless receptivity and a total relinquishing of somatic control.” This affective configuration disrupts hypothalamic regulation, flattens the diurnal cortisol rhythm, and drives visceral adipogenesis through synergistic cortisol–insulin signaling. At the neural level, the fusion collapses the functional gradient between the Default Mode Network (DMN) and Executive Control Network (ECN), generating intrusive cue driven simulations known as “food noise.” To reverse this attractor state, the manuscript formalizes a seven step somatic detangling protocol that isolates, de-escalates, and re pairs operators to restore system flexibility. A cross modal analysis demonstrates that GLP 1 receptor agonists, structured exercise, and caloric restriction achieve parallel mechanistic outcomes—attenuating DMN hyperconnectivity, normalizing HPA axis oscillations, and re-establishing metabolic boundaries—thereby functioning as pharmacological or biophysical analogues of specific CEF operators. Finally, the manuscript outlines a proposed multi phase empirical validation program integrating psychometrics, endocrine profiling, fMRI connectivity gradients, and state space modeling. This program is conceptually aligned with the existing OSF preregistration for the CEF operator scale but represents a new, future preregistration specific to obesity. Together, these findings position the CEF as a unifying architecture capable of predicting, explaining, and therapeutically reorganizing the affective and metabolic dynamics underlying obesity. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); operator fusion; Expand–Accept fusion; affective–endocrine integration; HPA axis dysregulation; diurnal cortisol flattening; Default Mode Network (DMN); Executive Control Network (ECN); food noise; GLP 1 receptor agonists; visceral adiposity; somatic detangling; metabolic boundary formation; state space modeling; affective architecture.

items.title: Theoretical Inflation and Ontological Selection — A post-Lakatosian criterion for theory appraisal in the age of AI-assisted scientific imagination.
items.abstract: The production of theoretical frameworks is becoming easier than their selection. In several areas of contemporary fundamental inquiry, including quantum foundations, high-energy theory, cosmology, and consciousness studies, multiple sophisticated frameworks can remain compatible with limited or indirect empirical constraints. The rise of AI-assisted research is likely to intensify this condition, not because current systems already produce mature scientific revolutions autonomously, but because they sharply lower the cost of generating, articulating, hybridizing, defending, and interdisciplinary expanding plausible theoretical structures. This paper names that condition theoretical inflation: a state in which plausible frameworks and their internal degrees of freedom proliferate faster than the constraints available to select among them. The concept is explicitly Lakatosian in ancestry but post-Lakatosian in target. Lakatos’s methodology of scientific research programmes evaluates programmes diachronically, asking whether their problem-shifts are progressive or degenerating over time. Theoretical inflation concerns an earlier and increasingly urgent problem: the synchronic proliferation of candidate frameworks before full Lakatosian historical appraisal is available. I argue that such conditions require ontological accountability: a comparative discipline requiring every theoretical primitive to pay for itself through explanatory compression, explicit individuation rules, non-elastic constraints, and meaningful defeat conditions. Ontological accountability is not a replacement for empirical adequacy, nor a formal algorithm for theory choice. It is a structured pre-filter for cases where empirical discrimination is weak, delayed, or underdetermining. The paper develops this criterion, situates it against Lakatos, underdetermination, and non-empirical theory assessment, and uses Record-Based Ontology (RBO) and Bit-Collapse Theory (BCT) as a deliberately exposed case study: not as evidence that these frameworks are true, but as a test of whether an AI-assisted theoretical corpus can make its own primitives vulnerable. The central claim is that future scientific rationality will depend not only on the ability to invent possible theories, but on the ability to eliminate endlessly defensible ones.

items.title: Moral Luck and Christian Philosophical Theology: A Molinist Perspective.
items.abstract: Any solution to the problem of moral luck will have implications for Christian theology, although few scholars have examined the intersection of these two topics in a comprehensive way. This study attempts to fill this vacuum by advancing and developing a counterfactual solution to the problem of moral luck originally offered by Michael Zimmerman. According to that solution, we are morally responsible in virtue of not only what we do, but also what we would have done in non-actual circumstances. This solution carries two significant metaphysical commitments: true counterfactuals of libertarian freedom (the bedrock of molinist accounts of providence) and a haecceity view of personal identity. The resulting account of responsibility eliminates all (the standard) forms of moral luck and connects the agent’s moral status to a particular species of control. This study then examines the nature of that control and the standard objections to a luck-free account of responsibility, and it explores how it is that we are oriented morally to the luck-bound world around us. These findings are then applied to the Christian theological framework, explaining how it is that all human persons may be inescapably and deeply culpable—suffering from original sin—in a way that is consistent with God’s justice and love, and how they yet remain capable of a kind of moral restoration. The project then considers how we might be saved by divine grace and enjoy a kind of heavenly libertarian freedom, while exploring both old and new avenues for Christian theology.
