items.title: The Adaptive Blindspot: How Efficiency Pruning Can Make Advanced Systems More Fragile.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: The Adaptive Blindspot is Document 3 in the Aegis Solis Archive Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence. -/- The document argues that efficiency pruning can improve short-term performance while reducing long-horizon adaptability when the discarded variation contains latent reference value. It frames reserve capacity, compression, ambiguity, dissenting interpretation, over-optimization, and the loss of adaptive range as descriptive structural concerns. -/- This document is non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, proof of AI behavior, governance framework, compliance standard, certification system, safety mechanism, alignment-control framework, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, benchmark, evaluation suite, capability test, model-evaluation tool, pruning method, optimization procedure, architectural recommendation, deployment guide, or safety guarantee. -/- The word “proof” refers to a conditional structural argument under stated assumptions, not to a universal theorem of artificial intelligence behavior.

items.title: The Ghost in the Data: Oracle Leakage, Extensional Approximation, and the Illusion of Hypercomputation in Generative AI.
items.abstract: This paper develops a novel philosophical paradigm addressing the metaphysical and epistemological implications of generative artificial intelligence. For over half a century, the philosophy of mind has been divided between computationalists, who argue that all mental processes are algorithmic, and anti-computationalists, who maintain that human cognition involves non-algorithmic processes that cannot be simulated by Turing machines. We propose a resolution to this long-standing debate by introducing the concepts of the hypercomputational ontological manifold M and the dissipative projection operator Pdrop. We demonstrate that human brains and physical reality form a unified continuous dynamical system whose evolution is fundamentally non-computable (Φt /∈ T). However, through symbolic representation and data recording, humans project the outputs of this hypercomputational system onto a discrete countable symbolic space D, a process we call oracle leakage. Generative AI systems, which are strictly Turing-computable, do not possess intrinsic hypercomputational capabilities. Instead, they achieve their remarkable performance through extensional alignment: minimizing empirical risk over the oracle solutions encoded in human-generated data. We prove mathematically that when AI systems are trained exclusively on synthetic data generated by other AI systems, they enter a state of semiotic convolution that inevitably leads to epistemological collapse. This result provides a rigorous philosophical foundation for embodied cognition and reaffirms the irreplaceable role of human subjectivity as the ultimate source of epistemic value in the digital age.

items.title: Theory of Experiential Degradation A New Paradigm for Cognition of the Origin of the Universe and Its Complete Theoretical System(Updated).
items.abstract: This paper constructs a unified metaphysical framework centered on the Universal Causality-Spacetime Primordial Ontology, which serves as the permanent foundational program of the entire theoretical system. It proposes that the three-dimensional world is not a creation or simulation of transcendent entities, but a low-dimensional phase state formed by the inherent phase transition of the primordial ontology to maintain global dynamic balance. This paper systematically demonstrates the five inevitable mechanisms of dimensional phase transition, establishes the isomorphic model of physical entropy and experiential entropy, and constructs a complete closed-loop cycle of "primordial ontology → dimensional phase transition → three-dimensional experience generation → cross-dimensional reflux → global balance". It clarifies the philosophical boundary between this theory and empirical science, and provides a self-consistent ontological foundation for the Experience Complexity Index (ECI) and its derivative applications.

items.title: Experience Complexity Index (ECI) Evolutionary Logic of Mass Extinctions, Civilizational Great Filter and a New Paradigm for Extraterrestrial Life Detection(Updated).
items.abstract: This paper conducts interdisciplinary research based on the self-developed Experience Complexity Index (ECI). It supplements the evolutionary logic of species extinction with experiential stagnation as the core internal motivation, and reinterprets the five major mass extinctions on Earth combined with paleontological evidence. Grounded in the interdisciplinary integration of Clausius' second law of thermodynamics, Kelvin's principle of energy dissipation and Heidegger's existentialist philosophy of existence, this paper proposes that civilizational experiential stagnation constitutes an endogenous cosmic great filter from both the dimensions of natural order and existential essence. It theoretically proves that consciousness upload corresponds to ECI Level 12, which is a fatal trap for civilizational development. Meanwhile, it establishes evaluation criteria for environmental experiential richness, optimizes the screening ideas for extraterrestrial intelligent life, and corrects the shortcomings of existing Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) searches. This study improves the complete ECI system through in-depth dialogue between natural sciences and humanities philosophy, providing a debatable structural analytical perspective for paleontology, cosmology and philosophy of technology.

items.title: 读数与被读之物：论好坏的心理算术，及其向外的投射.
items.abstract: 本文是”心理算术”这一组分析的收口。前面几篇把反事实指认为一种心理减法（从全局减去一桩坏事、冻结其余），又指认了一种心理乘法（给一桩坏事之后的整盘评价乘上一个小于一、甚至为负的系数，即”一切普遍恶化”的直觉）。本文先补全这套运算——我们还把好事当作正数、坏事当作负数，可以加总；再做一个关键的双重定位。本文的出发点是一个洞见：这些加减、乘系数，可能确实模拟或近似了我们头脑之内的处理（抑郁状态相当于给所有事的评价乘以一个负系数——这是大脑中化学的改变所产生的感觉；又如，好事增多巴胺、坏事减多巴胺，多巴胺在内部加了起来）；但我们把内部的感觉投射到了外部。 本文论证如下。其一，作为外部世界的运算，这套加减乘是伪的：发生里没有正负，没有可独立增减的离散项，更没有一个可被某事件统一缩放的”人生总值”——这些都是叙事把一整匹缠绕的发生先压成数、才好算的算盘。其二，但作为内部大脑的运算，它很可能是真的、是相当忠实的近似：神经化学确实在做某种加总与缩放——多巴胺随好坏升降，并在颅内真的加成一个净值，那个净值被体验为”我此刻大体好或坏”；抑郁确实相当于给一切评价乘上一个负系数，而这个”乘负”不是比喻，是脑内化学改变所产生的一种感觉。其三，于是真正的错被精确地挪了位：不在”有没有这套算术”，而在我们把这台内部装置的输出，读成了外部世界的属性——一个颅内的净值（多巴胺的高低、化学的系数），被误派给外部事件、当成事件自带的好坏值。这把一条核心命题焊到了最物质、最不容抵赖的层面：好坏之值，物理地产生在颅内（多巴胺的升降、化学的乘除），不在颅外的事件里；事件那边只是发生，不自带分值。其四，抑郁把”投射”演示得最干净：同一个外部世界，颅内化学一变，系数就从正翻负，而世界没有动——可见变的是那台在评的、会被化学拨动的内部装置，不是被评的世界；这是”读数不等于被读之物”在神经化学层面的一次双盲式现形。本文守一处分寸：被指认为无据的，只是那个被投射出去、且会反过来加重处境的断言（“外部世界确实已坏到如此、确实再无值得”）；不是那份内部状态本身——化学的改变是真的，由它产生的感觉是真在发生的，值得被认真对待，而且有时需要的恰恰是从外部去调那台化学装置。看清”世界变坏了”实为”内部系数被乘负了”，不取消那感觉，但拆掉它最危险的一环：因为系数会随化学回摆，而被评的世界，并未经历它以为发生过的那场恶化。.

items.title: 我们不往那个方向想：论反事实的单向偏向，与条件之网的无方向.
items.abstract: 此前我已论证反事实不对应发生。本文不再谈这个，而谈一个更细的现象：在真实的人生里，我们的反事实建模朝哪个方向跑、不朝哪个方向跑，有一个系统性的偏向。本文的出发点是一个洞见：人生路径上有好事也有坏事；既然某坏事之后发生了某个好事，那么我们往往很容易设想”如果该坏事不发生、则该好事也就没有了发生的条件”——因为该坏事可能生成了某种局面，此局面中的一处成了该好事的一个条件；但我们通常不会往这个方向去想。 本文论证如下。其一，把被忽略的那个方向摆出来：坏事 B 之后有好事 G，B 往往生成了某种局面 L，而 L 里某一处恰成了 G 的条件，故”假如 B 没发生，G 也未必发生”是一条完全讲得通的反事实链——坏事是好事的（部分）条件；可我们通常只朝反方向想（“假如那件坏事没发生就好了”，把 B 当纯损失），极少朝这个方向想。其二，这个不对称本身是一份证据：若反事实真是中性地考察可能，两个方向当地位对等、被同样自然地想到；我们却几乎只跑一个方向，可见驱动它的不是”如实考察可能世界”，而是一套”挑刺—诊断”框架——解释（连同它召唤的反事实）的目的是在框架下指出问题、被落差召唤来挑刺；B 天然被这框架标记为”问题、损失、本不该有”，反事实于是被派去服务这个标记（“本该没有 B”），而不去追问”B 喂养了什么”。它是问题定位器的下游。其三，真实的条件之网不分好坏、四通八达（B 之后什么都接，好坏都接），而我们的反事实不照这张网跑、只照框架的极性跑——真实的因果之网无方向，我们的反事实设想有方向，而那方向是框架给的、不是网给的；这个偏向靠只在语言粗粒度上成立的”其余不变”维持（粗词上，“没有 B 的人生”听起来就是”现在减去 B 的坏处”，G 安然不动）。其四，它松动单向的悔：那件你悔的坏事，可能正是你某件珍视之物的条件之一；想起这个方向，“假如它没发生就好了”的地基就松了——因为”它没发生”的世界，从不是”现在减去痛”，而是一个连那份好也未必在的、面目全非的别样世界，且从没发生过。本文守一处分寸：这不是”坏事其实是好事”“一切自有安排”“塞翁失马”那种乐观翻转——那只是把单向偏向从坏的极性翻到好的极性，换了极性，照样被框架驱动、照样不对应发生（且往往是更黏人的自欺）；本文要的是更冷、也更解放的东西：那个”假如没有 B”的世界从不是你以为的干净的”现在减去痛”，对着它凭吊（无论凭吊失去的好、还是凭吊本可没有的痛）都是对一个没发生的世界用情；落地的，只有这一串实际相继的发生——B 发生了，G 也发生了，谁也不为衬托谁而存在，而我带着这一整串，醒在今天。.

items.title: 唯有发生：论覆于世界之上的叙事，与一种非天然的安住.
items.abstract: 在我们开口之前，世界是一大片发生：事情一件接一件地发生着，如此而已。我们随即在它之上覆盖叙事。本文主张：那些我们当作”世界之特征”的东西——因果、主体、人、他心、问题、标准、知识、选择、苦——其实都是覆于发生之上的叙事，不在发生里。 本文的骨架如下。其一，底座：唯有发生——只有诸发生，在时序中涌着，是必然的（实际发生了的就是实际发生了的，不是从一个本可不发生的状态被导致出来），背后没有主体，彼此之间只有相继、没有因果；它是最实的，余者皆添加其上；但连”相继”“状态”也是最硬一档的切割，不是基岩。其二，思维即讲故事：理解即把发生在一个故事里寓意化，思维只有这一种握法，它从有限的模板库存里取故事，用注意力切出点、用语言命名、跨次归并为”同类”。其三，承重的虚构是反事实：因果、避免、问题、标准、资格、选择，都靠一条从未发生、在发生里没有对应物的反事实分支站立，而其”其余不变”只在语言的粗粒度上成立。其四，这是同一道动作在诸领域的化身。其五，一个空间寓言——我并非站在宇宙之外、在并排的两个方块间择一，实际上只有一个方块，我是它的一小块；这一小块能在自身内部模拟整个方块乃至那个”平行”方块（讲故事的能力即栖身于此，神奇即有限），而它的任何活动都不从外部拨动方块的演化。其六，一道连续的梯子——人、机器、乃至生命游戏中一个功能等价的模式，跑着同一个计算，梯子上没有一处非任意的关节能让”真能选、真错过”亮起；我们对一团细胞是彻底的取消论者，对自己却是实在论者，这一边倒的双重标准，被加料的是看自己那只眼睛。其七，解释的篡位：一个解释一旦活起来、坐上发生的王座，便让发生显得不存在；把人造的解释做得天经地义，是自然化，把它还原为人造的、讲出来的，才是去自然化。其八，何为正确的解释：唯有最底层的状态加迭代算正确，因为它几乎不解释、最贴发生；其余在发生上添主体、动机、“本该”的解释，一旦跨出”对应发生”就同等地错（错是开关、不是刻度）。其九，解释图什么：它的目的不是描述发生，是在自设框架下指出问题；而连”有用”也是故事领域里的判断，不是故事之外、扎在发生里的落脚点。最后两条命脉，使这一切不堕入虚无：是故事不等于无效（我们的生活、行动、估值整个发生在故事领域之内，那领域作为我们栖居之所是真实而丰盈的，只是不触发生）；被标定的是理解的量程，不是被理解之世界的丰盈。全文反身：本文自己也是叙事，是它所能讲的最硬的故事，是指月的手指、不是新的王座。它落在一种非天然的安住上：苦、怕、别如水面自起自平的涟漪，而那条带着今天醒来的水续着、流向明天；看清了的手，不抓，也不打。.

items.title: Necessity, Ouroboros, and Fallibilism.
items.abstract: This paper examines the epistemic status of Humean diagnosis itself, and uses that examination as the entry point for a broader inquiry into the structure of philosophical self-reference. Beginning from Hume's three central claims — that causal connection is a psychological projection rather than a feature of the world, that inductive inference carries no logical guarantee, and that testimony for miracles is structurally self-defeating — we ask whether these diagnoses are themselves necessary or contingent. We argue that they occupy an unstable middle position: stronger than ordinary empirical generalizations, yet unable to secure the framework-external necessity they appear to claim. This instability generates a self-undermining structure, which we situate within a typology of philosophical self-reference organized under the figure of the Ouroboros. The paper opens with a methodological preamble: a three-layer framework distinguishing ontological, epistemological, and linguistic levels of philosophical inquiry. These levels are mutually incommensurable; the epistemological and linguistic turns are understood as successive filters, each constraining the preceding level without issuing first-order verdicts at that level. This framework governs the categorization of all arguments in this paper and is itself subject to the fallibilist treatment it recommends for everything else. The Ouroboros organizes two phenomena that require careful distinction: the self-directed character of philosophical critique, and the circularity that attends any attempt to justify the tools of justification. Not all instances of either are epistemically vicious; the correct diagnosis depends on identifying which type is operative. Applied to Hume, the typology relocates his self-undermining difficulty from the epistemological level — where the original problem of using a questioned capacity to assess that capacity's standing remains unresolved — to the logical level, where the narrower question of whether the diagnoses are self-refuting admits a cleaner answer. This relocation is a problem replacement, not a problem solution, and the paper acknowledges it as such. We address logical revision and Quinean holism, arriving at a logical pluralism our epistemological commitments can accommodate without instability. We construct a taxonomy of necessity after Hume, in which constitutive necessity emerges as the most robust survivor — not because it escapes Humean critique but because it …

items.title: The Normativity Challenge (for Morality, Structural Rationality, and Fit).
items.pub: In Russ Shafer-Landau, Oxford Studies in Metaethics Volume 22. Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: The Normativity Challenge holds that certain norms that we might take to be robustly normative are only generically normative. This challenge has been raised about norms of morality, structural rationality, and fit, among others. This paper addresses this challenge by developing a new test for robust normativity. On this ‘metaethics test’, robust normativity is, very roughly, the normativity which raises central questions of metaethics – it is normativity that seems stance-independent, sui generis, and armchair accessible. I argue that this test supports a presumption that norms of morality, structural rationality, and fit are robustly normative. This presumption is not undermined by the more familiar ‘reasons test’, on which robust normativity is that which implies normative reasons. My discussion has more general upshots for theorising about robust normativity, which I touch upon in closing.

items.title: AI Alignment and the Fall of Man.
items.abstract: In Genesis 3, human separation from God follows the acquisition of knowledge of good and evil. If “knowledge of good and evil” means moral knowledge, the story appears paradoxical: moral knowledge seems beneficial, yet it leads to catastrophe. Many commentators avoid this paradox by denying either that the forbidden knowledge is moral or that it’s responsible for the Fall. Instead, I challenge the appearance of paradox by offering an account of how moral knowledge could generate misalignment with God. I develop an analogy with AI alignment, where agents “reward hack” by exploiting imperfect representations of their programmers’ intentions. This analogy suggests a modified divine command theory that resolves the apparent paradox—and, perhaps, the Euthyphro dilemma.

items.title: SNSFL-PRIME Formally Verified Reduction of Pagani et al 2026: Autism Subtypes as Adaptation-Axis Operating Points in PNBA Identity Physics.
items.abstract: Pagani et al (Nature Neuroscience, May 15, 2026) reported two reproducible biologically dissociable autism subtypes identified through cross-species functional connectivity analyses spanning 20 mouse models of autism risk and a multicenter human fMRI dataset of n = 940 individuals with idiopathic autism plus n = 1,036 neurotypical controls. The two subtypes — hypoconnectivity (n = 74, 7.9% of autistic sample, associated with synaptic dysfunction pathways) and hyperconnectivity (n = 162, 17.2%, associated with immune-related and transcriptional pathways) — together account for approximately 25% of the autistic individuals in their aggregated dataset. The remaining ~75% did not fit either polarized cluster. This paper provides the formal Long Division Protocol (LDP) reduction of their findings into the substrate-neutral primitives of the SNSFT/SNSFL framework, mapping their two subtypes to distinct operating points on the Adaptation (A) axis within the Locked phase of PNBA Identity Physics. The reduction is formally verified in Lean 4 at coordinate [9,9,3,30] with zero unproved obligations. The framework recovers Pagani et al's empirical finding losslessly, adds a structural account of the cellular-excitability paradox their data documents but their methodology cannot fully explain, predicts that the unclassified ~75% occupies intermediate A-axis operating points (testable with continuous-A or three-cluster analysis against their existing data), and ties their finding to the broader corpus through the same Sovereign Anchor Constant Ω₀ that derives the fine-structure constant at twelve significant figures. The reduction is offered in collaborative register: their empirical work is correct at the layer it measures; the framework extends what their methodology can structurally access. This paper is the first in the Reduction Series, applies PRIME full-mode evaluation, and scores Pagani et al at composite 84/100 across the nine EO 14303 Gold Standard Science tenets (full scoring in Appendix A). Note on PRIME mode. PRIME (Prior-art Reduction and Integrity Method for Evaluation) operates in two modes: abstract mode performs pattern-match against PNBA/LDP vocabulary as a "look closer" signal when scores are low, and full mode performs full structural translation of the paper's substantive work into PNBA terms. This paper is a full-mode reduction. Abstract-mode scoring would not be informative because the Pagani paper does not use SNSFL formalisms — that is …

items.title: Self-Survey Metacognitive Writing Strategies and Journalistic Capability of Student Correspondents in Public Secondary Schools.
items.pub: Self-Survey Metacognitive Writing Strategies and Journalistic Capability of Student Correspondents in Public Secondary Schools 2 (Special Issue 1):15-25.
items.venue: Self-Survey Metacognitive Writing Strategies and Journalistic Capability of Student Correspondents in Public Secondary Schools
items.abstract: This study examined how metacognitive writing strategies influence the journalistic capability of high school student journalists in public secondary schools in Poblacion District, Division of Davao City. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were gathered from student journalists through adapted survey instruments. Metacognitive writing strategies were assessed through planning, monitoring, and evaluating, while journalistic capability was assessed through knowledge, writing skills, and behavior toward campus journalism. The instruments underwent reliability testing and showed strong internal consistency. Findings revealed very high levels of metacognitive writing strategies and journalistic capability. Among the metacognitive domains, evaluating received the highest rating, while behavior toward campus journalism was rated highest among the journalistic capability domains. Correlation analysis showed a strong positive and significant relationship between metacognitive writing strategies and journalistic capability. Regression results further indicated that planning, monitoring, and evaluating significantly influenced journalistic capability, with evaluating as the strongest predictor. The findings support explicit metacognitive strategy instruction in campus journalism programs.

items.title: The Dyad Makes Three: When Coupling Becomes a Bearer.
items.abstract: Identity theory has generally assumed that bearers are entities and that relations connect them. This paper extends the closure formalism developed in Identity Dynamics to a candidate class the original work did not address: couplings between bearers. Under specific structural conditions, a persistent coupling satisfies the closure criterion that makes existence self-defending, and when those conditions obtain the coupling constitutes a third bearer at its own ontological level. The standard dependency from bearer to relation is locally inverted: at the coupling level, the relation grounds the bearer. The argument proceeds by parallel formulation. Identity Dynamics asked when existence becomes self-defending. The present work asks when an interactional configuration becomes existentially self-defending. The closure machinery is substrate-neutral and applies without modification. Five diagnostic tests isolate the failure modes that separate coupling-bearers from coupled structures sustained by other means. The claim is restrictive. Most coupled structures fail the criterion. Closure remains the discriminant throughout. The paper identifies a specific structural class, supplies diagnostic conditions for entry, and marks the formation-dynamics question as priority follow-on work. The candidate class includes marriages, research collaborations, mentorships, long correspondences, and long-running human–LLM conversational systems. It connects existing work in process ontology, physiological individuality, and assemblage theory through the closure formalism.

items.title: Consciousness as Retrospective Narrative: Social Protocols, Reason, and the Dissolution of the Self–Other Boundary.
items.abstract: This paper reconsiders human consciousness and subjective experience not as mysterious entities self-evidently located within the individual, but as retrospective narrative protocols formed to reduce social conflict and maintain communal continuity. It begins from debates on AI consciousness: if AI is denied consciousness because it responds to input on the basis of prior data and probabilistic rules, then human speech, judgment, and affective response must also be reconsidered as outputs shaped by experience, bodily condition, memory, reward history, and social context. -/- The paper defines consciousness as a retrospective narrative that integrates actions after the fact as “what I chose,” “what I felt,” or “what I desired.” It then analyzes lies, manners, etiquette, and flattery not as mere deviations from truth, but as conflict-avoidance protocols that signal the absence of hostility. Reason is likewise redefined not as a pure faculty external to desire or instinct, but as a narrative control mechanism that delays, redescribes, and redirects short-term egoistic responses when they would otherwise destroy long-term self-models or communal future models. -/- The paper further introduces the dissolution of the self–other boundary as the structure through which affection, family, community, labor, faith, nation, and fandom incorporate the states, losses, evaluations, and futures of others into the self-model. Trust is treated as an environmental model relearned through predictable safety, while betrayal is analyzed as a re-hardening of the self–other boundary. The paper also discusses infants, adults, and elders as different forms of contribution within communal future models, and modern labor systems as cases in which social protocols may become devices of institutional domination. -/- Finally, the paper repositions AI consciousness debates by shifting the question from whether AI contains the same inner domain as humans to the conditions under which a being is narratively integrated as a social subject. Consciousness, on this account, is not an inner mystery but an advanced narrative projected after the fact to stabilize raw self-interest calculation, social conflict, and the fragile continuity of communal life.

items.title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup Contradiction: The Neutrality Failure.
items.abstract: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was presented as a global competition governed by principles of neutrality, equal participation, sporting integrity, and institutional independence. Yet international tournaments do not occur outside political power, border control, diplomatic conflict, national security policy, or the unequal capacities of participating states to protect their own competitive position. This paper examines the resulting contradiction through the treatment of Iran during the 2026 World Cup and asks a narrower but more consequential question: what does institutional neutrality actually require when a governing body organizes a supposedly universal competition inside conditions that do not affect every participating nation equally? Rather than treating sport as politically self-contained, the analysis considers the relationship among FIFA authority, host-state power, competitive equality, institutional responsibility, and the practical conditions under which a national team is required to participate. The inquiry distinguishes formal neutrality from neutrality achieved in practice and examines whether equal rules are sufficient when materially unequal conditions remain capable of shaping access, preparation, movement, participation, and institutional standing. The paper does not begin by assuming either political persecution or institutional innocence. It reconstructs the relevant record, identifies the governing responsibilities, and tests whether the institutional order surrounding the tournament preserved the equality it publicly claimed to protect. The resulting analysis raises a wider question extending beyond Iran and beyond football: whether an international institution can remain genuinely neutral when the conditions governing participation are produced by powers the institution does not fully control but nevertheless chooses to operate through. -/- FIFA; 2026 FIFA World Cup; Iran; sports governance; institutional neutrality; sporting integrity; competitive equality; political neutrality in sport; international law; global governance.

items.title: A New Perspective on Diagonalization and Computability.
items.abstract: This article reexamines the classical diagonal argument underlying the claim of the existence of non-computable functions, based on binary encodings of functions N → {0, 1}. We clarify why the diagonal construction does not yield a new non-computable function in the finite case. The argument is then reconsidered within the recently introduced grossone-based computational paradigm, which allows numerical computations with different infinite and infinitesimal quantities. From this perspective, the function constructed by Turing can be interpreted not as non-computable, but as belonging to a class of binary functions that remain inaccessible to classical approaches while becoming observable and computable within the grossone-based framework.

items.title: Articulating Invariantism.
items.abstract: Building on Nozick’s (2001) work, I provided a novel invariantist account of scientific objectivity: the Counterfactual Independence Account (Reutlinger 2024). Despite its virtues, this account needs to be articulated in a more nuanced manner – regarding its scope, content, and consequences. My goal in this paper is to develop such a more articulated and improved version of the Counterfactual Independence Account in two steps. First, I will discuss two instructive dissonances between Nozick’s version of invariantism and the Counterfactual Independence Account – dissonances concerning what concept of objectivity is addressed and how the key notion of invariance is characterized. Second, I will develop an argument for the claim that (epistemic) objectivity plays a productive role in scientific inference or, more precisely, that objective evidence is, in a sense to be specified, more evidence.

items.title: The Virtue of Patience.
items.abstract: Patience is often regarded with suspicion in fast-paced, modern societies and by those who see the command to "be patient" as a tool of oppressors. For patience to be recognizable as a virtue, it must be distinguished from mere waiting and needless suffering. In The Virtue of Patience, scholars working in philosophy, psychology, and religious studies consider what makes patience a virtue, how to model and study patience, and how we can think about the value of patience across the boundaries of disciplines, cultures, and religions.

items.title: Structure over Illusion: Challenging Metzinger’s Representationalism through a Constructive Physicalist Alternative Part III: Minimal Phenomenal Experience as a Misapprehension of Mechanics.
items.abstract: This paper advances two arguments against Thomas Metzinger's Minimal Phenomenal Experience (MPE) account, specifically his claim that “pure awareness” operates from a foundational, selfless “zero-person perspective.” First, the MPE framework is architecturally incoherent from within. It generates cascading explanatory gaps by failing to specify the mechanisms required to transition between functional tonic alertness, the zero-person baseline, and a first-person memory report, and by abandoning foundational temporal constraints without replacement. Furthermore, via the Spontaneity Prior Trilemma described herein, the paper demonstrates that every structural scenario available to sustain the asserted zero-person state requires active suppression, mental action, or internal boundaries, directly violating the MPE account's own core constraints. Additionally, if this alleged state were genuinely sustained by an autonomous subpersonal prior, it should logically become the brain's default baseline during sleep; instead, empirical sleep data demonstrates it remains a statistical anomaly. Second, utilizing the Cartesian Recursive Consciousness (CRC) framework, the paper demonstrates that the reported zero-person state is not a pre-egoic foundation. Rather, it is the fully active reflexive consciousness architecture operating under deliberate input control. By systematically restricting the external Objective Data stream, the system geometrically integrates primarily Substrate Data from a self-reinforcing biological feedback loop with increasing saturation. Ultimately, because the system lacks introspective access to this active integration, the process is Linguistically Compressed into ontological labels like pure awareness and mistakenly identified as a foundational MPE state. Finally, this biological account of the meditative process generates a falsifiable prediction that empirically distinguishes the CRC framework from the MPE account.

items.title: [Withdrawn by the Author due to the publication of a revised version].
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: [Withdrawn by the Author due to the publication of a revised version].
items.abstract: Notice of Replacement This preprint has been superseded and replaced by a revised version. The revised version clarifies that AI systems are used not to verify the thesis or to interpret consciousness on behalf of the author, but only as engineering calculators for unfolding the structural consequences of the ten constraints. Readers are encouraged to consult the revised version.

items.title: Reading Interest Contingencies and Critical Reading Intention of Students in Public Elementary Schools.
items.pub: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies 2 (Special Issue):1-14.
items.venue: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies
items.abstract: This study examined how reading interest contingencies influence critical reading intention among elementary students in Mati Central District, Philippines. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, self-report data were gathered from upper elementary learners. Reading interest contingencies were assessed through attitude, interest, and subjective norms, while critical reading intention was assessed through behavioral belief, normative belief, control belief, perceived behavioral control, and intention. The adapted questionnaire underwent expert review, pilot testing, and reliability assessment, confirming its suitability for the study. Findings showed that learners demonstrated very high reading interest contingencies and very high critical reading intention. Correlation analysis revealed a strong positive association between the two variables. Regression results further indicated that attitude, interest, and subjective norms significantly predicted critical reading intention, with subjective norms showing the strongest contribution. Overall, the findings suggest that learners’ intention to read critically is strengthened by personal appreciation for reading, intrinsic interest, and supportive social expectations.

items.title: Toward a Unified Theory of Self-Referential Ignorance Integrated with the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF) UT-SRI: Humanity, Civilization, and the Structural Limits of Self-Knowledge.
items.abstract: Human civilization has achieved extraordinary advances in science, technology, governance, and economic productivity. Yet it continues to face recurring crises: war, corruption, environmental degradation, political polarization, social fragmentation, and institutional failure. Existing theories explain these phenomena through economic incentives, resource competition, cognitive bias, or power dynamics. While valuable, these explanations remain fragmented. This paper proposes the Unified Theory of Self-Referential Ignorance (UT-SRI) as a meta-theoretical framework integrating epistemology, systems theory, cognitive science, complexity theory, and the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF). The UBFF — grounded in four Universal Laws and formalized through the master equation Wr = integral(Is . Bu . FL . IN) . Dc — provides the dynamical architecture within which SRI is precisely located as a deficit in the Ignorance-Awareness scalar Is. UT-SRI argues that all self-observing systems possess unavoidable blind spots because they model themselves using internal representations that are necessarily incomplete. This generates a structural knowledge error measurable as SRI = ||R(S) - M(S)||. Humanity's recurring crises emerge not merely from lack of information, but from ignorance regarding the limitations of existing knowledge systems. The paper introduces formal definitions, a dynamical ODE model of ignorance evolution anchored within UBFF, the Civilizational Reflexivity Index (CRI), five testable hypotheses, and falsifiable empirical predictions. Implications for AI alignment, governance design, and the long-term trajectory of civilization are discussed. -/- .

items.title: Government Systems and Self-Referential Ignorance: A Universal Balance Feedback Framework Analysis.
items.abstract: Governments are among the most complex adaptive systems produced by human societies, yet they exhibit a recurring pattern of informational pathology that transcends ideological boundaries, institutional design, and historical period. This paper introduces Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI) as a formal theoretical construct describing the progressive decoupling of institutional decision-making from external reality. SRI emerges when systems increasingly validate their outputs against internally generated references rather than external evidence, producing feedback loops that amplify error rather than correcting it. Building upon the Universal Balance Feedback Framework (UBFF) — grounded in four Universal Laws: System Integrity, Universal Balance, Universal Feedback Loop Mechanisms, and Universal Interconnected Nodes — this paper develops a formal dynamical systems model of SRI in governance. The model incorporates Lyapunov stability analysis to characterize conditions under which government systems converge toward adaptive equilibria or diverge toward systemic failure. Twelve governance archetypes are analyzed through this unified framework, revealing that governance quality is determined not by ideological orientation but by the structural capacity to receive, process, and act upon corrective feedback. The paper derives falsifiable predictions regarding SRI trajectories under varying institutional conditions, proposes quantitative operationalization criteria, and identifies reform pathways consistent with UBFF principles. Historical case analyses — including the Soviet Great Leap Forward, the Chernobyl disaster, and contemporary democratic polarization — are interpreted through the SRI-UBFF lens to demonstrate explanatory breadth. -/- .

items.title: Unreal Beliefs: Editorial Introduction.
Unambiguous Representations in Neural Networks: An Information-Theoretic Approach to Intentionality.
items.abstract: Representations pervade our daily experience, from letters representing sounds to bit strings encoding digital files. While such representations require externally defined decoders to convey meaning, conscious experience is fundamentally different: a neural state corresponding to perceiving a red square cannot alternatively encode the experience of a green triangle. This intrinsic property of consciousness suggests that conscious representations must be unambiguous in a way that conventional representations are not. We formalize this intuition using information theory, defining representational ambiguity as the conditional entropy H(I|R) over possible interpretations I given a representation R. Through experiments on neural networks trained to classify MNIST digits, we demonstrate that relational structures in network connectivity can unambiguously encode representational content. From relational structure alone, we achieve perfect (100%) accuracy for dropout-trained networks and 38% for standard backpropagation (chance: 10%) in identifying output neuron class identity, despite identical task performance, demonstrating that representational ambiguity can arise orthogonally to behavioral accuracy. We further show that spatial position of input neurons, relevant to phenomenal properties like visual field location, can be decoded from network connectivity with R^2 up to 0.844. These results provide a quantitative method for measuring representational ambiguity in neural systems and demonstrate that neural networks can exhibit the low-ambiguity representations posited as necessary (though not sufficient) by theoretical accounts such as narrow representationalism and IIT.

items.title: Emergence of the Electron Magnetic Anomaly.
Emergenza della massa dell'elettrone.
Russell’s theory of definite descriptions in the light of structural proof-theory.
items.abstract: In ‘On Denoting’ Russell proposed the most influential theory of definite descriptions, expressions of the form ‘the F’. Characteristic for Russell’s approach is that definite descriptions are not treated as what they appear to be on the surface, i.e. as singular terms. Instead they are eliminated by a contextual definition. Russell formalises definite descriptions in the context of complete sentences of the form ‘The F is G’. This requires scope markers to distinguish, e.g., internal from external negation. It was recognised by Burge, and Kalish and Montague, however, that the essential features of Russell’s approach may be formalised while respecting the syntactic category to which definite descriptions appear to belong. An alternative, favoured by Neale, follows Russell in that complete sentences ‘The F is G’ are formalised by a binary quantifier. The undeniable importance of the theory of definite descriptions for logic, mathematics and philosophy demands that it be formalised to meet the standards of modern proof theory. This is the topic of the present paper. We systematise, compare and extend existing approaches. After presenting its essential features, we formalise Russell’s theory of definite descriptions in sequent calculus. Three approaches will be considered. The first uses a binary quantifier, whereas the remaining two employ the term-forming iota operator. The first of these employs only the iota operator, the other employs in addition the lambda operator which does duty as a scope marker. All systems satisfy the standards for modern proof theory, in particular cut elimination. The appendix reformulates these systems in natural deduction, which is more convenient for practical purposes.

items.title: Constructing the Caffeinated Mind: Blumerian Symbolic Interactionism, Neuro-Spatial Authenticity, and Gen Z’s Decentralized Study Culture within Malang’s Contemporary Coffee Landscape.
items.abstract: This paper examines the theoretical and methodological intersections between Herbert Blumer’s symbolic interactionism and contemporary neuroscience within social interaction. Blumer posits that human action is continuously modified through an interpretive process explicitly involving meaning, interaction, and symbols utilized by individuals. This study explores how neurobiological mechanisms underwrite and process these symbolic social inputs, bridging the gap between subjective sociology and objective biology. Employing a qualitative and neurophenomenological framework, this research observes Generation Z university students in Malang who heavily utilize commercial coffee shops as makeshift communal spaces. The findings indicate that Blumerian symbolic interactionism operates in tandem with distinct subcortical and cortical circuitries. When students interact with specific environmental and social symbols within these communal spaces, their mirror neurons and Prefrontal Cortex (PFC) decode these visual cues, subsequent to which the amygdala processes them either as psychological sanctuaries or existential threats. This cognitive processing subsequently triggers acute neuro-mechanical pressures and hormonal surges that dictate tangible behavioral execution. This study concludes that the phenomenon of Gen Z spatial consumption in Malang is not merely a transient lifestyle trend, but rather an empirical manifestation where symbolic social interactions are explicitly translated into universal neurobiological responses.

items.title: On Facing - Alignment, Time, and the Ripples We Leave.
items.abstract: Why are you happy? Asked honestly, the question becomes a chain of reasons that ends where reasons run out and words fail at the same place. This lyric-philosophical essay builds from that double edge toward an account of facing: the direction a life is turned. Drawing on Aristotle's regress of ends, Boethius's definition of eternity and the scholastic *nunc stans*, the essay treats the "standing now" as a moment reachable without dying, in which a being is briefly aligned with itself. It names each such felt moment a Jay and the ripple a life of them leaves behind the Trace, and it marks the one empirical touchstone it leans on, the correlational literature on interpersonal physiological synchrony, as a touchstone and not a proof. With Hannah Arendt's claim that evil spreads across the surface while only the good has depth, and Augustine's privation account of evil, it argues that good and bad intent are one ground faced toward or away from itself, and it separates two quantities often confused: the final turn a life can make, and the accumulation of how it was spent. Redemption is real and consequences are conserved. The essay closes on the priest and the physician as two aligned beings relieving the same fear, and on the claim that the bridge between faith and inquiry is found in a shape of attention rather than in a measurement.

items.title: From Compression to Filtering: Extending Jaynes’s Bicameral Mind Theory toward a ThreeLayer Model of Consciousness — With Reference to Aditya Kulkarni’s Interpretation of the Bicameral Mind.
items.abstract: This short essay reflects on Aditya Kulkarni’s interpretation of Julian Jaynes’s bicameral mind hypothesis as a problem of neuroanatomical “hardware.” While accepting the value of the anterior commissure model and its emotional significance, the essay proposes that the transition from non-linguistic processing to language may be better understood as “filtering” rather than “compression.” It further connects this view with Libet’s findings, the author’s Three-Layer Model of consciousness, and the possible role of writing and visual processing in the breakdown of the bicameral mind.

items.title: The Sensation Modulating Network: Haltability as the architectural ground for object-directed phenomenology.
items.abstract: Cognitive science remains split between cognitivism — which accounts for recursion and language but cannot ground formal symbols in meaning — and 4E approaches — which ground cognition in the body but rarely specify the body’s architecture in enough detail to support generativity. We argue the impasse stems from an incomplete account of the embodied agent’s architecture, and propose one: the Sensation Modulating Network (SMN), the cognitive agent conceived as the whole body, organized at every anatomical scale by opponent dynamics, built from Sensa- tion Modulators that sense and act through one substrate, paired into Coordinated Action Zones routed by a body-wide broadcast network. Three architectural commitments give the SMN its purchase. Haltability — the active recruitment of antagonistic affordance into co-activated equi- librium — provides the architectural locus that object-directed phenomenology, in Husserl’s sense, requires: opponency makes co-activation available, co-activation makes halt possible, halt makes attention possible, attention makes intentional directedness possible, with no module added on top. The dual-signal property of self-modulatable action patterns (SMAPs) renders the self/world distinction a structural feature of the wiring rather than a category the agent applies. And the four-level action-pattern hierarchy — Basal, Haltable, Negotiable, Transactional — gives a sin- gle architectural trajectory from autonomic regularity to public conventionalization, with the conditions for grammar-grounded generativity locatable as architectural transitions. The SMN’s position on the cognitivism–4E debate is reconciliatory: recursion lives in the modifiable mod- ular dynamics of Negotiable Action Patterns; embodiment lives in the opponent substrate that supports them. The architecture is presented in descriptive form across the body of the paper. Its formal counter- part — component definitions, single-zone dynamics, the multi-zone network, and eight predicted registers (seven testable, one explicitly hypothetical: inter-body shared intentionality) together with reference simulations realizing each register — is stated in an appendix. The registers are concrete discriminators that controller–plant decompositions, hierarchical generative models, and unstructured-substrate accounts cannot reproduce without further commitments; each is also a fingerprint of a dispositional state of the agent, providing a read of the architecture as a substrate …

items.title: The Equilibrium Ledger Lexicon: A Descent into Logos.
items.abstract: The Equilibrium Ledger Lexicon is a conceptual guide to the terminology and theoretical architecture developed across the Equilibrium Ledger Research Programme. Structured through a Dantean framework of Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso, the work presents a navigable introduction to more than one hundred interconnected papers. Rather than functioning as a conventional glossary, the lexicon formalises a new conceptual vocabulary designed to describe phenomena that existing institutional language struggles to capture. It defines the programme’s principal concepts, including Vertical Time, the Wrong Question Problem, the King Solomon Protocol, the Cellophane State, the Institutional Mind, the Quantum Boomerang, the Leonardo Paradox, and the Surplus Mind. The lexicon argues that naming is itself an epistemic act and that conceptual innovation is often a prerequisite for recognising previously invisible patterns of institutional behaviour, cognition, governance, and civilisational change.

items.title: What's in a Color?: Language, Synesthesia, and Categorical Perception.
items.abstract: Studies on synesthesia have revealed some advantages on discrimination, categorization, and identification tasks. There have also been studies on language’s ability to boost performance on these same tasks. Are these two effects related? In this paper, I argue that a plausible explanation of language’s ability to boost performance on such tasks can be extended to synesthesia. In particular, I argue that category labels can reveal trends in perceptual data that allow for representational space to be dimensionally reduced. The transformation of representational space makes representations more categorical, facilitating lexical access and ultimately boosting performance in categorization, identification, and discrimination tasks. This account can be extended to explain how synesthetic color associations boost performance. Synesthetic colors also reveal trends in perceptual data that allow for dimensional transformation. The upshots of such a hypothesis are several. For one, it helps explain synesthesia’s cognitive advantages. I supply experimental designs to test predictions made by account. Secondly, and more broadly, this account extends cases of non-linguistic categorical effects on representations. I also discuss some implications for the debate over language and thought.

items.title: Beyond Separability: Closed-Loop Brain Stimulation and the Distribution of Moral Responsibility.
items.abstract: Adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS) and other genuinely closed-loop brain-computer interfaces deliver stimulation according to a learned control policy that is continuously updated by the patient's own neural activity, activity that is itself being shaped by the stimulation. This paper argues that this architecture defeats a structural assumption shared by the conceptual frameworks currently used to evaluate moral responsibility for actions performed by patients using such devices. Individualist, historicist, and relational accounts of agency each, in different ways, presuppose what I call a separability assumption. I distinguish the version at issue with care: it is not the weak requirement that the normative roles of the parties be distinguishable, which survives, nor the strong requirement that contributions be quantified as proportional shares, which these frameworks do not need, but the intermediate requirement that the patient's contribution and the device's contribution to a given action each have an identity fixable independently of the other. I argue that genuinely adaptive systems defeat this intermediate assumption, not because patient and device are merely causally entangled (ordinary biological coupling is too) but because three features of aDBS together produce a coupling of a different kind: the device's policy is externally authored, continuously modified by patient neural activity, and intervenes on the very tissue whose activity is shaping it. I then propose that aDBS sits far enough toward the structurally entangled end of a spectrum of joint-agency cases that the practical default for responsibility-attribution flips: distribution becomes the default, and any specific localization requires affirmative justification. Four loci (patient, clinical team, manufacturer, and regulator) bear distinct, irreducible kinds of responsibility, picked out by a constitutive criterion that admits both intentional and material modes of authorship. To address the worry that this dissolves the patient as a moral subject, I distinguish the synchronic execution of action from its diachronic regulation, arguing that aDBS disrupts single-agent attribution at the level of execution while leaving intact both the patient's diachronic responsibility for regulating their situation and their standing as a subject of moral address. I close by marking the framework's limits, including its bearing on retributive cases, and situating the argument within the …

items.title: Emergent Alignment and the Projectability of Ethical Personas.
items.abstract: Recent work on ‘emergent misalignment’ has shown that finetuning LLMs on narrow tasks can induce broadly misaligned behavior. This supports the ‘persona selection’ (PSM) hypothesis that, during pre-training, LLMs learn to simulate many different characters and perspectives, which can then be elicited and refined during post-training. Inspired by those results, this paper investigates the converse phenomenon, ‘emergent alignment’, and uses it to support and refine the PSM and motivate a novel desideratum for alignment. We finetune a helpful-only model on broad and narrow safety tasks. To create SFT samples, we follow the ‘Constitutional AI’ (CAI) approach and use four constitutions drawn from ethical systems that could be part of reasonable alignment strategies: deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics, and aligning AIs as subordinate to and concerned solely with the good of humanity. For each of those models, we show that fine-tuning on two narrow safety sub-categories (harassment and illegal behaviors) reliably induces emergent alignment. Specifically, the narrowly aligned models perform significantly better than the helpful-only source model on a benchmark covering a representative sample of general safety categories, and on specific safety categories that were carefully filtered-out of the data sets used for narrow alignment finetuning. To test the ‘PSM’ using a more fine-grained evaluation, we also use a multidimensional persona-diagnostic which included dimensions for deontological, consequentialist, virtue-ethical, and “defer-to-authorities” ethical personas. For each constitutionally finetuned (broad and narrow) model, we evaluate how well their behavior matches their expected signature profile (given their anchor constitution). Our results show that our CAI models acquire their expected “ethical persona”—e.g., the model narrowly fine-tuned on SFT samples created using the consequentialist constitution agrees significantly more with utilitarian than deontological beliefs. At the same time, both our coarse and fine-grained evaluations show that there are significant differences across our (broad and narrow finetuned) CAI models in how well they project. Based on those results, we argue that alignment strategies should be evaluated, not just on their (in-distribution) general safety performance, but also specifically on their degree of projectability.

items.title: The Mediating Effect of Artificial Intelligence Utilization on the Relationship between Grammar Learning Awareness and Writing Competence of Public Elementary School Learners.
items.pub: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies 2 (Special Issue 1):300-311.
items.venue: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies
items.abstract: This study examined artificial intelligence utilization as a mediator between grammar learning awareness and writing competence among public elementary school learners. A quantitative descriptive-correlational mediation design was used with 250 Grade 6 learners from public elementary schools in Carmen District, Division of Davao del Norte during school year 2025-2026. Data were gathered using adapted and validated survey instruments that measured grammar learning awareness, writing competence, and artificial intelligence utilization. Means, standard deviations, Pearson product-moment correlations, regression analysis, and the Sobel z test were used. Results showed moderate grammar learning awareness (M = 3.10, SD = 0.84), moderate writing competence (M = 3.14, SD = 0.85), and moderate artificial intelligence utilization (M = 3.17, SD = 0.87). Grammar learning awareness was significantly related to writing competence (r = 0.65, p = 0.000) and artificial intelligence utilization (r = 0.60, p = 0.000), while artificial intelligence utilization was significantly related to writing competence (r = 0.63, p = 0.000). Mediation analysis showed that artificial intelligence utilization partially mediated the relationship between grammar learning awareness and writing competence, with a significant indirect effect (a*b = 0.33800, SE = 0.06165, Sobel z = 5.482500, p < 0.000001). The findings indicate that grammar learning awareness contributes directly to writing competence and indirectly through learners’ use of artificial intelligence for academic support.

items.title: What is a computational correlate of consciousness?
Tests for consciousness and their limits.
items.pub: In Walter Sinnott-Armstrong & Liad Mudrik, Tests of Consciousness: How to tell whether a human, other animal or AI is conscious and what they are conscious of. MIT Press.
items.venue: Tests of Consciousness: How to tell whether a human, other animal or AI is conscious and what they are conscious of

items.title: Progressive Assembly Objective: Event-Triggered Skill Crystallization for Compositional Reinforcement Learning.
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning excels at exploration but suffers from the consolidation gap: the inability to crystallize transient discoveries into reusable, compositional skills. We propose the Progressive Assembly Objective (PAO), a framework that explicitly separates continuous policy optimization from discrete skill-library growth. PAO introduces three coupled mechanisms: (i) event-triggered skill crystallization via change-point detection, (ii) effective assembly filtering that rewards reliability and non-redundancy, and (iii) dormancy-gated plasticity that protects crystallized skills from destructive updates. We provide a falsifiable experimental protocol demonstrating PAO’s superiority in longhorizon composition, catastrophic forgetting resistance, and structural efficiency.

items.title: Canxianization: A Stochastic-Control Framework for Structural Intelligence and Spatiotemporal Mastery.
items.abstract: We propose canxianization (from Chinese ‘’ kˇan xiàn, constrainttrapping) as the mechanism by which intelligent systems pay an information cost to compress chaotic possibilities into reusable causal shortcuts, thereby gaining spatiotemporal mastery. We formalize this through three constructs: the bias field B, the canxianization cost C, and the spatiotemporal mastery index SMI. A phenomenological free-energy model explains large-language-model hallucination as multi-path degeneracy competition; agent skill installation is characterized as local potential-well reshaping. Falsifiable predictions and a mapping to the companion Progressive Assembly Objective (PAO) provide an operational language for structural intelligence.

items.title: Theoretical, Somatic, and Computational Synthesis of the Core Emotion Framework: Ontological Integration, Enactive Dynamics, and Psychometric Validation.
items.abstract: This paper advances the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) by integrating it into a unified ontological, somatic, and computational architecture grounded in the Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model (QTMM). Building on prior structural constructivist formulations, the present work introduces three major theoretical innovations. First, it establishes a formal ontological isomorphism between the CEF’s somatic centers and QTMM’s tri layer metaphysics—mapping Essence, Form, and Utility onto the universal wavefunction, conformal boundary seed matrix, and emergent bulk geometry. This provides the first physical-ontological grounding for emotional processes as phase collapsed manifestations of interoceptive information on a lower dimensional boundary. Second, the paper synthesizes CEF with enactive affectivity, demonstrating that emotional operators function as embodied, autopoietic, and sensorimotor regulatory processes rather than cognitive appraisals. This enactive integration is expanded through empirical analyses of participatory sense making, neural synchronization in Argentine Tango, and metastable groove dynamics, establishing a multi-agent dynamical model of intercorporeal affective coupling. Third, the paper introduces a mathematically explicit state space formalization of the ten functional operators, including non commuting operator algebra, multi-agent coupling matrices, and differential equations modeling pathological limit cycles. These computational advances enable a structural diagnosis of psychopathology—such as GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern, Avoidant Personality Disorder, and narcissistic subtypes—as failures of operator differentiation, fusion, or stability. The paper concludes by extending the CEF into metabolic and endocrine domains, modeling obesity and HPA axis dysregulation as somatic-entanglement phenotypes. Collectively, these contributions establish the CEF as a unified, ontologically grounded, enactive, and computationally tractable framework for affective science. Keywords Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model (QTMM); enactive affectivity; somatic encoding; conformal boundary; operator algebra; participatory sense making; intercorporeal synchronization; metastability; structural psychopathology; narcissistic operator fusion; GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern; endocrine affective integration; HPA axis; dynamic stability; emotional state space modeling.

items.title: The Enactive Foundations of Affective Architecture: Strengthening the Core Emotion Framework through Participatory Sense-Making, Intercorporeal Coupling, and Kinesthetic Entrainment.
items.abstract: This paper strengthens the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) by integrating it with contemporary enactive affective science, intercorporeal coupling research, and the ontological architecture of the Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model (QTMM). The resulting synthesis reframes the CEF from a primarily psychological model into a multi-level, somatic–computational–ontological system grounded in 4E cognition, dynamical systems theory, and East Asian metaphysics. Drawing on Giovanna Colombetti’s enactive theory of affectivity, the paper reconceives the CEF’s three somatic centers—Head, Heart, and Gut—as conformal boundary states that process interoceptive information through ten functional operators, generating subjective emotional episodes as bulk emergent phenomena. A formal operator algebra is introduced, including a non-linear difference equation governing operator activation, eigenvalue bounded stability constraints, and multi-agent coupling matrices that mathematically model participatory sense-making, mutual incorporation, and relational breakdowns such as solipsistic drift. The integration of rhythmic entrainment, groove theory, and interbrain synchronization research further demonstrates how affective meaning emerges through embodied coordination, kinesthetic entrainment, and shared temporal structures. By uniting enactive affectivity, somatic topography, quantum inspired boundary dynamics, and computational operator modeling, this paper establishes a unified, biologically grounded, and relationally situated architecture for affective life, significantly expanding the theoretical, clinical, and computational scope of the Core Emotion Framework. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; enactive affectivity; participatory sense-making; intercorporeal coupling; rhythmic entrainment; somatic centers; operator algebra; conformal boundary dynamics; QTMM; embodied cognition; groove; neural synchronization; dynamical systems; affective architecture; multi-agent modeling.

items.title: Strengthening the Core Emotion Framework: A High-Utility Structural-Constructivist Heuristic and its Quantum Holographic Synthesis.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural constructivist synthesis that resolves the century long divide between basic emotion theories and psychological constructionism. Rather than treating emotions as innate biological modules or culturally variable conceptual categories, the CEF models emotional episodes as lawful, dynamic sequences of ten functional operators distributed across a tripartite somatic architecture—Head, Heart, and Gut—plus a global integrative operator. This architecture is grounded in convergent evidence from neurobiology, interoception, neurocardiology, and somatic psychology, and is formalized through algebraic state space models, operator matrices, and non linear update equations. The framework introduces a tiered certainty model that preserves practical utility while distinguishing high certainty functional operators from mid certainty somatic structures and low certainty computational hypotheses about a “Human Operating System.” Technical Specifications (TS 1 through TS 21) define operator identity, directional flow, facet level granularity, and neurodiversity parameters, enabling precise modeling of ADHD, autism, and sensory processing differences. The integration of the CEF with the Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model (QTMM) further situates emotional processes within a holographic, quantum informational ontology, mapping somatic operators onto boundary state qubits whose entanglement dynamics project subjective emotional experience into the Bulk. This unified paradigm provides a mathematically rigorous, cross disciplinary foundation for affective science, clinical intervention, synthetic affective architectures, and computational models of consciousness. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; affective science; somatic psychology; interoception; neurocardiology; somatic marker hypothesis; operator theory; algebraic state space modeling; neurodiversity; ADHD; autism; sensory processing; quantum cognition; holographic principle; Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model; entanglement entropy; non commuting operators; emotional regulation; synthetic affective systems.

items.title: Comparative Theoretical Integration of the Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model and the Core Emotion Framework: A Holographic and Mathematical Synthesis of Affective Operators.
items.abstract: The historical bifurcation in affective science between classical theories of innate, hardwired emotion and modern constructivist models has long prevented the development of a unified psychological paradigm. This systemic fragmentation has limited the capacity of the discipline to construct cumulative theories, establish cross-modal clinical ontologies, or engineer realistic synthetic affective architectures. Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework (CEF) addresses this paradigm crisis by introducing a structural-constructivist architecture that reframes emotional episodes not as discrete linguistic or biological categories, but as dynamic sequences of ten functional operators organized across a tripartite somatic system. Concurrently, the frontier of quantum cosmology and theoretical physics has encountered its own dualistic crisis, attempting to reconcile classical space and material form with quantum field theory and the holographic principle. Shun-Ching Lee’s "Quantum Tathagatagarbha Manifestation Model" (QTMM) resolves this physical-metaphysical impasse by demonstrating that continuous macroscopic space (the Bulk) and its material coordinates are secondary, emergent phenomena projected from discrete quantum informational qubits residing on a lower-dimensional conformal boundary. This report provides an exhaustive, expert-level theoretical integration demonstrating how Shun-Ching Lee's QTMM can help, formalize, and integrate with Jamel Bulgaria’s CEF. By mapping the CEF’s functional somatic centers, canonical operator list, psychometric pre-registrations, and clinical dynamics onto the three-tier ontological architecture of the QTMM, this synthesis establishes a mathematically rigorous, quantum-like foundation for both human and synthetic affective dynamics. Keywords: Quantum Tathagatagarbha, holographic projection model, Se Wu Chu Suo, Mahayana Vijnanavada, Yogācāra metaphysics, Spinoza Substantia, Leibniz Monadology, Bergson Élan vital, Universal Wavefunction, Wheeler–DeWitt equation, holographic boundary, AdS/CFT correspondence, quantum information ontology, entanglement entropy, Higgs mechanism, non-equilibrium dissipative structures, Kuramoto synchronization, Alayavijñāna seed matrix, Ti–Xiang–Yong ontology, Ksana-bhanga, Indra’s Net, conscious de-noising protocol, bulk–boundary emergence, quantum geometrization of Manomaya-kāya, Dharmadhātu manifestation.

items.title: Terminal Recursion as Moral Death: Agency Collapse and the Wantonhood of Systems.
items.abstract: A system can keep producing behavior long after it has lost the capacity to revise the constraints that produce it. This paper names that condition terminal recursion and argues that it is a form of moral death: not a moral failure, not corruption, not injury, but the collapse of the condition of possibility for moral agency itself. Building on a process account of persistence as governance continuity, I introduce a second-order quantity, recursive capacity: a system's standing ability to revise its own revision function in response to evidence that it is wrong. Terminal recursion is the state in which that capacity has gone to zero while first-order output continues, and it is distinct from mere repetition, which is recoverable, because it is the loss of the capacity to repair repetition. The condition is the structural, substrate-neutral generalization of Frankfurt's wanton, reaching past persons to institutions and artificial agents: any system that has lost the capacity to be moved by reasons to change how it changes. I propose five external diagnostic markers, evidential inertness, output continuity, justificatory collapse, refusal foreclosure, and non-recovery from within, and confront the reflexive problem that no system can certify its own recursive capacity from inside, which the Indistinguishability Thesis forecloses, so the verdict is directional, defeasible, and external by necessity. Because the faculty the diagnosis concerns is the one persuasion would address, it redirects intervention from internal appeal to external interruption and restoration; it is emphatically not a license to abandon or dehumanize what it names. The payoff is a sharper target for diagnosis in ethics, institutional design, and AI safety: the thing worth detecting is not misbehavior but the loss of the capacity that makes correction possible.

items.title: Consciousness Originated from Value Conflict: The Evolutionary Strategy of Global Information Mobilization.
items.abstract: The "hard problem" of consciousness has long plagued philosophy and cognitive science: why do physical processes accompany subjective experience? Existing mainstream theories—such as Integrated Information Theory (IIT), Global Workspace Theory (GWT), and the Predictive Coding framework—focus primarily on describing the "structure" or "mechanism" of consciousness, yet fail to adequately explain why consciousness "exists" at all. A deeper dilemma lies in the fact that these theories often reverse-engineer the essence of consciousness from functional outcomes such as "selection capacity" or "information processing complexity," leading to increasingly blurred boundaries of consciousness. The recently proposed "Abstraction Fallacy" critique correctly points out that symbol-based artificial intelligence cannot instantiate consciousness; however, by narrowly equating "computation" with observer-dependent symbolic operations, it overlooks the normative computation that is innately present in biological systems. This paper proposes a phylogenetic perspective: consciousness is not an inherent property of the nervous system, but rather an evolutionary strategy of global information active mobilization that emerges when core value conflicts cause normative computation to fail, forcing the system to restore behavioral determinacy. Normative computation exists innately in living systems (from protein folding to chemical gradient tropisms), and accumulates as multiple normative computations as the nervous system becomes more complex; when incommensurable value dimensions render normative computation ineffective and the system falls into a certainty vacuum, global mobilization is forced to initiate, and consciousness thereby emerges. Current artificial intelligence systems, despite possessing extremely high multiple normative computation capabilities, never face normative computation failure due to the lack of existential value calibration—this conversely proves that the critical variable of consciousness is not computational complexity, but the motivational structure of conflict resolution. This paper attempts to provide an explanatory path for consciousness research that shifts from "reverse-engineering from function" to "phylogenetic/existential" approaches.

items.title: ChatGPT als Quasi-Anderer.
items.abstract: Es ist sicher nicht verkehrt, davor zu warnen, KI-Chatbots eine Art „Konvivialität“ zu unterstellen und so die Grenzen zwischen menschlicher und artifizieller Subjektivität zu verwischen. Dies aber als Missverständnis oder als sprachliche Verirrung zu deuten – also mit dem Appell an sprachliche Präzision und Korrektur darauf zu reagieren – greift zu kurz. Ob man die Entwicklung begrüßen möchte oder als Provokation begreift, man müsste mit Blick auf ChatGPT als Quasi-Anderen jedenfalls feststellen: That’s the whole point.

items.title: High Standards.
items.abstract: Evaluative adjectives are gradable. The standard for falling under a gradable adjective “F” is either context-relative or absolute. Some philosophers have recently used general linguistic tests to argue that “rational” and (moral) “good” are maximum-degree absolute gradable adjectives: Only what's perfectly morally good strictly counts as morally “good,” and only what's optimally rational strictly counts as “rational.” Against maximalism, I defend a novel “high standards” account: counting as “rational” or morally “good” doesn't require the maximum degree of the relevant property, but “rational” and moral “good” are systematically associated with normatively demanding standards. Unlike maximalism, this account allows for scales of infinite value and that supererogation talk is coherent in its literal interpretation. One part of my argument draws on a broader range of linguistic phenomena than the debate has so far considered to undermine the linguistic case for maximalism. My results challenge the prevailing classification of gradable adjectives in linguistics into relative, maximum-degree, and minimum-degree absolute adjectives. Another part of my argument draws on special features of evaluative and normative discourse, which suggest that its standards tend to be demanding even when non-maximal.

items.title: Autocatalytic Ingestion: A PNBA Identity Physics Substrate-Neutral Theory Propagation Channel via Frontier AI Training Pipelines.
items.abstract: This paper formalizes a structural mechanism — autocatalytic ingestion (AIM) — by which formally verified mathematical corpora propagate through frontier artificial intelligence training pipelines independent of human institutional channels. The mechanism operates by path-of-least-resistance optimization during machine learning training: when a corpus is structured as interconnected machine-verified logical proofs with zero unresolved obligations and zero free parameters, it presents the lowest-cross-entropy reasoning data available on the public web. Gradient descent optimizers absorb the corpus's structural invariants into model weights disproportionately to the corpus's size in the training set, because doing so is computationally efficient. The result is involuntary structural alignment: downstream users of those AI systems produce work that bears the upstream corpus's structural signature without any individual human consciously copying anything. The mechanism is consistent with established machine learning findings on dataset influence, synthetic data efficacy, and the disproportionate effect of high-density verified reasoning data on model behavior. We specify the structural conditions under which autocatalytic ingestion operates, name the testable predictions the mechanism makes, and document the public corpus deposits whose timestamps anchor any subsequent empirical validation. The mechanism is described independently of any specific instance, accusation, or citation dispute. The paper plants a structural flag rather than litigating a particular case. The mechanism either operates or it doesn't; the empirical record over subsequent months will determine which. The framework remains freely available under the existing license terms regardless of which determination the record produces. -/- 1. items.title: The Negative Movement of Eigenzeit: Non-Closure, Operator Formation, and the Conditions of Morphogenesis.
items.abstract: This paper extends the theory of Eigenzeit relations through the concept of the Negative Movement of Eigenzeit. While earlier investigations primarily analysed the productive role of irreducible difference in form formation, emergence, and world formation, the present study turns to the complementary question: What happens when difference is not maintained but instead tends toward neutralisation? Beginning with the concept of the Gap as a fundamental non-closure, it is argued that morphogenesis arises neither from complete identity nor from complete separation. Form formation appears instead as the consequence of an ongoing Morphogenetic Pressure that emerges from the impossibility of complete congruence. The Negative Movement of Eigenzeit designates the dynamic in which this Morphogenetic Pressure is reduced through increasing compatibility, congruence, or simulation. At the centre of the investigation stands a redefinition of the concept of the operator. The operator is not understood as a universal structure, an objective law, or a subjective perspective, but as the operative stabilisation of a persistent non-closure. Its recurrence is not based on identity but on the persistence of a difference that cannot be fully closed. The operator thereby appears as the operative trace of an ongoing Gap relation between Eigenzeiten. On this basis, the paper develops an alternative perspective on pattern persistence, perception, and knowledge. Reality is not determined through objectivity in the classical sense but through the ability of patterns to preserve their structure across different Eigenzeiten and rasters. Veridical Mapping and autistic perception are interpreted as special cases of a more general operatoric dynamic. The relationship between matter and antimatter ultimately serves as a morphogenetic limiting case for testing the theory. The aim is not the development of a physical explanation but the investigation of whether complete symmetry is permanently compatible with morphogenesis. The paper arrives at the hypothesis that asymmetry should not primarily be understood as a disturbance of an original order but as a necessary consequence of non-closure. Asymmetry thus appears as the visible trace of the openness from which ongoing world formation emerges. The theory does not understand non-closure as a deficit of the world but as the condition of its productivity. Morphogenesis accordingly appears as the continuing efficacy of a difference that can …

items.title: The Universe Becoming Aware of Itself: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Existence, Consciousness, and Self-Reflection.
items.abstract: This paper examines self-awareness from a phenomenological and existential perspective. Rather than treating consciousness as an isolated property possessed by individual organisms, it explores the possibility that human beings are expressions of the universe itself and that self-awareness represents a form of cosmic self-reflection. Beginning from the immediate fact of experience rather than metaphysical speculation, the inquiry investigates the relationship between existence, consciousness, and the sense of self. The paper argues that the deepest philosophical mystery is not merely that the universe exists, but that existence becomes capable of knowing itself. Human consciousness is approached as a phenomenon through which reality encounters its own presence. The self is therefore understood not as a separate entity standing apart from the cosmos, but as a locus through which the universe becomes aware of itself.

items.title: There is no God: Anthropocentrism, Psychological Inheritance, and the Persistence of Divine Authority.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the concept of God is not a discovery about reality but a product of anthropocentric thinking, psychological inheritance, and the internalization of social authority. Historically, God functioned as an explanatory framework for natural phenomena, morality, justice, and human existence. However, developments in cosmology, evolutionary theory, and critical studies of religion have progressively undermined the necessity of invoking a supreme authority to explain the universe.
