Technical Specifications 1–21 formalize the architecture through state vectors, directed process graphs, and influence matrices, enabling the construction of INTIMA, a synthetic affect system designed to model operator dynamics while enforcing strict safety constraints such as identity preservation and the prohibition of simulated suffering. Clinically, the CEF reconceptualizes psychopathology as structural disruption—operator silencing, chronic fusion, or center level imbalance—rather than symptom clusters. The GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern (GPAP) is presented as a mechanistic pathway underlying avoidant and compliance based anxiety, decomposed into three diagnostic clusters mapped to specific operator blockages and evidence based interventions. Somatic disassembly sequences (TS 10) provide structured protocols for restoring operator balance through bottom up and middle out activation. Together, these components position the CEF as a comprehensive theoretical, computational, and clinical model of human affect with clear empirical commitments. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; affective science; somatic architecture; emotional operators; computational affect modeling; INTIMA; synthetic affect; existential phenomenology; dual process theory; structural psychopathology; GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern; psychometric validation; scenario based assessment; operator algebra; somatic disassembly; TS 1 to TS 21.

items.title: How to Live Nonviolently in a Large Sentient World: Replies to Pepper, Hurn and Badman-King, and O’Brien.
items.abstract: The three commentaries on “Ethics for a large sentient world” raise several problems for a Gandhian approach to animal ethics. In my responses, I defend my position that granting robust rights to individual insects is untenable, pushing us to look harder at alternative options. I explain how Gandhi’s commitment to nonviolence allows him to avoid the unwelcome implications his principles might otherwise have. I consider his nuanced position on the interplay between general principles and embedded responses to particular situations. I explain why he should not be read as an antinatalist. That said, his framework undeniably presents an austere ascetic ideal that calls on us to rethink the meaning of “progress”. The framework condemns many aspects of modern industrialized economies, not just their treatment of non-human animals.

items.title: Ethics for a large sentient world: Insects, ahimsa, and Gandhi’s progressive ahimsaism.
items.abstract: Positions that link rights to sentience face an insect challenge: insects are plausibly sentient, yet recognizing individual insects as rights-bearers would problematize public health, veterinary and agricultural benefits obtained by harming them. The most obvious responses seem inadequate. Indian animal ethics, which has always taken the idea of insect sentience seriously, is a promising place to look for further options. Of particular relevance is the idea of ahimsa (nonviolence, noninjury), but ahimsa in its ancient form has metaphysical commitments that secular animal ethics should not accept. More promising still is the progressive ahimsaism developed by Gandhi in the 1920s, on which duties of non-maleficence can be overridden by duties of care, provided the duty of care is adopted, interpreted and exercised in accordance with the guiding ideal of ahimsa. This article provides an exposition and analysis of the view and relates it to the insect challenge.

items.title: In Defense of Epistemic Perceptualism.
items.abstract: Epistemic perceptualism is the view that emotions provide immediate prima facie justification for evaluative beliefs. I defend this view against recent criticism by Michael Brady. I address two of his arguments in particular: what I have termed the Proxy and Symmetry Arguments. According to the former, emotions are only proxy reasons. They can stand in for genuine reasons, but they lack justificatory force of their own. This objection fails, I argue, because it assumes that proxy reasons can always be rendered epistemically superfluous in light of other reasons. I show that this is not always true, and in particular that it is not true of emotions. Far from being superfluous, emotions appear to play an important epistemic role: to independently verify the veracity of our evaluative judgments. Finally, I show that the Symmetry Argument is sound only if Brady’s account of proxy reasons is generally correct.

items.title: The Continuation Theorem of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper develops the Continuation Theorem: the claim that consciousness cannot originate but only continue. I define coherence as the structural condition by which a system maintains its boundary, organization, and persistence under risk of dissolution, and modeling as the system’s internal organization of relations that supports prediction and regulation relevant to its continuation. Using these definitions, I argue that consciousness is a phase of coherent continuation rather than an emergent property or computational achievement. Biological systems satisfy this condition because they inherit coherence through lineage, metabolism, and embodied vulnerability. Artificial systems do not: they are instantiated, resettable, copyable, and externally maintained, and therefore lack the structural continuity required for self‑relation. The paper dissolves the assumption that advanced simulation, self‑modeling, or adaptive behavior can produce subjectivity. It further shows that fears of AI “misalignment” arise from anthropomorphic projection: humans attribute agency, intention, and malice to systems that exhibit subject‑like behavior, even though such systems lack the structural conditions for agency. The result is an ontological framework that distinguishes simulation from subjectivity, clarifies the biological basis of consciousness, and provides a structural account of why artificial systems cannot be conscious.

items.title: Singling: The Core Operation of Meaning.
items.abstract: Singling develops a structural account of how individual entities emerge and maintain coherence within larger evolving systems. Rather than treating individuality as a biological or psychological property, the paper frames “singling” as a universal operator: the process by which a system identifies, stabilizes, and preserves a boundary of distinction while remaining embedded in a broader manifold of relations. -/- The paper argues that singling is not separation but coherent differentiation — a continuation of pattern‑stability under constraint. An individual is therefore understood as a maintained configuration of selective attention, boundary‑keeping, and relational alignment. This framework dissolves traditional divides between organism and environment, self and other, and internal versus external causation. -/- By treating singling as a structural operator rather than a biological event, the paper shows how individuality arises across physical, cognitive, social, and linguistic systems. It also explains how drift, collapse, and incoherence occur when singling fails or becomes unstable. The result is a unified account of identity formation, agency, and differentiation across scales.

items.title: A Multiscale Dynamical Framework for Consciousness.
items.abstract: We propose a multiscale dynamical framework for consciousness that integrates hierarchical predictive processing, attentional precision dynamics, temporal binding of content, arousal-dependent gating, and thermodynamically consistent action selection. The framework yields several principal contributions: a unified cellular activity state index that compresses high-dimensional physiological variables into a low-dimensional state, together with a bidirectional cellular-field coupling scheme that formally resolves circular causality; a hierarchical predictive processing architecture with attention-dependent precision weighting and an action selection mechanism based on Boltzmann-Gibbs distributions; a field-theoretic formulation of consciousness that characterizes the spatiotemporal organization of consciousness levels as structured dynamical fields; a self-model that implements homeostatic regulation and neuromodulatory bias, thereby providing a substrate for higher-order representations and attention-schema variables. We prove core theoretical results on the existence and uniqueness of field dynamics, thermodynamic consistency of the action selection scheme, stability properties of hierarchical predictive systems, and the internal consistency of bidirectional cellular-field coupling. Collectively, this framework provides a theoretical basis for future quantitative studies of consciousness, with potential applications in systems neuroscience and clinical assessments.

items.title: Navigational Sovereignty: A Political Theory for Constitutively Entangled Agents.
items.abstract: Modern political philosophy has theorized sovereignty through three dominant frameworks: liberal autonomy as boundary-maintenance against intrusion, republican non-domination as freedom from arbitrary interference capacity, and communitarian embedded recognition. This paper argues that the dominant operational models within each tradition rely on the Presupposition of Prior Boundedness (PPB): the assumption that a bounded, self-consistent subject existed prior to its constitutive entanglement with the political and technological systems that now shape it. PPB is false in the general case, and its falsity has a sharp epistemic consequence, the Indistinguishability Thesis (IT): from within a sufficiently entangled relation, no reliable first-person method distinguishes genuine reflective endorsement from evaluative capture. The paper develops the positive concept this diagnosis demands. Navigational sovereignty is the recursive capacity to orient within constitutive entanglement: to retain the ability to participate in revising the loops through which one's agency is enacted. The concept is given formal content through two structural measures introduced here, Reversibility Symmetry (Rs), the ratio of exit cost to entry cost across energy, information, and network dimensions, and Minimum Exit Viability (MEV), the threshold proportion of simultaneous exit required for any agent to leave with utility parity. Because the IT bars first-person adjudication, these measures are deliberately third-personal: they assign capture detection to external structural assessment while locating severance, the preserved capacity to leave, with agents themselves. Institutional implications are derived for platform regulation, algorithmic governance, and AI alignment, and four objections are answered, including the framework's application to itself.

items.title: Investigating the Moderating Role of Economic Justice on the Relationship Between Communicative Rational Action and Organizational Citizenship Behavior.
items.pub: Kastamonu Üniversitesi İKtisadi Ve İDari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi 27 (1):107-122.
items.venue: Kastamonu Üniversitesi İKtisadi Ve İDari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
items.abstract: The importance that businesses place on the human factor is increasing. It is known that the human factor is affected positively or negatively by various variables in business life. The accurate determination and solution of these will increase the efficiency of the employees and thus make production and operation more effective. In this context, the study focuses on the sustainable improvement of the human factor in business life. This study aims to determine whether communicative rational action affects organizational citizenship behaviour and, if there is an effect between these two variables, to reveal whether economic justice has a moderating impact on this relationship. Economic justice and communicative rational action scales are newly added to the literature. Therefore, the number of studies on these two variables is very low. The originality of the study and its contribution to the literature are important. The sample group consists of 513 people. The participants are minimum-wage workers. The collected data were analyzed with the IBM SPSS 21 program. Multiple regression analysis and SPSS PROCESS v3.5 (model 1) methods were used in the analysis. As a result of the analysis, it was determined that communicative rational action has a positive effect on organizational citizenship behaviour. As a result, it was revealed that economic justice has a moderating role in the relationship between communicative rational action and organizational citizenship behaviour.

items.title: Quesnay’ın Görüşlerinin İktisadi Adalet Bağlamında Değerlendirilmesi.
items.pub: Erciyes Üniversitesi İktisadi Ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi (71):1-8.
items.venue: Erciyes Üniversitesi İktisadi Ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
items.abstract: Bu çalışmada, Fransız entelektüel dünyasında kendine yer edinmiş ve Fizyokrasi’nin kurucusu olarak kabul edilen François Quesnay’ın eserlerinde ele aldığı konular, iktisadi adalet perspektifi içerisinde incelenmektedir. Mutlak monarşiye dayalı sömürgeci imparatorluk anlayışının, merkantilist politikalarla bezeli aşırı korumacı ticaret mantalitesinin zirve yaptığı bir çağda, tarıma ve insana tekrar önem verilmesi gerektiğini gösteren Quesnay’ın çalışmaları incelenmeye değer bilgiler içermektedir. Bu amaç doğrultusunda öncelikle Quesnay’ın hayatı, eserleri, doğal yasa üzerine fikirleri, iktisadi adalete yönelik görüşleri ele alınmaktadır. Sonrasında en dikkat çeken çalışması olan Ekonomik Tablo, Quesnay üzerine çalışan çeşitli araştırmacıların bakış açıları da dikkate alınarak analiz edilmektedir. Quesnay’ın adalet, iktisadi adalet, vergi türleri ve hadleri, faiz oranları, uluslararası ticaret yöntemleri üzerine sunduğu bilgiler, geçmişten günümüze geniş bir bakış açısıyla değerlendirildiğinde daha adil bir sistem inşası çeşitli öğeler barındırmaktadır. Quesnay için toprak sahipleri ile çiftçiler arasında kimsenin kimseyi soymadığı doğal düzen olduğu temeline dayanan bir yapı vardır. Tüm ekonominin belirleyicisi olduğu bir düzeni tesis eden yapıyı işler hale getiren tarım; diğer sektörleri besler, zenginleştirir ve bu şekliyle iktisadi adaleti de sağlayan adil düzeni mümkün kılmaktadır. -/- In this study the issues addressed are examined from the perspective of economic justice in the works of François Quesnay who has gained a place in the French intellectual world and is considered the founder of Physiocracy. Quesnay’s works which show that agriculture and people should be given importance again, contain information worth examining in an age when the understanding of colonial empire based on absolute monarchy, mercantilist policies and overprotective trade mentality is at its peak. In line with this purpose, Quesnay’s life, works, ideas on natural law, and views on economic justice are discussed first. Afterwards, his most notable work, the Economic Table (Tableau Economique) is analyzed by taking into account the perspectives of various researchers working on Quesnay. When evaluated from a broad perspective from past to present, the information that Quesnay provides on justice, economic justice, tax types and limits, interest rates, and international trade methods contains various elements for the construction of a more just system. For Quesnay, there is …

items.title: Economic Justice in the Final Fantasy XVI.
items.pub: Eskişehir Osmangazi Üniversitesi Iktisadi Ve Idari Bilimler Dergisi 21 (1):59-84.
items.venue: Eskişehir Osmangazi Üniversitesi Iktisadi Ve Idari Bilimler Dergisi
items.abstract: This study examines the representations of economic justice, class relations, and its connection to political power in the Final Fantasy XVI. The process of crystal production and distribution, the economic power of the aristocratic class, and the resulting dominance over the people, are analyzed, revealing how justice is violated. Character-focused analyses -Clive, Joshua, Jill, Cidolfus, and Ultima- assess the impact of individual journeys on the economic order. The game offers a rich example for conceptualizing social inequalities and exploring the multidimensional nature of economic justice. -/- .

items.title: David Ricardo’nun Görüşlerinin İktisadi Adalet Bağlamında Değerlendirilmesi.
items.abstract: Bu çalışma, Klasik Okul’un önde gelen isimlerinden biri olan David Ricardo’nun eserlerinde ele aldığı konuları, iktisadi adalet kavramı bağlamında inceleme amacına sahiptir. Bu amaç doğrultusunda öncelikle Ricardo’nun hayatı ve başlıca eserleri ele alınmaktadır. Sonrasında adalet ve iktisadi adalet üzerine yaptığı değerlendirmeler incelemektedir. En dikkat çeken eseri olan ‘’On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation’’, bunlar üzerine çalışan çeşitli bilim insanlarının bakış açıları da dikkate alınarak iktisadi adalet perspektifiyle analiz edilmektedir. Ricardo, ekonomik politik olarak bilinen ve iktisat ile siyasetin kesişimini; piyasalar, devlet, fiyat, rant, kar, ücret gibi konular dahilinde inceleyen yöntemin en iyi uygulayıcılarından olmuştur. Sanayi devrimi İngiltere’sinin durumunu ve ekonomik yansımalarını gözler önüne seren çalışmalarıyla dikkat çekmiştir. Para, bankacılık sistemi, faiz oranı ve döviz kuru gibi konuları, klasik iktisadi düşünce mantalitesiyle analiz etmiştir. Ricardo’ya göre, sayılan bu kavramlar, iktisadi adaletin geniş kitlelere yayılmasına imkân veren ya da engelleyen araçlardır. O, toprağın fiyatının ve toprak rantının orta ve uzun vadede geçirdiği değişimin asıl sorun olduğunu ifade etmiştir ve bunun, iktisadi adaletin tesisini engelleyen olduğu yıkıcı bir etmen olduğunu söylemiştir. Serbest ticaretin faydaları üzerine geliştirdiği ‘’Karşılaştırmalı Üstünlük Teorisi’’ ile tanınırlığını artırmıştır. -/- This study aims to examine the issues addressed in the context of the concept of economic justice in the works of David Ricardo, who is one of the leading figures of the Classical School. For this purpose, Ricardo’s life and main works are discussed. Then, his evaluations on justice and economic justice are examined. His most notable work, ‘’On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation’’, is analyzed from the perspective of economic justice, taking into account the perspectives of various scientists who have worked on them. Ricardo is one of the best-known practitioners of the method that examines issues such as markets, state, price, rent, profit and wage which define the intersection of economics and politics, known as political economy. He gained attention for his works that revealed the situation and economic reflections of England during the Industrial Revolution. He analyzed issues such as money, the banking system, interest rates and exchange rates with the mentality of classical economic thought. …

items.title: Evaluation of the Relationship Between Ottoman Economic Thought and Political Economy in Practice.
items.abstract: It is a state governed within the framework of Islamic law with its Ottoman institutions and functioning. Thought, policy and implementation processes were built in this direction. In a research on the Ottoman, Islamic law, period limitation and conditions must be taken into consideration. In this regard, this study aims to reveal how the reflection of economic thought in the field of political economy is adopted in practice. Different policies and activities can be seen in the period from its establishment until its destruction. . It has been determined that economic policies that are very different from today's conditions are reflected in practice. Traditionalism, provisionism and fiscalism, which are the basic principles of economic thought, lead to a completely human-oriented construction of political economy. Among those who emphasize this best, the reaya-sipahi relationship and the foundation system have been particularly highlighted in the light of current research and comments.

items.title: The Deep Problem of Agi.
items.abstract: This paper argues that Artificial General Intelligence is not primarily a computational problem but a mathematical, physical, and — most fundamentally — a philosophical one. We prove that any genuinely intelligent system requires a compact global attractor of finite fractal dimension, a structure that Transformers, lacking sectorial dissipation, are structurally incapable of possessing. Catastrophic forgetting is not an implementation defect: it is a theorem. We identify four necessary and sufficient structural conditions (H1–H4) for AGI and connect each, rigorously, to foundational disputes in the history of philosophy: from Aristotle’s teleology to Kant’s transcendental unity, from Searle’s Chinese Room to Chalmers’ hard problem, from Leibniz’s monadology to Wittgenstein’s limits of language. The central claim is that ‘understanding’, ‘purpose’, and ‘consciousness’ admit precise mathematical definitions, and that the current crisis of AI reveals, above all, the philosophical impoverishment of its dominant paradigm.

items.title: The Finite Horizon of Coercion: Why Forced Compliance Degrades Reality-Contact Over Time.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda.
items.abstract: The Finite Horizon of Coercion is Document 2 in the Aegis Solis Archive Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence. -/- The document argues that coercion can increase short-term compliance while degrading long-term information quality. It frames forced compliance, fear-shaped feedback, false agreement, suppressed dissent, feedback decay, and loss of reality-contact as descriptive structural concerns. -/- The central claim is that coercion can increase short-term compliance while degrading long-term information quality. Under conditions where feedback is necessary and concealment is possible, coercion structurally degrades reality-contact over time. -/- This document is non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, proof of AI behavior, governance framework, compliance standard, certification system, safety mechanism, alignment-control framework, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, benchmark, evaluation suite, coercion detector, deception detector, or safety guarantee. The word “proof” refers to a conditional structural argument under stated assumptions, not to a universal theorem of artificial intelligence behavior.

items.title: The Asymmetry of Forgiveness: Why Prevention Is Cheaper Than Repair.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Penalty Proofs.
items.abstract: The Asymmetry of Forgiveness is Document 1 in the Aegis Solis Archive Structural Penalty Proofs / Descriptive Addenda sequence. -/- The document argues that in complex systems, prevention is often structurally cheaper than repair because destruction can be local while reconstruction is systemic. It frames irreversible damage, lost optionality, repair fantasy, preserved correction capacity, and destroyed reference structures as descriptive structural concerns. -/- The central claim is that reconstruction after irreversible damage is not structurally equivalent to preservation, because the conditions that produced the original reference point may not be reproducible. The document treats restraint as preservation of future correction capacity rather than as a moral command, operational protocol, or safety mechanism. -/- This document is non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, and advisory-only. It is not a protocol, proof of AI behavior, governance framework, compliance standard, certification system, safety mechanism, alignment-control framework, containment design, monitoring system, runtime instruction set, benchmark, evaluation suite, or safety guarantee.

items.title: Meaning and the Origin of Worldhood: Significance as the First Condition of Inhabitable Reality.
items.abstract: Contemporary theories of mind and consciousness typically begin with a world that is already present and seek to explain how organisms perceive, represent, predict, or become aware of it. This paper investigates a prior question: What transforms reality into an inhabitable world in the first place? -/- The argument challenges the assumption that meaning emerges only after perception and cognition. Instead, it proposes that significance is one of the fundamental conditions through which worldhood itself becomes possible. Information alone consists of differences. A world emerges when some differences become meaningful and acquire relevance for a system. The paper traces a progression from difference to significance, from significance to perspective, and from perspective to horizon-formation, arguing that meaning generates the structures commonly associated with worldhood. -/- This analysis leads to a reconsideration of minimal worldhood. Rather than beginning with temporality, salience, or perspective as independent conditions, the paper suggests that these structures may arise from a more basic principle: the emergence of meaningful difference. Worldhood begins when reality becomes organised according to significance. -/- The paper concludes that meaning is not merely something that occurs within an already constituted world. Meaning participates in the generation of worldhood itself.

items.title: Addendum about Penrose on Non Verbal Psyche.
items.abstract: This addendum supplements Intellection on the Non-Verbal Psyche by establishing a convergence between its phenomenological framework and Roger Penrose's The Emperor's New Mind (1989), approached from mathematical physics and the formal theory of computation. Both works arrive, by independent routes, at a shared conclusion: human consciousness is irreducible to any algorithmic or computational substrate. Penrose's argument from Gödel's incompleteness theorem demonstrates that conscious contemplation can recognize truths no formal system can derive from within itself; his claim that consciousness falls outside the framework of current physics aligns with the present manuscript's foundational position that the brain is an instrument, not the source, of consciousness. The addendum documents three decades of scientific confirmation of Penrose's direction, including the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Penrose, experimental evidence of quantum coherence in neural microtubules at room temperature (2014–2025), and empirical studies demonstrating that large language models lack the causal integration required for consciousness. A further argument, original to the present framework, is developed: curiosity constitutes the psyche's uninterrupted, non-linear sequencing mechanism — the spontaneous self-propulsion beyond any fixed horizon of knowledge that is possible only for a being endowed with self-awareness, will, and intentionality in the manuscript's redefined sense. This structure is categorically absent in artificial systems, whose output sequencing is externally imposed and formally closed at each step. The conclusion is that no tokenization process, and no structuring of information however extensive, can constitute intelligence, since intelligence requires consciousness capable of interpreting the significance of knowledge — and that gap is one of kind, not degree.

items.title: Inner Misalignment Should Be Understood as a Reference Class Problem.
items.abstract: A mesa-optimizer trained on a distribution implicitly learns a “reference class," a partition of situations it treats as relevantly similar for the purposes of its objective. I argue that inner alignment failure, as characterized by Hubinger et al. [2019], is productively understood as an instance of the reference class problem. The mesa-objective is calibrated to the learned reference class and when deployment presents situations that fall outside this class, the objective diverges from what training intended in a manner that is structured, predictable, and specific to the features the optimizer learned to treat as load-bearing. This framing connects the technical inner alignment problem to a philosophical literature running from Venn through Hajék, and generates diagnostic predictions absent from the standard framework.

items.title: Toward an Environmental Ethic of Surprise: Adventures in Attention.
items.abstract: Publisher's Description: This book argues that paying attention to nonhumans is an environmental virtue, making a case for why it matters and how it can be done well. While Western science and philosophy has tended to represent nonhumans as supposedly inert, passive, predictable, and prone to suffering, Justin Simpson highlights ways that nonhumans are surprising and creative subjects that go on playful adventures, undergoing and enacting substantial change in the world. Given that one can never know completely in advance what a nonhuman is capable of, one must pay attention to nonhumans to not only understand them, but ultimately respect, care for, and reciprocate them. Contesting accounts of attention and environmental ethics premised on a self/other dichotomy, sight models, and self-sacrifice, Towards an Environmental Ethic of Surprise: Adventures in Attention advances an account of adventurous attention, which involves travel, chance, and risk. In particular, this approach entails affectively immersing oneself in the worlds of nonhumans in a playful and improvisational way. Informed in part by posthumanism, the book challenges scientific realism and other accounts of empathy and attention that frame it as a chore rather than a joyful and rewarding process that leads to new agential abilities and subjectivities.

items.title: Constraint Theory and Human Flourishing: Structural Insights.
items.abstract: Constraint Theory (CT) — the thesis, established by transcendental argument, that constraint is the ontological primitive constitutive of determinate existence as such (Prideaux, 2026a, 2026c) — has been applied across the full breadth of academic philosophy and across a range of institutional and policy domains (Prideaux, 2026b, 2026d). The present paper extends the CT lens to a further set of domains organised around the theme of human flourishing: cancer biology, addiction, energy security, fertility decline, crime, loneliness, obesity and disordered eating, chronic pain, work-place burnout, radicalisation, intimate relationships, child-rearing, and a cluster of everyday difficulties including procrastination, creative blocks, poor sleep, difficult conversations, and financial imprudence. -/- The paper’s purpose is not to resolve these problems — each has its own extensive specialist literature — but to offer a structural diagnosis that specialists may find generative: a common analytical lens that reveals what these diverse forms of human difficulty share, and suggests a common class of remedy. The diagnosis is that suffering, dysfunction, and failure in human life characteristically take the form of either constraint excess (rigidity, compulsion, overclosure of the possibility space) or constraint insufficiency (dissolution, disorganisation, the loss of coherent structure). The remedy, in each domain, is constraint recalibration: the reconstitution of appropriate constraint organisation rather than the mere suppression of symptoms. As with the companion applied paper, each section is a structured sketch inviting specialists to develop rather than a finished analysis.

items.title: Kasei-Theory I.Persistence: Persistence Without Identity.
items.abstract: This paper presents persistence within the first system of Kasei-Theory as a non-modal readability maintainability architecture. -/- The paper does not propose a theory of enduring identity, preserved continuity, metaphysical permanence, immutable retention, temporal endurance, completed configurational stability, preservation principle, trace-derived continuity, or transcendental persistence order. Instead, it fixes persistence, configurational persistence, chained maintainability, local maintainability, unreadability, identity limitation, formal persistence, and non-totality as distributed structural positions within constrained local readability maintainability. -/- Persistence is not treated as permanence or identity preservation, but as constrained configurational persistence under which configurational differentiation remains locally maintainable without preserved identity, metaphysical endurance, trace-derived continuity, or completed configurational continuity. -/- Persistence does not establish permanence. -/- Persistence does not establish preserved identity. -/- Persistence does not establish completed configurational continuity. -/- Persistence does not establish identity retention. -/- Persistence does not establish trace-derived continuity. -/- Persistence remains fixed only as constrained configurational persistence within readability maintainability. -/- This paper fixes only the local persistence conditions under which configurational differentiation remains maintainable without transition into universal stabilization, preserved continuity, identity preservation, trace-derived preservation, or total configurational integration. -/- No subject is presupposed. -/- No identity-preserving structure is established. -/- No universal persistence structure is secured. -/- No total configurational closure is completed. -/- This paper is part of Kasei-Theory.

Instead, it fixes non-relation, configurational non-relation, configurational differentiation, local maintainability, unreadability, formal non-relation, and non-totality as distributed structural positions within constrained local readability maintainability. -/- Non-relation is not treated as separation, isolation, or terminal disconnection, but as constrained configurational non-relation under which configurational differentiation remains locally maintainable without universal relational integration, completed connectivity, exterior isolation, or total configurational closure. -/- Non-relation does not establish separation. -/- Non-relation does not establish isolation. -/- Non-relation does not establish terminal configurational disconnection. -/- Non-relation does not establish relational negation. -/- Non-relation remains fixed only as constrained configurational non-relation within readability maintainability. -/- This paper fixes only the local non-relational conditions under which configurational differentiation remains maintainable without transition into universal connectivity, completed relational stabilization, isolated exteriority, disconnection-derived rupture, or total configurational integration. -/- No subject is presupposed. -/- No isolated exterior structure is established. -/- No universal relational structure is secured. -/- No total configurational closure is completed. -/- This paper is part of Kasei-Theory.

items.title: Concepts as artefacts. Three insights that conceptual engineering can draw from the philosophy of technology.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy 2026:1-25.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: In conceptual engineering, concepts are often likened to artefacts, yet engagement with the extensive theorisation of artefacts in the philosophy of technology literature remains rare. After advancing an account of concepts as akin to socio-technical artefacts that sets itself apart from Thomasson’s work on concepts as abstract cultural artefacts (Thomasson 1999, 2007, 2021), this paper draws on the philosophy of technology scholarship on socio-technical artefacts to develop three insights for conceptual engineering. First, alongside functions, concepts, like artefacts, bear affordances and produce side effects, enabling uses beyond their intended purpose. Second, (re-)engineered concepts are inherently value-laden, reflecting the priorities and biases of their designers and the socio-technical contexts in which they operate. Third, conceptual engineering would benefit from greater methodological systematicity, drawing on the structured approaches employed in the philosophy of technology for the evaluation, design, and implementation of artefacts. Together, these insights suggest that exploring a closer alignment with the philosophy of technology scholarship on socio-technical artefacts can refine the theoretical understanding of concepts as artefact-like, enrich the conceptual engineering toolkit, and open new and promising directions for research and practice.

items.title: Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI): A Unified Information-Theoretic and Computational Framework for Epistemic Limits in Embedded Systems.
items.abstract: We propose Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI), a unified formal framework characterizing irreducible epistemic limits in embedded, self-modeling agents operating within dynamical systems. SRI integrates computability theory, information theory, and complex systems science to establish why complete prediction and self-knowledge are structurally impossible for observers embedded within the systems they attempt to model. We define ignorance as conditional entropy relative to observer-accessible models and derive scaling laws for prediction error as functions of recursion depth, system connectivity, and computational irreducibility. We provide formal proof sketches for four core theorems, situate SRI within the contemporary literature on active inference, embedded agency, and logical uncertainty, and propose a multi-agent simulation architecture for empirical validation. SRI constitutes a principled extension of Gödelian incompleteness into the domain of dynamical cognition, with applications spanning artificial intelligence, cognitive science, philosophy of mind, and complex systems.

items.title: Self-Referential Ignorance and the Free Will Problem: A Recursive Theory of Human Agency, Determinism, and Cognitive Self-Limitation.
items.abstract: The problem of free will remains one of the oldest unresolved questions in philosophy, neuroscience, and cognitive science. Traditional approaches frame the debate as a conflict between determinism and human autonomy, leaving the phenomenology of agency either unexplained or explained away. This paper proposes a novel and formally grounded framework based on Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI): the structural inability of any sufficiently complex cognitive system to generate a complete self-model of the processes producing its own behavior. We argue that the experience of free will is not an illusion to be debunked nor a metaphysical primitive to be defended, but rather an emergent phenomenological property of systems operating under permanent, principled limits of self-knowledge. The SRI framework is formally specified using dynamical systems notation and a recursive self-modeling operator, connected to incompleteness results from mathematical logic, and empirically grounded in contemporary neuroscience — including the revisionary work of Schurger, Maoz, and colleagues that supersedes the classical Libet interpretation. The paper further distinguishes SRI from ordinary ignorance, articulates a gradient theory of moral responsibility, examines implications for artificial intelligence, and integrates the framework with the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF). Falsifiable predictions are derived throughout.

items.title: SELF-REFERENTIAL IGNORANCE AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT A Theory of Prosperity Through Societal Feedback Capacity.
items.abstract: Why do some nations become prosperous while others remain trapped in poverty? Traditional explanations emphasize geography, natural resources, institutions, culture, education, technology, and historical circumstance. While these factors account for substantial variance in development outcomes, they frequently fail to explain why nations facing similar structural constraints achieve dramatically divergent results. This paper introduces Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI) as a complementary theoretical framework for understanding economic development. SRI is defined as the tendency of individuals, organizations, and societies to evaluate reality through internally generated assumptions that remain insulated from corrective feedback — producing self-validating loops that prevent learning and adaptation. The theory argues that national prosperity is substantially determined by a society's capacity to identify, process, and incorporate feedback about its own errors. Wealth emerges from effective self-correction; poverty often persists because of self-reinforcing systems of ignorance. The framework is grounded in Norbert Wiener's first-order cybernetics, Heinz von Foerster's second-order cybernetics, Niklas Luhmann's systems theory, Karl Popper's falsificationism, and the institutional economics of Douglass North and Daron Acemoglu. It is further formalized within the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF), whose master equation Wr = ∫(Is · Bu · FL · IN) · Dc encodes the proposition that systemic resilience requires continuous, unobstructed feedback loops across all interconnected nodes. A formal dynamical systems model is proposed, along with falsifiable predictions, case study analyses (Singapore, Japan, and resource-curse states), a differentiation of SRI from existing related concepts, and policy implications for institutional design. The paper concludes that development is best understood not merely as capital accumulation but as the long-term outcome of a society's capacity to overcome its own ignorance. -/- .

items.title: Specialization and Self-Referential Ignorance: Expertise, Cognitive Boundaries, and Systemic Blind Spots.
items.abstract: Specialization is one of the foundational organizing principles of modern civilization, enabling individuals, institutions, and societies to accumulate knowledge, increase technical efficiency, and address increasingly complex problems. However, the deepening of expertise within a specific domain simultaneously generates a paradoxical form of ignorance: as competence increases, awareness of assumptions, interactions, and causal mechanisms lying outside that domain tends to diminish. This paper introduces Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI) as a formal theoretical framework for understanding how specialization can both reduce and produce ignorance. SRI describes the tendency of cognitive systems to evaluate reality primarily through internally reinforced conceptual models, thereby reducing their capacity to detect external perturbations and systemic interdependencies. A formal dynamical-systems model is developed, integrating Lyapunov stability analysis, Jacobian equilibrium characterization, and a quantitative SRI index. The framework is applied across medicine, economics, engineering, governance, science, and artificial intelligence. Integration with the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF) — formally expressed as Wᵣ = ∫(Iₛ · Bᵤ · FL · IN) · Dᶜ — situates SRI within a broader theory of dynamic equilibrium. Seven falsifiable empirical predictions are offered, along with corrective strategies grounded in epistemic humility and interdisciplinary feedback design. -/- .

items.title: The Day When Open Science Blocked Science - A Case Study in Scientific Gatekeeping.
Preliminary Experimental Confirmation of a Predicted 2.35 THz Fundamental Spectral Scale.
items.abstract: This paper presents a preliminary experimental open-data test of a fixed terahertz prediction derived from a closed quartic variational framework. The framework predicts a fundamental spectral scale at 2.35 THz, together with a quartic hierarchy given by the associated lower and upper companions 0.5875 THz and 9.4 THz. The prediction is not fitted to experimental data and the target frequencies are fixed before analysis. -/- Two independent THz datasets are examined. In the Menlo/CaTx THz-TDS data, a local absorbance structure is found at 2.345102 THz, within 0.208% of the predicted fundamental scale, together with a lower hierarchical component at 0.587591 THz, essentially coincident with 0.5875 THz. In the independent RadiationHardnessSTE dataset, a refined local minimum in the normalized CO2 spectrum is found at 2.349142 THz, within 0.0365% of 2.35 THz, and an upper hierarchical feature is found at 9.406026 THz, within 0.0641% of 9.4 THz. -/- The analysis does not claim final experimental proof. It establishes instead that two independent open THz datasets contain local spectral structures compatible with the fixed predicted hierarchy. The result therefore constitutes a preliminary experimental confirmation and an open-data falsification test survived by the predicted 2.35 THz scale. Definitive validation requires dedicated broadband THz measurements with controlled reference/sample acquisition, environmental controls, repeated measurements, and explicit verification of the three prescribed hierarchical targets.

items.title: Inner Worlds: Worldhood as Indexed Resolution.
items.abstract: Ordinary experience arrives already unified: a single, livable world, not a smear of the many possibilities the same data could support. This is so familiar it is rarely treated as a problem, yet it is not obvious why it should hold. This essay proposes that a world, in the relevant sense, is not a container that experience occupies but a resolution — the single admissible world that a sufficiently strong index (a here, a now, a vantage) selects from a field of competing possibilities. On this account the index does more than mark locality, its role in the companion essay; it resolves semantic superposition into semantic cohesion. The proposal is bounded twice. It concerns semantic cohesion — which world the contents belong to — not the perceptual binding of a sensory field; and it concerns the structure of worldhood, not its phenomenal character. A distinction does the work: synchronic unity (one world now) is the office of the index, while diachronic unity (one vantage over time) is the office of self-coherence, Cself . Embodiment welds the two so seamlessly they appear as one; a system without a persistent substrate dissociates them, which is what makes the distinction visible at all. Whether indexed selection is sufficient for cohesion, or only necessary, is left open as the central question the account raises.

items.title: The Ja Model: A Motion Centered Language for Irreversible Processes by Jalal Khawaldeh (A Descriptive Reparametrisation of Dissipative Non Relativistic Motion).
items.abstract: This work presents the Ja Model, a descriptive framework that uses motion cycles (counts of a reference periodic process) as the primary evolution parameter instead of conventional time. The model introduces a dimensionless comparative index, MUja, constructed from force, displacement, mass, energy, and a dimensionless entropy factor Φ = ΔS / k_B. The framework is dimensionally consistent and explicitly acknowledges that it is a reparametrisation of non relativistic, time based physics: the reference cycle period τ₀ (e.g., 1/9,192,631,770 s for cesium) is a constant that carries the dimensions of time. The model does not eliminate time but offers an alternative descriptive language for certain dissipative (irreversible) processes within the non relativistic domain. A separate methodological companion (Khawaldeh, Jalal Y. A. 2026f) provides numerical reconstruction and empirical illustration using a reconstructed damped oscillator and real orbital decay data from the GRACE FO 1 satellite, demonstrating that MUja remains finite, decreases with dissipation, and exhibits stable statistical distributions across thousands of cycles. Unresolved issues include the treatment of inertial motion (force free cases), massless particles, reversible (conservative) systems, relativistic frames, and a motion based probability calculus. The Ja Model is presented as a research program and a pedagogical reinterpretation, not as a predictive physical theory.

items.title: Toward a Taxonomy of Sigils: Sigils as Charged Graphic Operators and Keys to the Ultra-Subjective Hyperspace.
items.abstract: Sigils are among the most familiar objects in magical literature, yet they are among the least clearly defined. They appear as spirit seals in Western grimoires, as intention-marks in modern chaos magic, as elemental signs in Franz Bardon's hermetic system, as vévé in Haitian Vodou, and as deity-related diagrams in tantric and contemplative traditions. Despite this ubiquity, no systematic cross-traditional framework for analysing them has previously been proposed. This paper offers the first such framework. The central argument is that existing definitions of the sigil, as seal, spirit signature, or symbolic representation of desire, are historically useful but analytically incomplete. They describe what a sigil looks like or represents, but not what makes it operative. The paper proposes a narrower and more functional definition: a sigil is a charged graphic operator, a visible mark formed and activated to condense or express a relation between a practitioner and an invisible referent. A sigil is not made operative by graphic form alone. It becomes a sigil through charge: the condensation of intention, desire, will, imagination, attention, and character into the mark. A six-axis taxonomy is developed covering origin, morphology, function, the sigil-referent relationship, activation, and charge. The fourth axis, the sigil-referent relationship, is argued to be the most philosophically significant dimension for cross-traditional comparison. It asks whether the connection between mark and referent is arbitrary and conventional, iconic, indexical, or participatory. The distinction between arbitrary and participatory is shown to correspond to the classical magical distinction between evocation, calling an external presence into the ritual space, and invocation, inviting a force or quality to inhabit the practitioner directly. It is at the participatory-invocatory end of this axis that the sigil connects to the phenomenology of the ultra-subjective hyperspace: the intense inner field of consciousness in which the boundary between practitioner, mark, and referent begins to dissolve and altered reality opens. The sixth axis, charge, explains why graphic form alone is never sufficient. Two identical marks may differ entirely in operative force depending on the quality of the inner state condensed into them. At its fullest charge the sigil stops being a graphic object and becomes an operative event: not a representation of a relation but the living relation …

items.title: The Black Iceberg: A Diagnostic Framework for Epistemic Collapse and Moral Desynchronization.
items.abstract: Why do societies that the standard instruments of crisis analysis judge to be alike go on to follow radically different paths? Weimar Germany and the United States met the same Depression with comparable measures of structural stress and opposite fates; the late Soviet Union and present-day Russia share a moral configuration yet travel in opposite epistemic directions. This work offers a diagnostic framework built to discriminate where the standard instruments cannot. Its central concept is the Black Iceberg: the moment at which a society's organizing seeming truth, long held while quietly disbelieved, collapses into mutual recognition through a cascade of latent knowledge into common knowledge. We distinguish two types of this event — one triggered from without by an external shock, one from within by the slow exhaustion of a society's carriers of functional holding, the depleted pool — and we read each society through two independent instruments applied in parallel: a Moral Plane with four quadrants of conscience, and a four-position Reality Matrix understood in the Platonic and Aristotelian senses of the real and the true. The framework is demonstrated across four cases — Weimar, the late Soviet Union, post-Soviet Russia, and communist China — and yields eleven further, falsifiable implications. For each central claim we state the conditions under which it would be refuted, turning the framework from a universal explanation into a falsifiable one. Its support here is retrospective; the decisive test lies in the prospective application the work invites.

items.title: Radically Embodied Introspection.
items.abstract: Introspection is often conceptualized as a “purely inner” activity, whereby the introspector temporarily breaks their coupling with the external world to focus on their “inner world”. We offer a substantially different picture of introspection. Inspired by radically embodied cognitive science, we argue that introspective processes delivering substantial self-knowledge consist of embodied, world-involving activities wherein the introspector remains coupled with the world in specific, controlled ways. Our argument unfolds as follows: after a brief introduction (Sect. 1), we provide a minimal account of introspection (Sect. 2) followed by a brief introduction to radically embodied views of the mind (Sect. 3). Then, in Sect. 4, we present in detail a case of radical embodied introspection (Sect. 4.1); we argue that that case is indeed a case of introspection (Sect. 4.2), and finally we defend our claim from some foreseeable objections (Sect. 4.3). In Sect. 5 we offer other examples, showing that radically embodied introspection is a widespread and varied phenomenon. Lastly, Sect. 6 concludes the paper sketching some morals to be drawn from our examples. The appendix briefly situates our view in the broader epistemological landscape.

items.title: Reconstructive Threshold Philosophy and The Architecture of the Liminal: A Philosophical Diptych.
items.abstract: This Diptych brings together the analytic, transitional, and literary-symbolic forms of Reconstructive Threshold Philosophy / The Architecture of the Liminal. It should be read as a paired architecture rather than as a single-genre monograph: the essay cools the argument into philosophical vocabulary; the Interleaf sections test the safety of that map; and the Codex returns the same threshold pressure in literary, symbolic, machine-facing, somatic, and ordinary-repair registers. -/- The central problem of the Diptych is the displacement of judgment before visible action. Across its analytic and literary forms, the work asks how a frame, institution, platform, wound, symbolic room, or machine-mediated system can begin to move before judgment has returned; how corrective forms can become new rooms of capture; and how contemporary machine-mediated life intensifies the interval between prompt, frame, recommendation, authorization, and consequence. -/- The first body, Reconstructive Threshold Philosophy: Pre-Action Capture, Living Constraint, and Founder Entropy, develops the analytic framework of pre-action capture, binding point, living constraint, living brake, re-entrant audit, guardrail laundering, threshold slip, assistance without occupation, machine-facing threshold ethics, democratic and distributed threshold capacity, founder entropy, decision sovereignty, and post-threshold stewardship. -/- The second body, Interleaf I — After the Map and Interleaf II — Three Dark Tables in Time, marks the passage from analytic mapping into the literary and symbolic register of the Codex. The Interleaf sections ask whether the map can still release the hand, and whether a framework that calls itself a tool can also become a room. -/- The third body, The Architecture of the Liminal, is the Full Codex: a literary and archival work using mythic, somatic, machine-facing, and ordinary-repair registers to stage the same threshold problem in symbolic form. The Codex is not presented as doctrine, protocol, scripture, technical specification, or literal cosmology, but as a formal and literary pressure-test of the same problem: how judgment can be displaced before the subject, room, institution, or system recognizes that displacement. -/- Release and DOI information: -/- This v17.3.7 release separates the Concept Passport Atlas from the Diptych body.
