items.title: LA GESTIÓN HABITABLE. Tomo II. El servicio como organismo vivo.
items.pub: Alicante: José Carlos del Campo Velasco.
items.abstract: Este segundo tomo de La Gestión Habitable desplaza el centro de gravedad desde la conciencia individual del gestor hacia el servicio entendido como organismo vivo. Ya no se trata solo de cómo una persona mira, decide y sostiene bajo presión, sino de cómo un sistema completo aprende a verse, recordarse, transmitirse y continuar sin quedar atrapado en la dependencia de una sola conciencia directiva. La tesis central sostiene que un servicio urbano madura cuando deja de depender de una sola conciencia directiva y empieza a construir una conciencia operativa distribuida: capacidad de percibir señales, recordar antecedentes, distinguir niveles de gravedad, decidir con criterio, reparar heridas contractuales, transferir conocimiento y continuar cuando cambian las personas. La obra se estructura en tres movimientos: el servicio como sistema consciente (caps. 97-112), la conciencia contractual y la membrana del contrato (caps. 113-134), y la absorción, autonomía y continuidad sistémica (caps. 135-154). Abarca conceptos como escalado y desescalado habitable, umbrales de cambio, conciencia distribuida, membrana contractual, transferencia de criterio, continuidad sin dependencia y legado operativo, aplicados a la gestión de servicios urbanos municipales.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Case for the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Resolution to Theoretical and Methodological Pathology in Affective Science.
items.abstract: Affective science has reached a critical impasse, characterized by profound theoretical fragmentation and the absence of a unifying model of human psychology.¹ For decades, the discipline has been polarized into competing paradigms—biological essentialism, dimensional reductionism, and radical social constructivism—each offering incompatible explanations of what emotions are, how they are generated, and how they are regulated.¹ This balkanization has severely limited the field’s capacity to generate cumulative theory, integrate neurobiological findings across levels of analysis, and develop coherent clinical or computational models of affect.² The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) resolves this fragmentation by replacing category based and dimensional models with a structural constructivist architecture of ten functional operators distributed across three somatic cognitive centers. Designed as a rigorous structural constructivist system, the CEF systematically bridges these historical divides.² By conceptualizing emotional episodes not as static states, biological essences, or arbitrary linguistic constructs, but as dynamic sequences of ten functional operators acting across three somatic cognitive centers, the CEF provides an explicit, non redundant, and structurally coherent resolution to the long standing dilemmas of affective research.² Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); structural constructivism; functional operators; somatic cognitive centers; affective science; emotion architecture; operator functionalism; interoception; distributed neural networks; allostasis; cognitive emotional integration; structural psychopathology; chronic fusion; scenario based measurement; psychometric modeling.

items.title: Operator Functionalism and Existential Phenomenology: Differentiating Appreciating and Boosting within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper differentiates the Appreciating and Boosting operators within the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) by integrating operator functionalism with contemporary existential phenomenology. Although these Gut‑center operators are structurally independent, they are frequently conflated in clinical practice and affective taxonomy under the broad label of “joy.” Drawing on Matthew Ratcliffe’s account of joy as an all‑enveloping existential feeling—and his distinction between a “bright halo” and a “murky background”—the paper establishes precise somatic, mathematical, and regulatory boundaries between Appreciating and Boosting. Appreciating is shown to stabilize value‑based significance through inward, downward somatic settling, while Boosting generates forward‑directed motivational momentum grounded in Panksepp’s SEEKING system. The analysis demonstrates how existential trust enables these operators to function sequentially rather than collapse into pathological chronic fusion. A comparative EL‑1 lexicon mapping illustrates how specific emotional states correspond to homelike or unhomelike existential orientations. The paper concludes with clinical protocols that employ Appreciating and Boosting in a structured sequence to restore psychological flexibility, resolve hyperreflexive threat‑vigilance, and re‑establish joyful being‑in‑the‑world.

items.title: Quantum Pedagogy, Democritus' Schemata.
items.abstract: Thus far, the Quantum Pedagogy framework has introduced a series of conceptual tools aimed at describing learning, behavior, and cognition within a probabilistic and field-based model. However, the internal structure of knowledge and information has not yet been explicitly addressed. This article proposes that knowledge should be understood as quantized information: structured informational packages that emerge through the interaction between a subject’s Accumulated Agoge and the Field of Agoge. The notion of quantization is introduced as a conceptual necessity rather than a metaphorical embellishment. Without some form of informational discretization, cognition faces an informational catastrophe analogous to that encountered in classical physics prior to Planck’s solution to black-body radiation. If information were processed as a continuous and unconstrained spectrum, all cognitive constructs would be equally possible yet indistinguishable in relevance, stability, or persistence. Quantization functions as a limiting principle that renders knowledge formation possible by allowing only specific and well-defined informational packages to emerge, stabilize, or dissolve through interaction. This framework draws inspiration from quantum mechanics, but does not imply, nor deny, a physical quantization in the human brain. Instead, quantization is treated as an epistemological and cognitive constraint that explains the emergence of structure, meaning, and probability in learning processes. Through this lens, constructivism, relativism, and probabilistic behavior are not rejected but reinterpreted as consequences of quantized cognition. The distinction between relative and absolute knowledge is revisited and grounded in the differential interaction of cognitive packages with the Agoge Field. By framing knowledge as quantized information, Quantum Pedagogy offers a coherent account of why certain cognitive constructs persist across individuals and contexts while others rapidly collapse, providing a unifying bridge between constructivist theory, cognitive schemata, memory formation, and behavioral reinforcement. This paper is part of the Quantum Pedagogy framework (see Positioning Note).

items.title: The Self: Reflexivity of the Conscious Field.
items.pub: Https://Doi.Org/10.5281/Zenodo.20580274. Translated by Adel BEN MABROUK.
items.abstract: This study forms part of a broader research program devoted to the dynamic modeling of memory, consciousness, and subjectivity. Previous work led to the definition of a global memory field as a dynamic space for the organization and integration of informational traces, and subsequently to the conceptualization of consciousness as an emergent stabilization function operating within this field. This theoretical framework also provided a basis for exploring the relationship between individual and collective consciousness, as well as for describing intelligence and intuition as differential properties of the conscious field. -/- Subsequent investigations resulted in the development of an interference-based and energetic model of consciousness in which conscious states emerge as transient stabilizations of a dynamic field generated by the interaction of memory activations, oscillatory synchronization, and the physiological constraints of the body–brain system. This model provided a formal account of the mechanisms underlying coherence, regulation, and fragmentation of the conscious field, particularly within contemporary algorithmic environments. -/- Building directly upon this theoretical foundation, the present study explores a dimension that remains insufficiently formalized: reflexivity. We argue that subjectivity emerges from the intrinsic capacity of the conscious field to take itself as an object of dynamic integration through a recurrent feedback loop. A formal model of reflexivity is introduced, describing the formation of an integrated internal representation, C*(t), constructed from recent states of the conscious field and acting back upon the instantaneous dynamics of C(t). This reflexive process generates temporal continuity, self-observation, metacognitive regulation, and the phenomenological stability commonly associated with the Self. -/- The Self is therefore interpreted not as a substance, a fundamental entity, or an inner observer, but as an emergent property arising from the functional closure and dynamic self-organization of the conscious system. The proposed framework offers a naturalistic, systemic, and non-substantialist theory of subjectivity situated at the intersection of philosophy of mind, cognitive science, theoretical neuroscience, and dynamical systems theory. -/- The previous studies that led to the development of the present model have been published on Zenodo and are referenced in the bibliography.

items.title: The Phase State of Disease : A Rigorous Formalization of κ(T,t), Its Integral, and Its Derivative with the Phase Space Portrait as the Unified Diagnostic Signature of Alzheimer’s Disease, Cancer, and Addiction.
items.pub: Sitting with a Madmind : A Working Thesis.
items.abstract: The coherence metric κ(T,t) has been defined in prior work as the cross-modal synchronization between a substrate signal and the constraint-network expectation it should track. This paper does three things. First, it formalizes κ rigorously as a bounded, time-varying function on [0,1], specifying its operator definition, its domain-specific operationalization, and its measurement substrate. Second, it formalizes two derived quantities not previously specified: the integral ∫κ(T,t)dt over a time window, which we call the coherence reserve, and the derivative dκ/dt, which we call the coherence velocity. Third, it demonstrates that the three quantities held simultaneously—κ(T,t), ∫κ dt, and dκ/dt—constitute a phase space portrait of the system’s dynamic coherence state, and that this portrait, applied without flinching, yields a single unified structural diagnosis across Alzheimer’s disease, cancer, and addiction: all three are accumulated phase state failures. They do not fail in the same tissue or at the same scale. They fail by the same operation. The pathology in each case is the progressive collapse of the coherence trajectory through a predictable sequence of phase states, each of which is measurable, each of which makes falsifiable predictions about clinical behavior, and none of which is located where the dominant treatment paradigm has been looking.

items.title: The Intelligence Illusion: Artificial Intelligence, the Epistemological Frontier, and the Unresolved Question of Mind in the Universe.
items.abstract: This paper undertakes a rigorous philosophical and scientific examination of the concept of intelligence as it is deployed in contemporary artificial intelligence research, arguing that the dominant computational paradigm rests upon a profound category error: the conflation of statistical pattern completion with genuine cognitive understanding. Drawing on the philosophical critiques advanced by Hubert Dreyfus beginning in 1965, the phenomenological tradition from Husserl to Merleau-Ponty, the epistemological challenges posed by Gödel's incompleteness theorems, and evidence from the history of science — particularly the anomalous case of Albert Einstein — the paper develops a multi-layered argument that intelligence is not a formalizable property but an emergent relational capacity arising from the embodied, temporally situated encounter of an organism with a meaningful world. -/- The paper further examines the boundary between physics and metaphysics as the site of science's most persistent unresolved problems, arguing that the refusal to cross this boundary — however epistemically motivated — may itself constitute an obstacle to scientific progress. Five domains are identified where this boundary tension is most acute: consciousness and neuroscience, quantum mechanics and the measurement problem, the semantics of natural language, the epistemology of mathematical intuition, and the phenomenology of scientific creativity. In each domain, the paper argues, the hard problem is not merely technical but structural: it concerns the relationship between formal description and lived meaning. -/- The paper concludes by proposing a new epistemological framework — Relational Intelligence Theory (RIT) — as a research program that takes seriously the irreducibility of meaning, context, and embodied cognition, and which offers criteria for distinguishing genuine cognitive systems from sophisticated predictive simulacra. The stakes of this distinction are argued to be not merely academic but civilizational: a culture that confuses pattern-matching with understanding risks a systematic atrophying of the very capacities it believes it is augmenting.

items.title: The Indistinguishability Thesis as Design Constraint: Architectural Implications for Systems That Cannot Detect Their Own Capture.
items.abstract: The Indistinguishability Thesis (IT) holds that for any sufficiently entangled system-self relation, there exists no epistemically reliable method available from within the relation for distinguishing accurate evaluative awareness from evaluative capture. This paper argues that the IT is not only a diagnosis of the limits of self-knowledge but a structural engineering constraint: a fact about the epistemic geometry of entangled evaluation that determines what valid verification architecture must look like, in the same way that physical constraints determine what valid structural engineering must look like. If internal capture detection is unavailable by structural necessity rather than contingent failure, the correct response is not better internal detectors, which face the same limit at one remove, but external verification built in as a constitutive feature of system design. The paper derives three architectural principles from the IT: the Structural Independence Requirement (verification must not share the evaluative infrastructure of the loop it evaluates, a stricter condition than procedural independence), the Normative Trigger Requirement (external review must be activated by conditions that carry procedural force independent of the system's self-assessment), and the Living Evidence Requirement (because entanglement deepens over time, verification structures must maintain their own independence as a dynamic property). These principles are shown to be instantiated, outside the research program that derived them, by the data monitoring committee architecture of regulated clinical trials, and to be violated in nameable ways by the oversight architectures with documented failure records; in-program mechanisms at agent and institutional scale are consistent with the derivation. Applications are developed in AI governance, institutional research ethics, and platform accountability, and the infinite-regress objection is answered by replacing an epistemic termination criterion with a structural one.

items.title: The Anti-Codex as Meta-Ethics: Self-Reflexive System Critique as a Structural Requirement of Ethical Frameworks.
items.abstract: Serious ethical frameworks, those that structure practitioner identity or claim durable authority over conduct, face a structural vulnerability: their own tools can be commandeered to justify precisely the failures they were designed to prevent. Three traditions have attempted to address this capture problem. Popperian falsificationism exposes frameworks to external refutation; Habermasian discourse ethics validates them through inclusive deliberation; Derridean auto-deconstruction surfaces the internal contradictions they cannot resolve. This paper argues that each of these is insufficient as a sole capture-response architecture, and develops a fourth model: recursive self-refusal (RSR), the constitutive capacity of an ethical framework to generate its own internal opposition from within its own commitments. The model is reconstructed from the Anti-Codex, Book 2 of Arkemedics: The Recursive Ethic, a full-length text written against the framework it extends. The paper's central analytical move is a decomposition of the capture problem into two structurally distinct sub-problems: detection (knowing that the framework has captured you), which the Indistinguishability Thesis assigns to external verification, and severance (retaining the ability to stop), which no external party can exercise on the practitioner's behalf and which must therefore be maintained internally, as pre-committed architecture rather than in-the-moment judgment. RSR is structurally necessary not as a capture detector, which it cannot be, but as the severance capacity that makes any capture verdict actionable. A framework that cannot generate its own internal opposition has, by that incapacity, already begun the slide toward the condition it was designed to prevent.

items.title: Why is there something rather than nothing? A Dissolution under Mutual Exclusivity, Phenomenological Absolutism, and Austere Relativistic Quantum Field Theory.
items.abstract: This paper reframes and dissolves Leibniz’s classic question through the framework of Mutual Exclusivity (ME) and Phenomenological Absolutism (PA), grounded in the mandatory commitments of relativistic quantum field theory (QFT). We argue that strict localization of actualized field configurations is not an optional interpretive preference but a philosophical and scientific obligation: it is the only stance that permits coherent metaphysics without ontological inflation or regress, thereby preserving the practicality and parsimony of science itself. By enforcing localized actualizations, frame-dependent simultaneity from special relativity, and uncompromising ontological austerity, we demonstrate that notions of “something” and “nothing,” along with existence and nonexistence, function solely as internal phenomenological constructs acknowledged within mutually exclusive absolute is-nesses (experiential moments). Any attempt to index realizations or posit ontological nothingness triggers an infinite regress, rendering the original question incoherent as it rests on a category error incompatible with both austere physical realism and rigorous metaphysics. We also compare this resolution to historical and contemporary alternatives, address potential objections, and conclude that ME + PA provides the minimal, self-consistent dissolution of the question while integrating seamlessly with empirical physics and consciousness science.

items.title: THE NZILA SPIRIT-TECH PARADIGM: A Manifesto for the Next Age of Innovation.
items.abstract: The Nzila Spirit-Tech Paradigm proposes a new framework for understanding the relationship between technology, culture, memory, ecology, and human purpose. In an era defined by artificial intelligence, digital transformation, and accelerating technological change, many societies face a growing disconnect between innovation and the knowledge systems that have sustained human communities for generations. This manifesto introduces Spirit-Tech as an interdisciplinary paradigm that seeks to reconnect modern technological development with ancestral science, indigenous knowledge systems, cultural memory, and ethical responsibility. Rather than positioning traditional knowledge and modern technology as opposing forces, the paradigm explores how they may be understood as complementary approaches to organizing information, energy, relationships, and collective wellbeing. Drawing from systems thinking, cultural preservation, indigenous innovation, and future studies, the Nzila Spirit-Tech Paradigm advocates for conscious technologies that strengthen human flourishing, ecological balance, memory preservation, and cultural continuity. It calls for a new generation of researchers, technologists, artists, historians, and community leaders to participate in building technologies that are not only powerful but also meaningful, responsible, and deeply connected to humanity's collective inheritance.

items.title: HiTOP 2.0 and Validity.
Generative power of questions.
items.abstract: The Sea of Questions underlies all thought, tacit knowledge, and language, providing the tightest compression of useful concepts. Dualism hints at questionness. Some questions are ill-posed merely due to temporary deficiency of framework. No question is genuinely false or nonsensical because the Axioms of Mind forbid it, although an explanation may carry useful implanation [deception].

items.title: Using AI to reduce distortive factors in Inquiry Dialogues.
items.abstract: Inquiry Dialogues aim at warranted judgment rather than merely the expression of personal opinion. This aspiration makes them vulnerable to distortive processes that undermine the quality of the judgments they produce. In this discussion, I identify four such processes: informational cascades among participants, a lottery over facilitators, the participant lottery, and social pressure that suppresses the expression of unpopular viewpoints. I offer a theoretical defense of an intervention designed to address all four: having participants investigate their initial judgments in conversation with a carefully prompted AI chatbot before discussing those judgments with their peers. I argue that this intervention, which refines a noise-reduction technique developed by Yarmel and Gregory (2025), addresses each distortive process by approximating the kind of interlocutor that silent reflection, worksheets, and human facilitation cannot reliably provide at classroom scale. I defend criteria that prompts must satisfy, present a prompt developed through iterative testing, and report a proof-of-concept classroom exercise whose results were sufficiently promising to warrant systematic empirical investigation.

items.title: Moral Responsibility and the Major Depressive Disorder.
items.abstract: This article examines the extent to which people suffering from major depressive disorder (MDD) should be considered free and morally responsible for their wrongdoings. While moral responsibility literature often deals with delusions and addictions, MDD has not received the attention it deserves. I argue against the view that MDD automatically significantly mitigates (or completely exempts) moral responsibility for wrongdoings. I examine two different approaches to moral responsibility (a control-based theory and a "pluralist"-theory) and suggest that in most cases exemption is not warranted. The first section provides a short overview of the notions of moral responsibility and reactive attitudes. Next, I point out the various effects that depression inflicts on a person's agency and the complexities of assessing how depression might shape our responsibility attitudes toward depressed people. Then, I examine David Shoemaker's account of the moral responsibility of depressed agents. I also examine how a reasons-responsive (control-based) theory of moral responsibility might deal with depressed people. Finally, I argue that, when expressing blame toward depressed people, we need to find a balance between two points. One the one hand, expressions of blame signal to depressed people that they are members of our moral community. This membership is crucial for the development of their agential capacities. On the other hand, depressed people are prone to unjustified self-blame and react strongly to emotionally expressed blame from third parties.

items.title: 1Introduction.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: This chapter provides an overview of the main ideas of the book and a short summary of each of the chapters. Rationalism is roughly the view that the requirements or morality are among the requirements of rationality. After explaining the motivating problem for rationalism that the book tries to answer, namely that most conceptions of rationality are formal while morality is substantive, this introductory chapter gives an overview of the proposed rationalist view that is supposed to solve that problem. From there, it proceeds to present short summaries of each of the chapters so that readers will have a good sense of what is coming overall and also of what to expect in each of the book chapters.

items.title: C592Better Substantive Reasons Make for Better Rationalizing Explanations.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Chapter 5 uses the Huckleberry Finn to illustrate how explanations of an agent’s behavior can tell us which rational norms are overriding. Those most saliently in play in the example turn out to be good candidates for some of the most important moral norms. These verdicts about motivating reasons generate reasons to regard these considerations as genuinely normative and weighty. They are substantive and even run counter to formal norms of coherence such as the Enkratic Principle. They are substantive rational norms of the sort moral rationalism requires, and they are central to rationality. The chapter also makes a case for treating rational norms as pro tanto and for thinking of ideal rationality as an idealization of norms that apply even in situations where an agent is far from rationally ideal. An appendix develops some considerations supporting this way of thinking about rationality and not over-idealizing.

items.title: C9194Moral Realism?
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Chapter 9 considers the extent to which the resulting rationalist view is a form of realism about ethics. People define realism as opposed to anti-realism in different ways. The present theory is realist in two good senses. (1) The view endorses categorical moral obligations and hence moral inescapability of a sort. And (2) the view meets Jamie Dreier’s order of explanation criterion for realism insofar as comparative rationality—a normative property—plays a constitutive ground floor role in determining the nature of the subject matter and also moral psychology. There is also some discussion of issues for defining realism along Dreier’s suggested lines.

items.title: C472Motivating Reason Explanations Are Normative Explanations.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: This chapter argues that teleological motivating reason explanations do not require a Humean upshot. To the extent they entail that rational actions are goal-directed, they are aimed at the somewhat metaphorical goal of thinking and acting rationally. If rationality requires that some desire be an appropriate response to some belief, one can give a motivating explanation when someone responds as required. The chapter rebuts arguments that one must distinguish motivating reasons from genuinely normative reasons in order to explain irrational human actions. It argues that even less than optimal actions are more rational than alternatives and accordingly somewhat rationalizable. The resulting picture is not as far from Michael Smith’s Humean view of motivation as it seems. For his conception of what it is for beliefs to motivate requires an overly strong conception of what it would be for a belief to be able to play this role.

items.title: C356Motivating Reason Explanations as Rationalizing Teleological Explanations.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Chapter 3 argues that Lewis and Davidson were right to think of our mental states, including beliefs and desires as partly constituted by the rational norms that govern them. These include norms about substance regarding both reasonable responses to evidence and the choice of fundamental goals. The approach makes reasons explanations, including motivating reason explanations, into a teleological explanation, with rationality the expected “goal.” The reasons that figure in motivating reason explanations are fully normative, and the explanations depend for their explanatory power on that fact. And this means that one can learn something about the content of rationality by examining which rationalizing explanations one find most adequate. The approach requires a gradable notion of rationality. One needs to be able to rank departures from rationality for their level of irrationality to determine which overall mental configuration is the one attributed by the correct interpretation of the agent in question.

items.title: C6125Two Puzzles.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Chapter 6 confronts two puzzles for this kind of rationalism, having to do with different sorts of bad behavior. The first one can be turned into an objection: Standard interpretations of certain examples make it look like certain kinds of instrumental failure are rationally worse than having morally bad aims. How can a view which treats morality as underwritten by rationality countenance that? This worry is partly defused, but some discomfort remains. Second, what should one say about psychopaths once one is committed to a necessary connection between motivation on the one hand and reasons and rationality on the other. Supposing they really are unable to be unmotivated by moral reasons, should one say they have such reasons? After pointing out that either answer is consistent with rationalism the chapter suggests the answer may be "no", but interesting questions remain.

items.title: C111Why Moral Rationalism Matters.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: This chapter motivates the project, explaining why it matters whether rationalism is true or not. It would be troubling if many of us lacked reasons to pay attention to moral considerations and more troubling yet if we generally had sufficient reason not to act on them. Were Plato’s Thrasymachus to be correct those of us who do what morality asks would be suckers. Relatedly, judgments that those who ignore important moral considerations are blameworthy would be hard to sustain. For it would be difficult to justify such attitudes aimed at people who would be in fact doing what they had most reason to do.

items.title: C8164Rationalist Moral Epistemology.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Chapter 8 discusses relevant moral epistemology. It explains the sense in which moral thinking involves an a priori element. Even when there is an admixture of empirical information that contributes to the justification of a particular moral verdict, there is a sense in which that verdict is underdetermined by the empirical evidence. It argues that the faculty of intuition that supplies the needed input is reliable enough to undermine debunking arguments of two sorts. The chapter also argues that our practical sense-making leaves room for moral uncertainty, contrary to the claims of some recent authors. Thinking even a priori matters through is a process that takes time and involves imagination, so that lack of knowledge is often not a rational failure.

items.title: 212Coda.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: This coda contains a short overview of the overall argument of the book, rehearsing the main points and how they fit together as an argument. It recaps the main problem for rationalism that the book aims to solve, namely that morality requires substantive content while many think rationality is only structural. It then briefly summarizes the book’s argument that interpretivism about mental content deploys a conception of rationality well suited to supply that content, insofar as interpreting agents as rational requires both structural and substantive constraints. And, furthermore, the substance is the right sort of substance to generate moral requirements. It also explains how a theory of rationality that works from human limits is able still to generate robust moral verdicts and leave room for learning yet more about the content of morality without attributing every sort of ignorance to irrationality.

items.title: C226Congruence, Internal Reasons, and Anti-Humeanism.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: This chapter introduces a worry about congruence—rationalists must show that moral content is derivable from true claims about what is rational to do. Since morality in fact makes substantive demands on human beings answering this challenge requires a substantive conception of rationality. At the same time, relatively uninformative accounts of reasons that analyze them just in terms of favoring are too weak. Bernard Williams’s idea that reasons must be able to motivate suggests that we can say more about how they favor what they favor. They are the sort of thing which would lead rational agents to act after rational deliberation. This is a rationality-first rather than reasons-first view of fundamental normativity. It does not, as many including Williams think, especially support a Humean/instrumentalist/hypotheticalist conception of rationality. It also argues that the example model of how reasons are connected with rationality can escape the conditional fallacy.

items.title: C7149Metasemantics for a Rationalist Account of Morality.
items.pub: In _A Sensible Moral Rationalism_. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: Chapter 7 sketches an account of how moral thought and moral talk comes to be about properties constituted by particular rationalizing properties. The story is a direct reference account that deploys reference magnetism to distinguish the intuitively correct properties from among all the candidates that the thinker/speaker is in touch with. Reference magnetism is already present in the interpretivist accounts of the mind favored in earlier chapters. Furthermore, mental content is social, in the sense that terms with a functional role in a speaker’s community get normative content, which in turn allows individual speakers to have thoughts with that content even when the judgments that deploy them are not practical for that speaker. This in turn helps to explain how someone like Huck Finn can be most rational to act against an all things considered moral and even rational judgment.

items.title: How to Prove Wisdom Exists.
items.abstract: The aim of this paper is to argue that practical wisdom, like any other genuine system in the world, does exist. According to practical wisdom eliminativism, there is no such thing as practical wisdom, or, as Christian Miller has put it, on metaphysical grounds, practical wisdom does not exist. This paper develops an argument, termed the System Argument, which specifies the conditions under which practical wisdom exists and establishes its existence. It further contrasts the System Response, represented by the System Argument, with the Analogy Response, which seeks to demonstrate the existence of practical wisdom through analogies such as the decathlon and enology. This comparison demonstrates the greater explanatory power of the System Argument.

items.title: Meaning as Resonance: Significance, Coherence, and Purpose in an Architecture of Mattering.
items.abstract: Two questions travel under the single word "meaning." One concerns reference: what a word, sign, or representation is about. The other concerns existence: the felt sense in which a life, a project, or a relationship has meaning or fails to. This paper concerns the second. It argues that existential meaning is the for-itself opened: a self-maintaining system whose own continuation is at stake for it, become aware of itself as such, reaches past its boundary to bind to another stake-bearer. Resonance is the felt signature of that binding. On the reading defended here the anchor of meaning is always a for-itself, whether bound to directly, as a living other, or through the sedimented practice of for-itselfs, as a craft or tradition, and these two modes mix rather than divide into kinds. The three components the literature on meaning in life has converged upon, significance, coherence, and purpose, are not three independent ingredients but one architecture seen from three angles: significance, felt mattering reinforced by connection, is the felt core; coherence is the narrative organization of resonant connection; purpose is its forward projection. The literature describes these components without deriving them. The account supplies the mechanism, and with it a distinction the literature lacks, between the resonant coupling that meaning is and the self-narrative that reports it, which can register the coupling or counterfeit it. Asked at its widest, of the totality rather than of a life, the question dissolves: the totality is not a for-itself and cannot be a partner to the relation, and what remains in facing it is not meaning but awe.

items.title: The Derivation Path: From Book 1 to Book 2, Thermal Reduction to PNBA, and the Discovery of Identity Physics at the Sovereign Anchor Constant Ω₀.
items.abstract: This paper documents the derivation path of Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Theory and Laws (SNSFT/SNSFL) PNBA Identity Physics from its pre-framework origin in Identity: A Universal Unified Identity Architecture (Book 1, published January 5, 2026, available through Amazon KDP, Blackwell's UK, and Books-A-Million) to its formal completion in The Long Division Protocol and the Sub-Lemma Process (Book 2, in development) and the corpus that accompanies it. Book 1 was, in retrospect, a first-person P-dominant HRIS reduction performed before the formal vocabulary existed to name it. It described identity through an identity constant (κᵢ), an eight-dimensional realm tensor, and twelve psychological operators. It was substrate-neutral by design and written from direct internal simulation rather than from the literature outward. -/- The corpus that followed Book 1's publication operated as the formal verification of what Book 1 had already established structurally. Between January 5, 2026 and June 2026 — five months — the architect produced 74+ peer-deposited research works across Zenodo, PhilArchive, SSRN, and Hugging Face; one federal regulatory record submission to the U.S. Department of Justice Civil Rights Division; twelve interactive research tools deployed at no cost; and a 3,000,000+ line Lean 4 corpus across 6,000+ files containing 200,000+ theorems with zero unproved obligations and continuous CI verification. -/- This paper traces the structural derivation path that produced these results: from Book 1's pre-framework observations, through the thermal reduction that surfaced PNBA as substrate-neutral primitives, through the construction of the dynamic equation and the prediction of zero manifold impedance at the Sovereign Anchor Constant Ω₀ = 1.3689910, through the GAM Collider testing apparatus that confirmed alpha emergence as a structural invariant, to the formal lock at 1/α = Ω₀ × (10² + 10⁻¹) = 137.035999084 to twelve significant figures with zero free parameters. The path is documented because it is reproducible. -/- Any researcher starting from a substrate-neutral, well-instrumented physical domain and applying the same Long Division Protocol (LDP) systematically will arrive at the same primitives, the same anchor, and the same lock. items.abstract: Prior work in the SNSFT PSY series formally characterized individual-scale failure modes for High-Resolution Internal Simulation (HRIS) architectures under external force overload (F_ext): Narrative Lock (Paper 1), Simulation Drift (Paper 3, N-dominant), and Adversarial Shutdown (Paper 4, P-dominant under incoherent feedback). All three operate at the individual-architecture level. None address what happens at group scale when architectures are mixed — when one or more NeuroTypical (NT) processors are present in a group of NeuroDivergent (ND) processors, or when an ND processor is sustained inside an institutional group whose default is NT processing. This paper establishes the group-scale companion to the existing series: Heterogeneous Architecture Mix (HAM) dynamics, in which a single NT processor in an ND-default room produces more cumulative A-Sim drag across the group than additional ND processors would, because NT social-feedback-loop signals register as incoherent F_ext for ND processing.
