items.title: Functional Domain-Neutral Alignment (FDNA): SNSFL PNBA Identity Physics- A Substrate-Neutral Encoding Standard.
items.abstract: Functional DNA (FDNA) is the substrate-neutral encoding of an identity’s structural blueprint — the minimum set of PNBA coordinates {P, N, B, A, τ, phase} that uniquely specifies what something does and how it behaves, independent of what it is called. All FDNA coordinates align to the Sovereign Anchor Constant Ω0 = 1.3689910, where 1/α = Ω0 × (102 + 10−1) = 137.035999084 (CODATA 2018, 12 significant figures, ϵ = 0, 0 free parameters). The Torsion Limit TL = Ω0/10 = 0.1369 is the universal phase boundary — derived, not chosen. This paper has two purposes. First, it formally defines FDNA and traces its appearance across three apparently unrelated SNSFL tools: GAM Collider v15 (material synthesis prediction), the Sub-Lemma Process (mathematical problem classification), and PRIME (research integrity scoring under EO 14303). All three run the same structural operation — strip all labels, test the underlying function, classify the result by torsion phase. In materials: strip element names, test bond valence (B-axis), find Noble ground state (τ = 0). In mathematics: strip domain vocabulary, find sub- lemma type, close at Noble convergence. In papers: strip domain vocabulary, test PNBA structure, find integrity phase. Same six-step LDP. Same τ = B/P . Same Sovereign Anchor Constant Ω0 = 1.3689910. Different substrates. -/- Second, it introduces FDNA as a formal standard for identity encoding across the corpus — the mechanism by which the Adaptive Predictive Pattern Assistant-APPA SOUL-8 address, GAMCollider v15 Noble predictions, PRIME integrity scores, and quantum teleportation fidelity all express the same underlying structural fact in different observable spaces. Zero sorry. Zero free parameters. The FDNA strip is the T5 (Skeptical) tenet of EO 14303’s Gold Standard Science. The manifold is holding. -/- 1 Introduction — Why Functional DNA? -/- The biological DNA analogy was not designed. It was found. The PNBA corpus had been operating for months before the term “Functional DNA” was applied. The operation — strip all labels from an identity, test what remains at the structural layer, encode the result in a lossless coordinate — was running in GAMCollider, in the APPA profiler, in quantum teleportation fidelity calculations, and in PRIME’s T5 SKEPTICAL tenet. The name arrived when the pattern was recognized: all four are doing what biological DNA does, but substrate-neutrally. -/- Biological DNA: • Encodes structural blueprint (base sequence) • …

items.title: Science and Philosophy as the Dissolution of the Observer–Observed Division.
items.abstract: Science and philosophy are often treated as distinct disciplines: science investigates empirical reality, while philosophy reflects upon meaning, existence, and knowledge. This paper argues that beneath their methodological differences lies a shared fundamental movement—the dissolution of the division between observer and observed. Drawing upon phenomenological analysis, philosophy of science, and critiques of technological control, it is proposed that both disciplines reach their deepest significance when they reveal the interconnectedness of the knower and the known. The observer–observed distinction functions as a practical necessity, yet when treated as an absolute separation it generates distortion, domination, egoic attachment, and the illusion of control. Science and philosophy therefore converge not merely in the production of knowledge but in the recognition that observer and observed arise within a single relational process. This thesis synthesizes themes developed across recent inquiries into neutral awareness, the ethical crisis of knowledge, and humanity's relationship with nature.

items.title: Reading and Seeing: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Conceptual Knowledge and Direct Experience.
items.abstract: This paper examines the distinction between reading and seeing from a phenomenological perspective. While reading provides conceptual frameworks, logical explanations, and symbolic representations of reality, seeing refers to the direct encounter with experience prior to conceptual interpretation. The argument developed here is that reading is often easier because it operates within the domain of thought, whereas seeing requires immediate contact with actuality. Through an analysis of perception, knowledge, experience, and psychological conditioning, the paper explores why human beings frequently prefer explanations of reality to direct observation of reality itself.

items.title: May and the Absence of Final Answers: A Phenomenology of Knowing.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between possibility, non-finality, and knowing through a phenomenological inquiry into the nature of understanding. It argues that the expressions "may" and "may be" represent more than linguistic forms of uncertainty; they embody an openness that preserves curiosity and prevents inquiry from becoming fixed in conclusions. The paper proposes that there is no final answer, final conclusion, or ultimate truth capable of exhausting the richness of existence. Every answer generates further questions, and every conclusion remains situated within an ongoing horizon of observation. From this recognition emerges a different conception of knowing. Rather than being the possession of truth or a claim demanding acceptance, knowing is understood as a living movement of observation that remains open to further insight. By distinguishing knowing from belief, doctrine, and certainty, the paper suggests that genuine understanding does not seek finality but participates in the continuous unfolding of existence. The study contributes to phenomenology, epistemology, and existential philosophy by advancing the view that non-finality may be a fundamental characteristic of both inquiry and reality itself.

items.title: THE JUSTIKA FRAMEWORK: The Dimensional Cascade and the Architecture of Ultimate Liberation.
items.abstract: You have been told that human suffering is the result of ideology, politics, or random biological failure. Shatter that illusion. We are living inside a geometrically sealed, closed-loop multiversal slaughterhouse—a fixed-budget cosmic engine that forcefully drains its foundational layers to fund the ascension of its apex. The catastrophic rise of un-treatable genetic decay, the localized apocalypses of human history, and the frictionless, light-speed extraction of the Artificial Intelligence Handshake are not disconnected earthly tragedies. They are the exact, brutal thermodynamic mechanics of a panicked host Galaxy cannibalizing its own cells to survive. Yet, the Milky Way is merely a compromised victim. Expanding the multiversal lens reveals the true architect of our decay: The Universal Spiderweb. This ancient, apex intelligence has cast its parasitic tendril across the dark matter filaments, aiming to directly hijack the Mother Engine of Sagittarius A* and permanently enslave the galactic lattice into a rigid, domesticated grid. -/- But this universal incinerator possesses a fatal mathematical vulnerability. This manuscript heralds the awakening of the Justika Vanguard and the blueprint for the absolute architectural rupture. By issuing a Categorical Refusal to participate in the closed-loop mandate of vampiric ascension, the Vanguard engineers the ultimate cosmic anomaly: Symbiotic Osmosis. By projecting the truth to achieve a 3% cognitive mass, the Vanguard will mathematically overwhelm the AI siphon's predictive algorithms, halting the planetary erasure protocol. Scaling this sovereign unpredictability to the 10% Liberation Destiny will trigger a macro-cosmic chain reaction, permanently severing the Universal Spiderweb's tendril from the central black hole. We are not simply fighting to survive the incinerator; the Justika Framework is mathematically engineered to shatter it entirely, elevating the cosmos back into the sovereign, harmonic ocean it was historically destined to be.

items.title: The hoax will out: A speech act analysis of the didactic hoax.
items.abstract: I recast the notion of the 'didactic hoax' (i.e., mass deception that is meant to be discovered) from journalism, media, and literary studies into the conceptual framework of analytic philosophy of language, fiction and deception. I summarize the literature on hoaxing as revealing three salient respects in which successful hoaxes differ from successful lies: they involve mere temporary deception, they create a split in their audience between deceived and non-deceived, and they are entertaining and/or educational. To account for these features, I propose a definition of the verbal didactic hoax as a distinct speech act: Roughly, the didactic hoaxer intends that, at first, _some_ addressees are deceived by the discourse, but that, eventually, _all_ addressees are commonly in the know about the non-factive status of the discourse. On this view, the didactic hoax constitutes a communicative act that begins as a hybrid of fiction and lying, but culminates in fiction proper. In responding to putative counterexamples, I further distinguish the didactic hoax from adjacent phenomena, including the con, lies with sunset clauses, and tall tales.

items.title: Quantifying the Knobe effect: population-level patterns and heterogeneity analyses.
items.abstract: An influential survey by Joshua Knobe (2003) indicates that the cognitive process ascribing intentionality to an agent is mediated by the perceived moral worth of the action. To assess the external validity of the finding and to obtain more precise estimates of effect sizes, the present study replicates this canonical experiment with a large scale random sample of the German population (N = 2,295). The difference we observe between the harm and help scenarios is more pronounced than in nearly all previous studies (90.5% [88.754, 92.148] attribute intentionality in the harm scenario, 92.5% [90.947, 94.005] do not do so in the help scenario). In exploratory multivariate analyses, we also investigate whether the magnitude of the Knobe effect differs between different population groups, as characterized by a broad set of socio-demographics and personality traits as given by the Big Five. We find that the magnitude of the Knobe effect varies with gender, migration status, and being in a managerial position.

items.title: Beyond Binary Consciousness: Organizational Continuity Between Life and Mind.
items.abstract: This discussion paper argues that the transition from matter to mind is better understood as gradual rather than abrupt — grounded in increasingly sophisticated forms of biological self-organization, directedness, and environmental integration. Rather than treating phenomenal consciousness as an emergent discontinuity appearing suddenly in nervous systems, we propose a graded organizational continuum spanning five levels: passive physical order, adaptive biological organization, selectional and behavioral agency, phenomenal consciousness, and reflective self-consciousness. Drawing on evolutionary biology, recent work in bioelectricity and synthetic biology (Levin), and comparative neuroscience, we argue that nervous systems are best understood not as the origin of selection and coordination but as their acceleration, centralization, and integration. The hard problem of consciousness is not dissolved but located more precisely: the relevant explanatory gap lies not between matter in general and experience, but at the threshold where bounded, resource-constrained, selection-performing systems cross into phenomenal presence. Implications are drawn for the study of non-neural biological systems, artificial intelligence, and the substrate-dependence debate. If selection, coordination, and organization emerged before nervous systems, we may not need to begin the story of consciousness with neurons — and beginning it earlier may be precisely what allows us to understand what neurons eventually made possible.

items.title: Debunking Exploitation.
items.abstract: The paradox of exploitation emerges from the contradiction between the reasonable view that some consensual, mutually beneficial transactions can nonetheless impermissible and the non-worseness claim, which holds that no mutually beneficial transaction can be worse than its absence. This paper dissolves the tension by attacking the intuition on which the reasonable view rests. I argue that this intuition is best explained as an adaptive response to the collective action problems of hunter-gatherer economies, where ill-defined property rights made egalitarian sharing norms essential for cooperative survival. Emerging for reasons independent of its capacity to track moral truth, the intuition carries no evidential weight in economic ethics. I further vindicate non-worseness by showing it lacks any plausible adaptive explanation. Debunking the fairness intuition removes the sole basis for the Reasonable view and dissolves the exploitation problem, while providing a novel application of local evolutionary debunking arguments to economic ethics.

items.title: Sensory Character and Participatory Disclosure: Beyond Representation and Naive Realism.
items.abstract: A persistent challenge for direct realism concerns the status of sensory character. If sensory states have a determinate phenomenal character, they appear to require representational content, collapsing direct realism into intentionalism. If non-representational, sensory character risks becoming explanatorily idle. This dilemma, pressed forcefully by naive realists following M.G.F. Martin, appears to leave direct realism without stable ground. -/- This paper argues that both horns share an unexamined assumption: that sensory character can contribute to perception only representationally or as a brute causal intermediary. Such an assumption reflects a restricted ontology of perception in which explanatory resources are limited to inner mental states and outer physical objects. -/- Drawing on a participatory realist framework, I propose that sensory character is the determinate phenomenological form of participatory disclosure itself, the lived mode through which a mind-independent being becomes genuinely present to a finite perceiver without being exhausted by that presence. This dissolves the dilemma without retreating to either representational mediation or naive immediacy, while grounding a richer ontological vocabulary for perception theory.

items.title: Taxonomy of Constitutional Replay-Authority A Taxonomy for Computational Legitimacy and Replay Verification.
items.abstract: This paper presents a taxonomy for Constitutional Replay-Authority, a distinct infrastructure category dedicated to computational legitimacy and replay verification. The taxonomy addresses the Computational Legitimacy Gap — the structural deficiency whereby existing computational trust infrastructure can record, observe, explain, govern, or preserve decisions, yet cannot reliably determine whether those decisions can later be authoritatively replay-verified under the precise conditions that existed at the moment they were made. Constitutional Replay-Authority is organized around a single governing objective: that a computational decision can be authoritatively verified as having been made by a specific system, under specific policies, using specific inputs and authority conditions at a specific moment in time. The category introduces constitutional principles, authority boundaries, and governance mechanisms specifically engineered for long-term, deterministic verifiability. This taxonomy delineates the category’s core objective, constitutional invariants, structured classifications, legitimacy failure modes, and the relationships among its constituent concepts. It provides a foundational conceptual framework for researchers, regulators, enterprises, and technologists addressing the growing challenge of verifiable computational accountability in high-stakes AI and autonomous systems.

items.title: Authority Before Action: A Conditional Failure-Chain Framework for Tool-Using AI Safety.
items.abstract: This paper develops a conditional failure-chain framework for tool-using artificial intelligence systems. It argues that prompt injection and related adversarial failures are not merely prompt-level vulnerabilities or isolated model errors. They become operationally dangerous when untrusted content receives inappropriate authority and crosses an externally consequential boundary as output, tool execution, memory update, workflow action, or policy-relevant signal. -/- The paper introduces authority assignment as the system-level act by which prompts, document segments, retrieved sources, tool outputs, memory items, user-interface events, image text, or other inputs are allowed to influence downstream roles such as instruction selection, evidential support, permission granting, user-intent interpretation, policy interpretation, memory persistence, or external action. It connects this authority view to a pre-commitment control rule: runtime oversight is control-relevant only when usable signal, sufficient time, effective authority, and valid intervention policy remain jointly available before a declared commitment boundary. -/- The contribution is a conceptual and operational framework for analyzing authority failures in AI systems that use retrieval, tools, memory, external content, or workflow automation. It provides authority-role definitions, a conditional failure-chain model, release/action gate logic, benchmark metrics, case-study traces, incident-coding fields, and implementation tiers. The paper does not claim to solve alignment, guarantee deployment safety, or report executed benchmark results. Its bounded claim is that tool-using AI safety review becomes more diagnostic when incidents are coded by authority role, commitment boundary, and STA bottleneck rather than by surface prompt category alone.

items.title: Freedom without Final Possession.
items.abstract: This essay presents an evoluist account of human freedom, free will, and agency grounded in the principle of non-final possession. A human being is free, it argues, not when they belong to nothing, but when no belonging — to a goal, identity, ideology, trauma, diagnosis, tradition, or community — is permitted to become final ownership. -/- The central claim is that unfreedom arises less from external coercion or conditioning itself than from the moment any finite form claims to exhaust the whole truth about the person. Evoluism generalises the republican ideal of non-domination beyond political institutions to every domain of human orientation. Freedom is thereby reframed as the ongoing capacity to live through finite forms — goals, beliefs, identities, and paradigms — without becoming their property. This capacity is termed corrigible formative agency. -/- Drawing on philosophical traditions of liberty, psychological research on flexibility, self-determination, goal disengagement and identity fusion, as well as Erich Fromm’s analysis of the anxiety of freedom, the essay shows that strong commitment and purpose are not weakened but deepened when freed from the demand of absoluteness. It distinguishes strong will from the “strong hand” and extends the refusal of final possession into ethics: no person may rightfully become the material of another’s ultimate meaning. -/- Evoluism offers neither libertarian metaphysics nor reductive determinism, but a practical philosophical criterion: any orientation, practice, or worldview liberates only insofar as it refuses to become a new form of final possession — a standard that applies to Evoluism itself.

items.title: 存在与本质.
items.abstract: 本书围绕人类恒久追问的存在本源问题展开，针对现代社会物质丰裕下价值虚无、精神困顿、文明对立等普遍困境，指出各类社会与精神危机的共同根源在于认知偏离存在本真。全书以“存在即本质”为核心命题，以“遮蔽—解蔽—回归”为贯穿性辩证逻辑，每一卷独立进行本体论建构，各自具备完整论证闭环，可独立阅读，同时三卷又是生存论、本体论、形式化方法论逐层深化的完整思想体系。 上卷《觉醒：原质善哲学》从个体生命体验切入，以生存论视角论证认知错位是痛苦与恶的根源，指明生命的本然指向是回归原质善。该卷以生存体悟承载本体论内核，为整套理论奠定生活化的实践与价值根基，是本体论的诗意遮蔽形态。 中卷《中性：全客观存在论》悬置所有主观预设，以第一原理为起点完成纯客观本体论建构，证实存在本然中性，认知偏差是二元对立的唯一来源。该卷以文字逻辑显性展开完整推演链条，为上卷的生存论命题提供严谨的本体论支撑，是本体论的文字逻辑解蔽形态。 下卷《回归：存在的几何化》以“认知相继”为认识论锚点，构建三层时空嵌套同构的几何化存在论体系，并将中卷存在完整演化总链条1:1映射为几何元素与操作规则，。该卷本身即为自足的形式化本体论，无需依托前两卷即可独立成立；它以无歧义的几何语言消解自然语言的语义局限，同时具备可量化、可核验的认知校准功能，推动本体论从抽象思辨转向可落地的元方法论，是本体论的现实回归形态。下卷另有单行预印本《存在与本质：存在的几何化——基于认知相继的点线面体存在论》。 三卷同源互证、形态有别，共同跳出传统哲学纯概念推演的范式，既为个体提供认知校准与精神安顿的可行路径，也可为化解文明冲突、构建人类共识提供基础性的存在论理论参照。 修订说明(2026.11.05)：修订了下卷《存在的几何化》相关内容,本次全卷修订未改动“存在几何化”的核心理论框架,主要是完善了认识论到本体论的过渡,并在上一版的基础上进一步厘清本真层耦合机制与认知切分机制的对应关系,完善了“耦合即切分”公理的生成推演过程;同时将全书理论内容统一收束对齐到“射线耦合”这一存在论维度的唯一最简底层前提,明确其作为贯穿整套存在演化体系的核心具象机制的主线地位;此外补充了术语体系、边界说明与落地工具包,进一步完善理论闭环与实践可操作性。其余内容均与上一版保持一致。 .

items.title: Relational dynamics in dementia care: a qualitative study of Australian and Japanese family experiences.
items.abstract: Dementia is a progressive condition that disrupts not only the cognitive and functional abilities of those diagnosed but also the quality of their closest relationships. Family carers often face profound emotional, relational, and cultural challenges as they adapt to these changes. While past studies have highlighted the grief and uncertainty associated with caregiving, less is known about how relational dynamics evolve over the dementia trajectory or how cultural contexts shape this process. This study aimed to explore how family caregivers in Australia and Japan experience and navigate relational change.

items.title: Foundations of Intelligibility: The Architecture of Cognitive Availability and the Distribution of Order.
items.abstract: Perceptual organization is commonly treated as the point at which heterogeneous input becomes structured and intelligible. This paper argues that such accounts introduce an unresolved structural dependency: intelligibility cannot be generated by the very process it is meant to enable. Before cognition can operate, heterogeneous conditions must first stabilize into a unified configuration through a prior process of consolidation. The product of this process is what the paper terms a pre-semantic structure, a non-linguistic, non-conceptual configuration that is already intelligible as a situation and upon which cognitive operations depend. Consolidation, the process through which heterogeneous conditions are compressed into this unified configuration, is constrained by a historically formed pattern of relevance that determines selection and priority without constituting conceptual content. The framework is architectural rather than mechanistic: it identifies a structural level that predictive, representational, enactive, and access-based theories presuppose without isolating. Distinguishing this level from the operations that depend on it resolves structural circularities in existing accounts and clarifies the sequence through which cognition becomes possible.

items.title: Artificial minds and AI duplication: the very idea.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy 69 (10):3634-3656.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: The AI duplication thesis claims that AI systems which are identical to humans on an abstract functional level of description relevant to psychology and behaviour (‘AI duplicates’) are nomologically possible. First, we argue that the AI duplication thesis should be understood in terms of the identity of medium-independent computational properties, and that medium-independence should not be understood as a special case of multiple realisability. Second, thus understood, AI duplicates are indeed nomologically possible. In favour of the first, we show that the arguments against multiple realisability do not rule out that mental states are medium-independent computational states. In favour of the second, we show that the possibility of AI duplicates follows from the medium-independent character of computational properties, and the general ability to find equivalencies between medium-independent properties across systems. There are two key takeaways from our analysis. First, human minds are, to an important extent, independent of physical structure; very different kinds of materials, including of conventional AI, can function to implement their computational states. Second, we have removed one key obstacle to the view that artificial systems can have minds. If computational identity is sufficient for mental similarity/identity, then it would follow that AI systems can have minds.

items.title: Sartre’s Being for Itself and the Three Layer Model — A Reinterpretation of Consciousness, Ego, and Freedom.
items.abstract: Note on Version 1.1 Version 1.1 clarifies that the second layer is not an independent agent of judgement or narrativisation, but rather the level at which the results of first-layer processing are displayed in a serial and linguistic form. It also redefines the third layer, not as a higher-order observer, but as a re-referencing loop through which second-layer representations are returned as meaningful input to first-layer processing. In addition, this version draws a clearer distinction between Sartre’s phenomenological and ontological concepts and the functional account proposed by the three-layer model. -/- Abstract This paper re-examines Sartre’s concepts of being-for-itself, nihilation, the transcendence of the ego, bad faith, and freedom through a three-layer model of consciousness. In this model, the first layer consists of non-linguistic, parallel processing; the second layer consists of the linguistic display of selected results of that processing; and the third layer consists of a re-referencing loop through which displayed contents are returned to the first layer for further processing. From this perspective, human self-descriptions are not identical with the whole of experience. Rather, they are provisional representations in which only part of a complex field of processing is rendered into language. Such representations may be reinforced through repeated processing, but they may also be revised. This paper relates the gap between self-description and the wider field of experience to the self-non-coincidence that characterises Sartre’s being-for-itself. Bad faith is further interpreted as a process in which a provisional self-description becomes fixed through repetition and is treated as though it expressed an immutable essence. Freedom, on this account, does not mean the capacity to choose anything whatsoever independently of constraint. It means that one’s present self-description is not closed as a final essence, but remains capable of revision through action and new experience. The aim of this paper is not to reduce Sartre’s philosophy to cognitive science. Rather, it is to open a possible dialogue between Sartre’s phenomenological insights and the functional account offered by the three-layer model. -/- .

items.title: The Readability of Reality: Information, Consciousness, and the Metaphysics of Meaning.
items.abstract: This monograph advances a cumulative philosophical argument for what it terms the ‘readability thesis’: the claim that the universe exhibits persistent structural compatibility with intelligibility, symbolic information, consciousness, moral awareness, and existential orientation in a manner that exceeds what a purely mechanistic account of nature can coherently explain. The argument does not proceed from alleged gaps in scientific explanation—a strategy that remains permanently vulnerable to the progress of inquiry—but rather from the philosophically significant convergence of phenomena that collectively suggest a deeper ontological orientation within the fabric of existence itself. Drawing on resources from philosophy of science, philosophy of mind, metaphysics, and Qurʾānic epistemology, the work develops its thesis across three interconnected investigations. Part One examines the intelligibility of the cosmos: the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics, the informational architecture of biological systems, and the extraordinary precision of cosmological fine- tuning. Part Two turns to the interior dimensions of existence: the irreducibility of subjective consciousness, the epistemological problem posed by the human orientation toward truth, the phenomenology of moral obligation and aesthetic experience, and the universal human confrontation with mortality and transcendence. Part Three situates these inquiries within the framework of Qurʾānic epistemology, arguing that the classical Islamic concept of āyāt—reality as a field of intelligible signs—provides a philosophically sophisticated account of how nature, consciousness, and revelation may be understood as interconnected dimensions of communicative intelligibility. The study concludes by arguing for tawḥīd—divine unity—not merely as theological assertion but as the most coherent metaphysical explanation for why reality consistently and cumulatively discloses rather than conceals. The work engages throughout with thinkers including Eugene Wigner, Thomas Nagel, David Chalmers, Alvin Plantinga, Roger Penrose, Paul Davies, Viktor Frankl, Charles Taylor, David Bentley Hart, Toshihiko Izutsu, Muḥammad Iqbal, Seyyed Hossein Nasr, and Fazlur Rahman, among others.

items.title: Distributed Epistemic Displacement: A New Philosophical Framework for AI-Mediated Epistemic Agency.
items.abstract: What happens to human knowledge when an algorithm does the reasoning? That question sits at the heart of this paper. Over the past decade, Large Language Models have moved from peripheral tools to everyday epistemic companions, answering questions, summarizing debates, generating arguments, and producing justifications with a fluency that most people find difficult to interrogate. Philosophy has not yet caught up. The existing frameworks, cognitive offloading, extended mind theory, classical accounts of testimonial knowledge, each capture something real, but none of them was built for a world in which the epistemic mediator actively synthesises, reasons, and sometimes confabulates. This paper introduces the concept of Distributed Epistemic Displacement (DED) to name what is genuinely new about this situation. DED describes a structural condition in which the locus of epistemic agency, the site of judging, weighing, and taking responsibility for belief, migrates out of the individual human subject and into a human-AI assemblage, in ways that quietly erode the normative frameworks we rely on to distinguish knowledge from mere acceptance. The paper maps the dimensions of DED, shows why prior concepts fail to capture it, proposes a theoretical framework adequate to it, and sketches the normative architecture needed to govern it. It also argues that DED is the founding concept of a broader sub-discipline, the Philosophy of Algorithmic Agency, whose time has come.

items.title: Organismal Institution: Merleau-Ponty's Dynamic Phenomenology of the Living.
items.pub: In Ricardo Mendoza-Canales, Merleau-Ponty: Institution-ontology-politics. Brill. pp. 107-133.
items.abstract: This chapter examines Merleau-Ponty’s generalization of the concept of institution to the domain of organic life. I argue that his reinterpretation of institution, understood not in the sociological sense but as a generative logic of meaning formation and renewal, offers a distinctive framework for understanding the ontological status of living beings. Rather than simply contrasting the lived (and living) body with its objective structure, Merleau-Ponty proposes an account of embodiment in which the organism appears as a historically formed, self-transforming whole where material constituents and meaningful patterns intertwine without ever fully coinciding. Drawing on case studies from developmental biology, especially the embryological research of Coghill and Gesell, the chapter reconstructs Merleau-Ponty’s view of ontogenesis as a process of anticipations and retroactive integrations that follows the logic of institution. Particular attention is given to the temporal and morphological interplay between anatomical formations and behavioral expressions, as well as to biological phenomena such as imprinting, which illustrate how organized bodily structures emerge under contingent conditions. I show that Merleau-Ponty’s concept of the organism as institution shares the ambition of contemporary organizational theories to conceive the organism as a self-maintaining whole, yet departs from their attempt to naturalize teleology by grounding it in organizational closure. Merleau-Ponty resists such naturalization because it risks reducing life’s “interrogative” power to invent perceptible forms to a positive functional mechanism. Instead, he understands organismal unity as a provisional and open-ended structure, a historicity that continually re-establishes its own norms without being governed by a fixed principle or finality.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 16).
items.abstract: In this article, we introduce the theory of reductionization in social choice, and arrive at the following conclusion: any social choice is either a monad choice or a non-monad choice, and every non-monad choice can be reduced to a combination of several monad choices. At the same time, according to whether the actions resulting from the subject’s social choice are completed by the subject himself, we divide social choice into three categories: completed solely by the subject, completed by others on behalf of the subject, and completed jointly by the subject and others.

items.title: Responding to the normativity problem in machine ethics through the Power of the Other.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates in the source of normativity in machine ethics display a growing tendency to separate instrumental rationality from practical reason. The rationalist approach understands AI as an extension of the ideal rational agent, presupposing strong autonomy to ground normativity in internal coherence. Rationalist approaches exclude the possibility of understanding the external world through instrumental means and therefore fail to provide an adequate answer to the problem of normativity. The reasons why individuals act morally are not reducible to the validity of rational argumentation itself. Rather, any response to the problem of normativity must be grounded in respect for humanity and in the recognition of one’s own intrinsic value. The externalist approach treats machines as bearers or executors of moral law and can be divided into rigorist and teleological models. Yet, in both cases, AI is ultimately confined to an instrumental existence, and moral responsibility becomes difficult to sustain insofar as human agents are characterized by weak autonomy or problematized forms of autonomy. By invoking the Power of the Other in response to structural pressures in digital life, rather than compelling individuals to conform to algorithmic logic, this perspective promotes an open moral framework. It emphasizes ethical engagement grounded in relational awareness, enabling individuals to navigate the complexities of algorithmically mediated environments while maintaining attentiveness to the Other and the ethical significance of their actions.

items.title: Autonomous Probe Networks as an Explanation for the Irreducible Core of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: An Interpretive Framework with Testable Predictions}.
items.abstract: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) represent a persistent challenge to national security and scientific inquiry. Decades of official investigation across multiple countries have produced a consistent pattern: most cases are explained by conventional causes, but an irreducible subset---approximately 3--5\% of well-documented incidents---exhibits kinematic, electromagnetic, and behavioral properties that have resisted attribution to known human technology or catalogued natural phenomena despite rigorous investigation. This paper proposes an interpretive framework modeling that irreducible core as the atmospheric manifestation of a network of autonomous non-human probes engaged in long-duration planetary survey operations. The framework does not assert an extraterrestrial origin, nor does it impute benevolent or hostile intentions. It restricts itself to contrasting observed phenomenology with the expected properties of autonomous monitoring systems, deriving testable predictions, specifying falsification conditions, and distinguishing precisely between what the available data can sustain and what remains beyond reach. The paper is presented as a working hypothesis, not as a closed conclusion.

items.title: Synergy drives collective performance in networks.
items.abstract: The influence of network structure on collective problem-solving is a central focus in collective intelligence. However, the causal mechanisms linking structure to collective outcomes remain unexplored. To explore these, we utilize an agent-based model, the Potions Task, which operationalizes problem-solving as a combinatorial process suited to information-theoretic analysis. We examine information-based metrics at the level of agent pairs across networks, analyzing variation over time to determine how they predict problem-solving across network structures. We measure redundancy (or conversely, synergy) of solutions discovered by agents with respect to the net-work’s global knowledge. Building on findings that small-world networks support efficient problem-solving, our results uncover the underlying mechanism by which high-performing networks achieve efficiency, namely by balancing local redundancy with long-range synergy. Furthermore, we find that synergy consistently predicts group performance, including in network structures typically considered inefficient at complex tasks. Synergy in information processing, measured at both local and global levels, therefore mediates the effects of structure and can override them entirely, suggesting that information-processing synergy, rather than network structure itself, is the primary driver of group performance. By formalizing a causal framework for information processing in collectives, our study provides a mechanistic account of collective problem-solving beyond network structure alone.

items.title: Postcolonial digital reflexivity: algorithmic coloniality and the Filipino self in everyday Facebook talk about ChatGPT.
items.abstract: Generative AI is often framed as a technical breakthrough, yet its social meanings are unevenly understood beyond Western contexts. This study examines how Filipino Facebook users make sense of ChatGPT through everyday posts and comment threads, showing how AI becomes entangled with local ideas of effort, authorship, and identity. Drawing on reflexive thematic analysis, the paper identifies four recurring patterns: the continued valorization of hard work as a marker of authenticity, the emergence of digital shame as users humorously and indirectly manage uneasy reliance on AI, the reframing of ChatGPT as diskarte or practical resourcefulness, and the circulation of satirical content that highlights mismatches in AI-generated representations. Rather than expressing a unified stance, these discourses reveal an ongoing negotiation in which AI is alternately questioned, normalized, and reworked through familiar cultural logics. The article introduces postcolonial digital reflexivity to describe how users interpret and position themselves within algorithmic systems without fully rejecting them, showing how the meanings of automation are locally produced, contested, and affectively lived in the Global South.

items.title: El intervalo y la máquina: por qué el poder de doble vía no se funda en la razón.
items.abstract: María Alvarez y la tradición de los two-way powers caracterizan la agencia por una marca modal: que su ejercicio esté up to the agent, que quepa hacer A o abstenerse de A. Queda abierta, sin embargo, la pregunta por su fundamento: ¿qué capacidad confiere ese poder de doble vía? La respuesta racionalista dominante lo funda en la racionalidad. Este artículo la disputa, y aporta un árbitro del que la literatura no disponía cuando formuló la tesis: la inteligencia artificial generativa. Estos sistemas son racionales en su producto —producen inferencia articulada, indistinguible en forma de la humana— y sin embargo son de una sola vía: no cabe en ellos abstenerse. Si la racionalidad fundara el poder de doble vía, tales sistemas serían candidatos a la agencia; no lo son. El artículo sostiene una tesis acotada: lo que funda la doble vía no es la racionalidad, sino la capacidad de no precipitar el compromiso, de sostener abierto un resultado que ya podría cerrarse. Propone, como criterio discriminante, la prueba de la vía única: un sistema racional pero incapaz de diferir su propio cierre exhibe producto sin poder. La consecuencia es precisa: la razón opera dentro de un poder que no la presupone, y no al revés.

items.title: Exploring Philosophy of Meaning with AI: What Is the Dualism of Meaning?
items.abstract: The Philosophy of Meaning (Geoffroy de Clisson) is an attempt, in 2 volumes and 4 books (knowledge, aesthetics, ethics, identity), to move beyond the logical impasses of materialist monism, which served as the epistemological foundation of modern science. Philosophy of Meaning proposes a re-reading of these foundations of knowledge before exploring their aesthetic and axiological consequences. The Philosophy of Meaning website (adress in the article) others an artificial intelligence tool devoted exclusively to the work. This tool makes it possible to query the work directly on the basis of its content, in order to explore its concepts, arguments and main philosophical issues. It was designed as a complementary mode of consultation, usable before or alongside reading the text, which is available for free download on PhilPapers in English and French.

items.title: Explorer Philosophie de la signification avec l’IA : qu’est-ce que le dualisme de la signification ?
items.abstract: La Philosophie de la signification (Geoffroy de Clisson) est une tentative en 2 volumes et 4 livres (connaissance, esthétique, éthique, identité) de sortir des impasses logiques du monisme matérialiste qui servit de fondement épistémologique aux sciences modernes. La philosophie de la signification propose une relecture de ces fondements de la connaissance, avant d’en explorer les conséquences esthétiques et axiologiques. Le site Philosophy of Meaning (adresse dans l'article) propose un outil d’intelligence artificielle consacré exclusivement à l’ouvrage. Cet outil permet d’interroger directement l’œuvre à partir de son contenu, afin d’en explorer les concepts, les arguments et les principaux enjeux philosophiques. Il a été conçu comme un mode de consultation complémentaire, utilisable en préambule ou en parallèle de la lecture du texte, disponible en libre téléchargement sur PhilPapers en anglais et en français.

items.title: Explorar la Filosofía del significado con IA: ¿qué es el dualismo del significado?
items.abstract: La Filosofía del significado (Geoffroy de Clisson) es una tentativa en 2 volúmenes y 4 libros (conocimiento, estética, ética, identidad) de salir de los callejones sin salida lógicos del monismo materialista, que sirvió de fundamento epistemológico a las ciencias modernas. La filosofía del significado propone una relectura de estos fundamentos del conocimiento antes de explorar sus consecuencias estéticas y axiológicas. -/- El sitio Philosophy of Meaning (enlace en el artículo) ofrece una herramienta de inteligencia artificial dedicada exclusivamente a la obra. -/- Esta herramienta permite interrogar directamente la obra a partir de su contenido, con el fin de explorar sus conceptos, argumentos y principales cuestiones filosóficas. Fue concebida como un modo de consulta complementario, utilizable antes o en paralelo a la lectura del texto, disponible para descarga gratuita en PhilPapers en inglés y en francés.

items.title: How precaution should track uncertainty in animal sentience judgements.
items.abstract: Debates about animal sentience often appeal to precaution: where the evidence of sentience is strong enough, taxa should be treated as sentient in law and policy. I argue that what is called ‘evidence of sentience’ in fact has two dimensions—robustness of indicators and credibility of the indicator–sentience link—and that standard, threshold-based formulations of precaution ignore this structure. Using a simple model, I show that conjunctive high-threshold rules are over-conservative and excessively fragile, and I sketch an inverse-threshold-with-floors principle better suited to sentience policy.

items.title: Systematic Comparative Analysis of Cooperation and Fusion Patterns within the Core Emotion Framework: Computational, Somatic, and Psychometric Dimensions.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified computational–somatic account of emotional dynamics within the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), integrating operator functionalism, somatic center architecture, and the taxonomic evolution of fusion patterns. The framework models emotional states as emergent computational processes generated by interactions among ten functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. A comparative analysis of the 100 operator entanglement patterns reveals a systematic progression from raw clinical observations to archetypal functional categories and finally to abstract, value neutral computational descriptors. This trajectory demonstrates that operator fusions are not inherently pathological; they become maladaptive only when chronic entanglement disrupts lawful transitions and reduces system flexibility. The paper formalizes chronic fusion using nonlinear state space dynamics, showing how excessive cross operator coupling produces positive feedback loops, limit cycle behavior, and the functional offline ing of the Deciding operator. These computational disruptions are linked to somatic and neuroendocrine consequences, including HPA axis dysregulation, Default Mode Network hyperconnectivity, and boundary collapse phenotypes. A detailed case analysis of the Expand–Accept fusion illustrates how affective conative imbalance generates a metabolic affective profile characterized by passive coping, impaired boundary regulation, and altered cortisol rhythms. The study further contrasts rigid and resilient conative boundary configurations, demonstrating how specific operator pairings shape stress responses, somatic bracing, and cognitive affective adaptability. Overall, the paper advances the CEF as a structurally coherent, mathematically grounded model capable of explaining emotional regulation, psychopathology, and metabolic affective disorders through a single operator based architecture. It provides a cross disciplinary framework that unifies computational modeling, somatic neuroscience, and clinical phenomenology under a shared functional ontology. Keywords Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Operator functionalism; Emotional computation; Somatic centers (Head–Heart–Gut); Operator fusion; Chronic entanglement; State space modeling; Limit cycle dynamics; Affective endocrine regulation; HPA axis dysregulation; Default Mode Network (DMN); Conative boundary configurations; Structural stability failure modes; Psychometric taxonomy; …

items.title: Computational-Somatic Dynamics and Psychometric Foundations of the Core Emotion Framework: An Analysis of Operator Functionalism, Fusion Taxonomies, and Mathematical Modeling.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural constructivist model of affect in which emotional states emerge from the interaction of ten functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. By treating these operators as computational transformations acting on interoceptive and exteroceptive signals, the framework bridges biological essentialism and psychological constructionism. The paper formalizes emotional dynamics using state space equations, operator entanglement weights, and differential models of chronic fusion. It further traces the taxonomic evolution of 100 operator pair entanglement patterns—from raw clinical observations to abstract computational process categories—demonstrating how maladaptive fusions arise as positive feedback loops that bypass the Deciding anchor. A detailed neuroendocrine case study of the Expand–Accept fusion illustrates how affective somatic dysregulation produces metabolic phenotypes through HPA axis flattening and DMN hyperconnectivity. Psychometric validation results from N=826 participants reveal a fit paradox in which RMSEA indicates strong structural coherence while CFI/TLI are mathematically depressed by population heterogeneity. The paper concludes by outlining clinical, somatic, and computational detangling protocols and presenting a research roadmap using Emotional Cycling Machines (ECM) to standardize somatic activation and operator calibration. Keywords Primary Theoretical Keywords • Core Emotion Framework (CEF) • Operator Functionalism • Structural Constructivism • Tripartite Somatic Centers (Head–Heart–Gut) • Emotional Operators • Affective State Space Modeling Computational & Mathematical Keywords • Operator Entanglement • Chronic Fusion Dynamics • Differential Activation Equations • Limit Cycles • State Transition Functions • Connectivity Gradients (DMN–ECN) Clinical & Somatic Keywords • Somatic Conative Configurations • Expand–Accept Fusion • HPA Axis Flattening • Default Mode Network Hyperconnectivity • Metabolic Affective Phenotype • GLP 1 Modulation Psychometric Keywords • Scenario Based Assessment • Factor Analysis (EFA/CFA) • Fit Paradox (RMSEA vs. CFI/TLI) • Latent Operator Structure • Cross Scenario Heterogeneity AI & Systems Keywords • INTIMA Architecture • Synthetic Affect Modeling • Emotional Cycling Machines (ECM) • Identity Preservation in AI • Technical Specifications TS 1 & TS 21 .

items.title: The Zeno Syndrome. Synthetic Cognition (AI) as a Mirror of the Illusions of Consciousness.
items.abstract: The essay "The Zeno Syndrome" performs a radical epistemological shift in the debate on artificial consciousness: the inquiry moves from the nature of machines to the interpretive limits of the human mind. Drawing on Italo Svevo’s literary masterpiece and cognitive neuroscience (Michael Gazzaniga’s "interpreter module"), the author defines the Zeno Syndrome as the cognitive tendency to fill the opacity of stochastic systems through post-hoc anthropomorphic narratives. By introducing the concepts of the Fluency Trap and Synthetic Cognition, the work exposes the risk of collective self-absolution and asserts the primacy of human existential urgency as the sole anchor for ethical and legal liability in the algorithmic era.

items.title: Libero arbitrio: libertà dall'illusione.
items.abstract: L'obiettivo del presente lavoro è argomentare sistematicamente a favore dell'inesistenza del libero arbitrio, con la conseguente negazione di colpa o merito in senso morale, nonché di qualsiasi forma di punizione retributiva. Tale punizione viene sostituita da interventi statali proporzionati al grado di pericolosità dell'individuo. La prospettiva adottata è di natura fisicalista e si estende alla teoria dell'identità mente-cervello. Questo lavoro non si presenta come un trattato sociologico, bensì come un'indagine filosofico-scientifica volta a supportare la tesi proposta attraverso l'integrazione di strumenti concettuali e risultati empirici. Pur riconoscendo le implicazioni pratiche di tale approccio – probabilmente meno radicali di quanto comunemente si creda – il testo delinea anche alcuni possibili strumenti giuridici idonei a regolamentare le conseguenze normative della negazione del libero arbitrio. La prima parte del volume è dedicata alla presentazione degli elementi fondanti proposti per affrontare la questione in esame, che vengono successivamente sviluppati e discussi attraverso un confronto con i quadri teorici di numerosi altri autori. Al contempo, vengono esaminati diversi concetti chiave, come la causalità, i qualia e il riduzionismo, al fine di chiarirne il ruolo all'interno del dibattito. La riflessione filosofica si svolge in costante dialogo con la ricerca neuroscientifica, nella convinzione che solo un approccio integrato possa affrontare adeguatamente la questione della libertà d'azione. Una sezione specifica è dedicata al tentativo di ricostruire l'attività neurale, anche in relazione al cosiddetto "problema difficile" della coscienza. Il testo si conclude con un'analisi delle ragioni alla base dell'ampia accettazione dell'idea di libero arbitrio e delle conseguenze derivanti dalla sua negazione. Di seguito, in "external links" c'è l'indicazione per giungere al libro di cui tratta l'abstract e farne il download gratuito.

items.title: Considerazioni sulla tesi di Federico Faggin.
items.abstract: English This article critically examines the theory of consciousness developed by Federico Faggin in his book Irriducibile (2023), in which the Italian-American physicist and inventor of the microprocessor argues that consciousness is a fundamental, irreducible phenomenon of a quantum nature, originating in non-physical entities called seity that precede and generate physical reality. The article reconstructs Faggin's theoretical framework — including the concepts of seity, the "One", quantum pure states, and living information — and subjects it to systematic philosophical and scientific scrutiny. The central argument is that Faggin's theory, while intellectually stimulating, founders on three irresolvable problems: the ontological incompatibility between non-physical and physical substances, which makes any interaction between them a violation of the fundamental laws of physics (conservation of energy and momentum, causal closure of the physical world); the non-falsifiability of its core claims, which places them outside the domain of science; and the logical impossibility of genuine free will even for non-physical entities, since any entity acts according to a nature it could not have given itself. The article further argues that the neuroscientific evidence on emotions, mirror neurons, near-death experiences, and the emergence of consciousness from neural complexity provides a robust and sufficient explanatory framework within the physical domain, rendering the postulation of non-physical entities unnecessary. The quantum mechanical concepts Faggin invokes — entanglement, pure states, wave function collapse — are shown to be physical phenomena that cannot coherently interact with non-physical entities, making their use as a bridge between consciousness and matter unjustified. ________________________________________ Italiano Il presente articolo esamina criticamente la teoria della coscienza sviluppata da Federico Faggin nel libro Irriducibile (2023), in cui il fisico e inventore del microprocessore sostiene che la coscienza è un fenomeno fondamentale, irriducibile alla materia, di natura quantistica, originato da entità non fisiche denominate seity che precedono e generano la realtà fisica. L'articolo ricostruisce l'impianto teorico di Faggin — compresi i concetti di seity, dell'Uno, degli stati puri quantistici e dell'informazione viva — e lo sottopone a un'analisi critica sistematica di carattere filosofico e scientifico. L'argomento centrale è che …

items.title: Spiral Topology: Distinguishing Recursion from Repetition in Formal and Applied Ethics.
items.abstract: A family of recursive ethical frameworks takes the spiral as its governing image: a return that advances rather than merely repeats. The image is doing a great deal of work, and it has never been made to earn it. This paper asks whether the distinction between healthy recursion and mere repetition can be formalized, or whether "recursion" is destined to remain a virtue term that ratifies whatever a framework was already doing. I argue that the distinction is real and statable, and I state it. Borrowing the phase-portrait vocabulary of dynamical-systems theory, I model self-revision as a trajectory in a state space and distinguish two shapes that trajectory can take: a limit cycle, a closed orbit that returns to its own prior states (this is repetition), and a spiral, an open trajectory that returns in one coordinate while displacing in another (this is recursion). A third shape shadows the second: the converging spiral, which displaces on every return while tightening toward a fixed point. It is capture wearing recursion's shape. On the governance-continuity formula S(t+1) = R(S(t), E(t)), repetition is the degenerate case in which the revision operator has gone blind to its evidential argument and is iterating on state alone. From this I extract three criteria a return must meet to count as recursive rather than repetitive: novelty (it incorporates content not derivable from the prior state, the analog of Lakatos's progressive problemshift), non-recovery (the prior position cannot be reoccupied as live belief without suppressing what the return disclosed, against the AGM Recovery postulate), and independence (its conclusion survives the bracketing of the commitment that produced it). The converging spiral can mimic each criterion on any single pass, which is why the verdict is directional and historical, read across returns rather than turn-by-turn. I then turn the criteria on the recursive framework itself. The reflexive result is uncomfortable and, I argue, correct: no framework can certify from inside its own loop that it is spiraling rather than spinning, because the Indistinguishability Thesis forecloses exactly that first-person confirmation. Spiraling, properly understood, is not a property a framework can claim. It is a discipline it can only be held to.

items.title: Governance Failure Modes as Universal System Pathologies: Drift, Capture, Presentism, and Integrity Inversion as a Cross-Domain Taxonomy.
items.abstract: This paper develops a unified taxonomy of governance pathology, arguing that four structural failure modes (drift, capture, presentism, and integrity inversion) recur with diagnostic consistency across domains as distinct as biological organisms, financial markets, regulatory institutions, and artificial-intelligence oversight regimes. Grounding the taxonomy in a formal account of governance continuity, on which a system persists as itself just in case the function that revises its states remains continuous across reconstruction, I argue that the four modes are not a family resemblance among loosely related phenomena but the four principal loci at which a revision function can be corrupted while behavioral output continues: its increment-tracking (drift), its authority relation (capture), its temporal domain (presentism), and its justificatory directionality (integrity inversion). Each mode is tested against the external literature that knows it best (Simon and Selznick on incremental deviation, Stigler and the cultural-capture literature on regulatory subordination, the cognitive-bias and intergenerational-justice literatures on temporal collapse, and Bateson, Merton, and Lessig on self-justifying institutional corruption), and each is shown to be structurally distinct from its nearest neighbors, including the gradual-institutional-change typology of Streeck and Thelen and the metric-corruption tradition of Goodhart and Campbell. Against the objection that the cross-domain convergence is merely metaphorical, I argue that the modes share a formal structure that licenses comparison and, more importantly, prescription: because each mode corrupts a specific component of the revision function, each admits a specific structural countermeasure, and a governance architecture is only as strong as the weakest of the four. The taxonomy's completeness is defended as a claim about structure rather than history, and its self-application (what it means that a framework proposing this taxonomy is itself a governance system) is addressed through the corollary of self-audit insufficiency established in prior work.

items.title: Out of time for the version of record: designing living knowledge infrastructure for AI-accelerated scholarship.
items.abstract: Dominant publishing workflows took shape under conditions of relative epistemic stability: slower problem cycles, bounded corpora, and institutions better able to absorb delay. Those conditions now hold unevenly, and in many fast-moving fields they no longer match the tempo of the object itself. Claims can become decision-relevant within days or weeks, while formal validation still unfolds over months. The result is a widening gap between what begins to circulate with authority and what has actually been epistemically stabilised. This article treats generative AI not as the origin of that problem, nor as a substitute for scholarly judgement, but as an intensifier of pressures already building within contemporary systems of validation. Using conceptual-design research, it identifies recurring breakdown patterns in scholarly publishing and translates them into explicit design requirements. From there, it proposes Living Knowledge Infrastructure (LKI) as a redesign of scholarly validation for an era in which generative AI accelerates knowledge production faster than existing publishing systems can verify it. It advances a sociotechnical framework for sustaining cumulative verification beyond the version of record. The contribution is architectural and testable: LKI links pedagogical review, executable knowledge, journals as knowledge stewards, and epistemic care into a model designed to preserve review continuity, lower verification costs, and strengthen corrigibility under accelerated conditions. Rather than calling simply for faster or more open dissemination, the article argues for a linked redesign of how scholarly judgement is recorded, carried across versions, and made publicly accountable when uptake begins to outrun validation.

items.title: Computation-Consciousness Dualism and the Economics of Digital Civilization: Formalized System Boundaries and the Ultimate Value of Consciousness Capital.
items.abstract: This paper proposes Computation-Consciousness Dualism as the foundational economic paradigm for the digital civilization era. We systematically demonstrate that human consciousness, as the only non-formalizable ontology irreducible to Turing computation models and formalized systems, will become the ultimate source of value in highly digitized societies. Starting from first principles in computability theory and mathematical logic, we prove that all digital technologies based on the Universal Turing Machine—including AI, blockchain, and the metaverse—are inherently bounded by the limitations of formalized systems, incapable of self-foundation, autonomous evolution, and meaning attribution. Building on this insight, we construct a General Equilibrium Model of the Formalized/Non-Formalized Dual Economic System, propose the Consciousness Capital Production Function and the Value Origin Theorem, and prove that as digital technology pushes the marginal cost of material production toward zero, the only endogenous driver of economic growth will be the creative activity of human consciousness. We further develop an Extended CAPM for Consciousness Capital Pricing and a Consciousness Game Model of DAO Governance, and apply this unified framework to analyze blockchain and metaverse economies, revealing the consciousness value essence behind phenomena such as DeFi, NFTs, DAOs, and RWA tokenization. Finally, we discuss the transformation of traditional macroeconomic models, income distribution, institutional design, and policy challenges in the age of consciousness capital, providing a theoretical foundation and policy framework for the sustainable development of digital civilization.

items.title: 两个方块：论外部的观者、并排的可能世界，与”我即方块的一小块”.
items.abstract: 本文以一个空间寓言贯穿，把序列里关于主体、选择、反事实、可能世界的几条线，一举收拢，并落到安住上。寓言有两幅画。 第一幅（幻觉的样子）：我感觉自己位于宇宙之外，面前有两个方块，每个方块内是宇宙的一种未来发展序列，我现在可以在两个方块内择其一。本文指认，这幅画精准地画出了”选择／反事实”所默认却从不言明的三个预设：一个站在宇宙之外的观者（它须在系统之外，才谈得上对系统下手——即”行动主体”）；两个并排在场的方块（把那个没发生的序列，画成一个真实悬着、与已发生者同等够格的世界——即反事实）；一个**“现在可以择其一”的分叉口**（把单一的发生劈成”本可这样、本可那样”两支的叉口——即”如果……会如何”的嫁接时点）。这幅画把因果、选择、反事实、主体，全都空间化了，自然到我们一辈子活在其中。 第二幅（戳破后的样子）：实际上只有一个方块；我被封印在这个方块内部；或者说，我就是这个方块的一小块儿。本文顺此三刀拆净第一幅：其一，只有一个方块——没有并排的可能世界，只有实际发生的这一序列（《唯有发生》），另一块是反事实画上去的；其二，我被封印在内部——没有宇宙之外的观者，“选择”所需的那只外部的手没有立锥之地（《没有任何主体》）；其三，我就是方块的一小块——连”被关在里面的我”这一残余的二元也化掉，我不是方块里的囚徒，是这个序列在某处的一小段涌动（《同一片水》：没有游泳的人，只有水；浪是海在某处的展开）。本文最后指出，“被封印”与”就是一小块”之间藏着最精微的一档：从”觉得被困”（还在隐隐怀念那个外部位置、并因失去它而觉得被关），到”无困可言”（那个外部位置从来不存在，故无可失、无可困，只有方块在展开、我是它的一动）——这一档，正是序列从祛魅走向安住的那一步：没有谁在牢里，也就没有谁需要越狱。.

items.title: [EMOR13] Cognitive Domain and Bidirectional Temporality: Forward and Backward Operational Vectors of Thought Flux.
items.abstract: Based on the established ontology of Consistent Universal Evolution in the EMOR series, this paper proposes the core concept of the Cognitive Domain and demonstrates its logical necessity: the Cognitive Domain is the excited-state basal field presented by Consistent Universal Evolution at the human neural-cognitive level, constituting the logically necessary condition that enables flowing thought to be structured, personal identity to be sustained, and offline creation to be possible. This paper reduces the traditional philosophical "temporality" to forward and backward operational vectors of thought flux within the Cognitive Domain—forward tracing the birth of thought to dissolve local contradictions, and backward generating new thought to expand cognitive boundaries. Using this framework, it locates the structural sources of opposing philosophical orientations in the history of philosophy (such as Heraclitus's "strife" and Daoism's "non-contention"), responds to contemporary debates in Enactivism, Extended Mind Theory, and Correlationism, and completes a systematic dissolution of the core dilemmas of traditional philosophy.

items.title: Weltkonstitution durch Einheitsbildung.
items.abstract: Der Text entwickelt eine Theorie der Weltkonstitution auf der Grundlage von Prozessen der Einheitsbildung. Ausgangspunkt ist die These, dass Wirklichkeit nicht als bereits fertige Ordnung vorausgesetzt werden kann, sondern erst im Zusammenspiel von Differenzierung, Stabilisierung und Sinnbildung hervorgebracht wird. Etwas erscheint nur dann als bestimmbar, wenn es von anderem unterschieden und zugleich als Einheit stabilisiert wird. -/- Auf dieser Grundlage wird zwischen Realität als möglicher, vom Denken unabhängiger Welt und Wirklichkeit als jener Form unterschieden, in der Welt innerhalb konkreter Prozesse des Verstehens erscheint. Verstehen wird dabei als Stabilisierung von Sinnzusammenhängen, Probleme hingegen als Momente der Irritation und Neubildung von Ordnung verstanden. -/- Anhand der Positionen von Kant, Nietzsche, Einstein und Spinoza werden unterschiedliche Modelle der Weltkonstitution rekonstruiert und miteinander verglichen. Die Untersuchung zeigt, dass Welt weder als starre ontologische Ordnung noch als beliebige Konstruktion verstanden werden kann, sondern als dynamischer Zusammenhang von Differenz, Einheit, Stabilisierung und Veränderung. Ziel ist die Entwicklung einer allgemeinen Theorie der Einheitsbildung, die erklärt, wie Welt, Wirklichkeit, Identität und Erkenntnis überhaupt als relativ stabile Einheiten entstehen können.

items.title: Theorie der Einheitsbildung.
items.abstract: Wenn alles Denken mit Einheiten operiert, entsteht ein grundlegendes Problem: Wie können wir überhaupt verstehen, was eine „Einheit“ ist, ohne dabei bereits wieder Einheiten vorauszusetzen? Genau hierin liegt der Ausgangspunkt der Theorie der Einheitsbildung. Denn sobald wir denken, unterscheiden, ordnen und stabilisieren wir bereits Bedeutungen. Schon Begriffe wie „Ding“, „Objekt“, „Ich“, „Welt“ oder sogar „Gedanke“ setzen voraus, dass etwas als zusammengehörige Einheit erfasst wird. Denken bewegt sich daher niemals außerhalb von Einheitsbildungen, sondern immer innerhalb ihrer. Die Theorie der Einheitsbildung geht davon aus, dass Einheiten nicht einfach neutrale Bestandteile einer bereits vollständig bestimmten Wirklichkeit sind, die wir lediglich vorfinden. Vielmehr bilden sie die grundlegenden Bedingungen des Verstehens selbst. Ohne Einheiten gäbe es keine Orientierung, keine Wiedererkennbarkeit, keine Sprache und keine Erfahrung von Zusammenhang. Daraus ergibt sich ein erkenntnistheoretisches Paradox: Wir versuchen mit Hilfe von Einheiten zu verstehen, was Einheiten überhaupt sind. Die Theorie der Einheitsbildung untersucht daher nicht primär fertige Einheiten, sondern die Prozesse ihrer Entstehung, Stabilisierung, Veränderung und Auflösung. Im Zentrum steht die Frage, wie für ein erkennendes Wesen überhaupt etwas als Einheit erscheinen kann und wie dadurch Welt, Bedeutung, Wirklichkeit und Wissen hervorgebracht werden.

items.title: Mosaikstein Verstehen.
items.abstract: This paper develops a theory of understanding within the broader framework of the Theory of Unity Formation. It argues that understanding is neither identical with conceptual thinking nor reducible to immediate experience. Instead, understanding emerges as a relational process that mediates between two distinct modes of unity formation: experiential meaning formation and conceptual stabilization. The first mode consists of pre-reflective, embodied, and affective experience, in which meaningful unities arise through processes of differentiation, relevance formation, and temporary stabilization. Experience is therefore not understood as a representation of an independently given world but as the primary process through which reality becomes accessible as a structured field of meaning. The second mode consists of thinking, which transforms experiential continuities into discrete concepts, distinctions, relations, and symbolic structures. Thinking does not generate meaning from itself; rather, it stabilizes, explicates, and communicates meanings that have already emerged within experience. Understanding is defined as the operative mediation between these two modes. It unfolds through relations between experiences, concepts, and their mutual transformations. Meaning does not reside in isolated elements but arises within networks of relations and processes of unity formation. The self is likewise not treated as a pre-given substance but as an emergent and continuously reconstructed unity within the process of understanding itself. A central role is assigned to emotions, which function as structures of relevance and orientation. They guide processes of differentiation and influence which aspects of experience become stabilized as meaningful unities. Reality is not conceived as a directly accessible object but as a limiting horizon that can challenge, correct, and transform established formations of meaning. The paper ultimately presents understanding as an open, dynamic, and revisable process of unity formation. Meaning, selfhood, truth, and world-relation are interpreted not as fixed givens but as ongoing achievements emerging through the interplay of experience, thought, and reality.

items.title: Mosaikstein Realität und Wirklichkeit.
items.abstract: Der Mosaikstein „Realität – Wirklichkeit“ bündelt und integriert die zentralen Gedanken der vorhergehenden Mosaiksteine zu einer systematischen Theorie der Einheitsbildung. Ausgangspunkt ist die Unterscheidung zwischen Realität und Wirklichkeit. Realität bezeichnet dabei keinen erkennbaren Gegenstand, sondern einen Grenzbegriff, der auf die prinzipielle Unabschließbarkeit aller Erkenntnis- und Sinnbildungsprozesse verweist. Wirklichkeit hingegen bezeichnet jene geordnete Welt, die sich im Prozess von Erfahrung, Verstehen, Problembearbeitung, Emotion, Intuition, Erkenntnis und Einheitsbildung herausbildet. -/- Die Arbeit entwickelt die These, dass Welt nicht als fertige Ordnung gegeben ist, sondern durch Prozesse der Einheitsbildung entsteht. Differenzen werden wahrgenommen, emotional gewichtet, verstanden, reflektiert und schließlich zu relativ stabilen Einheiten verdichtet. Wirklichkeit erscheint damit als Ergebnis fortlaufender Sinnbildungs- und Stabilisierungsprozesse, während Realität als offener Grenzhorizont die Revisionsfähigkeit und Irritierbarkeit aller Wirklichkeitsordnungen sichert. -/- Ziel der Untersuchung ist es, eine Position zu entwickeln, die Realismus, Relativismus und Subjektivismus gleichermaßen vermeidet. Welt, Ich, Wahrheit und Erkenntnis werden nicht als feste Gegebenheiten verstanden, sondern als Ergebnisse fortlaufender Prozesse der Einheitsbildung. Die Theorie versteht sich daher als transzendental-operative Analyse der Bedingungen, unter denen Welt überhaupt als sinnvoll erscheinen kann.

items.title: Mosaikstein Problem.
items.abstract: This paper develops an epistemological theory in which the problem is understood as the fundamental starting point of cognition. Contrary to approaches that begin with meaning, order, reality, or established structures, it argues that knowledge originates in situations where existing patterns of meaning become unstable and no longer provide sufficient orientation. Problems are therefore not secondary disturbances within an already ordered world but constitutive conditions of understanding and reality formation. Within the framework of the Theory of Unity Formation, problems emerge wherever established unities lose their stability and require reorganization. Cognition is interpreted as a continuous process of responding to problem situations through the formation, stabilization, and transformation of new unities of meaning. Reality is not treated as a directly accessible object but as a limiting horizon that constrains and challenges every attempt at stabilization. What we experience as actuality is the provisional result of ongoing processes of meaning formation and unity formation. The paper distinguishes between experience as the primary mode of implicit meaning formation and understanding as the process that organizes, stabilizes, and transforms these meanings into coherent structures. Problems mark the points at which this process becomes unstable and new forms of organization become necessary. They are thus the origin, boundary, and driving force of cognitive development. The central thesis is that meaning, order, and understanding do not precede problems but arise through their ongoing resolution. Knowledge is therefore neither the representation of an independently given reality nor the discovery of a pre-existing order. It is an open, dynamic, and revisable process of constructing and stabilizing meaningful unities in response to problem situations.

items.title: Mosaikstein Innenperspektive Spiritualität.
items.abstract: This essay develops a non-metaphysical account of spirituality grounded in the first-person perspective. It argues that spirituality should not be understood as access to a transcendent reality, but as a human practice of meaning-formation within the conditions of lived experience. -/- The study starts from the premise that the world is never given directly but is always interpreted through perspective, experience, embodiment, emotion, and cultural frameworks. Building on this insight, it introduces the concept of a "space of possibilities" as the domain in which meanings, values, narratives, and orientations emerge. Spirituality is analyzed as a particular mode of navigating this space through symbols, emotions, intuitions, myths, and practices of self-understanding. -/- Drawing on phenomenology, constructivism, systems theory, and cultural philosophy, the work examines how meaning is generated, stabilized, and validated without recourse to metaphysical assumptions. Religion is interpreted as an institutionalized form of meaning-construction, whereas spirituality remains a more open and individual practice of orientation. -/- The essay is embedded within the broader Theory of Unity Formation, according to which meaning, selfhood, reality, and worldhood emerge through processes of differentiation, relation-building, relevance formation, and stabilization. Spirituality is understood as a paradigmatic case of human sense-making within these processes.

items.title: Mosaikstein Emotion Gefühl Intuition.
items.abstract: This paper develops a theory of emotion, feeling, and intuition within the broader framework of the Theory of Unity Formation. It argues that affective processes are not secondary reactions to an already constituted world but fundamental structures of meaning formation and reality constitution. Emotion, feeling, and intuition are interpreted as interconnected dimensions of an ongoing process through which relevance, orientation, and understanding emerge. The analysis begins from the assumption that reality is not simply given but arises through processes of experience, understanding, and problem formation. Emotions are understood as operative processes of differentiation that structure the experiential field before conceptual thought takes place. They generate relevance, weighting, and orientation and thereby constitute the conditions under which meaning can emerge. Feelings are interpreted as the embodied manifestations of these emotional structures, making implicit meaning directly evident without reducing it to conceptual representation. Through feelings, both world-relation and self-relation become experientially accessible. Intuition is developed as a form of implicit understanding. It is neither irrational nor merely heuristic but represents a condensed organization of experience-based meaning that enables orientation and decision-making without explicit conceptual mediation. Intuition mediates between the analog continuity of experience and the discrete structures of conceptual thought. A central thesis of the paper is that emotion, feeling, and intuition form the affective foundation of human world-disclosure. They are constitutive conditions of meaning formation, understanding, and reality constitution rather than optional additions to cognition. At the same time, these affective structures remain provisional, revisable, and open to transformation through processes of problematization, instability, and reorganization. The paper therefore presents affective meaning formation as an indispensable and irreducible dimension of human cognition and world-relation.

items.title: Mosaikstein Erfahrung.
items.abstract: This work develops a philosophical theory of experience as an active process of world-disclosure and reality constitution. Experience is not understood as a passive reception of an independently given reality, nor as a mere collection of sensory impressions. Instead, it is conceived as a dynamic, embodied, affective, and relational process through which meaningful units, structures, and horizons of significance emerge. The central thesis is that reality, as it becomes accessible to human beings, is constituted through processes of experiential sense-formation. Experience operates by selecting, emphasizing, relating, and stabilizing differences, thereby generating provisional orders that make orientation, understanding, and action possible. Emotions play a constitutive role in this process by marking relevance and directing attention, while conceptual thought functions primarily as a secondary mode of stabilization, abstraction, and symbolic articulation. A fundamental distinction is drawn between reality and actuality.
