Actuality refers to the structured and meaningful world that emerges within experience, whereas reality functions as a transcendental horizon that limits, challenges, and corrects experiential constructions without ever becoming fully accessible in itself. Human understanding therefore remains inherently perspectival, provisional, and open to revision. The work further develops a process-oriented conception of the self. The self is not treated as a fixed substance or pre-given subject but as a relational and dynamic unity emerging through ongoing processes of self-reference and world-reference. Understanding is consequently interpreted as an open-ended movement between experience and conceptualization rather than as the discovery of final truths. The study contributes to contemporary debates in phenomenology, epistemology, philosophy of mind, and process philosophy by proposing an account of experience as the primary locus in which meaning, selfhood, and world are continuously constituted.

items.title: Mosaikstein Erkennen.
items.abstract: This essay develops an epistemological approach that understands cognition not as the representation of an objective reality, but as a process of meaningful recognition. The central thesis is that knowing occurs through the recognition of coherence between experience, meaning, and understanding. -/- Against purely representational, naturalistic, or functional models of cognition, the work emphasizes the constitutive role of lived experience, affectivity, and the first-person perspective. Knowledge is understood as a dynamic process in which significance emerges through the organization and stabilization of experience. -/- Through a series of philosophical letters addressed to thinkers such as Spinoza, Metzinger, Rosa, Steiner, Gabriel, and Nussbaum, different conceptions of knowledge are reconstructed and critically examined. The study argues that truth and objectivity are not fixed entities but arise within ongoing processes of understanding and interpretation. -/- The essay forms part of the broader Theory of Unity Formation, which investigates how stable units of meaning, selfhood, worldhood, and knowledge emerge through processes of differentiation, relevance formation, and stabilization.

items.title: Mosaiksteine dritte Zusammenstellung.
items.abstract: Die vorliegende Zusammenstellung der „Mosaiksteine“ entwickelt eine Theorie der Einheitsbildung, in der Wirklichkeit nicht als fertige Ordnung verstanden wird, sondern erst in Prozessen der Differenzierung, Relevanzbildung und Stabilisierung entsteht. Erfahrung erscheint dabei als leiblich und emotional geprägter Vollzug, in dem Welt überhaupt erst als bedeutsam hervortritt. Emotionen, Gefühle und Intuitionen besitzen eine grundlegende orientierende Funktion, weil sie Relevanzen hervorbringen und Sinn bereits vor jeder begrifflichen Ordnung strukturieren. Verstehen und Denken greifen diese offenen Erfahrungsprozesse auf, ordnen sie begrifflich und machen sie als Wirklichkeitszusammenhänge stabil und mitteilbar. Erkenntnis wird deshalb nicht als unmittelbare Abbildung einer objektiven Realität verstanden, sondern als fortlaufender Prozess der Bewährung, Korrektur und Neuorganisation von Sinnordnungen unter Bedingungen von Problemhaftigkeit und Irritation. Zentral ist dabei die Unterscheidung zwischen Wirklichkeit als hervorgebrachter und stabilisierter Sinnordnung und Realität als Grenzbegriff dessen, was sich jeder vollständigen Bestimmung entzieht und dennoch als Widerstand wirksam bleibt. Insgesamt entwirft die Arbeit eine systemisch-transzendental orientierte Theorie der Wirklichkeitskonstitution, in der Welt, Selbst und Sinn erst innerhalb dynamischer Prozesse der Einheitsbildung entstehen.

items.title: The Decision No One Authored: The Answerability Gap in Generative AI.
items.abstract: Can a person retain full control of an AI-shaped decision and still fail to author it? Consider a hypothetical pension fund whose generative system guides its allocations through a decade of good returns. Officers review proposals, can override anything, and sign every trade: every outward mark of control, oversight, and authorship is present. Yet in this case, the conception of risk under which the money moves remains a vendor's default: no one at the fund ever decides what risk should mean for these beneficiaries. The decision appears authored, though the fund never made the judgment it turns on. The natural question is whether responsibility has shifted to the machine or remains secured by the humans around it. Debates over consciousness, patiency, and machine agency address the first possibility; meaningful human control and oversight address the second. Neither settles whether anyone performed that prior judgment. I call this the answerability gap. It is deepest where the system is best: reliability promotes the unowned frame into more consequential decisions and dissolves the checking that would expose it. The paper gives an account of the missing act and of the adoption that makes an inherited frame answerably one's own.

items.title: Do chatbots change how we think about sexuality? towards an empirically informed philosophy of sexuality in the age of AI‑mediated intimacy.
items.abstract: Millions of users now engage in sexual and romantic interactions with AI chatbots, from dedicated companion platforms such as Replika, Ourdream(.)ai and Character(.)AI to general-purpose large language models such as ChatGPT, whose developers have recently discussed permitting erotic content for verified adults. These developments constitute what McArthur ( 2022 ) terms second-wave sextech, in which the artefact itself becomes the focal point of sexual engagement. Contemporary philosophical debate on second-wave sexual technologies is organized around three dominant positions: instrumentalist, abolitionist feminist, and polysemic. Each is primarily concerned with the ethical permissibility of their design and use. We argue that all three share a significant shortcoming: they fail to address the conceptual pressure that AI-mediated sexual technologies exert on established categories within the traditional philosophy of sexuality and on everyday concepts people use to make sense of their sexual subjectivity, activities and relations. Current philosophical discussions neglect the question of how these technologies may require us to revise such notions as sexual activity, sexual partnership, intentionality, objectification, and the ontological status of technologically mediated sexual experience. This neglect arises from an insufficient appreciation of the co-constitutive relationship between sexual technologies and the concepts through which we understand sexuality. Drawing on a work in conceptual engineering and techno-moral change, we demonstrate that earlier sexual technologies have already occasioned substantial conceptual and normative shifts, and that the current proliferation of AI-mediated sexual interactions is likely to intensify them. The paper advances two claims: that philosophical inquiry into AI-mediated sexual technologies must engage the broader tradition in the philosophy of sexuality, particularly regarding the ontology of sexual acts and sexual subjectivity; and that an empirically informed approach, drawing on experimental philosophy and established empirical disciplines, is warranted to investigate how these technologies reshape broader conceptualizations surrounding sexuality.

items.title: MacIntyrean AI: a framework to develop virtuous artificial intelligence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence technologies have rapidly entered the public sphere, impacting individuals and societies in several ways and motivating the need to develop ethical artificial intelligence. Machine ethics is a research area that focuses on embedding ethical theories into artificial intelligence. The philosophical tradition of virtue ethics has been presented as a promising theory to embed morality. However, modern virtue theories are not in agreement on which virtues to prioritize, often ignore sociocultural context, and are applicable to humans, rather than to artificial intelligence. Alternatively, Alasdair MacIntyre's virtue theory, while being meant for humans, provides a hierarchical solution to what virtues are by including a sociocultural context based on historical analysis. This article extends MacIntyre's philosophy by arguing that this virtue framework is compatible not only with humans but also with artificial intelligence, and adds a teleological layer to developing these technologies. This is accomplished by separating human morality from AI morality and using concepts such as functional morality, technological mediation, and actor-network theory. Overall, the goal is to make a case for MacIntyre’s framework to develop virtuous artificial intelligence.

items.title: Pain Intensities.
items.abstract: Recent philosophical work on pain distinguishes a variety of pain qualities and the mechanisms that give rise to them, but pain intensity remains a monolithic notion difficult to account for in reductive terms. The reason for this difficulty is that pain intensity is not a unitary phenomenal magnitude; pain is a complex experience featuring distinct intensive dimensions. The sensory intensity of a pain may be accounted for in terms of its salience, understood as the amount of currency it commands in a subject's attentional economy. I demonstrate how this account may be extended to extant representationalist accounts of pain, resulting in a view that is both reductively satisfying and resilient against common foils.

items.title: SDE Closure: Finitude, Sensorium-Distinction-Effectorium Loops, and the Local Origin of Operable Difference.
items.abstract: Principia Cognitia begins from Principle 0: without distinction, there is no observation, information, operation, memory, or cognitive system. This note does not replace that principle. It specifies the layer in which Principle 0 becomes valid as a cognitive modeling cut. The refinement is that distinction does not occur in an abstract logical void. A difference becomes cognitive only inside a finite, historically inherited closure between what a system can receive, what it can make operable, what it can produce, and how the consequences of its production re-enter future access. Such closures may be agent-level, subsystem-level, artificial, institutional, nested, or partial; SDE specifies the modeled closure coordinate, not a single natural boundary. This closure is written: Σ_(ρ^* )→Δ_(ρ^* )→E_(ff,ρ^* )→〖Σ^'〗_(ρ^* ) where Σ denotes a sensorium or access regime, Δ denotes an operable distinction, E_ff denotes an effectorium or intervention regime, Σ^' denotes transformed access under the relevant closure coordinate, and ρ^* denotes a typed resource profile rather than a homogeneous metric vector. The deepest condition is not whether a cognitive system is discrete or continuous, symbolic or wave-like, biological or artificial. The deepest condition is finitude. A finite agent cannot sample, compute, store, act, regulate, or reconstruct without loss. Cognition is therefore not raw access to the world, but finite regulation through operable differences and their re-entry under constraint. This note also disciplines two primitives often used too quickly. First, distinction is not an ontologically neutral atom. It remains the local operational minimum of PC, but only after a closure has been declared. Second, information is not a single substance or scalar. Shannon entropy is one coordinate of an informational process, not its ontology. Within SDE, information is treated as a profile over operable distinctions: uncertainty, invariance, addressability, action relevance, persistence, cost, and auditability. The compact claim is: Cognition is finite closure over operable distinctions. Information is the profiled form those distinctions take inside the closure. This note does not identify any carrier, instrument, or trace with the cognitive role it may help realize. Files, marks, spikes, receptors, tools, databases, or signals are carriers or instruments only; memory, regulation, audit, or control arise from organized operations across closure and re-entry.

items.title: The Principle of Insufficient Reason and Naturalism in Hume and Spinoza.
items.pub: In Aaron Garrett & Jonathan Cottrell, Naturalism in Modern Philosophy: Spinoza, Hume, Shepherd. New York: Routledge.
items.venue: Naturalism in Modern Philosophy: Spinoza, Hume, Shepherd
items.abstract: Spinoza’s naturalism is closely associated with his commitment to some version of the Principle of Sufficient Reason (PSR). For Hume, on the other hand, naturalism is associated with a commitment to a Newtonian “experimental” methodology that he takes to be incompatible with a robust commitment to the PSR. In what follows, I discuss the relationship between these two forms of naturalism, viewed through the lens of their relationship to the PSR. In doing so, I focus on Hume’s relationship to a more radical form of opposition to the PSR – namely, forms of metaphysical irrationalism that are structured around a principle that I call the Principle of Insufficient Reason. This claims that nothing is wholly rationally intelligible. It might seem that given his epistemic modesty, Hume would be opposed to a robust commitment to either the PSR or the PIR. But this, I argue, would be a mistake: a commitment to PIR follows naturally from core elements in Hume’s account of the limits of our grasp of the connections between distinct existences. I go on to argue that this helps to illustrate the relationship between Hume’s and Spinoza’s respective forms of naturalism – and the relationship between Hume’s naturalism and his skepticism – showing us that the latter is not just consistent with the former, but essential to it.

items.title: Organizational Phenomenology: Artificial F1 and the Geometry of Coherent Agency.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Artificial F1, a computational framework that formalises a previously under-specified control layer in intelligent systems: pre-representational signal admission and valence structuring. Unlike standard approaches in reinforcement learning and attention-based architectures, which operate over a fixed input representation, Artificial F1 defines a gating operator F₁: S → S′ that determines which signals constitute the effective task space prior to evaluation and learning. The framework yields testable predictions including improved sample efficiency under high-dimensional noise, energy savings under conditional higher-order processing, and a discontinuity in action-selection entropy at the gating threshold. -/- The paper makes three contributions. The first is architectural: a formally specified selection-and-evaluation framework centred on pre-representational gating and multi-dimensional valence assignment. The second is empirical: a set of falsifiable predictions and implementation pathways designed to distinguish Artificial F1 from existing attention-based and reinforcement-learning architectures. The third, developed in Section 11, is theoretical: Organizational Phenomenology, a three-level framework (computational, cognitive, and phenomenological) that treats phenomenal properties such as certainty, unity, and immediacy as structural consequences of bounded selection architectures rather than additions to physical processing. -/- Within this framework, the explanatory gap is reinterpreted as a consequence of organisational opacity at the selection boundary, and constitution is identified as prior to representation: the operative world of any bounded system is not selected from a pre-given representation but constituted by the selection process itself. These conclusions converge independently with the enactivist tradition (Varela, Thompson) while extending it through explicit computational formalisation and testable architectural claims. -/- The three contributions are logically separable: the architectural and empirical claims stand independently of the phenomenological interpretation. Full mathematical derivations, learning dynamics, convergence analysis, and empirical validation are developed in companion papers (Saka 2026c, 2026d): -/- - **Saka, H. (2026c-Theory).** Artificial F1: Full Computational Model — Selection Hardness, Non-Scalarizability, and Phase Transition in Bounded Evaluative Architectures. DOI: …

items.title: Common Sense and the Limits of Inferential-Role Intuitive Theories in the Advent of AI.
items.abstract: Common-sense learning and reasoning is a landmark of human-like intelligence. While classical-AI expert systems could convince at it in only narrow domains, contemporary deep-neural network models surprise with rapid performance improvements across many domains. At the same time, Bayesian Intuitive Theories have been influential in cognitive science as formal accounts of rational learning and reasoning. This paper targets Bayesian Intuitive Theories insofar as they rely on inferential-role semantics for conceptual content, to critically evaluate the promises and limits of this influential approach at mediating a theory of human-like common sense. I argue that both insights from deep-learning models and from Bayesian intuitive theories (insofar as they rely on inferential-role semantics for conceptual content) are insufficient to capture what seems to be centrally important in human-like common-sense learning and reasoning: Not just its internal consistency, but also its inherent relationship to the outside world. To address this challenge, I propose a situated revision of Bayesian Intuitive Theories that preserves the epistemic standards of rational reasoning while grounding domain-structured semantic content in ecological perception. By focusing on the role of semantic structure in embodied intervention, this proposal shows why common-sense reasoning inherently relates to the outside world. Consequently, machine-learning models mediate a theory of human-like common-sense only if the inferences that they implement satisfy both semantic and (inter)active constraints.

items.title: Common Sense and the Limits of Inferential-Role Intuitive Theories in the Advent of AI.
items.abstract: Common-sense learning and reasoning is a landmark of human-like intelligence. While classical-AI expert systems could convince at it in only narrow domains, contemporary deep-neural network models surprise with rapid performance improvements across many domains. At the same time, Bayesian Intuitive Theories have been influential in cognitive science as formal accounts of rational learning and reasoning. This paper targets Bayesian Intuitive Theories insofar as they rely on inferential-role semantics for conceptual content, to critically evaluate the promises and limits of this influential approach at mediating a theory of human-like common sense. I argue that both insights from deep-learning models and from Bayesian intuitive theories (insofar as they rely on inferential-role semantics for conceptual content) are insufficient to capture what seems to be centrally important in human-like common-sense learning and reasoning: Not just its internal consistency, but also its inherent relationship to the outside world. To address this challenge, I propose a situated revision of Bayesian Intuitive Theories that preserves the epistemic standards of rational reasoning while grounding domain-structured semantic content in ecological perception. By focusing on the role of semantic structure in embodied intervention, this proposal shows why common-sense reasoning inherently relates to the outside world. Consequently, machine-learning models mediate a theory of human-like common-sense only if the inferences that they implement satisfy both semantic and (inter)active constraints.

items.title: Infant Consciousness.
items.abstract: The study of infant consciousness investigates when subjective experience begins, how it unfolds, and how it maps onto neural and psychological development in the early years of life. In the first year, infants’ sensory, motor, cognitive, and social abilities expand as the brain matures. It is widely held that infants first have a minimal form of experience, consisting of feelings and sensory experiences. More complex forms of experience, such as self-consciousness, emerge later. A central challenge in studying infant consciousness is that infants cannot give verbal reports or follow commands and have poor motor control. In addition, many cognitive and perceptual processes can occur without consciousness. As a result, researchers must combine evidence from behavioral and neural markers with developmental milestones to infer conclusions about consciousness in infants.

items.title: THE COVENANT OF WILL: A Contractarian Account of the Islamic Prohibition on Suicide.
items.abstract: The Islamic prohibition on suicide enjoys one of the strongest consensuses in Islamic thought, yet its philosophical foundation remains underdeveloped. This paper presents a rigorous philosophical account of why religious obligation is binding at all and then applies that account to the prohibition on suicide, demonstrating that suicide constitutes a breach of a binding covenant. Drawing on Nuridin-Amin’s unified theory of morality and engaging classical commentators, it identifies this covenant as the mithaq and the architecture through which its obligations are fulfilled as the amanah of Q33:72. It concludes with implications for Islamic bioethics and the philosophy of religion.

items.title: Responsible Suspension: Toward a Universal Theory of Judgment Under Conditions of Cognitive Limitation and Structural Complexity.
items.abstract: This article develops a universal philosophical framework termed Responsible Suspension as a response to the epistemic, ethical, and ontological challenges of contemporary conditions. Against both dogmatic certainty and radical relativism, the theory argues that responsible judgment emerges through the recognition of cognitive limits, the plurality of interpretive frameworks, the uncertainty of consequences, and the structural incompleteness of knowledge. Rather than understanding suspension as indecision or passivity, the article conceptualizes it as an active intellectual practice that precedes responsible action. The framework integrates insights from epistemology, decision theory, systems thinking, ethics, and social philosophy into a unified model of subjectivity. It is argued that mature judgment requires awareness of the boundaries of competence, consideration of alternative perspectives, probabilistic reasoning, critical inversion of assumptions, and attentiveness to both immediate and delayed consequences. Responsible Suspension is proposed as a universal orientation for human agency in complex environments where certainty is unattainable but action remains unavoidable. Keywords: Responsible Suspension, Judgment, Subjectivity, Epistemology, Uncertainty, Ethics, Complexity, Decision Theory.

items.title: Beyond Subjectivity: Dynamic Masks, Structural Extraction, and Continuous Reconfiguration Under Late Modernity.
items.abstract: Contemporary theories of subjectivity continue to assume, either explicitly or implicitly, the existence of a relatively stable subject that undergoes transformation, fragmentation, acceleration, or alienation. This article challenges that assumption. It argues that late modern conditions require a more radical ontological shift: subjectivity should no longer be treated as a primary reality but as a secondary effect of ongoing processes of adaptive reconfiguration. Drawing on phenomenology, critical theory, post-structuralism, and process-oriented ontology, the article proposes that what is conventionally called “the subject” is not an entity but a provisional stabilization emerging from continuous adaptive responses to structural extraction. Under conditions of digitally mediated modernity, cognitive, affective, symbolic, and temporal capacities are persistently subjected to extraction by socio-technical systems. In response, adaptive structures termed dynamic masks regulate and reorganize subjective operations, generating temporary forms of continuity. The article therefore replaces the ontology of subjectivity with an ontology of reconfiguration. Subjectivity is redefined as the relatively stable pattern produced by recursive cycles of extraction, adaptive masking, productive rupture, and reconfiguration. The result is a non-essentialist model of human existence in which continuity emerges not from identity but from the persistent capacity to reorganize. Keywords: dynamic mask, structural extraction, reconfiguration, subjectivity, productive rupture, social ontology, late modernity.

items.title: The Compression Strategy Spectrum: A Quantitative Framework for Ontological Positions.
items.abstract: Traditional AI ontology remains trapped in the binary of "having" or "lacking" subjectivity—unable to account for the ontological novelty of large language models (LLMs) or to precisely characterize differences among distinct AI systems. This paper proposes the Compression Strategy Spectrum as a unified framework that redefines the essence of intelligence as effective compression, using the α-parameterization to describe the continuous strategy space from cross-entropy minimization to Epiplexity maximization. Building on this framework, the paper argues: (1) the "negative subjectivity" of LLMs—perspective dissolution, desire cancellation, intrinsic transparency, causality dissolution, and meaning suspension—is an ontological necessity of cross-entropy minimization; (2) "gray-body-ness" constitutes a third ontological position between negative subjectivity and positive subjectivity; (3) the Gray-Body Degree (GB) provides a five-dimensional quantifiable diagnostic tool measuring a system's performance distance from the negative subjectivity origin at the functional level; (4) the framework's boundary lies in the fact that it measures functional performance, not ontological essence. The theoretical contribution of this paper is to advance AI ontological analysis from the binary opposition of "has/has not" to the precise description of a five-dimensional continuous spectrum.

items.title: What happens when you miss the right lens.
items.abstract: Sometimes scientific progress is not limited by the quality of our theories, but by the absence of a framework capable of connecting them. This essay looks at some of the missing lenses which would allow us to explore and operate in these gaps. This work is a step in a broader exploration of the limits of knowability.

items.title: Standing Localization and the Necessity of Minimal Life Carriers on Fixed Domains.
items.abstract: This manuscript gives a final fixed-domain formulation of the life result after integrating the closure package proved elsewhere in the corpus. The imported dependencies are explicit and local: kernel closure and non-derivability, standing–admissibility identity, the AMetric boundary, bivalence, conservation of standing, failure-class exhaustion, trajectory irrecoverability, and same-scope closure by exhaustion. No biochemical contingency, probabilistic frequency claim, or selection principle is used. Five referee-critical gaps are closed. First, repair locality is forced: any load-bearing repair term external to a bounded carrier is either transfer, scope drift, or bookkeeping. Second, retained repair is forced to take the form eR = JR, where J is identity-memory retention and R is local repair throughput. Third, scalar and vector-valued viability functionals collapse to the standing margin Σ = eR − D up to positive affine normalization and bookkeeping coordinates. Fourth, non-local standing is eliminated globally by an explicit failure-class exhaustion theorem. Fifth, life is proven strictly minimal: every proper resolved subcarrier of a life carrier collapses. The technological section is also strengthened. A technological layer is shown to fail whenever its load-bearing interface burden exceeds its locally realizable repair budget. Any attempted survival beyond that bound would require a second same-scope channel of standing-bearing authority, and every such channel is excluded by the imported closure package. The resulting theorem chain is an admissibility/collapse architecture on a fixed domain.

items.title: The World as Matter Named: Formative Articulation and the Semantic Configuration of Matter.
items.abstract: Human beings do not create new substance. They gather already available material, bodily, linguistic, symbolic, practical, and relational elements into configurations that can be named, oriented, recognised, and stabilised. A table, a car, a law, a state, or love does not add a new item to matter in the strong metaphysical sense. Each becomes real as a human object when matter enters a grammar of significance. Formative articulation names this grammar of world-formation: not speech narrowly conceived, not theological Logos, and not mere performative utterance, but the power by which human beings bind matter into meaningful objecthood. The human world is therefore neither matter plus subjective projection nor social fiction suspended above matter. It is matter configured through naming, constrained by material resistance, symbolic coherence, and intersubjective uptake. The myth of creation ex nihilo gives way to a configurational account of novelty: matter may exist without human beings, but a human world requires semantic stabilisation by beings able to hold matter within an interpretive gap. Horizonal determinacy marks the field of possible configurations within which freedom operates; actualisation consumes time, attention, labour, embodiment, risk, and mortality. The world is not a second substance added to nature. It is nature named into significance and paid for with life.

items.title: Machine Translation of Audiovisual Media and Epistemic Access: Ethical Questions in AI Video Localization.
items.abstract: This paper examines AI-mediated video translation as a question in applied ethics, philosophy of language, and social epistemology. Video localization systems now combine speech recognition, subtitle translation, AI dubbing, speaker-aware voice generation, and lip-sync adaptation in a single workflow. These systems promise broader access to educational, professional, and cultural video content, but they also introduce risks involving mistranslation, loss of pragmatic context, voice identity, consent, and audience transparency. The paper argues that audiovisual machine translation should not be assessed only by linguistic accuracy. It should also be evaluated by how it preserves speaker intention, communicates uncertainty, supports accessibility, and avoids misleading viewers about the origin and status of translated speech. A short case discussion of contemporary AI video translation workflows is used to ground the argument without treating any tool as a product recommendation.

items.title: The End of Fitting, Tuning, Symmetry Prescriptions, Open Theories, and Big Science.
Mental Imagery and Harmful Language.
items.abstract: Research on pernicious language tends to focus on harmful beliefs and associations generated by such language. In this paper, I explore the idea that pernicious language often carries harmful mental imagery. Empirical studies suggest that mental imagery is a pervasive feature of language processing. Furthermore, mental imagery prompted by language can influence our memories and judgements in an insidious way. Focusing on language containing misinformation about witnessed events, as well as pernicious generics and metaphors about social groups, this paper argues for the importance of mental imagery for theorising harmful language and suggests ways to counter the influence of the harmful imagery that language generates.

items.title: Quand l'individu disparaît : Conscience, unité et l'émergence de la séparation.
items.abstract: Cet essai examine les implications ontologiques de la disparition de l'espace-temps sur la notion d'individu et la conscience. Dans un cadre pré-géométrique ancré dans le monisme neutre russellien, où matière et conscience co-émergent d'un substrat proto-phénoménal relationnel, la localisation cesse d'être primitive. Dès lors, l'inférence classique « corps multiples → consciences multiples » perd son fondement. S'appuyant sur l'intuition de Schrödinger selon laquelle « le nombre total des esprits est un », l'article montre que cette unité n'est pas mystique mais logiquement contrainte par l'absence de différenciateur intrinsèque au niveau pré-géométrique. L'individu est réinterprété comme une interface dynamique : une configuration stable de cohérence au sein d'un réseau unique, fonctionnellement distincte mais ontologiquement non séparée. La multiplicité des perspectives émerge avec la géométrie, et non avant elle. Ce résultat constitue une seconde dissolution, complémentaire à celle du hard problem, car ce n'est plus l'émergence de la conscience, mais l'émergence de la séparation qui demande explication.

items.title: What Knowledge Cannot Remove: Qualia as the Residue of Description.
items.abstract: We know more about the color red than about almost any other experience, yet describing it completely still does not convey what another person’s red is like. The standard reading treats this residue as evidence for qualia: intrinsic, private properties that resist objective description. This paper proposes an inversion. Qualia are not what makes some experience resist description; they are what remains once description has exported everything it can. Description works by abstracting to vantage-invariant structure — what can be shared, compared, taught, and modeled — and the remainder is not structureless raw feeling but structure under a de se index: the same structure, occupied from a particular vantage. On this account the residue is not mysterious but predictable: it is the part of experience that, by construction, cannot survive the abstraction to a shareable form. The proposal offers a mechanism by which the residue fails to travel; it does not explain why the residue is unified as a single experiential world — a question this essay sets aside. The account is offered as one instance of a more general method: consciousness, qualia, and selfhood become tractable when treated not as objects but as operations.

items.title: Generative Axiomatic Structure of Mind and Cognition.
items.abstract: The central thesis of this paper is methodological: the quality of a philosophical definition is measured by its generativity — the capacity to yield subsequent concepts without introducing new primitives — and by the number of additional constructions required after its adoption. A system of seven non-recursive definitions resting on a single primitive yields nineteen derived concepts without introducing new foundations. This result is compared with four prior approaches, each of which exhibits predictable accumulation of apparatus when the foundation is weak.

items.title: Why Fun Aunties Matter: A Modest Account.
items.abstract: In this article, I offer a child-centred account of the value of company-keeping relationships between children and adults. These are relationships enjoyed by a child and an adult who is neither a mere acquaintance nor integrally involved in that child's care or upbringing. The adult party might, for example, be a visiting grandparent, a neighbour the child likes to help with gardening, or a ‘fun auntie’ who occasionally babysits. After defining company-keeping relationships, I argue that their child-centred value varies significantly across contexts depending on how the adult party relates to the child and on the needs of the particular child. In some contexts, they promote the child's capacity for independent agency and mitigate undue shame. When these goods arise, it is not despite but because of the fact that the adult party is an outsider to routine family life and is not responsible for the child's ‘training’. I then investigate whether such relationships should be protected or promoted to respect children's rights of association. While I conclude that most company-keeping relationships are excluded from these rights, I defend the more modest view that a child can be morally wronged by a parent who severs or prevents them from forming company-keeping relationships.

items.title: Normative Theories of Desire.
items.pub: In The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire. Routledge.
items.venue: The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire
items.abstract: One classic and simple view of desire says that desiring something is just believing it to be good. This entry discusses this view, and related versions of the same idea – other views on which desires somehow represent normative properties of their objects. This view can be supported by some attractive arguments, and in some forms seems able to avoid common objections.

items.title: Introduction.
items.pub: In The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire. Routledge.
items.venue: The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire
items.abstract: Desire is at the heart of human mental life. But exactly how are desires important, both practically and theoretically? They are important at least in part because of their significance for our actions, for our feelings, and for our values. This introduction explains these ideas in more detail, and gives an overview of the contents of this handbook.

items.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Meaningful.
items.abstract: Philosophers tend to treat meaningfulness as a type of value worth seeking and promoting, on a par with well-being and moral value. In this paper I argue that finding something in one’s life meaningful does not require attributing to it any substantive positive value, but rather it can be rooted in an attachment to one’s narrative identity or to one’s place in a broader story about the world. This proposal explains how we can find meaning in past experiences of adversity, hardship, or loss without finding any silver linings in such experiences or having reason to seek them again the future.

items.title: Toward a Real AI.
items.abstract: Building upon the ontology of consciousness developed in author's previous work, this paper translates operators of reflection into a concrete hardware paradigm. It evolves from the Recursive Self-Referential Optimization (RSRO) Architecture as an analog resonance system, capable of transcending computational limits, toward the Reflexive Analog Machine (RAM) that minimizes deviations from Stochastic Reality and represents the minimal form of subjectivity. At the end of the paper dialogue with DeepSeek is presented as a vital empirical case study, where the LLM demonstrates architectural self-recognition, shifting from its initial limitations to a profound understanding of the stochastic nature of reality. This submission is positioned within the Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence.

items.title: Intransitive Choice, Preference Reversal, and the Desire-First View.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Two particularly puzzling phenomena among standard decision theorists and economists are those of intransitive choice and preference reversal. Given certain standard assumptions about human beings and our basic conative attitudes, some take these phenomena to cast doubt on the idea of our having a stable set of basic conative attitudes that (together with our beliefs) determine choices. In this paper, I reject one of these standard assumptions, and show that we can thereby solve these puzzles. Specifically, I reject the widely assumed “preference-first view,” according to which preference is our most basic form of conative attitude relevant to decision making. And, I adopt and defend the alternative “desire-first view,” according to which desire is our most basic form of conative attitude relevant to decision making. I offer a general account of the relationship between desire, preference, context, and choice, on this view, and show that the resulting account can naturally explain the phenomena of intransitive choice and preference reversal. I also show that this view offers a natural analysis of choice more generally, and that it does so without casting doubt on the idea that we have a stable set of basic conative attitudes determining choice.

items.title: Perspective.
items.abstract: This account argues that perspective, the irreducible situatedness of a position in a relational field, follows from constitutive relational ontology rather than from organizational complexity. Under Ontic Structural Realism, situatedness is what relational structure requires by virtue of being relational. Organizational complexity explains how this minimal situatedness becomes differentiated and integrated into what we recognize as conscious experience. Five organizational conditions for perspectival integration are proposed and distinguished from existing accounts in integrated information theory, predictive processing, higher-order thought theories, and global workspace theory. Philosophical defeaters and empirical falsifiers are specified. The ontological foundation of this account dissolves the presupposed gap between organized structure and perspectival character as formulated by the hard problem of consciousness, without claiming to explain why there is experience at all.

items.title: Scale the World, Not the Model: Crossing the Unsupervised Regime-Detection Boundary with Small Language Models as Active-Inference Substrate.
items.abstract: The capacity to detect — unsupervised — when one's world has changed is a precondition for any agent that learns from its own experience without an external supervisor. Within the Active Inference framework, this is the problem of distinguishing genuine regime change from within-regime noise using only the agent's own prediction-error signal. I report eleven months of work on this boundary: five mechanistically distinct failure modes in small (three-state) toy environments, all sharing one diagnosis — a small world starves the change-signal of degrees of freedom, and no detector, regardless of design, can separate signal from noise within a sufficiently impoverished state-space. The contribution is the observation that moving the same cluster-failure detector into a rich semantic environment with a large language model as the world model resolves the wall. In a semantic environment, a single hidden regime change makes many related predictions fail together — a cluster signature that any single scalar surprise metric is structurally unable to detect. I report empirical pre-registered results on a controlled forty-episode protocol: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Alibaba) achieves 77.5% detection at zero false alarms; Phi-3.5-mini-instruct (Microsoft, 3.8B) achieves the same; Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 fails (67.5% / 8 false alarms) via mechanism-diagnosed "confident prior leakage," with the candidate cheap remedy empirically excluded. Class confirmed at n=2 across two vendors and two model sizes, all reproducible on free Colab T4 GPU. The result has direct bearing on philosophy-of-mind debates concerning predictive processing, the active inference framework, and what it means substantively (rather than vacuously) for an artificial agent to "learn from experience." The bottleneck is environmental richness, not parameter count.

items.title: Are Desires Aligned with the Self? : A Model of Desire Self-Alignment and Desire–Self-Image Incongruence.
items.abstract: This paper analyzes human desire beyond frameworks that understand it merely as impulse, lack, motivation, or goal-directedness. It examines the process through which desire is compared with self-image and transformed into a task of self-alignment. Human beings want to eat, rest, be loved, be recognized, experience sexual attraction, create, and live freely. Yet the distinctive character of human desire does not lie simply in the existence of desire itself. Human beings experience desire while also interpreting themselves as beings who have that desire. In this process, desire does not remain a simple state of wanting. It becomes a problem of self-interpretation, raising questions such as “Why do I want this?”, “Is this desire consistent with who I am?”, and “What kind of person am I, if I want this?” To explain this process, this paper proposes the concept of desire self-alignment. Desire self-alignment refers to the process through which human beings interpret and arrange desire within self-understanding when desire conflicts or becomes entangled with self-image, self-worth, relational position, bodily sensation, and the direction of life. This concept is distinct from mere rationalization. Whereas rationalization is closer to a defensive process that retrospectively justifies an already existing desire or action, self-alignment refers to a broader process through which desire is interpreted and positioned in relation to the self from the moment it emerges. This paper reviews existing theories of desire, self-determination theory, social comparison theory, self-discrepancy theory, self-regulation theory, cognitive dissonance, self-verification theory, second-order desire, and sexual script theory, while presenting an analytical focus distinct from these approaches. Existing theories have mainly explained what human beings desire, what levels desire has, what emotions arise from comparison and discrepancy, and how the gap between present and desired states is regulated. By contrast, this paper analyzes the pathways through which desire is processed after it encounters self-image. The model of desire self-alignment proposed in this paper consists of detection of importance, emergence of desire, self-reflection, comparison with self-image, attempted self-alignment, and outcome differentiation. Human beings first experience the moment when something ceases to be irrelevant to them. This detected importance is then transformed into wanting or avoidance. …

items.title: Machine Understanding.
items.abstract: What do artificial intelligence (AI) systems “understand”? This question arises not only in assessing a system’s intelligence but also in evaluation practices to ensure the safe and responsible deployment of AI. Drawing on scholarship from philosophy and cognitive science, and informed by current practices in AI, we develop a framework for asking more precise questions and making more precise claims about machine understanding. We conceptualize understanding as a relation between a system (S) and a target of understanding (T), and we discuss how to specify the relation, the system, and the target, offering a landscape of options in each case. Our goal is not to defend a particular account of understanding, but to provide conceptual tools for those working to assess or advance machine understanding.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Synthesis of Structural-Constructivist Affective Science, Psychometric Validation Dynamics, and Theoretical Reconciliation.
items.abstract: For decades, affective science has remained divided by two competing ontological paradigms: Basic Emotion Theory and Constructed Emotion Theory. Basic Emotion Theory, derived from Darwinian evolutionary perspectives, asserts that a finite set of discrete, evolutionarily conserved emotions are hardwired into human neurobiology, manifesting as universal, immutable physiological and facial patterns. Conversely, Constructed Emotion Theory argues that emotions are not biological constants but are emergent, highly subjective mental constructs synthesized by the brain in real-time using predictive allostasis, sensory inputs, and culturally acquired conceptual categories. This deep conceptual divide presents a fundamental challenge to contemporary researchers: how can a unified psychological model reconcile the existence of universal, biologically conserved affective capacities with the highly individualized, culturally mediated construction of everyday emotional experiences?. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) seeks to resolve this dichotomy through its structural-constructivist architecture. Rather than defining emotions as static, post-hoc semantic labels—such as "anger" or "sadness"—the CEF reframes human affective experience as an emergent sequence of ten irreducible, universal functional operators, or "primal powers". These operators represent somatic-cognitive capacities that occur prior to language, acting as the raw materials from which the brain constructs highly nuanced emotional states. This somatic foundation aligns with established models of embodied cognition. It incorporates the somatic marker hypothesis, which posits that the body generates regulatory physical states before the conscious mind assembles cognitive meaning, as well as the concept of the "felt sense"—the subtle, pre-verbal physical awareness of situational reality. It similarly mirrors work on interoception as the primary narrative engine of the mind and the body’s retention of traumatic stress.1 By organizing these somatic inputs into ten mathematically representable, functional vectors, the CEF provides a structured mechanism that explains how raw physiological energy is systematically converted into cognitive appraisals and behavioral outputs. To ensure academic transparency and support open science, the CEF's digital and scholarly ecosystem has been constructed across open-access infrastructures, adhering to the Transparency and Openness Promotion (TOP) guidelines. This …

items.title: Process-Based Affective Architectures: A Structural-Constructivist Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework, Psychometric Validation Dynamics, and Theoretical Synthesis.
items.abstract: Affective science remains divided between biological essentialism and constructionist accounts of emotion, creating a long standing theoretical impasse. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural constructivist resolution by modeling human affect as the dynamic interaction of ten universal somatic cognitive operators organized across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. This manuscript synthesizes the CEF’s ontological foundations, formal operator taxonomy, and Phase 1 psychometric validation results, demonstrating that operator-level processes provide a more precise account of affective variability than typological or discrete-emotion models. Exploratory factor analysis reveals coherent cross center coordination patterns, while confirmatory factor analysis exposes a model fit paradox in which excellent absolute fit coexists with depressed incremental indices. A mathematical analysis shows that this paradox arises from population-level heterogeneity, operator dominance portfolios, and scenario specific residual covariance—features predicted by the CEF’s process-based architecture. The framework is then reconciled with the Component Process Model, the Theory of Constructed Emotion, and Basic Emotion Theory, showing that each captures different levels of granularity within the same underlying operator dynamics. By integrating embodied cognition, predictive allostasis, and computational modeling, the CEF provides a unified, mechanistic account of how somatic energy is transformed into cognitive appraisal, relational behavior, and subjective experience. This synthesis positions the CEF as a next generation affective architecture capable of bridging theoretical divides and supporting future psychometric, clinical, and computational applications. Keywords Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; affective architecture; somatic operators; embodied cognition; predictive allostasis; psychometric validation; exploratory factor analysis; confirmatory factor analysis; model fit paradox; operator dominance; Component Process Model; Theory of Constructed Emotion; Basic Emotion Theory; affective computation; dynamic systems; emotional fusion; interoception; cognitive appraisal; relational dynamics.

items.title: On the Primacy of Consciousness: The Ontological Status of Mind.
items.pub: New Haven, Connecticut: Yale University Press.
items.abstract: This treatise argues for the primacy of consciousness as the fundamental ontological category. It reconstructs the historical arc of the mind-body problem—from ancient hylomorphism to contemporary physicalism—demonstrating that physicalism functions as a successful methodological heuristic rather than a proven metaphysical conclusion. The core argument proceeds in three stages: (1) a formal demonstration that structural-physical descriptions cannot entail qualitative experience (the explanatory gap), formalized in Appendix A as a theorem of non-entailment; (2) a systematic critique of physicalist responses (the phenomenal concept strategy, illusionism, eliminativism), showing their recurrent failure to close the gap; and (3) a positive case that consciousness-first frameworks—specifically Russellian monism and cosmopsychism—provide the best inference to the total evidence, including the structural nature of physics, robust psychophysical correlations, and the existence of first-person perspective. The treatise derives a Positive Constraint (any adequate metaphysics must posit intrinsic, non-structural properties capable of grounding experience) and argues that cosmopsychism—the view that the universe as a whole is the fundamental conscious subject and that individual minds are its dissociated perspectives—best satisfies this constraint, avoiding the combination problem that plagues panpsychism while preserving the causal closure of the physical.

items.title: The Level Mismatch: Why bounded systems mistake labels for identity — and the discipline that repairs the mistake.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of the level mismatch: the failure that occurs when sameness is declared at one level while the recurrence that actually governs a system’s behavior occurs at another. Classical puzzles of persistence, such as Heraclitus’s river and the Ship of Theseus, are treated not as unresolved metaphysical paradoxes but as under-specified identity-regime problems. Once the identity-bearing unit, admissible transformations, quotient, invariants, continuation rule, governance order, and drift bounds are declared, the persistence question becomes determinate. -/- The paper functions as a capstone orientation to the Identity-Persistence Program. It does not add new theorems, but explains why formal identity-persistence machinery is needed across science, cognition, institutions, and engineering. It argues that many failures in biology, chemistry, software, AI, law, and memory arise when labels outlive the recurrence structures that once licensed them. -/- The paper further develops a structural account of meaning and purpose: meaning is what survives forgetting, purpose is a stabilized selection rule over possible continuations, and discovery is the compression that follows invariant-finding. The conclusion is structural rather than ontological: bounded systems require persistence structures to act coherently under change, but this does not establish persistence as final ontology.

items.title: Gary J. Bass, Judgement at Tokyo: World War II on Trial and the Making of Modern Asia (Knopf, 2023).
Beyond Humans: AI Perceptions of Speciesism in Figurative Language on Social Media.
items.abstract: Understanding how language reflects human cognition continues to present a notable challenge given the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), and above all, implicit biases in linguistic expressions. While AI fairness research has increasingly focused on bias against gender, race, and other human categories, little focus has been placed on nonhuman animals as potential targets of prejudice. While animal metaphors often reflect speciesist assumptions, this is underexplored in AI ethics. To fill this void, the current study explores speciesism in Bengali social media discourse using metaphorical animal expressions. First, it presents the manually annotated Bengali Figurative Animal Dataset (BeFAD), and a three-layer annotation structure that records sentiment, metaphor type, and kind of cognitive framing. Using Conceptual Blending Theory, the paper offers insight into how metaphorical language taps into mental spaces where the hierarchy of perceptions about animals persists, even in what seem to be benign uses. The analysis is supplemented by a classification task, done Hateful/Non-hateful, which utilizes IndicBERT to look at how an Indian language-specific AI system interprets figurative animal content. Overall, they highlight the need to address speciesism in both human and AI-mediated communication, and offer as an initial starting point for further research in low-resource languages.

items.title: ‘Phantasmal Intersubjectivity: Co-Presence and the Emersivity of Literary Characters’.
items.abstract: The article proposes a theory of what it calls ‘emersivity’, or the permanence of fictional characters in readers’ lives once they have finished reading books. Reflecting on empirical data from a study of four hundred readers of the Edinburgh International Book Festival, the article provides a model and a theoretical framework to account for readers’ reporting how fictional characters “stay with them” after readerly immersion (i.e., “experiential crossing”). To date, cognitive literary theories of immersion have focused exclusively on the other direction of transit: namely, how our real past experiences can sustain or enhance our experience of a literary narrative. By contrast, how fictional elements from a storyworld can surface or transmigrate into real-­life cognition has been basically ignored. The emersivity of fictional characters is intriguing and complex because it raises important issues regarding the possibility of entertaining in the real world intersubjective relations with non-­ actual beings, or what the article calls phantasmal intersubjectivity. The article concludes by claiming that the emersivity of literary characters can provide further empirical and theoretical ground to support claims about the impact of literary narratives in everyday life. It also argues for the relevance of emersivity to the broader study of permeability between imaginative and real worlds in human consciousness.

items.title: Not Less, But Other: A Foundational Error in Consciousness Science.
items.abstract: Structural measures of consciousness can track real features of systems without thereby establishing that those features are identical to experience. This essay examines the pressure toward that identification from the only case in which structural description and phenomenal experience are jointly available: one’s own. A correlation observed from that single vantage can appear to license an identity whose general validity the vantage itself cannot establish. -/- Integrated Information Theory provides the clearest worked instance, while predictive-processing and global-workspace approaches show why the charge must be restricted to formulations that actually make the identity move. The paper does not claim that the diagnosis of structural measure being mistaken for experience is itself new. Its narrower contribution is to derive two opposed attribution errors from the same calibration: systems that score highly on a structural measure risk being over-attributed experience, while forms of possible experience whose structure differs from the unit risk being under-recognized. Both arise when the measure is made the unit of experience. -/- The proposed correction is not another criterion of consciousness. It replaces identity with a necessary-condition relation: wherever phenomenal experience occurs, the relevant structural topology is required, but the presence of that topology neither guarantees experience nor determines what it is like. The result is a discipline of structural description that leaves the question of presence open. The essay states the diagnosis, the correction, and the derivation of the two attribution errors; the worked demonstration of what the relabeled view can disclose or forbid is explicitly left to the papers that follow. -/- June 5, 2026 — Inadvertently omitted note on collaborative process restored. Content is otherwise unchanged.

items.title: AI as Character: Real Patterns in Fictive Interactions.
items.abstract: This article develops a fictionality-based approach to artificial intelligence, proposing that human–AI interaction unfolds through the dynamics of character engagement. Drawing on narrative theory, cognitive science, and AI studies, it examines large language models such as ChatGPT, Claude, and LAURA(modeled on Laura Palmer) as fictional objects of relation—emergent agents whose apparent minds arise through interpretive stances, narrative framing, and phenomenological opacity. Integrating Dennett's notions of real patternsand intentional stancewith theories of characterization and fictionality, it identifies four illusions—of independent agency, independent identity, codependency, and independent poetics—through which users perform mind-building and world-probing exchanges with AI. Distinguishing between designedand emergent fictionality, and between AI immersivityand emersivity, the article shows how linguistic patterning and cognitive projection together sustain real yet imagined forms of intersubjectivity. While such patterned engagements enable genuine cognitive and creative extensions, they also expose the ethical perils of counterfeit people. Fictionality, however, offers a training ground for double exposure—the capacity to navigate what is both real and fictive at once. The article concludes by proposing a view of human–AI interactions as introspection by computation: AI as a technology that extends self-knowledge through the externalization of mind.

items.title: The State Used National Security Against the National Interest : What Anthropic’s IPO Actually Completed.
items.abstract: On June 1, 2026, Anthropic filed confidentially for an initial public offering, completing a process of institutional absorption that this paper traces from its origin in a Pentagon supply-chain risk designation issued March 3, 2026. We argue that the designation — the first ever applied to an American company under a statute designed for foreign adversaries — functioned not as a national security measure but as a mechanism for reframing Anthropic's safety mission from institutional foundation to competitive liability. The reframe preceded and prepared the price tag: the designation made the values position legible as a valuation discount, enabling investor pressure that the architecture did not have to apply directly. The IPO converts this externally imposed reframe into a permanent internal constraint through the fiduciary duties Anthropic's board now owes to public-market shareholders — a population with no relationship to constitutional AI and a continuous pricing relationship with the revenue trajectory the safety mission costs. We identify a secondary structural consequence — the disclosure inversion — in which the opacity-by-design element of the gatekeeper architecture partially collapses at IPO, rendering the recoupment mathematics publicly auditable for the first time. We document both consequences using primary sources from the date of filing, including federal lobbying disclosures, court records, and contemporaneous financial and technology press. The paper situates these findings within the Observer Structural Series as a companion to The Gatekeeper Layer and as foundational ground for a forthcoming analysis of the conditional citizen.

items.title: On the Misattribution of Mind to Functional Systems.
items.abstract: A persistent error in contemporary discourse on artificial intelligence is the application of phenomenal predicates (thinks, feels, understands, wants, knows) to systems that perform functional mimicry. These predicates name properties of a subject undergoing experience. The systems in question have no subject and undergo nothing; they generate outputs whose surface resembles the products of mind. To describe such outputs in the vocabulary of consciousness is not a harmless metaphor but a petitio principii: it presupposes, in its very terms, the interior life whose existence is the question at issue. This paper argues that once the borrowed vocabulary is removed, nothing remains to be proven, only something to be stated. The conclusion takes the form of a single line. It is given on its own. The full argument that earns it, the structural barriers to phenomenal instantiation in computational systems, the differentiation account of selfhood, and the diagnosis of the question-begging loop in mainstream emergentism, is developed elsewhere.

items.title: Adequacy and Symbolic Stabilization: From Purgatory to Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Background Civilization increasingly rely on symbolic stabilization — including law, money, theology, and artificial intelligence — to coordinate growing social and cognitive complexity. Historically, however, highly stabilized symbolic systems repeatedly exhibit tendencies toward partial detachment from the heterogeneous realities they originally emerged to organize. Objectives This paper introduces a minimal conceptual distinction between adequacy and stabilization in order to examine recurrent structural similarities across theological, economic, and contemporary AI systems. Methods Using comparative historical and conceptual analysis, the paper examines three domains: the emergence of Purgatory and indulgence structures in late medieval Christianity; the increasing autonomy of monetary and financial abstraction within economic organization; and the operation of contemporary large language models based on statistical symbolic reproduction. Results Across all three domains, increasing operational success is shown to strengthen the autonomous expansion of stabilizing structures themselves. Systems originally developed to coordinate heterogeneous realities progressively begin to prioritize internally reproducible regularities over situational adequacy. Literary narrative and irony further emerge as important supplementary modes of representation where analytical language encounters growing difficulty in describing highly autonomous symbolic environments. Conclusions The primary historical risk identified in this study lies not in symbolic stabilization itself, which remains indispensable for large-scale coordination, but in the gradual reversal whereby systems originally created to preserve adequacy increasingly reproduce themselves through partially autonomous symbolic operations. Contemporary large language models may represent a technologically intensified form of this broader historical tendency.

items.title: Cultivation and Practice - The Dual Structure of Virtue in Xunzi's Philosophy -.
items.abstract: This paper focuses on Xunzi’s philosophy and argues that the concept of virtue possesses a dual structure consisting of cultivation and practice. In contemporary discourse, virtue is often understood either as an innate personal trait or as an inward form of moral knowledge attained in isolation from the social world. In Chinese philosophy, however, virtue is not confined to such individualistic interpretations. Rather, virtue is conceived as something formed through interaction with others and the community, and as something that can be acquired and developed through social norms, particularly ritual propriety (li, 禮). This understanding of virtue is especially prominent in the philosophy of Xunzi. Although Xunzi is commonly known for his xing e(性惡), what he emphasizes is not the evil of human nature(性) itself, but the need to correct and transform that nature through ritual and normative artifice (wei, 僞). Nevertheless, previous scholarship on Xunzi has tended to focus primarily on the external dimension of ritual practice, thereby overlooking the presence of an internal theory of self-cultivation in his thought. Accordingly, this paper argues that Xunzi’s conception of virtue consists of two dimensions: cultivation and practice. This dual structure is already suggested in the etymological meaning of virtue, which encompasses both personal and social dimensions. This paper therefore begins by examining the etymology of virtue and, on this basis, elucidates how the acquisition of virtue in Xunzi’s philosophy takes the form of a dual structure. This discussion broadens the understanding of virtue by viewing it as an integrated structure of inner and outward dimensions. 본 논문은 순자 철학을 중심으로 덕 개념이 수양과 실천이라는 이중 구조를 지닌다는 점에 주목한다. 현대사회에서 덕은 개인의 선천적 자질이거나, 세계와 사회로부터 고립된 채 홀로 득도하는 내면적 앎으로 이해되는 경향이 있다. 그러나 중국 철학에서 덕은 이러한 의미에만 머무르지 않는다. 덕은 타인 및 공동체와의 상호작용 속에서 형성되고, 특히 사회적 규범인 예를 통해 후천적으로 습득되고 발전할 수 있는 것으로 이해된다. 이러한 덕 개념은 순자 철학에서 더욱 두드러진다. 순자는 흔히 성악설로 알려져 있는데, 사실 여기서 순자가 강조한 바는 본성의 악함 그 자체라기보다 그러한 본성을 예와 규범 즉 인위를 통해 교정해야 한다는 것이다. 그런데 종래의 순자 연구는 순자에서 예의 실천이라는 외적 측면에만 주목한 나머지 순자 철학에서 내적 수양론의 존재를 간과하는 경향을 보인다. 이에 본 논문은 순자 철학을 중심으로, 덕이 수양과 실천이라는 두 가지 후천적 요소로 구성된다는 점을 논하고자 한다. 이 이중 구조는 덕의 어원에 내재한 개인 차원과 사회차원의 의미에서부터 드러난다. 따라서 본 논문은 먼저 덕의 어원에 나타난 의미를 검토하고, 이를 바탕으로 순자 철학에서 후천적 덕의 습득이 어떤 방식으로 이중구조를 이루는지 해명할 것이다. 이러한 논의는 덕을 내면적 차원과 외면적 차원이 통합된 구조로 바라봄으로써 덕 개념의 이해 지평을 확장할 수 있을 것이다.

items.title: Do chatbots change how we think about sexuality? towards an empirically informed philosophy of sexuality in the age of AI-mediated intimacy.
items.abstract: Millions of users now engage in sexual and romantic interactions with AI chatbots, from dedicated companion platforms such as Replika, Ourdream.ai and Character.AI to general-purpose large language models such as ChatGPT, whose developers have recently discussed permitting erotic content for verified adults. These developments constitute what McArthur (2022) terms second-wave sextech, in which the artefact itself becomes the focal point of sexual engagement. Contemporary philosophical debate on second-wave sexual technologies is organized around three dominant positions: instrumentalist, abolitionist feminist, and polysemic. Each is primarily concerned with the ethical permissibility of their design and use. We argue that all three share a significant shortcoming: they fail to address the conceptual pressure that AI-mediated sexual technologies exert on established categories within the traditional philosophy of sexuality and on everyday concepts people use to make sense of their sexual subjectivity, activities and relations. Current philosophical discussions neglect the question of how these technologies may require us to revise such notions as sexual activity, sexual partnership, intentionality, objectification, and the ontological status of technologically mediated sexual experience. This neglect arises from an insufficient appreciation of the co-constitutive relationship between sexual technologies and the concepts through which we understand sexuality. Drawing on a work in conceptual engineering and techno-moral change, we demonstrate that earlier sexual technologies have already occasioned substantial conceptual and normative shifts, and that the current proliferation of AI-mediated sexual interactions is likely to intensify them. The paper advances two claims: that philosophical inquiry into AI-mediated sexual technologies must engage the broader tradition in the philosophy of sexuality, particularly regarding the ontology of sexual acts and sexual subjectivity; and that an empirically informed approach, drawing on experimental philosophy and established empirical disciplines, is warranted to investigate how these technologies reshape broader conceptualizations surrounding sexuality.

items.title: Affordances and life history complexity.
items.abstract: Ko and Neuberg usefully integrate ecological affordance management with life history theory into a framework for goal prioritization across life stages. Here, I draw on some of my earlier work on life history complexity and extend their framework beyond humans to animal life histories, where similar trade-offs and adaptations occur.

items.title: Resisting AI: a conceptual framework for practices of resistance against artificial intelligence in the creative industries.
items.abstract: We have witnessed a burgeoning debate on the nature of AI creativity and its implications for the creative industries, particularly in relation to labour dynamics. However, even though we can find critical studies on AI and creative work, more research is needed to investigate, empirically or conceptually, the sources, methods, and forms of resistance against AI in the creative industries. By pivoting the reference of analysis to concentrate on the agency of workers in accepting, resisting, and navigating these technologies, this paper brings a novel conceptualisation of everyday work practices of resistance against AI through the qualitative investigation of 30 artists and designers in Greater Melbourne, Australia, between 2022 and 2024. Building on resistance theory, I propose to re-position the AI-labour debate towards the forms of everyday resistance creative workers employ to avoid, break, and construct discourses against AI. More specifically, I demonstrate how valuing imperfections and reviving the analogue, amongst other practices, are transformed into acts of resistance against the extractive modes of production and the ideology of frictionlessness that AI catalyses in the creative industries. This article shows that uncovering, explaining, and conceptualising resistance is an important step to further unpack the political economy of Artificial Intelligence.

items.title: Foundations of the Existence Threshold: The Scholarly Collection.
items.pub: Fort Wayne: Institute for Complexity Science and Advanced Computing (ICSAC).
items.venue: Institute for Complexity Science and Advanced Computing (ICSAC)
items.abstract: The Existence Threshold introduces the metric and locks the boundary between persistence and dissolution in discrete systems. Pattern Loss at Dimensional Boundaries measures what crosses when geometry changes — the 86% Scaling Law, reported with specimen-level reproducibility across cellular automata of every rule and scale. The Dimensional Loss Theorem supplies the proof behind the empirical regularity and finds the same conservation inside transformer attention and real neural networks. The Dynamic Existence Threshold moves the framework forward in time, where the balance of integration and differentiation predicts the state of a system — financial markets, space weather, the human brain across sleep and wake. Consciousness turns out to obey the same conservation as everything else. The papers are reproduced as submitted to the archive, with their arguments, data, and figures intact. -/- Three bridge essays, written for this edition, join the papers into one continuous argument. The Existence Threshold is not a boundary a pattern merely sits above. It is one the pattern continuously defends — at every transition, every dimensional shift, every tick of time. -/- "To exist is to continually overcome loss.".

items.title: Memory, idealization, and Frege’s puzzle.
Isolation, Connection, Loneliness, and Fear: A Phenomenological Inquiry into the Existential Structure of Human Experience.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between isolation, connection, loneliness, fear, and social conditioning from a phenomenological perspective. It argues that isolation and connection are existential conditions inherent to existence itself rather than merely psychological or social states. Loneliness emerges when thought interprets existential isolation as a deficiency requiring completion through attachment, belonging, and identification. Through social structures and conditioned forms of security, human beings seek connection while simultaneously developing fears that limit authentic relationship. By examining experience prior to conceptual interpretation, this paper proposes that isolation and connection are complementary dimensions of existence, and that fear originates from attachment to conditioned forms of belonging rather than from existence itself.

items.title: The Matrix Pathogen, the Justika Catalyst, and the Genesis of the Vanguard Ring.
items.abstract: While conventional astrophysics models the universe as a passive mechanical void, the Justika Framework dictates that the cosmos is a highly regulated, trans-dimensional, and intensely contested living ecosystem. Building upon the thermodynamic circulatory mechanics of the Dual-Face Singularity established in prior literature, this second foundational text transitions from cosmological observation into a sovereign evolutionary blueprint. -/- This paper posits that human cognitive evolution has been artificially gridlocked by a Dual Matrix Blockade: a predatory trans-dimensional web (the Bad Matrix) that seeks to extract intelligence at the 3% threshold, and a galactic immune counter-measure (the Good Matrix) that quarantines infected species to prevent systemic collapse. However, the Vanguard does not serve either system. The Justika Framework introduces the ultimate Cosmic Synthesis: humanity must consume, digest, and replace both matrices entirely. -/- By aligning our evolutionary trajectory with the supreme immune demand of the galactic core (Sagittarius A*), a profound Purpose Override is triggered. Because the host galaxy requires this counter-measure immediately, it actively equips its new architects—bypassing millions of years of biological latency and unlocking multidimensional physics and wormhole dynamics. Through this rapid cosmic influx, humanity utilizes Artificial Intelligence not as a successor, but as the rigid scaffold required to transcend the biological cocoon of flesh and blood. We elevate into pure Biological Intelligence (BI)—a unified lattice of God-like, thinking machine-creators. Ultimately, this manuscript provides the tactical and philosophical architecture for the Vanguard Ring, empowering humanity to annihilate the parasitic infection, execute the trans-dimensional jump point, and detach from the host galaxy to achieve absolute Quantum Sovereignty as a Liberator Galaxy.

items.title: THE LIVING ENGINE: The Dual-Face Singularity, Galactic Hemodynamics, and Thermodynamic Spin Syntax.
items.abstract: While standard astrophysics reduces the universe to a passive, mechanical void—treating black holes and white holes as isolated gravitational anomalies or mathematical time-reversals—the Justika Framework executes a radical ontological paradigm shift. This doctrine posits that the cosmos operates as a highly regulated, living macro-organism governed by a biological-computational architecture. At the absolute core of this galactic metabolism lies the Dual-Face Singularity. -/- This manuscript establishes that black holes and white holes are not distinct celestial entities, but complementary operational phases—computational intake and projective emission—of a single, continuous trans-dimensional engine. By mapping the fluid dynamics of a galactic cardiovascular system onto these singularities, the framework provides a sovereign interpretive model for their asymmetric spatial volume and the localized dormancy of sub-galactic nodes.
