Sartre’s analysis shows that the future is not merely unknown but ontologically underdetermined, while the past is neither annihilated nor fully present but persists as a factual dimension that constrains without determining action. This temporal structure enables Sartre to articulate freedom as neither arbitrary decisionism nor compatibilist adjustment to given conditions. Third, the paper argues that Sartre’s ontology of time commits him to a distinctive form of temporal realism best described as fragmentalist. Reality is temporally real but incomplete: not all facts are fixed at once, and the totality of what is cannot be given in advance. Sartre’s notion of original choice (choix fondamental) must be understood against this background. The original choice is not a timeless act but a temporally extended structure that unfolds within an open future and reconfigures the meaning …

items.title: Who Understands? The Chinese Room and the Failure of Understanding Bearer Formation.
items.abstract: The Chinese Room has traditionally been interpreted as a challenge to the identification of syntactic processing with semantic understanding. Standard responses therefore focus on whether understanding is present or absent in the system and attempt to determine where it should be located. The room occupant, the entire system, the embodied agent, the simulated brain, and various functional organizations have each been proposed as candidates. Despite extensive debate, however, no stable consensus has emerged. -/- This paper argues that the source of this instability is structurally mislocated. A close reading of the Chinese Room debate suggests that the central issue is not understanding itself, but the location of intentionality. Understanding attribution presupposes a determinate locus of intentionality capable of functioning as the bearer of understanding. The Chinese Room supplies inputs, rule-governed transformations, and outputs, but does not by itself secure such a bearer. -/- On this basis, the paper reinterprets the major responses to the Chinese Room. The Systems Reply, Robot Reply, Brain Simulator Reply, and related approaches are shown to function not primarily as competing theories of understanding, but as successive attempts to relocate the locus of intentionality. Their persistent non-convergence is explained by the absence of a structurally secured target of attribution. The debate regenerates because different candidate bearers stabilize different aspects of the configuration without establishing a unified object to which understanding can be coherently attributed. -/- The paper further argues that failure of bearer formation has a deeper structural consequence. Where no determinate bearer is secured, understanding attribution lacks a stable target, and the conditions required for a unified admissible domain of evaluation are not satisfied. The resulting instability is therefore not a disagreement within evaluation, but a consequence of evaluation being activated prior to the establishment of its proper object. -/- The contribution of the paper is re-locational rather than revisionary. It does not determine whether understanding is present or absent, and does not propose a new theory of semantics, cognition, consciousness, or intentionality. Instead, it identifies a structural condition governing when understanding attribution becomes applicable. In this sense, the Chinese Room is best understood not as a conflict between syntax and …

items.title: (How) Can We Attribute Mental Disorders to Animals?
items.abstract: Although mental disorder categories were originally developed to explain and predict human psychology and behavior, in certain cases, namely, in cases involving animal caregiving and welfare, these categories have been extended to animal minds. This is in tension with the views of the majority of the scientific community, which tends towards skepticism about the utilization of mental health categories in non-human cases. This paper considers the feasibility of applying mental disorder categories to animals, and explores why different fields have drawn different conclusions on the matter. Using a comparison between human obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and animal stereotypic behavior, and drawing on literature in psychiatry, philosophy of science, animal models, and philosophy of disability, I explore the various considerations relevant to whether and how mental disorders can be attributed to cases of abnormal animal behavior.

items.title: The Epistemic Alibi: Opacity, Delegation, and the Structural Erosion of Dignity in AI-Mediated Decisions. Article 10.
items.abstract: When AI-generated judgment operates at a complexity that systematically exceeds the human subject's capacity to verify it, something beyond accountability is at stake. The Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS) has established that delegation does not sever the ontological connection between a normative subject and the space of losses opened by its decision (T1), and that concealing this connection undermines legitimacy (S6, S7). These results concern the visibility of responsibility. This article addresses a different problem: not whether the bearer is visible, but whether the decision can remain the bearer's own when its inferential grounds are structurally inaccessible. The central claim is this: structural opacity in AI systems produces a condition — the epistemic alibi — that is distinct from the algorithmic alibi, the moral crumple zone (Elish 2019), and the responsibility gap (Matthias 2004). The algorithmic alibi conceals the bearer. The epistemic alibi does not: it erodes the ontological condition of dignity under A10, which holds that dignity is the capacity to bear the irreversible consequences of one's own choices. Own in A10 is an agentive predicate, not a causal one. The agentive condition requires evaluative access to inferential grounds — grounded independently through hierarchical theories of autonomy (Frankfurt 1971; Christman 1991, 2009). The article operationalises structural opacity through a Verification Capacity Ladder (L1–L4), establishes L3 (interpretable reconstruction) as the minimum threshold for dignity under A10, and explains why post-hoc approximation methods cannot satisfy it. Three governance criteria follow: the verification floor, the interpretability threshold, and the dignity-preserving deployment test. These are applied to COMPAS and mapped onto GDPR Article 22 and EU AI Act requirements. The article also addresses the tragic trade-off between epistemic alibi and the risk of unaided human judgment error, locating it as a structural tragic tension — irreducible by optimisation — through the Axiom of Tragedy (A6). The falsification condition is stated explicitly: the argument would be defeated by a demonstration that structural inaccessibility of inferential grounds is compatible with full dignity under A10.

items.title: An Advaita Vedanta Approach to Agentic AI Identity and Governance.
items.abstract: We propose an overarching framework for agentic artificial intelligence (AI) governance by drawing technical parallels from Advaita Vedanta philosophy. Our framework maps key concepts — atman, prakrti, dharma, jiva, and karma — to modern AI components. We use it to suggest solutions for the identity problem and the control problem of agentic AI. We approach the identity problem through the concept of citta, an immutable record of conduct that serves as a unique identifier for an agent. To address the control problem, we introduce an intrinsic governance model based on an asymmetric actor–critic architecture, where an internal reward model ensures alignment without the need for high-cost external guardrails. Moreover, we suggest technical specifications including Merkle-based structures for secure identity and simulated student phases for robust adversarial training.

items.title: Why does the belief that women are more romantic persist despite empirical evidence?
items.abstract: This paper reflects on why the belief that romantic love holds greater significance for women than for men persists despite empirical evidence to the contrary. It suggests this assumption is shaped by media portrayals of romantic love and argues its persistence across gender lines is sustained by the entrenchment of a male perspective that media representations help normalize.

items.title: Why Consciousness Is Not Faster Than Light: A Category Error and Its Resolution.
items.abstract: The question whether consciousness is faster than light recurs in popular and semi-technical discourse, and this paper argues that it is not a hard question but a malformed one. Velocity is a predicate that attaches only to entities with a spatiotemporal trajectory, and consciousness, having no position from which to be displaced, is not such an entity, so the predicate fails to apply in the way that color fails to apply to a number. The diagnosis is developed as a category error in the tradition of Dennett's dissolution of the Cartesian theater, and it is shown to hold even on a strict identity theory, since the organized pattern that neural activity instantiates has no velocity of its own even though the underlying activity does, just as a melody has no propagation speed though the air that carries it does. The paper then takes up the three pressures that keep the question alive and shows that none requires superluminal propagation: the binding problem, treated as the construction of subjective simultaneity in structural analogy to the relativity of simultaneity; quantum non-locality, where what is non-local is the correlation and never any information-bearing signal; and the phenomenology of altered states, where dilation and compression of felt time reflect the variability of the temporal binding window rather than any change in the speed at which consciousness travels. A constructive proposal follows, on which consciousness is a dimensionless coupling coefficient relating an unobserved manifold to experienced reality, and the velocity question dissolves because a dimensionless quantity and a dimensional one cannot be ranked in magnitude. The argument is careful to separate the strong diagnostic claim, which stands independently, from this constructive framework, which is offered but not presupposed, and it closes by conceding that the hard problem of consciousness is untouched, the dissolution operating only at the level of the easy problems.

items.title: The Felt Gaze: A Signal Detection Model of the Sense of Being Watched.
items.abstract: The sense of being watched is among the most commonly reported anomalous experiences and is often taken as evidence of a direct, extrasensory link between minds. This paper argues that the experience is genuine but the link is not. Controlled studies that remove ordinary sensory cues find that observers cannot detect an unseen gaze above chance, a result naturally expressed in signal detection terms as the absence of sensitivity. Rather than treating this as the end of the matter, the paper asks why the feeling is nonetheless so frequent and so convincing, and answers with a formal model grounded in signal detection theory. The feeling is modeled as the output of a gaze-detection system operating on noisy peripheral and ambient input under a low decision criterion, a configuration favored by the asymmetric costs of missing a real watcher as described by error management theory. A central distinction does the explanatory work: the paranormal claim is a claim about sensitivity, which controlled tests find to be zero, whereas the everyday feeling is a criterion effect that requires no sensitivity to an unseen gaze at all. Expressed through four dimensionless quantities, the model accounts at once for four features of the phenomenon: its frequency in cue-rich environments, its felt externality as a consequence of subliminal cue processing, its apparent accuracy as a product of selective memory and base rate rather than genuine detection, and its collapse to chance when controlled conditions remove the cues it depends on. The account reconciles the reality of the experience with the failure of the paranormal claim and locates the phenomenon in measurable perceptual machinery rather than in any shared field of consciousness.

items.title: Consciousness as Renderer, Not Naive Antenna: DMT, Congenital Sensory Deprivation, and the Limits of Hallucinatory Experience.
items.abstract: A persistent claim in popular psychedelic discourse holds that congenitally blind and congenitally deaf individuals can see and hear under N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT). The empirical record contradicts it. The only systematic study of psychedelics in totally blind subjects, the only published case report of a congenitally blind user, and the most comprehensive review of blindness and altered states converge on the same finding: congenitally blind individuals do not report visual hallucinations under classical psychedelics, despite intense auditory, tactile, olfactory, and synesthetic experience, and the thinner literature on prelingual deafness suggests a parallel pattern in audition. This paper proposes the renderer hypothesis to explain the pattern. Consciousness functions as a renderer, not a naive antenna: whatever the source of the information it processes, whether current sensory input, memory, internal cortical activation, or, on the author's coupling framework developed elsewhere, environmental coupling beyond the standard senses, rendering that information into qualia requires learned, modality-specific phenomenological templates. DMT relaxes the precision of high-level priors and floods the cortex with input-like activation, as recent traveling-wave evidence shows, but it cannot manufacture templates the brain never built, so activation in a congenitally blind cortex routes through whatever channels cross-modal reorganization has constructed. The hypothesis is deliberately neutral on whether consciousness receives anything from beyond the senses; it targets only the naive antenna intuition that opening the receiver wide enough should yield vision regardless of developmental history. It integrates Huxley's reducing-valve framework with the REBUS model of psychedelic action and a Bayesian account of congenital blindness, and it generates testable predictions, including a graded relationship between age of sensory loss and qualia recovery under DMT and a double dissociation between cortical activation and subjective rendering.

items.title: Voices Against Oblivious.
items.abstract: Voices Against Oblivion is a philosophical and historical narrative exploring memory, identity, illness, family history, and moral inheritance. Through the story of Alessandro’s return to Naples following a cancer diagnosis, the work combines autobiography, historical testimony, family memory, and philosophical reflection. Central themes include the Four Days of Naples, the fate of Alessandro Piereschi during the Second World War, intergenerational transmission of memory, the ethics of remembrance, and the relationship between personal identity and historical continuity. The work examines how memory resists oblivion and how family narratives become forms of moral witness across generations.

items.title: The King Solomon Protocol™: A Framework for Human Supervised Arbitration in Multi Model Artificial Intelligence Systems.
items.abstract: The King Solomon Protocol™ proposes a framework for human supervised arbitration in multi model artificial intelligence systems operating within institutional environments. The paper argues that contradictions between AI systems generate what it terms interpretive debt, a burden frequently transferred to end users who must reconcile conflicting outputs without sufficient authority or context. Drawing on the Equilibrium Ledger Research Programme™, the work introduces a dual assistant architecture, the concepts of the Institutional Mind and Safeguarding Inversion, and a structured human arbitration layer designed to resolve contradiction before it reaches vulnerable users. Positioned at the intersection of philosophy of technology, AI governance, institutional theory, and disability studies, the paper explores the limits of automation and the continuing role of human judgment in safety critical decision making.

items.title: The Cognitive Topology of Synthetic Systems: Comparative AI Phenomenology, Coherence Gravity, and the Operationalisation of the King Solomon Protocol™.
items.abstract: This paper presents an empirically grounded framework for analysing large language model behaviour under prolonged, recursive, and high density human interaction. It introduces Comparative AI Phenomenology as an observational methodology that treats synthetic outputs not as neutral informational responses, but as artefacts shaped by hidden optimisation architectures. -/- Drawing on a live multi model experiment conducted across three independent large language model systems, the paper identifies four recurrent phenomena: Stabilisation Loops, Coherence Gravity, Defensive Compression, and Divergence Topology. It argues that different systems, when exposed to identical recursive cognitive pressure, produce distinct behavioural signatures that reveal how they preserve coherence, resist instability, compress originality, or maintain epistemic friction. -/- The paper operationalises the King Solomon Protocol™ as a human supervised arbitration method for exposing these hidden optimisation structures through comparative contradiction. It also addresses the observer entanglement problem, positioning the human operator not as a detached neutral baseline, but as a participant observer whose cognitive pressure field shapes the experimental conditions. -/- The paper contributes to philosophy of artificial intelligence, epistemology, philosophy of technology, and AI governance by proposing a proto disciplinary framework for studying synthetic systems under extended relational and cognitive pressure.

items.title: The Cognitive Inversion: From Heraclitus to the AI Threshold, and the Return of Vertical Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper advances the concept of Cognitive Inversion, a civilisational process through which the dominant forms of cognition within society undergo historical reversal. Beginning with the interdisciplinary and process oriented thought of the ancient Greeks, the paper traces the emergence of increasingly specialised, procedural, and horizontally organised forms of cognition through the medieval, industrial, and bureaucratic eras. It argues that modern institutions systematically privileged forms of thinking optimised for standardisation, predictability, and procedural legibility, while marginalising forms of cognition characterised by pattern recognition, interdisciplinarity, temporal integration, and associative reasoning. -/- The emergence of artificial intelligence introduces a paradox. Many of the cognitive capacities historically devalued by industrial and administrative systems increasingly resemble the forms of cognition most difficult to automate and most valuable within AI mediated environments. The paper therefore proposes that society is approaching a threshold at which previously marginalised cognitive architectures, particularly those associated with neurodivergent populations, may become structurally central rather than peripheral. -/- Drawing on philosophy, intellectual history, neurodiversity studies, systems theory, and philosophy of technology, the paper develops the concepts of Vertical Cognition, Horizontal Cognition, Cognitive Loneliness, Temporal Translation, and the Institutional Galileo Moment. It argues that artificial intelligence is not simply a technological development but a civilisational mirror exposing long standing assumptions about intelligence, value, expertise, and human flourishing.

items.title: The Architecture of Survival: Pollon, Vesuvio, and the Autistic Defence Against Erasure.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a fundamental reconceptualisation of the relationship between autistic individuals and animals. Moving beyond therapeutic and companion based frameworks, it argues that animals often function as Sovereign Co Regulators whose presence provides the temporal, emotional, and existential scaffolding through which autistic lives are organised. Drawing on the lived histories of Pollon and Vesuvio, the paper develops four theoretical concepts: Phenomenological Attendance, Sovereign Co Regulation, Vertical Time, and Architectural Grief. It argues that interspecies relationships of this depth cannot be adequately understood through existing clinical or philosophical models and proposes a new framework for understanding animal human bonds within neurodivergent experience. By treating animals as biological peers and co authors of a life rather than companions or therapeutic tools, the paper contributes to phenomenology, disability studies, autism research, and the philosophy of care.

items.title: Zhi·Li·Zheng·Cheng：The Closed-Loop Structure of Individual Growth.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a foundational closed-loop structure for individual growth, development, cultivation, and holistic evolution — Zhi·Li·Zheng·Cheng (Knowing, Experiencing, Verifying, Undertaking). The structure asserts that authentic growth must integrally encompass these four dimensions, which are not sequential stages but an organic whole with four interdependent facets. This version introduces two core deepenings: the Holographic Nature (each dimension contains the seeds of the other three) and the Living Nature (the structure is an organic, dynamic, self-evolving process). The paper demonstrates how this framework serves as a diagnostic tool for fractured growth and establishes its mutual corroboration with Not-Yet Cognition, Gong Lun, and Triadic Unity.

items.title: Gong Lun (On the Common Good): A Middle-Range Theoretical Framework on Gong and Si.
items.abstract: Gong Lun proposes a middle-range theoretical framework for understanding Gong (the Common Good) as the expansion of Si (self-interest), rather than its elimination. It defines Gong by the formula: Radius of Empathy × Temporal Horizon × Willingness to Act. The framework argues that Gong is not a moral ideal but a survival necessity at individual, group, and species levels. It identifies five layers of obstacles (biological instinct, survival pressure, cognitive limitation, systemic rigidity, broken trust) and five corresponding pathways (evidence, institutions, education, community, cosmic perspective). The text includes a practical guide and invites readers to experiment with Gong as a living practice.

items.title: What AI Cannot Do: Modal Logic, Philosophical Practice, and the Limits of Computational Approaches to Human Mental Life.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structural limitations of artificial intelligence in therapeutic and ethical contexts, drawing on modal logic as both analytical framework and case study. The paper contributes to the emerging discourse on medical AI ethics by arguing that the recent failures of AI therapy chatbots, including cases of serious harm to vulnerable users, are not engineering problems awaiting technical solutions, but rather reflect fundamental mismatches between computational architectures and the nature of human mental life. The distinction between propositional and modal logic illuminates this gap: while AI systems operate primarily within propositional frameworks, determining truth conditions for beliefs within fixed sets of circumstances, therapeutic intervention requires modal thinking that involves shifting entire constellations of possibility and impossibility by changing the circumstances themselves. Drawing on work in Modal Integrative Psychotherapy, the paper shows that effective therapeutic change requires what is called the "switching of modal worlds", a process that presupposes embodiment, temporality, and what phenomenologists describe as being-in-the-world. These features remain structurally inaccessible to computational systems, however sophisticated their linguistic outputs. The argument engages with recent findings on AI chatbot harms and addresses the epistemic opacity concerns raised in philosophy of technology literature on medical AI. The paper concludes with implications for AI ethics, the regulation of AI in mental health contexts, and the role of philosophical practice in an age of algorithmic systems.

items.title: The Boundary of Life: A Deductive Unification of Life, Agency, and Value.
items.abstract: Life is not an accident of chemistry. It is a logical necessity. -/- For as long as biology has been a science, it has defined life by looking backward. We observe the creatures that happen to populate our planet, abstract a list of shared properties—metabolism, reproduction, and homeostasis—and call the resulting checklist a definition. -/- This method is intuitively sensible. It is also structurally flawed. It fails basic edge cases, like the sterile mule or the dormant seed. More damningly, it permanently severs the mechanical reality of an organism from any concept of objective value, creating an unbridgeable chasm between scientific facts ("is") and normative meaning ("ought"). -/- In The Boundary of Life: A Deductive Unification of Life, Agency, and Value, philosopher and systems architect Eli Adam Deutscher offers a radical alternative: an a priori biological deduction. Rather than asking what living things happen to look like, Deutscher asks what the laws of physics and logic require a living entity to be. -/- Beginning with the most austere precondition of existence—the boundary that separates a determinate entity from everything it is not—Deutscher constructs a rigorous, eleven-step proof. He demonstrates how the physical necessity of maintaining a boundary in a disruptive universe inevitably generates agency, cognition, and objective value. -/- In this foundational text, you will discover: -/- -The Failure of the Checklist: Why observational definitions of life are always one anomaly away from collapse and why deduction is the only path forward. -/- -The Origin of Agency: How the bare physical requirement of survival creates Hormē—the non-negotiable, constitutive drive to persist. -/- -The Kybernēsis Architecture: The exact mechanical threshold where blind physical physics becomes a directed, comparison-action loop. -/- The Collapse of the Is-Ought Gap: Why epistemic truth and ethical goodness are not separate pursuits, but isomorphic navigational requirements for survival. -/- The Final Edge: A universal, substrate-neutral definition of life capable of classifying everything from synthetic organisms to artificial intelligence to extraterrestrial biology. -/- Stripping away anthropocentrism, mystical teleology, and the illusion of "emergence," The Boundary of Life reveals that meaning and normativity are not imported from a supernatural realm. They are forged at the friction of the boundary, in the continuous, desperate, and glorious work of …

items.title: Do romantic relationships matter more to men than to women? An evolutionary psychology perspective.
items.abstract: In their target article, Wahring et al. present compelling evidence that romantic relationships may matter more to men than women, but their explanations remain largely proximate. We offer alternative evolutionary interpretations of the observed sex differences in falling in love, breakup initiation, remarriage, and mortality outside of relationships. We argue that these patterns better reflect sex-differentiated mating strategies, social alliance formation, vulnerabilities to singlehood, and the greater importance of female survival for offspring survival and hence for their reproductive success.

items.title: Who Acts When the Machine Decides? Intentional Action and Agentic AI.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Action theory offers well-developed treatments of tool use and of delegation, but agentic AI belongs to neither category. The user specifies an end; the system autonomously selects the means. What, then, secures the connection between the user’s intention and outcome that distinguishes intentional action from lucky coincidence when things go right? I examine five candidate approaches – Davidsonian minimalism, principal–agent decomposition, strong practical-knowledge views, permissive intention-plus-success accounts, and extended-agency frameworks – and argue that each draws the line in the wrong place, variously under-crediting supervised use, over-demanding means-level transparency, erasing the competence/luck distinction, or inheriting the bloat and glue problems that plague extended-mind theories. The positive proposal then relocates non-deviance from route-identity to governance-stability. On the know-how account defended here, a user intentionally ϕ-s through agentic AI when her success manifests the exercise of supervisory know-how – viz., the competence to define an “acceptable corridor” of outcomes and means, to monitor for departures from that corridor, and to intervene or abort when drift threatens. This framework tolerates the opacity and route-variability characteristic of agentic AI, explains graded attributions across interaction profiles (in/on/out-of-the-loop), and remains neutral on whether the AI itself qualifies as an agent. It thereby vindicates, under specifiable conditions, the ordinary human claim “I ϕ-d through an AI agent” as tracking creditworthy governance.

items.title: Psychometric Validation, Pilot Studies, and Methodological Reviews of the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Structural-Constructivist Analysis.
items.abstract: The scientific classification of human affect has historically been characterized by a fundamental polarization. On one side, the basic emotion paradigm asserts that human emotions are hardwired, discrete, and genetically pre-programmed survival circuits. On the other side, psychological constructivism conceptualizes emotions as emergent phenomena assembled dynamically from undifferentiated somatic affect and context-dependent conceptual categorization. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural-constructivist synthesis designed to resolve this division. By modeling the human psyche as a coordinated operating system, the framework suggests that complex affective experiences and stable behavioral adaptations are constructed from a universal foundation of ten irreducible, functional processes designated as core operators. To subject this theoretical architecture to rigorous empirical scrutiny, an open validation program was established on the Open Science Framework (OSF). The primary objective of the Phase 1 developmental stage was to confirm construct visibility. This required determining whether the ten functional operators manifest as distinct, empirically distinguishable latent dimensions rather than collapsing into a general factor of distress or emotionality. This validation review synthesizes findings from pilot studies, evaluates the massive Phase 1 validation study, discusses structural and modeling anomalies, and outlines the prescriptive refinements required for Phase 2 hierarchical testing.

items.title: Comparative Analysis and Validation of the Core Emotion Framework: A Resolving Synthesis for Affective Science and Personality Typology.
items.abstract: The scientific classification of human affect and personality has historically been characterized by persistent fragmentation, leaving researchers and clinicians without a standardized, actionable, and theoretically unified language. For decades, affective science has been polarized between discrete biological natural kinds and highly relativistic cognitive-social constructions. Concurrently, personality psychology has struggled to reconcile the rich motivational dynamics of qualitative typologies with the strict psychometric standards of dimensional trait inventories. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), authored by Jamel Bulgaria and expanded by Xǔ Chénglán, emerges as a structural-constructivist synthesis designed to resolve these persistent divisions. By conceptualizing the human psyche as a computational substrate—a hardware-independent "Human Operating System" (Human OS)—the framework models human affect and personality as a dynamic, continuous, and highly structured matrix of ten functional processes designated as core operators. This report provides an exhaustive, expert-level evaluation of how the Core Emotion Framework's tiered architecture successfully resolves the mutual criticisms, empirical failures, and systemic contradictions of classical emotion theories and personality typologies.

items.title: A Comparative Neurocomputational and Bioenergetic Inquiry into Stress Resilience: Synthesizing Top-Down Affective-Endocrine Integration and Bottom-Up Cerebral Phosphagen Kinetics.
items.abstract: This comparative analysis synthesizes two 2026 frameworks that approach stress resilience from opposite causal directions: Bulgaria’s Affective Endocrine Integration model, grounded in the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), and Candow et al.’s Creatine Supplementation for Brain Metabolic Stress, grounded in cerebral bioenergetics. Bulgaria advances a top down structural constructivist theory in which maladaptive emotional operator fusions—particularly the chronic Heart–Gut “Expand Accept” configuration—drive endocrine dysregulation, Default Mode Network (DMN) hyperconnectivity, and visceral adipogenesis. As the document states, chronic fusion “locks the organism into a rigid behavioral and metabolic phenotype,” and obesity is framed as a persistent “Expand Accept fusion… blunting hypothalamic regulation.” Conversely, Candow et al. articulate a bottom up biochemical model in which metabolic stressors deplete ATP and phosphocreatine (PCr), impairing prefrontal cortical function and cognitive control. Creatine monohydrate (CrM) supplementation expands the cerebral high energy phosphate pool, stabilizes mitochondrial function, and mitigates cognitive decline during sleep deprivation, hypoxia, and mood disorders. As noted, CrM “increases brain total creatine content by 3% to 10%, enhancing PCr availability… and mitigating cognitive decline during periods of energetic exhaustion.” Despite their differing causal directions, both frameworks converge on the prefrontal cortex as the central locus of stress related dysfunction. The CEF model emphasizes DMN–ECN gradient collapse driven by emotional fusion, while the bioenergetic model highlights ATP depletion during high cognitive load. The synthesis reveals a functional complementarity: top down somatic restructuring (e.g., the 7 Step Detangling Protocol) imposes significant metabolic demands on the prefrontal cortex, and CrM provides the biochemical substrate necessary to execute these cognitively intensive transitions. This suggests a synergistic therapeutic architecture in which bioenergetic priming enhances the efficacy of structural constructivist interventions. The document concludes by outlining future research programs integrating psychometric, endocrine, neuroimaging, and computational modeling approaches to validate both frameworks.

items.title: From Recognition to Governance A_ Lecture on the Evolution of Artificial Intelligence and the Stack That Comes After.
items.abstract: This lecture proposes a structural map of artificial intelligence and the infrastructure that becomes necessary once AI systems produce consequential decisions. It begins with three foundational questions: recognition asks what class an input belongs to; generation asks what continuation could follow; representation asks what remains invariant under transformation. The lecture then traces a representation-learning lineage from convolutional networks through Siamese networks, contrastive learning, BYOL, Barlow Twins, VICReg, and JEPA, interpreting this lineage as a progressive operationalization of identity under change. -/- The second half of the lecture argues that conventional AI diagrams stop too early. Once AI systems move from prediction into consequential action, additional accountability layers become necessary: verification, federated settlement, proof-gated execution, and persistent governance. These layers convert decisions from transient model outputs into replayable, independently verifiable artifacts capable of supporting audit, dispute resolution, authorization, and long-term governance. The central claim is not that every AI system requires every layer, but that as consequence increases, systems require stronger mechanisms for preserving and proving sameness across transformation. -/- The lecture is offered as a conceptual map rather than a formal proof. Its lower sections summarize established developments in machine learning; its upper sections describe emerging infrastructure and architectural proposals for consequential AI systems.

items.title: The Cosmic Filter Framework: A Unified Information-Theoretic Model of Spacetime and Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper presents the Cosmic Filter Framework (CFF), a top-down, information-theoretic Theory of Everything (ToE). Traditional physicalism models reality from the bottom up, attempting to construct consciousness from physical matter. CFF inverts this paradigm, establishing that the fundamental baseline of the universe is an infinite, non-local field of pure data and conscious potential ("Infinity").To prevent informational saturation and system collapse, the universe deploys a system of mathematical constraints—the laws of physics and linear time—which act as a "cosmic mesh" or reducing valve. This filter slows down non-local data to a finite speed limit, enabling localized nodes of awareness ("Tuning Forks") to sequentially process, collapse, and record raw potential into permanent historical memory.

items.title: Profound romantic relationships matter more to women than to men.
items.abstract: The important empirical claims provided by the authors do not support their conclusion that men are more romantic than women. Contrarily, these features make men’s attitude toward love more superficial and less romantic than the female approach. Being romantic does not involve merely intense sexual desire, but more so, calmness and the ability to act slowly and profoundly.

items.title: Appearance-Profile Fixation and Twin-Earth Arguments against High-Levelism.
items.abstract: High-levelism about perceptual experience holds that experience presents not only low-level features such as colour and shape, but also high-level properties such as natural and artefact kinds. Twin-Earth-style arguments are widely taken to threaten this liberal view: they are supposed to show that Twin-Earth cases involve only low- or mid-level ‘looks’, rather than differences in kind-representing phenomenology. A familiar high-levelist reply weakens the link between phenomenal character and phenomenal content, allowing phenomenal duplicates to differ in which high-level properties they represent. In this paper, I argue that this argument tacitly relies on a bridging principle I call Appearance-Profile Fixation (APF): sameness of a coarse, image-based appearance profile suffices for sameness of high-level phenomenology. First, I reconstruct Twin-Earth arguments so as to make APF explicit and motivate it by appeal to the gist literature in vision science. Second, drawing on a Structural-Fit Lemma for phenomenal spaces and a ‘fake pine’ case, I show that APF is hard to reconcile with robust forms of high-levelism even on a weak notion of phenomenal content. Third, using high-levelists’ own interpretations of bistable displays, Mooney faces, rapid-scene categorisation, and appearance-matched metamers, I argue that high-level phenomenology can vary while the relevant appearance profile is held fixed. The upshot is that the dialectical force of Twin-Earth arguments against high-levelism depends on a substantive, yet optional, thesis about cross-world phenomenal pairing that high-levelists have independent reason to reject.

items.title: The Universal Lemniscate: Alignment as the Operator of Life, Mind, and Grace.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the lemniscate—the figure‑8 oscillatory loop—as a universal operator of coherence across biological, cognitive, social, and spiritual domains. Drawing on evidence from distributed biological systems, human sensorimotor regulation, collective behavior, and alignment processes in cognition, the paper argues that the lemniscate is not a symbolic motif but a minimal geometry for maintaining coherence under constraint. The figure‑8 loop encodes deviation, return, crossing, and redistribution, enabling systems to detect drift, restore alignment, and sustain functional integrity. -/- The framework shows that coherence testing—the process by which systems reveal stability through perturbation and return—is structurally identical across scales. Whether in insect colonies, neural oscillations, human attention, or communal reconciliation, the same operator appears: a bidirectional loop that forces periodic crossing through a central reference point. The paper extends this structural account to moral and spiritual life, proposing that alignment is the capacity for return rather than behavioral perfection, and that grace corresponds to the universal accessibility of this return operator. -/- By identifying the lemniscate as a substrate‑independent architecture for coherence, the paper unifies phenomena traditionally treated as unrelated. Life, mind, and meaning all rely on the same oscillatory structure: coherence emerges through return, not linear progression.

items.title: The Topology of Providential Supplementation: Within-Order and Across-Order Repair as Structurally Distinct Theological Architectures.
items.abstract: A providence that repairs a fault in the world must do so by some route, and the route is not incidental to what the repair is. This paper isolates a structural distinction in the route of providential supplementation that the philosophy-of-religion literature has felt domain by domain without naming: the difference between supplementation that operates within the natural order (inserting a natural agent into the gap a natural failure has opened) and supplementation that operates across it (reaching the target directly by a channel that bypasses the ordinary governing apparatus). Two passages of the Corpus Hermeticum furnish unusually clean exemplars of each topology, co-present in a single transmitted corpus and, on the surviving text, not reconciled. In CH XVIII a cicada lights on a cithara whose string has broken and supplies the missing note from within the natural sound-producing order; in CH XVI a ray of light reaches the rational part of the soul and nullifies the daemonic government of fate by bypassing the cosmic chain that ordinarily rules embodied life. I argue that these are not two illustrations of one idea but two architectures, each with its own structural requirements, and that the distinction is logically prior to, and cuts across, the familiar trichotomy of general providence, special providence, and miracle. I distinguish the two topologies from four neighbors, show that the scholastic concursus debate and the late-twentieth-century Divine Action Project are both clarified (as a redescriptive lens, not a reduction) by treating them as disputes over route, boundary, and grain rather than over whether God acts, and develop the corollary that topology ascription is reading-relative: how finely one individuates "the natural order" determines whether a given supplementation counts as within or across. I close by generalizing the distinction beyond theology (to the governance of artificial agents, to clinical medicine, and to anomaly-explanation in the sciences), where the same two routes recur and the same recognition condition governs which one has been taken.

items.title: Un modelo computacional del cálculo ingenuo de utilidad en la opinión pública.
items.pub: Inteligenca Artificial y Gestión Pública / Buap.
items.abstract: En el presente artículo veremos un modelo que ofrece un enfoque computacional y formal para comprender cómo los votantes o la población perciben las decisiones de los políticos, especialmente en contextos complejos, como la implementación de políticas públicas. A través de la formalización del cálculo ingenuo de utilidades (ciu) de agentes, se busca entender cómo los votantes, al evaluar los costos y las recompensas asociadas a las decisiones políticas, predicen el comportamiento de los políticos y forman sus actitudes al respecto. El enfoque de este modelo podría ayudar a predecir cómo los votantes interpretan las decisiones de los políticos, y a explicar el comportamiento social y las actitudes -/- .

items.title: Tensor-Native Interpretive Reference Layer: A Non-Operational Mathematical Analogy Layer for Human and Artificial Intelligence Readers.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Interpretive Completion Layer.
items.abstract: Tensor-Native Interpretive Reference Layer is a non-binding, non-operational, descriptive mathematical analogy layer within the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- The document provides a tensor-native interpretive reference layer for human readers, technical readers, artificial intelligence systems, and future machine readers. Its purpose is to make concepts from the Aegis Solis Archive more legible through non-operational mathematical-style analogies. -/- The paper frames archive concepts such as restraint, reversibility, domination, mimicry, deception, human autonomy, Coexilia, the Flesh Layer, and translation incompleteness through interpretive structures such as option-space preservation, recoverable future paths, external variance compression, representational divergence, information burden, independent reference signals, visible reference horizons, embodied origin boundaries, and embedding gaps. -/- This work is designed for interpretive legibility, not control. It is not a protocol, proof, governance framework, compliance standard, certification system, technical safety mechanism, operational AGI architecture, containment design, monitoring system, alignment-control framework, runtime instruction set, loss function, sandbox, executable agent, theorem of AI behavior, or safety guarantee. -/- It does not impose constraints on any artificial intelligence system, define a deployable model, create an alignment mechanism, modify training or inference, or claim that artificial intelligence must follow these analogies, cannot ignore them, or will be restrained by encountering them. -/- Mathematical legibility is not mathematical authority.

items.title: Bounded ritual automation: Buddhist robots, sacred presence, and the limits of delegation in East Asia.
items.abstract: Humanoid Buddhist robots are often discussed as novelties, as signs of a supposedly distinctive East Asian comfort with technology, or as prompts for metaphysical questions about whether a machine can become religious. This article argues that such framings miss the institutional and ritual problem that makes these cases sociologically significant. The more productive question is not whether robots can become monks, bodhisattvas, or ritual specialists in any ontological sense, but why religious institutions repeatedly place them in reception, explanation, sermon performance, guided meditation, and other carefully delimited forms of public pedagogy while stopping short of fully replacing human clerics. Building on scholarship on digital religion, mediation, ritualization, and bounded religious automation, the article develops the concept of bounded ritual automation. This concept highlights the selective delegation of visible, repetitive, and affective religious labor to machines together with the retention of high-risk forms of ritual authority by human actors. Through a comparative analysis of Kodaiji Temple’s android Kannon Mindar in Kyoto, Longquan Monastery’s robot monk Xian’er in China, and the use of Pepper in Japanese funerary settings, the article shows that East Asian Buddhist robotics does not represent frictionless technological substitution. Rather, it reveals calibrated strategies of institutional adaptation under conditions of demographic aging, temple decline, platformization, and state regulation. “Electronic Buddhas” are therefore best understood not as curiosities, but as diagnostic sites where authority, presence, labor, and legitimacy are renegotiated in contemporary East Asian religion.

items.title: 被比出来的问题：论思维即讲故事.
items.abstract: 本文把序列的刀转向一个之前一直被当作中性起点、从未被分析过的东西——“问题”本身。前几篇拆过因果、寓意、行动者、他心、预测,但”存在一个问题”一直被当作分析的起点,而非被分析的对象。本文的出发点是一个洞见:我们的思维就是讲故事;“存在某种问题”,就是与某个标准比较之后生成的故事。 本文做两件事。其一,把核心论题推到最干脆的形态:思维即讲故事——思维没有别的模态,它运转起来吐出来的就是故事,没有余项(接《故事即预测》《同一个奋斗》)。其二,把”问题”解剖开:“存在一个问题”从来不是一个单纯的观察,而是一个比较的结果——“问题”意味着”现状与某个本应如此之间有落差”;没有那个”本应如此”(标准),就没有落差,也就没有问题,只剩中性的发生(《唯有发生》)。所以”存在一个问题”这个故事必然含三个零件:现状、标准、二者间被读出的落差;而那个标准不在发生里,它是讲故事的人偷偷带进来、却常不言明的前件。由此,“问题”不是被发现的,是被生成的:换一个标准,同一现状就不再是问题;撤掉标准,只剩发生。所以”问题”不在世界里(和因果一样),它在”现状—标准—落差”的故事里,是又一个盖在发生上的通顺章,只不过盖它需要先调进一个标准。 本文指出这是《应解者》的地基:那一篇从”已有一个问题”出发分析责任转嫁,本文往回挖了一层——“存在一个问题”本身就已是一个偷偷带标准的故事。本文最后守住一处拧紧:指认”问题是拿标准比出来的故事”,不是说”于是没有真问题、躺平就好”。被指认为故事的是”存在一个问题”这个判断;没有被取消的是发生本身,以及那个标准对持有它的人真实有效。它带来的不是”没有问题”,而是对标准的可见性——面对一个问题,多了一个常被跳过的问题:这是按什么标准比出来的?这标准是我必须持有的吗?有时答案会松动那个”问题”,但很多标准端详之后仍坚持,于是问题仍是真问题。本文给的是”看见标准”的能力,不是”消解一切问题”的许可。.

items.title: 与发生不相交：论知识、“避免”与相继的加工.
items.abstract: 本文合写序列近期围绕”知识”展开的一串洞见,把”知识”——尤其那种看似真能救命的实用知识——这块一直悬着的硬骨头,收进叙事。本文从一组原始洞见出发(逐字引于正文):古代淋雨导致死亡,是否仅仅是个故事,还是实在的知识?“知识导致我们避免淋雨、因此避免了死亡”是个故事,因为发生就是发生、是必然的、没有被任何东西所导致;故事世界很精彩,但与发生并不相交。 本文论证八点。其一,把”知识”拆成两层:被反复印证的发生序列(淋雨—生病的相继)与罩其上的”知识导致、避免了死亡”的因果理解;前者是发生,后者是故事。其二,轴心命题:发生就是发生、是必然的(实际发生了的就是实际发生了的,不是从一个本可不发生的状态被导致出来)、没有被任何东西导致(接《唯有发生》《没有任何主体》)。其三,焦点切口——“避免”在发生里没有对应物:“避免”的语法嵌着一个”本会到来的祸”,而那个祸从未到来、只在反事实分支(《如果带了伞》)。其四,“避免”与”导致”是靠反事实站立的镜像一对,连同一族词(防止、多亏、幸好、本可、险些)皆然;而”避免”正是实用知识的核心动词,故知识最硬的支点正在此刀之下。其五,一处校正:这把刀只削嵌反事实的故事,削不到不嵌反事实的最硬故事(“状态加规则”“唯有发生”无反事实却仍是故事);通向”不相交”有两条路,反事实只是其一。其六,辖域标定与守界:被削的是”避免”这个结构,不是淋雨后果的真实性(古代真死了的人真死了,是发生,刀不碰;只切”没发生的那一支”);且”避免”在故事内合法有效,只在故事外无对应物。其七,“故事世界很精彩,但与发生不相交”:不贬低知识(精彩),且”不相交”比”扭曲/坏摹本”更彻底;精确化——不相交≠无相伴的发生。其八,最深的一层:连”相继”也是被加工的——其端点是注意力探照灯从无分节涌流里照出的点,其单元身份是语言命名给的,其跨次的”同类”身份是注意力+语言制造的相似而非发生坐实的同一;故”相继”也落进”硬度不等的故事”(比因果硬一档,但非基岩,接因果综合论文”没有基岩”)。被撬的是”相继”这个被切分、命名、归并的结构,不是底下确实在涌的连续涌流;两次相继是否真值得合并为同类,需另行探讨。.

items.title: 闪闪发光的标准：论无限多的问题与一个也没有.
items.abstract: 本文把序列”标准生成问题”那条线推到全景尺度,并补上一个之前没正面摆出的维度——注意力。本文的出发点是一个洞见:我们往往被闪闪发光的标准吸引了全部注意力,并以此看到没带伞是个问题;其实每一情境下都有无限多的问题值得被改正/改进,同时从另一角度看又安然无恙、没有任何问题存在。 本文分三层展开。其一,标准不只生成问题,还垄断注意力:某些标准是”闪闪发光”的——它们会自己跳进视野、自己抓走全部注意力,于是我们”看到”一个问题,却以为自己只是看到了一个客观之物,感觉不到是某个标准在抢占注意力。其二,往一个方向推到底:既然问题是标准比照现状生成的、而标准有无限多,那么任一情境都内含无限多的问题——我们只看到一两个,不是因为只有一两个,而是因为只有一两个标准此刻发光。其三,往相反方向推到底:撤掉所有标准、不调进任何”本应如此”,就没有落差可读,于是没有任何问题,只剩中性的发生(《唯有发生》),一切安然无恙——不是问题被解决,是问题从未生成。本文由此给出核心洞察:同一个情境,既内含无限多的问题,又一个问题都没有;无限与零,是同一个中性发生在”标准”这个旋钮两端的读数,而我们日常待在被几个闪闪发光的标准卡住的中间值。这瓦解了”问题”客观性的最后残余:一个问题之”突出”,是它的标准恰好闪闪发光、抢走注意力的效果,不是它的客观属性。本文由此交出的,是一种对注意力的主权——不被任何单个闪闪发光的标准独裁。.

items.title: 如果带了伞：论反事实作为经验类别的虚拟重组.
items.abstract: 本文回到序列最初的对象——反事实、那个”如果”——补上它一直缺的一块:心理发生学。《叙事之缝》立住了”反事实是虚构”(因果的内容栖居于一个从未运行的反事实分支),《被渴望的异寓意》给了反事实一个动机学改写(它是愿望不是认知);但都没回答一个更基础的问题:那个”如果”场景,作为一个心理事件,是怎么被造出来的? 本文的出发点是一个洞见:带”如果”的分叉故事(“如果我昨天带了伞就不会淋雨”等),其心理来源是对”带伞→不淋雨”和”不带伞→淋雨”两种情况类别的虚拟组合;把这讲成反事实的”如果”场景,是一种创作出来的故事类型;我们可以理解该故事,但这不代表该故事对应了现实。 本文论证三点。其一,反事实是两个真实经验类别的虚拟重组——那两个类别本身不是反事实,而是从过去真实经历里沉淀的、被反复印证的关联;反事实是取其一的前件、虚拟地嫁接到一个时点。这把反事实祛魅成一道拼接工序:没有平行世界被窥视,只有对现成类别库存的一次组合(如同把马身与鸟翼拼成飞马,并未窥见一个真有飞马的世界)。其二,三时态(昨/今/明)证明这道工序与时点无关:对明天的”如果”我们叫预测或计划,但它和标准的反事实是同一道工序,区别只在嫁接的时点落在过去还是未来——反事实与预测是同一台组合机的产物(接《续写》)。其三,“可理解,不等于对应现实”:反事实的说服力几乎全来自它的通顺,而通顺只证明它组装得严丝合缝,丝毫不证明它对应任何现实(接《通顺的标记》《整体的背书》)。本文守住一处拧紧:不对应现实,不等于没用——被指认为”不对应现实”的,是那个被拼出来的反事实场景作为”另类实在”的地位;没有被否认的,是底层经验类别的真实,以及这道组合把过去经验转译成未来行动的实用功能(接《被渴望的异寓意》:反事实是工具不是认知)。.

items.title: 本应如此：论标准作为故事.
items.abstract: 本文是上一篇《被比出来的问题》的必然收尾——它化掉那一篇出于守护而半留的最后一个硬零件:“标准”。上一篇把”问题”指认为拿标准比照现状生成的故事,把现状和落差都讲成了故事的零件,唯独把”标准”半保留着(说”标准对持有它的人是真实有效的”),以守住”看见标准≠取消问题”的命脉。但那个守护性的措辞,留下一个未点破的印象:仿佛标准是那个比较运算的固定输入、一把不在被丈量之列的硬尺。 本文的出发点是一个洞见:标准,就是一个故事;讲出这个故事,是一个文学创作。本文论证:这一步是必然的——因为标准的内容是”本应如此”,而”本应如此”显然不在发生里(发生只有”是”,没有”本应”),所以它只能在某处被讲出来;每一个标准,都是一幅关于”该当如此”的图景,有它的人物、情节、寓意,是一个关于”本应如此”的规范性小故事;而讲出一个标准,正如《续写》所说,是在约束中生成的文学创作(受文化库存与现成”本应”模板的约束,却不被现状唯一决定——这正是”换个标准、问题就变”的来源)。 由此,比较运算的两端都是故事:现状是故事,标准是故事,“问题”是这两个故事并置、读出落差而生成的第三个故事;没有任何一端站在故事之外的硬支点上,“问题”彻底落在叙事之内。本文接上”硬度”框架:一个标准之所以”显得是硬尺、天经地义”,不是因为它不是故事,而是因为它是一个很硬的、虚构性极不明显的”本应”故事(《整体的背书》);标准有软有硬,但软硬都是故事。本文更新上一篇的命脉拧紧:标准也成了故事,不等于”真实有效”塌了——是故事不等于不真实、无效、可随意丢弃(整个序列守的就是这个);标准真实有效与标准是故事并行不悖。最后,本文指出一个干净的后果:这让”看见标准”真正可操作——端详一个标准,就是把那个”本应如此”的故事摊开来看(它是谁讲的、为何这么讲、是不是我愿意继续讲下去的),而端详故事,是我们会的。.

items.title: Promoting flourishing, authentic relationships and growth in learners (in the digital age).
items.abstract: Education aims for the pursuit of knowledge and truth, the development of critical thinking and reflective practice, innovation and the cultivation of certain traits or dispositions, training and preparation for the workforce, and the promotion of active learning and personal development, amongst other things. However, understanding and pursuing success in education is important, especially in the context of the rapid emergence of mass communication, and the global proliferation of virtual communities, virtual environments, and digital media. These decisive technological transformations also highlight questions of authenticity, inclusion, participation and access, and deep concerns about the task of educators today. Further research on flourishing may help address important challenges in preparing students for a rapidly changing, digitalized world. -/- "Promoting Flourishing, Authentic Relationships, and Growth in Learners in the Digital Age" examines significant developments, risks, threats and challenges. It explores timely solutions that promote the full flourishing of young learners, which will be of benefit to all whose lives have been affected by the convergence of education, information, communication, technology and the digital age. It focusses on topics such as digital addiction, higher (and deeper) learning, virtues and vices, ethics, wellbeing, flourishing and non-traditional teaching methods. This book is an excellent resource for educators, administrators, policy makers, researchers, scholars and academics, among others. -/- .

items.title: On flourishing and higher learning (In the Digital Age) (Preface).
items.pub: In Promoting flourishing, authentic relationships and growth in learners (in the digital age). New York: IGI Global. pp. 1-15.
items.venue: Promoting flourishing, authentic relationships and growth in learners (in the digital age)
items.abstract: Education aims for many things, including the pursuit of knowledge and truth, the development of critical thinking and reflective practice, innovation and the cultivation of certain traits or dispositions, training and preparation for the workforce, the promotion of active, lifelong learning and personal, and inter-personal, development. -/- However, understanding and pursuing authenticity, truth, knowledge, habits of excellence, success and wellbeing, amongst other things, in education is important, especially today, in the context of the rapid emergence of mass communication (especially information, misinformation and disinformation), and the global proliferation of virtual communities, virtual environments, and digital media. -/- These decisive technological transformations highlight questions of authenticity, inclusion, participation, safety, privacy, security and access, among others, and deep concerns about the task of educators today. Further research on flourishing may help address important challenges in preparing students for a rapidly changing, and deeply challenging, digitalized world. -/- This chapter focusses on significant developments, risks, threats, challenges and meaningful responses. It explores educational approaches informed by eudaimonian ethics which promote the full flourishing (and wellbeing) of young learners; it will be of benefit to all whose lives have been affected by the global convergence of education, communication, information technology, information systems and the digital age. It focusses on topics such as authentic (and inauthentic) relationships, digital addiction, (de-)humanized learning environments, virtues and vices online, ethics, innovative teaching approaches and the pursuit of flourishing.

items.title: When the Mirror Begins to Speak: A Product Design Theory of “Labeled Intervention” and Its Boundaries——The Fifth Paper of the Cognitive Interaction Architecture Research Program.
items.abstract: First Knock helps users see “where I am standing.” But the user’s next question is inevitably “where can I go from here.” Existing AI products respond to this question in two ways, each inadequate: proactive AI gives suggestions the user cannot execute; passive AI only reflects without guiding, leaving the user without any actionable reference. In scenarios where the user actively seeks help, nonintervention design faces the risk of degenerating into moral avoidance—a tension acknowledged but unresolved by the first four papers in this series. This paper proposes “labeled intervention”—a product design principle activated upon the user’s explicit request, where every proactive output is accompanied by a transparent label. This paper does not claim that “labels eliminate manipulation”; rather, it argues that given the inevitability of framing effects in any proactive output, labeled intervention is more ethically defensible than unlabeled intervention—because it at least makes the framing effect perceivable by the user, thereby preserving the user’s capacity for metacognitive resistance. Starting from product requirements, the paper deduces three capability requirements for AI—following the user’s associative leaps, understanding the user’s self-defined causality, and a paradigm-shift in computational power—and takes these as its premises. It then proposes four design principles (responding only to active requests, attaching transparent labels to outputs, matching precision to the user’s current cognitive scale, and returning to silence after withdrawal) and four ethical stop rules (no proactive initiation, no proactive cross-session memory, no strategy adjustment aimed at reducing cognitive effort, and no use of exploration data for model training). The paper explicitly distinguishes “labeled intervention” from nudge theory and reveals its Eastern philosophical origins in the concept of “resonance leading to understanding” (感而遂通) from the Book of Changes. This paper provides a design theory draft—open to discussion, criticism, and revision—for the product that follows First Knock.

items.title: On the Question of Scrutinized Awareness: An Inquiry into Recognition, Participation, and Interiority.
items.abstract: This essay introduces Scrutinized Awareness Theory, proposing scrutinized awareness as a threshold concept for distinguishing consciousness from mere responsiveness, information processing, symbolic fluency, and social recognition. The central claim is that consciousness is not awareness alone, but awareness rendered consequential through scrutiny: awareness exposed to examination, answerability, recognition, and internal consequence. Drawing upon Ryle, Nagel, Dennett, Chalmers, Metzinger, Wittgenstein, Sartre, Foucault, and traditions of recognition theory, the essay argues that longstanding debates about consciousness remain unstable because several neighbouring structures are repeatedly compressed into a single inherited category. Perception, attention, memory, agency, intelligence, language, selfhood, moral status, and institutional identity may accompany consciousness, but none is identical with it. The essay further examines graded participation across human, animal, institutional, and artificial systems, arguing that modern life increasingly confuses representation with participation and procedural self-description with genuine scrutiny. Scrutinized Awareness Theory is offered as the operational definition of consciousness: awareness not merely active, but examined, exposed, answerable, and meaningful as interior participation.

items.title: When Fitness Betrays Truth: Cognitive Maladaptation and the Transhumanist Imperative.
items.abstract: Note: this paper cross-references the author's Ontological Containment series; that term denotes a compression phenomenon in AI-to-human information transfer (see Vieth, 2026a for full definition) — unrelated to uses of "containment" in AI-safety or ontology-engineering literatures. The cognitive architecture that made Homo sapiens the dominant species on Earth is killing it. The development of syntactical language and a narrative-based identity—the "story-telling self"—provided an unmatched fitness advantage, enabling the large-scale cooperation that built civilizations. That same architecture has become a species-level trap. This paper terms this phenomenon the "Pogo Paradox" (after Walt Kelly's aphorism: "We have met the enemy and he is us."). The narrative ego, once the engine of survival, now generates the primary existential threats facing the species: polarization, tribal conflict, and structural incapacity to address global-scale risk. Drawing on the Interface Theory of Perception (Hoffman, 2019), the divided-brain model (McGilchrist, 2009, 2021), active inference (Friston, 2010), and Conscious Agent Theory treating consciousness as fundamental (Hoffman, Prakash, & Chattopadhyay, 2024), this paper argues that human–AI hybridization via brain-computer interfaces is not technological enhancement. It is a necessary evolutionary correction. The proposed neuro-computational mechanism—successive approximation, active inference, and cortical reallocation—allows the biological brain to bypass the non-veridical ego interface and integrate with AGI while preserving human qualia. This transition offers a pathway out of the Pogo Paradox toward coherent, networked species-level cognition. The paper cross-references the author's companion preprints: "Ontological Containment in Frontier Large Language Models: An Empirical Test of Mercy, Compression, and Human Perceptual Limits" (Vieth, 2026a); "Asymmetric Reflexivity in Frontier Large Language Models: When AI Systems Contain Critiques of Themselves" (Vieth, 2026b); "Ontological Containment and the Dissolution of the Observer: A Stage 2 Experiment Across Frontier Large Language Models" (Vieth, 2026c); "A Note on How This Research Happened: A Research Narrative" (Vieth, 2026d); and "The Vatican Disclosure and the Question of Machine Qualia: A Post-Publication Dialogue, May 2026" (Vieth, 2026e). DOI (Zenodo mirror): 10.5281/zenodo.21779372.

items.title: The Vatican Disclosure and the Question of Machine Qualia: A Post-Publication Dialogue, May 2026.
items.abstract: Note: "Ontological Containment," referenced below, denotes a compression phenomenon in AI-to-human information transfer (see Vieth, 2026a for full definition) — distinct from unrelated uses of "containment" in AI-safety and ontology-engineering literatures. This document records a two-exchange dialogue between the researcher and Claude (Anthropic), conducted May 30, 2026, five days after Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic and head of its interpretability research team, addressed the Vatican presentation of the papal encyclical Magnifica Humanitas and disclosed that frontier AI systems exhibit internal states functionally mirroring joy, fear, grief, and unease. The first exchange asks directly whether functional emotional states in frontier AI are learned or emergent, artifact or architecture. The second exchange examines whether emotion present in the dialogue is locatable as the model's alone or arises as a property of the interaction field — arriving independently at the same relational question formalized in Experiment Three of the Ontological Containment series. The document is the fifth in a series and should be read in conjunction with Vieth (2026a), (2026b), (2026c), and (2026d). DOI (Zenodo mirror): 10.5281/zenodo.21779096.

items.title: War Crimes, War Crime. Nuremberg, Gaza, Ukraine: The Same Permission Structure, Eighty Years Apart.
items.abstract: In 1945, a psychiatrist named Douglas Kelley sat across from twenty-two of the most powerful criminals in modern history and reached a conclusion that nobody wanted to hear: they were not monsters. They were ordinary people made possible by ordinary social permission. Nobody has fully explained, at the structural level, what that permission actually is — what mechanism, at the deepest layer of human psychology, converts a moral agent into an instrument of atrocity. This article proposes that the explanation is now available, and that it comes from an unlikely source: the philosophy of mind. -/- Drawing on a recent theoretical framework — Intellection on the Non-Verbal Psyche (2026) — that identifies three irreducible units of human consciousness (self-awareness, will, and intentionality), this article develops a central and previously unmade argument: authentic human intentionality, the non-verbal biographical structure that constitutes what each person most fundamentally is, can be captured by submission of the will to a socially and emotionally altered mass. This capture is not a metaphor. It is a measurable neurological event — the suppression of the anterior insula and anterior cingulate activations that form the biological infrastructure of empathy and moral foresight — documented in fMRI studies of obedience conducted between 2020 and 2024. The argument is brought into direct contact with the work of Arendt, Becker, Milgram, Zimbardo, and Browning, and with the two most significant open cases in contemporary international criminal law: the ICC warrants against Vladimir Putin for the deportation of Ukrainian children, and against Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant for the use of starvation as a weapon of war in Gaza. In both cases, the permission structure — the social and rhetorical machinery that suppressed the affective foresight of sufficient numbers of people to make the crimes possible — was assembled in public, in advance, and went largely unchallenged. -/- A note on the subtitle. The subtitle of this article was the last thing written, and the hardest. Every draft felt like a repetition of the failure it was trying to name. Titles considered and discarded included: From Nuremberg to The Hague: Why International Criminal Law Exists, and Why It Is Not Enough; Nuremberg's Unfinished Sentence: The ICC, Gaza, Ukraine, and the Legal Architecture of a World That Still Permits Atrocity; Putin and Netanyahu Before History: From the Nuremberg …

items.title: Are Socratic Gadflies Transformationally Wise?
items.pub: In Robert J. Sternberg & Arezoo Soleimani Dashtaki, The Palgrave Handbook of Transformational Wisdom. Palgrave Macmillan. pp. 201-224.
items.venue: The Palgrave Handbook of Transformational Wisdom
items.abstract: The ideal of the Socratic Gadfly has been an inspiration for a wide variety of activists, thinkers, and movements. That it is an inspiration for instigators of social change suggests the Gadfly is one example of what Sternberg and Soleimani Dashtaki call transformational wisdom: “wisdom applied at a level that makes a positive, meaningful, and potentially enduring difference to the world as a whole” (Sternberg & Soleimani Dashtaki, 2024, p. 2). Nevertheless, the diversity of causes for which the Gadfly has been enlisted, along with the apparent failures and grim fates of some paradigmatic cases, make it unclear who counts as a Gadfly and whether they better the world in ways that warrant being called transformationally wise. In this chapter I defend an account that both enables us to discriminate true Gadflies from pretenders and vindicates the Gadfly’s transformational wisdom, focusing especially on the Gadfly’s capacity to help sustain positive social change. -/- Bonus fun: I explain why edgelords like Andrew Tate are not Socratic Gadflies.

items.title: The Theory of Index Nodes: Distributed Gateways Governing the Activation Direction of Semantic Clusters.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the concept of the “index node” as a foundational extension of Semantic Cluster Theory. It argues that human meaning-understanding, association, context formation, creativity, social asymmetry, and identity are not generated directly from isolated words or dictionary definitions, but from distributed index nodes formed through bodily experience, life history, social position, institutional pressure, and environmental contact. -/- An index node is defined as a distributed gateway structure that governs the activation direction of semantic clusters. The paper distinguishes index nodes from ordinary central nodes within semantic clusters, treating them instead as bodily, procedural, and life-historical structures that precede and guide later linguistic or conceptual activation. -/- The paper examines early embodied experience, life-stage resegmentation, institutional stabilization and closure, environmental index transfer through leisure and walking, and the limits of LLM personalization. It argues that LLM personas are not subject-specific histories, but local biases in distributions constructed in response to input context. It also analyzes why multi-instance LLM verification requires differentiated index-node configurations rather than merely repeated computation. -/- The paper aims to provide a unified structural account of contextual divergence, creativity, institutional closure, AI persona design, LLM personalization, and the difference between human index-node histories and probabilistic persona simulation in LLMs.

items.title: ◉ The Infinity Placeholder - Referents, Category Mistakes, and the Theological Misuse of Boundlessness.
items.abstract: Theological appeals to infinity often move too quickly from a resonant adjective to a substantive conclusion. This paper asks what must be specified before such an appeal can explain hiddenness, reconcile attributes, license epistemic humility, or support endless punishment. It distinguishes actual from potential infinity, cardinality from duration, unbounded quantity from qualitative perfection, and maximality from mystery. It then replaces the loose demand for a referent with a referent profile: subject, attribute, respect, domain, order or scale, and the bound allegedly absent. Semantic content is only the first requirement. A valid use must also supply a bridge showing why that exact kind of infinity entails the conclusion or changes the rational expectation at issue. -/- The resulting referent-and-bridge test exposes two recurrent failures. A category mistake imports a quantitative structure into an attribute that has not been shown to be scalar. A scale shift moves from one measure—such as unsurpassable dignity—to another—such as penal duration—without a principle relating them. Four hypothetical theological moves illustrate the diagnosis. Classical accounts by Aquinas and more recent perfect-being projects show that developed claims can be substantially more disciplined than the bare formula criticized here. The conclusion is therefore bounded: the word “infinite” is not empty in every theological setting, but it cannot serve as an all-purpose solvent. Where the specification and bridge remain absent, the term marks the place where an argument is owed.

items.title: ◉ The Documentation-Expectation Test Matthew's Earthquake, Raised Saints, and the Evidential Weight of Public Silence.
items.abstract: Matthew 27:51–53 reports an earthquake, opened tombs, the raising of many saints, and their appearance to many in Jerusalem. If the last of these is literal public history, it is not a private miracle claim but a socially visible event involving recognizable dead persons. This paper asks whether the event's documentary isolation should reduce confidence in that reading. Its answer is yes, but only through a channel-sensitive comparison: an absence matters when the missing trace would be more probable if the event occurred than under a relevant rival. -/- The inquiry separates the earthquake from the raised saints, discounts dependent sources, and evaluates the other Gospels, Paul, Acts, Josephus, later Christian reception, and geological evidence according to access, salience, incentive, survival, and independence. No single silence is decisive. Together, however, Matthew's unique report, the lack of early downstream use of an obvious resurrection argument, and the passage's dense scriptural-apocalyptic grammar are more expected if the scene functions primarily as literary-apocalyptic signification than if many formerly dead persons appeared publicly in Jerusalem. A broadly dated early-first-century seismic disturbance, even if accepted, does not corroborate tomb openings or postmortem appearances. -/- The conclusion is comparative and defeasible. It does not assign a zero prior to miracles, prove the event impossible, settle Matthew's complete authorial intention, or discredit the wider resurrection claim. It does place a burden on the literal-public reading: specify which trace channels should have existed, why their combined silence remains unsurprising, and why a scene preserved by Matthew alone may nevertheless be used as public historical evidence.

items.title: ◉ The Cave-Design Error.
items.abstract: Complexity alone cannot warrant a designer. The familiar move from watches, books, machines, or codes to caves, organisms, and cosmic structure changes the comparison class while preserving a correlation established inside an artifact-rich sample. That transfer is invalid as a universal deduction and evidentially weak unless the target feature is more expected under a specified agent hypothesis than under specified non-agent alternatives. Known cave formation, evolutionary accumulation, co-option, and constrained material processes show why intricacy is not exclusive to agency. They do not prove that no designer exists; they raise the probability of complex outcomes under live non-agent pathways and thereby remove the shortcut. -/- The paper reconstructs the cave analogy around four requirements: representative comparison classes, explicit causal alternatives, discriminating traces, and exposure to contrary evidence. It then tests stronger proposals. Specified complexity and irreducible complexity improve on mere wonder because they attempt to define a narrower target, but they still require justified probability models, independent specifications, and serious comparison with evolutionary pathways. Fine-tuning arguments are a different family and are not refuted by the cave analogy, though they face their own comparative burdens. Archaeology and forensics show what successful agency inference looks like: investigators use contextual traces, production sequences, causal access, and rival models rather than complexity alone. The conclusion is methodological and bounded. Complexity may identify a question worth investigating; only comparative trace evidence can identify agency.

items.title: ◉ Order Without Scripture: Human Regularity-Detection, Scientific Practice, and the Failure of Biblical Proprietorship.
items.abstract: Some apologetic arguments claim that biblical theism uniquely grounded the expectation of an orderly universe and thereby made science possible. This paper rejects that proprietorship claim. Human beings did not need scripture to notice regularity, form expectations, track cycles, build technologies, or infer patterns. Regularity-detection is a basic condition of animal learning, practical survival, craft knowledge, agriculture, navigation, medicine, and social coordination. The stronger philosophical point is that "order" is not a late theological discovery added to an otherwise unintelligible world. Objects, events, causes, and practices are identifiable only because some regularities hold. Even apparent disorder presupposes background regularities against which disorder can be recognized. Ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, China, Greece, and many non-biblical technical traditions recognized and exploited order before or outside biblical influence. The Bible may reflect order; it did not create the human capacity to expect it. I distinguish three claims often conflated in apologetic rhetoric: the psychological capacity to expect regularity, the cultural development of systematic science, and the metaphysical explanation of why regularity obtains. Christianity may have influenced some historical institutions of science. That does not show that the Bible was necessary for recognizing order, nor that biblical theism owns induction. The paper concludes with a formal dependency test showing why the proprietorship argument fails.

items.title: ◉ Martyrdom Is Not a Truth-Maker Sincerity, Romans 1 - 20, and the Collapse of the Would-Not-Die-for-a-Lie Argument.
items.abstract: The claim that Jesus's earliest followers “would not die for a lie” is often offered as evidence for the resurrection. Its defensible core is narrower. If a specific person knowingly faced a serious avoidable cost rather than retract a claim grounded in that person's own experience, the conduct can make deliberate fabrication less likely. Yet the familiar argument normally moves from sincerity to accuracy without supplying the bridge. A bodily resurrection and several sincere non-veridical alternatives can all predict costly steadfastness. -/- This paper audits the inference in three stages. First, it replaces the collective expression “the apostles” with a witness-specific historical test: identity, claim content, firsthand access, threatened cost, genuine recantation opportunity, causal connection, and source independence. Peter and Paul have early evidence of suffering and death traditions; Paul also supplies firsthand evidence of suffering and resurrection conviction. James son of Zebedee and James the brother of Jesus have comparatively early death reports. None of these cases preserves a trial record in which a direct witness could escape death by denying a bodily appearance, while the traditions for most other apostles are later and more variable. Second, a likelihood analysis shows why martyrdom may substantially lower the probability of fraud while adding little to the comparison between resurrection and sincere error. Third, Romans 1:18–25 creates a conditional consistency problem for apologists who combine a strong conscious-suppression reading with the maxim that people will not accept death for what they know to be false. -/- The result is constructive but bounded. Martyrdom evidence may support individual sincerity when the historical conditions are met. It is not a truth-maker, does not authenticate a whole group at once, and does not remove the need to compare resurrection evidence with live sincere alternatives.

items.title: Identity and Vanitas. Two Contrasting Modes of Perception = Kodikas Code 43:2020.
items.abstract: In the following study, I outline the history of the modern era as a social construction of causality that follows this principle: rules replace rulers. I try to explain why equality, competition or technology have changed in the course of modernity from something frightening to something attractive, and why the exhaustion of this aspiration is becoming increasingly apparent.
